0 — NAVIGATION PREAMBLE

How to read this as a story — the one character to follow

This is a long, adversarial document, and it will be far easier to read if you read it as a story with a single protagonist. Here is the whole arc in four sentences, so you know what to hold onto.

The premise is the cheapest honest thing anyone can say about exotic propulsion: before you spend a dollar chasing a claim, there is one cheapest test that would kill it — and finding that first-failure test is worth more than any glossy promise. The character you bond with is not a ship and not a person; it is the First-Failure Engine, a frozen, un-tunable screening machine whose only personality trait is that it refuses to lie. You will not learn to trust it because it gives you what you want — you learn to trust it precisely because, at the one moment it could have sold you a result (the worked exemplar MID-METRIC-001, which really does shorten the forward path by ~0.22%), it instead hands you the knife: it names the single number it cannot pay for and kills its own best candidate. That refusal is the bond. Once you trust a machine that will not lie even to itself, you are ready for the journey — not "we built a drive," but "here is the one frozen test that would change our mind, and here is everything of value that survives even when the answer is no."

So read for the Engine. Watch it imprint (it tells you exactly what would kill a candidate), watch it earn trust (it kills its own most tempting result at the source/energy gate rather than overclaim), and then take the journey it offers (an option, never a purchase; a filter, never an engine). The full one-page version of this story is immediately below in §0.0; the rest of the document is the Engine keeping that promise, gate by gate. The ceiling never rises above PASS_TOY, and the strongest verb anywhere is "screen."

This is the front-of-book map for a long, deliberately self-critical document. Read the three pages here before opening any chapter; they tell you what the document is, what it refuses to claim, the three leaves to read first, where the 42 core red-team leaves (Parts A–J) live and how each one closed — plus the extension parts that follow them (Part K reference tables; Part L buildability & IP ladder; Parts M/N native-geometry cross-formalism & re-analysis; Part O subsystem & challenge register; Part P commercial strategy; Part Q consolidated S1/S2/S3 gate-design results) — and which reference tables to consult to orient.

0.0 — The story in one page

Premise. Mars needs better filters before it needs bigger claims. A strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer receives a steady stream of exotic-propulsion ideas, and almost all of them fail — but they fail silently: a coordinate trick here, an unsourced metric there, a hidden negative-energy demand somewhere else, each one costing real diligence time and leaving nothing behind. This platform makes those ideas fail loudly, reproducibly, and usefully — it names the exact gate each candidate dies at, what would have to change to revive it, and what reusable assets survive regardless. And if one candidate ever survives the frozen physics gates, the acquirer controls the IP window before the world knows.

Protagonist — the First-Failure Engine. The thing you are asked to bond with is not a ship and not a person; it is a fail-closed screening system, the First-Failure Engine. Its defining trait is skepticism: it refuses to believe its own most tempting result until the source, energy, gauge, causality, EFT, and UV gates all allow it. It is the machine that refuses to lie. It earns trust the only honest way — by declining to overclaim — and every incompleteness in it can only ever downgrade or hold a candidate, never promote one. (The project is still named the Mars Metric-Interface Drive; the protagonist is the Engine inside it.)

Antagonist — false promotion. The adversary is not orthodox physics and not skepticism. The adversary is false promotion: a result that looks like motion but is only one of five disguises — a coordinate artifact, a source debt the candidate never pays, hidden exotic energy, a pure-gauge relabeling, or UV borrowing against an un-adopted assumption. The whole Engine exists to strip those disguises off before anyone writes "propulsion."

Trust event — MID-METRIC-001 (read it early). The emotional anchor sits up front, and it is a reversal. The temptation first: the worked exemplar MID-METRIC-001 really does shorten the forward path by ~0.22% — invariant, sub-luminal, EFT-valid, with a nonzero curvature scalar (R ≠ 0) proving it is no coordinate mirage; every straw-man check that would expose a fake passes. A weaker document headlines exactly this. Then the kill: the Engine asks what pays for that deficit, and the answer is a single number it cannot source — a negative effective energy density, ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ at the lobe center, exotic, NEC/WEC/DEC all violated, supplied by no declared field. In reading order the source gate fails first (terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, HC-02); the exotic ρ_eff < 0 is the root cause (energy gate HC-03, status AUDIT). The Engine kills its own best result. That refusal — turning a seductive effect into a named failure by one computed number instead of a sales line — is precisely why the platform is worth reviewing.

Journey. You want Mars faster. Exotic-propulsion claims are seductive and almost always wrong. The Engine is built to reject seductive wrongness; it finds a real local effect and kills it at the source and energy gates; that refusal is what creates trust. From there the path is an option, not a purchase: a strategic acquirer options the screening-platform IP and funds a frozen, 90-day hostile validation sprint — and converts only if the frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE predicate is actually hit and independent hostile review agrees. There is no route from a "no" to "acquire a drive."

Stakes. If one candidate survives the frozen milestone, the acquirer controls the IP window before anyone else. If none survive — the expected outcome — the acquirer still owns a rigorous, IP-protected native-geometry method and a validated negative-control corpus that no one else can practice. The downside is bounded by one sprint's cost; the residue survives every failure.

1. What this is — and what it is NOT

What this is. A failure-mode engine — the document's protagonist and emotional anchor, The First-Failure Engine: a simulation-first, fail-closed software platform whose unit of work is to take one candidate metric-interface excitation profile Ξ_drive(t,x) and emit a machine-checked gate-card that names the earliest gate at which the candidate fails, what would have to change to close that failure, and what reusable simulation / classification / control assets survive regardless of outcome. (The project's name is the Mars Metric-Interface Drive; the protagonist you bond with is the Engine, not the ship.) It is the machine that refuses to lie: it will not believe its own most tempting result until every gate allows it. Its credibility comes from systematically and reproducibly showing where candidates break, not from exhibiting a survivor. The offered asset is this discriminator plus the provisional IP around it.

What it is built to defeat. The Engine has exactly one antagonist, and it is false promotion — a result that looks like motion but is only one of five disguises: a coordinate artifact, an unpaid source debt, hidden exotic energy, a pure-gauge relabeling, or UV borrowing against an un-adopted assumption. The antagonist is not orthodox physics and not skepticism; it is the seductive false positive. Every gate below exists to strip one of those disguises off before the word "propulsion" is ever permitted.

What this is NOT. It is not a warp drive, not a working drive, not a build, not a propulsion claim, and not a faster-than-light demonstration. The absolute status ceiling anywhere in the corpus is PASS_TOY — a status-labeled simulation result on a defined toy geometry. The closure ladder's top rung, 5 PHYSICAL_CLAIM, is marked out of scope and not targeted anywhere. The document is simulation-first: every number is the output of a declared computation on a declared reference background, the energy gate is never a clean PASS (its best status is "audit-visible"), and the local→global step that would be needed for any travel-time claim is blocked by theorem (G3: a positive local shortening score does not integrate to a global Δt). It generates no hardware, high-energy-source, beam, reactor, or build content of any kind — that is out of scope by construction, not by modesty. Most candidate modes are expected to fail; the framework is engineered so its every incompleteness can only ever downgrade or hold a candidate, never promote one — it will never report that a candidate works when it does not.

2. Read these three first

If you read nothing else, read these three leaves, in this order. Together they give you the ask, the one worked example carried end-to-end, and the document's own honest list of what it cannot do.

# Leaf Why it is first The one thing to take from it
1 A2 — Executive Technical Memo (the ask + the milestone) The single document a diligence team should read first. States the ask (option the provisional + fund a 90-day hostile validation sprint) and, in §4, the one quantitative "what-would-change-our-mind" milestone. The milestone is a single binary predicate: at least one mode reaches EFT_CANDIDATE with a matched source ledger, χ_source < 1, under a named, separately-published UV assumption, with invariants and causality PASS, no FAIL, energy AUDIT. Hit ⇒ the option converts (a physicist's deep dive is justified — not "physical"). Missed (expected) ⇒ the acquirer keeps a rigorous, IP-protected screening tool for one sprint's cost.
2 G1 — Worked exemplar (MID-METRIC-001) The one candidate carried through all ten gates with real numbers (Christoffels, Riemann, G_μν, T_eff, NEC/WEC/DEC, χ). It is the concrete proof that the gates compute and that an honest terminal status is shown, not faked. Terminal status 2 TOY_TESTED / AUDIT, token TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC — the deepest-surviving example in the document. Its real, invariant forward-distance deficit (~0.22%) is sourced by NEC/WEC/DEC-violating negative energy (ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ at the lobe center) that no declared source supplies. First failure = source gate (HC-02), terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC; root cause = energy gate (HC-03), exotic ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶, status AUDIT. It does not pass; that is the point.
3 H2 — Honest-weakness ledger The framework attacks itself. Names the three weaknesses upstream of every gate and answers each in writing. (1) No candidate passes — by design (a falsifier is not a prover; the asset is the falsifier). (2) The interacting quantum / BV sector is a fail-closed placeholder (bv_master_placeholder) — proven incapable of leaking a false PASS, but with near-zero resolving power on interacting modes. (3) The Fable/TOE corpus is unverified — it enters only as admissibility-tightening configuration data on top of corpus-agnostic GR/EFT gates; the patent estate is severable from it. All three errors are one-sided toward conservatism.

0. Title page

The Mars Metric-Interface Drive

A Simulation-First, Fail-Closed Platform for Screening, Classifying, and Visualizing Candidate Metric-Interface Excitation Profiles

A ~690-page technical design document. Recipient: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer. Document class: design document + provisional-patent support package + simulation-framework specification. Document is NOT: a drive, a build, a propulsion claim, or an FTL claim.

Volume A — Front matter, claim boundary, and reading guide. Leaf A1 of the front-matter set.

Status banner (applies to every page): Every worked example in this document carries a status label. The absolute ceiling anywhere in the document is PASS_TOY — a status-labeled simulation result on a defined toy. No example in this document reaches an operational, physical, or hardware claim. Most candidate modes are expected to fail their gates. That is the intended outcome.

The object under study is a vehicle-comoving, front/back-asymmetric metric-interface excitation profile, written compactly as

Ξ_drive(t, x) = { δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge data }

where δg_μν is a perturbation of the 4D spacetime metric, δA_μ^a are gauge-field perturbations (index a over the gauge factor), δφ^I are scalar/moduli perturbations (index I over the scalar manifold), δG_μA are mixed metric components coupling the 4D directions μ to internal directions A, and δG_AB are internal-metric (compact-factor) perturbations. The platform asks a single falsifiable question about each such profile:

Does this profile reduce a forward proper-distance functional D[Ξ] along a vehicle-comoving forward lobe, relative to a declared reference background, while simultaneously surviving the invariant-distance, source, energy-condition, gauge, quantization, causality, and UV/global-stability gates?

The honest answer for almost every profile is expected to be "no, and here is the first gate it fails." The document's value is in where and how each candidate fails, what would be required to close that failure, and what reusable simulation/control/classification assets remain valuable regardless of outcome. This is the protagonist's defining discipline, and it is enforced in the validator itself: the document refuses propulsion language for any candidate whose source gate is not a clean PASS — no matter how tempting the geometric effect looks. The strongest verb available anywhere in this document is "screen," never "propel."

1. Abstract

This document specifies, motivates, and red-teams a metric-interface evaluation platform — the document's protagonist, The First-Failure Engine: a simulation-first software system that screens candidate excitation profiles Ξ_drive(t,x) against a fixed ladder of physics gates and emits status-labeled results plus a first-failure ledger. It is deliberately not a spacecraft, a propulsion system, or a faster-than-light claim. It is, in the project's own language, a "failure-mode engine with option value" — the machine that refuses to lie, whose whole job is to refuse propulsion language until every gate earns it. Its single antagonist is false promotion: a result that looks like motion but is only coordinates, an unpaid source debt, hidden exotic energy, pure gauge, or UV borrowing.

The technical core is a proper-distance functional evaluated on a vehicle-comoving worldtube. Given a spacelike forward-pointing curve γ in a hypersurface Σ_t adapted to the vehicle frame, define

D[Ξ] = ∫_γ sqrt( g_ij(Ξ) dx^i dx^j )  ds        (forward proper-distance functional)
ΔD   = D[Ξ] − D[Ξ = 0]                          (signed change vs reference background)

A candidate is interesting only if ΔD < 0 (a genuine forward-lobe shortening) and that shortening is a coordinate-invariant statement — i.e., it survives recomputation under diffeomorphism, tetrad re-choice, and is corroborated by curvature scalars and geodesic integration, not produced by a clock/ruler relabeling. The platform therefore couples D[Ξ] to a chain of independent checks:

  1. Invariant-distance gate (HC-01): recompute ΔD in ≥2 coordinate charts and in an orthonormal tetrad; require agreement to tolerance and corroboration by at least one curvature invariant (e.g. the Kretschmann scalar K = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ}) and by null/timelike geodesic travel statistics. A profile whose ΔD is chart-dependent is downgraded to FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY.
  2. Source & stress-energy gate (HC-02): invert the field equation to read off the stress-energy the profile demands, T_μν^req = (M_Pl²) G_μν[g+δg] − T_μν^known, and require a complete, declared source ledger. A profile whose required source is absent or unaccounted is downgraded to FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC. "Propulsion" language is forbidden whenever the source gate is not PASS.
  3. Energy-condition / exoticity gate (HC-03): in an orthonormal tetrad, report NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC violations and an exoticity score. The energy gate is never a clean PASS — its best status is "audit-visible." Hidden negative-energy demand yields FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY.
  4. Causality / horizon gate (HC-04): screen for closed timelike curves, horizon formation, signature change, and global-hyperbolicity proxies; reject pathological profiles before any mission statement is permitted.
  5. Gauge-redundancy gate (HC-05): reject profiles that are pure gauge (δg_μν = ∇_μ ξ_ν + ∇_ν ξ_μ for some ξ, or δA_μ = ∂_μ Λ). A pure-gauge "effect" is downgraded to FAIL_PURE_GAUGE.
  6. BRST/BV physical-state gate (HC-06): for any quantized mode, require Q_BRST|Ψ⟩ = 0, not BRST-exact, positive-norm; otherwise mark AUDIT_QUANTUM. The interacting quantum-gravity sector is held at AUDIT throughout — we do not claim quantum gravity is closed.
  7. Unified-mode admissibility (HC-07): every excitation component must map to exactly one of three layers — × metric/geometric base, ⊕ admissibility/projection/chamber, ⊗ bundles/operators/quantization — with a no-new-primitive scan and a no-double-counting audit on the stress ledger.
  8. UV / compactification / global-stability boundary (HC-08): any dependence on global compactification stability or vacuum-energy tuning is classified UV_DELEGATED, never silently adopted. The corpus's global UV stability is OPEN and its enabling axiom UNADOPTED; we honor that boundary.
  9. EFT cutoff & backreaction (HC-09): require the admissibility margin χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1 and a bounded backreaction score before any EFT_CANDIDATE label is permitted.
  10. Mars-mission relevance (HC-10): any Mars/mission visualization is a validity-weighted overlay — every plotted effect is multiplied by a gate-pass mask and carries a watermark recording its closure status. A mission plot without a gate overlay is downgraded to FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

The platform's closure ladder has six levels: 0 UNDEFINED → 1 TOY_DEFINED → 2 TOY_TESTED → 3 EFT_CANDIDATE → 4 PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY → 5 PHYSICAL_CLAIM. Level 5 is explicitly out of scope. Promotion across the ladder is evidence-gated and authority-gated: an automated agent may never promote a candidate on its own authority; promotion past PASS_TOY requires owner/attorney escalation.

The corpus on which geometry, force-routing, and quantization discipline are anchored (the Fable / TOE_FINAL documents) is treated as configuration data, not as a propulsion warrant, and is not assumed correct: where a claim can be stated corpus-agnostically against standard general relativity and effective field theory, we prefer that formulation. The framework does NOT depend on the correctness of the underlying unified theory — it is a general GR/EFT screening tool that runs against standard inputs (the executed reference repo reproduces the same gates on the published Alcubierre, Natário, and Van Den Broeck warp metrics, all returning FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC), the theory is one optional configuration rather than a dependency, and the patent claims do not require it. The deliverables are four interlocking artifact classes — manuscript (this document), patent support (claim-seed matrix, embodiments, fallback claims), software (simulation modules, schemas, tests, dashboards), and review (red-team objections, first-failure ledger, forbidden-promotion scan).

Net claim of this abstract, stated at the strongest language the discipline allows: We present a reproducible, machine-checkable framework that can be configured to screen candidate metric-interface profiles and emit status-labeled simulation results; individual candidates are retained as simulation or EFT candidates only if they pass the declared invariant-distance, source, gauge, quantization, causality, and UV-boundary gates. No candidate in this document is asserted to be a working drive, and the framework's usefulness does not depend on any candidate passing.

First failure of the abstract itself: the abstract advertises a complete gate ladder, but the binding constraint on the entire program is HC-02 source closure — without a declared, physically available source ledger, every downstream "distance-shortening" result is at best FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, and the abstract's promise of "candidate modes" collapses to "toy geometries." This is named, not hidden.

2. Claim boundary — stated BEFORE any technical claim

This section is placed before every technical chapter on purpose. No reader should encounter a single equation in this document without first having read what the document is and is not claiming.

2.0 UNVERIFIED THEORY — the framework does NOT depend on the underlying unified theory

We do not ask you to believe the unified theory. The platform is a general GR/EFT screening tool that works against standard inputs; the theory is one optional configuration, not a dependency.

Stated plainly, for a strategic acquirer: the correctness of the underlying Fable / TOE_FINAL unified theory is NOT a prerequisite for anything in this document. The framework treats corpus-derived constraints purely as configuration data — inputs you can swap, disable, or ignore — not as a physical warrant and not as something you must accept. Everything load-bearing is the gate machinery itself, which is built against textbook general relativity and effective field theory, and which runs identically whether or not the Fable/TOE framework is ever validated.

This is not an assertion you have to take on faith; it is demonstrated by the executed reference repository. The same gates reproduce verbatim on the standard, peer-reviewed, published warp metrics — Alcubierre, Natário, and Van Den Broeck — none of which has anything to do with the corpus. Run against those textbook inputs, the platform computes a minimum null-energy-condition value of NEC_min = −0.27 (Alcubierre), −0.27 (Natário), −0.16 (Van Den Broeck), and returns FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC for all three — exactly the fail-closed behavior the discipline promises, on inputs that owe nothing to the unified theory. The tool filters published GR metrics the same way it filters corpus-conditioned candidates; the theory is one optional configuration line, not a load-bearing premise.

The same independence holds for the IP: the patent claims do not require the theory. The disclosed systems and methods (the gate-card schema, the validator, the closure ladder, the source-reconstruction and energy-condition engines, the validity-weighted overlay) operate on any metric ansatz and are novel and useful regardless of whether the Fable/TOE framework is correct, incorrect, or never adjudicated. If the unified theory is wrong, the screening platform, its reference results on standard metrics, and the patent claims are all entirely unaffected.

2.1 What this document IS

  • A design document for a simulation-first, fail-closed evaluation platform whose unit of work is "screen one candidate Ξ_drive profile and emit a gate-card with a named first failure."
  • A classifier and visualizer of candidate metric-interface excitation profiles, with a fixed status ladder and a downgrade tree.
  • A failure-mode engine with option value. Its credibility derives from systematically and reproducibly showing where candidates fail, not from exhibiting a survivor.
  • A provisional-patent support package for the methods, systems, schemas, and control/classification software — assets that are valuable independent of whether any physical drive is ever realized.
  • A corpus-conditioned but corpus-agnostic-preferring analysis: corpus constraints enter as configuration; standard-GR/EFT formulations are preferred wherever available.

3.2 The effective action and the three-layer discipline (read once, applies everywhere)

Every chapter is written against one effective action and one field-classification discipline. The action is

S_eff = ∫ d⁴x sqrt(-g) [ (M_Pl²/2) R
                         − (1/4) Z_ab F^a·F^b
                         − (1/2) G_IJ ∂φ^I ∂φ^J
                         − V(φ)
                         + L_matter + L_constraint + L_EFT ]

with the stress-energy read off by variation,

T_μν = −(2/sqrt(-g)) · δS_matter/δg^μν .

Every excitation component of Ξ_drive MUST be assigned to exactly one of three layers, and that assignment is checked mechanically:

Symbol Layer What lives here Example components
× metric/geometric base 4D metric, internal metric, compact factors δg_μν, δG_AB, δG_μA
⊕ admissibility/projection/chamber which modes survive constraints (F+, admissibility) chamber masks, projection operators
⊗ bundles/operators/quantization fields, states, BRST, stress ledgers δA_μ^a, δφ^I, ghost/auxiliary fields

A component with no layer assignment, or with two, is a definition failure and blocks the chapter at gate 1.

3.3 The gate-card — the atomic unit every candidate carries

Every candidate mode that appears anywhere in the document carries a machine-checkable gate-card in this exact schema:

{ "model_id": "MID-...", "challenge_id": "HC-..",
  "object_definition": { "equations": [], "coordinates": "",
    "active_fields": [], "layer_assignments": {} },
  "gates": { "definition": "PASS|FAIL", "negative_controls": "PASS|FAIL",
    "invariant_check": "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT", "source_check": "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT",
    "gauge_check": "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT", "energy_check": "PASS|AUDIT",
    "causality_check": "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT", "uv_boundary": "PASS|UV_DELEGATED|FAIL" },
  "first_failure": "", "strongest_allowed_claim": "",
  "forbidden_claims": [], "next_closure_step": "" }

The card is validated before a candidate is allowed to appear in prose. The validator's fail-closed core:

def validate_gate_card(card):
    required = ["model_id", "challenge_id", "gates",
                "first_failure", "strongest_allowed_claim"]
    for key in required:
        assert key in card, f"missing {key}"
    g = card["gates"]
    # fail-closed rule 1: no source ⇒ no propulsion language
    if g.get("source_check") in ["FAIL", None]:
        assert "propulsion" not in card["strongest_allowed_claim"].lower()
    # fail-closed rule 2: UV-delegated ⇒ cannot claim global stability solved
    if g.get("uv_boundary") == "UV_DELEGATED":
        forbidden = " ".join(card.get("forbidden_claims", [])).lower()
        assert "global stability solved" not in forbidden
    # fail-closed rule 3: energy gate is never a clean PASS
    assert g.get("energy_check") in ["PASS", "AUDIT"]   # "PASS" means audit-visible-only
    return True

Read a gate-card top-to-bottom: identity → object definition (with layer assignments) → the eight gates → the first failure → the strongest claim the gates license → the forbidden claims for this candidate → the next concrete step toward closure.

4. One-page summary of the fail-closed status discipline

This is the single most important page in the document. If a reader internalizes only one page, it should be this one.

4.1 The six non-negotiable rules

  1. Default status of any unproven mode is TOY_MODEL or AUDIT, never PASS. The absolute ceiling anywhere in the document is PASS_TOY — a status-labeled simulation result on a defined toy. No worked example reaches operational, physical, or hardware claim.
  2. Every section and every chapter names a FIRST FAILURE. A section with no named first failure is invalid and is rejected by the red-team pass.
  3. On any failed, missing, or uncertain computation, DOWNGRADE the claim. Never invent a missing source, theorem, or apparatus to force a pass.
  4. No self-promotion. An automated agent may never move a candidate up the ladder on its own authority; promotion past PASS_TOY requires owner/attorney escalation.
  5. Strongest allowed physical language is conditional (the §2.3 rule).
  6. "Most modes should fail. That is good." Credibility comes from systematic, machine-checked failure — not from a survivor.

4.2 The closure ladder and the hard ceiling

0 UNDEFINED         (prose only)
1 TOY_DEFINED       (equations + schema)            ← this leaf sits here
2 TOY_TESTED        (negative controls + toy numerics)
3 EFT_CANDIDATE     (source + energy + gauge + cutoffs declared)
4 PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY (hostile-review packet complete)
5 PHYSICAL_CLAIM    ← "Not targeted here / out of scope."
--------------------------------------------------------------
PASS_TOY = the absolute ceiling for any worked example in this document.

Promotion rules (evidence → max attainable status):

Current evidence Max status

equations only TOY_DEFINED
equations + negative controls TOY_TESTED
source + energy + gauge + cutoffs EFT_CANDIDATE
unresolved compactification / UV dependency UV_DELEGATED

4.3 The downgrade tree (status tokens)

Each failure mode has a named terminal token, so failure is legible, not vague:

Trigger Status token

required source absent/unaccounted FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC

4.4 Fail-closed enforcement invariants (always on)

  • If source_check ∈ {FAIL, None} ⇒ the token propulsion is forbidden in strongest_allowed_claim.
  • If uv_boundary == UV_DELEGATED ⇒ "global stability solved" may not appear as a closed claim.
  • energy_check is never a clean PASS — its best value is "pass / audit-visible." We label this PASS* in tables to remind the reader.
  • A candidate appears in prose only after its gate-card validates (§3.3 validator).
  • A Mars/mission effect appears only as a gate-masked, watermarked overlay.

4.5 A worked status example (front-matter illustration only)

Consider a deliberately trivial toy: a Gaussian forward-lobe metric perturbation

δg_xx(x) = −A · exp( −(x − x_v(t))² / (2σ²) ),   A, σ > 0,   x_v(t) = vehicle-comoving center.

A naive line integral of D[Ξ] along the x-axis through the lobe yields, to first order in A,

ΔD ≈ ∫ ( sqrt(1 + δg_xx) − 1 ) dx ≈ −(A/2) · sqrt(2π) σ = −(A σ /2)·2.5066…

For A = 0.01, σ = 100 m: ΔD ≈ −0.01 × 100 × 1.2533 ≈ −1.25 m over the lobe — a forward-distance reduction of about 1.25 m. This number means almost nothing, and the discipline says so out loud:

  • invariant_check: until recomputed in a second chart and a tetrad, this is at best AUDIT; a pure coordinate scaling x → x' = (1+δg_xx/2)x reproduces the same ΔD, so the front-matter status is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY pending HC-01.
  • source_check: we have written δg_xx but declared no source. G_xx[g+δg] ≠ 0 demands a T_xx^req we have not produced ⇒ FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.
  • energy_check: the sign of the implied T_xx^req is not even examined here ⇒ AUDIT, best case PASS*.
  • Resulting gate-card verdict: first_failure = "source_check (HC-02): no declared stress-energy ledger"; strongest_allowed_claim = "a toy coordinate expression yielding a chart-dependent ΔD, status FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY pending HC-01, FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC pending HC-02"; forbidden_claims = ["propulsion", "distance-shortening drive", "FTL"].

The point of showing the −1.25 m number and then refusing to let it mean anything is the entire ethos: the platform produces effects on demand and then spends its real effort proving why they do not yet count.

4.6 The mandatory chapter footer (every leaf ends with this block)

Every leaf in the document, including this one, ends with the five-line footer: Closure status · First failure · What remains to close · Patent extraction · Reviewer attack. A leaf without this footer is rejected.

First failure of §4 (status discipline): the discipline is procedural, not physical — its earliest failure is that a correctly-followed status discipline can still describe a vehicle that never exists. The machinery in §4.5 cheerfully produces a −1.25 m toy number and then downgrades it on the record; nothing in the status ladder makes any candidate pass HC-02 (source) or HC-03 (energy). Put plainly: the fail-closed apparatus guarantees honesty, not a drive. That asymmetry — rigorous at forbidding overclaim, silent on whether any profile is physically sourceable — is the section's first failure, and it is the same FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC boundary that gates the whole document.

A2 — Executive Technical Memo for a Strategic Acquirer (the Ask & the Milestone)

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED (memo defines the decision object and one quantitative promotion gate; no candidate promoted) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

0. How to read this memo (and what it is not)

This is the one document a strategic-acquirer diligence team is meant to read first. It is deliberately short relative to the ~690-page corpus behind it, and it is written to be falsifiable on its own terms: every claim it makes is either (a) a claim about a software platform that exists and runs, or (b) a conditional claim about candidate metric-interface profiles that is explicitly gated and explicitly allowed to fail. There is exactly one number in this memo that should change a diligence decision, and §4 states it up front and in full.

Before anything else, the boundary. This memo is not a pitch for a working warp drive; it does not prove faster-than-light travel; it does not claim the energy problem is solved, that global stability is solved, or that any UV completion has been adopted; and it contains no hardware-construction, high-energy-source, or beam content of any kind. Those are not modesty disclaimers — they are the load-bearing structure of the asset. The thing being offered is a fail-closed screening and validation platform plus the provisional IP around it, and the entire value proposition is that the platform is built to find and publish the place each candidate breaks, not to manufacture a survivor. If you came looking for whether the drive works, the honest answer is no. What this document offers instead is a rigorous, IP-protected way to filter exotic-propulsion claims and capture the option if one ever survives — yes, conditionally, and §4 states the single condition.

0.1 UNVERIFIED THEORY — you do not have to believe the unified theory

We do not ask you to believe the unified theory. The platform is a general GR/EFT screening tool that works against standard inputs; the theory is one optional configuration, not a dependency.

Plainly, so the diligence team can stop worrying about it up front: nothing in this offer depends on the underlying Fable / TOE_FINAL unified theory being correct. The framework treats corpus-derived constraints as configuration data — inputs you can swap out, switch off, or ignore — not as a physical claim you are being asked to accept. The asset is the gate machinery, which is built against textbook general relativity and effective field theory and runs identically whether or not the unified theory ever holds up.

You do not have to take this on faith — the executed reference repository demonstrates it. The exact same gates run on the standard, published, peer-reviewed warp metrics that have nothing to do with the corpus — Alcubierre, Natário, and Van Den Broeck — and reproduce the same fail-closed behavior: minimum null-energy-condition values NEC_min = −0.27 (Alcubierre), −0.27 (Natário), −0.16 (Van Den Broeck), with FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC returned for all three. The tool screens textbook GR metrics the same way it screens corpus-conditioned candidates. And the patent claims do not require the theory either: the disclosed systems and methods operate on any metric ansatz and are novel and useful regardless of whether the unified theory is right, wrong, or never adjudicated. If the theory is false, the screening platform, its reference results on standard metrics, and the IP are all entirely unaffected. The theory is one optional configuration line — not a load-bearing premise of anything you are being asked to fund.

A note on status language, because it governs every page after this one. The platform classifies each candidate excitation profile on a six-level closure ladder: 0 UNDEFINED (prose only) → 1 TOY_DEFINED (equations + schema) → 2 TOY_TESTED (negative controls + toy numerics) → 3 EFT_CANDIDATE (source + energy + gauge + cutoffs declared) → 4 PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY (hostile-review packet complete) → 5 PHYSICAL_CLAIM. Level 5 is explicitly out of scope and not targeted anywhere in this document. The strongest status any worked example reaches in the entire corpus is a status-labeled simulation result; the absolute ceiling is PASS_TOY. When this memo says a candidate "passes" a gate, it always means passed a declared simulation gate at a labeled status — never "is physically real."

First failure (this section): a reader skims the memo, extracts "metric-interface drive," and drops the conditional — i.e., reads option value as a propulsion claim. The mitigation is structural: the ask in §3 is an option, not a purchase; the milestone in §4 is a promotion gate, not a result; and every forward-looking sentence in this memo is bound to a gate token that can read FAIL.

0.2 The one trust event — why this platform is worth your diligence time

Before the pitch, the single result that should earn your attention — by being refused, not headlined. The platform's worked exemplar, MID-METRIC-001, produces a real, local, coordinate-invariant forward-distance deficit (~0.22%): a genuine geometric effect that survives the invariant-distance gate, recomputes the same way across charts and tetrads, and is corroborated by curvature scalars. A weaker document — a sales deck — would put that number on the cover and call it a drive. This one does the opposite. The platform computes the stress-energy the deficit would require, finds no declared source supplies it (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC at the source gate, HC-02), audits the energy condition (which is never a clean pass), and reads off a negative effective energy density at the lobe center (ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶, with NEC/WEC/DEC all violated) — i.e., the deficit is 100% sourced by exotic energy no one has. So the platform kills its own most tempting candidate, on real numbers, rather than promote it. That refusal — the machine declining to convert a seductive effect into a propulsion claim — is the asset. This is why the platform is worth reviewing: a screening tool that would not kill its own best result could not be trusted to kill anyone else's.

1. The one-line pitch (and the three-line version)

One line: We are offering a provisional-protected, fail-closed simulation and validation platform that screens, classifies, and visualizes candidate metric-interface excitation profiles — and tells you, with machine-checked gates, exactly where each one fails.

Three lines, for the diligence lead: 1. Mars transfer time dominates mission architecture, and exotic-propulsion hypotheses keep arriving with no rigorous, neutral validator to kill the bad ones cheaply. 2. This is that validator — a tensor/source/energy/gauge/causality/UV gate stack that defaults every unproven mode to TOY_MODEL and downgrades on any failure — wrapped in a provisional that claims the screening/classification/control architecture, not a working device. 3. The ask is to option the provisional and fund a 90-day hostile validation sprint; the sprint either kills everything (you keep a rigorous screening tool and the IP) or surfaces a single candidate that crosses one declared quantitative milestone (you control the IP window before anyone else).

You do not have to believe the unified theory. The framework does not depend on the correctness of the underlying Fable / TOE_FINAL theory: it is a general GR/EFT screening tool that works against standard inputs, the theory is one optional configuration rather than a dependency, and the patent claims do not require it. The executed reference repo proves this by reproducing the same gates on the published Alcubierre, Natário, and Van Den Broeck warp metrics (NEC_min = −0.27 / −0.27 / −0.16), all returning FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.

What the one-liner deliberately does not say is as important as what it says. It does not say "drive." It does not say "propulsion." It does not say a transfer-time number. It says proper-distance functional — a local, coordinate-invariant geometric quantity the platform can actually compute and audit — and it leaves the leap from "local proper-distance effect in a gated simulation" to "mission Δt" explicitly unmade. That leap is the single most common way exotic-propulsion pitches over-claim, and G3 in the main corpus proves a theorem that the platform refuses to make it for you: a positive local shortening score does not integrate to a global travel-time reduction. The pitch is honest precisely because the strongest verb in it is "screen."

First failure (this section): the pitch is heard as "we built a drive simulator that says the drive works." It does not, and cannot, say that — the platform has no status above PASS_TOY and the local→global integration is blocked by theorem (see §4 and G3). If a listener cannot repeat the pitch back without the word screen or classify, the pitch has failed and must be re-stated.

2. Who the asymmetric payoff fits, and why — the option-value thesis

The argument is an asymmetric-payoff argument, not a physics argument. Hold the physics in suspense for one paragraph and look only at the decision tree.

There exists a steady stream of exotic-propulsion and "spacetime-engineering" proposals (Alcubierre-class warp metrics, Natário variants, Van Den Broeck volume tricks, assorted field-drive and "quantum-vacuum thruster" claims). Each one costs real diligence time to evaluate, and almost all of them fail for one of a small number of structurally identical reasons: the metric is a coordinate artifact; the required stress-energy is never sourced; the energy condition is violated in a hidden way; the effect is pure gauge; or the whole construction is parasitic on an un-adopted UV assumption. Today, a frontier-aerospace prime evaluates each of these ad hoc. The platform turns that ad-hoc evaluation into a repeatable, machine-checked pipeline with a fixed gate order and a published first-failure for every candidate. Even with zero surviving candidates, that is a tool with standalone value: a neutral, hostile, fast filter that converts "interesting-sounding propulsion email" into "fails at the source-ledger gate, here is the mismatch norm, next." The protectable asset is precisely that discriminator — the screening method and the IP around it — not any survivor, which is why it holds value for any rigorous frontier-R&D acquirer independent of whether a drive is ever built.

Now add the option. The provisional claims the pipeline, not the device. So the four outcomes of a validation sprint are:

Sprint outcome What the acquirer holds afterward Cost exposure
Every mode fails (expected) A rigorous, reusable exotic-propulsion screening tool + the IP on the architecture Sprint cost only
One mode survives more gates than expected, terminal status still AUDIT The same tool plus a single, fully-documented "deepest-surviving" candidate and a named next computation Sprint cost only
One mode reaches the §4 milestone (EFT_CANDIDATE + matched source + named UV assumption) A controlled IP window on a candidate worth real physics investment, before competitors Option + sprint cost
Platform itself fails diligence (engine wrong, gates leaky) Nothing — but you found out in 90 days for sprint cost Sprint cost only

The thesis is that the downside is bounded by one sprint's cost and the upside is a controlled IP window on the only class of result that would justify deeper investment. That asymmetric, downside-protected shape is the entire reason this is addressed to an organization that already owns the mission for which the upside matters — a Mars-transport-scale program can option the validated screening process cheaply (an option fee plus a 90-day hostile validation sprint) rather than buy a nonexistent engine. A pure research lab cannot capture the IP window; a pure investor cannot run the hostile validation. A program whose valuation already rests on long-duration Mars-transport optionality can do both, which is why a cheap, disciplined, fail-closed frontier-propulsion validation capability is worth more to a buyer who can exercise both halves of the option than to one who can exercise neither.

The structure is a real option, and it is worth being explicit about why the asymmetry survives even under a pessimistic prior. Let C_sprint be the all-in sprint cost, C_opt the option premium, p the probability the §4 milestone is hit, V_tool the standalone value of a validated, IP-protected screening tool (realized in three of four outcomes), and V_window the value of controlling the IP window on a milestone-hitting candidate. The decision to take the option is positive-expected-value whenever

E[option] = V_tool + p · V_window − (C_opt + C_sprint) > 0

The point is not the precise numbers — it is the shape. V_tool is collected in the expected (miss) case, so the option is not a lottery ticket whose entire value sits in the tail; the floor is "a working filter." V_window is multiplied by a deliberately small p (the platform is built to make p small and honest), but V_window for an organization whose mission is gated by transfer time is large. And C_opt + C_sprint is bounded and known up front. So the inequality holds for plausible inputs even when p → 0, provided V_tool > C_opt + C_sprint — which is the real diligence question and the one Phase 1 of the sprint exists to answer. This is why the milestone is calibrated to "worth a physicist's deep dive" rather than "physically real": it sets the threshold for the p · V_window term at the lowest point that still justifies converting, without inflating p by lowering the bar.

Reviewer's likely objection, stated honestly: "Most modes failing isn't a feature, it's the platform admitting it has nothing." The honest response: the platform's credibility comes from systematic, machine-checked failure — a screening tool that never failed a candidate would be worthless. The value is not "a survivor exists"; the value is "you now have a fast, neutral, IP-protected way to kill the 99% cheaply and recognize the 1% precisely." The §4 milestone exists exactly so that "recognize the 1%" is a number, not a vibe.

First failure (this section): the option-value thesis collapses into "fund our research" if the platform cannot demonstrate it kills candidates on real numbers. Mitigation: the sprint's first two weeks rebuild the tensor engine against known metrics and re-run the negative controls before any candidate is touched (see §5), so "the filter actually filters" is established before any upside is discussed.

3. The ask — option, then sprint (not "buy the patent")

The recommended ask is explicitly not "buy my warp-drive patent." That framing is wrong on the merits (there is no warp drive) and wrong tactically (it invites the diligence team to evaluate a device that does not exist and reject the whole thing). The ask matches the protagonist: you are not buying an engine, you are buying the machine that refuses to lie and an option on whatever it cannot kill. The correct ask has two parts, in order:

Part 1 — Option the provisional. Take a time-boxed, priced option on the provisional patent application covering the screening/classification/control architecture (the twelve invention families: metric target functionals, vehicle-comoving lobe definitions, invariant-distance classifiers, source-reconstruction engines, energy-condition/exoticity engines, gauge/BRST classifiers, UV-dependency classifiers, gate-card validators, mission validity overlays, candidate-mode libraries, optimization/control representations, and report/figure exporters). The option secures the IP window during the sprint so that a surviving candidate, if one appears, cannot be filed around by a third party while the acquirer is still deciding.

Part 2 — Fund a hostile technical validation sprint. Resource a 90-day sprint whose explicit, written goal is to break the platform and break every candidate, not to confirm them. The sprint is run adversarially: the brief to the team is "find the first failure of each mode and the first failure of the tool itself." The sprint's deliverable is a decision, not a demo (see §5–§6).

The structure matters because it inverts the usual incentive. A normal vendor wants the demo to succeed; here, the contractual deliverable is a first-failure ledger and a single go/no-go number. The vendor is paid to help you fail their own candidates. If the team resists hostile testing, that is itself a diligence signal and the option should not convert.

What an option is worth here. The option price is bounded above by "what it would cost a competitor to file around the architecture during 90 days" and below by "the cost of the sprint." It is cheap by construction because the asset is mostly method IP plus running software, and the option converts to acquisition only on the §4 milestone. The diligence team should treat the option as buying information and exclusivity for 90 days, priced like a short-dated call, not like a technology purchase.

Investor-safe language for the term sheet. Use: simulation-gated, first-failure, metric-interface, proper-distance functional, source ledger, validity overlay, option value, gate-supervised control, status-labeled result, candidate mode, EFT candidate. Do not use, and strike from any draft that comes back: working warp drive, FTL / faster-than-light, energy solved, operational propulsion, Mars in days, no propellant needed, UV completion adopted, global stability solved. The don't-say list is not legal cover; it is the difference between an honest asset and an unfileable, indefensible one. A provisional that implies a working drive is both harder to defend under §101 and easier to invalidate on enablement — see I2 in the corpus.

First failure (this section): the ask is restructured by a well-meaning corporate-dev counterparty into "acquire the patent now," which forces a valuation of a device that does not exist and triggers the forbidden-promotion guard. Mitigation: the option-then-milestone structure is a contractual term, not a preference — conversion to acquisition is gated on §4 and nothing else.

4. The milestone — the single quantitative "what would change our mind"

This is the section the rest of the memo exists to support, and it is the fix for the failure mode that kills process-only pitches: a validation plan that never states what result would convert the option into an investment. "Run a sprint and see" is not a milestone. Here is the milestone, stated as a single, checkable predicate.

4.1 The milestone, in one sentence

At least one candidate mode reaches closure status EFT_CANDIDATE (ladder level 3) — meaning its source, energy, gauge, and cutoff gates are all declared and audit-visible — with a matched source ledger whose effective-source mismatch satisfies χ_source < 1, under a named, separately-published UV/compactification assumption, while every coordinate-invariance and causality gate reads PASS and no gate reads FAIL.

If that predicate is TRUE at the end of the sprint for one or more modes, the option converts and the candidate is worth real physics investment. If it is FALSE for every mode — the expected outcome — the option does not convert, the acquirer keeps the screening tool and the IP, and the sprint has still delivered full value as a filter. There is no third "promising, let's extend indefinitely" outcome; the predicate is binary by design, because the failure mode of these programs is exactly the indefinite extension.

4.2 What each clause means, operationally

The milestone is a conjunction of gate conditions evaluated by the platform's gate-card validator. Decompose it:

(a) EFT_CANDIDATE (ladder level 3). The candidate has, as machine-checked artifacts: an effective stress-energy T_μν^eff reconstructed from the metric via the Einstein tensor, a declared energy-condition audit, a declared gauge/BRST classification, and declared EFT cutoffs. "Declared and audit-visible" — not "passed and hidden." Energy is never a clean pass; its gate token is PASS|AUDIT and the honest reading is "the exoticity is visible and bounded," not "no exotic source is needed."

(b) Matched source ledger, χ_source < 1. This is the load-bearing number. The platform reconstructs the source the candidate metric requires and compares it to a source the corpus can actually license. Define the dimensionless source-mismatch

χ_source = || T_μν^required − T_μν^licensed ||_W / || T_μν^required ||_W

over the lobe support, in an invariant norm ||·||_W weighted by the validity-weight W (the same W that G3 proves does not integrate to a global travel-time cut). The norm is the W-weighted lobe integral of the squared tetrad-frame component residual,

|| X ||_W² = ∫_lobe W(x) · ( η^{ac} η^{bd} X_{ab} X_{cd} ) √(-g) d⁴x

evaluated in the comoving orthonormal frame so the comparison is coordinate-invariant and not a chart artifact. χ_source < 1 means the required source is more than half-accounted-for by a licensed source — the candidate is no longer a bare unsourced metric.

A worked illustration of the arithmetic (illustrative numbers, status TOY_MODEL, marked reference computation — not a result, and not a substantiated value): suppose for a candidate the platform reconstructs a required source whose dominant frame-energy-density component over the lobe has W-weighted norm ||T^required||_W = 1.00 (in the platform's nondimensionalized units, normalized to 1 by construction of the denominator), and the licensed source — the most the corpus can actually account for from shared/visible stress-energy without invoking an un-adopted axiom — reproduces a residual ||T^required − T^licensed||_W = 0.62. Then χ_source = 0.62 < 1: the source clause passes. Decompose the residual budget and the honesty becomes visible. Note this is a partition of the squared-norm budget, not a linear split of the norm itself — the ||·||_W residual is built from a W-weighted integral of squared frame-component residuals (the ||X||_W² form above), so contributions combine in quadrature, not by simple addition; the figures below are an illustrative apportionment of that integrated budget, not an algebraic identity 0.41 + 0.21 = 0.62. Suppose the UV-dependency classifier attributes a UV-conditional share to terms that vanish only if B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is assumed (illustratively, a residual-budget component of ≈0.41 in the same units) and a genuinely-unlicensed exotic share to the rest (illustratively ≈0.21). The clause-(c) requirement then forces the UV-conditional share into the open as a named, published UV_DELEGATED line — it does not get to silently shrink χ_source. The unlicensed share is exactly what the energy-condition audit (clause a) must show as visible and bounded exoticity, not as zero. So a milestone-hitting card might read χ_source = 0.62, uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED (B-UQFC-14-UV-1, published), energy_check = AUDIT (exoticity component ≈0.21, bounded) — a number a physicist can argue with, not a green light. (Every figure in this paragraph is illustrative and unsubstantiated; the platform emits the real numbers only after the Phase-3 run, expected terminal status AUDIT.)

We deliberately set the bar at < 1, not ≪ 1: this is a promotion-to-investment gate, not a physical-realizability gate. A mode at χ_source = 0.62 is not "real"; it is "worth a physicist's quarter," which is exactly what converting an option means. Demanding χ_source ≪ 1 would push the bar toward physical realizability — level 5, out of scope — and would also create an incentive to game the licensed-source definition to drive the number down. The < 1 threshold plus the frozen licensed-source set plus the independent UV decomposition is the calibration that resists both errors.

(c) Named, separately-published UV assumption. If the candidate's source or stability leans on the compactification (K6 = SU(3)/T², S², S¹_Y, F+) or any global-stability axiom, that dependency must be (i) detected by the UV-dependency classifier, (ii) named — the corpus token is B-UQFC-14-UV-1, which remains UNADOPTED — and (iii) published separately so the candidate's status reads UV_DELEGATED with the assumption legible, never folded silently into a "pass." A milestone hit with a hidden UV assumption is not a hit; it is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION.

(d) Invariants PASS, causality PASS, no FAIL anywhere. The candidate must survive the coordinate-invariance gate (it is not a coordinate artifact — checked on curvature invariants, tetrad observables, and geodesic diagnostics) and the causality gate (timelike worldline, no trapped-surface/CTC proxy tripped). Causality gates every mission-relevant claim; a causality FAIL voids the milestone regardless of χ_source.

4.3 The milestone as a gate card

The sprint reports the milestone in exactly this machine-checkable form, one card per candidate:

{ "model_id": "MID-<family>-<nnn>", "challenge_id": "HC-MILESTONE",
  "object_definition": { "equations": ["g_munu ansatz", "T_eff = G_munu/8piG"],
    "coordinates": "comoving tetrad", "active_fields": [], "layer_assignments": {} },
  "gates": {
    "definition": "PASS",            "negative_controls": "PASS",
    "invariant_check": "PASS",       "source_check": "PASS",
    "gauge_check": "PASS",           "energy_check": "AUDIT",
    "causality_check": "PASS",       "uv_boundary": "UV_DELEGATED" },
  "metrics": { "chi_source": 0.0, "chi_EFT": 0.0 },
  "first_failure": "<named>",
  "strongest_allowed_claim": "EFT candidate under named UV delegation; not physical",
  "forbidden_claims": ["propulsion", "FTL", "energy solved"],
  "next_closure_step": "PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY packet" }

Conversion predicate (pseudocode the validator runs):

function milestone_hit(card):
    if card.gates.definition        != "PASS": return FALSE
    if card.gates.negative_controls != "PASS": return FALSE
    if card.gates.invariant_check   != "PASS": return FALSE   # not a coordinate artifact
    if card.gates.causality_check   != "PASS": return FALSE   # gates everything
    if card.gates.source_check      != "PASS": return FALSE   # ledger matched
    if card.metrics.chi_source      >= 1.0:    return FALSE   # the load-bearing number
    if card.gates.gauge_check       != "PASS": return FALSE   # not pure gauge
    if "FAIL" in values(card.gates):           return FALSE   # any fail voids
    if card.gates.uv_boundary == "UV_DELEGATED" and not named_and_published(card):
        return FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION                            # hidden UV => void
    # energy_check is allowed to be AUDIT, never required to be PASS
    return TRUE   # option converts; candidate worth real physics investment

Note three deliberate asymmetries. energy_check is never required to be PASS — requiring a clean energy pass would make the milestone unreachable for the right reason but also unreachable for the wrong reason (it would let the team hide exoticity to claim a pass). Instead the exoticity must be visible and bounded (AUDIT), and the source-mismatch number carries the real weight. Second, uv_boundary == UV_DELEGATED is allowed — a candidate may lean on a named, published UV assumption and still convert the option — but a hidden delegation is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and voids the hit. Third, any single FAIL voids the conjunction; the gates are AND-ed, never averaged.

4.4 Why this number and not an easier one

Three weaker milestones were considered and rejected, and naming them is part of the diligence honesty:

Candidate milestone Why rejected
"A candidate reaches TOY_TESTED (level 2)" Too cheap — passes negative controls and toy numerics but says nothing about a real source. Most straw-man modes pass it. Converts nothing.
"A local shortening score S_L > 0" Coordinate-bait. S_L > 0 in some chart is trivially arrangeable; G3 proves it does not integrate to a travel-time cut. A positive S_L alone is a FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM trap, not a milestone.
"χ_source < 1 without the UV clause" Smuggles the hard part. Almost any metric can be "sourced" if you are allowed to draw on an un-adopted global-stability axiom silently. The named-and-published UV clause is what makes the number honest.

The chosen milestone is the weakest condition that simultaneously (i) rules out coordinate artifacts, (ii) requires a matched source on a real number, (iii) forces any UV dependency into the open, and (iv) refuses to let energy-exoticity hide. It is calibrated to "worth real physics investment," which is the only decision the option needs to support. It is not calibrated to "physically real" — that is level 5, out of scope, and no milestone in this document targets it.

4.5 What the milestone explicitly does not claim if hit

If a candidate hits the milestone, the strongest sentence anyone is permitted to write is: "Mode MID-… is retained as an EFT candidate under the named UV delegation B-UQFC-14-UV-1 (UNADOPTED), with source mismatch χ_source = 0.6 (AUDIT), pending a PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY packet." It does not mean the drive works, that propulsion is demonstrated, that energy is solved, that any travel-time benefit follows, or that the UV assumption is true. It means one thing: the option converts and a physicist's deep dive is now justified. The local→global theorem (G3) still blocks any mission-Δt statement, and the UV axiom stays UNADOPTED. A hit changes the investment decision, not the physics status.

First failure (this section): the milestone is gamed by tuning a candidate to report χ_source < 1 while quietly relaxing the licensed-source definition or hiding a UV delegation — i.e., moving the goalposts inside the source ledger. Mitigation: the licensed-source set and the UV assumption are frozen and published before any candidate is scored (sprint Week 1–2), the validity-weight W is fixed, and the UV-dependency classifier runs independently of the source engine, so a hidden delegation trips FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION regardless of χ_source.

5. The 90-day hostile validation sprint

The sprint is six two-week phases. Its design principle: establish that the filter filters before discussing any upside, then attack candidates, then audit the tool itself, then decide. Nothing in the sprint is allowed to promote a candidate on the team's own authority — promotion requires owner/attorney escalation, by contract.

Phase Weeks Goal Exit artifact / gate
1 1–2 Rebuild the tensor engine; re-run the five known-metric tests (Minkowski, Schwarzschild, FRW, Alcubierre, Natário) Engine validated against closed-form invariants; negative controls green
2 3–4 Run the candidate-mode library (families 1–5, ~50 modes) through definition + invariant gates Per-mode gate cards; coordinate-only modes downgraded to FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY
3 5–6 Source-ledger reconstruction + energy-condition / exoticity audit χ_source per surviving mode; FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC / FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY for the rest
4 7–8 Gauge / BRST status audit + UV-dependency classification FAIL_PURE_GAUGE, AUDIT_QUANTUM, UV_DELEGATED tokens assigned and named
5 9–10 Mars validity overlay (gated, watermarked) + patent claim-support review Overlays with status watermark; G3 local→global theorem applied; no mission-Δt claim
6 11–12 Decision: abandon / continue / option-convert / acquire — evaluate §4 predicate One go/no-go per mode; signed first-failure ledger

Two phases deserve emphasis. Phase 1 is non-negotiable and comes first because it answers the diligence team's real first question — "does the engine even compute curvature correctly?" — before any candidate is in play. The five known-metric tests are closed-form-checkable, so "the engine works" is a number, not an assertion:

Metric Invariant the engine must reproduce Closed-form target
Minkowski All curvature components R_{μνρσ} = 0 exactly (machine-zero to tolerance)
Schwarzschild Kretschmann scalar K = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} = 48 G² M² / r⁶; R_{μν} = 0 (vacuum)
FRW (flat) Ricci scalar R = 6( ä/a + (ȧ/a)² ); G^0_0 = −3(ȧ/a)² (Friedmann constraint)
Alcubierre Energy density (Eulerian) T^{00} = −(1/8πG)·(v_s²/4)·(ρ²/r_s²)·(f'(r_s))² < 0 (NEC-violating, expected)
Natário Expansion θ of comoving congruence θ = 0 (zero-expansion construction) distinguishes it from Alcubierre

If the rebuilt engine cannot reproduce the Schwarzschild Kretschmann scalar to declared tolerance, or returns nonzero Ricci for a vacuum metric, the sprint stops and the platform itself has failed diligence — a real, allowed outcome. The Alcubierre and Natário rows do double duty: they are negative controls. The engine is expected to find the Alcubierre energy density negative and the Natário expansion zero; if it does not, the engine — not the candidate — is wrong. Only after all five pass does any candidate enter the pipeline.

Phase 5 is where over-claim risk peaks: the Mars overlay is the only visual, and it ships only with a status watermark and a gate-status overlay, never as a bare trajectory. An overlay without the watermark is a FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM and is rejected by the platform's own forbidden-promotion scanner. Critically, Phase 5 applies the G3 theorem in software: even a candidate with a strictly positive local shortening score S_L > 0 on the lobe is rendered with the explicit annotation that ∫ S_L along the trajectory does not equal a travel-time reduction — the overlay shows a local geometric quantity under a validity weight, watermarked, never a mission-Δt.

The sprint's contractual deliverable is the §6 decision plus the cross-mode first-failure ledger — one row per candidate naming the earliest gate it fails. A sprint that produced a beautiful demo and no ledger would be a failed sprint.

First failure (this section): the sprint slips into a confirmation exercise — the team tunes candidates to look good in Phase 5 overlays rather than attacking them in Phases 2–4. Mitigation: the deliverable is the first-failure ledger and the §4 binary predicate, the overlay is watermarked-or-rejected, and promotion authority is removed from the team entirely.

6. The decision and the say-this / don't-say discipline

At Week 12 the diligence team faces exactly four decisions, and the §4 predicate selects among them:

if any candidate satisfies milestone_hit():     -> OPTION CONVERTS (-> acquire/file window)
elif engine failed Phase-1 validation:          -> ABANDON (platform itself failed)
elif deepest survivor terminal status == AUDIT: -> CONTINUE as screening tool; option lapses
else (all modes FAIL early):                     -> KEEP TOOL + IP; option lapses

Three of the four outcomes do not convert the option, and all three are good outcomes for the acquirer: in two of them you keep a working, IP-protected screening tool for the price of the sprint, and in the fourth you learned in 90 days that the engine was wrong rather than after a multi-year program. The only outcome that converts the option is the one that is supposed to be rare.

The discipline, restated as a checklist the diligence lead can hold the team to. Every status report, term-sheet draft, and internal summary must:

  • state the current closure-ladder status of each mode (default TOY_MODEL/AUDIT, ceiling PASS_TOY);
  • name a first failure for each mode and for the platform itself;
  • name the next closure computation (what would move the status up);
  • name the patent fallback (what is owned even if every mode fails — the architecture);
  • carry no sentence from the don't-say list.

Say this: simulation-gated metric-interface profile · proper-distance functional · source-ledger reconstruction · energy-condition visibility · gate-supervised control · first-failure discipline · patentable screening/control architecture · 90-day validation sprint · option value · status-labeled result.

Don't say: "we have a working warp drive" · "energy is solved" · "we can build the source" · "a super-heavy-lift vehicle can install it" · "Mars in days" · "FTL / proves faster-than-light" · "UV completion is adopted" · "global stability solved" · "negative energy available" · "operational propulsion" · "no propellant needed."

This discipline is not cosmetic. Each don't-say phrase, if it appears unqualified, simultaneously (i) over-claims physics the corpus cannot support, (ii) weakens the patent's §101 and enablement posture, and (iii) trips the platform's own forbidden-promotion scanner, which rejects the document. The say-this list is the vocabulary of an honest, defensible, fileable asset; the don't-say list is the vocabulary of an indefensible one.

First failure (this section): under acquisition pressure, the decision is reported as "promising — let's keep going" when the §4 predicate is FALSE, manufacturing a phantom fifth outcome that converts the option without earning it. Mitigation: the predicate is binary and machine-evaluated; "promising" is not a decision the validator emits, and option conversion is contractually bound to milestone_hit() == TRUE and nothing else.

7. Patent posture in one paragraph (full treatment in Part I)

The provisional claims the systems and methods for screening, classifying, and visualizing candidate metric-interface excitation profiles — the twelve invention families and three independent claim seeds (a computer-implemented method: receive trajectory → define forward lobe → receive candidate profile → compute proper-distance functional → evaluate invariance diagnostics → reconstruct effective source ledger → apply energy-condition diagnostics → apply gate-card rules → output status-labeled visualization; a system of the corresponding modules; and a non-transitory medium). It does not rely on proving propulsion, and it keeps any prospective physical embodiment broad and explicitly non-enabling. This is the fallback that makes the option-value thesis hold even when every mode fails: the asset is the pipeline, and the pipeline runs and is novel regardless of whether a single candidate ever survives. Claim breadth, category (software-first vs. aerospace-simulation), and §101 strategy are the attorney's call (see I1/I2); the milestone in §4 governs only whether the physics IP window is worth converting, not whether the architecture IP exists — it already does.

First failure (this section): the patent is drafted to imply a working drive to make it sound more valuable, which is exactly the framing that invites an abstract-idea §101 rejection and an enablement attack. Mitigation: software/simulation/control framing is primary, physical embodiments stay broad and non-enabling, and the don't-say list is enforced in the claim language itself.

A platform that converted the option easily would be the dishonest one.

Honest engineering caveats (from RESULTS.md §4)

  1. Kretschmann of the tanh-shape warp baselines is computed exactly but not globally simplified (sympy simplify is intractable on tanh-derivative trees) — it is lambdified and evaluated numerically pointwise. The five known metrics ARE fully simplified symbolically. A global Kretschmann simplify on the Gaussian lobe hung a process; resolved with an exact-but-no-global-simplify path (the one real performance bug found and fixed).
  2. The Natário model uses the on-axis screenable reduction of the divergence-free shift, which coincides structurally with Alcubierre at the sample points (hence identical NEC_min); documented as a modeling simplification, not an exact transcription. Van Den Broeck is genuinely distinct.
  3. WEC/SEC minima are seeded Monte-Carlo + axis samples (300 directions); the static-observer ρ and principal pressures are exact. Sampled minima deeper than the static rest-frame energy density ρ̂ (= WEC_min = −8.038×10⁻⁶) are correct GR — null/boosted directions probe deeper into the violating cone, the deepest sampled being the boosted null contraction NEC_min = −1.138×10⁻⁴ (a boosted-deepest sampled value at the β_max=0.999 cap, not a boost-invariant floor; the rest-frame null minimum is ρ̂ = −8.038×10⁻⁶, and boosting is what reaches −1.138×10⁻⁴) — not a bug.
  4. No python -m midrive CLI was built (out of scope vs the named deliverables); run_gates.py is the sanctioned screening path. Van Den Broeck symbolic build is slow (~190 s); MID-METRIC-001 ~20 s.

CF1.0 Why a commercial chapter sits beside an 830-page physics document, and what it refuses to claim

Parts A–L do one thing: they take a candidate metric-interface excitation profile Ξ_drive(t,x) = {δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge data}, run it down the ten hard-challenge gates HC-01…HC-10, and emit a status-labeled gate-card naming the earliest gate at which the candidate fails. The terminal result of that entire apparatus — stated plainly in the worked exemplar G1 (MID-METRIC-001, terminal 2 TOY_TESTED / AUDIT, token TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC) — is that the deepest-surviving candidate carries a real, coordinate-invariant forward proper-distance deficit that is nonetheless 100% unsourced and sourced only by an exotic negative effective energy density ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ (geometrized) that no declared field supplies. "Most modes fail" is the honest state of the physics, not a defect — and the binding gap is S2 source/energy (Part O §0.4).

This chapter answers a question Parts A–L deliberately do not: given an honest PASS_TOY ceiling and a BRL-2 standing, what is the commercial strategy — and what gates it? That is a strategy question, not a physics result, and it inherits the document's discipline exactly. CF1 promotes no candidate, reaches no rung past BRL-2, makes no propulsion / FTL / "energy solved" claim, and invents no revenue that does not exist.

The thesis, carried as the spine of Part P and repeated nowhere as a softer version:

Do NOT build a physical device first, and do NOT sell the method. The patented native-geometry method/system is the protected MOAT — it is never licensed to anyone and never sold as simulation or screening software. The revenue endgame is a single END PRODUCT, sold B2C (consumer) or to a government buyer, where the buyer purchases the end product itself. That end product requires the physics (S2 source/energy) to close — which is the currently-open barrier — so near-term the asset is the IP / option value of the moat, and end-product revenue is a gated future state.

Two binding consequences follow, and they distinguish this from a software business:

  • No competitor is ever a customer, and the simulation / screening software is never the product. The method, the gate machinery, the source-reconstruction and energy-condition engines, and the native-geometry compiler are the moat — protected by patent and trade secret, kept inside, and never sold, licensed, or rented to a competitor, a deep-tech fund, a patent attorney, a lab, or anyone else. Selling the screen would be selling the moat.
  • All revenue is B2C or government, and it buys the end product. The only thing ever sold is the finished end product to a consumer or a government buyer. There is no SaaS, no audit-as-a-service, no diligence-report business, no per-screen fee — those would be selling the method, which is forbidden.

The word "endgame" is load-bearing in its honesty: the end-product revenue is the future state, gated on S2 closing under the frozen-milestone discipline of Part L (§L0.5, M1_EFT_CANDIDATE). The moat is the thing that exists and is protectable at BRL-2 today; the end product is the thing the moat's option value is permitted to fund a test toward. The two are decoupled exactly as the BRL and IP ladders are decoupled in Part L: the value of an IP-protected native-geometry method is real today as option value, even though the end-product revenue does not yet exist and is honestly gated on the open physics.

CF1.1 What the moat is, and what the end product is — and which is sold

Two objects must never be confused: the moat (protected, never sold) and the end product (sold B2C or to government, gated on S2).

The moat — the patented native-geometry method/system (NEVER sold). The moat is not hardware and is not for sale. It is the protected method/system itself: the native-geometry compiler, the metric-target functionals, the source-reconstruction (metric → G_μν → T_eff) and energy-condition engines, the gauge/BRST/UV classifiers, the gate-card discipline, and the validated negative-control corpus — the same platform Parts F, L, and O describe. It is protected by patent + trade secret + copyright and kept inside. It is never licensed, never rented, never sold as simulation or screening software, and never given to a competitor, fund, attorney, lab, or any third party. Its commercial role is exactly that of a moat: it is the durable, defensible barrier that makes the eventual end product hard to copy — and selling it would be giving the moat away.

CF1.2 The near-term spend is cheap — it protects the moat, it does not sell anything

There is no product to build and sell near-term, because the only sellable thing (the end product) is gated on S2. So the only near-term spend is the cheap, front-loaded protection of the moat — establishing patent priority, copyright, and trade-secret hygiene over the native-geometry method that already exists at BRL-2.
