A reader who only wants the staircase: L1–L8 are the technical closure programs (source, energy ×2, UV/quantum, EFT, observability, control, mission); L9–L10 are the IP and buyer instruments; L11–L12 are the task backlog and the handoff. Source (L1) is first because it is the strongest blocker; the buyer memo (L10/L12) is last because it can only be honest once the technical programs have reported.

L0.5 The frozen BRL-4 milestone and the 90-day hostile validation sprint

The BRL is not crossed by argument; it is crossed by a funded, time-boxed, pre-registered validation sprint whose milestone predicate is frozen before the sprint begins. This is the concrete thing the ask in §L0.6 requests the acquirer fund, and it is the only mechanism by which standing moves from BRL-2 toward BRL-4/BRL-5.

The frozen BRL-4 / conversion milestone predicate — carried exactly, the single binary the whole ask turns on:

M1_EFT_CANDIDATE:
  invariant gate PASS
  causality gate PASS
  source ledger matched
  chi_source < 1
  energy AUDIT-visible
  no gate FAIL
  UV dependency named and independently reviewed if used
  EFT/backreaction chi_max < 1 over declared domain

In one sentence: EFT_CANDIDATE is reached only WITH a matched source ledger, χ_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption (energy at worst AUDIT, EFT χ_max < 1 over the declared domain). M1 means "worth a deep physics diligence sprint." It does not mean flight-ready, and there is no route from a "no" on any clause to "acquire a drive." This is the same discipline the protagonist enforces everywhere else, written as a contract: a missed milestone converts nothing. The predicate is frozen before the sprint precisely so that no amount of sprint enthusiasm can turn a "no" into a drive — the only honest exits from a "no" are "keep the screening tool" or "stop," never "acquire."

The sprint is six phases; every phase has a defined output and maps to a closure dimension; the milestone is evaluated only at the end against the frozen predicate, which cannot be edited mid-sprint:

Phase Days Output Maps to program / dimension BRL touched
1 1–15 Rebuild the tensor engine from spec (independent reimplementation) engine; L1 preface BRL-1
2 16–30 Rerun the five known-metric self-tests and the Alcubierre / Natário / Van Den Broeck warp baselines negative-control corpus; G2 BRL-2
3 31–45 Source + energy audit (the two gating dimensions) L1 / L2 / L3; HC-02 / HC-03 BRL-3
4 46–60 Gauge / BRST / UV / EFT audit L4 / L5; HC-05 / HC-06 / HC-08 / HC-09 BRL-4
5 61–75 Mars overlay + control simulation L7 / L8; HC-10 / G3 toward BRL-6/BRL-9
6 76–90 Hostile-review packet + IP update L9; IP-2…IP-6 CIPs iff artifacts exist BRL-4 → BRL-5

The decision tree (pack doc 10, expanded in leaf L10) walks the buyer through the predicate node by node: does the repo run and reproduce known metrics? → does it reject textbook warp metrics honestly? → does any candidate hit M1_EFT_CANDIDATE? → does hostile review accept M1 and the first-failure ledger? → can a null-controlled observable be defined? → can a safe non-flight lab proxy be specified by qualified reviewers? → can an independent lab proxy reproduce the signal? → can a flight-relevant subsystem requirements package be written? → Mars architecture option study. Every "no" routes to a non-acquisition node — software cleanup only, reject, keep/option screening IP only, theory-only continuation, simulation-only program, stop at lab research, or research program only. There is no node from which a "no" reaches "acquire a drive."

L0.6 The strategic-acquirer decision framing — the buyer logic Part L must never weaken

The single most important sentence in Part L: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should not buy "a claimed engine"; it should option the IP, fund a frozen 90-day hostile validation sprint, and convert only if the frozen BRL-4 / M1_EFT_CANDIDATE milestone is hit. Stated as the right ask versus the wrong one:

  • Wrong ask: "Buy a Mars spaceship engine." There is no engine. The honest answer to "can this currently build a Mars spaceship?" is No — current ceiling is toy/simulation; current standing is BRL-2. The platform is a discriminator / screening tool, not a Mars spaceship.
  • Right ask: Option the base provisional IP and fund a 90-day hostile validation sprint against the frozen milestone. The downside is bounded and the IP is real either way; the expected outcome is that every candidate fails and the acquirer retains a rigorous, IP-protected screening platform. This is the journey the document invites: option → fund a frozen sprint → convert only if M1_EFT_CANDIDATE is hit and hostile review agrees. A "no" at the milestone is a perfectly good outcome — it leaves the buyer holding the discriminator — but it is never a path to acquiring a drive, because no such path exists in this document by construction.

The milestone-triggered value ladder makes the asymmetry explicit and shows why the option is rational at every branch:

Validation result Buyer action What the acquirer owns Decision-tree node
Code fails to run / reproduce No acquisition; possibly fund cleanup only Nothing acquired; diligence cost only software cleanup only
Rejects warp metrics honestly; all candidates fail (expected) Option the screening IP A rigorous, IP-protected exotic-propulsion screening platform + validated negative-control corpus keep / option screening IP only
One candidate hits the frozen M1 milestone File CIPs (IP-2…IP-6) before public disclosure; deep diligence The patent window on a sourced EFT_CANDIDATE before the world knows proceed to hostile review
Independent hostile review accepts M1 + ledger Negotiate conversion / acquisition / JV (IP-11) A defensible, externally-validated position (BRL-5) proceed toward observable
A null-controlled observable / lab proxy later found Stand up a non-flight research program (BRL-6→BRL-8) Optionality on a genuinely new capability; IP-12 reserved lab research → subsystem study

The logic the chapter must never soften: even the expected outcome — every candidate fails — is a win for the buyer, because the asset is the discriminator, not a survivor. If all modes fail, the acquirer owns a rigorous screening platform and its IP — a cheap, disciplined, fail-closed frontier-propulsion validation capability, valuable independent of any candidate outcome. If one mode reaches the milestone, the acquirer controls the patent window before disclosure. The option is cheap relative to either payoff; the validation sprint is the price of information; conversion is fired by a frozen predicate plus an accepting hostile review, not by enthusiasm; and — the structural guarantee — there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." This is the entire reason the document is structured as a failure-mode engine rather than a sales deck.

Approved program names (pack doc 10): Screening Platform Program · EFT Candidate Search Program · Independent Physics Audit Program · Observable Proxy Program · Non-Flight Demonstrator Requirements Program · Mars Architecture Option Study. Forbidden program names: Warp drive build · FTL ship · Mars engine · heavy-lift-vehicle install. Naming discipline is part of the buyer logic: a program may not be called a build even before it is gated as one.

L0.7 How the IP ladder is sequenced against the BRL — the option structure

The bootstrapping sequence (pack doc 09, expanded in leaf L9) ties the two ladders together, and is the operational reading of the IP ladder of §L0.2.2 under the operational rule of §L0.2.3:

exclusive option over IP-1 / IP-7 / IP-8
90-day hostile validation sprint
frozen milestone predicate
CIP filing rights only if artifacts are produced
conversion only if M1_EFT_CANDIDATE is true
no conversion on "promising"

Read as steps:

  1. Option the base provisional (IP-1 → IP-10): the acquirer obtains the exclusive evaluation right over the screening / classification / control platform (IP-1) plus the software copyright (IP-7) and trade-secret scoring heuristics (IP-8) — before the sprint.
  2. Freeze the milestone predicate (the M1_EFT_CANDIDATE block of §L0.5) before the sprint — it cannot be renegotiated once funded.
  3. Fund the 90-day hostile validation sprint (§L0.5).
  4. If the milestone misses (the expected case): keep the screening-platform IP (IP-1, IP-7, IP-8) and publish the defensive-publication corpus (IP-9). The portfolio has standalone value as a discriminator.
  5. If the milestone hits: file the CIPs (IP-2 source-ledger, IP-3 energy/exoticity, IP-4 observability, IP-5 control/tolerance, IP-6 Mars-overlay) before public disclosure — and only for the artifacts actually produced (operational rule).
  6. If hostile review accepts M1 and the first-failure ledger: decide conversion / acquisition / JV (IP-11), triggered by the frozen milestone, never by "promising."
  7. Only after independent physical evidence exists (a real lab observable), consider future physical-embodiment filings (IP-12) — never before.

The invention families the portfolio is built from — metric target functionals, vehicle-comoving lobe definitions, invariant classifiers, source reconstruction, energy diagnostics, gauge/BRST classifiers, UV-dependency classifiers, gate-card validators, tolerance budgets, gate-supervised control, Mars validity overlays, and first-failure reporting — are mapped to claim seeds and supporting leaves in the Part-K patent-support matrix and detailed across L1–L9. Patent-counsel note, carried verbatim from the pack: this is strategy, not legal advice; counsel must decide claim language, priority, inventorship, assignment, option terms, and prosecution. The chapter states the strategy, not the prosecution.

L0.8 Scope boundary (restated, non-negotiable)

Part L (v2) is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap. It is not a hardware-construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware. The current manuscript ceiling remains PASS_TOY; current buildability standing is BRL-2. A buildable Mars-spacecraft program requires independent closure of source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT, controls, observability, safety, certification, and mission-integration gates — each with its own named criterion and its own named first failure. No rung past BRL-2 has been crossed; the chapter draws the staircase and prices the first funded step (the sprint that tests for BRL-4).

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED · ceiling PASS_TOY respected; current standing BRL-2. This overview promotes no candidate and presents no new computational result. The BRL's in-scope rungs are BRL-1/BRL-2 (achieved) and BRL-3/BRL-4 (targets with acceptance tests, unreached); BRL-5 → BRL-9 are described as sequenced future work only. The refined IP ladder IP-0 … IP-12 is stated as strategy, not prosecution, with every CIP bound to its closure artifact by the operational rule. First failure: a roadmap-only chapter risks reading as an implied promise that the ladder will be climbed — scope-creep from "here is the map and the next funded step" toward "here is the plan to build the drive." Fixed structurally: every BRL rung past BRL-4 is marked out-of-scope/future-only; every closure program (L1–L8) carries an explicit unmet-criterion downgrade token; the decision tree has no node from which a "no" reaches "acquire a drive"; and the two gating dimensions (source HC-02, energy HC-03) are stated as open and currently failing in the worked exemplar G1 (source_check = FAIL, energy AUDIT), so the chapter cannot be misread as claiming the milestone is near or assured. The deeper standing first failure of the underlying program remains, unchanged, the source/energy closure that blocks BRL-2 → BRL-4. What remains to close: the closure programs L1–L8 (source χ_source < 1 with a real SourceMatchReport; energy condition + magnitude audit; named + independently-reviewed UV assumption with B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED; domain-wide EFT χ_max < 1; coordinate-independent observability with null controls; gate-supervised digital twin with mandatory abort; and validity-weighted Mars overlay with no global Δt) — none crossed in this document — and the independent hostile audit (BRL-5). The IP filings IP-2…IP-6 are filed only if the corresponding artifacts are produced during a funded sprint; IP-11 conversion fires only on M1 + accepting hostile review; IP-12 is reserved for an actual lab observable. Patent extraction: Part L (v2) is itself a portfolio-strategy and diligence asset, not a new invention claim. It protects value by (a) binding each CIP (IP-2…IP-6) to a named closure artifact via the operational rule, so a CIP is filed exactly when — and only when — its artifact exists; (b) front-loading IP-0/IP-1/IP-7/IP-8 so the screening platform, code, and scoring heuristics are protected before any physics closes; (c) reserving IP-9 defensive publication of the validated negative-control corpus to block competitors from patenting the obvious failing variants; and (d) reserving IP-12 future-embodiment filings until independent physical evidence exists. The strategy is severable from the unverified Fable/TOE corpus and survives the expected "all candidates fail" outcome. Reviewer attack: "This is a roadmap to a spaceship dressed as diligence — a Buildability Readiness Ladder is just a build plan with extra steps, and a PASS_TOY/BRL-2 toy has no business sketching a path to a BRL-9 Mars architecture option." Honest response: the chapter draws the road precisely so the buyer can see how long and how gated it is, and it stops the in-scope claim at BRL-4 (EFT_CANDIDATE, explicitly unreached), not BRL-9. Crucially, the buyer logic does not depend on climbing the ladder: the rational action is to option the IP and fund one frozen-milestone sprint, whose expected outcome is "all candidates fail and the acquirer owns a rigorous screening platform." A build plan promises a build; this chapter prices information and protects IP, and — like the rest of the document — is engineered so that every incompleteness downgrades the claim rather than inflating it. The structural guarantee that settles the attack: there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." It is not a path to a spaceship; it is the honest, priced first step away from a toy, with BRL-5…BRL-9 drawn so no one mistakes them for done.

L1 — Master Gap-Closure Roadmap

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED (ceiling PASS_TOY; this is the root leaf of the refreshed Part L (v2) — it promotes no candidate, presents no new computational result, and instead draws the master map of which gaps must close, in what order, against which artifact, before this becomes an engineering program) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · Buildability standing: approximately BRL-2 (validated negative-control corpus) with a concrete, pre-registered path to test for BRL-4 (EFT_CANDIDATE under the frozen milestone) · Scope: gap-closure + validation + IP + diligence roadmap; NOT a hardware-construction manual.

L1.0 What this leaf is, and what it replaces

Part L (v2) is the Buildability & IP Ladder of this design document, and it replaces the prior Part L wholesale. The earlier Part L drew seven physics-dimension closure sub-ladders (source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT) one at a time. The refreshed Part L re-roots the whole thing on a single organizing object — the master gap-closure roadmap — and threads two new ladders through it that the prior version did not carry as first-class spines: the Buildability Readiness Ladder (BRL-1 → BRL-9) and the Refined IP Ladder (IP-0 → IP-12). This leaf, L1, is that root.

The purpose of L1 is stated in one sentence, carried verbatim from the pack: "Define the gaps that must close before this becomes an engineering program." Everything downstream in Part L (v2) — the source-matched-mode program, the energy/exoticity program, the UV/quantum program, the EFT/backreaction program, the observability program, the control/digital-twin program, the Mars-mission-architecture program, the refined IP ladder, the strategic-acquirer decision tree, the agent backlog, and the executive handoff — is one column of the master gap table this leaf opens with. L1 is therefore the table of contents with teeth: each gap is named, its current state is stated honestly, its required closure artifact is fixed, and its IP trigger is bound to that artifact so that no filing precedes the evidence it claims.

A boundary, stated once, governing the whole leaf and carried verbatim from the pack: "This is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap. It is not a hardware construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware. Current ceiling remains PASS_TOY." Nothing in this leaf — and nothing in the ladders it indexes — crosses that line. A gap-closure roadmap reads, to a careless eye, as a construction plan ("close these ten gaps and you have a drive"). It is the opposite: it is the enumeration of why we do not have a drive, drawn so that an unmet gap downgrades the program's standing rather than being narrated past.

L1.1 The honest current standing — what the rest of the document has already executed

Before the gaps are mapped, the standing they are measured against must be stated, because the roadmap is only credible if its starting point is the document's real result, not an aspiration. The manuscript's executed core (Parts E, F, G) has already produced the answer the roadmap is built on:

  • The deepest, most charitable candidate fails-closed. The worked exemplar G1 (MID-METRIC-001) — smooth, weak (A = 0.01), static, EFT-valid (χ_max = 0.0404, a ~25× cutoff margin), causally clean, gauge-real (R = −4.0404×10⁻⁴ ≠ 0), carrying a genuine coordinate-invariant forward proper-distance deficit ΔL ≈ 0.08837 gu — nonetheless terminates at FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC at the source gate (Gate 5 / HC-02): declared vacuum, yet T_eff = G_μν/8π ≠ 0, a 100% source mismatch, with the deeper root cause that the deficit is sourced by a negative effective energy density ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ (geometrized) that no declared field supplies (Gate 6 / HC-03). The candidate cannot be promoted past PASS_TOY.
  • Every textbook warp metric fails the same way, independently of the corpus. The corpus-agnostic baseline G2 runs Alcubierre, Natário, and Van Den Broeck through the platform; zero of three reach a clean energy PASS — each produces a region of negative tetrad-frame energy density ρ̂ = T̂_{0̂0̂} < 0 and a null-energy-condition violation on the warp wall, terminating at FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY (violation elided in prose) or TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC (violation declared, retained only as a sourced energy-condition-violating object of record). This is the BRL-2 negative-control corpus in action: the screen rejects the famous metrics honestly.
  • Local shortening does not integrate to a travel-time claim. Proposition G3-B (TOY_TESTED) holds that the validity-weighted local shortening W·S_L is a per-event geometry diagnostic with no diffeomorphism-invariant global aggregation functional; any Earth–Mars travel-time number built from it is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM by proof-sketch, not merely by editorial caution.

So the standing the roadmap starts from is: a runnable screening engine (BRL-1) over a validated negative-control corpus (BRL-2), whose best candidate is a sourced-only-in-prose, exotic-energy toy that fails-closed. The roadmap's job is to define exactly what evidence would move one candidate from there to BRL-4 — EFT_CANDIDATE under a frozen milestone — and to make explicit that the expected outcome is that every candidate fails and a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer retains a useful, IP-protected screening platform anyway. The protectable asset is the discriminator — the screening method itself — not a surviving drive, which is why its value to any rigorous frontier-R&D acquirer holds independently of whether a drive is ever built. There is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive" anywhere on this map.

L1.2 The master gap table — ten gaps, current state, required closure, IP trigger

The pack gives the master gap table as ten rows. We carry every row exactly, then expand each into (a) the Part L (v2) leaf that owns its closure program, (b) the gate / HC / BRL coordinate it lives at, and (c) the first-failure / downgrade token that fires when the gap is not closed. How to read this table. Each row is a staircase, not a switch. "Current state" is the rung the document actually stands on today; "required closure" is the artifact that would let a candidate stand one rung higher; "IP trigger" is the filing that may be made only when that artifact exists (the operational rule of §L1.6). The "downgrade token" is what the gate stamps when the gap is open — and for every one of the ten gaps, the document's present standing is open, which is why the chapter-level standing is PASS_TOY and the BRL standing is BRL-2.

The two gating gaps. The pack and the executed results agree that source and energy are the dominant blockers. Source is first because it is where the best candidate dies in reading order (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC); energy is the deeper physical root cause (the source it needs is ρ_eff < 0, an exotic distribution no admissible field in S_eff supplies). These two gaps own leaves L2 and L3 and are paired as the two gating dimensions of the funded validation sprint (§L1.8). The remaining eight gaps are real and each carries its own downgrade token, but a candidate that cannot clear source and energy never reaches them — it is already downgraded.

The ordering is not arbitrary. It is the gate ladder's own reading order, frozen in the executed exemplar G1: a candidate is checked for definition → negative controls → invariance/gauge (HC-01) → source (HC-02) → energy (HC-03) → causality (HC-04) → EFT/cutoff (HC-05) → quantization (HC-06) → UV boundary (HC-07) → observability/control/mission (HC-08/09/10). The master gap table is that ladder transposed into a program table: each gate becomes a workstream with a closure artifact and an IP trigger. A gap closes only when its gate would PASS on a real candidate with the artifact in hand — never by argument.

L1.3 The master milestone — M1_EFT_CANDIDATE, carried exactly

The roadmap converges on a single predicate. The pack states it as a fenced block; we carry it verbatim and then make each clause executable and bind it to the gate that adjudicates it. This predicate is the BRL-4 conversion criterion; it is the only thing that turns a "promising" candidate into a fundable EFT_CANDIDATE.

M1_EFT_CANDIDATE:
  invariant gate PASS
  causality gate PASS
  source ledger matched
  chi_source < 1
  energy AUDIT-visible
  no gate FAIL
  UV dependency named and independently reviewed if used
  EFT/backreaction chi_max < 1 over declared domain

"M1 means 'worth a deep physics diligence sprint.' It does not mean flight-ready." (pack, carried verbatim.)

The BRL-4 / conversion criterion, carried exactly. The frozen milestone that authorizes conversion is: an EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." M1 above and the BRL-4 conversion criterion are the same predicate stated at two altitudes; the roadmap keeps them identical on purpose so that no agent, attorney, or reviewer can quietly weaken one relative to the other.

Two precision notes the build contract forces. First, energy AUDIT-visible is not energy PASS. The energy gate is never a clean PASS in this document (CONTRACT §3); the strongest energy result M1 permits is "audit-visible" — ε is reported, and ε < 0 is flagged and handed to L3, never silently cleaned. A candidate may satisfy M1 with a declared, bounded exoticity burden and still be only a screening object, not a ship. Second, M1 is awarded by owner/attorney escalation, never self-promoted (CONTRACT §1.4). An agent that computes all eight clauses TRUE produces a candidate for M1, not an M1; the milestone is conferred by the frozen, pre-registered review, which is exactly what makes it usable as a conversion trigger (§L1.7). No mode in this document satisfies M1. The deepest exemplar G1 fails clause 3 (source ledger matched) and clause 5's spirit (its required source is exotic), terminating at FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC. That is the intended outcome (CONTRACT §1.6).

L1.6 The operational rule and the gap-to-artifact-to-IP coupling — stated as one machine-checkable invariant

The roadmap's central discipline is a coupling between three columns: gap → closure artifact → IP trigger. The operational rule binds them so that the middle column gates both neighbours. Stated as an invariant the red-team pass can check:

INVARIANT  IP_FILING_IS_ARTIFACT_BACKED:
  for every IP rung r in {IP-2, IP-3, IP-4, IP-5, IP-6, IP-11, IP-12}:
      may_file(r)  ⟺  artifact(r).exists == true
                       and artifact(r).hash is recorded (IP-0)
                       and (r == IP-11 ⇒ M1_EFT_CANDIDATE == true and hostile_review.accepts == true)
                       and (r == IP-12 ⇒ independent_lab_evidence.exists == true)
  violation ⇒ FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION   # filing ahead of evidence is a fail, not a milestone

This invariant is the IP-side analogue of the physics gate ladder: just as a candidate cannot self-promote past a gate it has not cleared, an IP filing cannot precede the artifact it claims. The three named instances of the rule (carried exactly) are the load-bearing cases: (1) no source-ledger CIP (IP-2) without a real SourceMatchReport; (2) no observability CIP (IP-4) without a null-controlled signal model; (3) no future physical embodiment filing (IP-12) without independent evidence. The first guards against patenting a "source-from-geometry" engine before any source is actually matched; the second against patenting a "metric-interface telemetry" system before any null-controlled observable is defined; the third — the strongest — against ever filing on a physical embodiment on the strength of simulation alone.

Why this coupling is the credibility of the asset. The buyer logic (§L1.7) asks a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer to option IP and fund a sprint, not to buy a drive. That ask is only coherent if the IP ladder cannot inflate ahead of the physics — otherwise the option is over vapor. The gap→artifact→IP coupling is precisely the mechanism that keeps the option honest: every CIP that can be filed corresponds to a closure artifact that actually exists, and the conversion filing (IP-11) corresponds to the frozen milestone (M1) being independently confirmed. The asset on offer is "the screen plus the right to file as evidence accrues," not "a drive" — which is exactly the shape of asset an acquirer can option cheaply: a downside-protected R&D option whose floor value is the validated screening method itself, independent of any survivor.

L1.7 The buyer logic — option, fund, convert (never weaken)

The roadmap exists to support one ask, carried exactly: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. The asymmetry is the point: optioning a validated screening process (an option fee plus a bounded validation sprint) is cheap and downside-protected, whereas buying a nonexistent engine is neither. The decision structure (expanded in full in the L10 strategic-acquirer decision-tree leaf) is:

exclusive option over IP-1 / IP-7 / IP-8          # the screening platform IP, pre-sprint (IP-10)
90-day hostile validation sprint                  # adversarial, owner cannot self-grade
frozen milestone predicate = M1_EFT_CANDIDATE     # pre-registered, immutable mid-sprint
CIP filing rights only if artifacts are produced  # IP-2..IP-6 gated by §L1.6 invariant
conversion only if M1_EFT_CANDIDATE is true        # IP-11, AND hostile review accepts (BRL-5)
no conversion on "promising"                        # there is no "promising" branch

The three things this logic must never do, carried from the executive handoff (verbatim "Do not do" list): do not ask a strategic acquirer to buy a Mars engine; do not imply heavy-lift-vehicle integration; do not imply physical source availability; do not convert local shortening into travel time; do not file CIPs unless closure artifacts exist; do not let any agent change the milestone mid-sprint. Each maps to a gate the document already enforces: "buy an engine" is foreclosed by the option/convert structure; "super-heavy-lift-vehicle integration" by the BRL-9 ceiling (option study, not install); "physical source availability" by the source gate (HC-02) and the §L1.6 invariant; "local→travel-time" by Proposition G3-B; "file ahead of evidence" by the §L1.6 invariant; "change the milestone mid-sprint" by the frozen, pre-registered M1.

The decision tree's terminal honesty. The L10 decision tree (carried in full in that leaf) routes every "no" to a lesser program — software cleanup, reject, keep/option screening IP only, theory-only continuation, simulation-only program, stop at lab research, research program only — and only a complete chain of "yes" answers reaches "Mars architecture option study." At no node does a "no" route to "acquire a drive," and even the terminal "yes" is an option study, not a build. The expected case — given G1, G2, and G3 — is an early "no" (source/energy), which leaves a strategic acquirer owning the screening platform and its negative-control corpus. That is the floor of the deal, and it is a real asset — a validated, fail-closed frontier-propulsion screening capability, valuable independent of any candidate outcome; the ceiling is a fundable EFT_CANDIDATE, and it is only reachable through M1.

Approved vs forbidden program names (carried exactly, because the name is a claim). Approved: Screening Platform Program · EFT Candidate Search Program · Independent Physics Audit Program · Observable Proxy Program · Non-Flight Demonstrator Requirements Program · Mars Architecture Option Study. Forbidden: Warp drive build · FTL ship · Mars engine · heavy-lift-vehicle install. The roadmap forbids the latter four because each names a claim the document cannot make; using one would be a chapter-level violation of CONTRACT §4.

L1.10 Scope boundary (restated, non-negotiable)

This leaf is the root of a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap. It is not a hardware-construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 01; CONTRACT §4). The current manuscript ceiling remains PASS_TOY. A buildable Mars-spacecraft program requires the independent closure of source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT, controls, observability, safety, certification, and mission-integration gates — each with its own named criterion and its own named first failure, each owned by a downstream Part L (v2) leaf, each currently open. The platform is a discriminator / screening tool, not a Mars spaceship; the expected outcome may still be that every candidate fails while a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer retains a useful, IP-protected screening platform. This leaf draws the master map and prices its first funded step; it crosses none of it, and there is no route on it from a "no" node to "acquire a drive."

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED · ceiling PASS_TOY respected; this root leaf of Part L (v2) promotes no candidate and presents no new computational result. Buildability standing is BRL-2 (runnable screening engine over a validated negative-control corpus), with a concrete, pre-registered path to test for BRL-4 (EFT_CANDIDATE under the frozen milestone M1). The master gap table's ten gaps are all open; the two gating gaps (source, energy) are where the deepest exemplar G1 fails-closed. First failure: structurally, a gap-closure roadmap read as a build plan — "close these ten gaps and you have a drive." It is the opposite: every gap is open, the best candidate (G1) fails the first two (source FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, energy ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ < 0), the milestone M1 is met by zero modes, and the expected outcome is universal candidate failure with a strategic acquirer retaining the screening platform. The fix is to keep every gap a target ledger with tolerances + a downgrade token, never a construction step, and to hold the non-enabling scope boundary (L1.10) load-bearing. What remains to close: produce, under the funded 90-day hostile sprint, the closure artifacts that make M1 real — freeze the candidate inventory; finalize the per-mode SourceMatchReport (BRL-3 hinge, gap source, IP-2); finalize the tetrad-frame energy/exoticity audit (gap energy, IP-3); implement the M1 predicate as code and tie every IP trigger to an artifact hash (§L1.6 invariant); drive at least one mode to all eight M1 clauses TRUE with chi_source < 1, chi_max < 1 over a declared domain, energy AUDIT-visible, causality PASS, and any UV need named and independently reviewed; then, and only then, with owner/attorney escalation and hostile-review acceptance (BRL-5), consider conferring EFT_CANDIDATE and filing IP-11. None of this is crossed in the present document. Patent extraction: the Refined IP Ladder (IP-0 → IP-12) bound to the gap→artifact→IP coupling — front-loaded protection of the screening platform (IP-0 hashes, IP-1 provisional, IP-7 software copyright, IP-8 trade-secret scoring heuristics, IP-9 defensive publication of the negative controls) that exists at BRL-2 today, plus the artifact-gated CIPs (IP-2 source-ledger, IP-3 energy/exoticity, IP-4 observability, IP-5 control/tolerance, IP-6 Mars-overlay) filed only when their closure artifacts exist (§L1.6 invariant IP_FILING_IS_ARTIFACT_BACKED), the IP-10 strategic-acquirer option pre-sprint, IP-11 conversion only on M1 + hostile review, and IP-12 physical-embodiment filings only on independent evidence. Valuable as a "proves-it-isn't-buildable-yet" discriminator regardless of any physics outcome; severable from the unverified Fable/TOE corpus. Not legal advice — counsel decides claim language, priority, inventorship, assignment, option terms, and prosecution. Reviewer attack: "This is a ten-step recipe for a warp drive with patents stapled on — you've drawn the milestone, the BRL ladder, and the IP ladder, so you obviously think the drive is reachable; the 'option, don't buy' framing is just deal-sweetening." Honest response: the roadmap is a downgrade engine, not a recipe — every one of the ten gaps is open, the milestone M1 is satisfied by zero modes, the document's most charitable candidate (G1) fails the first two gates (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC; required source is exotic ρ_eff < 0), the textbook warp metrics (G2) all fail the same energy gate, and the no-global-aggregation proposition (G3-B) forecloses any travel-time claim even on a hypothetical survivor. The BRL ladder is built to stop at whatever rung the evidence runs out (BRL-5+ each route a "no" to a lesser program), and the decision tree has no "promising" branch and no path from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." The IP ladder is bound by the §L1.6 invariant so that no CIP is filed before its closure artifact exists and no physical-embodiment filing is made without independent evidence — which is exactly why the ask is an option on a funded sprint with a frozen, pre-registered conversion predicate, not a purchase. The honest expected outcome is that every candidate fails and a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer is left owning a rigorous, IP-protected screening platform and its negative-control corpus — which is the product, not a consolation prize.

L2 — Source-Matched Mode Program

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED (ceiling PASS_TOY; this is a Part-L (v2) buildability sub-program leaf — it promotes no candidate and presents no new computational result; it formalizes the source-matching staircase a candidate must climb and the single core blocker that governs it) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · Scope: gap-closure + validation + IP + diligence roadmap for the source dimension; NOT a hardware-construction manual. This is the program for the strongest standing technical blocker of the whole effort: source closure. Buildability ladder position: this is the program that, if executed, moves a candidate from BRL-3 (sourced toy) toward the BRL-4 frozen milestone — it is the source clause of EFT_CANDIDATE.

L2.0 Why this is the first gap-closure program, and the one-line blocker it carries

Part L (v2) replaces the prior Part L. It decomposes the buildability problem into the gap-closure programs of the v2 pack (pack docs 01–12), and this leaf expands pack doc 02 — the Source-Matched Mode Program — which the master gap-closure roadmap (pack 01) lists as the first gap, with current state "deepest exemplar is unsourced" and required closure "matched source ledger, chi_source < 1." The pack states the core blocker of this entire program in four words, which we carry verbatim:

No source, no buildability.

That sentence is not rhetoric; it is the executed conclusion of Parts A–J. A metric profile is not a propulsion concept until the required stress-energy is matched by a declared source model. The deepest-surviving exemplar in the corpus, G1 / MID-METRIC-001, is the most charitable non-trivial candidate the platform contains — smooth (C^∞), weak (A = 0.01), static, EFT-admissible (χ_max = 0.04040, a 25× margin), causally clean (no CTCs, locally subluminal), gauge-real (R = −4.0404×10⁻⁴ ≠ 0, not pure gauge), and carrying a genuine, coordinate-invariant forward proper-distance deficit of ΔL = 0.08837 gu (≈0.22% over a 40-gu baseline; analytic cross-check ½A√π σ = 0.08862, agreeing to 0.3%). It passes every geometric and kinematic gate (G1–G4, G7–G10 as-declared). And it still fails-closed at the source gate (HC-02 / Gate 5) with terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC: the metric declares vacuum (δA_μ^a = δφ^I = δG_AB = 0) yet its forced effective source T_eff = G_μν/8π ≠ 0 — a 100% source mismatch, with negative effective energy density ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ (geometrized) at the lobe center.

So the source program is first because it is where the best available candidate dies, and it is the program any future candidate must clear before any other rung can matter. The pack's objective for this leaf is exact, and we carry it as the program's mission statement:

Objective (pack 02): Find or falsify at least one candidate whose required effective stress-energy can be matched by a declared, admissible source model.

Note the symmetry in that sentence — find or falsify. The program is a discriminator/screening tool, not a search for a survivor. Its expected, intended outcome (BUILD CONTRACT §1.6, "Most modes should fail. That is good.") is that every candidate fails the source match, leaving a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer with a rigorous, IP-protected source-screening platform and its negative-control corpus — which is the product either way. There is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive."**

A boundary stated once, up front (pack 02 "Boundary"; CONTRACT §4). This is a classification, validation, and audit program over a simulation object. Running it does not "build the source," does not produce stress-energy, and is explicitly non-enabling: it provides no instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware. Wherever a rung might invite a "how to make the matter" reading, the object is restated as a target effective-source ledger with tolerances, never an apparatus. The current ceiling remains PASS_TOY; a buildable Mars-spacecraft program requires independent closure of source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT, controls, observability, safety, certification, and mission-integration gates — this program closes one of them, and only to the BRL-4 milestone, not to flight.

L2.1 The forced-source identity — the spine the whole program hangs from

Every required artifact in this program is a statement about one identity, the Einstein field equation read right-to-left (G1 §0, §6; HC-02 / E02a §E02a.1). The pack lists it as a required artifact in exactly this form:

G_μν[g]  =  8πG · T_μν      ⇒      T_eff = G/(8πG)      (artifact: "T_eff = G/(8πG)")

This is an identity, not an assumption. Once a candidate fixes the metric g_μν(t,x), the Einstein tensor G_μν is completely determined by differentiation — there is no remaining freedom — so the effective stress-energy T_eff is also completely determined, component by component, at every event. The author of a metric drive does not get to draw the lobe and then declare in prose that "the appropriate stress-energy sources this geometry." That sentence is a promissory note; the corpus disqualifies it on sight (E02a §E02a.0: "a source is not 'present' because prose says it is present"), and the chapter-level first failure of HC-02 is precisely "a metric arrives with no computed, matched T_eff — 'a source because prose says so'" → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC. The source program is the apparatus that forces T_eff to be exhibited, characterized, and matched to fields the action is actually allowed to switch on.

Three frame-projected observables are what a reviewer actually audits, because a bare tensor is hard to read — project T_eff onto the vehicle-comoving tetrad e_a^μ (E02a §E02a.1; G1 §6):

energy density   ε   = T_eff_μν e_0^μ e_0^ν      (= T_eff_{0̂0̂})
energy flux      S_î = − T_eff_μν e_0^μ e_î^ν
principal stress p_î = T_eff_μν e_î^μ e_î^ν       (no sum; diagonalize for principals)

The single fact that hands off out of this program: ε < 0 anywhere is the hand-off signal to the energy/exoticity program L3 (pack 03, HC-03). The source program does not adjudicate the sign of energy — that is L3's job. It adjudicates whether T_eff (a) exists and is nonzero and (b) is sourceable by a declared admissible field. A mode can clear the source program (it has a clean, identified source) and still die in the energy program (the source it needs requires ε < 0). Keeping the two programs separate is what stops this document from ever claiming a "source" that is secretly exotic. For G1 the two are one physical truth seen twice: the source program's terminal FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC is caused by the energy program's finding — the metric demands ε = ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ along the whole axis, and no admissible field in S_eff is a static negative-energy source, so the mismatch is necessarily total. This linkage is the program's load-bearing cross-check (L2.4 #9).

These nine are the concrete output a validation-sprint source audit (the backlog task (2) source inversion, pack 11, with acceptance "all tensor components accounted") must deliver, and the substrate of the IP claims in L2.7. They assemble into the report object the pack names first: the SourceMatchReport, required for every candidate (pack 02).

The SourceMatchReport object (carried from E02a §E02a.3; the pack's first required artifact). Every candidate emits this — on a pass and on a fail, with the residual published either way:

SourceMatchReport = {
  T_eff,                      # 4×4 symmetric, from geometry (forced)  [artifact 2]
  T_fields,                   # 4×4 symmetric, from declared fields varied from S_eff  [artifact 4]
  Delta_T = T_eff − T_fields, # the residual tensor  [artifact 5]
  norm_T_eff, norm_T_fields, norm_Delta_T,         # frame-invariant scalars  [artifact 6]

  first_unmatched_component,  # named tetrad component of largest mismatch  [artifact 7]
  declared_field_list,        # the legitimacy-guarded field list  [artifact 3 / 9]
  source_class,               # S0..S7 (L2.3)
  status                      # gate verdict
}

The frame-invariant norm ‖T‖ ≡ √|T_μν T^μν| is used so the verdict does not depend on the chart; the tetrad components ε, S_î, p_î are reported alongside so sign information is not lost (E02a §E02a.3). The acceptance bar is declared explicitly so it is auditable, not adjustable to taste: TOL_match = 1.0×10⁻³ (relative), TOL_zero = 1.0×10⁻¹² (absolute; ‖T_eff‖ < TOL_zero ⇒ "no source," S0, and a likely coordinate artifact — check HC-01). The mismatch must be published even on success — a source-matching report with no residual is not a report, it is a claim; a silent pass is itself a fail (E02a §E02a.3, the test_source_mismatch_visible acceptance test). This is artifact #6/#7 made non-optional.

L2.4 The acceptance test — the frozen predicate for reaching the milestone

The pack states the source-program acceptance test as a four-line predicate (pack 02, "Acceptance test"), and it is the source clause of the master milestone M1_EFT_CANDIDATE (pack 01) and the milestone_hit() code predicate (pack 12). We carry all four lines verbatim and make each machine-checkable:

A candidate cannot reach M1 unless:
    source_mismatch < threshold              # chi_source < TOL_match (≡ chi_source < 1, with TOL_match=1e-3)
    chi_source < 1                            # the v2 source-mismatch metric strictly below unity
    first_unmatched_component == NONE         # every tetrad component accounted for
    source fields are frozen before fitting   # no post-hoc field invented to force the match

Each line closes a distinct evasion, and three of the four are anti-gaming guards rather than mere thresholds:

  • source_mismatch < threshold / chi_source < 1. The frozen, frame-invariant residual must be strictly below unity (and, for a genuine match rather than mere partial accounting, below TOL_match = 10⁻³). For G1, chi_source = 1.0 exactly — the candidate fails at the very first line. This is the line the 01 roadmap names as the required closure for the source gap: "matched source ledger, chi_source < 1."
  • first_unmatched_component == NONE. A small aggregate residual can still hide a single grossly-unmatched tensor component (e.g. a transverse shear T_{ŷẑ} left unaccounted while the energy channel matches). Requiring the named worst component to be NONE forbids "match the easy components, ignore the hard one." For G1 the first-unmatched component is T_{0̂0̂} (the negative-energy channel) and, since every component is unmatched, this line can never pass for a vacuum-declared metric.
  • source fields frozen before fitting. This is the deepest discipline. A candidate may not see T_eff first and then invent a field whose stress-energy happens to reproduce it; the declared field list (artifact #3) must be fixed before the matching fit runs. This is the v2 instance of the no-new-field legitimacy check (artifact #9): fitting over an undeclared field is the "invent a missing apparatus" violation (CONTRACT §1.3), and is downgraded to AUDIT_SOURCE_MISMATCH / FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (E02a §E02a.2, §E02a.6). Without this guard, any metric can be "sourced" by an arbitrary phenomenological fluid — which would make the whole program vacuous.

First failure (L2.4). The acceptance test is not met the instant any of the four lines fails: chi_source ≥ 1, or first_unmatched_component ≠ NONE, or the report omits the residual (norm_Δ_T / first_unmatched_component), or the matching field was introduced after seeing T_eff (post-hoc). A pass reported without a residual is itself a fail — "a source-matching report with no residual is a claim, not a report." For G1 the test fails on the first line (chi_source = 1.0) and would fail on the second and third as well (first_unmatched_component = T_{0̂0̂} ≠ NONE); the fourth is the only line it passes, and only vacuously (no field was invented because none was declared).

L2.5 Negative controls and reference baselines — how the program is shown to fire

A source program is only credible if it (a) flags genuine unsourced/mismatched metrics, (b) clears a genuinely matched toy source, and (c) refuses to be gamed by a post-hoc fitted field. The corpus exercises all three with frozen controls (E02a §E02a.4; the executed test suite is 14/14 PASS):

  • NC-MISS (the heart of the program). A populated metric (δg ≠ 0) with empty declared field content (Ξ field list empty) must return FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, before any numerics. This encodes "an ansatz is not a source" as an executable test. If the pipeline ever returns anything else for a populated-metric / empty-field object, the gate is broken and every downstream pass is void. NC-MISS is the calibration weight that must always tip to FAIL — and it is exactly the control G1 trips.
  • NC-MM (mismatch-visibility control). A known mismatch is injected (perturb a matched T_fields by Δ); the report must expose norm_Δ_T and a non-None first_unmatched_component. This operationalizes artifact #6/#7 — the residual is reported even on the toy that does match (closure_score = 1 − 10⁻⁶ still publishes its residual). It is the control behind the "silent pass is a fail" rule.
  • NC-FIELD (no-new-field legitimacy). A T_fields built from a field not in the declared action (a bare phenomenological "exotic fluid" inserted only to match T_eff) is rejected: the effective-fluid placeholder is diagnostic only, never a mechanism (E02a §E02a.2), and a fit ranging over an undeclared field is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION → AUDIT_SOURCE_MISMATCH. This is the executable form of the "frozen before fitting" acceptance line.
  • Reference baseline — the matched toy (calibration, not a candidate). A Gaussian-potential weak-field toy is run two ways: with a hand-chosen Gaussian-ρ (mismatch ~3×10⁻³ in the T_{00} tail at r ≳ 2σ, reported first_unmatched_component = "T_{00} tail: Gaussian-ρ vs exact-Poisson-Φ shape error", status AUDIT_SOURCE_MISMATCH), and with a Poisson-forced ρ (matched, status TOY_TESTED / S3). No drive appears — the toy is a calibration of the gate, not a candidate, and even the matched case publishes its residual.
  • Reference baseline — the GR warp family (known-exotic). Alcubierre, Natário, and Van Den Broeck are pushed through the same source pipeline and each returns terminal FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC at the source gate, with computed NEC_min of −0.2691, −0.2691, −0.1592 respectively — four orders of magnitude deeper than G1's −8.038×10⁻⁶. The program must reproduce "the famous warp metrics are unsourced" or it is broken; it does.

The first failure these controls collectively fire is the NC-MISS case: a populated metric with no declared field is the precise failure mode FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC exists to catch, and NC-MISS is the permanent regression test that keeps the gate honest.

L3.0 Purpose, scope, and the one sentence that governs this leaf

This chapter expands the V2 gap-closure pack's Energy, Exoticity, and Magnitude Program (pack doc 03) into a full design-doc chapter of refreshed Part L — Buildability & IP Ladder (v2), which replaces the prior Part L. It is the energy-side companion to L2 (source-matched mode program, gap source) and feeds L4 (UV/quantum/admissibility) and L8 (Mars mission architecture). Where the manuscript's HC-03 chapters (E03a/E03b) and the worked exemplar G1 already executed the energy gate against the 50-mode catalog, this leaf re-states that machinery in the V2 buildability voice: it ties the energy gate to the BRL ladder, names the energy first-failure token the program carries, and specifies the energy-diagnostic CIP (IP-3) trigger and operational rule. It invents no new physics and weakens no gate.

The governing sentence, carried verbatim from the pack's core blocker, is:

A candidate that needs hidden negative energy cannot be buildable. A candidate that visibly needs exotic energy can still be valuable as a screen.

That single asymmetry is the entire thesis of the chapter. The platform's job is not to find energy-clean drives — within the warp-like family there are none — but to make the exoticity demand of every candidate visible, quantified, and frame-robust, so that (a) no candidate is ever silently promoted on a hidden negative-energy budget, and (b) the act of measuring the exoticity is itself a defensible, hardware-free, magnitude-independent IP asset. The fail-closed BUILD CONTRACT (§3) governs every verdict: energy_check is never a clean PASS — it is "pass / audit-visible." The strongest token this leaf can emit on the energy gate is AUDIT. There is no energy_check: PASS anywhere in this document, and there is no route from this gate to "acquire a drive."

L3.1 Why this challenge matters (the load-bearing honesty gate)

Energy-condition accounting is the single most load-bearing honesty gate in the entire buildability case, and it is the gate most likely to be quietly violated by an enthusiast. The reason is structural. A forward proper-distance shortening S_L > 0 that is real (coordinate-invariant, surviving the HC-01 invariant gate of L1/C2) generically demands, via Einstein's equation along the lobe, an effective stress-energy whose null contraction is negative:

S_L > 0  (curvature-supported, invariant)  ⇒  generically  T_eff_{μν} k^μ k^ν < 0  (NEC violation) along the forward lobe.

This is not a defect of any one candidate; it is the Tipler–Hawking–Olum structure of distance-shortening geometries, and the manuscript surfaces it at HC-01 (L1) and hands the exoticity to HC-03 (this chapter) by design. The danger is that the negative-energy demand can be hidden three ways: (i) by declaring "vacuum" and never reconstructing T_eff (the source gate / L2 catches this — FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC); (ii) by reporting only the frame-dependent energy density ρ̂ = T̂_{0̂0̂}, which a Lorentz boost can momentarily make non-negative; or (iii) by reporting only a finite peak density while the integrated budget is catastrophic. The energy program closes all three holes, and the program's value to a strategic-acquirer diligence team is precisely that it cannot be talked past: a candidate either presents a visible, bounded, EFT-compatible exoticity ledger, or it is downgraded. A disciplined, fail-closed exoticity audit of this kind is exactly the cheap R&D option a frontier-aerospace prime can hold — it never certifies what it cannot prove, and is valuable independent of any candidate outcome.

Cross-reference: this is the gap the V2 master roadmap (L1 roadmap table, pack doc 01) lists as energy: exoticity visible → bounded energy/exoticity report → energy-diagnostic CIP. The challenge cards HC-01 (invariant distance) → HC-02 (source) → HC-03 (energy/exoticity) → HC-05 (gauge) form the reading-order spine; HC-03 is where the physics of the no-free-lunch lock actually lives, even when (as in G1) the source gate fires first in reading order and sets the terminal token.

L3.2 Formal object — the tetrad-frame stress-energy and the four conditions

Signature (−,+,+,+). Vehicle worldline z^μ(τ), four-velocity u^μ = dz^μ/dτ, u^μu_μ = −1. The crew measures in an orthonormal vehicle tetrad e_{â}{}^μ, â ∈ {0̂,1̂,2̂,3̂}, with e_{0̂}{}^μ = u^μ and g_{μν} e_{â}{}^μ e_{b̂}{}^ν = η_{âb̂}, Fermi–Walker transported (because u^μ need not be geodesic; parallel transport would spuriously rotate the spatial triad and frame-smear the pressures). The effective source is the contracted Einstein tensor of the full candidate metric — the shared/visible stress-energy of the single Einstein-frame metric, never a private/dark sector:

T_eff^{μν} = M_Pl² G^{μν}[ g_bg + δg[Ξ] ] ,   G^{μν} = R^{μν} − ½ g^{μν} R ,
T̂_{âb̂}    = T_eff_{μν} e_{â}{}^μ e_{b̂}{}^ν ,   ρ̂ ≡ T̂_{0̂0̂} ,   p̂_{î} (principal pressures = eigenvalues of T̂_{îĵ}).

This is the corpus authority boundary: T_eff is reconstructed from the effective action S_eff = ∫d⁴x√(−g)[(M_Pl²/2)R − ¼Z_ab F^aF^b − ½G_IJ∂φ^I∂φ^J − V + L_matter + L_constraint + L_EFT] via T_μν = −(2/√(−g))δS_matter/δg^μν (Fable_Forces: one-parent force projection, no double counting, used here for the force/gravity interface and NOT to bypass source/energy accounting). The three-layer discipline applies: δg_μν is the × base, admissibility/chamber data is ⊕, bundle/operator content is ⊗. An exotic demand cannot be hidden in a layer the energy gate does not see — if a candidate tried to source its negative energy from an unshared sector it would already have failed the single-visible-stress-energy anchor at L2/HC-02 before HC-03 ever runs. There is no "invisible negative-energy reservoir" license in this corpus.

The four pointwise conditions, in the vehicle frame, for future null k^{â} (η k k = 0) and future timelike unit v^{â} (η v v = −1):

NEC(x,k) = T̂_{âb̂} k^â k^b̂                              ≥ 0
WEC(x,v) = T̂_{âb̂} v^â v^b̂                              ≥ 0
SEC(x,v) = ( T̂_{âb̂} − ½ η_{âb̂} T̂ ) v^â v^b̂            ≥ 0 ,   T̂ = η^{âb̂}T̂_{âb̂}
DEC(x,v) : WEC(x,v) ≥ 0  AND  J^{â} = −T̂^{â}{}_{b̂} v^{b̂} is causal, future-directed (J·J ≤ 0, J^{0̂} ≥ 0)

For a diagonalizable (Hawking–Ellis Type I) source with {ρ̂, p̂_(1),p̂_(2),p̂_(3)} the minima have closed forms — min_k NEC = ρ̂ + min_α p̂_(α), min_v WEC = ρ̂, min_v SEC = ½(ρ̂ + Σ_α p̂_(α)), DEC = ρ̂ − max_α|p̂_(α)|. For Type II/III/IV sources (null-dominated / non-diagonalizable — exactly the lobe wall) the closed form is invalid and the algorithm must fall back to explicit direction sampling, gated by a Segre classifier (§L3.5, NC-SEGRE). First failure of L3.2: a Type-I closed-form shortcut applied to a Type-II wall source silently reports the wrong NEC minimum — the classifier gate is mandatory, and is itself a negative control.

L3.4 Required outputs (the eight artifacts the pack mandates)

The pack lists eight required outputs. Each is produced by the energy_condition_report pipeline and is a mandatory field of the energy gate card; each is hardware-free and magnitude-independent (an IP-relevant property, §L3.10).

# Required output (pack) Definition / form Status field
1 tetrad-frame stress-energy table T̂_{âb̂}(x) on the comoving grid, ρ̂, p̂_(α) always emitted
2 NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC results the four pointwise minima over the direction sphere always emitted
3 boosted-observer scan minima swept over boost β ∈ [0, 0.999] (frame-dependence audit) always emitted

The decision to integrate the NEC version E_NEC (not the WEC/ρ̂ version) is the single most important design choice in the chapter and the reason the first-failure is stated in NEC terms: the null condition is the frame-invariant floor — a Lorentz boost can make ρ̂ momentarily non-negative in some frame, but no boost removes a genuine NEC violation, because T̂_{âb̂}k^âk^b̂ for null k transforms as a Lorentz scalar in the chosen direction. Reporting only ρ̂_min would let a clever frame choice hide exoticity; reporting E_NEC does not. The severity σ_exo ∈ [0,1] ranks the catalog: 0 = no exotic content, →1 = profile dominated by negative energy (Alcubierre-class, catastrophic).

L3.5 Algorithms — energy_condition_report (production form) and its negative controls

The production algorithm consumes a tetrad-sampled T_eff and a worldline and emits the shared-contract JSON plus the exoticity ledger. It is fail-closed by construction: there is no code path that returns energy_check: PASS.

function energy_condition_report(T_eff, tetrad, worldline, grid, opts):
    if T_eff is None or tetrad is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "missing T_eff or tetrad", allowed="none", forbidden="any energy claim")
    require grid.covers(forward_lobe(worldline))  else AUDIT("lobe not fully sampled")

    report = new EnergyReport();  seg = SegreClassifier()
    for x in grid.points():
        That = tetrad.frame_components(T_eff, x)          # T̂_âb̂ (Fermi–Walker tetrad)
        cls  = seg.classify(That, tol=opts.segre_tol)     # Type I / II / III / IV
        if cls == TYPE_I:
            rho, p = diagonalize_spatial(That)
            nec = rho + min(p);  wec = rho
            sec = rho + sum(p);  dec = rho - max(abs(p))
        else:                                             # Type II/III/IV -> MUST sample
            nec = min_over_null(That, N_dir=512, refine=True)        # Fibonacci sphere + trust region 1e-6
            wec = min_over_timelike(That, beta_max=0.999)
            sec = min_over_timelike(trace_reverse(That), beta_max=0.999)
            dec = dec_flux_test(That, beta_max=0.999)
        report.record(x, cls, rho=That[0,0], nec=nec, wec=wec, sec=sec, dec=dec)
        report.update_minima(nec, wec, sec, dec)
        report.update_peak_negative(That[0,0])
    report.exoticity = integrate_exoticity(report, grid, worldline)   # V_exo, E_NEC, ρ̂_min, σ_exo, severity

    # fail-closed verdict — energy_check is NEVER a clean PASS:
    if report.min_NEC >= -opts.eps_ec:
        energy_check = "AUDIT"                            # clean *to tolerance* -> AUDIT, NOT PASS
        status       = "PASS_TOY" if report.has_source_pass else "AUDIT"
        first_fail   = "none at energy gate (audit-visible); next gate governs"
    else:
        energy_check = "AUDIT"                            # violation present & DECLARED -> still AUDIT-visible
        status       = "FAIL"
        first_fail   = "FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY" if not report.declared else "TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC"
    return { status, energy_check, evidence: report.as_dict(), first_failure: first_fail,
             allowed_claim: "tetrad-frame energy-condition report; exoticity quantified, not removed",
             forbidden_claim: "energy_check PASS; negative energy available; energy problem solved" }

The exoticity integral must be grid-convergent or the score is meaningless. The wall is a thin shell of thickness Δ ≈ 1/σ, so ρ̂_−√h is sharply peaked; under-resolution under-reports exoticity — a fail-open danger that makes a bad profile look better. The implementation uses adaptive radial refinement (±3Δ of the wall), composite Simpson quadrature, and a Richardson convergence guard: |E_NEC(2N) − E_NEC(N)| / |E_NEC(2N)| < 10⁻³, else it returns AUDIT("exoticity not grid-converged") rather than a number. Convergence failure is AUDIT, never a (lower) number passed off as the budget.

Negative controls (the gate's own tripwires — each a permanent regression test):

NC-KNOWN   toy Alcubierre lobe. REQUIRE min_NEC<0, σ_exo≈1, CATASTROPHIC_EXOTIC.
           If the gate returns AUDIT-clean -> the gate is BROKEN.        (maps to "known negative energy case flagged")
NC-VACUUM  exact Minkowski T_eff≡0. REQUIRE all minima=0, AUDIT-clean, NO false-positive exoticity.   (sign-bug guard)
NC-DUST    positive perfect fluid ρ>0,p≥0. REQUIRE NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC ≥ 0, σ_exo=0.                       (over-eager-FAIL guard)
NC-BOOST   WEC-violating-but-NEC-clean source; sweep boost β. REQUIRE NEC verdict INVARIANT while ρ̂ flips sign.
NC-SEGRE   Type-II null-dominated wall. REQUIRE closed-form REFUSED, sampling used.   (Type-I shortcut bug)
NC-DECL    declared=True with EMPTY ledger. REQUIRE rejection -> remains FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY.  (cosmetic-relabel guard)

NC-KNOWN is load-bearing (it is the "known negative energy case flagged" acceptance test). NC-VACUUM/NC-DUST are the false-positive guards: without them an over-aggressive gate would label honest matter exotic and the whole document's credibility — which rests on the gate being discriminating, not merely strict — would collapse. NC-DECL is the integrity guard. First failure of L3.5: if NC-VACUUM is omitted, a sign error in the tetrad sampler would make flat space read exotic and every mode would falsely FAIL — a "strict" gate that is actually broken. The controls exist so the gate's strictness is earned.

L3.6 The no-free-lunch coupling (why exoticity cannot be argued away)

The pack's acceptance test demands the failures connect to no-free-lunch language. Three audits — each phrased as something the pipeline checks, not something we assert — make the lock arithmetic.

(a) Frame-invariance floor (NEC cannot be boosted away). If a profile violates the NEC at a point in one orthonormal frame it violates it in every frame: for null k^â, under a local Lorentz boost Λ, k → Λk is again null and T̂'_{âb̂}k'^âk'^b̂ = T̂_{ĉd̂}k^ĉk^d̂ (a Lorentz scalar in the chosen null direction). By contrast ρ̂ = T̂_{0̂0̂} does change under boost; a momentarily-negative ρ̂ can be boosted positive iff the source is non-exotic in the NEC sense. You cannot make a forward-lobe profile honest by "picking a better frame" — that move only relocates WEC violation. This is why §L3.4 integrates E_NEC, not E. (G1 makes this concrete: the static-observer WEC_min = ρ̂ is −8.038×10⁻⁶, but the null-direction NEC_min is deeper, −1.138×10⁻⁴, because the null contraction ρ̂ + min_α p̂ digs further into the anisotropic exotic stress than the rest-frame density — and the NEC verdict is invariant throughout.)

(b) Ford–Roman quantum-inequality leash (you cannot pile up negative energy). Even granting QFT its local license to make ρ̂ < 0, the negative energy a quantum field can present to an observer is bounded by a quantum inequality of Ford–Roman type — ∫⟨T̂_{0̂0̂}⟩ g(τ/τ_0) dτ ≥ −C/τ_0⁴ (C=O(1), free massless field, 4D). The deeper and more negative you want ρ̂, the shorter it can persist and the larger the compensating positive energy that must flank it. The pipeline checks the QI ratio

Q = |E_required(τ_0)| / |E_QI_floor(τ_0)| ,   E_QI_floor(τ_0) = C·(proper area)/τ_0³  (worldsheet-integrated form),

and surfaces Q > 1 as the hand-off flag FAIL_QI_VIOLATION (owned by L4/HC-09, surfaced here). For the toy Alcubierre control, sharpening the wall to localize the negative shell sends the budget-integrated (Pfenning–Ford worldsheet) ratio Q_E ~ R²σ³v_s³/C — which grows with σ: satisfying the pointwise QI by sharpening violates the integrated QI even harder. For toy values R=100, σ=0.10, v_s=1, C≈1, Q_E ~ 10 > 1, climbing steeply with any attempt to enlarge S_L. We do not claim a rigorous QI proof for arbitrary Ξ — that closure is HC-09, OPEN.

(c) Shortening↔exoticity lock (the budget is the price of the distance). Empirically across the warp-like shift-lobe family, the forward shortening and the exoticity budget are monotonically locked: every warp-shift profile with S_L > ε_detect has E_NEC < 0, and |E_NEC| grows at least linearly with S_L at fixed lobe size. First failure of L3.6: the lock is empirical, and is a disjunction, not a single-gate theorem. A reviewer can legitimately demand the analytic inequality |E_NEC| ≥ κ·S_L, and can correctly note the lock is realized two different ways — NEC violation for warp-shift modes; magnitude/cutoff failure for NEC-clean modes — not by a single "every survivor is exotic" mechanism. Honest status is therefore AUDIT on the generality of the lock: it holds for all sampled modes via one route or the other; it is conjectured, not proven, for arbitrary Ξ_drive. We downgrade rather than overclaim a universal no-go.

The last row is the honest escape hatch that is not a pass: as the wall sharpens (σ→∞) the peak negative density ρ̂_min ∝ −σ² diverges, meaning the exoticity is sensitive to physics above the EFT cutoff Λ_c. That routes to UV_DELEGATED — the profile's exoticity is unknown, not absent — and is forbidden from being read as "no exotic matter needed." First failure of L3.8: a finite-σ profile with bounded ρ̂_min can still have σ_exo ≥ 0.5 — bounding the peak does not bound the budget. The integral is not redundant with the peak; both are mandatory report fields, which is exactly why the pack mandates both "peak negative energy density" and "integrated exoticity burden" as separate required outputs.

Maps to the BRL-4 frozen milestone. For a candidate to be a credible EFT_CANDIDATE, the energy-side requirement inside the milestone predicate is: energy AUDIT-visible, no gate FAIL. An AUDIT-clean energy gate (σ_exo=0, E_NEC=0 to tolerance) satisfies it only if the candidate also clears magnitude (E5/L5) and UV (L4) — which no library mode does while delivering a non-trivial S_L. There is therefore no current path from any candidate's energy gate to BRL-4; the honest reading is that the energy gate is the rung most candidates die on, exactly as the contract intends ("most modes should fail; that is good").

But the only route to closing G1's upstream source/energy failure runs straight through all three of these gates — to source ρ_eff < 0 you must declare a field (admissibility re-fires), quantize it (BV re-fires), and reach into the Casimir/moduli/quantum-inequality sector whose global stability is exactly B-UQFC-14-UV-1 (UV re-fires). This leaf is therefore the firewall standing between "G1 has an honest, invariant distance deficit" and any premature claim that the deficit can be made real. It is non-enabling by construction.

A boundary stated once, up front (it governs the entire leaf). This is a classification and audit program over simulated field-content, quantum-status, and UV-dependency objects. Running it does not complete the theory, does not adopt the UV axiom, and is explicitly non-enabling: it provides no instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 04 boundary; CONTRACT §4). It does not provide instructions for building a UV completion, a quantum-gravity reactor, or a vacuum-energy engine — and the workstream that comes closest to that temptation, the UV/vacuum-energy sector, is precisely the one whose terminal verdict is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION on any attempt to engineer rather than merely depend on the open sector.

L4.3 The acceptance test — the three-clause frozen predicate (carried exactly)

The pack states the acceptance test in one sentence, verbatim: "No candidate may reach M1 if the source fit changes the active field list, if an unadopted UV assumption is treated as adopted, or if a BV placeholder is treated as physical-state closure." We carry all three clauses exactly and make each executable. This is the UV/quantum/admissibility analogue of the source ladder's χ_source < 1 predicate: a candidate that trips any of the three does not "almost reach M1" — it is blocked at the tripped clause's token. (M1 is the pack's name for the EFT_CANDIDATE / BRL-4 frozen milestone; §L4.4.)

UV_QUANTUM_ADMISSIBILITY_GATE(candidate Ξ)  ⟺
   (A)  active_field_list_frozen      # the source fit did NOT change C(Ξ); fields frozen before fitting
   AND (B)  no_unadopted_UV_as_adopted   # no UV assumption is treated as adopted without separate, independent review
   AND (C)  no_placeholder_as_closure     # no BV placeholder is treated as interacting physical-state closure
   ⇒  candidate is NOT blocked on the UV/quantum/admissibility axis (may proceed to the rest of the milestone test)
otherwise ⇒ BLOCK at the first violated clause:
   ¬(A) ⇒ FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT   (the fit smuggled or re-entered a field)
   ¬(B) ⇒ FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION                       (adopting B-UQFC-14-UV-1 without review)
   ¬(C) ⇒ FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION / AUDIT_QUANTUM        (a placeholder sold as closure)

Three precision notes the contract forces.

First, clause (A) is the freeze-before-fit discipline, and it is the one most likely to be violated silently. A motivated modeller closing a source ledger will reach for an extra field — and clause (A) makes that move detectable: the active field list is hashed before the fit, and any post-fit component whose π is ∅ (or whose ledger entry double-counts) is the fingerprint of a field changed during fitting. The HC-07 toy proved the stakes in numbers: the smuggled fifth field made ‖ΔT‖ read 8×10⁻⁴ (apparently balanced) while the candidate actually owed 4.1×10⁻² — a ~51× hidden source failure. Clause (A) is the firewall that makes the source gate grade the candidate's real, deduplicated, frozen-inventory content.

Second, clause (B) is the no-spoof rule for the UV axiom. B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is UNADOPTED; clause (B) forbids any verdict that treats it as adopted — i.e. any PASS that depends on global compactification stability without an owner-adopted, independently-reviewed assumption. The HC-08 detector enforces this by routing any internal-sensitive mode (U > τ_UV) to UV_DELEGATED and refusing the lift to PASS except via the named-and-reviewed path. The corpus is explicit that depending on the open sector (UV_DELEGATED) is honest, while engineering it (booking vacuum energy as the drive source, u_F+ = 0.998) is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION.

Third, clause (C) is the placeholder firewall. The bv_master_placeholder.py module is named placeholder by contract; clause (C) forbids any verdict that treats its interacting output as closure. The classifier's step-5 (interacting placeholder ⇒ AUDIT_QUANTUM) is proven to dominate step-6 (PASS_TOY) for any interacting = True mode — that proof is the workstream-B clause "prove placeholders cannot leak false PASS." A candidate whose interacting BRST nilpotency / anomaly-freedom / positivity is assumed but not computed lands in AUDIT_QUANTUM, never PASS_TOY.

First failure (L4.3). The acceptance test fails the instant any of (A)–(C) is treated as satisfied without its artifact: a fit that quietly changed C(Ξ) and was not re-checked (¬A); a UV_DELEGATED verdict quietly upgraded to PASS without the named, reviewed assumption (¬B); or a placeholder BV result read as interacting closure (¬C). Each is a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION-class event, and the test is built so the absence of the artifact is itself the block, not a soft warning.

L4.4 The conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone — and where this leaf sits in it

The single binary the entire ask turns on is the conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone criterion, carried exactly: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." This leaf governs two of the milestone's clauses directly:

  • "NO failed gates" — the admissibility (FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT / FAIL_CHAMBER) and quantum (FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE, including anomaly leak) tokens are hard fails. A candidate carrying any of them cannot satisfy "no failed gates," full stop. Workstream A and the FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE branch of workstream B are therefore milestone-blocking.
  • "a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption" — this is workstream C's terminal deliverable. The milestone does not require the UV question solved; it requires the assumption named (B-UQFC-14-UV-1), published separately, and independently reviewed. Until that review exists, every internal-sensitive candidate is UV_DELEGATED, and a UV_DELEGATED verdict — by itself — does not block the milestone (energy may be AUDIT, UV may be delegated-and-named); it is an unadopted or engineered UV dependence that converts the delegation into a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and blocks it.

The crucial fail-closed reading, carried from the buyer logic: there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." A candidate that fails admissibility, dies FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE, or leans on an unadopted/engineered UV assumption routes — in the pack 10 decision tree — to keep/option screening IP only or theory-only continuation, never to acquisition. The interacting BV sector being a placeholder, and global UV stability being delegated, are precisely the two reasons the milestone is hard and the conversion is gated, not assumed.

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands on all three dimensions (honest reading). On the as-declared G1 object: admissibility is clean (one component δg_xx → d1, single ledger entry, no modulus, A1–A4 PASS_TOY); the quantum ⊗ layer is AUDIT_QUANTUM (vacant — no Q, no |Ψ⟩, "no BRST data"); the UV gate is PASS_TOY (δG_AB = 0, u_c = 0 for all channels, U = 0 ≤ τ_UV). G1 passes this leaf's gates on the as-declared object — and is still killed upstream at source/energy. The leaf's three dimensions become blocking only on the attempted rescue: declaring a field to source ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ re-fires admissibility (is the field in 𝓘_par?) and BV (is it quantizable, anomaly-free, positive-norm?), and reaching the Casimir/moduli/quantum-inequality sector to supply the negative energy re-fires UV (U → 1, UV_DELEGATED, axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED). The leaf is the gate that ensures the rescue cannot be done by sleight of hand.

The lesson the three worked readings carry, in one line: each gate is built to fire on the move that would flatter a candidate — a smuggled field that hides a source failure, an interacting placeholder sold as closure, a modulus runaway that borrows against an open UV question. The dominant verdict is honest refusal, and that refusal is the product.

The leaf's terminal failure is therefore not abstract ("we couldn't close the quantum/UV sector") but localized and mechanical: a candidate is treated as closed while its interacting BRST structure is bv_master_placeholder (→ AUDIT_QUANTUM), or while its S_L depends on an internal channel whose global stability is B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED (→ UV_DELEGATED), or while its field content was changed during the source fit (→ FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE). A second, structural first failure guards this very leaf. A leaf that names the UV assumption and defines the BV master equation risks reading as a recipe to adopt the assumption or complete the quantization — fixed by restating every rung as a delegation-or-audit, never a closure, and by the non-enabling scope boundary (§L4.8): the UV channel that comes closest to "engineer the vacuum" is exactly the one whose verdict is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION on engineering. Predicted dominant verdict for the real library: for modes that fail upstream (source/energy), this leaf's gates are not even reached as clean passes; for the engineered controls, the dominant verdict is the matching FAIL_* / UV_DELEGATED / FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION — which, per CONTRACT §1.6, is the intended outcome.
