L5.0 Why this dimension gets its own leaf, and the one sentence it hangs from

Part L (v2) decomposes the buildability gap map into self-contained closure programs, one per pack document. This leaf expands pack document 05 — the EFT, Backreaction, and Domain Program — whose entire purpose the pack states in a single line we carry verbatim as the leaf's thesis: "Stop local toy success from being mistaken for a controlled effective theory." Every other gate in this document asks whether a candidate does something (is it invariant? is it sourced? is it exotic? is it causal?). This gate asks the subtler question that decides whether any of those answers can be trusted: is the candidate inside the regime where the effective field theory it is written in actually applies? A lobe can be perfectly invariant, perfectly sourced, marginally exotic, and causal — and still be physically meaningless if the curvature, stress, or gradient that produced those answers sits at or above the cutoff Λ, where the truncated S_eff is no longer the right theory and the omitted higher-dimension operators dominate the ones that were kept.

This is the dimension most prone to a specific and seductive self-deception, which the pack names and this leaf is built to defeat. A modeller closes every upstream gate on a small, smooth, well-resolved toy — A = 0.01, σ = 10, a coarse-but-pretty grid — reads off a comfortable χ_max = 0.04, and declares the candidate "EFT-valid." But the productive limit of the same family — the larger amplitude and sharper wall that actually shorten the proper-distance functional — drives χ toward 1, and a coarser grid under-reports every ratio (a violation is local; a coarse grid steps over the hotspot). The honest verdict for the productive object is UV_DELEGATED or FAIL_BACKREACTION; the dishonest verdict is the toy's PASS_TOY smuggled out of its domain. The load-bearing job of this leaf is to make that smuggle mechanically impossible: every EFT pass is bound to a declared domain, a declared cutoff, a declared grid, and a sup-over-domain (never an average) of the ratios — so a pass that is true here cannot be silently read as true there.

These objects are not new to Part L. They are the re-use, at the buildability layer, of the document's executed hard challenge HC-09 (leaves E09a / E09b):

  • HC-09 (EFT cutoff & backreaction) built the four cutoff ratios with their canonical mass-dimension definitions — χ_R = |R|^{1/2}/Λ (Ricci/R² channel), χ_K = |K|^{1/4}/Λ (Kretschmann/Weyl/tidal channel, K = R_μνρσ R^μνρσ), χ_T = |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ (matter-stress channel, |T_eff| = (T_eff^{μν}T_eff_{μν})^{1/2}), and χ_grad = 1/(Λ ℓ_var) (derivative-expansion channel, ℓ_var = min_f |f|/|∂f|) — plus the fifth, separately-named gauge channel χ_F = |F^aF^a|^{1/2}/Λ² used only when a candidate carries gauge content (it is never folded into χ_K). It built the admissibility scalar χ ≡ sup_{x∈D} max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad[, χ_F]) < 1, the cutoff Λ ≤ M_KK ≲ M_Pl (default Λ = M_KK, never the most-permissive Λ = M_Pl), the backreaction object β = max(β_amp, β_dyn) with the perturbative-split criterion β < 1, and proved its negative controls fire — including the coarse-grid cheat (NC-GRID) where coarsening N: 4096 → 256 lowers χ (a fail-open hazard) and is therefore routed to AUDIT (under-resolved), never trusted.

The leaf's load-bearing thesis, stated once: this dimension does not kill the surviving exemplar G1 first — and that is exactly why it is dangerous. On the as-declared small-amplitude G1 object (MID-METRIC-001, A = 0.01, σ = 10), the EFT gate is the candidate's strongest card: χ_R = |R|σ² = 0.0404, χ_K = √K σ² = 0.0286, χ_T = |G_tt|σ² = 0.0202, χ_grad = 0.00858, so χ_max = 0.0404 < 1 with a ~25× margin (J1 §G1 EFT row). G1 dies upstream at the source gate (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, HC-02) with the exotic ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ as physical root cause (HC-03). But the EFT gate passing here is precisely what forbids dismissing G1's energy failure as a cutoff artifact — the exotic stress is demanded inside the EFT's domain of validity, so it is a real demand on a real effective theory, not numerical noise at the edge of the regime. And the only route to making G1 "work" — sharpening the wall and raising the amplitude to deepen the proper-distance deficit — is exactly the move that drives χ → 1 and converts the EFT pass into UV_DELEGATED / FAIL_BACKREACTION. This leaf is therefore the firewall standing between "G1's deficit is real and EFT-valid at this point" and any premature claim that the deficit survives into the regime where it would matter for a mission. It is non-enabling by construction.

A boundary stated once, up front (it governs the entire leaf). This is a classification and audit program over simulated curvature, stress, gradient, and cutoff objects. Running it does not complete the theory, does not adopt the UV axiom, does not supply a cutoff value for any real apparatus, and is explicitly non-enabling: it provides no instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 05 boundary; CONTRACT §4). It computes whether a simulated profile is inside its own declared validity window — and the channel that comes closest to a "make the effect bigger" reading, the productive/sharp-wall limit, is precisely the one whose verdict is FAIL_BACKREACTION / UV_DELEGATED.

Five precision notes the contract and the executed engine force.

First, the gate uses the supremum over the domain, never the average. χ ≡ sup_{x∈D} max(...). This is not a stylistic choice: a cutoff violation is local (a sharp wall, a curvature spike, a sub-grid hotspot), and an average over the lobe hides it — the very mechanism the pack's program exists to prevent. The sup-not-mean rule is the first line of defence against "local toy success mistaken for a controlled EFT."

Second, χ_K is reported separately from χ_R because the Ricci scalar is blind to Weyl (tidal) curvature. A Ricci-flat lobe can carry enormous tidal curvature; χ_R ≈ 0 while χ_K ≈ 1, and only χ_K catches it. This is the curvature analogue of the HC-03 lesson that T_00 alone is blind to off-diagonal stress. Folding χ_K into χ_R would re-open exactly the failure the channel exists to close — so the engine forbids it, and forbids overloading χ_K with the gauge channel χ_F (which carries its own symbol).

Third, χ_source is the L2/HC-02 quantity, imported, not recomputed here. The pack's chi_source = source mismatch / source budget is the source-ledger ratio that L2 owns (the < 1 clause of the frozen BRL-4 milestone, §L5.4). This leaf carries it into χ_max because the EFT gate must see the unmatched-source scale — an unsourced stress is also an operator the truncated theory cannot account for — but it does not re-adjudicate the source match; χ_source ≥ 1 routes to L2's tokens, not L5's. The leaf's own breaches are the four curvature/stress/gradient channels.

Fourth, the cutoff is Λ ≤ M_KK ≲ M_Pl, default Λ = M_KK, and we never assume Λ = M_Pl. Gravity's own EFT cutoff is M_Pl, but the internal-geometry cutoff M_KK (the lightest compactification mode of the frozen parent M4 × K_gauge × F+, K6 = SU(3)/T², S², S¹_Y) is generically far lower and is therefore the binding one. Choosing Λ = M_Pl would be the most permissive and least honest choice — it would make almost everything "EFT-valid." If Λ is unknown for a candidate, the channel is flagged UV_DELEGATED, not given the benefit of the doubt.

Fifth, under-resolution is a fail-open hazard, and is treated as one. A coarse grid steps over local hotspots and under-reports every ratio — it makes a breaching candidate look valid. The engine therefore requires grid.covers(lobe) (else AUDIT("lobe not fully sampled")) and a grid-convergence (Richardson) check; a χ computed on a grid that has not converged is AUDIT (under-resolved), never PASS_TOY. This is the NC-GRID negative control, made load-bearing.

L5.2 The backreaction object and the domain requirements, carried exactly

The pack's program has two further pillars beyond the ratios: a backreaction requirement ("backreaction score below threshold") and a domain requirement (the eight declarations every claim must carry). Both are executed in HC-09 and both are carried here exactly.

L5.2.1 The backreaction object β

The cutoff ratios ask "are the omitted operators sub-leading?" The backreaction object asks the complementary question: "is the perturbative split g = ḡ + δg even valid — does the metric shift the candidate's own stress would induce stay small against the background it was computed on?" A candidate can have all four χ ratios < 1 and still fail here if its first-order shift δg sources a second-order shift of comparable size — the derivative expansion is then not convergent, and the linear analysis that produced every upstream number is invalid.

HC-09 defines the backreaction object in two complementary forms, aggregated as β = max(β_amp, β_dyn):

β_amp = ‖λ_amp · δg₁‖_D / ‖ḡ‖_D                       # amplitude: is the shift small vs the background?
β_dyn = ‖λ_amp² · δg₂‖_D / ‖λ_amp · δg₁‖_D             # dynamic: is the SECOND-order shift small vs the first?
β     = max(β_amp, β_dyn)
gate:   β < 1   (controlled criterion: β ≪ 1)         # β ≥ 1 ⇒ FAIL_BACKREACTION (perturbative split invalid)

β_amp catches a shift that is large in absolute terms; β_dyn catches a shift whose expansion does not converge (a small leading term with an equally-large next term — the most insidious case, because β_amp alone would pass it). The token is FAIL_BACKREACTION: the perturbative split g = ḡ + δg is invalid, so every linearised upstream result is suspect. This is a separate gate from χ: a candidate must satisfy both χ_max < 1 (omitted operators sub-leading) and β < 1 (perturbative split valid) to be EFT-clean on this dimension.

This is the domain-validity certificate — the object that makes a χ_max < 1 pass non-portable. spatial domain D the explicit region the ratios were sup'd over (the lobe and its support) claim made outside D → FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION
time interval the t-window of validity (a quasi-static toy is not a dynamic claim) static result read as dynamic → AUDIT / FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION
chart the coordinate system; invariants are chart-free but grids and sup's are not chart-dependent sup → re-check on second chart (NC-COORD analogue)
tetrad frame the frame in which T_eff, ε, and χ_T are evaluated (frame-invariant magnitudes used) frame-dependent stress number → AUDIT
grid resolution N the sampling N and the Richardson-convergence evidence unconverged / coarse → AUDIT (under-resolved) (NC-GRID; fail-open hazard)
boundary condition how the lobe is closed; boundary effects must be bounded unbounded boundary effect → fails the acceptance test (§L5.3)
excluded regions any region carved out (e.g. a coordinate singularity) and why silent exclusion of a hotspot → FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION
failure if extrapolated the explicit statement of what breaks outside D (e.g. "χ → 1 for A > A*") no extrapolation-failure statement → claim is non-certifiable

The certificate is the anti-smuggle device. A χ_max < 1 verdict is worthless without it, because the verdict is only true on the declared domain, chart, frame, and grid. The certificate is what converts "the toy passed" into "the toy passed here, at this resolution, and breaks thus if you push it there" — which is exactly the pack's purpose. The most common silent failure is the missing grid resolution / Richardson line (a coarse grid that under-reports χ) and the missing failure-if-extrapolated line (a small-amplitude pass quietly carried into the productive limit). Both are AUDIT-or-worse by construction, never PASS_TOY.

L5.3 The acceptance test — the five-clause frozen predicate (carried exactly)

The pack states the acceptance test as a fenced block of five conditions a candidate must meet to reach M1 on this dimension. We carry all five exactly and make each executable. This is the EFT/domain analogue of the source ladder's χ_source < 1 predicate and the UV/quantum/admissibility leaf's three-clause gate (§L4.3): a candidate that trips any clause does not "almost reach M1" — it is blocked at the tripped clause's token. (M1 is the EFT_CANDIDATE / BRL-4 frozen milestone; §L5.4.)

A candidate cannot reach M1 unless:
   chi_max < 1
   domain is declared
   boundary effects are bounded
   backreaction score below threshold
   no hidden extrapolation to mission scale

Made executable, with the clause-by-clause binding and the token each emits:

EFT_DOMAIN_GATE(candidate Ξ, domain D, cutoff Λ, grid N)  ⟺
   (1)  chi_max < 1                 # sup_D max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad,χ_source) < 1, on a CONVERGED grid
   AND (2)  domain_declared          # all 8 certificate fields present (§L5.2.2)
   AND (3)  boundary_effects_bounded # the lobe's boundary contribution is computed and bounded
   AND (4)  beta < threshold         # β = max(β_amp,β_dyn) < 1 (perturbative split valid)
   AND (5)  no_hidden_extrapolation  # the declared domain D actually contains the claimed (mission-relevant) regime
   ⇒  candidate is NOT blocked on the EFT/backreaction/domain axis
otherwise ⇒ BLOCK at the first violated clause:
   ¬(1) ⇒ FAIL_BACKREACTION / UV_DELEGATED   (first-breaching χ channel; UV_DELEGATED if Λ unknown)
   ¬(2) ⇒ claim non-certifiable               (missing domain certificate)
   ¬(3) ⇒ FAIL_BACKREACTION                   (boundary leak)
   ¬(4) ⇒ FAIL_BACKREACTION                   (perturbative split invalid)
   ¬(5) ⇒ FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION           (toy validity smuggled to mission scale)

Five precision notes the contract forces.

First, clause (1) chi_max < 1 must be computed on a converged grid, or it is not computed at all. The NC-GRID negative control proved that coarsening N: 4096 → 256 lowers the ratios (the coarse run read χ ≈ 0.19–0.31 where the fine run breached) — a fail-open hazard. So clause (1) is satisfied only when the Richardson-convergence check passes; an unconverged χ_max < 1 is AUDIT (under-resolved), which does not satisfy clause (1). This is the single clause most likely to be gamed by a hurried modeller, and the engine refuses it by default.

Second, clause (2) domain declared is a hard structural requirement, not a courtesy. A χ_max < 1 with no domain certificate is non-certifiable — there is no claim, because there is no statement of where the claim holds. The certificate's eight fields are checked for presence before the ratio is even read.

Third, clause (3) boundary effects bounded guards the lobe's edge. A forward/back-asymmetric lobe is closed by some boundary condition; if the boundary contributes an unbounded stress or curvature (a hard edge, a discontinuous wall), the sup_D is dominated by an artifact and the result is FAIL_BACKREACTION. The boundary contribution must be computed and shown bounded, not assumed away.

Fourth, clause (4) backreaction below threshold is the β < 1 gate of §L5.2.1, and it is independent of χ. A candidate can pass all four χ channels and still fail clause (4) if its second-order shift δg₂ is comparable to its first-order δg₁ (β_dyn ≥ 1). The derivative expansion is then not convergent and the linear analysis is void.

Fifth, clause (5) no hidden extrapolation to mission scale is the clause that makes this whole leaf a buildability gate and not merely an EFT bookkeeping check. It forbids the exact move the pack's thesis targets: a χ_max < 1 proven on a small, lab-scale, sub-cutoff toy read as if it licensed a mission-scale effect. The certificate's "failure if extrapolated" field is its evidence: if the declared domain D does not contain the regime in which the candidate is claimed to matter (e.g. the amplitude/wall-sharpness that would actually shorten a transit), the claim is FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION. This is the EFT-axis instance of the mission-overclaim watermark (HC-10 / FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM): a validity proven here may not be plotted there.

First failure (L5.3). The acceptance test fails the instant any of clauses (1)–(5) is treated as satisfied without its artifact: a χ_max read off an unconverged grid (¬1); a pass with no domain certificate (¬2); an unbounded boundary swept under the lobe (¬3); a β ≥ 1 ignored because χ looked clean (¬4); or — the headline failure of this leaf — a small-amplitude PASS_TOY carried, undeclared, to mission scale (¬5). Each is a FAIL_BACKREACTION / FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION-class event, and the test is built so the absence of the artifact (the convergence evidence, the certificate, the bounded-boundary computation, the extrapolation-failure statement) is itself the block, not a soft warning.

L5.4 The conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone — and where this leaf sits in it

The single binary the entire ask turns on is the conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone criterion, carried exactly: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." This leaf governs two of the milestone's clauses directly and conditions a third:

  • "NO failed gates" — FAIL_BACKREACTION (any of the four χ channels ≥ 1, an unbounded boundary, or β ≥ 1) and FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION (a hidden extrapolation to mission scale) are hard fails. A candidate carrying either cannot satisfy "no failed gates," full stop. The EFT/backreaction/domain gate is therefore milestone-blocking on its hard-fail branch.
  • chi_max < 1 over the declared domain — the M1 predicate carries this clause verbatim (EFT/backreaction chi_max < 1 over declared domain, L1 §L1.3). This leaf owns that clause. The milestone does not ask for χ_max < 1 everywhere; it asks for it over a declared domain that contains the claimed regime — which is clauses (1)+(2)+(5) of the acceptance test fused into the milestone. A pass on an undeclared or extrapolated domain does not satisfy the milestone clause.
  • It conditions the UV clause. When a χ channel breaches because the cutoff Λ = M_KK is unknown or the lobe lives in a compactification modulus, the verdict is UV_DELEGATED, and the milestone's "NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption" clause (owned by L4) becomes the only path forward. The EFT gate is where the need for that named UV assumption is detected (a productive-limit χ → 1 driven by internal geometry); L4 is where the assumption is named and reviewed. The two leaves hand off here.

The crucial fail-closed reading, carried from the buyer logic: there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." A candidate that fails the EFT gate (FAIL_BACKREACTION), smuggles its validity to mission scale (FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION), or leans on an unknown cutoff (UV_DELEGATED) routes — in the pack 10 decision tree — to keep/option screening IP only or theory-only continuation, never to acquisition. "Stop local toy success from being mistaken for a controlled effective theory" is precisely the reason the milestone is hard on this axis and the conversion is gated, not assumed.

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands on this dimension (honest reading). On the as-declared small-amplitude G1 object (MID-METRIC-001, A = 0.01, σ = 10, the metric g_xx = 1 − A e^{−x²/2σ²}): the EFT gate is PASS_TOY and is G1's best card. The four ratios, recomputed and verified (J1 §G1, VER-modes report):

# and is corrected here to the curvature-over-cutoff² form that does.
χ_R    = |R|/Λ²   with |R| = |−4.0404×10⁻⁴|, Λ = 1/σ      ⇒  χ_R = |R|σ²   = 0.0404
χ_K    = √K/Λ²    with K = 8.1624×10⁻⁸                     ⇒  χ_K = √K σ²   = 0.0286
χ_T    = |G_tt|/Λ²  with |G_tt| = 2.0202×10⁻⁴              ⇒  χ_T = |G_tt|σ² = 0.0202
χ_grad = 1/(Λ ℓ_var)                                       ⇒  χ_grad       = 0.00858

G1 passes this leaf's gate on the as-declared object — at a comfortable 25× margin — and is still killed upstream at source/energy. Two honest consequences follow, and the leaf insists on both. (i) The EFT pass strengthens, not weakens, G1's death: because χ_max < 1 holds at this point, the exotic source ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ is demanded inside the EFT's validity window, so the FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC / exotic-energy verdict cannot be dismissed as a trans-cutoff artifact — it is a real demand on a controlled effective theory. (ii) The pass is non-portable: it holds for A = 0.01, σ = 10 and breaks in the productive limit. The proper-distance deficit scales with amplitude and wall-sharpness, so the useful G1 (the one that would shorten a transit) has larger A and smaller σ, driving χ → 1 — at which point the verdict is UV_DELEGATED (cutoff approached) or FAIL_BACKREACTION (cutoff breached). The leaf records this as G1's extrapolation-failure certificate field: failure_if_extrapolated: χ_max → 1 as A → A*(σ); the small-amplitude EFT pass does NOT survive to the productive regime. The leaf is the gate that ensures this non-portability cannot be hidden by quoting the comfortable small-amplitude number out of its domain.

L5.5 Worked readings — the program answering, on toy and control numbers

So the reader sees the program answering and not deflecting, here are the engine's behaviours on its canonical objects, with explicit numbers carried from the executed HC-09 machinery.

(1) The minimal scalar/metric toy — PASS_TOY on the declared domain. The small-amplitude conformal/Gaussian contraction toy at A = 0.01, σ = 10, sampled on a converged grid: all four channels small (χ_R = 0.0404, χ_K = 0.0286, χ_T = 0.0202, χ_grad = 0.00858), χ_max = 0.0404 < 1, β < 1, domain certificate complete with failure_if_extrapolated stated. Verdict PASS_TOY — and the status line says so explicitly: "EFT-valid at Λ = M_KK on the sampled domain D at A = 0.01, σ = 10 only; not global; breaks for A > A*." The pass is the floor, scoped to its domain, not the ceiling.

(2) The productive limit — the same family, pushed. Increase A and sharpen the wall (decrease σ) to deepen the proper-distance deficit. χ_grad = 1/(Λ ℓ_var) rises first (the wall is where ℓ_var = |f|/|∂f| collapses), then χ_R, χ_K as curvature concentrates. At the amplitude/sharpness where the deficit becomes mission-interesting, χ_max → 1. Verdict: UV_DELEGATED as χ approaches 1 with Λ = M_KK (the candidate now probes the cutoff, and global stability of the internal geometry is B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED), escalating to FAIL_BACKREACTION once χ_max ≥ 1 or β ≥ 1. This is the central worked lesson: the EFT pass and the useful effect live in different regimes, and the gate refuses to let the first vouch for the second.

cutoff_ratios(invariants, Λ, grid, lobe):
  require grid.covers(lobe)        else AUDIT("lobe not fully sampled — ratios incomplete")
  require richardson_converged(grid) else AUDIT("under-resolved — χ under-reported, NOT trusted")  # NC-GRID
  χ_R = sup_lobe |R|^{1/2}/Λ ;  χ_K = sup_lobe |K|^{1/4}/Λ
  χ_T = sup_lobe |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ ; χ_grad = sup_lobe 1/(Λ·ℓ_var)
  χ_max = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad, χ_source)
  if χ_max ≥ 1:  return FAIL_BACKREACTION(channel = argmax)        # or UV_DELEGATED if Λ unknown
  return PASS_TOY(domain = D, Λ = Λ, grid = N, extrapolation_failure = stated)

(3) The coarse-grid cheat — NC-GRID, the fail-open hazard caught. Take a candidate that breaches on a fine grid and coarsen it: N: 4096 → 256. The coarse run reads χ ≈ 0.19–0.31 (apparently valid) where the fine run breached — because the coarse grid steps over the local hotspot and the sup misses it. Verdict: AUDIT (under-resolved), never PASS_TOY. The engine requires grid.covers(lobe) and Richardson convergence; a χ from an unconverged grid is flagged and not trusted. The lesson: under-resolution is the one numerical error that flatters a candidate (lowers χ), so the gate treats a coarse pass as a non-pass by default. This is why the domain certificate's grid-resolution field is load-bearing.

(4) The Weyl-huge / Ricci-flat control — why χ_K is separate. A lobe tuned so R ≈ 0 (Ricci-small) but R_μνρσ R^μνρσ large (tidal-huge): χ_R ≈ 0 (would pass a Ricci-only gate) but χ_K ≈ 1 (breaches). Verdict: FAIL_BACKREACTION on the χ_K channel. The lesson: a single curvature scalar is blind; reporting χ_R and χ_K separately is what catches the tidal trans-cutoff lobe a naive observer would call valid.

(5) The backreaction control — χ clean, β dirty. A candidate with all four χ channels < 1 but a second-order shift δg₂ comparable to its first-order δg₁: β_amp < 1 (the shift looks small) but β_dyn = ‖λ²δg₂‖/‖λδg₁‖ ≥ 1 (the expansion does not converge). Verdict: FAIL_BACKREACTION (perturbative split invalid). The lesson: χ < 1 is necessary but not sufficient; the β_dyn channel catches the candidate whose linearisation is self-undermining even though every ratio looks comfortable.

The lesson the five worked readings carry, in one line: each check is built to fire on the move that would flatter a candidate — quoting a small-amplitude pass out of its domain, coarsening the grid to lower χ, hiding tidal curvature behind a small Ricci scalar, or trusting a first-order shift whose second order is just as big. The dominant verdict is honest refusal, and that refusal — "this is valid here and breaks there, with the breakage named" — is the product.

The chapter's named first failure is the pack 05 thesis reused as a buildability gate. The pack states it exactly: "Stop local toy success from being mistaken for a controlled effective theory." The leaf's terminal failure is therefore not abstract ("we couldn't prove EFT validity globally") but localized and mechanical: a candidate is treated as EFT-valid while a curvature/stress/gradient channel breaches the cutoff (χ ≥ 1 → FAIL_BACKREACTION), or while its perturbative split is invalid (β ≥ 1 → FAIL_BACKREACTION), or while its small-amplitude pass is carried out of its declared domain to mission scale (FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION), or while its cutoff is unknown (UV_DELEGATED). The standing negative controls — the productive-limit χ → 1, the coarse-grid NC-GRID cheat, the Weyl-huge/Ricci-flat lobe, the β_dyn-divergent split — are the corpus's calibration that the gate fires as built.

A second, structural first failure guards this very leaf. A leaf that gives the cutoff Λ = M_KK and the four ratios risks reading as a recipe to tune a candidate just under the cutoff — i.e. as engineering advice. It is fixed by (a) the sup-not-average rule and the converged-grid requirement, which make "just under the cutoff" undetectable-by-cheating impossible to fake; (b) the FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION clause, which forbids carrying a sub-cutoff toy to mission scale even if it passes; and (c) the non-enabling scope boundary (§L5.8), which supplies no real cutoff value for any real apparatus and no hardware. Predicted dominant verdict for the real library: for modes that fail upstream (source/energy), this leaf's gate is often the candidate's strongest card (a clean small-amplitude χ_max < 1, as for G1) — which the leaf uses to strengthen the upstream verdict (the exotic demand is EFT-real), never to rescue it; for the productive limits and engineered controls, the dominant verdict is FAIL_BACKREACTION / UV_DELEGATED / AUDIT (under-resolved) / FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION — which, per CONTRACT §1.6, is the intended outcome.

L5.8 Where this leaf sits in the funded sprint and the buyer logic

The EFT/backreaction/domain program is exercised across Phase 5 (EFT / cutoff / backreaction audit) of the 90-day hostile validation sprint, immediately downstream of the source + energy audit (Phase 3) and the gauge/BRST/UV audit (Phase 4) — because a χ_max < 1 is only meaningful once the candidate has a real, deduplicated, sourced T_eff and a named cutoff to compare against. It is also the lower-reasoning-agent backlog task whose acceptance test is itself a failure demand: the EFT check passes the small toy by binding it to its domain and breaks the productive object by catching χ → 1; the grid check passes by refusing an unconverged χ; the extrapolation check passes by forbidding the mission-scale smuggle. For the productive limits and engineered controls, each does fire its token — that passing-by-failing is the product.

The buyer logic this leaf must never weaken: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. Applied to this axis: a buyer's first move on any exotic-propulsion claim — this document's or a competitor's — is "show me that your effect is EFT-valid in the regime where you claim it matters, on a converged grid, with the cutoff named, and with the failure-if-extrapolated stated — not a comfortable small-amplitude number quoted out of its domain." This leaf is that move, automated and IP-protected. Even the expected outcome — candidates pass the EFT gate only at small amplitude and breach it (FAIL_BACKREACTION / UV_DELEGATED) in the productive limit, with the coarse-grid cheat caught (AUDIT) and the extrapolation blocked (FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION) — leaves a strategic acquirer owning a rigorous EFT-validity discriminator and its negative-control corpus. A candidate that breaches the cutoff in its useful regime, fails the perturbative split, or smuggles its validity to mission scale routes to keep/option the screening IP or theory-only continuation, never to acquisition — and the expected outcome may still be that every candidate fails while a strategic acquirer retains a useful IP-protected screening platform.

L5.9 Scope boundary (restated, non-negotiable)

This leaf is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap for the EFT, backreaction, and domain dimension. It is not a hardware-construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 05; CONTRACT §4). It specifies no real cutoff value for any real apparatus, no UV completion, and no "tune the candidate just under the cutoff" recipe — the sup-not-average rule, the converged-grid requirement, and the FAIL_DOMAIN_EXTRAPOLATION clause together make a cutoff-tuned, mission-extrapolated pass impossible to fake, and the channel that comes closest to an engineering reading — the productive/sharp-wall limit — is precisely the one whose verdict is FAIL_BACKREACTION / UV_DELEGATED. The current manuscript ceiling remains PASS_TOY. The EFT gate is not global: it certifies validity only on a declared domain, chart, frame, and converged grid, with the failure-if-extrapolated explicitly stated; an unknown cutoff or a modulus-resident lobe is delegated (UV_DELEGATED, B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED, Gap-04 OPEN, handed to L4). No rung of this ladder past its current standing has been crossed by any mode: the deepest-surviving exemplar (G1) passes the as-declared small-amplitude EFT gate (χ_max = 0.0404 < 1, ~25× margin) — its strongest card — and is killed upstream at source and energy, while the useful (productive-limit) G1 breaches the cutoff. The platform is a discriminator/screening tool, NOT a Mars spaceship. L6 — Observability & Lab-Proxy Program

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED (ceiling PASS_TOY; this is a Part-L v2 buildability sub-ladder leaf — it promotes no candidate, defines no apparatus, and presents no new measured datum; it formalizes the observable ladder O0→O7, the required observability packet, and the null-controlled acceptance test by which the observability dimension must climb the buildability ladder, and it reuses the executed HC-01 / HC-04 / HC-05 / HC-10 invariant, causality, gauge, and local-vs-global machinery as the gate behind each observable) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · Buildability standing: approximately BRL-2 (validated negative-control corpus), with a concrete path to test for BRL-4 — and this leaf governs the dimension whose first physical rung is BRL-6 (lab-observable proxy), the earliest place a simulated candidate could touch a bench. · Scope: gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap for the observability / lab-proxy dimension; NOT a hardware-construction manual. The core discipline of this leaf, carried verbatim from the pack: "Define what would need to be observed before a physical research program is justified" — observability is the gate that stands between a status-labeled simulation result and any claim that something is, or could be, measured.

L6.0 Why observability is a separate closure dimension, and the one sentence it hangs from

Part L (v2) decomposes the buildability gap map into self-contained closure programs, one per pack document. This leaf expands pack document 06 — the Observability and Lab-Proxy Program — whose purpose the pack states in a single line we carry verbatim: "Define what would need to be observed before a physical research program is justified." That sentence is the entire load of the leaf. Every other closure dimension in Part L (source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT, controls) grades a candidate inside the simulator — it asks whether the candidate is internally honest. Observability is the dimension that asks the orthogonal, and harder, question: if this candidate were real, what would a detector see, how would we tell that signal from a coordinate artifact or from noise, and could an independent party reproduce that simulated observable before anyone is asked to fund a bench? It is the bridge dimension — the first one whose terminal rungs (O5, O6, O7) live outside the simulator entirely — and so it is the dimension most prone to the single failure mode this whole document exists to refuse: mistaking a number that moved in a chart for a thing that could be measured.

The leaf's load-bearing thesis, stated once: observability does not rescue a candidate that has already died upstream — it is the gate that prevents a candidate from appearing observable when the only thing that moved was the gauge. The observable ladder is built so that the very first non-trivial rung (O1, invariant scalar) is already a coordinate-invariance gate, and the explicit coordinate-only negative control in the required packet (pack 06: "coordinate-only signal fails") is the standing calibration that the ladder fires as built. This re-uses, at the buildability layer, four of the document's executed hard challenges:

  • HC-01 (invariant proper-distance functional) computed T_eff from any metric as a demand quantity and produced the invariant scalar S_L (the forward proper-distance functional) and its toy values — S_L = 9.8×10⁻⁵ at E₀D² = 9×10⁻³ for the HC-01 lobe, reproduced by the verifier to displayed precision. Every O1 observable is, in the first instance, an invariant built the way S_L is built: from curvature/stress invariants, never from raw chart components.
  • HC-04 (causality veto) built the global-hyperbolicity / closed-timelike-curve veto whose semantics the verifier confirmed: "causality can only withhold, never grant; the mission-overlay runs HC-04 first and voids ALL distance claims on a single FAIL point." An observable that requires a causality-violating configuration to register is FAIL_CAUSALITY before it is ever a "signal."
  • HC-05 (gauge invariance of the linearized observables) proved δR[£_ξḡ] = 0 and the two-key gauge classifier (rejection requires both small residual and vanishing invariants). This is the machinery behind the coordinate-only negative control: a δg that is pure gauge produces zero change in every O1 invariant, so a candidate whose "signal" survives only in chart components is caught at O1 as FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY / FAIL_PURE_GAUGE.
  • HC-10 (local-vs-global firewall) proved — corpus-agnostically — that a local comoving arc-length differential ΔD_local is not and does not integrate into a global travel-time cut Δt_global; the forbidden contraction T = T_baseline(1 − ⟨S_L⟩) is a non-law. This is the firewall that caps the observable ladder: an O1–O4 simulated observable, even if real, is a local frame-relative quantity, and the ladder forbids reading it as a flight-relevant (O7) or mission-relevant observable without the separate, currently-open, congruence-level closure.

These four are not new to Part L. They are the reuse, at the observability layer, of the invariant, causality, gauge, and firewall gates already executed and verified. The leaf is therefore the firewall standing between "G1 has an honest, invariant proper-distance deficit S_L" and any premature claim that the deficit is observable — let alone measured, let alone flight-relevant. It is non-enabling by construction.

A boundary stated once, up front (it governs the entire leaf), carried verbatim from the pack 06. "This is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap. It is not a hardware construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware." The observability program is a specification of what would need to be observed and how a claimed observation would be null-controlled — it is not a sensor build, an interferometer design, a beam-line layout, or a flight-instrument spec. The rungs O5 (non-flight lab proxy), O6 (independent lab reproduction), and O7 (flight-relevant observable) are named as requirements with closure criteria and first-failure tokens; they are explicitly not built here, and the pack's closing line is the ceiling: "Current ceiling remains PASS_TOY. A buildable Mars-spacecraft program requires independent closure of source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT, controls, observability, safety, certification, and mission-integration gates."

L6.3 The acceptance test — the four-clause null-controlled predicate (carried exactly)

The pack states the acceptance test as four lines, verbatim:

target signal above threshold
null control below threshold
coordinate-only signal fails
independent reviewer can reproduce simulated observable

We carry all four clauses exactly and make each executable. This is the observability analogue of the EFT leaf's chi_max < 1 predicate and the source ladder's chi_source < 1: a candidate that fails any clause does not "almost reach O4" — it is blocked at the failed clause's token. (O4 is the highest rung this program builds; reaching it is the precondition the pack 06 purpose sentence calls "justified" for a physical program, and is the trigger for the IP-4 observability CIP.)

OBSERVABILITY_GATE(candidate Ξ, packet P)  ⟺
   (1) signal(P.target)      >  P.threshold          # the predicted observable clears the false-positive floor
   AND (2) signal(P.null)     <  P.threshold          # the matched null (vacuum/flat) reads below threshold
   AND (3) signal(P.coord)    <  P.threshold          # the PURE-GAUGE / coordinate-only control reads null
   AND (4) reproducible(P)                            # an independent reviewer reproduces the SIMULATED observable
   ⇒  candidate is NOT blocked on the observability axis (the O4 simulated-sensor rung is honestly reached)
otherwise ⇒ BLOCK at the first violated clause:
   ¬(1) ⇒ FAIL_NO_SIGNAL          (nothing rises above the noise floor)
   ¬(2) ⇒ FAIL_NO_NULL            (the "off" state already reads as signal — the observable is mis-baselined)
   ¬(3) ⇒ FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY    (the signal was pure gauge — HC-05 invariant is identically zero)
   ¬(4) ⇒ FAIL_IRREPRODUCIBLE     (the simulated observable cannot be independently regenerated)

Four precision notes the contract forces.

First, clause (3) is the load-bearing one, and it is the gate HC-05 already enforces. A motivated modeller can always exhibit a δg whose chart components move — that is trivial, since a coordinate transformation moves chart components by construction. Clause (3) demands that the observable be built from a coordinate invariant (an O1 scalar), so that a pure-gauge transform δg = £_ξ ḡ produces δR[£_ξḡ] = 0 exactly (HC-05, verifier-confirmed as a textbook GR identity). The standing coordinate-only controls — the tanh-squeeze and Rindler "flat-in-disguise" backgrounds that HC-01/HC-05 use — read null under an honest O1 observable and non-null under a chart-component pseudo-observable. Clause (3) is the firewall that makes the observability gate grade the candidate's invariant content, not its coordinate dressing. It is the same discipline the source leaf uses to refuse FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY metrics; here it refuses FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY signals.

Second, clause (2) guards against a mis-baselined observable. It is not enough that the signal is large; the matched null (the same observable computed on the vacuum/flat background) must read below threshold. If the null already reads as signal, the observable is mis-baselined — it is measuring the background, not the candidate. The HC-05 flat-background δR = 0 result is the canonical null: on flat space the linearized curvature invariants vanish, so an honest observable returns its null value there.

Third, clause (4) is reproduction of the simulated observable — not a physical measurement. This is the clause that keeps the entire ladder on the software side of the O4/O5 line. The pack is precise: "independent reviewer can reproduce simulated observable." Clause (4) is satisfied when a second party, given the published packet (fields 1–7) and the platform code, regenerates the same target/null/coordinate-only readings — it does not require a bench, a detector, or any physical reproduction (that is O6, a separate rung). This is exactly the BRL-5 independent hostile physics audit applied to the observability dimension: the audit reruns the simulated observable, not an experiment.

Fourth, the acceptance test certifies O4, not reality. Passing all four clauses means the candidate has a null-controlled, gauge-clean, reproducible simulated observable — the artifact that justifies considering a physical program (the pack's word). It does not mean the candidate is real, observable in a lab, or flight-relevant; those are O5/O6/O7, each gated separately. First failure (L6.3). The test fails the instant any clause is treated as satisfied without its artifact: a target read off a chart component (¬3), a null that already reads hot (¬2), a threshold pulled after seeing the signal (¬1, an FAIL_UNDEFINED_THRESHOLD-class violation), or a packet a second party cannot rerun (¬4). Each is a fail-closed block at the first violated clause, and the test is built so the absence of the artifact is the block.
