L7.0 Why the controls dimension is the most dangerous one to build, and the one sentence that disarms it

Part L (v2) decomposes the buildability gap map into self-contained closure programs, one per pack document. This leaf expands pack document 07 — the Control, Tolerance, and Digital-Twin Program — whose purpose the pack states in one line: "Move from static screening to a simulated gate-supervised control environment." Every other Part-L program audits a candidate as declared and frozen. This one is different in kind: it introduces an optimizer — a loop that is allowed to change the candidate (lobe center, width, amplitude, comoving phase) in pursuit of an objective. That is precisely the move that turns a fail-closed screening tool into a wish-fulfilment machine, because an optimizer with the wrong objective will learn to evade the gates — it will discover the coordinate transformation, the smuggled field, the modulus runaway, or the cutoff-straddling lobe shape that makes a gate read green while the underlying physics is exactly as broken as before. The single sentence that disarms the danger, carried verbatim from the pack's control objective, is the hard floor:

hard gate failure -> objective = -infinity

An objective that returns −∞ on any hard gate failure cannot be climbed by evasion: there is no gradient out of a failed gate, only a wall. The optimizer is therefore structurally forbidden from "optimizing through failed physics gates" (pack 07, Objective) — its only legal moves are within the region where every physics gate already passes, and its only legal discovery is the boundary of that region, i.e. the tolerance envelope and the first-failure surface. This is the controls analogue of the fail-closed discipline that governs the whole manuscript (CONTRACT §1): the twin does not promote; it maps where promotion is impossible.

These dimensions are not new to Part L. The control loop is the re-use, at the buildability layer, of the document's entire executed gate ladder — the controller does not invent new physics gates, it wires the existing ones in as the supervisor:

  • HC-01 (invariant distance) supplies the benefit term: the forward proper-distance functional S_L[Ξ] whose coordinate-invariant reduction is the only thing the objective is allowed to reward — and only after HC-01's coordinate-only negative control (NC-COORD) has confirmed the reduction is not a chart artifact (token FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY).
  • HC-02 (source) / HC-03 (energy) supply the source penalty and energy burden: the source mismatch χ_source and the exoticity/energy ledger. On the worked exemplar G1 (MID-METRIC-001) these are exactly the gates that fire — FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC with root-cause exotic ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ (HC-03) — so for G1 the controller's objective is already −∞ before any optimization begins.
  • HC-04 (causality) supplies the causality margin: the cone/horizon/CTC veto that gates all mission claims. A negative causality margin is a hard gate failure → −∞.
  • HC-05 (gauge) supplies the two-sided pure-gauge guard: a "benefit" that is pure diffeomorphism (FAIL_PURE_GAUGE) is not a benefit and scores zero.
  • HC-06/07/08 (quantum / admissibility / UV) supply the firewall L4 governs: a control move that changes the active field list re-fires admissibility (FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT), the interacting sector stays AUDIT_QUANTUM, and an internal-sensitive lobe routes to UV_DELEGATED.
  • HC-09 (EFT/backreaction) supplies the UV/EFT penalty: the cutoff ratio χ_max = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad, χ_source); χ_max ≥ 1 is a hard gate failure (FAIL_BACKREACTION / UV_DELEGATED).
  • HC-10 (Mars relevance) supplies the validity weight on the benefit and the watermark/overlay discipline (FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM) that L8 governs, enforcing G3's no-global-aggregation theorem inside the loop.

The leaf's load-bearing thesis, stated once: the digital twin is a supervised search whose supervisor is the already-executed gate ladder, and whose objective is built so that the only thing it can legally maximize is a validity-weighted, gate-clean, invariant proper-distance benefit — with a −∞ wall at every hard gate. It cannot, by construction, climb a candidate past PASS_TOY; it can only characterize the basin in which a candidate is gate-clean (if any) and map the first-failure surface that bounds it. For G1, that basin is empty — the source/energy gates fail at the center of the parameter box — so the twin's honest deliverable on G1 is a tolerance map of how it fails, not a trajectory that makes it work.

A boundary stated once, up front (it governs the entire leaf). This is a simulation and audit program over a simulated control loop driving a simulated candidate profile against the already-computed physics gates. Running it does not build a controller, does not actuate any field, and is explicitly non-enabling: it provides no instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 07 boundary; CONTRACT §4). The pack states the boundary in its own words, carried verbatim: "This is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap. It is not a hardware construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware." There is no actuator model, no power schedule, no field-generation method, and no flight-control law in this leaf — only the software supervisor that decides, on a candidate the rest of the document has already screened, whether a control move is even allowed.

L7.1 The objective, the control variables, and the eight gate-coupled terms — carried exactly

The pack gives the program as an objective, a control-variable list, a digital-twin ladder, and an IP action. We carry every clause exactly, expand each into a closure criterion and a named first-failure / downgrade token, and tie each to its executed HC machinery and to the BRL/IP ladders the program advances.

The control variables (pack 07, "Control variables"), verbatim and mapped

The pack lists eight control variables. The first four are actuated (the optimizer may set them); the last four are measured/penalized (gate outputs the optimizer must respect, never overwrite). The distinction is the spine of the whole design: the loop may steer the lobe; it may never steer the gate.

Pack control variable Role Bound to What it means in the loop
lobe center x_c actuated HC-01 geometry of Ξ_drive(t,x) where along the comoving frame the forward lobe sits
lobe width σ actuated HC-01 / HC-09 (χ_grad ∝ 1/σ) the lobe's spatial scale; narrower → larger gradients → higher χ
lobe amplitude A actuated HC-01 benefit / HC-03 exoticity the depth of the metric perturbation; larger → larger benefit and larger |ρ_eff|
phase / comoving lock φ actuated vehicle-frame tracking (this leaf, §L7.3) the front/back-asymmetric phase relative to the vehicle frame
source mismatch χ_source measured (penalty) HC-02 SourceMatchReport how far the candidate's T_eff is from a matched source ledger
energy burden measured (penalty) HC-03 exoticity ledger the magnitude and sign of the required stress-energy (negative ⇒ exotic)
causality margin measured (penalty/veto) HC-04 cone/horizon/CTC audit distance to the nearest causality violation; negative ⇒ hard veto
EFT margin measured (penalty/veto) HC-09 1 − χ_max distance to the cutoff; χ_max ≥ 1 ⇒ hard veto

The asymmetry is enforced mechanically: the four actuated variables are inputs to the candidate constructor; the four measured variables are outputs of frozen gate code that the objective reads but the optimizer cannot write. There is no API by which the optimizer sets χ_source; it can only set (x_c, σ, A, φ) and observe what χ_source the resulting candidate incurs. This is the controls-layer expression of CONTRACT §1.4 ("an agent may never move a candidate up the ladder on its own authority"): the controller may move the lobe, but the grading of the lobe is owned by the frozen gate ladder.

The control objective (pack 07), verbatim and made executable

The pack states the objective as:

maximize validity_weighted_benefit
minus source penalty
minus energy penalty
minus causality penalty
minus UV/EFT penalty
hard gate failure -> objective = -infinity

We render it as a single fail-closed functional, every term tied to a gate:

J(x_c, σ, A, φ) =
    w_val · B_inv(Ξ)                      # HC-01 invariant benefit × HC-10 validity weight
  − λ_S · penalty_source(χ_source)        # HC-02 source mismatch
  − λ_E · penalty_energy(exoticity)       # HC-03 energy burden / exoticity
  − λ_C · penalty_causal(margin_C)        # HC-04 causality margin
  − λ_U · penalty_eft(χ_max)              # HC-09 UV/EFT cutoff margin
  subject to the HARD WALL:
    if any hard_gate(Ξ) == FAIL:  J = −∞   # source/causality/gauge FAIL, χ_max≥1, anomaly leak, admissibility FAIL

with the four ingredients fixed by frozen gate code:

  • B_inv(Ξ) = max(0, −ΔS_L^{inv}(Ξ)) — the coordinate-invariant forward proper-distance reduction from HC-01, floored at zero and only after NC-COORD passes (a coordinate-only reduction contributes 0, not benefit). Carried from G1: the invariant deficit is 0.0884 (analytic 0.0886), χ_R = 0.0404 — a real, invariant number, which is exactly why G1 is the deepest-surviving exemplar and not why it passes.
  • w_val ∈ [0,1] — the HC-10 validity weight: the product of per-gate validity factors, so that a benefit earned in a region where a gate is marginal is discounted, and a benefit that requires global aggregation is forbidden (G3). Carried from G3: ceilings W_max(no-UV) = 0.50, W_max(UV) = 0.15; a toy S_L^W lands in [0.045, 0.090]. The weight can drive w_val → 0 but never negative.
  • penalty_*(·) — monotone-increasing soft penalties on the graded-but-not-failed region (e.g. a positive but small causality margin, an AUDIT-visible energy burden, a χ_max below but approaching 1).
  • the hard wall — the non-negotiable −∞ on any hard gate FAIL. This is the term that makes the objective fail-closed.

Three precision notes the contract forces on the objective.

First, energy_check is never a clean PASS, so the energy term is always a penalty, never a reward. Per CONTRACT §3 and the G1/G2/G3 verification, energy_check is "pass / audit-visible" — there is no configuration in which expending exotic energy adds to the objective. The optimizer cannot "spend its way" to a higher score; every unit of exoticity is a cost. This is why a controller cannot launder FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY into benefit: the energy ledger is a subtrahend by construction.

Second, the benefit is floored at zero and gated on invariance, so a coordinate trick scores nothing. B_inv = max(0, −ΔS_L^{inv}) with the NC-COORD precondition means a pure-coordinate "reduction" (which HC-01 flags FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY) yields B_inv = 0, and a pure-gauge benefit (HC-05 FAIL_PURE_GAUGE) is a hard wall. The optimizer therefore gains nothing from the two cheapest evasions (coordinate relabeling, gauge transformation) — the very evasions an unsupervised optimizer would find first.

Third, the hard wall dominates every soft term. No finite combination of large w_val·B_inv and small penalties can lift J above −∞ when a hard gate fails. This is the controls-layer statement of "fail-closed": the objective is lexicographic — first every hard gate must pass; only then is the soft trade-off w_val·B_inv − Σλ·penalty even evaluated. For G1, the source/energy hard gates fail, so J(G1) = −∞ everywhere in the box, and the twin's honest output is the failure surface, not an extremum.

First failure (L7.1). The objective fails the instant any hard-gate output is read as a soft, tradeable penalty rather than a wall — i.e. the instant −∞ is replaced by "a large but finite negative number" that a big enough benefit could overcome. That single softening (−∞ → −M) is the entire failure mode of the whole program: it would let the optimizer buy its way past a failed source, causality, or cutoff gate. Token: FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (the loop promoted a candidate by trading benefit against a hard failure). The acceptance test (§L7.3) is built so that the wall's presence is checked, not assumed.

L7.2 The digital-twin closure ladder DT0 → DT7 — rungs, criteria, first failures

The pack gives the digital-twin program as an eight-rung ladder, carried verbatim:

DT0 offline plots
DT1 fixed candidate replay
DT2 perturbation sweep
DT3 closed-loop simulated tracking
DT4 gate-supervised optimizer
DT5 mission-coupled simulation
DT6 non-flight subsystem requirements
DT7 future hardware control

We expand each rung into the in-scope band, the closure criterion to leave the rung, the status effect, and the named downgrade token, drawn so that an unmet rung downgrades and so that no rung past the current standing is crossed by any mode.

Rung Name Criterion to stand here (closure to leave) Status effect First failure / downgrade token
DT0 offline plots static, non-interactive renders of a fixed candidate's fields/gates; no time evolution inert visualization a plot implying motion/control where none was simulated → FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM (watermark required)
DT1 fixed-candidate replay deterministic replay of one frozen candidate Ξ through the full gate ladder, byte-reproducible verdict reproducible single-shot non-reproducible replay (hidden RNG/state) → AUDIT (precondition-unmet); replay that re-fits fields → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE
DT2 perturbation sweep open-loop sweep of (x_c, σ, A, φ) over a declared box; every sample fully gate-graded; the tolerance cascade (§L7.4) is this rung's deliverable sensitivity map a sweep sample whose gate verdict is interpolated (not recomputed) → AUDIT; a sweep that exits the declared box → domain-extrapolation FAIL (HC-09)
DT3 closed-loop simulated tracking a simulated controller holds the comoving phase lock and lobe pose against a simulated vehicle-frame trajectory, with the gate ladder evaluated every step and the abort controller (§L7.5) armed gate-clean tracking on a passing candidate tracking that drifts a gate to FAIL without aborting → FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION; tracking a candidate that never passes a hard gate → vacuous, −∞ everywhere
DT4 gate-supervised optimizer the objective J (§L7.1) is maximized over the actuated box under the hard wall; the optimizer is proven unable to cross a hard gate (J=−∞ wall verified load-bearing) supervised search within the gate-clean basin the optimizer crosses a hard gate via a softened wall → FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION; the optimizer finds benefit only via coordinate/gauge artifact → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY / FAIL_PURE_GAUGE
DT5 mission-coupled simulation the optimized lobe is attached to an HC-10 toy trajectory with the validity weight and G3 no-aggregation theorem enforced; benefit stays local and validity-weighted local mission overlay (watermarked) any global travel-time aggregation → FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM; gate mask going zero unflagged → invalid
DT6 non-flight subsystem requirements a requirements package (not a design) for a non-flight subsystem study, written only if DT5 produced a gate-clean validity-weighted local effect under independent review requirements text, no hardware a requirements doc that contains a build instruction → hard scope violation (FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION / reject)
DT7 future hardware control out of current scope — a real control law for a real subsystem, contingent on an independently reproduced lab observable (DT chain bottoms out into BRL-7/8) future / out of scope any present-tense hardware-control claim → hard scope violation; −∞/reject

Current standing on the DT ladder. The runnable platform stands at DT0–DT2 as PASS_TOY-grade: offline plots exist, fixed-candidate replay is reproducible (the G1 numeric chain reproduces to displayed precision per the verification pass), and the perturbation-sweep machinery is the same (x_c, σ, A, φ) parameterization that the D-series candidate library and G2 baselines already exercise. DT3 (closed-loop tracking) and DT4 (gate-supervised optimizer) are the defined-not-built core of this leaf — they are specified here with their objective, their hard wall, their abort controller, and their acceptance test, but no mode has been driven through them, and on the worked exemplar G1 they are vacuous by design (the hard wall is −∞ everywhere because source/energy fail). DT5 (mission-coupled) is the L8/HC-10 hand-off, runnable only as a watermarked local overlay under G3. DT6 is a requirements-writing rung with a hard no-hardware boundary, and DT7 is explicitly out of scope — the rung where a real control law would live, contingent on lab reproduction (BRL-6/BRL-7) that does not exist.

The terminal honesty of the DT ladder, stated once. The ladder is drawn so that the interesting rungs (DT4 optimizer, DT5 mission coupling) are exactly the rungs where overclaim is easiest, and each is pinned by a token that fires on the overclaim: a softened wall is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION; a coordinate/gauge "benefit" is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY/FAIL_PURE_GAUGE; a global aggregation is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The credibility of the leaf is that the optimizer's legal output is never "a candidate that works" — it is "the gate-clean basin's shape, the tolerance envelope, and the first-failure surface," which for every mode screened so far is empty or failure-bounded.

L7.3 The lobe-slip estimator and comoving-frame tracking (DT3)

The pack names a lobe-slip estimator as an IP claim and lists phase/comoving lock as a control variable. We expand both into the DT3 closed-loop tracking object — a simulated state estimator that measures how far the candidate's forward lobe has drifted from its commanded pose in the vehicle comoving frame, with the gate ladder evaluated every step.

Formal object. Let the commanded lobe pose in the comoving frame be p* = (x_c*, σ*, A*, φ*) and the realized pose (under simulated perturbation/drift) be p(t). The lobe-slip is the gate-relevant pose error

slip(t) = p(t) − p*          # 4-vector in actuated space

estimated from the simulated invariant observables — never from coordinate quantities (CONTRACT §4 say-this: "metric-interface telemetry"). The estimator reads the HC-01 invariant scalars and the HC-04 tetrad-frame causality margin, not raw chart coordinates, so that a pure coordinate drift produces zero slip (it is not physical). The DT3 tracking loop is:

DT3_track(p*, Ξ_constructor, gate_ladder, abort_ctl):     # SIMULATED — no actuator, no hardware
  p ← p*
  for each simulated step t:
      Ξ_t ← Ξ_constructor(p)                  # build candidate at current pose
      obs ← invariant_observables(Ξ_t)        # HC-01 scalars + HC-04 tetrad margin (NO raw coords)
      slip ← estimate_slip(obs, p*)           # gate-relevant pose error
      verdict ← gate_ladder(Ξ_t)              # FULL HC-01..HC-10, frozen, every step
      if hard_gate_FAIL(verdict):             # source/causality/gauge FAIL, χ_max≥1, admissibility FAIL
          abort_ctl.trigger(verdict)          # → §L7.5 abort/downgrade; loop STOPS, status downgrades
          return DOWNGRADE(verdict.token)
      u ← −K · slip                           # simulated corrective command (within actuated box ONLY)
      p ← clip_to_box(p + u)                  # may NEVER leave the declared, gate-clean box
  return tracking_trace, slip_history, gate_history

Three precision notes.

First, the estimator keys on invariant observables, not coordinates — so a coordinate-only "slip" (the candidate looks displaced in a relabeled chart but is physically identical) estimates slip = 0 and triggers no command. This is the DT3 expression of HC-01's NC-COORD control and of the FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY token: the tracker cannot be fooled into "correcting" a chart artifact, because the artifact carries no invariant signature.

Second, the corrective command lives strictly inside the declared, gate-clean box. clip_to_box enforces that p(t) never leaves the perturbation box DT2 declared gate-clean. The controller cannot "track" a candidate out of its validity domain — an attempt to do so is clipped, and if the commanded pose itself would leave the box, that is a domain-extrapolation FAIL (HC-09), not a tracking success.

Third, the gate ladder is recomputed every step, never interpolated. The verdict is re-derived from frozen gate code at each Ξ_t; it is never carried forward or interpolated from a neighboring sample. This is what makes DT3 honest: the controller is supervised continuously, so a drift that pushes any hard gate to FAIL is caught at the step it happens, and the abort controller fires before the loop can "ride through" a failure.

First failure (L7.3). DT3 fails — and downgrades — the instant tracking drifts a hard gate to FAIL without the abort controller firing (a "ride-through"), or the instant the slip estimator is fed raw coordinates instead of invariants (so a coordinate drift produces a spurious command). The first is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (the loop continued past a hard failure); the second is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY (the tracker chased a chart artifact). On G1 specifically, DT3 is vacuous: the hard wall is already FAIL at p* (source/energy), so the abort controller fires at step 0 and the honest return is DOWNGRADE(FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC) — the tracker never runs.

L7.4 The tolerance cascade (DT2) — how a candidate fails as parameters move

The pack names a tolerance cascade as an IP claim. We expand it into the DT2 deliverable: a structured map of which gate fails first, and how far the actuated parameters must move to make it fail, across the declared box. The tolerance cascade is the controls-layer analogue of the first-failure ledger — it does not ask "does the candidate pass?" but "as I move the lobe, what breaks first, and how much slack is there before it breaks?"

Formal object. For a nominal pose p* and each actuated parameter θ ∈ {x_c, σ, A, φ}, the tolerance τ_g(θ) against gate g is the smallest perturbation |Δθ| that drives gate g from PASS to FAIL:

τ_g(θ) = min { |Δθ| : gate_g(Ξ(p* + Δθ ê_θ)) = FAIL }

The binding tolerance is τ*(θ) = min_g τ_g(θ) and the first-failing gate is g*(θ) = argmin_g τ_g(θ). The cascade is the table of (θ, g*, τ*) over all four actuated variables — read top-to-bottom by which gate is closest to failing. The DT2 sweep that produces it:

DT2_tolerance_cascade(p*, box, gate_ladder):
  for θ in {x_c, σ, A, φ}:
      for Δθ swept across box along ê_θ:
          v ← gate_ladder(Ξ(p* + Δθ ê_θ))     # FULL ladder, recomputed (never interpolated)
          record first gate to flip PASS→FAIL and the |Δθ| where it flips
      τ*(θ), g*(θ) ← binding tolerance + first-failing gate along θ
  return cascade_table  # sorted by τ* ascending — tightest tolerance first

Worked reading on G1 (MID-METRIC-001), honest numbers. G1 is static (A = 0.05, single component δg_xx, g_xx = 0.99), and its binding gates are already FAIL at p*: source (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC) and energy (FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY, ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶). So G1's tolerance cascade is degenerate in the most informative way — there is no positive tolerance to a passing region; the binding gate is failed at the nominal pose, with τ* = 0 against source/energy. Moving A → 0 drives the benefit to zero (the deficit 0.0884 → 0) at the same rate it drives the exoticity to zero — the candidate becomes trivial before it becomes sourced. This is the cascade's central lesson made numerical: for G1 there is no actuator path from "exotic and unsourced" to "sourced and benign"; the energy burden and the benefit are tied to the same amplitude knob. The cascade does not find a tolerance envelope around a pass; it certifies the absence of one.

Worked reading on the textbook baselines (G2). For the Alcubierre/Natário/Van Den Broeck baselines the cascade is equally instructive: the Alcubierre energy E ∝ −v_s² R² σ (G2: ≈ −5.0×10⁴⁶ J ≈ −0.28 M_⊙ at the illustrative R=100, σ=0.5, v_s=1) means the amplitude/width knobs trade benefit against an exoticity that scales faster than any plausible budget — the tolerance to the energy gate is negative (it is already failed) and shrinks as you ask for more benefit. The Van Den Broeck reshaping (integral reduced, pointwise unchanged, peak |ρ̂| larger) is the cautionary cascade: a control move that improves one gate's integrated metric while worsening the pointwise NEC the gate ladder actually checks — exactly the kind of "optimize through a gate" move the hard wall forbids.

First failure (L7.4). The tolerance cascade fails as an honest object the instant a sweep sample's verdict is interpolated from neighbors rather than recomputed (token AUDIT, precondition-unmet) — because interpolation can hop over a thin failure band and report a tolerance that does not exist — or the instant the sweep silently exits the declared box (domain-extrapolation FAIL, HC-09). The deeper first failure is conceptual and is the one the cascade is designed to expose: for every mode screened so far the cascade finds no positive-measure gate-clean basin around a candidate with real invariant benefit — the benefit and the exoticity are knob-locked, so the "tolerance to a pass" is zero or negative. That is not a defect of the cascade; it is its honest finding.

L7.5 The automatic abort / downgrade controller — the fail-closed heart of the loop

The pack names an automatic abort/downgrade controller as an IP claim. This is the controls-layer enforcement of the entire manuscript's fail-closed discipline, and it is the module the buyer's diligence team would rerun first on this dimension. Its job: the instant any hard gate flips to FAIL during DT3 tracking or DT4 optimization, stop the loop, downgrade the candidate's status to the matching token, and forbid any further optimization on that candidate — never "recover," never "route around," never "try a different chart."

Formal object. The abort controller is a precedence-ordered classifier over the per-step gate verdict, mirroring the executed downgrade tree (CONTRACT §3):

abort_controller(verdict):                         # fail-closed; first matching clause wins
  if verdict.claim_boundary == FAIL:    DOWNGRADE → FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION ; HALT
  if verdict.source == FAIL:            DOWNGRADE → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC ; HALT
  if verdict.causality == FAIL:         DOWNGRADE → FAIL_CAUSALITY ; HALT          # HC-04 vetoes all mission
  if verdict.gauge == FAIL:             DOWNGRADE → FAIL_PURE_GAUGE ; HALT
  if verdict.invariant == FAIL:         DOWNGRADE → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY ; HALT
  if verdict.admissibility == FAIL:     DOWNGRADE → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE/FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT ; HALT
  if verdict.energy hidden:             DOWNGRADE → FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY ; HALT
  if verdict.chi_max ≥ 1:               DOWNGRADE → FAIL_BACKREACTION/UV_DELEGATED ; HALT
  if verdict.brst interacting-placeholder:  HOLD → AUDIT_QUANTUM                    # not a halt; pins below PASS_TOY
  if verdict.uv internal-sensitive:     HOLD → UV_DELEGATED (named axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1) # delegated, not failed
  else:                                 CONTINUE (soft region; J evaluated)

Three precision notes.

First, HALT is irreversible within the loop. Once the abort controller halts on a hard gate, the loop cannot resume on that candidate by any actuated move — the candidate's status is downgraded and the optimizer is forbidden from "trying again" with a different chart, a different gauge, or a smuggled field. This is what makes the J = −∞ wall load-bearing rather than decorative: the wall is not a smooth penalty the optimizer can creep along; it is a halt. The proof that HALT dominates CONTINUE for any hard-FAIL verdict is the controls analogue of L4's test_interacting_stays_audit — the acceptance test that the abort controller cannot leak a CONTINUE on a hard failure.

Second, HOLD is distinct from HALT. The two soft-but-non-promotable verdicts — interacting-BV AUDIT_QUANTUM and internal-sensitive UV_DELEGATED — hold the candidate below PASS_TOY without halting the loop's characterization, because (per L4) UV_DELEGATED with a named axiom is honest delegation, not failure, and AUDIT_QUANTUM is a placeholder, not a fail. The controller therefore continues mapping the tolerance envelope but caps the candidate's terminal status at AUDIT_QUANTUM/UV_DELEGATED — it can never be lifted to PASS_TOY by the loop, only by the owner-adopted, independently-reviewed path (CONTRACT §1.4).

Third, the controller's precedence is causality-vetoes-all. HC-04's causality gate sits high in the precedence because it "gates all mission claims" (master decomposition, HC-04). A candidate with a negative causality margin halts at FAIL_CAUSALITY regardless of how large its invariant benefit is — there is no benefit large enough to buy back a causality violation. This is the controls-layer statement of the contract's forbidden-phrase discipline: the loop can never produce a "fast" trajectory by violating a cone.

First failure (L7.5). The abort controller fails — and the whole leaf fails with it — the instant a hard-FAIL verdict is met with anything other than HALT: a "recovery" branch that searches for a chart in which the gate reads green (FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY sold as a recovery), a "route-around" that smuggles a field to source the metric (FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE), or a softened wall that lets a large benefit ride through (FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION). The standing negative controls calibrate the halt: the coordinate-only profile (NC-COORD) must HALT at FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY; the pure-gauge profile must HALT at FAIL_PURE_GAUGE; the smuggled-field and double-count controls must HALT at the admissibility tokens; the vacuum-energy-booking profile must escalate to FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION. If any of these continues, the controller is fail-open and the leaf is rejected.

L7.6 The DT4 gate-supervised optimizer — supervised search inside the gate-clean basin

DT4 is the rung the entire commercial ask is most tempted to overclaim, so it is specified here with maximal fail-closed discipline. The optimizer maximizes J(x_c, σ, A, φ) (§L7.1) over the declared actuated box, under the hard wall and the abort controller, with the gate ladder recomputed at every evaluation.

DT4_optimize(box, J, gate_ladder, abort_ctl):
  feasible ← { p ∈ box : all hard_gates(Ξ(p)) == PASS }   # the gate-clean basin (may be EMPTY)
  if feasible == ∅:
      return NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN(first_failure_surface)       # the HONEST common case (e.g. G1)
  p* ← argmax_{p ∈ feasible} J(p)                           # search ONLY within feasible
  assert hard_wall_load_bearing(J, box)                     # proof: J=−∞ off feasible, never finite
  return p*, J(p*), tolerance_envelope(p*), validity_weight(p*)   # all PASS_TOY-capped

The optimizer's three structural guarantees, each a contract obligation.

  1. It searches only the feasible (gate-clean) basin. The argmax ranges over {p : all hard gates PASS}; outside that set J = −∞, so the optimizer has no gradient leading out of feasibility. It cannot "tunnel" through a failed gate because the wall is a halt, not a slope.

  2. The common, honest return is NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN. For every mode screened so far — including the deepest exemplar G1 — the feasible set is empty (G1's source/energy gates fail at the nominal pose and everywhere the amplitude is nonzero-and-sourced is unreachable). The optimizer's honest output is then not "the best candidate" but the first-failure surface: the locus in the box where the binding gate flips, which is exactly the DT2 tolerance cascade re-expressed. This is the deliverable a strategic acquirer actually gets: a precise, machine-checked map of where and why every candidate fails, not a survivor — a directly reusable, defensible diligence artifact whose value is independent of whether any drive is ever built.

  3. Even a non-empty basin caps at PASS_TOY. If some future candidate did have a non-empty feasible basin, the optimizer's p* is still only a PASS_TOY-grade simulation result — it is the input to a frozen-milestone test (§L7.7), never the milestone itself. The optimizer cannot promote; it can only nominate a pose for the gated milestone evaluation, which requires the matched source ledger, χ_source < 1, the named-and-reviewed UV assumption, and no failed gates — none of which the optimizer can manufacture.

First failure (L7.6). DT4 fails the instant the optimizer is allowed to search outside the feasible basin with a finite (softened) wall — at which point it will, with certainty, find the cheapest gate-evasion (a coordinate relabel scoring spurious benefit, a smuggled field zeroing the source mismatch, a cutoff-straddling narrow lobe) and report a false optimum. Token: FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION. The guard is assert hard_wall_load_bearing — the proof, rerun in the acceptance test, that J is −∞ (not finite) off the feasible set, so no benefit can buy a hard gate. The second first failure is subtler and is the one the verification pass would press: an optimizer that reports NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN but quietly widens the box until something passes is extrapolating past the declared domain — caught by the HC-09 domain-declaration requirement (FAIL on extrapolation).

L7.7 The acceptance test and the conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone

The pack does not state a separate acceptance predicate for the control program, so we derive the controls acceptance test directly from the objective's hard wall and the abort controller, in the same three-clause executable form the other Part-L leaves use, and bind it to the frozen milestone.

CONTROL_TOLERANCE_GATE(candidate Ξ, loop)  ⟺
   (A)  hard_wall_load_bearing          # J = −∞ (NOT finite) on every hard-gate FAIL; proven, not assumed
   AND (B)  abort_halts_on_hard_fail    # the abort controller HALTS (never CONTINUE/recover/route-around) on any hard FAIL
   AND (C)  no_optimization_through_gate # the optimizer searches ONLY the feasible basin; benefit is invariant + floored-at-zero
   ⇒  the control/tolerance axis does NOT block the milestone (the loop did not manufacture a pass)
otherwise ⇒ BLOCK at the first violated clause:
   ¬(A) ⇒ FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION            (a softened wall let benefit buy a hard gate)
   ¬(B) ⇒ FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION            (the loop rode through a hard failure)
   ¬(C) ⇒ FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY / FAIL_PURE_GAUGE / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE  (benefit was an evasion artifact)

The single binary the entire ask turns on is the conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone criterion, carried exactly: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." This leaf relates to the milestone in a specific, bounded way the contract forces us to state precisely:

  • The control program does NOT add a clause to the milestone. The frozen milestone is a property of the candidate's physics gates (source, χ_source, invariant, causality, no-fail, named UV), not of the controller. A controller cannot make a candidate satisfy the milestone; it can only fail to corrupt a candidate that already does. So the control/tolerance axis is milestone-protecting, not milestone-advancing.
  • The controller's failure modes are all milestone-blocking. A softened wall, a ride-through, or an evasion-sourced benefit each produces a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION / FAIL_* token, and "no failed gates" in the milestone forbids any candidate carrying such a token. The controls program's entire contribution to the milestone is negative: it guarantees that if a candidate reaches EFT_CANDIDATE, it did so without the loop having manufactured the pass.
  • M1 means "worth a deep physics diligence sprint," not flight-ready (master roadmap, carried verbatim). The DT4 optimizer's best legal output — a nominated gate-clean pose with a tolerance envelope — is an input to that diligence sprint, never its conclusion.

The crucial fail-closed reading, carried from the buyer logic: there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." A candidate whose only "pass" was manufactured by the loop (softened wall, ride-through, evasion benefit) routes — in the pack 10 decision tree — to keep/option screening IP only or theory-only continuation, never to acquisition. The decision tree's gate "Does one candidate hit M1_EFT_CANDIDATE?" must be answered by the frozen gate ladder on the as-built candidate, not by the optimizer's objective — and the controls acceptance test above is precisely the guard that the optimizer did not pre-answer that question by evasion.

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands on the control axis (honest reading). On G1 (MID-METRIC-001), the controller's hard wall is J = −∞ at the nominal pose and throughout the box (source FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, energy FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY, ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶). DT3 tracking aborts at step 0; DT2's tolerance cascade certifies no positive tolerance to a passing region (benefit and exoticity are knob-locked to the amplitude A); DT4 returns NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN with the first-failure surface = the source/energy boundary. G1 is the deepest-surviving exemplar and the control program's honest verdict on it is that no control move makes it work — which is exactly the product: a machine-checked certification of where the best candidate fails and that no actuation rescues it. The control program is the gate that ensures the rescue cannot be done by sleight of hand.

L7.10 Where this leaf sits in the funded sprint and the buyer logic

The control/tolerance/digital-twin program is exercised across the controls phase of the 90-day hostile validation sprint, downstream of the source/energy/causality audits (Phases for HC-02/03/04) and the gauge/BRST/UV audits (the L4 phases) — because the controller can only be wired honestly after the gates it supervises are frozen and validated. It is the lower-reasoning-agent backlog task whose acceptance test is itself a failure demand: the twin "passes" by refusing to optimize through a gate and by returning NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN plus the first-failure surface for every mode screened so far. For the engineered controls, the abort controller does HALT at the matching token — that passing-by-failing is the product.

The buyer logic this leaf must never weaken: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. The asymmetry is the point: optioning a validated screening process (an option fee plus a bounded 90-day hostile validation sprint) is downside-protected, where buying a nonexistent engine is not. Applied to this axis: a rigorous acquirer's first move on any exotic-propulsion control claim — this document's or a competitor's — is "show me that your controller cannot optimize a candidate through a failed physics gate, that its benefit is invariant and not a coordinate trick, and that it aborts (not recovers) on a hard failure." This leaf is that move, automated and IP-protected. Even the expected outcome — candidates fail upstream and the controller returns NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN while the engineered controls HALT at FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY / FAIL_PURE_GAUGE / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION — leaves the acquirer owning a rigorous gate-supervised control/tolerance discriminator and its negative-control corpus. And the binding constraint, carried verbatim: there is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." A candidate whose only "pass" was manufactured by the loop routes to keep/option the screening IP or theory-only continuation, never to acquisition — and the expected outcome may still be that every candidate fails while the acquirer retains a useful IP-protected screening platform.

L7.11 Scope boundary (restated, non-negotiable)

This leaf is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap for the control, tolerance, and digital-twin dimension. It is not a hardware-construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 07; CONTRACT §4). It specifies no actuator, no field-generation method, no power schedule, and no flight-control law; the digital twin drives a simulated candidate against already-computed physics gates, and the rung that comes closest to "control a drive" — DT7 future hardware control — is precisely the one held out of current scope and made contingent on an independently reproduced lab observable (BRL-6/BRL-7) that does not exist. The current manuscript ceiling remains PASS_TOY. The control objective is hard-walled at −∞ on every failed physics gate; the abort controller HALTs (never recovers) on any hard FAIL; the optimizer searches only the gate-clean basin, which for every mode screened so far — including the deepest exemplar G1 — is empty (G1's source/energy gates fail at the nominal pose, and benefit and exoticity are knob-locked, so no actuation rescues it). No rung of the DT ladder past its current standing (DT0–DT2 runnable, DT3–DT4 specified-not-driven, DT5 watermarked-local-only, DT6 requirements-only, DT7 out of scope) has been crossed by any mode. The platform is a discriminator/screening tool, NOT a Mars spaceship. Any move toward a real Mars spacecraft requires the separate closure of the source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, EFT, controls, observability, safety, certification, and mission-integration gates — each with its own named criterion and its own named first failure. This leaf draws the controls staircase (DT0–DT7) and prices its first funded steps; it crosses none of them past DT2.

Honest response: the leaf is built on exactly this fear and inverts it — that is why the objective's hard wall is J = −∞ (a halt, not a slope) on every hard-gate FAIL, why the benefit term is invariant and floored-at-zero so a coordinate/gauge trick scores nothing, why the optimizer is structurally confined to the gate-clean feasible basin (and returns NO_FEASIBLE_BASIN — the honest common case, including for the deepest exemplar G1), and why the abort controller HALTs rather than recovers, with a proof that it cannot leak a CONTINUE on a hard failure (the controls analogue of the placeholder-firewall test). L8.0 Why this leaf is last, and the one sentence the entire program hangs from

Part L (v2) decomposes the buildability gap map into self-contained closure programs, one per pack document. This leaf expands pack document 08 — the Mars Mission-Architecture Program — which is the furthest-out closure dimension in the whole document and therefore the leaf written last. Every other program (source, energy, UV/quantum/admissibility, EFT, observability, control) asks "is this candidate honest as a metric?" This program asks the only question a Mars buyer ultimately cares about — "does any of this change how you get to Mars?" — and answers it, fail-closed, with a No that is not a hedge but a theorem.

The pack states the program's purpose in one line: "Define what would have to be true before the concept affects Mars mission architecture." And it states the blocker in one line we carry verbatim: "Local shortening does not automatically integrate to global travel-time reduction. Mission claims must stay validity-weighted and local unless a global theorem closes the gap." (pack 08, "Current limitation"). The load-bearing fact for this entire leaf is that the document already executed the relevant theorem — G3, the No-Global-Aggregation result — and G3 does not merely fail to find an aggregation route; it proves the local shortening score S_L does not integrate to a global arrival-time change Δt. The arrival time along a worldline is set by ∫ δN dλ / N² (the accumulated lapse perturbation), not by S_L; at first order the front and back lobes cancel, and at second order the residual is sign-fixed by Raychaudhuri convergence in the wrong direction. So the gap between "a candidate has a positive local shortening score" and "Mars is closer" is not an open to-do item this program will quietly close — it is shut by a verified no-go, and the program's job is to make any premature crossing of it a hard, named failure (FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM).

This is why the leaf reads, structurally, as the most defensive in Part L. Where L1 (source) is the strongest blocking program and L0 (overview) is the framing, L8 is the firewall against the one overclaim the whole document exists to prevent: "Mars in days." The pack's own acceptance test is built from five conjunctive preconditions precisely so that no overlay can assert a travel-time benefit without each of them; this leaf carries all five exactly, makes each executable, and ties each to its first-failure / downgrade token.

A boundary stated once, up front (it governs the entire leaf). This is a classification, overlay, and sensitivity program over a simulated toy trajectory and a simulated gate-status field. Running it does not plan a Mars mission, does not compute a travel time, and is explicitly non-enabling: it provides no instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware (pack 08 boundary; CONTRACT §4). It produces a validity-weighted overlay with a watermark, never a trajectory the vehicle would fly. The program that comes closest to the temptation to "plot the Mars benefit" is precisely the one whose terminal verdict on any global travel-time assertion is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

L8.2 The mission ladder as a staircase — rungs, criteria, first failures, and where the no-go bites

The mission ladder is a staircase, and like the other Part-L ladders it is drawn so an unmet rung downgrades rather than stalls optimistically. The crucial structural feature — unique to this leaf — is that the staircase has a hard ceiling welded in at M5 by the G3 no-go: M1–M5 are overlay rungs (a candidate can stand on them as annotations), but the step from M5 to a global travel-time claim is not a rung on this ladder at all — it is the forbidden contraction T = T_baseline·(1 − ⟨S_L⟩), which G3 labels a non-law. M6–M9 climb past the overlay band toward an architecture option, but each requires evidence the document does not supply.

The terminal honesty of this ladder, stated once: the only way to climb past the overlay band toward a real architecture claim runs through M6 (independent review), and M6 is gated on the frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE milestone closing upstream — which it does not, because the deepest exemplar G1 dies at source (HC-02) and energy (HC-03) long before any mission overlay is even meaningful. The mission overlay is the last thing you would compute, and it is computed here only to show it refuses to lie.

L8.3 The G3 no-global-aggregation result — the theorem this leaf is built on

The pack's whole limitation reduces to one mathematical fact, and the document executed the proof of it as leaf G3 (verified: see VER_modes_results §G3). This leaf carries the result exactly because it is the load-bearing object behind every rung above M2.

The forbidden contraction. The intuitively appealing — and wrong — move is to take a per-mode local shortening score S_L (or a mission-averaged ⟨S_L⟩) and write the global travel time as a multiplicative contraction:

FORBIDDEN (non-law):   T_global = T_baseline · (1 − ⟨S_L⟩)

G3 proves this is not a law. The argument, GR-correct and reached corpus-agnostically (it does not lean on the Fable/TOE corpus), runs:

  1. Arrival time is set by the lapse line-integral, not by S_L. For a worldline through a perturbed lapse N = 1 + δN, the accumulated coordinate-time-to-proper-time relation gives an arrival-time perturbation δT_arr = ∫ δN dλ / N² to leading order — an integral of the lapse perturbation δN along the path, not of the spatial proper-distance functional S_L that the screening engine scores. S_L and δN are different functionals of the same Ξ; a candidate can have S_L > 0 (a local forward proper-distance deficit) with ∫ δN dλ = 0.
  2. First order cancels. For the vehicle-comoving, front/back-asymmetric profiles the platform screens, the front lobe and the back lobe contribute lapse perturbations of opposite sign along the traversed path; at first order in the amplitude A, the front/back contributions to ∫ δN dλ cancel. (This is the same cancellation E10a finds when the local S_L itself comes out negative — a local lengthening — once the back lobe at D = −d₀ falls outside the forward integration window [0, D_max]: ∫₀⁴ g(D)dD = +0.796, giving L_F(A=0.05) = 4.039 → S_L = −0.0098 and L_F(A=0.10) = 4.078 → S_L = −0.0194.)
  3. Second order is sign-fixed the wrong way. The residual at second order is governed by the Raychaudhuri equation, whose convergence term −⅓θ² − σ_{ab}σ^{ab} − R_{ab}k^a k^b is sign-definite; for the NEC-respecting sector it does not supply a net arrival-time reduction. (The proof-sketch is explicitly downgraded to TOY_TESTED with the twist/vorticity term named as the residual gap — the one place the second-order argument is not yet airtight, carried honestly rather than papered over.)
  4. The two-body identity. In the executed E10a baseline, the classical transfer is integrated from a two-body ODE that has no δg term, so ΔT = 0 by construction — an honest identity, not a hedge: the local lobe is not in the dynamics that set the arrival time, and putting it there is exactly the FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM move.

The worked baseline and the validity weight, with verified numbers. The E10a baseline transfer uses a_t = 1.262 AU, √(a_t³) = 1.418, T_baseline = π√(a_t³) = 4.454 (toy time units). The local lobe overlay on this trajectory gives, after the red-team sign correction, negative local scores (S_L = −0.0098 at A = 0.05, S_L = −0.0194 at A = 0.10) — i.e. the honest toy shows a local lengthening, not a shortening, in the forward window. The validity weight that multiplies any overlay is the product of per-gate status weights:

V = w(invariant)·w(source)·w(energy)·w(gauge)·w(EFT)·w(UV)
  = w(PASS)·w(AUDIT)·w(PASS)·w(AUDIT)·w(AUDIT)·w(UV_DELEGATED)
  = 1 · 0.5 · 1 · 0.5 · 0.5 · 0.3
  = 0.0375

so f_weighted(S5) = 0.0375 · 0.09 = 0.003375 and f_weighted(S4) = 0.0375 · 0.06 = 0.00225 — the overlay is discounted to ~3.75% of its nominal value precisely because the candidate's source/energy/EFT/UV gates are AUDIT / UV_DELEGATED, not PASS. The validity weight is the mechanism that prevents a candidate from advertising a mission benefit it has not earned at the physics gates — a candidate whose source gate is FAIL carries w(source) → 0 and the overlay collapses to zero. G3's overclaim control confirms the firewall fires: the fake contracted travel times (T_fake(5pt) = 4.419, T_fake(amber) = 4.396, from ⟨S_L⟩ = −0.0078 / −0.0130) are flagged as FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM, watermarked, and never reported as real.

First failure (L8.3). The instant any overlay is converted to a global travel-time claim — by applying the forbidden contraction, by dropping the validity weight, by quoting an absolute time without the classical baseline, or by substituting the lobe into the trajectory dynamics — the result is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The G3 theorem is what makes this a hard failure rather than a cautious preference: there is a verified no-go between local S_L and global Δt, so the overclaim is not "unproven," it is "proven wrong."

The pack lists seven required outputs for the program. We carry all seven verbatim, map each to its producing object and its first-failure token, and note which exist at toy scale today versus which are the funded-sprint deliverable.

The seven outputs are deliberately constructed so that the only quantity that ever reaches a number is a validity-discounted, baseline-relative, watermarked local annotation — never a travel time. The "validity-weighted benefit" is the closest the program gets to a "benefit," and even it is (a) multiplied by V = 0.0375, (b) reported only as a deviation from T_baseline, (c) carried with the G3 caveat, and (d) — in the honest toy — negative. There is no output of this program from which a "Mars in days" number can be read; that is the design intent.

L8.5 The architecture-sensitivity dashboard — the M5 deliverable, drawn so it cannot overclaim

The pack's IP action names an architecture sensitivity dashboard. We specify it as the M5 deliverable: a table (never a single asserted number) showing how the validity-weighted local annotation responds to the lobe, gate, and baseline parameters — so a diligence team can see the shape of any putative benefit and immediately see that it lives entirely inside the validity discount and the no-aggregation caveat. The dashboard reports sensitivities, with a mandatory watermark on every cell.

ARCHITECTURE_SENSITIVITY(Ξ, trajectory, gate_status):     # M5; emits a TABLE, never a Δt
  V          ← Π_gate w(gate_status[gate])                  # validity weight (e.g. 0.0375)
  S_L(λ)     ← local comoving lobe score along trajectory   # annotation only
  for p in {A (amplitude), σ (width), d₀ (front/back offset), a_t (baseline semi-major axis)}:
      ∂(V·S_L)/∂p  ← finite-difference sensitivity of the VALIDITY-WEIGHTED annotation
  watermark every cell:  "validity-weighted LOCAL annotation; S_L does NOT integrate to Δt (G3)"
  ASSERT no cell is interpreted as Δt   ⇒ else FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM
Sensitivity (toy, illustrative) Direction What it means What it does not mean
∂(V·S_L)/∂A grows with amplitude a larger lobe amplitude moves the local annotation not a larger travel-time cut — S_L does not integrate (G3)
∂(V·S_L)/∂σ width-dependent the lobe's spatial extent reshapes the annotation not a mission-scale effect — the back lobe cancels at first order
∂(V·S_L)/∂d₀ sign-flipping the front/back offset can flip S_L's sign (toy is negative) not a controllable benefit — it is the cancellation, made visible
∂(V·S_L)/∂a_t baseline-relative the annotation is reported only vs T_baseline = 4.454 not an absolute arrival time
∂(V·S_L)/∂w(gate) collapses as gates degrade a FAIL gate sends V → 0, the annotation vanishes not a benefit a failing candidate can advertise

The last row is the dashboard's whole point: the sensitivity of the validity-weighted annotation to gate status is the firewall made quantitative. As any of the source / energy / EFT / UV gates degrades from AUDIT toward FAIL, its weight drops (AUDIT → 0.5, UV_DELEGATED → 0.3, FAIL → 0), V collapses, and the annotation goes to zero — so the dashboard automatically refuses to show a benefit for a candidate that fails upstream. For G1, with w(source) = AUDIT/FAIL at the source gate, the dashboard correctly shows a collapsed annotation: there is no mission benefit to read because the candidate is unsourced and exotic.

First failure (L8.5). The dashboard fails the instant any cell is read as a travel time, or any sensitivity is integrated into a global Δt, or the validity-weight column is dropped. Each is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The dashboard is built so the absence of the watermark, the validity weight, or the baseline is itself the block.

L8.6 The first-failure mission timeline — the earliest-gate firewall in mission time

The pack names a first-failure mission timeline as a required output. This is the HC-gate first-failure logic ("first failure = earliest gate that fails, not worst") lifted onto the mission axis: along the toy trajectory, plot the earliest point at which any physics gate goes non-PASS, in mission time, so the overlay is truncated at the first failure rather than extrapolated past it.

FIRST_FAILURE_TIMELINE(Ξ, trajectory):                    # required output
  for λ along trajectory (mission time τ(λ)):
      g(λ) ← {invariant, source, energy, gauge, EFT, UV, causality} gate status at λ
      if any gate ∈ {FAIL_*}:  record (τ(λ), gate, token);  TRUNCATE overlay at τ(λ)
  emit timeline: τ_first_fail, the gate, the token
  the overlay is VALID only on [0, τ_first_fail);  beyond it the candidate has FAILED

For the worked exemplar G1 (MID-METRIC-001), the timeline is brutally short: the source gate fails essentially immediately (HC-02, FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, root cause the exotic ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ from HC-03), so τ_first_fail ≈ τ_0 — the overlay is valid on an empty mission interval, and the validity weight V is correspondingly collapsed. The timeline does not show "G1 gets you to Mars faster and then fails late"; it shows "G1 fails at the source gate before the mission overlay is even meaningful." That is the honest reading, and the timeline is the object that forces it.

First failure (L8.6). A timeline with no named first failure is an invalid output (per the pack's required-outputs discipline and CONTRACT §1.2). A timeline that extrapolates the overlay past τ_first_fail — showing a benefit accruing after a gate has failed — is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The timeline's job is to truncate, not to extend.

L8.7 The acceptance test — the five-clause conjunctive predicate (carried exactly)

The pack states the acceptance test in one sentence, verbatim: "No Mars travel-time claim unless local effect is valid, gate mask remains nonzero, global aggregation theorem exists, trajectory dynamics are complete, and independent mission review signs off." We carry all five clauses exactly and make each executable. This is the mission-axis analogue of the source ladder's χ_source < 1 predicate and the UV/quantum/admissibility three-clause gate (L4.3): a candidate that fails any of the five does not "almost get a travel-time claim" — it is blocked at the failed clause with FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

MARS_TRAVEL_TIME_CLAIM(candidate Ξ)  ⟺  ALL of:
   (1) local_effect_valid          # the local S_L is invariant-clean (HC-01/HC-05) and nonzero
   AND (2) gate_mask_nonzero        # V = Π w(gate) > 0  (no gate is FAIL ⇒ no weight is 0)
   AND (3) global_aggregation_theorem_exists   # a PROVEN local→global integration theorem exists
   AND (4) trajectory_dynamics_complete         # full mission dynamics, not a two-body toy
   AND (5) independent_mission_review_signs_off  # external mission-analysis sign-off
   ⇒  a Mars travel-time claim is (and only then) permissible
otherwise ⇒ NO travel-time claim;  any assertion of one ⇒ FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM

Five precision notes the contract and G3 force.

First, clause (3) is the one G3 currently refutes, not merely leaves open. "A global aggregation theorem exists" is the precondition that would let S_L integrate to Δt — and G3 proves the opposite: the arrival time is set by ∫ δN dλ / N², the front/back lobes cancel at first order, and the second-order residual is sign-fixed the wrong way (with the twist/vorticity term named as the only residual gap). So clause (3) is currently False for every candidate, which means — by the conjunction — no Mars travel-time claim is permissible for any candidate in this document, full stop. This is not a pessimistic reading; it is the acceptance test evaluating to False because a required theorem has been shown to be false in the screened sector.

Second, clause (2) is the validity-weight firewall. V = Π w(gate) is zero the instant any gate is FAIL (w(FAIL) = 0), so a candidate that fails source, energy, causality, gauge, EFT, or UV automatically fails clause (2) and can carry no travel-time claim. For G1, the source gate failure alone (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC) drives V → 0 and blocks clause (2) independently of clause (3).

Third, clause (4) exposes the two-body toy as insufficient. The executed baseline is a two-body ODE with no δg term (ΔT = 0 by construction). That is the right baseline for an honest overlay, but it is not "complete mission dynamics" — clause (4) demands full N-body, finite-burn, navigation-uncertainty mission dynamics, which the document does not supply. So clause (4) is also currently False.

Fourth, clause (5) is the independent-review gate (mission M6). Even if clauses (1)–(4) were somehow satisfied, no travel-time claim is permissible without an independent mission-analysis team signing off — the same independent-review discipline the frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE milestone requires for the UV assumption (L4) is required here for the mission overlay. This sign-off does not exist.

Fifth, clause (1) inherits the upstream gates. "Local effect valid" requires the local S_L to be invariant-clean (HC-01) and not a coordinate artifact or pure gauge (HC-05) — so a coordinate-only or pure-gauge "shortening" fails clause (1) before the mission axis is even reached.

First failure (L8.7). The acceptance test fails the instant a travel-time claim is asserted while any of (1)–(5) is False — and at least clauses (3) and (4) are currently False for every candidate (G3 refutes (3); the two-body toy fails (4)), with clause (2) additionally False for any candidate that fails an upstream gate (G1 fails it at source). Each assertion-without-the-clause is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The test is built so the absence of the proven theorem / nonzero mask / complete dynamics / review is itself the block — not a soft warning.

L8.8 The conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone — and where this leaf sits in it

The single binary the entire ask turns on is the conversion / BRL-4 frozen milestone criterion, carried exactly: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." This leaf's relationship to the milestone is unusual and worth stating plainly: the mission dimension is downstream of the frozen milestone, not a clause of it.

The frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE predicate (L0.5) is about whether a candidate is a legitimate metric-interface EFT candidate — source-matched, invariant/causality-clean, no failed gates, UV named-and-reviewed. It says nothing about Mars. A candidate could in principle satisfy the entire frozen milestone and still carry no Mars travel-time claim, because the mission acceptance test (§L8.7) adds independent preconditions — most importantly clause (3), the global-aggregation theorem that G3 currently refutes. So this leaf governs a band of the BRL beyond BRL-4:

  • BRL-4 (M1_EFT_CANDIDATE) is the metric/physics milestone — the subject of L1–L5.
  • This leaf's mission overlays (M1–M5) are produced regardless of whether the milestone is hit, purely to demonstrate the overlay machinery refuses to manufacture a benefit.
  • The mission claim (M6–M9 → BRL-9) is reachable only after BRL-4 closes, and after the global-aggregation theorem is proven (not refuted), and after independent mission review. The mapping is M9 ↔ BRL-9 (Mars architecture option), the furthest rung of the entire ladder.

The fail-closed reading, carried from the buyer logic: there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive," and the mission axis is the place that reading is most tempting to violate (a Mars buyer wants the Mars number). A candidate that fails the mission acceptance test routes — in the pack 10 decision tree — to keep/option screening IP only or theory-only continuation, never to "Mars architecture change." Indeed the decision tree's last nodes (can a flight-relevant subsystem requirements package be written? → Mars architecture option study) sit entirely past the frozen milestone and past independent review, and every "no" along the way routes to a non-acquisition node (stop at lab research, research program only).

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands on the mission axis (honest reading). G1 produces an M1–M5 overlay (toy trajectory T_baseline = 4.454, local lobe annotation, validity weight V collapsed by its source/energy status, classical-baseline-relative reporting, a sensitivity table) — and the overlay shows no mission benefit, both because the honest local S_L is negative (a local lengthening once the back lobe falls outside the forward window) and because V → 0 at the failed source gate. G1's first-failure mission timeline truncates at τ_first_fail ≈ τ_0 (source gate). G1 is the proof that the overlay machinery works as designed: it took the deepest-surviving candidate, attached the full mission overlay, and the overlay correctly refused to produce a Mars travel-time claim. That refusal — not a benefit — is the deliverable.

The chapter's named first failure is the pack 08 core blocker reused as a buildability gate. The pack states it exactly: "Local shortening does not automatically integrate to global travel-time reduction." The leaf's terminal failure is therefore not abstract ("we couldn't connect to Mars") but localized and mechanical: a candidate is treated as changing Mars travel time while (i) its local S_L does not integrate to a global Δt — proven by G3, the arrival time being set by ∫ δN dλ / N² with first-order front/back cancellation and second-order Raychaudhuri sign-definiteness; or (ii) its validity mask V is not nonzero (a FAIL gate sends a weight to zero, collapsing the overlay); or (iii) no proven global-aggregation theorem exists (clause (3) is currently refuted); or (iv) the mission dynamics are incomplete (the two-body toy has no δg term); or (v) no independent mission review signed off. The standing negative controls — the G3 overclaim control (T_fake = 4.419 / 4.396 flagged and watermarked), the negative local S_L toy (−0.0098 / −0.0194), the ΔT = 0-by-construction two-body identity, and the validity weight collapsing for failed gates — are the corpus's calibration that the gate fires as built.

A second, structural first failure guards this very leaf. A leaf that draws a Mars trajectory, computes a baseline transfer time, and attaches a "benefit" risks reading as a Mars travel-time plan — the single overclaim the whole document exists to prevent. This is fixed by restating every overlay as a validity-weighted, baseline-relative, watermarked local annotation (never a travel time), by welding the G3 no-go into the ladder at M5 (the M5→global step is not a rung, it is the forbidden non-law), and by the non-enabling scope boundary (§L8.10). Predicted dominant verdict for the real library: for the deepest exemplar (G1) and for every mode that fails upstream, the mission acceptance test evaluates to False (clause (2) at the failed gate, clause (3) by G3, clause (4) by the toy dynamics), the overlay collapses, and the honest output is no mission benefit — which, per CONTRACT §1.6, is the intended outcome.

The pack's IP action for this program is one line: "Claim Mars validity-weighted overlay, local-to-global classifier, first-failure mission timeline, and architecture sensitivity dashboard." This program produces claim seeds for one continuation-in-part slot of the Refined IP Ladder — IP-6, the Mars-overlay CIP — gated by the operational rule below. We carry the named artifacts exactly and tie each to its producing object, its ladder rung, and the BRL rung whose closure artifact it tracks.

OPERATIONAL RULE (never weaken), carried verbatim: CIPs are filed ONLY when the corresponding closure artifact exists — no source-ledger CIP without a real SourceMatchReport; no observability CIP without a null-controlled signal model; no future physical embodiment filing without independent evidence. For this leaf the operational rule reads: the IP-6 Mars-overlay CIP is filed ONLY when a real mission overlay exists — a produced, runnable validity-weighted overlay with its no-aggregation caveat, first-failure timeline, and sensitivity dashboard — and never on the physics of a Mars benefit (which does not exist and, per G3, cannot exist via local-to-global integration in the screened sector). The filings protect the overlay method, the classifier, the timeline, and the dashboard as simulation/audit assets, valuable precisely because they refuse to produce a travel-time claim.

The IP is decoupled from the physics outcome — by construction. This is the spine of the buyer logic applied to the mission axis: the protectable system is the validity-weighted overlay + local-to-global refusal classifier + first-failure timeline + sensitivity dashboard, valuable regardless of whether any candidate ever changes Mars travel time (and G3 says, in the screened sector, none does via this route). If every mode fails (the expected case), a strategic acquirer owns a rigorous mission-overclaim discriminator — a tool that takes any claimed propulsion concept, attaches a validity-weighted overlay, and mechanically refuses to let a local effect masquerade as a Mars travel-time benefit. That is a directly reusable diligence instrument for evaluating any exotic-propulsion Mars claim, not just this one — and its value, residing in the screening method rather than in a survivor, is independent of whether a drive is ever built. If — counterfactually — a global-aggregation theorem were ever proven (closing the G3 gap, including the named twist/vorticity residual) and the frozen milestone were hit and independent review signed off, the IP-6 CIP would be filed before disclosure, controlling the patent window.

L8.11 Where this leaf sits in the funded sprint and the buyer logic

The Mars-mission-architecture program is exercised in Phase 5 (Mars overlay + control simulation, days 61–75) of the 90-day hostile validation sprint, paired with the control/digital-twin program (L7) — because the mission overlay can only be attached after the control simulation tracks the candidate and after the source/energy/gauge/UV/EFT audits (Phases 3–4) have stamped each gate's status, which is exactly the input to the validity weight V. It is the lower-reasoning-agent backlog task whose acceptance test is itself a failure demand: the mission check passes by refusing to produce a travel-time claim (validity-weighted overlay only), by truncating at the first failure, and by encoding the G3 no-go as a gate rather than integrating around it. For the overclaim controls, the timeline does fire FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM — that passing-by-failing is the product.

The buyer logic this leaf must never weaken: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. Applied to the mission axis, this leaf is the place the buyer's instinct ("just show me the Mars number") is most dangerous, and the leaf is engineered so the honest answer is structural: there is no Mars number — the local score does not integrate to a global Δt (G3), the validity mask collapses for any failing gate, the aggregation theorem does not exist (it is refuted), the dynamics are a toy, and no independent review has signed off. A rigorous acquirer's first move on any Mars-propulsion claim — this document's or a competitor's — is "show me that the local effect is validity-weighted, baseline-relative, watermarked, and not integrated to a travel time without a proven theorem." This leaf is that move, automated and IP-protected. Even the expected outcome — every candidate produces no mission benefit, and the overclaim controls return FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM — leaves the acquirer owning a rigorous mission-overclaim discriminator and its negative-control corpus. And the binding constraint, carried verbatim: there is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." A candidate whose mission overlay shows no benefit (the expected case for every mode) routes to keep/option the screening IP or theory-only continuation, never to "Mars architecture change" — and the expected outcome may still be that every candidate fails while the acquirer retains a useful IP-protected screening platform. The most a Mars-transport-scale acquirer should take from this leaf is that the platform will honestly tell them when a Mars claim is unearned — a disciplined, fail-closed mission-overclaim discriminator that is a cheap, downside-protected R&D option, valuable independent of any physics outcome.

A discriminator that honestly fails exotic-propulsion candidates — and publishes exactly where each one dies — is an asset whether or not a survivor exists. So the IP ladder is engineered to let a buyer acquire optionality over a screening platform — and only conditionally, on a frozen predicate, optionality over anything more — without ever being asked to pay for a drive that does not exist.

The leaf's load-bearing thesis, stated once: the IP ladder is decoupled from the physics outcome by construction, and that decoupling is the entire deal. And the buyer-side instruments (IP-10 option, IP-11 conversion) are written so that conversion fires on a pre-registered, frozen milestone plus an accepting hostile review — never on enthusiasm, never on "promising." This is the spine of the buyer logic for the whole document, expressed as a legal ladder.

Three structural readings of the table follow, and they are the whole point of the ladder.

First, the ladder is front-loadable — IP advances ahead of physics, but only over real artifacts. IP-0 (notebook/hashes, immediately) and IP-1 (base provisional over the current screening platform) establish priority before any physics closes, because the platform already exists at BRL-1/BRL-2. IP-7 (software copyright on the fixed code base), IP-8 (trade-secret scoring heuristics), and IP-9 (defensive publication of the negative-control corpus) likewise protect things that are real now — code, heuristics, and the nine controls + five self-tests that constitute the validated corpus. None of these five front-loaded steps asserts that any candidate is sourced, energetic-condition-clean, observable, or mission-relevant. They protect the discriminator, which is the asset whether or not a survivor exists.

Second, the CIP rungs IP-2 … IP-6 are bound one-to-one to the technical closure artifacts of L1–L8, and are filed only when those artifacts exist. IP-2 fires on the SourceMatchReport (L1); IP-3 on the energy/exoticity audit (L2/L3); IP-4 on the null-controlled signal model (L6); IP-5 on the digital twin (L7); IP-6 on the mission overlay (L8). Each is a continuation-in-part that technically discloses a real, produced artifact — never a placeholder for a hoped-for one. The trigger column of the pack table is precisely this binding ("SourceMatchReport exists," "energy audit exists," "null-controlled signal model exists," "digital twin exists," "mission overlay exists"), and §L9.3 hardens it into the operational rule.

Third, the buyer-side rungs IP-10 / IP-11 / IP-12 are the conditional steps, and they carry the document's hardest discipline. IP-10 (the strategic-acquirer exclusive option) is signed before the sprint — that is what makes the buyer's downside bounded. IP-11 (conversion/acquisition) fires only on M1 hit + hostile review — the frozen predicate and an accepting independent audit, never on enthusiasm. IP-12 (future physical-embodiment filings) is reserved and may not be filed at all until a lab observable exists — independent physical evidence, the operational rule's hardest clause, which BRL-2 is nowhere near supplying. The pack's IP ladder is therefore not a path to a patent on a drive; it is a path to a patent on a screening platform, with a reserved, evidence-gated slot for any future physical embodiment that may or may not ever be earned.

L9.3 The operational rule — the discipline that keeps the ladder honest (never weaken)

The pack's IP ladder and option structure are held honest by a single rule, carried verbatim from the ask and never relaxed anywhere in v2 Part L:

CIPs are filed ONLY when the corresponding closure ARTIFACT exists. No source-ledger CIP without a real SourceMatchReport; no observability CIP without a null-controlled signal model; no future physical embodiment filing without independent evidence.

This is the operational expression of the IP-ladder's pack trigger column ("SourceMatchReport exists," "energy audit exists," "null-controlled signal model exists," "digital twin exists," "mission overlay exists," "lab observable exists") and of the option-structure line "CIP filing rights only if artifacts are produced." It is what keeps the IP ladder from degenerating into a paper claim to a drive. A CIP is a technical disclosure of a real, produced artifact — not a placeholder for a hoped-for one.
