  IP-4  observability CIP      requires  null-controlled measurement model        # L6
  IP-5  control / tolerance CIP requires gate-supervised digital twin             # L7
  IP-6  Mars-overlay CIP       requires  validity-weighted mission overlay        # L8
  IP-12 embodiment filing      requires  INDEPENDENT lab observable               # BRL-6+
otherwise ⇒ OPERATIONAL_RULE_VIOLATION (rejected — file not permitted)

Three precision notes the contract forces.

First, the rule is fail-closed: the absence of the artifact is itself the block, not a soft warning. A motivated team racing to establish a patent window will be tempted to file a CIP on the expectation that the artifact is "almost done." The rule forbids it: IP-2 cannot be filed until L1's source program emits an actual SourceMatchReport with χ_source < 1; IP-3 cannot be filed until L2/L3 emit an actual NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC + magnitude audit; IP-4 cannot be filed until L6 emits an actual null-controlled measurement model; IP-5 cannot be filed until L7 emits an actual gate-supervised digital twin; IP-6 cannot be filed until L8 emits an actual mission overlay. There is no "provisional CIP on a forthcoming artifact" branch, by design.

Second, IP-12 carries the rule's hardest clause, and it is the firewall against the document's single most dangerous overclaim. A future physical embodiment filing — the one filing that would read as a patent on an apparatus — may not be filed at all until independent physical evidence exists: a real lab observable, reproduced. BRL-2 is nowhere near this; the lab-observable proxy is BRL-6, four rungs up, and is itself gated by an accepted hostile review (BRL-5). The operational rule's third clause ("no future physical embodiment filing without independent evidence") is therefore the legal expression of the manuscript's PASS_TOY ceiling: there is no patent on a thing the document has not, and cannot, demonstrate.

Third, the operational rule decouples the IP from the physics outcome — which is the spine of the buyer logic. Because the front-loaded slots (IP-0/IP-1/IP-7/IP-8/IP-9) protect real, produced assets and the CIP slots (IP-2 … IP-6) fire only on real, produced artifacts, the protectable system is the screening / classification / control platform and its negative-control corpus — valuable regardless of whether any candidate is ever sourced. The rule guarantees that the portfolio's value is grounded in what exists, not in what is hoped for, and that is exactly why the expected "all candidates fail" outcome is still a defensible commercial position.

First failure (L9.3). The rule fails the instant a CIP is filed without its artifact: an IP-2 source-ledger CIP with no real SourceMatchReport; an IP-4 observability CIP with no null-controlled signal model; an IP-12 embodiment filing with no independent lab observable. Each is an operational-rule violation and is rejected. The pack 12 "Do not do" list states the same firewall from the other side: "Do not file CIPs unless closure artifacts exist." The rule is built so that the absence of the artifact is the block, not a discretionary judgment call.

L9.4 The frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE predicate — the single binary the deal turns on

The option structure's conversion line — "conversion only if M1_EFT_CANDIDATE is true" — turns on one binary, the frozen BRL-4 / conversion milestone, carried exactly: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." The pack 12 gives the predicate in executable form, which we carry verbatim and bind to the IP-11 conversion right:

milestone_hit(candidate) =
  candidate.status == EFT_CANDIDATE
  and candidate.source.matched == true
  and candidate.source.chi_source < 1
  and candidate.invariance == PASS
  and candidate.causality == PASS
  and candidate.energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE}
  and no gate == FAIL
  and if candidate.uv_dependency then candidate.uv_assumption.named_and_independent == true

In one sentence: EFT_CANDIDATE is reached only WITH a matched source ledger, χ_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption (energy at worst AUDIT, EFT χ_max < 1 over the declared domain). M1 means "worth a deep physics diligence sprint." It does not mean flight-ready, and there is no route from a "no" on any clause to "acquire a drive."

The predicate is what fires IP-11. Three readings the deal requires:

The predicate is frozen before the sprint and cannot be edited mid-run. This is the option-structure line "frozen milestone predicate" and the pack 12 prohibition "Do not let any agent change the milestone mid-sprint." A predicate softened after results are seen is a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (self-promotion off the agent's own authority; CONTRACT §1.4) and voids the honesty of the test. The freeze is the legal device that prevents the option from degenerating into "buy it if it looks good."

Energy is never a clean PASS in the predicate — it is AUDIT / PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE. The predicate requires candidate.energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE}, exactly mirroring CONTRACT §3 ("energy_check is never a clean PASS — it is 'pass / audit-visible'"). The milestone does not require the energy problem solved; it requires the exoticity visible and bounded. The forbidden phrase "energy problem solved" can never appear in a conversion memo, because the predicate itself only ever certifies audit-visibility.

The UV clause requires the assumption named and independently reviewed, not solved. The predicate's last clause — if candidate.uv_dependency then candidate.uv_assumption.named_and_independent == true — is workstream-C's terminal deliverable (L4): the open UV axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 may be named as a dependency and independently reviewed, but never adopted as a mechanism. A UV_DELEGATED verdict with a named, reviewed axiom does not block the milestone; an unadopted-treated-as-adopted or engineered UV dependence converts the delegation into a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and blocks it.

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands against the predicate (honest reading). The deepest-surviving exemplar, G1 (MID-METRIC-001), fails the predicate at the first physics clause: it declares vacuum yet T_eff ≠ 0 (100% source mismatch), so candidate.source.matched == false and the engine emits the terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (G1 §8 / Gate 5 / HC-02). The root cause is the energy gate (Gate 6 / HC-03): the real, invariant forward-distance deficit is sourced by a negative effective energy density (ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ geometrized units at the lobe center, exotic — WEC/NEC/DEC violated, SEC marginal-static and violated-boosted), which no declared field source supplies. G1 passes G1–G4 (the lobe is real curved geometry with a real invariant distance deficit, R = −4.0404×10⁻⁴ ≠ 0, not the NC-2 coordinate illusion) and is the document's only affirmative structural pass — and it is killed at source/energy, exactly the two gating dimensions that block BRL-2 → BRL-4. Against the M1 predicate, G1 reads: source.matched == false ⇒ milestone_hit == false ⇒ no conversion. The terminal status is 2 TOY_TESTED / AUDIT, token TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC; the ceiling PASS_TOY is never exceeded. No candidate in this document satisfies the M1 predicate, and therefore the IP-11 conversion right is, today, un-fired by construction.

The IP ladder is decoupled from the BRL but tracks it: each filing names the BRL rung it accompanies and the decision-tree node (pack 10, L10) at which it is taken. We give the full crosswalk so a diligence team can see, at a glance, which filings are live now (front-loaded), which are artifact-gated (CIPs), and which are predicate-gated (buyer-side), and exactly which decision-tree branch fires each.

The decision tree (pack 10, expanded in L10) walks the buyer node by node, and every "no" routes to a non-acquisition node: does the repo run and reproduce known metrics? (no → software cleanup only) → does it reject textbook warp metrics honestly? (no → reject) → does one candidate hit M1_EFT_CANDIDATE? (no → keep/option screening IP only) → does hostile review accept M1 and the first-failure ledger? (no → theory-only continuation) → can a null-controlled observable be defined? (no → theory-only continuation) → can a safe non-flight lab proxy be specified by qualified reviewers? (no → simulation-only program) → can an independent lab proxy reproduce the signal? (no → stop at lab research) → can a flight-relevant subsystem requirements package be written? (no → research program only) → Mars architecture option study. There is no node from which a "no" reaches "acquire a drive." The IP filings are layered onto this tree so that the front-loaded assets are owned before the tree even begins, the CIPs fire only on "yes" at the M1 and observable nodes, and the conversion right fires only at the hostile-review-accepts node.

Naming discipline (carried from pack 10). A program may not be called a build even before it is gated as one. Approved program names: Screening Platform Program · EFT Candidate Search Program · Independent Physics Audit Program · Observable Proxy Program · Non-Flight Demonstrator Requirements Program · Mars Architecture Option Study. Forbidden program names: Warp drive build · FTL ship · Mars engine · heavy-lift-vehicle install. The IP portfolio is filed and marketed under the approved names only; a filing or memo that names the program a "Mars engine" or implies a "heavy-lift-vehicle install" violates the naming discipline and the pack 12 prohibitions ("Do not imply heavy-lift-vehicle integration"; "Do not ask a strategic acquirer to buy a Mars engine").

The ladder is a ladder to protecting a screening platform and optionally pricing information — not a ladder to selling a spaceship. Predicted dominant outcome: the milestone misses (the expected case), the front-loaded IP (IP-0/IP-1/IP-7/IP-8/IP-9) is retained, the CIPs are not filed (no artifacts), conversion does not fire, and the acquirer owns a rigorous, IP-protected screening platform — which, per CONTRACT §1.6, is the intended outcome.

L9.7 The patent-extraction posture this leaf itself carries

Unlike L1–L8, this leaf does not produce a new technical artifact whose simulation IP is then filed; it is the leaf that governs the filing of all the others. Its own patent-extraction posture is therefore meta: it protects value by structuring the portfolio, not by adding a claim seed. The protectable structure has four load-bearing features, each carried from the pack.

Structural feature What it protects / how IP-ladder slot it governs Why it is defensible
CIP-to-artifact binding (operational rule) each CIP (IP-2 … IP-6) filed exactly when — and only when — its named artifact exists IP-2 … IP-6, IP-12 a CIP discloses a real, produced, hashed artifact, not a hoped-for one — the disclosure is substantive and the priority date is earned
front-loading the screening platform, code, and heuristics are protected before any physics closes IP-0/IP-1/IP-7/IP-8 the discriminator exists now (BRL-2); its IP is real independent of any candidate outcome
defensive publication of the negative-control corpus publishing the nine controls + five self-tests blocks competitors from later patenting the obvious failing variants the platform already shows to fail IP-9 a published, validated "these variants demonstrably fail" corpus is prior art against trivial exotic-propulsion claims
evidence-gated embodiment reservation future physical-embodiment filings reserved until independent lab evidence exists IP-12 the reservation protects the slot without overclaiming — no apparatus patent is asserted on a thing the document cannot demonstrate

The IP is decoupled from the physics outcome — by construction, and that is the whole asset. The protectable system is the automated metric-target / invariant-classifier / source-reconstruction / energy-diagnostic / gauge-BRST-UV-classifier / gate-card-validator / gate-supervised-control / Mars-validity-overlay / first-failure-reporting platform plus its validated negative-control corpus — valuable regardless of whether any candidate is ever sourced, energetic-condition-clean, or UV-closed. If every mode fails (the expected case), a strategic acquirer owns a rigorous exotic-propulsion discriminator and its negative-control corpus, a directly reusable diligence tool for any exotic-propulsion claim — this document's or a competitor's — not just this one; the protectable value sits in the screening method, so it holds independent of whether a drive is ever built. If one mode reaches a genuine EFT_CANDIDATE under the frozen milestone, the relevant CIPs are filed before public disclosure, controlling the patent window.

Sequencing against the refined IP ladder (carried exactly): IP-0 lab notebook/hashes → IP-1 base provisional → IP-2 source-ledger CIP → IP-3 energy/exoticity CIP → IP-4 observability CIP → IP-5 control/tolerance CIP → IP-6 Mars-overlay CIP → IP-7 software copyright → IP-8 trade secrets → IP-9 defensive publication → IP-10 strategic-acquirer option → IP-11 conversion/acquisition → IP-12 future physical-embodiment filings. The front-loaded slots (IP-0/IP-1/IP-7/IP-8/IP-9) are filed/registered now; the CIP slots (IP-2 … IP-6) are filed only when the corresponding closure artifact exists under a funded sprint; the conversion slot (IP-11) fires only if M1_EFT_CANDIDATE is true under the frozen milestone and hostile review accepts — never on "promising"; and the embodiment slot (IP-12) is reserved until an independent lab observable exists. L9.8 Where this leaf sits in the funded sprint and the buyer logic

The IP ladder is exercised across the entire 90-day hostile validation sprint and closed out in Phase 6 (days 76–90: hostile-review packet + IP update), where the CIPs IP-2 … IP-6 are filed iff the artifacts produced in Phases 3–5 exist. But the option (IP-10) is executed before Phase 1, and the front-loaded filings (IP-0/IP-1/IP-7/IP-8/IP-9) are in place before the sprint is funded — that timing is the whole point of "exclusive option over IP-1/IP-7/IP-8 … before the sprint." The leaf is also the lower-reasoning-agent backlog task (L11) whose acceptance test is itself a discipline demand: the IP step passes by not filing a CIP whose artifact does not exist, and the conversion step passes by not converting on anything but the frozen predicate. Refusing to file, and refusing to convert, is the product.

The buyer logic this leaf must never weaken: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. Applied to the IP/deal axis, this leaf is that logic written as instruments: the wrong ask — "buy a Mars spaceship engine" — has no honest answer because there is no engine; the right ask — option the base provisional IP and fund a frozen-milestone sprint — has a bounded downside and a real IP payoff either way. That asymmetry (an option fee plus a bounded validation sprint, never the price of a nonexistent engine) is exactly why a Mars-transport-scale acquirer can rationally hold this as a cheap, downside-protected, fail-closed R&D option, valuable independent of any physics outcome. The milestone-triggered value ladder makes the asymmetry explicit: code fails to run → fund cleanup only, nothing acquired; all candidates fail (expected) → option the screening IP, the acquirer owns a rigorous discriminator + corpus; one candidate hits M1 → file CIPs before disclosure, control the patent window; hostile review accepts M1 + ledger → negotiate conversion/JV (IP-11); a lab observable later found → stand up a non-flight research program (BRL-6→BRL-8), IP-12 reserved. And the binding constraint, carried verbatim: there is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." Every "no" routes to software cleanup only, reject, keep/option the screening IP, theory-only continuation, simulation-only program, stop at lab research, or research program only — never to acquisition. The expected outcome may still be that every candidate fails while the acquirer retains a useful IP-protected screening platform; and that outcome is a win for the buyer, because the asset is the discriminator, not a survivor.

L10.0 Why the decision tree is a separate leaf, and the single guarantee it enforces

Part L (v2) decomposes the buildability gap map into self-contained closure programs, one per pack document. L1–L8 are the technical programs (source, energy ×2, UV/quantum/admissibility, EFT, observability, control, mission); L9 is the commercial/legal spine (the thirteen-step refined IP ladder and the option structure). This leaf — expanding pack document 10 — is the decision procedure that sequences all of them. It is the leaf a strategic-acquirer diligence team reads with a pen, walking each node and recording a "yes" or a "no," and it exists to make one structural fact mechanically checkable: there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." Every other leaf asserts that guarantee; this leaf is the guarantee, drawn as a branch tree whose every "no" edge terminates in a named non-acquisition node.

The pack states the purpose in one sentence we carry (with the acquirer generalized): "Define the decision tree from current asset to a possible strategic-acquirer build program." The word possible is load-bearing. The tree does not promise a build program; it defines the gauntlet a build program would have to survive, and it is engineered so that the gauntlet is failed by default. The honest answer to "can this currently build a Mars spaceship?" is No — current ceiling is PASS_TOY; current standing is BRL-2 (pack 00, "Current honest status": "The current asset is not a ship, engine, or propulsion claim. It is a fail-closed screening platform plus provisional-patent support."). The decision tree is the apparatus that makes that "No" survivable as a commercial position: it routes the buyer, at every honest "no," to a node where the acquirer still owns something real — a cleaned-up repo, an IP-protected screening platform, a theory-only continuation, a simulation-only program, a bounded lab-research effort — and never to a node where the acquirer has paid for a nonexistent engine.

The leaf's load-bearing thesis, stated once: the decision tree is a fail-closed filter, not a sales funnel. A sales funnel is built to deliver the maximum number of prospects to "buy"; this tree is built to deliver the maximum number of honest evaluations to "do not buy — and here is what you still own." It is the operational reading of the buyer logic carried through every Part-L leaf — option the IP, fund a frozen 90-day hostile validation sprint, convert only if the frozen BRL-4 / M1_EFT_CANDIDATE milestone is hit — expressed as the exact sequence of binary questions a buyer answers, and the exact non-acquisition fallback attached to each "no." The expected outcome, stated plainly and early, is that the tree halts at keep/option screening IP only — the third node — because no candidate in this document satisfies the milestone the third node tests.

A boundary stated once, up front (it governs the entire leaf). This is a decision procedure and diligence document over a simulation/audit platform. It is non-enabling by construction (pack 10 boundary; CONTRACT §4): it provides no instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware. It specifies no apparatus. Every terminal node of the tree that lies past today's standing is a requirements / option / study node — never a build node — and the one node that names "Mars" (BRL-9, the Mars Architecture Option Study) is an option study gated by every prior rung, not a construction milestone. The tree routes decisions; it builds nothing.

The tree is read top-to-bottom; a "no" at any node exits the tree to its fallback and the buyer does not descend further.

Five structural readings of the tree follow, and they are the whole point of it.

First, the tree is monotone in honesty: every "no" routes down and out, never up. There is no node from which a "no" reaches a more advanced state, and crucially no node from which a "no" reaches "acquire a drive." The nine "no" destinations — software cleanup only, reject, keep/option screening IP only, theory-only continuation (twice), simulation-only program, stop at lab research, research program only, and (at node 9) the absence of any "build" successor — are an exhaustive enumeration of the fallbacks, and none of them is acquisition of a working drive. This is the decision-procedure form of the structural guarantee carried through L0, L8, and L9. A diligence officer can audit it mechanically: trace every "no" edge; confirm each lands on a node in {cleanup, reject, keep/option, theory-only, simulation-only, lab-research-stop, research-only}; confirm none lands on "acquire."

Second, the tree's first two nodes are gates on the asset that already exists, and the document passes them. Node 1 (repo runs, reproduces known metrics) is BRL-1 — the reference implementation metric → G_μν → T_eff → NEC/WEC plus proper-distance quadratures, which runs end-to-end. Node 2 (rejects textbook warp metrics honestly) is BRL-2 — the nine negative controls plus the Alcubierre / Natário / Van Den Broeck warp baselines (G2), held as permanent FAILs no run may flip. These are the only two nodes the document affirmatively answers "yes," and they are exactly the achieved rungs (BRL-1, BRL-2). Passing them is what earns the document the right to be evaluated at all — and is the literal content of the current standing.

Third, node 3 is where this document halts, by construction. Node 3 asks "does one candidate hit M1_EFT_CANDIDATE?" — the frozen milestone (§L10.3). No candidate in this document does. The deepest-surviving exemplar, G1 (MID-METRIC-001), fails the milestone at its first physics clause: it declares vacuum yet T_eff ≠ 0 (100% source mismatch), so the engine emits the terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (G1 §8 / Gate 5 / HC-02), and the deficit it does produce is sourced by a negative effective energy density (ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ geometrized units at the lobe center, exotic — WEC/NEC/DEC violated, SEC marginal-static and violated-boosted; G1 Gate 6 / HC-03) that no declared field source supplies. Against node 3, G1 reads source.matched == false ⇒ milestone_hit == false ⇒ "no" → keep/option screening IP only. The tree therefore terminates, today, at its third node, on its expected branch — and that branch is a win for the buyer (it owns the screening platform), not a dead end.

Fourth, nodes 4–9 are future, gated, and out of manuscript scope — they are drawn so a diligence team can price the road, not so the document can claim to have walked it. Node 4 (hostile review accepts M1) is BRL-5; nodes 5–6 (null-controlled observable; safe non-flight proxy) are BRL-6/BRL-7; node 7 (independent lab reproduces) is the reproduced-BRL-6 → BRL-8 boundary; node 8 (subsystem requirements package) is BRL-8; node 9 (Mars architecture option study) is BRL-9. Every one of these requires evidence this document does not and cannot supply. They are presented as a sequenced gauntlet with acceptance tests, exactly as L0.2.1 frames BRL-5…BRL-9 — so the buyer sees that the road past node 3 is long, gated, and honestly drawn, and that the document is nowhere near it.

Fifth, the tree only enters after the IP is optioned and the sprint is funded. Nodes 1–2 are answered by inspecting the asset as it stands; node 3 is answered only by running the frozen 90-day hostile validation sprint (L0.5), whose milestone is frozen before the sprint begins. The IP-10 exclusive option over IP-1/IP-7/IP-8 is the gateway into the tree (it is executed before node 3 can be honestly evaluated), and the sprint is the price of answering node 3. The tree is thus the decision-procedure twin of the option structure (L9.2): the option pays for the right to ask node 3, and node 3's answer — almost certainly "no" — routes to keep/option screening IP only.

Three readings the fallbacks force.

The expected exit is node 3, and it is the design target, not a disappointment. Per CONTRACT §1.6 — "Most modes should fail. That is good." — the dominant predicted outcome of running the tree is "no" at node 3, routing to keep/option screening IP only. At that exit the acquirer owns the front-loaded IP (IP-0 notebook/hashes, IP-1 base provisional, IP-7 software copyright, IP-8 trade-secret heuristics) and the defensive-publication corpus (IP-9), all over a real, runnable BRL-2 platform — and a discriminator that honestly fails candidates and publishes where each one dies is a reusable diligence tool for any future exotic-propulsion claim, this document's or a competitor's. Its protectable value is the screening method itself, so the asset stands independent of whether a drive is ever built. The tree halting at node 3 is the platform doing its job.

The fallbacks are graded so that the buyer's standing only ever rises as it descends — there is no node where progress is lost by advancing. Exiting at node 6 (simulation-only program) means the acquirer got an accepted M1 and a defined observable but no safe proxy; exiting at node 7 (stop at lab research) means it additionally got a specified proxy that returned a negative. Each deeper "no" leaves the buyer holding more, not less, and at each the IP slots that can honestly fire (only those whose artifacts exist) have fired and the rest have not. The tree is monotone in owned value as well as monotone in honesty.

No fallback is "acquire a drive," and node 9 is not one either. The terminal node 9 is a Mars architecture option study (BRL-9), not a Mars engine, not a heavy-lift-vehicle install, not flight hardware. It is reached only after eight consecutive "yes" answers — including an accepted hostile audit (node 4) and an independently reproduced lab observable (node 7) — none of which this document supplies. Reaching node 9 still does not yield a build; it yields a reviewed option study, the last analytical artifact before any program would even contemplate hardware, and the manuscript ceiling PASS_TOY is never exceeded anywhere in the tree.

L10.3 The frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE predicate — the binary node 3 turns on

Node 3 — "Does one candidate hit M1_EFT_CANDIDATE?" — is the single physics gate of the entire tree, and it turns on the frozen BRL-4 / conversion milestone, carried exactly: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." The pack 12 and pack 01 give the predicate in executable form, which we carry verbatim and bind to node 3:

milestone_hit(candidate) =
  candidate.status == EFT_CANDIDATE
  and candidate.source.matched == true
  and candidate.source.chi_source < 1
  and candidate.invariance == PASS
  and candidate.causality == PASS
  and candidate.energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE}
  and no gate == FAIL
  and if candidate.uv_dependency then candidate.uv_assumption.named_and_independent == true

In one sentence: EFT_CANDIDATE is reached only WITH a matched source ledger, χ_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption (energy at worst AUDIT, EFT χ_max < 1 over the declared domain; pack 01). M1 means "worth a deep physics diligence sprint." It does not mean flight-ready, and there is no route from a "no" on any clause to "acquire a drive." Three readings node 3 requires:

The predicate is frozen before the sprint and cannot be edited mid-run. This is the option-structure line "frozen milestone predicate" (L9.2) and the pack 12 prohibition "Do not let any agent change the milestone mid-sprint." A predicate softened after results are seen is a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (self-promotion off the agent's own authority; CONTRACT §1.4) and voids the honesty of node 3. The freeze is the device that makes node 3 a test rather than a negotiation — a movable goalpost would turn "no" into "almost," and "almost" is exactly what the next node (and pack 12: "no conversion on 'promising'") forbids.

Energy is never a clean PASS in node 3's predicate — it is AUDIT / PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE. The predicate requires candidate.energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE}, mirroring CONTRACT §3 ("energy_check is never a clean PASS — it is 'pass / audit-visible'"). Node 3 does not ask whether the energy problem is solved; it asks whether the exoticity is visible and bounded. The forbidden phrase "energy problem solved" can never appear in a node-3 evaluation, because the node only ever certifies audit-visibility — and even a candidate that passed node 3 would carry a visible exoticity burden into hostile review at node 4.

The UV clause requires the assumption named and independently reviewed, not solved. The predicate's last clause — if candidate.uv_dependency then candidate.uv_assumption.named_and_independent == true — is workstream-C's terminal deliverable (L4): the open UV axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 (Gap-04, OPEN; the axiom UNADOPTED) may be named as a dependency and independently reviewed, but never adopted as a mechanism. A UV_DELEGATED verdict with a named, reviewed axiom does not, by itself, fail node 3; an unadopted-treated-as-adopted or engineered UV dependence converts the delegation into a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and fails it.

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands against node 3 (the honest reading that halts this document at the third node). G1 (MID-METRIC-001) passes G1–G4 — the lobe is real curved geometry with a real invariant distance deficit (R = −4.0404×10⁻⁴ ≠ 0, not the NC-2 coordinate illusion; this is the document's only affirmative structural pass) — and is then killed at exactly the two dimensions node 3 gates first: source and energy. Against the predicate, clause by clause: status == EFT_CANDIDATE? No — terminal status is 2 TOY_TESTED / AUDIT, token TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC. source.matched == true? No — 100% source mismatch, FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (Gate 5 / HC-02). energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE}? energy is AUDIT, but it is exotic-visible (ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶; WEC/NEC/DEC violated; Gate 6 / HC-03). no gate == FAIL? No — the source gate is FAIL. The predicate therefore evaluates false at its first physics clause, node 3 returns "no," and the tree exits to keep/option screening IP only. No candidate in this document satisfies node 3, so the tree halts at node 3 by construction, and every node from 4 onward is unreached.

L10.4 Where node 3's "yes" branch goes — the post-milestone gauntlet (future, gated, out of scope)

Should a future candidate (under a funded sprint, never in this document) answer node 3 "yes," the tree's remaining six nodes are the gauntlet that a real program would have to survive. We expand them not because the document reaches them, but because the pack requires the whole tree drawn so the buyer can see the road's length and gating. Each node past 3 is mapped to its BRL rung, its closure program, and the discipline that holds it non-enabling.

  • Node 4 — hostile review accepts M1 and the first-failure ledger (BRL-4 → BRL-5). A node-3 "yes" is not a conversion trigger by itself; it must be accepted by an independent hostile audit, together with the first-failure ledger (the document's record of where every candidate dies). This is the IP-11 conversion gate (L9): conversion fires only on M1 true and an accepting hostile review — never on "promising" (pack 12). A "no" here routes to theory-only continuation: the acquirer keeps the platform and the unaccepted claim, and the physics continues on paper. This is the node where the buyer logic's "convert only if hostile review agrees" lives as a branch.

  • Node 5 — a null-controlled observable can be defined (BRL-6). The candidate's invariant signature must become a measurement model: a target signal, a null signal, a noise model, a detection threshold, and a false-positive control (L6, the HC-01 invariant guard reused as a measurement gate). A "no" — a signal that is coordinate-only and vanishes in an invariant/tetrad frame — emits FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY and routes to theory-only continuation. (The second "theory-only" exit; the tree is willing to send the buyer back to paper twice before it ever contemplates a bench.)

  • Node 6 — a safe non-flight lab proxy can be specified by qualified reviewers (BRL-6 → BRL-7). The observable must be reducible to a safe, non-flight bench proxy, and — critically — the specification authority is qualified reviewers, not this document and not any agent. This is the firewall against the leaf becoming enabling: the tree never specifies the proxy; it only asks whether qualified reviewers can. A "no" routes to simulation-only program. No apparatus, no high-energy source, no beam/reactor/radiation content appears at this node or any other (CONTRACT §4).

  • Node 7 — an independent lab proxy reproduces the signal (BRL-6 reproduced → BRL-8). The proxy must be independently reproduced — the operational-rule firewall for IP-12 (L9: no future physical-embodiment filing without independent evidence). A "no" — the proxy does not reproduce — routes to stop at lab research, and the negative is itself a valuable result. Only a reproduced observable supplies the "independent physical evidence" that the operational rule demands before any embodiment filing is even reserved.

  • Node 8 — a flight-relevant subsystem requirements package can be written (BRL-8). Note the word requirements: the node asks whether a requirements package can be written, not whether flight hardware can be built. This document contains no flight-hardware content at this or any node. A "no" routes to research program only.

  • Node 9 — Mars architecture option study (BRL-9, terminal). The terminal node is an option study, gated by every prior rung and bound by the No-Global-Aggregation theorem (G3): one may not claim local S_L > 0 ⇒ global travel time reduced, because arrival time is set by ∫ δN dλ / N² with first-order front/back cancellation and second-order Raychaudhuri sign-definiteness, so the local shortening score does not integrate to a global Δt. Any overlay at node 9 asserting a global travel-time cut emits FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. Node 9 is an analysis, not a build, and the forbidden phrase "Mars in days" can never attach to it.

The single discipline that holds nodes 4–9: each is a requirements / review / study node, and each "no" routes to a non-acquisition fallback. The gauntlet's terminal reward is an option study, not a spacecraft — and the document stands four-to-six rungs below the first of these nodes.

L10.6 The decision tree as the operational reading of the buyer logic

The tree is the buyer logic (L0.6, L9.8) made into a procedure. The buyer logic states: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. The tree is exactly that, walked:

  • OPTION is the gateway into the tree: the IP-10 exclusive option over IP-1/IP-7/IP-8 is executed before node 3 can be honestly evaluated (nodes 1–2 are answered by inspecting the asset; node 3 requires the funded sprint the option pays for). The buyer is optioning a discriminator (the thing nodes 1–2 confirm exists), not a drive.
  • FUND is the mechanism that answers node 3: the frozen 90-day hostile validation sprint (L0.5, six phases) is the price of information, run to evaluate the milestone the third node tests. Phases 1–2 re-confirm nodes 1–2 (independent reimplementation; rerun the self-tests + warp baselines); phases 3–4 (source/energy, then gauge/BRST/UV/EFT) are the audit that answers node 3; phases 5–6 (Mars overlay + control; hostile-review packet + IP update) feed nodes 4 onward and file IP-2…IP-6 iff their artifacts exist.
  • CONVERT only if is node 4: conversion (IP-11) fires only on a node-3 "yes" accepted by an independent hostile review — never on a node-3 "almost," never on "promising" (pack 12).

The milestone-triggered value ladder (L0.6) maps one-to-one onto the tree's exits: code fails to run = node-1 "no" → software cleanup only; all candidates fail (expected) = node-3 "no" → keep/option screening IP only, the acquirer owns a rigorous discriminator + corpus; one candidate hits M1 = node-3 "yes" → file CIPs before disclosure, proceed to node 4; hostile review accepts = node-4 "yes" → negotiate conversion/JV (IP-11); a lab observable later found = nodes 5–7 → stand up a non-flight research program (BRL-6→BRL-8), IP-12 reserved. And the binding constraint, carried verbatim: there is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." The tree is the formal proof of that sentence: enumerate the "no" edges, observe that all nine land in {cleanup, reject, keep/option, theory-only, theory-only, simulation-only, lab-research-stop, research-only, (no successor)}, and observe that "acquire a drive" is in none of them. The expected outcome may still be that every candidate fails while the acquirer retains a useful IP-protected screening platform — node 3 "no," exit to keep/option screening IP only — and that outcome is a win for the buyer, because the asset is the discriminator, not a survivor.

L11.0 Why the backlog is a separate leaf, and the single thing it must guarantee

Part L (v2) decomposes the buildability gap map into self-contained closure programs (L1–L8 technical, L9–L10 commercial/legal, L12 handoff). Every one of those leaves is written for a reasoning reader — a diligence team, a hostile reviewer, an attorney, the acquirer's diligence principal — who can hold the whole document in view and judge a program's standing in context. This leaf, expanding pack document 11, is written for the opposite consumer: a lower-reasoning agent that has no global view, that sees only the single task in front of it, that cannot be trusted to "use judgment" about whether a result is good enough, and that must therefore be handed a work order so completely specified that the only honest outcomes are the ones the work order pre-declares. The leaf is the bridge between the human-legible closure programs and the line-level execution that would actually produce their artifacts during a funded sprint.

This consumer is a feature, not a limitation. The entire discipline of the document — fail-closed, ceiling PASS_TOY, every section names a first failure, no self-promotion (CONTRACT §1) — is easier to enforce against an agent that cannot improvise than against one that can. A reasoning agent can rationalize a soft PASS ("the source mismatch is small, surely it counts"); a lower-reasoning agent running a fixed template with a hard acceptance test and a pre-named first failure cannot, because the template does not contain a "use your judgment" field. The backlog is therefore the place where the document's honesty becomes mechanical: each task either emits its declared artifact and passes its declared acceptance test, or it emits its declared first-failure token and stops. There is no third branch, and there is — by construction, carried through every leaf of Part L — no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive."

The pack states the purpose in one sentence we carry verbatim: "Give lower-reasoning AI agents exact work orders to close gaps." The load-bearing word is exact. A vague task handed to a low-reasoning agent fails open (the agent fills the gap with a guess); an exact task fails closed (the agent has nowhere to put a guess). This leaf's job is to make all fourteen tasks exact — each with named inputs, named files touched, a named computed output, a pre-declared first failure, a status token drawn only from the closure-ladder vocabulary, a patent trigger bound to the operational rule, and a do-not-say list drawn from CONTRACT §4 and pack 12. The single thing the backlog must guarantee is that no task can leak a false PASS, because a low-reasoning agent given a leaky task is the most efficient overclaim-generator the document could possibly build.

A boundary stated once, up front, governing the entire leaf (carried verbatim from pack 11). "This is a gap-closure, validation, IP, and diligence roadmap. It is not a hardware construction manual. It does not provide instructions for building high-energy sources, beam systems, reactors, radiation systems, weaponizable systems, or flight hardware. Current ceiling remains PASS_TOY." No task in this backlog crosses that line; several tasks exist specifically to enforce it (Task 3 source-legitimacy, Task 7 BRST/BV placeholder boundary, Task 11 Mars-overlay no-global-claim, Task 14 buyer memo no-overclaims). The backlog automates a discriminator, never a drive.

The backlog is therefore not a parallel artifact to the sprint — it is the sprint expressed at the granularity at which a no-global-view agent can execute it.

L11.2 The required output format — carried verbatim, made fail-closed

The pack mandates a single fixed output template for every task. We carry it verbatim:

Task:
Inputs:
Files touched:
Computed output:
First failure:
Status:
Patent trigger:
Do-not-say list:
Next task:

This nine-field template is the leaf's central enforcement device, and each field is load-bearing in a specific, fail-closed way. The template is not bureaucratic boilerplate; it is the shape of an honest task result, designed so that the fields a low-reasoning agent is most tempted to fudge are the ones the template makes hardest to fudge.

Template field What the agent must put here Fail-closed function (why the field exists)
Task the exact agent task from the backlog table (verbatim) pins scope; an agent that rewrites its own task has already failed (self-promotion, CONTRACT §1.4)
Inputs the named artifacts/files/configs the task reads makes the task reproducible and bounded; an input not on the list may not be used (forecloses invented sources)
Files touched the exact files the task reads or writes, hashed provenance for IP-0 (notebook/hashes) and for the operational rule's "artifact EXISTS and is HASHED" gate
Computed output the named artifact the task emits (report / table / model) the artifact whose existence the IP trigger is bound to; "I computed something" is not enough — it must be the named artifact
First failure the pre-declared token the task emits if its acceptance test misses the field that makes the task fail-closed — it is filled before the run, so the agent cannot discover a way to pass that the task author did not foresee
Status a token drawn only from the closure-ladder vocabulary (≤ PASS_TOY) caps the claim at the ceiling; PASS, solved, works are not in the allowed vocabulary, so the agent cannot type them
Patent trigger the IP slot this task's artifact fires — iff the artifact exists binds filing to artifact (operational rule); "no artifact ⇒ no trigger ⇒ DO NOT FILE"
Do-not-say list the forbidden phrases this task must never emit CONTRACT §4 + pack 12 "Do not do," reproduced per-task so the prohibition travels with the work order
Next task the backlog row that runs next (and the branch on this task's outcome) routing without a global view; the agent does not choose what is next — the template tells it, including which "no" node it routes to

Two precision notes the contract forces.

First, the First failure field is filled before the task runs, not after. This is the inversion that makes a low-reasoning agent safe. In an ordinary pipeline, "what went wrong" is discovered after execution; here, the only failure the task is permitted to report is the one pre-declared in the work order. If the task's real-world outcome is "something else went wrong," the honest report is still the pre-declared first failure plus a downgrade — never an improvised "but actually it's fine." CONTRACT §1.2 ("every section AND every chapter MUST name a FIRST FAILURE") is thereby pushed down to the task level: a task with no pre-declared first failure is, per pack 11 acceptance discipline and CONTRACT §7, an invalid task and is rejected before it runs.

Second, the Status field draws from a closed vocabulary, and the ceiling is PASS_TOY. The only tokens an agent may write into Status are the closure-ladder levels and downgrade tokens of CONTRACT §3 — 0 UNDEFINED, 1 TOY_DEFINED, 2 TOY_TESTED, 3 EFT_CANDIDATE (only under the frozen milestone), PASS_TOY, or a downgrade token (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY, FAIL_PURE_GAUGE, FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY, AUDIT_QUANTUM, UV_DELEGATED, FAIL_BACKREACTION, FAIL_CAUSALITY, FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM, FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION). The forbidden phrases of CONTRACT §4 are not in the vocabulary; the agent literally has no token to express "it works." This is how a no-global-view agent is prevented from promoting a candidate: promotion above PASS_TOY requires owner/attorney escalation (CONTRACT §1.4), and the template gives the agent no field in which to assert it.

L11.3 The fourteen work orders, fully expanded

Each task below is given in the pack's exact nine-field template, expanded to full work-order depth. Inputs, files-touched, and computed outputs are named at the granularity an agent needs; first-failure and status are pre-declared from the closure vocabulary; patent triggers are bound to artifacts by the operational rule; do-not-say lists are drawn from CONTRACT §4 and pack 12; next-task routing carries the outcome branch (and names the "no" node it routes to, never "acquire a drive"). Where the worked exemplars G1/G2/G3 let us state the expected result honestly, we do.

Task 1 — rerun latest repo (BRL-1, engine layer)

Task:           rerun latest repo

                negative-control fixtures; the golden expected-value tables.

                quadratures); test fixtures; golden tables; reproduction_report.json (out).

                self-tests AND that all nine negative controls remain FAIL (a control that

First failure:  engine does not reproduce a golden value (self-test diverges) OR a negative

Task 1 is the floor: it establishes BRL-1 (a runnable screening engine over its metric → G_μν → T_eff → NEC/WEC chain plus proper-distance quadratures) and re-validates BRL-2 (the negative-control corpus). It is the only task whose failure routes to "fund cleanup, acquire nothing," and it is deliberately first because every downstream artifact is meaningless if the engine cannot reproduce a Schwarzschild Einstein tensor or holds a leaking control. Acceptance is golden tests match — a binary, machine-checked equality against frozen expected values, not a judgment.

It fires no IP trigger of its own; its product is the integrity of IP-2.

L11.4 The task-invariant fail-closed reading — why no task can leak a PASS

Across all fourteen work orders, five structural invariants hold by construction, and together they are the proof that a no-global-view agent running this backlog cannot manufacture an overclaim.

Invariant 1 — the first failure is pre-declared, so the agent cannot discover an unforeseen PASS. Every task's First failure field is filled before execution. The agent's only permitted failure report is the pre-declared token; if reality differs, the honest output is still the pre-declared first failure plus a downgrade (CONTRACT §1.3, "On any failed, missing, or uncertain computation: DOWNGRADE the claim"). There is no field in which the agent can write "but it actually passed."

Invariant 2 — the status vocabulary is closed and capped at PASS_TOY. The Status field draws only from the closure-ladder tokens (CONTRACT §3). The forbidden phrases of CONTRACT §4 are not in the vocabulary; the agent has no token for "it works," "FTL," "energy solved," or "operational propulsion." Promotion above PASS_TOY requires owner/attorney escalation (CONTRACT §1.4), which the template does not expose.

Invariant 3 — every IP trigger is artifact-bound (the operational rule, per task). A task's Patent trigger fires iff its Computed output artifact exists and is hashed (Files touched). No artifact ⇒ no trigger ⇒ DO NOT FILE. Tasks 2/4/9/10/11 fire IP-2/IP-3/IP-4/IP-5/IP-6 only on a real SourceMatchReport (χ_source < 1) / energy audit / null-controlled model / digital twin / mission overlay. Task 12 audits the bindings; Task 3 guards IP-2 against post-hoc sources; Task 13 gates IP-11; Task 14 frames the option ask. The operational rule is therefore enforced fourteen times, once per task.

Invariant 4 — the do-not-say list travels with the work order. Each task carries its slice of CONTRACT §4 and pack 12 "Do not do." The agent cannot emit a forbidden phrase because the forbidden phrases are listed in the task it is running, not in a distant style guide it has no view of. This is the only way a no-global-view agent can honor a global prohibition.

Invariant 5 — Next task routing has no "no → acquire" edge. Every task's Next task field routes its "no" outcome to a downgrade or a non-acquisition node — software-cleanup-only (Task 1), candidate-downgrade (Tasks 2–11), do-not-file (Task 12), theory-only continuation (Task 13), rewrite-to-option-ask (Task 14). There is no branch, in any of the fourteen tasks, from which a "no" reaches "acquire a drive." This is the backlog-level form of the document-wide structural guarantee.

The composition of these five invariants is the leaf's whole claim: a lower-reasoning agent running this backlog produces, on the current corpus, exactly the document's honest result — engine reproduces (Task 1, PASS_TOY), source fails (Task 2, FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC on G1), energy is exotic-but-visible (Task 4, AUDIT, ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶), and the IP map (Task 12) shows the front-loaded slots live and the CIP/conversion slots unfired. No task can do better than the physics allows, because no task has a field in which to claim it did.

Three structural readings of this backlog follow, and they are the whole point of the handoff.

First, the ordering is by leverage, and items 2–3 are the gating dimensions. Item 1 (freeze the inventory) is a discipline prerequisite — without a frozen, hashed candidate set, the milestone test is evaluated against a moving target and is meaningless. But the leverage sits in items 2 and 3: the SourceMatchReport (item 2, L1) and the energy audit (item 3, L2/L3). These are the source (HC-02) and energy (HC-03) closure dimensions — the two rows of the gap map (L0.1) that gate everything, and precisely the two at which the deepest-surviving exemplar G1 (MID-METRIC-001) dies. Building these two artifacts is what would let a successor say, of any candidate, "here is its source ledger and here is its exoticity burden," which is the substantive content of the BRL-3 → BRL-4 boundary. A successor who builds anything else first has mis-prioritized.

Second, items 4–5 are the anti-cheating artifacts, and they are as important as items 2–3. Item 4 (code the M1 predicate) removes human discretion from the milestone verdict: a coded boolean cannot be talked into a PASS the way a prose criterion can. Item 5 (tie IP triggers to artifact hashes) removes human discretion from CIP filing: a CIP slot that requires a content hash of its named artifact cannot be filed on the expectation that the artifact is "almost done." Together, items 4 and 5 are the mechanical enforcement of the document's two hardest disciplines — the frozen milestone (no self-promotion, CONTRACT §1.4) and the operational rule (no CIP without its artifact, pack 09). They are why the milestone test, once built, cannot be gamed by a motivated successor.

Third, item 6 (the sprint packet) is the deliverable that makes the whole thing hostile-reviewable. A milestone test that only the authors can run is not diligence; it is a claim. The sprint packet — frozen inventory, frozen predicate, six-phase plan, do-not-say list, artifact/hash map — is the object handed to an independent hostile reviewer (BRL-5) so the reviewer can re-run the screening engine, re-derive the source and energy audits, and attack the first-failure ledger. The packet is the bridge from "the authors believe the candidate fails" to "an independent reviewer confirms the candidate fails, and agrees the platform is a rigorous discriminator." That confirmation — not a survivor — is the expected and intended product.

The single load-bearing instruction, restated. The pack opens with "Do not write more sales copy." The successor's value is in the six artifacts, not in more argument. A team that produces a real SourceMatchReport, a real energy audit, a coded predicate, a hash-bound trigger map, and a hostile-review-ready packet has moved the program from BRL-2-with-a-written-test to BRL-2-with-a-built-test, and has done so without crossing a single physics rung or exceeding PASS_TOY.

L12.2 The M1 predicate — carried exactly, as executable code, with each clause read against the gates and against G1

The frozen milestone is the single binary the entire deal turns on, and item 4 of the handoff is implement it as code. The pack gives the predicate in executable form, which we carry verbatim:

milestone_hit(candidate) =
  candidate.status == EFT_CANDIDATE
  and candidate.source.matched == true
  and candidate.source.chi_source < 1
  and candidate.invariance == PASS
  and candidate.causality == PASS
  and candidate.energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE}
  and no gate == FAIL
  and if candidate.uv_dependency then candidate.uv_assumption.named_and_independent == true

This is the executable form of the conversion / BRL-4 frozen-milestone criterion carried through every leaf of Part L: EFT_CANDIDATE reached WITH a matched source ledger, chi_source < 1, invariant + causality gates PASS, NO failed gates, and a NAMED, independently-reviewed UV assumption. There is NO route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." M1 means "worth a deep physics diligence sprint." It does not mean flight-ready. Read clause by clause, with each clause's gate, its forward leaf, and its honest standing against the deepest exemplar:

Predicate clause (verbatim) What it requires Gate / leaf First-failure token if the clause is false

Three precision notes the contract forces on the coded predicate.

The predicate is frozen before the sprint and the code is immutable once funded. This is the option-structure line "frozen milestone predicate" (L9.2) and the pack 12 "Do not do" item "Do not let any agent change the milestone mid-sprint." Coding the predicate (item 4) is what makes the freeze enforceable: a version-pinned, content-hashed boolean cannot be silently softened the way a prose criterion can be re-interpreted. A successor who edits the predicate after results are seen commits a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (self-promotion off the agent's own authority; CONTRACT §1.4) and voids the honesty of the test. The freeze is the legal-and-technical device that prevents the milestone from degenerating into "call it a hit if it looks good."

Energy is never a clean PASS in the predicate — it is AUDIT / PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE. The clause candidate.energy in {AUDIT, PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE} mirrors CONTRACT §3 exactly ("energy_check is never a clean PASS — it is 'pass / audit-visible'"). The milestone does not require the energy problem solved; it requires the exoticity visible and bounded. This is why the forbidden phrase "solves the energy problem" can never appear in a successor's milestone report: the predicate itself only ever certifies audit-visibility, never resolution. A successor who codes the energy clause as a clean == PASS has mis-implemented the predicate and broken the contract.

The UV clause requires the assumption named and independently reviewed, not solved. The last clause — if candidate.uv_dependency then candidate.uv_assumption.named_and_independent == true — is workstream-C's terminal deliverable (L4, HC-08): the open UV axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 (global UV stability OPEN, axiom UNADOPTED, per the TOE_FINAL diff) may be named as a dependency and independently reviewed, but never adopted as a mechanism. A UV_DELEGATED verdict with a named, reviewed axiom does not block the milestone; an unadopted-treated-as-adopted or engineered UV dependence converts the delegation into a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and blocks it. The successor codes this as a conditional — it only fires when uv_dependency is true — and it certifies naming and independence, never closure.

Where the worked exemplar G1 stands against the coded predicate (honest reading the successor inherits). The deepest-surviving exemplar, G1 (MID-METRIC-001), fails the predicate at the first physics clause. G1 declares vacuum yet T_eff ≠ 0 (100% source mismatch), so candidate.source.matched == false and the engine emits the terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (G1 §8 / Gate 5 / HC-02). The root cause is the energy gate (Gate 6 / HC-03): the real, invariant forward-distance deficit is sourced by a negative effective energy density — ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ in geometrized units at the lobe center, exotic, with WEC/NEC/DEC violated and SEC marginal-static / violated-boosted — which no declared field source supplies. G1 passes G1–G4 (the lobe is real curved geometry with a real invariant distance deficit, R = −4.0404×10⁻⁴ ≠ 0, not the NC-2 coordinate illusion) and is the document's only affirmative structural pass — and it is killed at source/energy, exactly the two gating dimensions (items 2–3 of the handoff) that block BRL-2 → BRL-4. Against the coded M1 predicate, G1 evaluates: source.matched == false ⇒ milestone_hit == false ⇒ no milestone, no conversion. The terminal status is 2 TOY_TESTED / AUDIT, token TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC; the ceiling PASS_TOY is never exceeded. No candidate in this document satisfies the M1 predicate; the coded predicate is, today, un-satisfied by construction, and the successor's job is to build the artifacts that would let it be honestly evaluated on a future candidate — not to engineer a pass.

L12.3 The exact ask to a strategic acquirer — carried verbatim, and why it is the only honest ask

The pack states the exact ask as a single block-quoted sentence, which we carry verbatim:

Option the screening-platform IP and fund a 90-day hostile validation sprint. Conversion to acquisition/JV occurs only if the frozen M1_EFT_CANDIDATE predicate is hit and hostile review agrees.

This is the buyer logic of the entire document, compressed to one sentence and pointed at the decision-maker. It is carried, unweakened, from the buyer logic threaded through every leaf of Part L: a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer should NOT buy "a claimed engine" — OPTION the IP, FUND a 90-day hostile validation sprint, and CONVERT only if the frozen BRL-4 milestone is hit. The natural counterparty here is a Mars-transport-scale program: for such a buyer the validated screening method is a cheap R&D option — an option fee plus a bounded validation sprint — rather than a purchase of nonexistent hardware, and the structure is asymmetric and downside-protected.

This ask is the destination of the whole journey, and the journey is what makes the ask trustworthy. A strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer wants Mars sooner, and the road to "sooner" runs straight through exotic-propulsion proposals that are seductive precisely because they promise to collapse the trip — a buyer in this seat receives a steady stream of such ideas, and almost all of them fail silently. The reason a buyer should arrive at this sentence, and not at "buy the drive," is everything the platform did before reaching here: the screening engine is built to refuse its own most tempting result, it found a real, local, coordinate-invariant forward-distance deficit in the deepest exemplar G1 (MID-METRIC-001) — the single most headline-worthy thing in the corpus — and it killed that candidate at source and energy (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, energy AUDIT, ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ at the lobe center, exotic) rather than promote it. A weaker document would have led with that deficit; this one computed the required source, found no declared field supplies it, and let the candidate die. That refusal is the asset. The acquirer is therefore not asked to believe in a drive — the acquirer is asked to fund the continuation of that refusal under hostile conditions and to take the IP window only if the refusal finally has nothing left to refuse. Stated as the firewall that governs even the deal: there is no path from a "no" result to "acquire a drive." The discipline that earned the buyer's trust before the deal is the same discipline that binds the buyer at the deal; conversion fires on a frozen, coded predicate plus an accepting independent hostile review, never on the temptation of a good-looking local effect, and never on enthusiasm. The ask has exactly three moves, and the order and conditionality of the three are the whole point:

Fund a 90-day hostile validation sprint the six-phase, time-boxed, pre-registered validation sprint (L0.5) the buyer funds it the sprint is the price of information, not the price of an engine; its scope and milestone are frozen before funding

Why this is the only honest ask, and the asymmetry that makes it rational. The wrong ask — "buy a Mars spaceship engine" — has no honest answer, because there is no engine: the platform is a discriminator/screening tool, NOT a Mars spaceship, current ceiling PASS_TOY, current standing BRL-2, and the deepest candidate G1 dies unsourced and exotic. The right ask — option the IP, fund a frozen-milestone sprint, convert only on the predicate — has a bounded downside (the option premium plus the sprint cost) and a real IP payoff either way. The protectable value is the discriminator — the screening filter, method, and IP — not a survivor, so the asset is valuable to any rigorous frontier-R&D acquirer independent of whether a drive is ever built. If every candidate fails — the expected outcome (CONTRACT §1.6) — the acquirer retains a rigorous, IP-protected exotic-propulsion screening platform and its validated negative-control corpus, reusable as a diligence tool for any exotic-propulsion claim, this document's or a competitor's. If one candidate hits the frozen M1 and hostile review agrees, the acquirer controls the patent window before disclosure. The option is cheap relative to either payoff; conversion is fired by a frozen predicate plus an accepting audit, never by enthusiasm; and — the structural guarantee carried through every leaf — there is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive." The decision tree (L10) makes this concrete: every "no" routes to software cleanup only, reject, keep/option the screening IP, theory-only continuation, simulation-only program, stop at lab research, or research program only — never to acquisition.

Two readings the handoff requires.

The "do not do" list is the operational expression of the forbidden-phrase discipline (CONTRACT §4), pointed at the handoff moment. The most dangerous moment in the life of an honest failure-mode document is the handoff — the instant it leaves the disciplined authors and reaches a successor or an intermediary who may be tempted to "improve" the pitch. The six prohibitions are precisely the six "improvements" that would destroy the document's integrity: buy an engine (overclaim the asset), imply heavy-lift-vehicle integration (overclaim the readiness), imply physical source availability (overclaim the source — the very gate G1 fails), convert local shortening into travel time (overclaim the mission — the exact thing G3 proves is invalid), file CIPs without artifacts (overclaim the IP), and change the milestone mid-sprint (overclaim the result). Each is a forbidden phrase or downgrade token in disguise; each is foreclosed by a specific leaf and contract clause; and each is the kind of small dishonesty that, once admitted, would unravel the whole fail-closed posture.

The fourth item is the one most likely to be violated, and G3 is the firewall. "Do not convert local shortening into travel time" is the prohibition a sales-minded reader is most tempted to break, because the local lobe score S_L > 0 feels like "faster to Mars." It is not. The No-Global-Aggregation theorem (leaf G3, verified) proves the local shortening score S_L does not integrate to a global Δt: arrival time is set by ∫ δN dλ / N² with first-order front/back cancellation and second-order Raychaudhuri sign-definiteness, so a positive local score does not imply a reduced global travel time. Any handoff document, memo, or slide that writes "Mars in days" or "cuts the trip" on the strength of a local lobe score commits a FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM against a theorem, not merely against caution. The successor must carry G3 forward as the standing answer to the most seductive overclaim in the program.
