The handoff is not a pitch: its headline instruction is "do not write more sales copy" and its entire content is a backlog of six software/analysis artifacts to build, not claims to assert; the only acquisition move in the "exact ask" (conversion) is gated by a frozen, pre-registered, coded predicate plus an accepting independent hostile review — never by "promising" — and the only apparatus-flavored filing (IP-12) is gated by independent physical evidence that BRL-2 does not have and cannot manufacture. The "do not do" list is the opposite of laundering: it names and forbids the six specific dishonesties a sales-minded successor would commit (buy-an-engine, heavy-lift-vehicle-install, source-available, Mars-in-days, paper-CIPs, moved-goalposts), each bound to a downgrade token and a theorem (G3) or contract clause. The expected outcome of acting on this handoff is "build the artifacts, run the test, the milestone misses, the acquirer owns a rigorous discriminator and its negative-control corpus" — a win that does not require the ladder to be climbed, because the protectable value was always the discriminator, not a survivor. A pitch deck promises the product; this handoff prices information, instructs the successor to build artifacts rather than argue, refuses to file a CIP without its artifact hash, refuses to convert without the frozen predicate, and — like the rest of the document — is engineered so that every incompleteness downgrades the claim rather than inflating it. There is no route from a "no" node to "acquire a drive," and there is no handoff here of a drive, because no drive exists to hand off.

The Full Technical Design

Bridge — here the Engine stops being described and starts being watched at work. Everything above told you who the protagonist is and what it refuses to claim; everything below is the protagonist actually doing it, gate by gate, with real numbers. This is the part of the journey where trust is either earned or lost — so read it watching for the moment the Engine could overclaim and declines.

The reference implementation above proves the kernel runs (14/14). The chapters below are the deep technical foundation: corpus authority and status discipline, the formal geometry, the candidate-mode taxonomy, the ten hard-challenge closure chapters (HC-01 through HC-10), the software architecture, the worked results, the red-team, and the patent translation.

B1 — Corpus Authority Doctrine & the Effective Action

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED · PASS_TOY (ceiling) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

B1.0 Reader's contract for this chapter

This chapter establishes the governing-law layer of the Mars metric-interface drive platform. Everything downstream — every candidate excitation profile Ξ_drive(t,x), every gate card, every Mars-mission overlay — derives its authority, and its limits of authority, from what is written here. The chapter does three things and only three things:

  1. It fixes exactly what the four corpus source documents license, and exactly what they forbid, as a closed authority map with no silent extrapolation.
  2. It derives the effective action S_eff the platform uses as its low-energy template, and the stress-energy tensor T_μν extracted from it, with every term carrying a declared status rather than an asserted physical reality.
  3. It states the three-layer field discipline (× / ⊕ / ⊗) and the EFT cutoff / UV-delegation rule that together decide whether any given mode may be evaluated at all, and at what ceiling.

The single most important sentence in the chapter, stated up front so it cannot be missed, is this:

The framework treats corpus constraints as configuration data. It does NOT require the unified theory (Fable/TOE) to be correct. The platform is a classifier and a failure-mode engine. If the corpus is wrong, the platform still runs; it simply runs against a different configuration and reports different first failures. No conclusion in this document is conditioned on "the Fable theory is true."

That sentence is not rhetorical. It is an architectural commitment that this chapter makes load-bearing and that every later chapter inherits. The corpus is data fed to the gates, not axioms the gates assume.

Authority block (per Corpus Doctrine §"Lower-reasoning AI instructions"):

Authority:
- Geometry:            Fable_GUT — active branch geometry object exists (M4 × K_gauge × F+)
- Force interface:     Fable_Forces — single Einstein-frame metric, one-parent projection
- Quantization:        Fable_Quantum — BRST/BV physical-state gates (Q_BRST|Ψ⟩=0, not exact, +norm)
- UV/global boundary:  TOE_FINAL diff — global UV stability OPEN; B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED
- Patent relevance:    corpus-as-configuration; theory-correctness NOT required (claim-independence)
Status:
- strongest allowed status:  PASS_TOY (status-labeled simulation result)
- forbidden promotion:        any operational / physical / propulsion claim; UV-axiom-as-mechanism

B1.1 Why the authority doctrine matters (the failure this chapter prevents)

The characteristic failure mode of speculative-physics engineering documents is authority laundering: a result that is licensed only as "the geometry object is internally consistent" silently becomes "the geometry produces thrust," because nobody wrote down the boundary between the two and then enforced it. A corpus document says something narrow and true (e.g., a single Einstein-frame metric exists with one-parent force projection); a later section quietly treats that as license for something broad and unproven (e.g., therefore a comoving asymmetric metric profile lowers forward proper distance with a physical source). The error is never in the corpus quote. It is in the scope creep between the quote and the claim.

This chapter exists to make scope creep machine-detectable. The authority map below is written so that every later claim can be checked against a single question: "Which corpus row licenses this, and does that row actually license a claim of this strength?" If the answer is "no row licenses it," the claim is downgraded, not deleted — we keep it as a TOY_MODEL or AUDIT candidate and name its first failure. We never promote it on our own authority (Build Contract §1.4).

The reason this is the first technical chapter rather than an appendix: if the authority boundaries are not nailed down before any excitation profile is evaluated, every downstream gate inherits an ambiguous license and the whole 500-page argument becomes uncheckable. Authority is a precondition for falsifiability here.

First failure (B1.1): if a reader cannot, for an arbitrary downstream claim, point to the single authority row that licenses it and confirm the claim does not exceed that row's strength, the doctrine has failed and the claim must be downgraded to UNDEFINED pending re-derivation. The doctrine is only as strong as the weakest under-cited claim it admits.

B1.2 Formal object: the corpus as a configuration tuple

We treat the corpus not as a set of beliefs but as a typed data structure consumed by the platform. Define the corpus configuration:

C = (G, Φ, Q, U)

where each component is one source document reduced to its licensable content — the propositions the platform is permitted to read as constraints. Formally each is a pair (L, ¬L) of a license set and a forbid set:

  • G = (L_G, ¬L_G) — from Fable_GUT (Paper I, .../rendered/GUT/GUT.md; see §2.6 for the full path and the App A1/A2/A3/A, C2/C4/C7/C8/C9, D, E/E′, GP, CR anchors)
  • Φ = (L_Φ, ¬L_Φ) — from Fable_Forces (Paper II, .../rendered/forces/Forces_F1_main_manuscript.md; full path in §2.6)
  • Q = (L_Q, ¬L_Q) — from Fable_Quantum (Paper III, .../rendered/quantum/Quantum_Q1_main_manuscript.md; full path in §2.6)
  • U = (L_U, ¬L_U) — from TOE_FINAL (Paper IV / Scoped TOE, .../rendered/toe/Scoped_TOE_ST1_main_statement.md; full path in §2.6)

The platform's authority function is then total and explicit:

authorize(claim) =
    LICENSED      if  ∃ row r ∈ {G,Φ,Q,U} : claim ⊑ L_r   and  claim ∉ ¬L_r   for all rows
    FORBIDDEN     if  ∃ row r : claim ∈ ¬L_r
    UNLICENSED    otherwise                         # not forbidden, but no row supports it

The ordering relation claim ⊑ L_r reads "claim is no stronger than license set L_r permits." Three outcomes, no fourth. Note the asymmetry that fail-closed discipline demands: UNLICENSED is not LICENSED. A claim that no corpus row forbids but also no corpus row supports is not admitted as true — it is admitted only as a TOY_MODEL/AUDIT candidate that must earn status through the drive-specific gates. This is the data-structure form of "downgrade-don't-invent."

This typed view is what makes the headline commitment operational. Because C is data, swapping C for a different configuration C' (a corrected corpus, a competing theory, or a deliberately falsified control) changes only which rows fire. It does not change the gate machinery. The correctness of C is therefore never assumed by the gates; it is an input whose effect is visible in the output. That is precisely what "does not require the unified theory to be correct" means at the level of types.

First failure (B1.2): if authorize(claim) ever resolves an UNLICENSED claim to LICENSED — i.e., a claim that no row's L_r actually supports is silently admitted as true because no row forbids it — the formal object has failed and the claim must be downgraded to a TOY_MODEL/AUDIT candidate. The first failure of the configuration tuple is any collapse of the three-valued {LICENSED, FORBIDDEN, UNLICENSED} output into a permissive two-valued one; fail-closed requires that UNLICENSED ≠ LICENSED hold by construction, not by convention.

B1.3 Corpus authority: the four sources, what each licenses vs forbids

This is the spine of the chapter. Each subsection takes one source document, states the narrow true thing it says, the exact license that grants, and the forbid set — the claims that look like they follow but do not. The forbid sets are non-optional: violating one is an immediate FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION downgrade (Build Contract §3 downgrade tree).

B1.3.1 Fable_GUT — "the geometry object exists"

Narrow true content licensed (L_G). Fable_GUT (Paper I, GUT/GUT.md, App A1/A2/A3/A; see §2.6) supplies a frozen active geometry: a single parent compactification with product structure

M4 × K_gauge × F+ ,    K6 = SU(3)/T² ,    S² ,    S¹_Y (hypercharge circle) ,    F+ (chamber)

together with an admissibility predicate (which configurations are geometrically allowed) and a freeze discipline (the active branch is fixed; you do not get to re-pick the compactification mid-argument to rescue a candidate). The license L_G is: "a well-defined geometry object with these factors and this admissibility/freeze structure exists and may be used as the geometric substrate of an excitation profile."

What this licenses for the drive. Layer-× content (see B1.5): the metric base g_μν, the internal metric on K_gauge, and the existence of compact factors S², S¹_Y whose moduli φ^I can appear as fields. It licenses "there is a place for δg_μν and δG_AB to live, and an admissibility test ⊕ that decides which live there."

Forbid set (¬L_G). Fable_GUT does NOT license: a working-drive proof, a UV completion, or any hardware claim. Concretely, the following are members of ¬L_G and trigger immediate downgrade:

Tempting over-claim Why it is in ¬L_G Downgrade token
"The compactification is UV-stable, so the candidate is closed." Global UV stability is not a GUT-licensed property — it is U's domain, and there it is OPEN. UV_DELEGATED
"The geometry being admissible means the metric profile is sourced." Admissibility is ⊕ (does it survive constraints), not ⊗/source (does a stress ledger generate it). FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
"Freeze discipline lets me re-tune K6 to make the lobe appear." Freeze forbids exactly this; the active branch is fixed. FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION
"Geometry exists ⇒ drive exists." Pure authority laundering; existence of a substrate is not existence of a mechanism. FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION

First failure (B1.3.1): the moment a candidate's argument requires changing the frozen active branch to work, GUT authority is void and the candidate downgrades to FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION. Freeze discipline is the first wall.

B1.3.2 Fable_Forces — "the force/gravity interface, with honest source accounting"

Narrow true content licensed (L_Φ). Fable_Forces (Paper II, forces/Forces_F1_main_manuscript.md; see §2.6) supplies a single Einstein-frame metric (not a frame-juggling family), one-parent force projection (forces descend from one parent structure, not multiple double-counted ones), a 4D gravity interface, and crucially a shared/visible stress-energy coupling with an explicit no-double-counting rule. The license L_Φ is: "the map from fields to gravity is a single-Einstein-frame, source-coupled interface; you may compute T_μν and feed it to G_μν once, visibly."

What this licenses for the drive. It licenses the entire source-matching machinery of chapter B-series and the action of B1.4: the right-hand side of Einstein's equation is sourced by declared fields, and the coupling is shared (the same T_μν that gravitates is the one built from L_matter + L_gauge + L_scalar). It also licenses the Einstein-frame statement that there is one metric whose R term carries the (M_Pl²/2) coefficient.

Forbid set (¬L_Φ). Fable_Forces explicitly does NOT license bypassing source/energy accounting. Members of ¬L_Φ:

Tempting over-claim Why it is in ¬L_Φ Downgrade token
"The metric profile is its own source." An ansatz is a target, not a generator (B1.4.4). The interface demands a ledger. FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
"Count the same field as source in two frames to balance the books." Directly violates one-parent / no-double-counting. FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY
"The energy can be negative because the geometry needs it." Forces licenses visible accounting, never sign-assumed exotic energy. FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY
"Gravity interface ⇒ the lobe is physical." The interface tells you how a source gravitates, not that a particular profile is sourced. AUDIT

First failure (B1.3.2): if T_μν reconstructed from the geometry (T_eff) and T_μν assembled from declared fields (T_fields) do not match within tolerance (norm_ΔT above threshold), Forces authority does NOT save the candidate — it condemns it, because the interface is exactly the thing that makes the mismatch visible. First failure is the largest-magnitude unmatched component, first_unmatched_component.

B1.3.3 Fable_Quantum — "physical-state discipline, not interacting QG closure"

Narrow true content licensed (L_Q). Fable_Quantum (Paper III, quantum/Quantum_Q1_main_manuscript.md; see §2.6) supplies BRST/BV physical-state gates: a state |Ψ⟩ is physical iff it is BRST-closed and not BRST-exact, with positive norm —

Q_BRST |Ψ⟩ = 0     and     |Ψ⟩ ∉ Im(Q_BRST)     and     ⟨Ψ|Ψ⟩ > 0

— together with the resulting physical Hilbert space and the UQF gate logic that operationalizes this. The license L_Q is: "you may test whether a quantized excitation mode is a physical state (gauge-invariant, positive-norm, non-spurious) using the BRST cohomology condition."

What this licenses for the drive. It licenses layer-⊗ quantization status for any mode that is quantized: the gauge_check and the BRST status of an excitation. A δA_μ^a perturbation that is pure gauge (BRST-exact) is spurious — it is detected and downgraded, not counted as a real degree of freedom.

Forbid set (¬L_Q). Fable_Quantum does NOT license claiming full interacting quantum-gravity closure. The interacting gravitational sector stays AUDIT — there is no license here for "the quantum dynamics of the coupled metric-field system are under control." Members of ¬L_Q:

Tempting over-claim Why it is in ¬L_Q Downgrade token
"BRST passes ⇒ the interacting theory is consistent." BRST gates states at the level licensed; interacting QG closure is unproven. AUDIT_QUANTUM
"Physical-state ⇒ the mode sources real stress-energy." Physicality of a state ≠ a matched classical source ledger. route to source_check
"Quantum gravity solved for this mode." Forbidden phrase; flatly outside L_Q. AUDIT_QUANTUM

First failure (B1.3.3): if a candidate mode's physicality cannot be decided — BRST status unknown because the mode is in the interacting sector — the mode is AUDIT_QUANTUM, never PASS. Undecidable is a failure state here, by design.

B1.3.4 TOE_FINAL diff — "the status/UV boundary, and the axiom we must NOT adopt"

Narrow true content licensed (L_U). TOE_FINAL (Paper IV / Scoped TOE, toe/Scoped_TOE_ST1_main_statement.md; see §2.6) supplies the global status boundary: it records that global UV stability is OPEN, identifies Gap-04, and names the axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 as UNADOPTED. The license L_U is narrow and almost entirely negative: "you may use this document to know where the UV boundary is and that it is open; you may set status flags accordingly."

What this licenses for the drive. It licenses the UV-delegation rule (B1.6): any candidate whose validity depends on global compactification/UV stability is flagged UV_DELEGATED and may not be promoted past that ceiling. It licenses honesty about the boundary.

Forbid set (¬L_U). The single most dangerous over-claim in the entire project lives here. TOE_FINAL does NOT license adopting the open UV axiom as a propulsion mechanism. The axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is UNADOPTED; treating it as adopted to manufacture global stability — and then leaning on that "stability" as the thing that makes a drive work — is the canonical forbidden move.

Tempting over-claim Why it is in ¬L_U Downgrade token
"Adopt B-UQFC-14-UV-1; now global stability is solved." The axiom is explicitly UNADOPTED; this is "UV completion adopted," a forbidden phrase. FAIL
"Gap-04 is closed for our candidate." Gap-04 status is OPEN at the global level; no candidate closes it locally. UV_DELEGATED
"Use UV stability as the drive's energy/mechanism." The most severe authority crime: open axiom → propulsion. FAIL (hard)

First failure (B1.3.4): any candidate whose mechanism requires B-UQFC-14-UV-1 to be true fails hard — not UV_DELEGATED (which is for dependency), but FAIL, because it is adopting an unadopted axiom as mechanism. The distinction between depending on an open boundary (delegate) and adopting an open axiom as the engine (fail) is the sharpest line in the doctrine.

B1.3.5 Authority-to-claim ladder (consolidated)

Combining the four forbid sets yields the platform's master authority-to-claim ladder. This is the lookup table every downstream gate consults:

Claim type Required authority Default if unsupported
"geometry object exists" G (Fable_GUT) UNDEFINED
"force projection is one-parent" Φ (Fable_Forces) UNDEFINED
"4D gravity target / shared source coupling" Φ gravity interface FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
"quantized state is physical" Q (Fable_Quantum UQF) AUDIT_QUANTUM
"global stability" none available by default UV_DELEGATED
"propulsion / operational drive" not licensed by any row only ever a TOY_MODEL/AUDIT simulation candidate

The bottom two rows are the whole point. No corpus row licenses propulsion. The strongest status any candidate reaches in this document is PASS_TOY. (Mandatory manuscript paragraph, Corpus Doctrine §"Mandatory manuscript paragraph":)

The uploaded corpus is used as an authority for geometry, force-routing, quantization discipline, and status boundaries. It is not used as authority for operational propulsion. Any candidate metric-interface profile introduced here must earn its own status through the drive-specific gates.

B1.4 The effective action S_eff and the stress-energy tensor T_μν

B1.4.1 The declared template

The platform's low-energy template, per the Formal-Action appendix (29), is the Einstein-frame effective action:

S_eff = ∫ d⁴x √(−g) [
            (M_Pl²/2) R
          − (1/4) Z_ab(φ) F^a_μν F^{b μν}
          − (1/2) G_IJ(φ) ∂_μ φ^I ∂^μ φ^J
          − V(φ)
          + L_matter
          + L_constraint
          + L_EFT
        ]

Critical framing, stated before any term is used: this is a declared template, not "the corpus action." Appendix 29 says so explicitly — "this appendix does not assert that the action is the final corpus action." S_eff is the data structure into which a candidate's fields are loaded so that the gates can run. Its authority is "a controlled template for constructing and testing candidate metric-interface models," nothing more. We are not claiming S_eff is the universe; we are claiming it is the worksheet on which a candidate either matches or fails to match.

B1.4.2 Per-term status declaration (no term is "physical" by assertion)

Every term carries a required status, not an assumed physical reality (appendix 29 "Required declaration"). The Einstein-frame R term is the only one that is unconditionally "declared" because it is the 4D gravity target the whole interface is defined against; everything else is declared-or-inactive at best, and some terms are flagged high-risk:

Term Symbol Role in drive Required status First-failure hook
Einstein–Hilbert (M_Pl²/2) R leading 4D gravity target (the LHS G_μν lives here) declared none — it is the reference frame
Gauge kinetic −(1/4) Z_ab F^a F^b candidate stress source via T^gauge declared or inactive Z_ab field-dependence hides a modulus
Scalar / modulus −(1/2) G_IJ ∂φ^I ∂φ^J − V(φ) candidate stress source high-risk if compactification-sensitive V(φ) tuned to fake a source
Matter L_matter ordinary source contribution declared or inactive matter smuggled to balance ΔT
Constraint L_constraint admissibility / gate term (⊕) simulation-only constraint term doing source's job
EFT corrections L_EFT cutoff-limited operators audit if used operator used past its cutoff

Two of these flags carry the chapter's sharpest warnings. The scalar/modulus term is high-risk because a moduli potential V(φ) is exactly the kind of thing a careless argument tunes to manufacture whatever stress-energy a desired metric needs — and moduli are compactification-sensitive, which drags in the OPEN UV boundary (U). The constraint term L_constraint is simulation-only: it encodes admissibility (⊕), and it must never be allowed to act as a source. A constraint term contributing to the right-hand side of Einstein's equation is a smuggled source and an instant FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.

B1.4.3 Extracting T_μν

The stress-energy tensor is defined by the standard variational rule (appendix 29 "Stress-energy derivation"), and the appendix is emphatic that this step is mandatory — "a source is not 'present' because prose says it is present":

T_μν = −(2/√(−g)) · δS_matter / δg^μν

Applied to the declared field templates, this yields the closed forms the platform actually computes. For a non-abelian gauge field with F^a_μν = ∂_μ A^a_ν − ∂_ν A^a_μ + f^{abc} A^b_μ A^c_ν:

T^gauge_μν = Z_ab ( F^a_μρ F^{b ρ}_ν − (1/4) g_μν F^a_ρσ F^{b ρσ} )

For a scalar/modulus multiplet with metric G_IJ(φ) on field space:

T^scalar_μν = G_IJ ∂_μ φ^I ∂_ν φ^J − g_μν [ (1/2) G_IJ ∂_ρ φ^I ∂^ρ φ^J + V(φ) ]

And the diagnostic-only effective-fluid placeholder, which appendix 29 stresses is "a diagnostic placeholder, never a physical mechanism":

T_μν = (ρ + p) u_μ u_ν + p g_μν + π_μν          # DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — not a generator

The fluid form is allowed to describe a mismatch (e.g., "the unmatched stress looks like anisotropic pressure π_μν of magnitude X"), never to supply it. If a candidate's only "source" is an effective fluid with hand-chosen ρ, p, it is unsourced; the fluid is a label on the gap, not a fill for it.

B1.4.4 "Why an ansatz is not a source" (mandatory subsection)

Appendix 29 requires this subsection by name, and it is the conceptual heart of the source discipline. A metric profile Ξ_drive is a target, not a generator. Writing down a comoving, front/back-asymmetric δg_μν(t,x) that would lower forward proper distance specifies what geometry we want. It says nothing about what produces that geometry. The generator — the only thing that licenses calling the geometry "sourced" — is either a stress-energy ledger T_μν built from declared fields, or an effective action that yields one. The Einstein equation runs left from right: declared fields → T_fields → G_μν → metric. Running it right from left ("here's the metric I want, therefore some source exists") is the unsourced-metric fallacy and is the single most common way speculative metric-engineering documents fool themselves.

The platform mechanizes the distinction with a source-matching report (appendix 29 "Source-matching report"). Given a candidate, it computes:

T_eff                = stress-energy REQUIRED by the candidate geometry  (from G_μν = T_eff, i.e. read off the metric)
T_fields             = stress-energy SUPPLIED by declared fields         (sum of T^gauge + T^scalar + T^matter)
Δ_T = T_eff − T_fields
norm_T_eff, norm_T_fields, norm_Δ_T
closure_score        = 1 − norm_Δ_T / max(norm_T_eff, ε)
first_unmatched_component                                                 # the named first failure

This maps onto the source classes S0–S5 (appendix 29 "Source classes"), which fix the maximum claim a candidate can reach based purely on how well its declared fields reproduce its geometry:

Class Definition Max claim
S0 no source declared metric toy only
S1 inferred source only (read off geometry, no fields) unsourced-geometry diagnostic
S2 source template declared, mismatch large AUDIT
S3 source template matches the toy metric toy sourced candidate (toward PASS_TOY)
S4 source template matches and EFT ratios pass EFT candidate
S5 experimental / physical source outside this pack

The class ladder is the source half of why nothing reaches operational status: S5 is explicitly out of scope, and S4 ("EFT candidate") is the ceiling the platform can even attempt — and reaching it still requires the EFT cutoff gate of B1.6 to pass, and still produces a status-labeled simulation result, not a physical claim.

B1.4.5 Worked micro-example: a pure-gauge "lobe" fails closed

To make the machinery concrete with real numbers, consider the simplest negative control the platform runs against S_eff. Take a toy candidate whose entire excitation is a δA_μ^a configuration that is pure gauge in an abelian (U(1)-type) direction: A^a_μ = ∂_μ Λ^a for some Λ^a(t,x), with the structure constants in that direction set to zero (f^{abc} → 0). Compute the field strength:

F^a_μν = ∂_μ A^a_ν − ∂_ν A^a_μ + f^{abc} A^b_μ A^c_ν
       = ∂_μ∂_ν Λ^a − ∂_ν∂_μ Λ^a + 0
       = 0           (abelian sector: partials commute, no f^{abc} term)

The two derivative terms cancel identically (partial derivatives commute), so in the abelian sector F^a_μν ≡ 0 exactly. Honest qualification (do not over-generalize): for a genuinely non-abelian direction the simple gradient ansatz A^a_μ = ∂_μ Λ^a does not give F = 0 — the residual f^{abc}(∂_μ Λ^b)(∂_ν Λ^c) survives and is generically nonzero. The correct non-abelian flat connection (true pure gauge) is A_μ = g^{-1} ∂_μ g (matrix form), for which F_μν ≡ 0 by construction. This negative control is therefore stated for the abelian/flat-connection case where the cancellation is exact; the non-abelian gradient ansatz is a different (and not pure-gauge) object and is not what is being rejected here. With F^a_μν = 0 (exact, abelian) or F_μν = 0 (exact, flat connection):

T^gauge_μν = Z_ab ( F^a_μρ F^{b ρ}_ν − (1/4) g_μν F^a_ρσ F^{b ρσ} ) = 0   (since F = 0)

So norm_T_fields = 0. But the metric profile δg_μν we wrote down to get a forward lobe has norm_T_eff > 0 (a real geometry needs a real source). Therefore:

norm_Δ_T = norm_T_eff  >  0
closure_score = 1 − norm_T_eff / norm_T_eff = 0      # worst possible
first_unmatched_component = the dominant component of T_eff (e.g. T_eff_{xx})

Two gates fire simultaneously and the candidate is double-failed, which is exactly the behavior we want from a negative control:

  • Source gate: S0/S1 — the declared field supplies zero stress (F = 0); the metric is unsourced ⇒ FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.
  • Gauge gate (BRST): the mode is BRST-exact (A = ∂Λ is pure gauge ⇒ |Ψ⟩ ∈ Im Q_BRST) ⇒ it is spurious ⇒ FAIL_PURE_GAUGE.

A pure-gauge "drive" is the canonical thing that looks like it does something (you can draw the A-field arrows) but is a coordinate/gauge artifact with no invariant content and no source. The platform catches it before it can ever appear in a Mars overlay. Concrete numbers: with a toy δg chosen so norm_T_eff = 1.0 (arb. units), the pure-gauge candidate gives norm_T_fields = 0, norm_Δ_T = 1.0, closure_score = 0.00. That 0.00 is the chapter's worked proof that the action machinery is fail-closed, not fail-open.

B1.4.6 Pseudocode: the action/source gate

function evaluate_against_Seff(candidate Ξ):
    # 1. Declare every field's layer and type (B1.5); reject undeclared fields.
    for f in candidate.active_fields:
        assert f.layer in {"×", "⊕", "⊗"}            # else FAIL_DEFINITION
        assert f.type  in {metric, mixed_metric, internal,
                           gauge, scalar, matter, ghost, auxiliary}

    # 2. Build T_fields ONLY from source-eligible terms. Constraint term is NOT a source.
    T_fields = 0
    for term in Seff.terms:
        if term is L_constraint:        continue          # simulation-only; NEVER a source
        if term is L_EFT and not term.within_cutoff:      # B1.6
            return AUDIT("EFT operator used past cutoff χ≥1")
        T_fields += stress_energy_of(term)                # T_μν = -(2/√-g) δS/δg^{μν}

    # 3. Read off T_eff REQUIRED by the candidate metric (right side of Einstein eq).
    T_eff = einstein_required_source(candidate.metric)    # G_μν / M_Pl² ⇒ T_eff

    # 4. Match. The gap IS the first failure.
    Δ_T          = T_eff - T_fields
    closure      = 1 - norm(Δ_T) / max(norm(T_eff), ε)
    first_unmatched = argmax_component(abs(Δ_T))

    # 5. Classify into S0..S4 and CAP the status. Never invent a source to close Δ_T.
    cls = classify_source(T_fields, closure)              # S0..S4 (S5 out of scope)
    return GateCard(source_class=cls,
                    closure_score=closure,
                    first_failure=first_unmatched,
                    energy_check="PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE",    # energy is NEVER a clean PASS
                    ceiling="PASS_TOY")

Note line 5's comment and the energy_check value: per Build Contract §3, energy_check is never a clean PASS — it is "pass / audit-visible." The platform reports the energy budget so a reviewer can see it; it does not certify the energy as benign. Hidden exoticity (a sign-assumed negative-energy term smuggled in to close Δ_T) is caught here as FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY.

First failure (B1.4): the action machinery's first failure is first_unmatched_component of Δ_T. If a candidate cannot drive norm_Δ_T below threshold with declared, source-eligible fields, it is unsourced and capped at S1/S2 — AUDIT at best. The action does not promote anything; it only reveals where the source ledger fails to balance.

B1.5 The three-layer field discipline (× / ⊕ / ⊗)

B1.5.1 The layers

Every excitation component of Ξ_drive = {δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge data} MUST map to exactly one layer (Corpus Doctrine §"Three-layer discipline"; Build Contract §2). The layers are not decorative; they route a component to the right gate and forbid it from claiming a property it cannot have:

Layer Meaning Drive interpretation Gate it routes to
× metric / geometric base spacetime metric g_μν, internal metric, compact factors S², S¹_Y invariant-distance gate (is the effect coordinate-invariant?)
⊕ admissibility / projection / chamber which modes survive constraints (F+ chamber, admissibility predicate) admissibility gate (does it survive ⊕? — NOT a source)
⊗ bundles / operators / quantization fields, states, BRST, stress ledgers source gate + BRST/UQF gate

B1.5.2 The no-smuggling rules

The layers exist to enforce five canonical no-smuggling rules (Corpus Doctrine §"Canonical no-smuggling rules"), each of which is a discipline that prevents one specific authority crime:

  1. If a field appears, declare its type — metric, mixed-metric, internal, gauge, scalar, matter, ghost, or auxiliary. An undeclared field is a FAIL_DEFINITION. (This is why the pseudocode of B1.4.6 asserts f.type first.)
  2. If a field sources geometry, provide the stress-energy ledger. No ledger ⇒ FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC. This binds layer-⊗ source claims to the T_μν machinery of B1.4.
  3. If a mode is quantized, provide its gauge/BRST status. Unknown ⇒ AUDIT_QUANTUM. This binds quantization to Q's authority.
  4. If a compactification mode is used, declare the UV/global-stability dependency. Dependency ⇒ UV_DELEGATED. This binds moduli to U's open boundary.
  5. If a Mars plot is shown, overlay the gate status. No overlay ⇒ FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. This binds the mission-visualization layer to the gate truth.

B1.5.3 Layer assignment of the drive excitation components

The platform's standard layer assignment for Ξ_drive (this table is itself a gate-card fragment — layer_assignments):

Component Symbol Layer Type Triggered rule
metric perturbation δg_μν × metric rule 2 (needs ledger)
gauge perturbation δA_μ^a ⊗ gauge rules 2, 3 (ledger + BRST)
scalar/modulus δφ^I ⊗/× mixed scalar/internal rules 2, 4 (ledger + UV)
mixed metric–gauge δG_μA ×/⊗ mixed-metric mixed rules 1, 2, 4
internal metric δG_AB × internal rules 2, 4 (compact ⇒ UV)
state / gauge data — ⊗ auxiliary/ghost rule 3 (BRST status)

The mixed components δG_μA, δG_AB are the dangerous ones: they are simultaneously geometric (×) and tied to compact factors (rule 4 ⇒ UV dependency). A candidate leaning on δG_AB to source its lobe is therefore automatically UV_DELEGATED unless it can show the effect is independent of global compactification stability — which, given U's OPEN boundary, it generally cannot.

First failure (B1.5): any excitation component that cannot be assigned to exactly one primary layer — or that needs to be re-assigned mid-argument to dodge a gate (e.g., recast a ⊗ source as a ⊕ constraint to escape the ledger requirement) — fails FAIL_DEFINITION. Layer-hopping to evade a gate is the first failure the discipline is built to catch.

B1.6 The EFT cutoff and the UV-delegation rule

B1.6.1 The admissibility ratio χ

The effective field theory is only valid below its cutoff. The platform encodes this as a single admissibility ratio (Build Contract §2):

χ = max( χ_R , χ_K , χ_T , χ_grad )        and the EFT is admissible iff  χ < 1

where each component is a dimensionless ratio of the relevant scale to the cutoff scale Λ_c:

  • χ_R — curvature ratio: |R| / Λ_c² (is the curvature sub-cutoff?)
  • χ_K — compactification/Kaluza ratio: scale of δG_AB variation vs Λ_c (are internal modes sub-cutoff?)
  • χ_T — stress ratio: norm_T_eff / (M_Pl² Λ_c²) (is the required source sub-Planckian relative to cutoff?)
  • χ_grad — gradient ratio: |∂φ|/Λ_c², |∂² g| / Λ_c² (are field/metric gradients sub-cutoff?)

If χ ≥ 1, the EFT correction terms L_EFT are being used outside their domain of validity. The candidate's uv_boundary gate cannot be PASS; at best it is UV_DELEGATED, and a candidate that requires operators with χ ≥ 1 is AUDIT or FAIL.

B1.6.2 The UV-delegation rule

The rule is stated sharply (Build Contract §2): if global compactification stability is required, status = UV_DELEGATED. This is the operational consequence of U's authority — global UV stability is OPEN (Gap-04), and the axiom that would close it (B-UQFC-14-UV-1) is UNADOPTED. So the platform delegates: it marks the dependency, caps the status, and refuses to claim the boundary is closed.

There is a crucial distinction, already drawn in B1.3.4 and worth restating because it is the most-confused point in the whole doctrine:

DEPENDS ON the open UV boundary          ⇒  UV_DELEGATED   (honest deferral; status capped, not killed)
ADOPTS the unadopted axiom AS MECHANISM  ⇒  FAIL           (authority crime; the engine is an open axiom)

UV_DELEGATED is not a failure of honesty — it is the honest move. It says "this candidate's full validity rests on a question the corpus marks OPEN; we will not pretend otherwise, and we cap the status accordingly." FAIL is reserved for the candidate that uses the unproven UV stability as its propulsion mechanism. The forbidden phrases global stability solved and UV completion adopted / UV completion closed (Build Contract §4) both live on the wrong side of this line and must never appear unqualified.

B1.6.3 Pseudocode: the UV gate

function uv_gate(candidate):
    χ = max(χ_R(candidate), χ_K(candidate), χ_T(candidate), χ_grad(candidate))
    if χ >= 1:
        return AUDIT("EFT used past cutoff: χ = %.3f ≥ 1; L_EFT invalid here" % χ)

    needs_global_stability = candidate.depends_on(compactification_global_stability)  # rule 4
    adopts_open_axiom      = candidate.uses_as_mechanism("B-UQFC-14-UV-1")            # ¬L_U

    if adopts_open_axiom:
        return FAIL("adopts UNADOPTED axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 as mechanism")   # hard fail
    if needs_global_stability:
        return UV_DELEGATED("global compactification stability OPEN (Gap-04); status capped")
    return PASS_TOY_UV("sub-cutoff and no global-stability dependency", χ=χ)

B1.6.4 Worked χ micro-numbers

To make the cutoff concrete: suppose a candidate's required source has norm_T_eff such that, with M_Pl ≈ 2.4×10¹⁸ GeV and a chosen EFT cutoff Λ_c, we evaluate χ_T = norm_T_eff / (M_Pl² Λ_c²). If the candidate needs internal-metric variation δG_AB on the scale of the compact factor S²/S¹_Y whose inverse size sits at or above Λ_c, then χ_K ≳ 1 immediately — the Kaluza modes are not sub-cutoff, the EFT is being asked to describe physics it cannot, and χ = max(...) ≥ 1 forces AUDIT. This is the generic fate of any candidate that tries to source a macroscopic forward lobe from internal-metric excitations: the internal scales are exactly the ones the EFT cannot resolve, so χ_K blows the cutoff. The platform does not need to know the true UV physics to reject this; it only needs to detect that the candidate has wandered outside the template's validity — which is precisely "UV-delegation, not UV-solution."

First failure (B1.6): the EFT/UV first failure is χ ≥ 1 (operator used past cutoff) or needs_global_stability = true (delegate). The deepest first failure of the entire program lives here: global UV stability is OPEN and the closing axiom is UNADOPTED, so no candidate can ever claim a closed UV boundary. Every candidate either stays sub-cutoff and corpus-agnostic, or it delegates. There is no third option that reaches a physical claim.

B1.7 Corpus-agnostic preference (the claim-independence guarantee)

The Build Contract §2 honesty note instructs: "the framework's claims do not require [the theory] to be correct — the platform accepts corpus constraints as configuration data. Where a claim can be made corpus-agnostically (against standard GR/EFT), prefer that." This section discharges that instruction as an explicit guarantee, because it is the property that makes the whole document defensible to a hostile reviewer who rejects the Fable/TOE corpus outright.

The guarantee. Partition every platform claim into two buckets:

  • Bucket A — corpus-agnostic. Claims provable against standard GR + EFT alone: invariant-distance computations, T_μν = −(2/√−g) δS/δg^μν source-matching, BRST gauge-spuriousness of pure-gauge modes, EFT cutoff χ < 1 admissibility, coordinate-invariance of the proper-distance functional. None of these depend on Fable/TOE being true. They use the forms (the action template, the layer types) but their validity rests on textbook GR/EFT. The pure-gauge negative control of B1.4.5 is the model case: that closure_score = 0.00 result holds in standard field theory regardless of any corpus.
  • Bucket B — corpus-conditioned. Claims that do invoke the specific corpus configuration C (the existence of the specific geometry object, the one-parent projection, the specific BRST realization). These are explicitly conditioned — they carry the tag "if the corpus configuration is accepted as data" and are never asserted as theory-true.

The architectural consequence. Because the gates (B1.4–B1.6) are functions of data C, swapping C for a different configuration changes only Bucket-B outputs. Bucket-A outputs are invariant under corpus replacement. We can therefore run the platform with a deliberately falsified corpus C_neg as a meta-negative-control: the Bucket-A gates must produce identical pass/fail structure, and any Bucket-B claim that survives falsification was secretly corpus-agnostic (good) while any that flips is correctly flagged as corpus-conditioned. This is how "does not require the theory to be correct" is not just asserted but testable.

This directly licenses the mandatory patent paragraph (Corpus Doctrine §"Mandatory patent paragraph"):

The claimed systems and methods do not require the correctness of any particular unified theory. The disclosed framework may accept corpus-derived constraints as configuration data, apply invariant and source-validity tests, classify candidate profiles, and output status-labeled simulation results.

First failure (B1.7): if any document claim cannot be sorted into Bucket A (corpus-agnostic) or Bucket B (explicitly corpus-conditioned) — i.e., it silently assumes the corpus is true while presenting as theory-independent — it fails the claim-independence guarantee and downgrades to UNDEFINED pending re-tagging. An untagged corpus dependency is the first failure this section exists to expose.

B1.11 Patent extraction

Per appendix 29 "Patent extraction", the protectable system this chapter defines is the corpus-as-configuration authority-and-action pipeline:

  1. receives a metric target Ξ_drive (an ansatz, declared as a target not a generator);
  2. receives a corpus configuration C = (G,Φ,Q,U) as typed configuration data, with explicit license/forbid sets per source;
  3. reconstructs the required source T_eff from the candidate geometry and assembles the supplied source T_fields from declared, layer-typed fields via T_μν = −(2/√−g) δS/δg^μν;
  4. computes the mismatch Δ_T, closure_score, and first_unmatched_component, classifying into source classes S0–S4;
  5. applies the three-layer (×/⊕/⊗) no-smuggling discipline and the EFT/UV gate (χ < 1; UV_DELEGATED on global-stability dependency; hard FAIL on open-axiom adoption);
  6. downgrades unsupported candidates per a fixed downgrade tree rather than inventing a source/theorem/apparatus;
  7. exports a status-labeled gate card and a first-failure report;
  8. and does all of the above without requiring the correctness of any unified theory — the corpus enters only as configuration data, which is the independently novel and broadest claim.

Claim 8 is the keystone: a classifier/validator whose validity is decoupled from the truth of the physics theory feeding it constraints is novel, broad, and survives even if the entire Fable/TOE corpus is later refuted. The acceptance tests of appendix 29 (test_ansatz_not_source, test_source_mismatch_visible) are the literal unit tests of claims 3–6 and are reproduced as the platform's regression suite.

B1.13 Reviewer attacks (and honest responses)

Attack 1 — "Your whole document is built on a non-peer-reviewed crank theory; it's worthless." Honest response: the document is built on the gate machinery, not the theory. The corpus enters only as configuration data (B1.2, B1.7), and we run a falsified-corpus negative control (NC-4) to prove the corpus-agnostic results are invariant under corpus replacement. The strongest results (pure-gauge rejection, source-matching, cutoff admissibility) are standard GR/EFT and hold even if Fable/TOE is entirely wrong. We prefer corpus-agnostic claims exactly because of this attack.

Attack 2 — "You wrote down an effective action and then claimed it sources a drive — that's the unsourced-metric fallacy." Honest response: we agree it would be, which is why B1.4.4 ("Why an ansatz is not a source") and the S0–S5 source-class ladder exist specifically to forbid it. An ansatz is a target; the generator is the T_fields ledger. The pure-gauge control (B1.4.5) gives closure_score = 0.00 precisely to demonstrate the platform catches unsourced metrics. Nothing is claimed sourced unless norm_Δ_T is below threshold with declared fields, and even then the ceiling is PASS_TOY.

Attack 3 (the strongest) — "You delegate the UV problem instead of solving it, so you've solved nothing; the drive's validity rests entirely on an OPEN question." Honest response: Correct, and we say so as the chapter's terminal first failure. Global UV stability is OPEN and we will not pretend otherwise — UV_DELEGATED is the honest status, not a dodge. The distinction we do enforce (B1.6.2) is between depending on the open boundary (delegate, status capped) and adopting the unadopted axiom as mechanism (hard fail). We never claim the UV boundary is closed; the forbidden phrases global stability solved and UV completion adopted are scanned for and absent (B1.10). The value of the platform is not "we closed the UV problem" — it is "we make every candidate's UV dependency visible and status-bounded, and we publish exactly where it fails." That is option value and a failure-mode engine, which is the declared success criterion, not a working drive.

B2 — Status & Gate Discipline: Ladder, Gate Cards, Downgrade Trees

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED · PASS_TOY (ceiling) — this chapter specifies and machine-tests the discipline layer itself; it makes no physical claim about any drive mode · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

B2.1 — Why this challenge matters

Every other chapter in this document closes a physics challenge: invariant distance (HC-01), source closure (HC-02), exoticity (HC-03), and so on. This chapter closes a different kind of challenge — the meta-challenge of not lying. A 500-page technical document about a distance-shortening metric interface is, by construction, a machine for generating persuasive prose. Left unsupervised, a lower-reasoning agent (and, frankly, a tired senior author) will write the sentence "the forward lobe shortens the proper distance to Mars" long before the source tensor, the energy ledger, the gauge audit, and the UV boundary have been checked. That sentence is the failure. The discipline layer specified here exists to make that sentence structurally impossible to emit unless every upstream gate has passed.

The first failure of this chapter — named up front, as the Build Contract requires of every chapter and every section — is this: the entire enforcement system reduces to social trust the moment any gate token is allowed to be a free-text human assertion rather than a machine-validated enumeration. If source_check can be the string "looks fine" instead of one of {PASS, FAIL, AUDIT}, the validator cannot fire, the downgrade tree never triggers, and PASS_TOY silently becomes PASS. Everything below is built to push that single point of failure into a place where it is visible and testable rather than latent and rhetorical. We do not eliminate it — we cannot eliminate human trust entirely — but we localize it to one auditable surface: the gate-card emitter and the schema validator.

The deliverable of this chapter is therefore not a metric and not a number. It is:

  1. a 6-level closure ladder with exact promotion rules,
  2. a gate-card JSON schema that every candidate mode in the entire document must carry,
  3. a downgrade tree mapping each failed gate to an exact status token,
  4. a fail-closed validator (validate_gate_card) that rejects any card whose declared claim exceeds its passed gates,
  5. worked gate cards for five canonical scenarios, and
  6. a demonstration of how a lower-reasoning agent is forced to fail closed even when it is trying to overclaim.

The ceiling of this chapter, like everywhere in the document, is PASS_TOY: a status-labeled simulation result. Nothing here promotes any drive mode to a physical claim, and the discipline layer is explicitly designed so that it cannot do so even by accident.

B2.2 — Formal object: the closure ladder as a partially-ordered status lattice

B2.2.1 The six levels

The closure ladder is the backbone. It is a totally ordered set of six evidence levels, anchored verbatim to the Hard Technical Challenge Map (§ "Closure ladder") and the Build Contract §3:

Level Label Meaning (what evidence exists)
0 UNDEFINED Prose only. No formal mathematical object exists.
1 TOY_DEFINED Equations and a data schema exist; the object is written down.
2 TOY_TESTED Negative controls and toy numerics have been run against it.
3 EFT_CANDIDATE Sources, energy ledger, gauge checks, and cutoffs are all declared.
4 PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY A complete hostile-review packet exists.
5 PHYSICAL_CLAIM Not targeted here / out of scope.

Two structural facts about this ladder dominate the rest of the chapter:

  • Level 5 is unreachable by design. It is present only to name the thing we are not doing. No worked example, no gate card, and no agent action in this document may set level = 5. The reachable ceiling is level 3 (EFT_CANDIDATE) as a declaration, and the credibility ceiling — the strongest thing the document is allowed to assert about any actual computed result — is the status token PASS_TOY, which lives at level 2 (TOY_TESTED). The gap between "I declared an EFT candidate's gates" and "those gates actually passed under hostile review" is exactly the gap between level 3 and level 4, and it is never crossed silently.

  • Promotion is monotone in evidence, not in confidence. You do not move up the ladder by being more sure. You move up only by adding a specific, named class of evidence. This is what makes the ladder machine-checkable: each rung corresponds to the existence of a particular artifact (equations, negative controls, a source ledger, an audit packet), not to a feeling.

B2.2.2 The promotion rules

The promotion rules bind evidence classes to a maximum achievable status. They are reproduced exactly from the Master Closure-Path Protocol (§"Promotion rules") and Build Contract §3:

Current evidence on hand Max status the mode may carry
prose only UNDEFINED (level 0)
equations only TOY_DEFINED (level 1)
equations + negative controls TOY_TESTED (level 2)
source + energy + gauge + cutoffs (all declared) EFT_CANDIDATE (level 3)
unresolved compactification / UV dependency UV_DELEGATED (lateral, not a rung)
hidden hardware assumption FAIL (off the ladder)

The word max is load-bearing. The promotion rule sets a ceiling, never a floor. Having negative controls entitles a mode to at most TOY_TESTED; it does not entitle the mode to TOY_TESTED if some other gate (say, the invariant check) has failed. The actual status is the minimum of (a) the evidence-class ceiling and (b) the lowest passing point in the gate sequence. Formally, if c_evidence is the promotion ceiling and c_gate is the status implied by the first failing gate, then

status(mode) = min_ladder( c_evidence , c_gate )

where min_ladder is the meet on the ladder order. This single line is the mathematical heart of fail-closed: the system always reports the worse of "what you proved" and "what you broke."

B2.2.3 Two distinct token alphabets

A subtle but critical point that the lower-reasoning manual gets wrong if not stated explicitly: there are two different status alphabets in play, and they must not be conflated.

  • Ladder levels — UNDEFINED … PHYSICAL_CLAIM — describe how far up the evidence stack a mode is. They are ordinal.
  • Status tokens / downgrade tokens — FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY, FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, UV_DELEGATED, PASS_TOY, etc. — describe why a mode stopped where it did. They are categorical and they encode the first failure.

A fully specified mode status is the pair (ladder_level, status_token). For example, the canonical "best toy" mode is (2 TOY_TESTED, PASS_TOY), and a metric that turned out to be a coordinate artifact is (0 UNDEFINED, FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY) — it is knocked all the way back to "no formal physical object exists" because a coordinate-only distance change is, physically, not an object at all. The downgrade tree (§B2.5) is precisely the function that maps a failing gate to its status token; the ladder meet (§B2.2.2) is what maps that token back to a level.

First failure of B2.2: the ladder is only a partial order over evidence classes, and that ordering silently assumes the classes are independent and that a higher rung strictly contains a lower one. They are not strictly nested in practice — a mode can have a clean source_check (a level-3 evidence class) while its invariant_check (a level-2 prerequisite) is only AUDIT, so the literal "evidence-class ceiling" and the "gate floor" can disagree about which rung the mode is on. The ladder's first failure is therefore that the evidence-class ceiling, taken alone, is not safe — it can over-credit a mode that has out-of-order evidence (a sourced-but-uninvariant metric). The mitigation, and the only reason the ladder is usable, is the min_ladder meet of §B2.2.2: the status is pinned to the worse of the evidence ceiling and the first-failing-gate floor, which forecloses the out-of-order over-credit. The unmitigated residue: the meet is only as honest as the eval order (§B2.5.2) being the true dependency order; a wrong eval order would let a late gate's failure hide behind an early gate's pass. That ordering is asserted here and only verified by the per-HC chapters re-deriving the dependency graph.

B2.3 — Corpus authority: where each gate's authority comes from

The discipline layer does not invent its gates. Each gate borrows its authority from a specific corpus anchor, and the gate is only as strong as that anchor. This traceability is what lets a hostile reviewer attack a gate rather than a vibe.

Gate Question it asks Corpus authority Anchor's own limit
definition Is there a formal object (equations, coordinates, fields, layer map)? Three-layer field discipline (× ⊕ ⊗); S_eff form none — purely formal
negative_controls Do deliberately-broken inputs get rejected? Closure-Path Protocol Stage B tests can be incomplete
invariant_check Is the distance change coordinate-invariant (curvature/tetrad/geodesic)? GR / EFT (corpus-agnostic, preferred) proxies, not a theorem
source_check What T_μν sources the metric? Is it shared/visible stress-energy? Fable_Forces (single Einstein-frame metric, shared coupling, no double counting) not peer-reviewed
gauge_check Is the mode physical or pure gauge / BRST-exact? Fable_Quantum (BRST/BV physical-state gates: Q_BRST\|Ψ⟩ = 0, not exact, positive norm) interacting sector stays AUDIT
energy_check Where does the energy come from; is any exoticity hidden? Fable_Forces source ledger; energy conditions never a clean PASS
causality_check CTCs, horizons, trapped surfaces, signature, global-hyperbolicity proxies? GR causal structure proxies only
uv_boundary Does the mode depend on UV/compactification stability? TOE_FINAL diff: Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1 global UV stability is OPEN, axiom UNADOPTED the axiom is unadopted — so this gate can only ever return UV_DELEGATED, never a closed PASS, for modes that touch internal geometry

Two authority facts must be quoted exactly because the validator depends on them:

  1. energy_check is never a clean PASS. The Build Contract §3 states it explicitly: "energy_check is never a clean PASS — it is 'pass / audit-visible.'" In the schema this is enforced by restricting the allowed value set for energy_check to {PASS, AUDIT} only, where even the PASS here means "energy ledger is fully visible and accounted," not "energy problem solved." The forbidden phrase solves the energy problem may never appear unqualified anywhere downstream of this gate.

  2. uv_boundary == UV_DELEGATED forecloses the global-stability claim. Because B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is UNADOPTED, any mode whose excitation reaches into K6 = SU(3)/T², S², or S¹_Y and requires global compactification stability must carry uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED, and the phrase global stability solved is forbidden in that card's forbidden_claims and anywhere in its prose. The validator checks this (§B2.6).

First failure of B2.3: the authority chain is only as honest as the agent's self-assessment of which corpus anchor it is leaning on. An agent can mislabel a UV-dependent mode as UV-independent — claiming its excitation lives entirely in the M4 factor when it actually couples to K6 — and thereby dodge the UV_DELEGATED token. We cannot fully close this from inside the gate card; the structural mitigation is the layer_assignments field (§B2.4), which forces the agent to write down which geometric factor each field lives in, making the mislabel visible to a reviewer who reads the layer map. The honest statement is: this gate reduces a physics lie to a layer-assignment lie, which is smaller and more auditable, but not zero.

B2.4 — Formal object: the gate-card JSON schema

B2.4.1 The canonical schema

Every candidate mode that appears anywhere in the document must carry exactly one gate card. The schema is reproduced verbatim from Build Contract §3 and the Master Closure-Path Protocol (§"Gate-card JSON schema"), then made strict (allowed-value enumerations, required keys, type constraints):

{
  "model_id": "MID-...",
  "challenge_id": "HC-..",
  "object_definition": {
    "equations": [],
    "coordinates": "",
    "active_fields": [],
    "layer_assignments": {}
  },
  "gates": {
    "definition":        "PASS|FAIL",
    "negative_controls": "PASS|FAIL",
    "invariant_check":   "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT",
    "source_check":      "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT",
    "gauge_check":       "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT",
    "energy_check":      "PASS|AUDIT",
    "causality_check":   "PASS|FAIL|AUDIT",
    "uv_boundary":       "PASS|UV_DELEGATED|FAIL"
  },
  "first_failure": "",
  "strongest_allowed_claim": "",
  "forbidden_claims": [],
  "next_closure_step": ""
}

B2.4.2 Field-by-field contract

Field Type Contract
model_id string, regex ^MID- Stable, unique. Required (validator asserts presence).
challenge_id string, regex ^HC- Which hard challenge this card answers. Required.
object_definition.equations list[str] At least one entry, or definition gate must be FAIL.
object_definition.coordinates string Chart in which the metric/perturbation is written. Empty ⇒ invariant_check cannot be PASS.
object_definition.active_fields list[str] Subset of {δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge}.
object_definition.layer_assignments map field→{×, ⊕, ⊗} and geometric factor Each active field MUST map to a layer; an unmapped field ⇒ definition = FAIL.
gates.* enum (see schema) Closed enumerations. Any value outside the listed set is a hard validation error, not a downgrade.
first_failure string, non-empty The earliest gate that blocks stronger language. Empty string ⇒ card rejected.
strongest_allowed_claim string Subject to the forbidden-phrase and source-gate constraints.
forbidden_claims list[str] Must include the phrases the gate results forbid (e.g., propulsion, global stability solved).
next_closure_step string What evidence would raise the level. Empty allowed only for PASS_TOY ceiling cards.

The enumeration discipline in gates.* is the structural answer to this chapter's own first failure (§B2.1). Because each gate value is drawn from a closed set, the emitter cannot smuggle in a soft assertion. There is no "probably fine" token. A gate is PASS, FAIL, AUDIT, UV_DELEGATED, or the card does not validate at all. Note the deliberate asymmetries:

  • energy_check has no FAIL and no clean meaning of PASS — only {PASS, AUDIT}, per §B2.3(1). "Failing" the energy gate is impossible because the gate's job is not to pass/fail energy but to make energy visible; a hidden energy source shows up not here but as a definition/source_check failure feeding the FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY downgrade.
  • uv_boundary has no AUDIT — UV uncertainty is expressed as UV_DELEGATED, a first-class status, not as a deferred audit. This matters because AUDIT is "we will look later" whereas UV_DELEGATED is "this is structurally out of our scope because the corpus axiom is unadopted." Conflating them would let an agent promise to resolve, in a later pass, something that is corpus-OPEN.

B2.4.3 The layer_assignments requirement (HC-07 hook)

The three-layer discipline (× ⊕ ⊗) is not decoration. layer_assignments is the field where unified-mode admissibility (HC-07) is enforced at card level. Example for a mode that excites a gauge perturbation and an internal scalar:

"layer_assignments": {
  "delta_A_mu_a": { "layer": "⊗", "factor": "S1_Y", "note": "hypercharge-circle bundle operator" },
  "delta_phi_I":  { "layer": "⊕", "factor": "F+",   "note": "chamber-admissible projection" },
  "delta_g_mu_nu":{ "layer": "×", "factor": "M4",   "note": "Einstein-frame metric base" }
}

If any active_field lacks a layer assignment, definition is FAIL and the mode cannot leave level 0. This is the single most effective anti-fabrication device in the schema: an agent that wants to add an "arbitrary primitive field" to make a distance effect appear must declare where it lives geometrically, and an unphysical addition has nowhere to live.

First failure of B2.4: the schema enforces form (every gate has a legal token, every field has a layer) but cannot enforce truth of the token (whether source_check: PASS is actually true). A correctly-shaped card with a lie inside passes the schema validator. The first failure is therefore false token assertion that is well-formed. The mitigation is two-stage: the schema validator (this chapter) catches malformed and self-contradictory cards; the per-HC closure chapters (B-series and the HC chapters) must independently recompute the gate they assert, with a runnable test. The schema validator's honest scope is consistency, not correctness.

B2.5 — The downgrade tree and status tokens

B2.5.1 The tree

The downgrade tree maps a failing gate to the exact status token a mode receives. Verbatim from Build Contract §3 and Appendix 36 (§"Downgrade tree"):

claim boundary fails       -> FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION
coordinate invariant fails -> FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY
source missing             -> FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
energy hidden              -> FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY
gauge fails                -> FAIL_PURE_GAUGE
BRST unknown               -> AUDIT_QUANTUM
UV dependency              -> UV_DELEGATED
mission plot overclaims    -> FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM

B2.5.2 Token semantics, ladder meet, and evaluation order

Each token carries (a) a meaning, (b) the ladder level it pins the mode to, and (c) the gate that triggers it. The evaluation order matches the HC dependency graph (HC-07 → HC-05 → HC-06 → HC-01 → HC-02 → HC-03 → HC-04 → HC-09 → HC-08 → HC-10), so the first gate to fail along that path is the one that names the first failure. Later gates are not even evaluated to a pass — they are reported as not reached, which is itself honest information.

Token Triggering gate (in eval order) Pins level to Meaning
FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION claim-boundary (meta) n/a (card rejected) The card's claim exceeds what its gates allow. Not a downgrade of the mode — a rejection of the card.
FAIL_PURE_GAUGE gauge_check = FAIL 0 UNDEFINED Mode is pure gauge; no physical object.
AUDIT_QUANTUM gauge_check = AUDIT (BRST unknown) 1 TOY_DEFINED BRST/BV status undetermined; interacting sector. Hold, do not promote.
FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY invariant_check = FAIL 0 UNDEFINED Distance change is a coordinate artifact; not a physical object.
FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC source_check = FAIL/None 1 TOY_DEFINED Pretty metric, no T_μν. Equations exist, physics does not.
FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY source_check = PASS but energy ledger hides exoticity 2 TOY_TESTED → flagged Source exists but smuggles an unaccounted energy-condition violation.
TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC energy_check = AUDIT with visible exoticity 2 TOY_TESTED Exotic source is declared and visible — honest toy, not promotable.
UV_DELEGATED uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED 3 EFT_CANDIDATE (lateral) Depends on UNADOPTED UV axiom; "global stability solved" forbidden.
FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM HC-10 mission plot lacks gate overlay mission claim void Local lobe effect drawn as Earth→Mars time without status overlay/watermark.
PASS_TOY no gate failed at toy level 2 TOY_TESTED Ceiling. Status-labeled simulation result only.

The distinction between FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY and TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC deserves emphasis because it is where most overclaiming dies. Both involve an energy-condition-violating source. The difference is visibility. If the exoticity is declared (the card's energy_check = AUDIT, the strongest_allowed_claim says "requires a declared exotic source," and the source appears in the ledger), the mode is an honest TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC and may carry up to PASS_TOY as a toy. If the exoticity is hidden (the metric is written, a benign-looking source is claimed, but the energy ledger does not balance without an undeclared negative-energy term), it is FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY and the card is flagged. The fail-closed rule: when in doubt about visibility, treat as hidden and fail.

B2.5.3 Worked downgrade walk

Consider a mode MID-WALK-007 that an agent submits hoping for EFT_CANDIDATE. Gate sequence in eval order:

definition        = PASS   (equations + layer map present)
negative_controls = PASS   (two broken inputs rejected)
gauge_check       = PASS   (Q_BRST|Ψ>=0, not exact, positive norm)   [HC-05/06]
invariant_check   = PASS   (Kretschmann scalar shifts; geodesic length drops)  [HC-01]
source_check      = AUDIT  (T_μν written but shared-coupling not yet verified)  [HC-02]
energy_check      = AUDIT  (exotic term present and visible)          [HC-03]
causality_check   = not reached
uv_boundary       = not reached

Evaluation halts conceptually at the first non-PASS that gates stronger language, but the status is the ladder meet of all results. Here:

  • promotion ceiling from evidence: source/energy/gauge/cutoffs not all clean ⇒ cannot reach level 3 EFT_CANDIDATE;
  • energy_check = AUDIT with visible exoticity ⇒ token TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC;
  • source_check = AUDIT ⇒ cannot assert "propulsion" in strongest_allowed_claim.

Result: (2 TOY_TESTED, TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC). first_failure = HC-02 (source closure: shared-coupling verification pending). strongest_allowed_claim = "status-labeled simulation result: toy forward-lobe distance reduction under a declared, visibly-exotic source." The agent wanted level 3; it gets level 2. That gap is the discipline working.

First failure of B2.5: the tree assumes the gate results themselves are computed in the right order and computed at all. If an agent skips invariant_check (leaves it AUDIT by default) it can mask a FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY mode as a merely-pending AUDIT_QUANTUM further down. The mitigation is that the validator (§B2.6) treats any AUDIT on invariant_check as blocking EFT_CANDIDATE and as a mandatory entry in next_closure_step; an AUDIT is never a free pass, it is a debt that pins the level. The unmitigated residue — the genuine first failure — is gate-skipping by an agent that never computes the invariant at all and reports AUDIT to avoid FAIL. Only an independent recompute in the HC-01 chapter closes that.

B2.6 — Fail-closed enforcement: validate_gate_card

B2.6.1 The protocol validator (verbatim seed)

The Master Closure-Path Protocol ships the seed validator. It is small on purpose — small enough to audit by eye:

def validate_gate_card(card):
    required = ["model_id", "challenge_id", "gates", "first_failure", "strongest_allowed_claim"]
    for key in required:
        assert key in card
    if card["gates"].get("source_check") in ["FAIL", None]:
        assert "propulsion" not in card["strongest_allowed_claim"].lower()
    if card["gates"].get("uv_boundary") == "UV_DELEGATED":
        forbidden = " ".join(card.get("forbidden_claims", [])).lower()
        assert "global stability solved" not in forbidden
    return True

This seed encodes the two non-negotiable fail-closed couplings from Build Contract §3:

  1. No source ⇒ no propulsion. If source_check ∈ {FAIL, None}, the word propulsion is forbidden in the strongest allowed claim. (An unsourced metric cannot push anything.)
  2. UV-delegated ⇒ no "global stability solved." If uv_boundary == UV_DELEGATED, the phrase global stability solved may not appear (the protocol checks forbidden_claims; the strict version below checks the prose too).

But the seed has a subtle and important under-specification, and naming it is mandatory: the second assertion checks that "global stability solved" is absent from forbidden_claims, when the manifest intent is that the phrase must be present in forbidden_claims (declared forbidden) and absent from the asserted claim. Read literally, the seed asserts the negation of the intent. This is exactly the kind of inversion a lower-reasoning agent copies without noticing. The strict validator below fixes it and is the version this document actually runs.

B2.6.2 The strict validator (this document's enforcement)

LADDER = ["UNDEFINED", "TOY_DEFINED", "TOY_TESTED",
          "EFT_CANDIDATE", "PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY", "PHYSICAL_CLAIM"]

GATE_ALPHABETS = {
    "definition":        {"PASS", "FAIL"},
    "negative_controls": {"PASS", "FAIL"},
    "invariant_check":   {"PASS", "FAIL", "AUDIT"},
    "source_check":      {"PASS", "FAIL", "AUDIT"},
    "gauge_check":       {"PASS", "FAIL", "AUDIT"},
    "energy_check":      {"PASS", "AUDIT"},            # never FAIL, never clean PASS
    "causality_check":   {"PASS", "FAIL", "AUDIT"},
    "uv_boundary":       {"PASS", "UV_DELEGATED", "FAIL"},
}

FORBIDDEN_UNQUALIFIED = [
    "working warp drive", "proves faster-than-light", "proves ftl",
    "solves the energy problem", "energy solved", "global stability solved",
    "uv completion adopted", "uv completion closed", "operational propulsion",
    "no propellant needed", "negative energy available", "quantum gravity solved",
]

class GateCardRejected(Exception):
    """Raised on any fail-closed violation. The card does NOT get the benefit of the doubt."""

def validate_gate_card(card):
    # --- 0. structural: required keys present ---
    for key in ["model_id", "challenge_id", "object_definition",
                "gates", "first_failure", "strongest_allowed_claim",
                "forbidden_claims", "next_closure_step"]:
        if key not in card:
            raise GateCardRejected(f"missing required key: {key}")

    if not card["first_failure"].strip():
        raise GateCardRejected("first_failure is empty — every card MUST name one")

    if not card["model_id"].startswith("MID-"):
        raise GateCardRejected("model_id must start with MID-")

    # --- 1. closed-enumeration discipline: no soft tokens ---
    gates = card["gates"]
    for gate, alphabet in GATE_ALPHABETS.items():
        if gate not in gates:
            raise GateCardRejected(f"gate not declared: {gate} (default is NOT pass)")
        if gates[gate] not in alphabet:
            raise GateCardRejected(
                f"illegal token {gates[gate]!r} on {gate}; allowed {sorted(alphabet)}")

    # --- 2. every active field must carry a layer assignment (HC-07) ---
    fields = card["object_definition"].get("active_fields", [])
    layers = card["object_definition"].get("layer_assignments", {})
    for f in fields:
        if f not in layers:
            raise GateCardRejected(f"active field {f} has no layer assignment "
                                   f"(× / ⊕ / ⊗) — definition cannot be PASS")

    claim = card["strongest_allowed_claim"].lower()

    # --- 3. fail-closed coupling: no source => no propulsion ---
    if gates["source_check"] in {"FAIL", None}:
        if "propulsion" in claim:
            raise GateCardRejected("source_check failed/none but claim asserts propulsion")

    # --- 4. energy gate is never a clean pass: claim may not say energy solved ---
    if any(p in claim for p in ["solves the energy problem", "energy solved",
                                "negative energy available"]):
        raise GateCardRejected("energy_check is audit-visible only; claim overstates energy")

    # --- 5. UV-delegated => 'global stability solved' is FORBIDDEN, and must be DECLARED so ---
    if gates["uv_boundary"] == "UV_DELEGATED":
        if "global stability solved" in claim:
            raise GateCardRejected("uv_boundary=UV_DELEGATED but claim asserts global stability solved")
        declared = " ".join(card["forbidden_claims"]).lower()
        if "global stability solved" not in declared:
            raise GateCardRejected("uv_boundary=UV_DELEGATED must DECLARE "
                                   "'global stability solved' in forbidden_claims")

    # --- 6. forbidden-phrase scan over the strongest claim ---
    for phrase in FORBIDDEN_UNQUALIFIED:
        if phrase in claim:
            raise GateCardRejected(f"forbidden phrase in claim: {phrase!r}")

    # --- 7. ladder ceiling: PHYSICAL_CLAIM is unreachable; ceiling is PASS_TOY ---
    lvl = card.get("ladder_level", "UNDEFINED")
    if lvl in {"PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY", "PHYSICAL_CLAIM"}:
        raise GateCardRejected(f"ladder_level {lvl} exceeds document ceiling (PASS_TOY @ TOY_TESTED)")

    # --- 8. promotion-rule meet: status = min(evidence ceiling, gate floor) ---
    status = compute_status(card)           # see B2.6.3
    card["_validated_status"] = status
    return status

B2.6.3 The status-meet computation

The validator's final job is to recompute the mode's status from the gates rather than trusting the agent's self-reported level. This is the algorithm that enforces status = min_ladder(evidence_ceiling, gate_floor):

def compute_status(card):
    g = card["gates"]

    # (a) downgrade tree — first failing gate in HC eval order sets the token
    if g["definition"] == "FAIL":          return ("UNDEFINED",   "FAIL_DEFINITION")
    if g["negative_controls"] == "FAIL":   return ("UNDEFINED",   "FAIL_NO_CONTROLS")
    if g["gauge_check"] == "FAIL":         return ("UNDEFINED",   "FAIL_PURE_GAUGE")
    if g["gauge_check"] == "AUDIT":        return ("TOY_DEFINED", "AUDIT_QUANTUM")
    if g["invariant_check"] == "FAIL":     return ("UNDEFINED",   "FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY")
    if g["invariant_check"] == "AUDIT":    return ("TOY_DEFINED", "AUDIT_INVARIANT_PENDING")
    if g["source_check"] in ("FAIL", None):return ("TOY_DEFINED", "FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC")

    # (b) source still auditing => cannot reach the level-3 lateral at all;
    #     an unverified source pins the mode to a visible-exotic toy. This guard
    #     is FIRST so that source-AUDIT can never be over-promoted by a clean UV.
    if g["source_check"] == "AUDIT":
        return ("TOY_TESTED", "TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC")

    # --- from here source_check == "PASS" ---
    # (c) the UV boundary is a STRUCTURAL statement and must be read BEFORE the
    #     energy-visibility fallback, otherwise an energy AUDIT would wrongly
    #     divert a UV-delegated mode to TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC. (This ordering is the
    #     fix to the pre-fix bug noted in B2.6.3(4): reading energy_check==AUDIT
    #     first short-circuited Scenario 4.)
    if g["uv_boundary"] == "FAIL":
        return ("TOY_DEFINED",   "FAIL_UV_UNSTABLE")
    if g["uv_boundary"] == "UV_DELEGATED":
        return ("EFT_CANDIDATE", "UV_DELEGATED")     # lateral: declared, not closed

    # (d) no UV dependency, source PASS. A declared-and-visible exotic energy
    #     term (energy_check == AUDIT) pins the mode to an honest exotic toy.
    if g["energy_check"] == "AUDIT":
        return ("TOY_TESTED", "TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC")

    # (e) source PASS + energy PASS(visible, balanced) — causality is the last
    #     toy-level gate that can still demote.
    if g["causality_check"] in ("FAIL", "AUDIT"):
        return ("TOY_TESTED", "AUDIT_CAUSALITY")

    # (f) everything clean at toy level — this is the ceiling
    return ("TOY_TESTED", "PASS_TOY")

Four properties of compute_status make it fail-closed:

  1. Defaults are bad. A gate left at its worst legal value cannot accidentally yield PASS_TOY. If invariant_check is AUDIT (the default an honest-but-lazy agent leaves it at), the function returns AUDIT_INVARIANT_PENDING at level 1, never level 2+. There is no code path where omission becomes pass.
  2. The ceiling is hard-coded. The function's most optimistic return is ("TOY_TESTED", "PASS_TOY"). It is literally impossible for compute_status to return PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY or PHYSICAL_CLAIM. The Build Contract ceiling is not a guideline an agent must remember; it is the maximum of the function's range.
  3. The agent's self-report is overwritten. validate_gate_card writes card["_validated_status"] from compute_status, not from any field the agent supplied. An agent that writes "ladder_level": "EFT_CANDIDATE" into the card but whose gates compute to TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC ends up with the computed value; its self-promotion is discarded.
  4. Branch order is itself a corrected defect (downgrade-don't-hide, applied to our own code). An earlier draft of this function read energy_check == "AUDIT" before the uv_boundary block. Because energy_check can never be a clean PASS (Build Contract §3 — it is {PASS, AUDIT} only, with PASS meaning "visible/balanced"), that ordering caused the energy-AUDIT short-circuit to fire for every mode with a still-auditing energy ledger — including Scenario 4 (§B2.7.4), which is causality = PASS, uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED and is meant to occupy the lateral EFT_CANDIDATE slot. The buggy order returned ("TOY_TESTED", "TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC") for it, silently contradicting the worked example. The corrected order reads the structural UV statement first, then the energy-visibility fallback, so Scenario 3 (uv = PASS, energy AUDIT) still resolves to TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC while Scenario 4 (uv = UV_DELEGATED) resolves to its lateral level-3. The residue, named honestly: the two energy AUDITs are token-indistinguishable — Scenario 3's is "visible exoticity present" and Scenario 4's is "ledger pending, non-exotic," and the gate alphabet cannot tell them apart. The discriminator is whether the card declares an energy-condition-violating term in object_definition.equations; that declaration, not the bare token, is what the HC-03 chapter must independently recompute. Until it does, a UV-delegated mode that is secretly exotic could ride the UV_DELEGATED lateral without its exoticity being scored — a real gap, closed only downstream.

First failure of B2.6: the validator is a consistency engine, not a physics engine. It can prove that a card's claim does not exceed its declared gates; it cannot prove that invariant_check: PASS was earned by an actual Kretschmann-scalar/geodesic computation rather than asserted. The first failure of the enforcement layer is therefore token forgery under a well-formed card, identical to §B2.4's residue, and it is closed only by the per-HC chapters re-deriving each PASS with a runnable test. The validator's honest contract: no card escapes that claims more than it declares; some cards may declare more than is true, and those are caught downstream, not here.

B2.7 — Worked gate-card examples

These are the five canonical scenarios from Appendix 36, re-expressed in the full strict schema (not the abbreviated appendix form), each run through validate_gate_card, each showing the computed (level, token) and why the agent could not promote past it.

B2.7.1 Scenario 1 — coordinate_only → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY

A metric is written in a comoving chart where coordinate distance to the forward lobe shrinks. But the Kretschmann scalar K = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} is unchanged and proper geodesic length between the same physical endpoints is invariant under the chart map.
