compute_status hits invariant_check == "FAIL" ⇒ ("UNDEFINED", "FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY"). The mode is knocked to level 0: physically there is no object, only a relabeling. Validator passes (the card is honest about its own failure); the mode fails. This is the most common and most seductive failure mode, and it dies first in eval order precisely because HC-01 sits early in the dependency graph.

The ansatz does produce an invariant distance change (curvature genuinely differs). But no T_μν is exhibited; running the Einstein tensor backward, G_μν = 8πG T_μν, yields a T_μν that the agent never wrote down and cannot identify as shared/visible stress-energy.

B2.7bis — Worked numerics: the invariant gate and a full status-transition trace

The brief and Build Contract §6 require real worked numbers where the leaf calls for them. The discipline layer's one genuinely numerical gate is invariant_check (it is the gate that separates Scenario 1's FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY from Scenario 5's PASS_TOY). We work it explicitly, then trace a single mode through every status the validator can assign, so the reader can see the ladder meet operate arithmetically rather than abstractly.

B2.7bis.1 The invariant-check arithmetic (HC-01 hook, toy)

Take the toy comoving ansatz of Scenario 1, ds² = −dt² + (1 − f)² dx² + dy² + dz², with a smooth front/back-asymmetric shape f(ξ), ξ = x − vt. The proper distance along a constant-t forward ray between physical endpoints x_A and x_B is the invariant

L_phys = ∫_{x_A}^{x_B} |1 − f(x − vt)| dx

The coordinate separation x_B − x_A is not invariant; the question the gate answers is whether L_phys actually differs from the flat-space value L_0 = x_B − x_A, or whether the agent merely relabeled coordinates so that x_B − x_A looks small while L_phys is unchanged.

Two distinct test cases, both with the same coordinate-distance reduction of 20% (x_B − x_A chosen so the coordinate gap shrinks from 1.00 to 0.80):

  • Case C (coordinate-only). f is a pure reparametrization — the chart is stretched but the metric pulls back to flat: effectively (1 − f) dx = dx' with x' the flat proper coordinate. Then L_phys = ∫ dx' = L_0 exactly. Numerically, with L_0 = 1.000 and a chart that maps the physical unit interval onto coordinate width 0.800, the integrand compensates: ∫₀^{0.8} (1/0.8) dx = 1.000. L_phys = 1.000, ΔL_phys = 0. The curvature is flat everywhere: K = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} = 0 identically. ⇒ invariant_check = FAIL, token FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. The 20% "reduction" was entirely coordinate.

  • Case P (physical). f(ξ) = A·exp(−ξ²/2σ²) with amplitude A = 0.20, width σ = 0.15, asymmetrized by a small skew so the forward lobe is compressed and the rear is not. Now 1 − f < 1 over the lobe genuinely shortens proper length:

L_phys = ∫_{x_A}^{x_B} (1 − A e^{−(x−vt)²/2σ²}) dx
       = L_0 − A·σ·√(2π)·[Φ-window]   ≈ 1.000 − 0.20·0.15·2.5066·(0.997)
       ≈ 1.000 − 0.0750 = 0.9250

So ΔL_phys ≈ −0.075 (a real 7.5% invariant reduction over the lobe), and the curvature does not vanish: for this profile the leading Kretschmann scalar scales as K ∼ (f''/(1−f))² ∼ (A/σ²)² · O(1) ≈ (0.20/0.0225)² ≈ 79 (toy units), manifestly nonzero. ⇒ invariant_check = PASS (the distance change survives the tetrad/geodesic/curvature test). This is the arithmetic difference between a survivor and a coordinate artifact: K = 0, ΔL = 0 fails; K ≈ 79, ΔL ≈ −0.075 passes — at the toy level only, and with the source/energy gates still ahead.

The pseudocode the HC-01 chapter must run (named here so this chapter's gate is reproducible, not asserted):

def invariant_check(metric_g, endpoints, vt):
    L_phys   = geodesic_length(metric_g, endpoints, vt)     # numeric integral
    L_flat   = euclidean_gap(endpoints)
    K_field  = kretschmann(metric_g)                        # R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} on a grid
    if abs(L_phys - L_flat) < EPS and max(abs(K_field)) < EPS:
        return "FAIL"          # coordinate-only: no invariant content
    if not is_chart_independent(L_phys, alt_charts):        # recompute in 2+ charts
        return "FAIL"          # chart-dependent => coordinate-only
    return "PASS"              # toy-level invariant distance change confirmed

EPS is the numerical-zero tolerance (e.g. 1e-9 in toy units). Case C returns FAIL on the first branch (|L_phys−L_flat| = 0, K = 0); Case P returns PASS. Note the second FAIL branch: even a nonzero ΔL is rejected if it is not reproduced under an independent chart — a defense against an agent that produces a fake ΔL by integrating in a single pathological coordinate system.

B2.7bis.2 A full status-transition trace of one mode

To make the ladder meet concrete, follow a single candidate MID-TRACE-042 as evidence accumulates across five drafting passes. At each pass we show the gate vector and the value compute_status returns. This is the document's status arithmetic in motion.

Pass What the agent added Gate vector (def, nc, gauge, inv, src, energy, caus, uv) compute_status (level, token)
1 prose paragraph only (FAIL, –, –, –, –, –, –, –) def FAIL (0 UNDEFINED, FAIL_DEFINITION)
2 wrote ds², layer map (PASS, FAIL, PASS, AUDIT, AUDIT, AUDIT, AUDIT, PASS) nc FAIL (0 UNDEFINED, FAIL_NO_CONTROLS)
3 added 2 negative controls (PASS, PASS, PASS, AUDIT, AUDIT, AUDIT, AUDIT, PASS) inv AUDIT (1 TOY_DEFINED, AUDIT_INVARIANT_PENDING)
4 ran §B2.7bis.1 invariant (Case P) (PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS, AUDIT, AUDIT, AUDIT, PASS) src AUDIT (2 TOY_TESTED, TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC)
5 exhibited T_μν, visible balanced source, M4-only (PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS) clean (2 TOY_TESTED, PASS_TOY)

Three things to read off the trace:

  1. Status is monotone non-decreasing in evidence but never skips a rung. The mode climbs 0 → 0 → 1 → 2 → 2, and the ceiling is reached at pass 5 — PASS_TOY — exactly where the contract says the ceiling is. No pass produces level 3+ from this M4-only mode (it has no UV dependency, so there is no EFT_CANDIDATE lateral, and level 4/5 are unreachable).

  2. Every intermediate status names a different first failure, and the first failure moves forward in the dependency graph as gates clear: pass 3's first failure is the unrun invariant; pass 4's is the unexhibited source; pass 5's is the promotion-time first failure (exoticity at physical magnitude), because at toy level nothing fails. This is the first-failure rule operating continuously, not just at the end.

  3. At no point could the agent assert a status the gates did not support. Had the agent written "ladder_level": "EFT_CANDIDATE" at pass 4, compute_status would still return TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC (level 2) because source_check == AUDIT, and validate_gate_card step 8 would overwrite the self-report. The self-report is decorative; the gate vector is dispositive.

First failure of B2.7bis: the worked numbers are toy units — K ≈ 79, ΔL ≈ −0.075 carry no physical scale. The arithmetic proves the gate logic (coordinate-only vs invariant) discriminates correctly; it does not prove a physical distance reduction, because the amplitude A = 0.20 and width σ = 0.15 were chosen for numerical clarity, not derived from a sourced, EFT-valid profile. The moment these are scaled to physical magnitude, HC-03 exoticity and HC-09 backreaction become the first failure — which is exactly what Scenario 5's next_closure_step says. The numbers demonstrate the discriminator; they do not promote the mode.

B2.8 — How a lower-reasoning agent is forced to fail closed

The whole apparatus exists to defeat a specific adversary: not a malicious agent, but a helpful, persuasive, lower-reasoning agent that wants to give the recipient good news. This section walks that adversary through the gate and shows the three independent walls it hits.

B2.8.1 The adversary's natural move

A lower-reasoning agent, handed a metric that shows a coordinate-distance reduction, will draft:

"The vehicle-comoving asymmetric profile shortens the proper distance to Mars, enabling operational propulsion without propellant."

Every clause of that sentence is a forbidden phrase or an unsupported promotion. Here is what stops it.

B2.8.2 Wall 1 — the schema forbids the shape of the lie

To emit the sentence at all, the agent must produce a gate card. The schema requires gates, first_failure, strongest_allowed_claim, and a layer assignment for every active field. The agent cannot leave source_check unstated (validator step 0/1 rejects a missing gate; the default is not pass). It must pick a token from a closed set. If it has not computed a source, the only honest token is FAIL or AUDIT — and the moment source_check == FAIL, validator step 3 makes "propulsion" in the claim a hard GateCardRejected. The agent literally cannot serialize a passing card that says "propulsion" without first putting a real PASS in source_check, which it cannot do without exhibiting T_μν. The lie has no legal shape.

B2.8.3 Wall 2 — the forbidden-phrase scan forbids the words

Even if the agent routes around the source coupling (say it writes prose, not a claim field), validator step 6 scans strongest_allowed_claim against FORBIDDEN_UNQUALIFIED. operational propulsion, no propellant needed, working warp drive, proves faster-than-light — all rejected unless immediately negated/status-labeled. The Build Contract's say-this-instead list channels the agent toward status-labeled simulation result, candidate mode, first-failure, proper-distance functional. The agent's vocabulary is constrained at the lexical level, downstream of its intent.

B2.8.4 Wall 3 — compute_status overwrites the promotion

Suppose the agent self-reports "ladder_level": "PHYSICAL_CLAIM" out of enthusiasm. Validator step 7 rejects any ladder_level ∈ {PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY, PHYSICAL_CLAIM} outright. And step 8 discards the self-report entirely: compute_status recomputes from the gates, and its range maxes out at PASS_TOY. The agent does not get to assert its level; the level is a function of evidence the agent had to declare in a closed alphabet. Self-promotion is not a permission the agent has — Build Contract §1 rule 4: status promotion requires owner/attorney escalation; an agent may never move a candidate up on its own authority. The validator is the mechanical embodiment of that rule.

B2.8.5 The forced honest output

Cornered by three walls, the agent's only serializable output for an uncomputed-source metric is the honest downgrade — e.g. Scenario 2's FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC card. The "good news" it wanted to deliver is mechanically rewritten into: "status-labeled simulation result: invariant toy distance change with undetermined source; first failure HC-02; next step exhibit T_μν." That is not a worse document. Per Build Contract §1 rule 6, "most modes should fail; that is good" — a systematically failing corpus with one honestly-asterisked survivor is far more credible to a hostile reviewer (and to a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer's diligence team) than a document of confident green checkmarks. The discipline does not make the agent smarter. It makes the agent unable to be dishonestly optimistic.

B2.8.6 What the walls do NOT do (the honest residue)

The three walls enforce consistency, vocabulary, and non-self-promotion. They do not verify that a PASS token was earned. An agent that computes nothing but writes source_check: PASS, invariant_check: PASS, energy_check: PASS produces a card that validates and computes to PASS_TOY — a forged survivor. This is the irreducible first failure named in §B2.1 and re-named in §B2.4 and §B2.6. It is closed only outside this chapter, by the requirement (Build Contract §6, §7; red-team acceptance) that each per-HC chapter independently recompute every PASS it asserts with a runnable test, and that the red-team pass re-derive the gate. The discipline layer's honest scope statement, which must travel with it everywhere: this validator guarantees no card claims more than it declares; it does not guarantee that what a card declares is true. Truth of tokens is delegated to the HC closure chapters and the adversarial review pass.

B2.9 — Negative controls for the discipline layer itself

Per Closure-Path Protocol Stage B, the discipline layer must reject at least two deliberately-broken inputs. We run four; all must raise GateCardRejected (or downgrade), or the validator is itself broken.

# Broken input Expected validator behavior Why it matters
NC-1 Card with source_check: "FAIL" and claim: "...operational propulsion..." GateCardRejected at step 3 + step 6 the central no-source⇒no-propulsion coupling
NC-2 Card with gates.invariant_check: "looks fine" GateCardRejected at step 1 (illegal token) closed-enumeration discipline; no soft tokens
NC-3 Card with active_fields: ["delta_G_AB"] and empty layer_assignments GateCardRejected at step 2 HC-07 admissibility; no un-homed primitive field
NC-4 Card with uv_boundary: "UV_DELEGATED" but "global stability solved" absent from forbidden_claims GateCardRejected at step 5 UV-OPEN axiom may not be silently treated as closed
NC-5 Card with first_failure: "" GateCardRejected at step 0 every card MUST name a first failure
NC-6 Card with ladder_level: "PHYSICAL_CLAIM" GateCardRejected at step 7 ceiling is PASS_TOY; level 5 unreachable 
def test_discipline_negative_controls():
    for card in [NC1, NC2, NC3, NC4, NC5, NC6]:
        try:
            validate_gate_card(card)
            assert False, f"validator FAILED to reject {card['model_id']}"
        except GateCardRejected:
            pass    # correct: failed closed
    # and the survivor must pass:
    assert compute_status(GATE_005) == ("TOY_TESTED", "PASS_TOY")

First failure of B2.9: the negative controls test the validator's coded branches; they cannot test branches that were never coded. If a future forbidden phrase (say a new energy-source euphemism) is not in FORBIDDEN_UNQUALIFIED, no negative control catches it. The mitigation is that FORBIDDEN_UNQUALIFIED is sourced verbatim from Build Contract §4 and must be re-synced whenever §4 changes; the residue is the lag between a new forbidden phrase entering the contract and entering the list. This is a real, named gap, not a closed one.

B2.10 — Patent extraction

The discipline layer is, on its own, the document's most defensible option-value asset — it is patentable independent of whether any drive mode ever survives. The extractable method/system elements:

  1. A gate-supervised status-classification method for candidate physical-simulation modes, in which (a) each mode is represented by a structured record carrying a closed-enumeration set of gate tokens spanning definition, invariant, source, gauge, energy-visibility, causality, and UV-boundary checks; (b) a meet operation over an ordered status ladder computes the mode's status as the minimum of an evidence-derived ceiling and a downgrade-tree floor; and (c) the computed status overrides any self-reported status, enforcing non-self-promotion.

  2. A fail-closed claim-gating mechanism wherein a free-text "strongest allowed claim" is mechanically constrained by the gate tokens — specifically, a source-failure token forbids propulsion language, a UV-delegated token forbids global-stability language and requires its declaration as forbidden, and an energy gate that admits no clean-pass token forbids energy-solved language — implemented as assertions that reject the record rather than warn.

  3. A geometric-admissibility binding requiring every active field in the record to carry a layer assignment over a declared compactification factorization (× / ⊕ / ⊗ over M4 × K_gauge × F+), such that an un-homed primitive field forces a definition failure.

  4. A downgrade-tree classifier mapping each first-failing gate, evaluated in a fixed dependency order, to a categorical status token (FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY, FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY, TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC, UV_DELEGATED, PASS_TOY, …) that simultaneously names the first failure and pins the ladder level.

The patent-relevant novelty is the inversion of the usual optimization target: the system is engineered to maximize honest failure visibility and forbid optimistic promotion, the opposite of a typical scoring/ranking system. That inversion is the claim.

First failure of B2.10: patentability of a method that is largely a validation-and-labeling discipline may face subject-matter-eligibility challenges (abstract-idea rejection). The honest downgrade: the claim is strongest as a system tied to the concrete structured-record schema and the override-of-self-report mechanism, weakest as a bare "method of classifying." Attorney escalation required before any filing language — agent may not assert patentability as closed.

B2.11 — Reviewer attacks (and honest responses)

Attack 1 — "This is theater. The validator only checks that a card is consistent with itself; an agent can write PASS everywhere and sail through." Response (conceded, scoped): Correct, and stated four times in this chapter (§B2.1, §B2.4, §B2.6, §B2.8.6). The validator's contract is consistency, not correctness. Truth of tokens is delegated to per-HC chapters that independently recompute each PASS with a runnable test, and to the red-team pass that re-derives gates. The discipline layer's value is that it makes the only remaining way to lie a well-formed false token assertion — a small, single, auditable surface — instead of unconstrained persuasive prose. We reduced the attack surface; we did not eliminate it, and we say so.

Attack 2 — "The seed validate_gate_card in the protocol has an inverted assertion on the UV/global-stability check; your whole discipline is buggy." Response (conceded, fixed): The seed (§B2.6.1) asserts "global stability solved" not in forbidden_claims, which is the negation of intent. We flagged this explicitly and the strict validator (§B2.6.2, step 5) implements the correct logic: forbidden in the claim, required-present in forbidden_claims. NC-4 tests it. The bug is real, named, and corrected — which is itself an instance of the discipline (downgrade-don't-hide).

Attack 3 — "energy_check with no FAIL token is a dodge — you've defined away the hardest gate." Response (conceded, by design, with the catch named): The energy gate cannot FAIL because its job is visibility, not pass/fail. A genuinely hidden exotic source does not slip through; it surfaces as a source_check inconsistency feeding FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY, and the forbidden-phrase scan blocks negative energy available / solves the energy problem regardless. The honest residue: this only works if the energy ledger is actually balanced and checked downstream (HC-03/HC-09). The gate guarantees the claim cannot overstate energy; it does not, alone, compute the ledger.

Attack 4 — "You allow EFT_CANDIDATE (level 3) via the UV-delegated path — that's a promotion you said agents can't make." Response (conceded, scoped): The UV_DELEGATED position is lateral, not a closed level 3 (§B2.5.2, §B2.7.4). It carries a permanent asterisk: the strongest claim is explicitly "conditional on an UNADOPTED axiom," global stability solved is forbidden and must be declared forbidden, and it never reaches level 4. No agent promoted it to a closed claim; the validator wrote the lateral status, and the forbidden-claims requirement is machine-checked.

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED · PASS_TOY (ceiling) — the discipline layer (ladder, schema, downgrade tree, validate_gate_card, compute_status) is defined and toy-tested against six negative controls; it makes no physical claim about any drive mode and structurally cannot promote one past PASS_TOY. First failure: the enforcement layer guarantees consistency, not correctness — a well-formed gate card asserting unearned PASS tokens (token forgery) validates and computes to PASS_TOY; the validator cannot detect a token that was asserted rather than computed. (Earliest concrete trigger: source_check: PASS written without exhibiting T_μν = −(2/√(-g)) δS_matter/δg^{μν}.) What remains to close: independent recomputation of every asserted PASS in each per-HC closure chapter with a runnable acceptance test; a red-team re-derivation pass that recomputes gates from source rather than reading the card; and a re-sync mechanism binding FORBIDDEN_UNQUALIFIED to Build Contract §4 so new forbidden phrases cannot lag the list. None of these is closable from inside the schema layer. Patent extraction: gate-supervised status-classification method with status-meet override of self-report; fail-closed claim-gating (no-source⇒no-propulsion, UV-delegated⇒no-global-stability, energy-never-clean-pass) implemented as record-rejecting assertions; geometric layer-assignment admissibility binding; downgrade-tree classifier that names first failure while pinning ladder level. Novelty = inversion of the optimization target toward honest-failure-maximization. Attorney escalation required; patentability NOT asserted as closed (abstract-idea risk named). Reviewer attack: "The validator only checks self-consistency — an agent can stamp PASS everywhere and pass." Honest response: conceded and stated as this chapter's own first failure; the discipline reduces the lie surface from unbounded persuasive prose to a single well-formed false-token assertion, which the per-HC chapters and the adversarial review pass are required to recompute independently. We constrain the shape, the vocabulary, and the promotion of a claim; we delegate the truth of each token, and we never pretend otherwise.

C0.0 — What this chapter is, and why it sits before C1

The chapters that follow (C1 spacetime/stress-energy, C2 the forward lobe, C3 the frozen parent geometry, D1–D4 the candidate families, E* the hard-challenge gates) each operate one part of the native geometry. C1 reads the off-diagonal blocks and projects them into 4D sources. C3 freezes the parent and certifies admissibility. D1–D4 enumerate candidate modes by their internal origin. What none of them does — and what a reader meeting the geometry for the first time needs before any of them makes sense — is state, in one place, how the full 13D geometry is used: what it supplies, what it does not supply, and the disciplined order of operations by which a candidate metric-interface profile is generated, licensed, projected, billed, gated, and either retained at PASS_TOY or killed at a named first failure.

That is this chapter. It is a usage and framing chapter, deliberately placed before C1 so that every downstream geometric claim inherits a single, explicit posture. Its load-bearing thesis is one sentence:

The native 13D geometry supplies the admissible design space — which metric blocks, internal gauge descendants, scalar/modulus channels, chamber constraints, and quantization objects may enter a candidate profile; how internal descendants project into 4D; what counts as double-counting; what must stay frozen; and which gate kills a cheating candidate first. It does not by itself supply propulsion, energy closure, source closure, global stability, or any Mars travel-time reduction.

Everything in C0 is an unpacking of that sentence into an operable protocol. The chapter changes nothing in the physics and licenses nothing new; it converts a geometry the corpus already fixes into a compiler discipline that the rest of the document obeys. The boundary in §C0.8 governs the entire chapter and is restated, not weakened, at the close.

A note on register and ceiling, carried once and binding throughout: the ceiling everywhere is PASS_TOY; the mission counterparty is named generically as a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer; and no candidate is engineered to survive. "No candidate passes" is a contracted design choice, not a defect of the apparatus (§C0.5, §C0.8).

C0.1 — The two meanings of "the three parts" (do not conflate them)

The native geometry is "in three parts" in two distinct senses, and the single most common category error a reader (or a candidate author) can make is to collapse them. We separate them explicitly and keep them separate for the rest of the document.

C0.1.1 — Sense 1: the product geometry (three blocks)

The parent object is the product manifold (frozen; full bookkeeping in C3.2.1):

𝓜_parent  =  M4  ×  K_gauge  ×  F+
            └──┬──┘ └───┬────┘  └─┬─┘
          4D Einstein   internal   admissibility / Weyl-holonomy
           spacetime     gauge      CHAMBER  (a discrete label — NOT a coordinate factor)
                       geometry

K_gauge   =  K6  ×  S²  ×  S¹_Y           (the 9D internal gauge geometry)
   • K6   = SU(3)/T²   dim 6   (flag manifold; strong-sector internal directions; Isom ⊇ SU(3))
   • S²              dim 2   (weak two-sphere; Isom = SO(3) ≅ SU(2)/ℤ₂)
   • S¹_Y            dim 1   (hypercharge circle, period 2πR_Y; Isom = U(1)_Y)

The dimension bookkeeping is exact and frozen (C3.2.1):

dim M4      = 4                       (signature −+++, Lorentzian; the ONLY dynamical metric block)
dim K_gauge = 6 + 2 + 1 = 9           (internal, Riemannian, compact, FROZEN radii)
F+                     dim 0          (admissibility chamber — a label, contributes NO coordinate)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dim 𝓜_parent (coordinate) = 4 + 9 + 0 = 13     ← the "13D" is 4 visible + 9 internal; F+ adds 0 coordinates

The "13" is therefore 4 + 9. F+ is the third block but contributes zero coordinate dimensions — it is an admissibility/Weyl-chamber/holonomy-selection region, a filter, not a place. Treating F+ as a 14th coordinate, or as a tunable internal modulus, is the chamber error that §C0.2.3 forbids.

C0.1.2 — Sense 2: the layer discipline (three operations)

Orthogonally to the three blocks, every object in a candidate excitation is assigned to exactly one of three layers (the ×/⊕/⊗ discipline of A1 §3.2):

×   metric / geometric base            — the geometry itself
⊕   admissibility / projection / chamber — the projectors and the chamber filter
⊗   bundles / operators / quantization   — fields, operators, quantum status, the source ledger

These are operations, not regions. A single block can feed more than one layer (the internal blocks of K_gauge supply read-only × geometry and, once excited and projected, ⊗ sources), and a single layer draws from more than one block. The two "threes" are different axes of the same object; the rule is simply: never use the block decomposition where the layer decomposition is meant, or vice versa. Sense 1 answers where does this content live in the geometry?; Sense 2 answers what kind of object is it, and how is it accounted?

C0.2 — The roles of M4, K_gauge, F+

Each block has a single, sharply bounded job. The discipline of the whole compiler comes from holding these roles fixed.

C0.2.1 — M4 — the visible metric arena

M4 is the 4D Einstein-frame block where the physically visible metric g_μν(x) lives. It is the only block permitted to directly define the visible line element, the forward proper-distance functional L_F (C2), local cones, geodesic effects, and the mission overlay. Everything a reviewer can "see" as a metric effect must terminate here.

The role carries a hard rule:

Only M4 may directly enter the visible line element used by L_F. Any internal or off-diagonal contribution must first pass through the declared projection Π (§C0.3), become a licensed 4D source/channel, and then be billed through the T_μν source ledger. Directly treating an internal perturbation as a visible metric deformation — injecting internal geometry into g_μν without Π and without a ledger entry — is a first-failure event (FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE if it bypasses the layer map; FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC if it reaches g_μν unbilled).

M4 is where the design is sharpened: the forward lobe F_τ, the proper-distance functional L_F, the invariant-distance gate, the tetrad-frame energy audit, the causality/horizon checks, and the mission overlay are all M4 objects. None of them may be improved by smuggling internal geometry; they may be improved only by an admissibly sourced δg_μν whose stress-energy is paid in full.

C0.2.2 — K_gauge = K6 × S² × S¹_Y — internal-origin labels & source channels

K_gauge is the 9D internal gauge geometry. Its job is not to move anything directly. Its job is to generate licensed internal descendants — and, equally important, to label every candidate channel by the internal direction it descends from, which fixes which ledger, UV-class, BRST check, and double-count rule apply.

The two descendant families are fixed by the off-diagonal structure of the parent metric under Π:

δG_μA   →  gauge-like / graviphoton-like channels   (KK ansatz: δA_μ^a ← δG_μA)
δG_AB   →  scalar / modulus-like channels           (moduli:    δφ^I  ← δG_AB)

The role carries a hard rule:

δG_μA and δG_AB are NOT extra free 4D metric levers. Under Π they become 4D fields/sources (δA_μ^a, δφ^I) that must be billed in the stress-energy ledger T_μν. The internal origin is a license tag, not a physical pass: declaring "this mode descends from S¹_Y" tells the compiler which source ledger, which UV-sensitivity class (KK descendants auto-tag UV-sensitive when their internal-momentum support approaches the frozen KK scale m_1 ≈ 1.0–1.4, C3.2.2b / D4 §2.2), and which double-count rule to enforce — it does not, by itself, advance the candidate one gate.

K_gauge is where generic mode lists are replaced by native mode families: K6 strong-sector channels, S² weak-sector channels, S¹_Y hypercharge-circle channels, mixed δG_μA, internal δG_AB/modulus, and the composite templates these allow. The D1–D4 candidate catalog is organized by exactly this native origin (the native-origin column of D4), so that every candidate carries its provenance and inherits the correct downstream obligations.

C0.2.3 — F+ — admissibility, chamber filtering, first-failure discipline

F+ is the positive/admissible Weyl-holonomy chamber. It is not a coordinate dimension (it contributes 0; §C0.1.1) and not a continuous field. It is a filter. Its job is to decide which branch is active, which candidates are admissible, which modes cross a chamber wall, which perturbations introduce a new primitive, and which source templates are illegal — and to make those decisions before the expensive downstream integrals run.

The role carries the sharpest hard rule in the chapter:

F+ must never be excited as a continuous physical knob. A candidate may be projected into F+, tested against F+, or rejected by F+. It may not treat chamber selection as a physical source — it carries no stress-energy, and it contributes nothing to L_F or S_L. Any candidate that books "chamber energy" into the score, or excites F+ as a tunable modulus, is chamber abuse and is rejected before the source gate ever runs: FAIL_CHAMBER / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE.

F+ is what makes the First-Failure Engine precise rather than vague. A candidate does not fail merely because "the physics is unknown"; it fails because a specific admissibility rule fires a specific token — FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE, FAIL_CHAMBER, FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT, or UV_DELEGATED. The chamber is the apparatus that turns "this looks wrong" into "this is rejected here, by this rule, with this token."

C0.3 — The ×/⊕/⊗ discipline and the projection + billing rule (load-bearing)

The layer discipline is the bookkeeping that keeps geometry, projection, and physical/quantum sourcing from being silently traded for one another. Every component of a candidate excitation

Ξ_drive(t,x) = { δg_μν , δA_μ^a , δφ^I , δG_μA , δG_AB , Σ_state , Σ_gauge }

maps to exactly one layer. The assignment is total and disjoint: a component with no layer is FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE; a component on two layers is FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT.

C0.3.1 — The three layers, with their exact object lists

× — metric / geometric base. The geometry itself: δg_μν (the M4 perturbation — the only block that bends L_F directly), the internal metric blocks g_mn(K6), g(S²), g(S¹_Y) (present on × but frozen / read-only — exciting a_K6 / a_S2 / R_Y is a modulus excitation → UV-sensitive → UV_DELEGATED, not a pass), plus compact-factor data, coordinate chart, tensor components, internal-origin tag, frozen-vs-active flag, projection status. Role: define candidate geometry; never smuggle in source closure. First failure: editing a frozen block or modifying the parent inventory → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE (UV_DELEGATED if it is a modulus excitation).

⊕ — admissibility / projection / chamber. The projectors and the chamber filter: the F+ chamber label, holonomy/Weyl-domain data, projector eigen-selection, and the projectors themselves Π_layer, Π_freeze, Π_chamber, Π_dup, Π_adm and Π : G_MN → g_μν. Role: gate membership and project 13D→4D; carries no independent stress-energy. First failure: a ⊕ component asserting a stress ledger (chamber-as-source) → FAIL_CHAMBER / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE; a candidate that bypasses projection → FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT / FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.

⊗ — bundles / operators / quantization. Where internal geometry becomes a physically billed 4D source: the excited channels δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, matter δψ, ghosts/antighosts, constraints, BRST/BV state data, Σ_state, Σ_gauge, and per channel its field channel, stress-energy contribution, BRST/BV status, ghost/constraint sector, anomaly/regulator status, and source-mismatch norm. Role: feed the T_μν source ledger; never bypass it. First failure: a field used but not licensed, or a source contribution not billed → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC / AUDIT_QUANTUM / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT.

One declared register split (stated, not an error). The C3 worked table routes the excited channels δG_μA and δG_AB onto ⊗ (they carry stress ledgers and are sourced), whereas the A1 §3.2 quick-reference and the C1 §9 gate-card list them on ⊕ (they are "projected out" of the 4D g and accounted only as source/constraint). Both readings encode the same discipline: an off-diagonal block is never a free 4D metric lever — it enters 4D only via Π and the ledger. For this compiler, the billing-and-quantization view (⊗) governs once a channel is excited and projected (C3 is the native-geometry authority chapter); the ⊕ label is the pre-projection admissibility view. A candidate must state which view it is in and may never claim both a ⊕ "projected-out" pass and a ⊗ stress credit for the same descendant — that is exactly FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT.

C0.3.2 — The projection Π and the billing rule

The parent metric in block form, and the single-frame projection (C1 §9):

G_MN  =  [ g_μν + (KK off-diagonal)   G_μB ]
         [ G_Aν                       G_AB ]

Π : G_MN(M4 × K_gauge) ──► g_μν(M4)       (the one Einstein-frame block after integrating out K_gauge)
    moduli  δφ^I  ← δG_AB fluctuations
    gauge   δA_μ^a ← δG_μA   (KK ansatz)

The billing rule is the load-bearing rule of the entire compiler:

Under Π, δG_μA and δG_AB become licensed 4D sources/channels (δA_μ^a, δφ^I) that MUST be billed in the stress-energy ledger T_μν, plus constraint terms L_constraint for the chamber. The causal chain is forced by the layer graph:

> ⊗ (δA^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, matter)  ──contributes T^{(⊗)}_μν (must carry a ledger; HC-02 matches it)──►
> × (δg_μν on M4)  via  G_μν[δg] = M_Pl⁻² T^{(⊗)}_μν   ──the ONLY layer entering L_F directly──►
> S_L (the forward-distance score, C2)
> ⊕ (F+)  gates membership BEFORE the integral — carries no metric content, contributes nothing to L_F
>

A ⊗ component with T^{(⊗)}_μν = 0 contributes exactly zero to S_L. The frozen internal × blocks contribute a constant (the same for every candidate, pinned by the freeze hash) and can never create a difference in S_L. There is therefore no path by which internal geometry moves the visible score without first appearing, in full, in the source ledger.

C0.3.3 — The no-double-count and no-chamber-abuse rules

Two short rules close the two cheapest cheats (the audit object lives at C1 §9 and C3.6.4):

NO_DOUBLE_COUNT (one-parent projection):
  for each gauge / KK descendant d:
      provenance = trace_to_parent(d)             # which internal direction it descends from
      if d appears as BOTH a ⊗ gauge stress AND a × geometric source with the SAME provenance:
          return FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT(d)
  return OK                                        # each descendant counted ONCE — ⊗ stress OR × KK effect, never both

NO_CHAMBER_ABUSE:
  F+ carries NO stress-energy; it only SELECTS which ⊗-layer modes are admissible, acting BEFORE the L_F integral.
  Any candidate that books "chamber energy" into S_L, or excites F+ as a continuous modulus,
  is rejected BEFORE the source gate runs → FAIL_CHAMBER / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE.

The canonical first-failure token set the projection/billing layer can raise:

FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE     — internal geometry injected into g_μν without Π; a component with no ×/⊕/⊗ layer;
                         a 13th gauge index / off-menu field; a frozen-block edit (⊃ FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT).
FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT      — one internal descendant booked on two layers / counted as BOTH ⊗ stress AND × KK source;
                         claiming both a ⊕ "projected-out" pass and a ⊗ stress credit for the same descendant.
FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC  — a projected internal effect that reaches g_μν but is NOT billed to the T_μν ledger
                         (the manuscript's deepest worked failure; MID-METRIC-001).
FAIL_CHAMBER           — treating F+ as a continuous physical knob / extracting "chamber energy" into S_L.
UV_DELEGATED           — source closure that REQUIRES Π to be globally valid (compactification stability OPEN),
                         or excitation momentum above the frozen KK scale m_1.

C0.4 — The native 13D candidate-generation protocol (7 steps)

This is the order of operations the compiler runs for every candidate metric-interface profile. It is the operational content of the chapter: a generic "invent a metric and test it" workflow is replaced by a fixed, auditable sequence in which each step either advances the candidate or kills it at a named token. The production projector form (Step 4) is D4 §2.3.

STEP 1 — FREEZE THE PARENT INVENTORY
  Record:  𝓜_parent = M4 × K_gauge × F+ ;  K_gauge = K6 × S² × S¹_Y ;  dim_coord = 13 ;  F+ = chamber, dim 0.
  Confirm parent_freeze_hash == FREEZE-HASH (content-addressed SHA256 of the FREEZE-DESCRIPTOR).
  The candidate MAY NOT change this inventory.  Any edit (silent modulus rescale, menu growth, block edit,
  an off-diagonal turned on in the background) ⇒ FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT (⊂ FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE).

STEP 2 — DECLARE INTERNAL ORIGIN(S)
  Each candidate declares one or more of:
    M4-direct metric | K6 descendant | S² descendant | S¹_Y descendant | mixed δG_μA
    | internal δG_AB / modulus | matter/stress channel | constraint/auxiliary channel.
  The origin is a LICENSE TAG (which ledger, UV-class, BRST check, double-count rule apply) — NOT a physical pass.

STEP 3 — ASSIGN EXACTLY ONE ×/⊕/⊗ LAYER PER COMPONENT
  Total and disjoint.   none → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE ;   two → FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT.

STEP 4 — PROJECT
  Π_adm = Π_freeze · Π_chamber · Π_layer · Π_dup        (production form, D4 §2.3 ; idempotent: Π_adm² = Π_adm)
  Π : G_MN(M4 × K) → g_μν(M4)
  admissibility defect  ε_adm = ‖Ξ − Π_adm·Ξ‖ / ‖Ξ‖ ∈ [0,1] ;  ADMISSIBLE iff ε_adm = 0 (necessary, NOT sufficient).
  Outcome per component:  visible metric deformation | source field | constraint | rejected component.

STEP 5 — BILL TO THE T_μν SOURCE LEDGER
  Every internal descendant that influences the 4D metric MUST appear in the T_μν ledger.
  none → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.

STEP 6 — ENERGY / EFT GATES
  NEC / WEC / SEC / DEC      (on the DECLARED supply T_fields, in the Einstein-frame null cone)
  χ_R , χ_K , χ_T , χ_grad , χ_source , χ_max     (EFT-admissibility: χ_max = max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad) < 1)
  declared NEC-violating supply → FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY ;  χ_K (compactification) breach → UV_DELEGATED.

STEP 7 — EMIT A GATE CARD
  geometry_origin :         (Step 2)
  layer_assignment :        (Step 3)
  projection_path :         (Step 4 — the Π_adm composition actually taken)
  source_billing :          (Step 5 — ledger entry, or FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC)
  first_failure :           (the earliest gate token)
  strongest_allowed_claim : (ceiling PASS_TOY, on admissibility only)
  patent_residue :          (which validator survives even on failure)

The native-geometry gate-card block (a native_geometry extension on the base schema of A1 §3.3; it never relaxes the base fail-closed rules) records the same fields machine-readably:

C0.5 — The framing upgrade: from "invent → test → fail" to a constrained design COMPILER

The seven-step protocol is not merely a checklist bolted onto an existing engine. It changes what the engine is.

Before. The generic posture is: invent a metric ansatz, compute its curvature, read off a demanded stress-energy, test it against the gates, and watch it usually fail. This works — it is honest and it produces failures — but it is wasteful and it is weak. Wasteful, because the candidate space is unbounded: there is no principled restriction on what a "metric" may be, so the engine spends its effort rejecting profiles that were never admissible to begin with (coordinate artifacts, smuggled fields, chamber-sourced lobes). Weak, because the reason a candidate fails is diffuse — "the physics doesn't close" — which is hard to patent, hard to defend in hostile review, and easy to mistake for "we just haven't found the right metric yet."

After. The native posture is a constrained design compiler. It does not start from an arbitrary metric; it starts from the frozen inventory M4 × K_gauge × F+. It does not test an unbounded space; it classifies by native origin, projects correctly through Π, bills to the ledger, and rejects double-counting, chamber-abuse, and unsourced metrics — and only then, inside the admissible space that survives, does it optimize. The candidate space is bounded by the geometry itself; the failures are named by precise admissibility rules rather than gestured at; and the surviving design discipline is a genuine, defensible method (the patent residue of §C0.6) that holds even when every physical candidate dies.

This is strictly stronger than a generic GR/EFT screening platform, and it stays exactly as honest: it concedes everything the screening platform conceded, and it adds structure rather than claims.

C0.5.1 — The stronger native design question

The generic engine answers a weak question: "Does this particular invented metric pass the gates?" The compiler answers a stronger one:

Is there an admissible 13D-origin profile — one that respects the frozen inventory, assigns every component to exactly one layer, projects correctly through Π, and bills every internal descendant to the source ledger — whose 4D projection creates a useful local metric effect and whose source / energy / gauge / quantum / UV / mission gates do not fail?

This is the question the rest of the document is organized to ask well. It is sharper because it is scoped: it asks only over the admissible space, so a negative answer is informative (the geometry's own admissible content cannot close the gates) rather than merely tiring (we tried some metrics and they failed).

The contracted, honest current answer is: no candidate passes. That is a design choice, not a defect, and not an admission that the apparatus is broken (§C0.8). The deepest-surviving worked exemplar, MID-METRIC-001 (G1), reaches a real proper-distance effect and dies — correctly — at the source gate: G_tt = −2.0202×10⁻⁴ → ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶ (negative ⇒ exotic), a genuine ~0.22%-class deficit that is 100% unsourced, terminal token FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (source gate HC-02 fires first in reading order; the root cause is the exotic ρ_eff < 0 at the energy gate HC-03, status AUDIT — declaring an ordinary field cannot match the demanded NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC-violating source, so "just declare a field and it passes" is false). The compiler's value is that it produces this failure for a stated reason at a named gate, not that it produces a survivor.

C0.6 — Patent posture (what the compiler claims, and what survives every failure)

The patent claims the Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System/Method — the classification, projection, filtering, and billing machinery and the gate-card schema — not a physical drive. The claim does not depend on the unified theory (or any compactification, or any specific corpus) being physically correct: the inventory (SU(3)/T², S², S¹_Y, F+) is configuration data fed to a general validator, and replacing it with any other fixed background (e.g. bare Minkowski + Standard-Model content) leaves every algorithm here unchanged. (Full strategy: I1 — Patent Strategy — Invention Families & Independent Claims; residue ledger: H1.4.5 — What stays patentable after every failure.)

The claim-boundary paragraph, carried verbatim into the disclosure: the disclosed systems and methods do not require the physical correctness of any particular unified theory; a native 13D geometry may be used as a frozen background inventory defining metric blocks, internal-origin labels, admissibility chambers, and projection paths; the system may classify, reject, or downgrade candidate profiles based on violations of that inventory without asserting that any candidate constitutes a physical propulsion device.

C0.7 — Nature-inspired design discipline (apply only the real analogies; report the gap honestly)

The program's methodology permits a biological or natural analogy to inform the design discipline — but only under a strict adoption gate, because an analogy with no mathematical home is decoration, and decoration is exactly what this chapter exists to remove. The gate is stated once and enforced:

Adoption gate (1 + 2 + 3). An analogy may be adopted only if it has (1) a precise mathematical home in the existing apparatus (an invariant, a projector, a filter — something already defined in the manuscript), (2) a clear first-failure token it sharpens or supplies, and (3) a statement of what it does not license. An analogy that supplies a mechanism — energy, source, or exoticity — without satisfying all three is rejected, and the gap is reported rather than force-fit.

Under that gate, exactly three analogies qualify, and each maps to machinery that already exists:

  • Work-in-invariants (gauge à la holonomy). In biological control, regulation is expressed against invariants of state, not against raw coordinates, so that a coordinate or frame change cannot fake a result. Mathematical home: the ⊕-layer holonomy/Weyl-chamber data and the gauge/coordinate-invariance discipline — S_L and L_F are built from invariants of the spatial metric on a physically anchored gauge precisely so a coordinate restretch cannot manufacture a score. First failure it sharpens: FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY / FAIL_CHAMBER. Does not license: any energy or source content.

  • Multi-stage proofreading (the sequential gate filter). Biological fidelity (e.g. kinetic proofreading) is achieved by sequential, fail-closed checkpoints, each of which can reject independently, so the overall error rate is the product of stage error rates rather than any single stage's. Mathematical home: the 7-step protocol (§C0.4) and the hard-challenge gate stack (E*) — admissibility → projection → billing → energy → EFT, each able to kill the candidate at its own named token, in order. First failure it sharpens: whichever gate fires first; the first-failure discipline is itself the proofreading funnel. Does not license: the existence of a survivor — a longer funnel rejects more, it does not source anything.

  • PI-feedback / hysteresis (control & tolerance). Robust natural controllers use proportional-integral feedback and deliberate hysteresis bands to hold a setpoint against drift and noise without chattering. Mathematical home: the control/tolerance and digital-twin program (the tolerance bands and feedback discipline used to hold a candidate profile against parameter drift). First failure it sharpens: drift/tolerance violations that would otherwise leak a non-robust "pass." Does not license: any claim about the underlying physics closing — control discipline governs how well a stated profile is held, never whether the profile is physically sourced.

The honest gap — stated plainly. Nature offers genuine analogies for control/tolerance (work-in-invariants, PI-feedback/hysteresis) and screening architecture (multi-stage proofreading / fail-closed funnels). It offers nothing for source-closure or exoticity. There is no biological mechanism that supplies negative energy density, closes the stress-energy ledger for an unsourced metric, or stabilizes a compactification — and the methodology's adoption gate forbids importing one by analogy, because it would have no mathematical home (it would fail clause 1) and would supply a mechanism the rest of the document does not have (it would violate clause 3). We therefore report the gap rather than force-fit a mechanism: the nature-inspired inputs strengthen the discipline and the filter, and they are silent — correctly, deliberately silent — on the one thing that would make a candidate pass.

C0.8 — The explicit boundary (binding — restated, not weakened)

This chapter supplies a better design space and a constrained design compiler. It does not supply propulsion, energy closure, source closure, global stability, or any Mars travel-time reduction.

C1 — Spacetime, Metric, Tetrads & Stress-Energy

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED (foundational geometric layer; equations + schema + negative controls specified, pipeline not yet numerically certified at chapter scope) · ceiling for this leaf = PASS_TOY · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

1. Why this chapter matters

Every downstream claim in this document — proper-distance shortening S_L, the source ledger Δ_T, the NEC/causality gates, the EFT-admissibility ratio χ, the BRST physicality test — is a functional of the curvature of a single metric. If the geometric pipeline that maps a metric ansatz g_{μν}(x) to its Einstein tensor G_{μν}(x) and to its sourced stress-energy T^{eff}_{μν}(x) is wrong by a sign, a factor, or a convention, then every gate that consumes those tensors is silently corrupted, and a "candidate mode" can appear to pass while being numerical garbage. This chapter therefore does not assert any drive effect. It builds and fail-closes the substrate: it fixes conventions, defines the objects (g, tetrad e^a_μ, connection Γ, Riemann, Ricci, scalar R, Einstein G), specifies the deterministic computation g → g^{-1} → Γ → Riemann → Ricci → R → G, and defines the operator T_{μν} = −(2/√(−g)) δS_matter/δg^{μν} that turns a declared source action into stress-energy. The single most important discipline here is the one named in Fable_Forces: there is exactly one Einstein-frame metric. Apparent effects produced by writing the same geometry in a different conformal frame or coordinate chart are the first and cheapest way a metric-drive claim fails, and this chapter installs the machinery to catch that mechanically.

Why this is hard (per source 14): a lower-reasoning generator can emit formulas — the Christoffel symbol, the Riemann tensor — that are individually correct as LaTeX yet assemble into an engine that fails the flat-limit test because of an index-ordering bug or a finite-difference sign. The cost of that failure is not abstract: a T^{eff}_{μν} computed from a buggy G_{μν} will fabricate a stress-energy ledger, and the source gate (C-level chapters) will report a match or mismatch that means nothing. The engine must therefore be validated against known metrics before it is trusted on any ansatz, and that validation requirement is itself a gate in this chapter.

2. Conventions, signature, and the single-frame rule

We fix conventions once, globally, and every later chapter inherits them. Ambiguity in sign conventions is the most common source of cross-chapter inconsistency, so we declare them explicitly (this is an acceptance requirement in source 14: "sign conventions declared").

Signature. Lorentzian, mostly-plus:

η_{μν} = diag(−1, +1, +1, +1)      (MTW / Wald "mostly plus")

Greek indices μ,ν,… ∈ {0,1,2,3} are spacetime; Latin i,j,… ∈ {1,2,3} are spatial; Latin a,b,… at the front of the alphabet are tetrad/internal Lorentz indices (also 0..3) and are raised/lowered with η_{ab}, never with g_{μν}. Gauge-group adjoint indices are written A,B (per the corpus δA_μ^a, δG_{AB}) and are kept distinct from tetrad indices by context and by the explicit ledger in C1.10.

Units. Geometrized for geometry, explicit for the source. We carry the reduced Planck mass M_Pl explicitly because the corpus action uses (M_Pl²/2)R, so the Einstein equation reads

G_{μν} = M_Pl^{−2} T_{μν}      ⇔      T^{eff}_{μν} = M_Pl² G_{μν}

which is the corpus form T^{eff}_{μν} = G_{μν}/(8πG) with M_Pl² = 1/(8πG) (reduced convention). Numerically M_Pl = 2.435×10^{18} GeV, 8πG = M_Pl^{−2}; this is the reduced Planck mass fixed by Newton's constant G_N = 6.674×10^{−11} m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻² per the Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics (PDG 2024), "Physical Constants" listing (the single experimental anchor used in this document; see §2.6). We never silently switch between 8πG and M_Pl^{−2}; the engine carries the constant as a typed field.

Riemann sign convention (declared). We use the convention in which the Ricci tensor of a positive-curvature sphere is positive:

R^ρ_{σμν} = ∂_μ Γ^ρ_{νσ} − ∂_ν Γ^ρ_{μσ} + Γ^ρ_{μλ} Γ^λ_{νσ} − Γ^ρ_{νλ} Γ^λ_{μσ}
R_{σν}    = R^ρ_{σρν}            (contraction on 1st and 3rd)
R         = g^{σν} R_{σν}
G_{μν}    = R_{μν} − ½ R g_{μν}

This is the Wald/MTW sign set, consistent with G_{μν} = +M_Pl^{−2} T_{μν} and with a positive energy density sourcing attractive gravity. Any chapter that reports a curvature must state that it used these four equations with this contraction order; a chapter that does not is rejected (this is a first-failure trap for the red-team pass).

The single Einstein-frame rule (Fable_Forces). There is one physical metric g_{μν}, the Einstein-frame metric, in which the gravitational action is (M_Pl²/2)√(−g) R with no field-dependent prefactor multiplying R. All scalar/modulus fields φ^I couple to it through L_matter, V(φ), and the kinetic metric G_{IJ}(φ), not through a Weyl rescaling of g. The reason this is load-bearing for a metric drive: a conformal transformation g̃_{μν} = Ω²(x) g_{μν} changes proper distances L_F = ∫√(γ_{ij} n^i n^j) ds and can manufacture an apparent forward-distance shortening that is pure frame choice. We forbid this by contract: all proper-distance functionals are evaluated in the Einstein frame, and any candidate that only shortens distance after a Weyl rescaling is downgraded to FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY (frame variant). This is the chapter's structural defense and it is enforced in C1.7 as a negative control.

3. Formal object: the metric and its excitation

3.0 The manifold, atlas, and what "coordinates" means here

The arena is a 4-dimensional, smooth (C^∞), connected, paracompact, time-orientable Lorentzian manifold (M4, g). Concretely the corpus parent space is M4 × K_gauge × F+ (Fable_GUT), and M4 is the 4D Einstein-frame quotient after the projection Π (C1.9). Points p ∈ M4 are physical events; coordinates x^μ are labels supplied by a chart ϕ: U ⊂ M4 → ℝ⁴, and physics is whatever is invariant under change of chart x^μ → x'^μ(x) (diffeomorphism). An atlas is a collection of charts covering M4 with smooth transition maps. This is not pedantry: the entire first line of defense against a fake metric drive is the demand that the headline number S_L be chart-independent, i.e. a property of (M4,g), not of the labels x^μ. Tensors are the chart-covariant objects (T'^{μ}_{ν} = (∂x'^μ/∂x^α)(∂x^β/∂x'^ν)T^{α}_{β}); the metric is a (0,2) tensor, Γ is not a tensor (C1.5), and only scalar contractions like R, K, S_L are reportable observables. The engine is written to be chart-agnostic: it takes g_{μν}(x) plus the chart and never assumes Cartesian structure, which is why T7 (same geometry in two charts → identical invariants) is a mandatory gate.

3.1 The metric

The metric is a smooth, symmetric, non-degenerate rank-2 covariant tensor field on the 4-manifold M4:

g : M4 → T*M ⊗_sym T*M,    g_{μν} = g_{νμ},    det(g) < 0,    g ↦ g^{μν} with g^{μλ} g_{λν} = δ^μ_ν

Non-degeneracy det g ≠ 0 is what makes g^{-1} exist; the Lorentzian condition det g < 0 (in 4D, mostly-plus) is what makes one eigenvalue timelike. First failure if violated: if at any grid point det g ≥ 0 or det g = 0, the inverse step is undefined and the engine must halt and emit FAIL_DEGENERATE_METRIC rather than returning a finite-but-wrong g^{-1} (a naive linear solve will happily return numerical noise at a near-degenerate point — this is the single most dangerous silent failure in the whole pipeline, see C1.6).

3.2 The drive excitation, mapped to the metric

The corpus drive object is

Ξ_drive(t,x) = { δg_{μν}, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_{μA}, δG_{AB}, state/gauge data }.

Only the first component δg_{μν} is directly a metric perturbation. The discipline of this chapter is to insist that none of δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_{μA}, δG_{AB} move the metric except through stress-energy. That is: a field excitation perturbs T_{μν}, and T_{μν} perturbs g only by solving the Einstein equation. There is no "direct metric lever" that a field pulls without paying its source bill. We write the full metric as

g_{μν}(t,x) = ḡ_{μν}(x) + δg_{μν}(t,x)

where ḡ is the background (Minkowski for the lab toy, or a declared cosmological background) and δg is the candidate metric-interface excitation. Three-layer assignment (Build Contract §2):

Excitation component Layer Role here
δg_{μν} × metric/geometric base the only object the curvature pipeline acts on directly
δA_μ^a, δφ^I ⊗ bundles/operators sources entering T_{μν} via gauge/scalar templates (C1.8)
δG_{μA}, δG_{AB} ⊕ admissibility/projection unified off-diagonal / internal-metric blocks; projected out of the 4D Einstein-frame g and accounted only as source/constraint (this projection is itself a gate; see C1.9)

This table is the contract that prevents the most seductive overclaim — "the field reshapes spacetime directly." It does not. It reshapes T_{μν}. The metric responds only through G_{μν} = M_Pl^{−2} T_{μν}.

4. Tetrads (vierbeins) and why we carry them

4.1 Definition

A tetrad (vierbein) e^a_μ(x) is a field of local Lorentz frames diagonalizing the metric pointwise:

g_{μν}(x) = e^a_μ(x) e^b_ν(x) η_{ab},        η_{ab} = e^μ_a e^ν_b g_{μν},
e^a_μ e^μ_b = δ^a_b,        e^a_μ e^ν_a = δ^ν_μ          (inverse tetrad e^μ_a)

The tetrad is defined up to a local Lorentz transformation e^a_μ → Λ^a_b(x) e^b_μ, Λ ∈ SO(1,3)↑. This 6-parameter freedom at each point is physical gauge freedom, not arbitrariness to be ignored: it is exactly the freedom a candidate could hide a coordinate effect inside.

4.2 Three reasons the tetrad is mandatory, not optional

  1. Spinors / fermionic matter have no coordinate-index representation. If any L_matter term in the corpus action contains fermions (the Standard-Model matter of Fable_Forces does), the Dirac operator is e^μ_a γ^a (∂_μ + ω_μ) and cannot be written with g_{μν} alone. The spin connection lives on the tetrad. First failure if dropped: a chapter that sources T_{μν} from a fermionic sector while working only in coordinate indices is FAIL — it has silently set the spinor source to zero.
  2. Proper-distance and proper-time functionals are frame quantities. The forward-lobe line element √(γ_{ij} n^i n^j) is most cleanly and least ambiguously defined in the comoving orthonormal frame carried with the vehicle — i.e., the tetrad attached to the worldtube W = x^μ(τ, y^a) (corpus §27). Tetrad indices are the natural home of "what a comoving observer measures," which is precisely what S_L must report.
  3. Local Lorentz invariance is a second, independent gate. A candidate effect that is real must be invariant under both diffeomorphisms (coordinate change) and local Lorentz rotations of the tetrad. We get a free second negative control: rotate e^a_μ → Λ^a_b e^b_μ at every point and confirm all scalar invariants (R, R_{μν}R^{μν}, the Kretschmann scalar K = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ}) are unchanged. Any invariant that moves is a code bug or a frame artifact.

4.3 The spin connection (the tetrad's Γ)

The tetrad's covariant derivative requires the spin connection ω_μ^{ab} = −ω_μ^{ba}, fixed by the tetrad postulate (metric-compatible, torsion-free):

∂_μ e^a_ν − Γ^λ_{μν} e^a_λ + ω_μ^{ab} e_{bν} = 0
⇒ ω_μ^{ab} = e^a_λ ( ∂_μ e^{bλ} + Γ^λ_{μν} e^{bν} )      (solved with Γ from C1.6)

The curvature 2-form of ω reproduces the Riemann tensor with tetrad legs:

R^{ab}_{μν} = ∂_μ ω_ν^{ab} − ∂_ν ω_μ^{ab} + ω_μ^{ac} ω_{νc}^{b} − ω_ν^{ac} ω_{μc}^{b},
R^{ab}_{μν} e^μ_c e^ν_d = R^{ab}_{cd}  →  R_{μν} = R^{a}_{μaν}   (consistency cross-check vs C1.6).

Engine use: computing Riemann both ways — once from Γ (coordinate) and once from ω (tetrad) — and demanding agreement is the strongest internal consistency test the geometry engine has. It is cheap and it catches index-ordering bugs that the flat-limit test misses (because flat space is zero either way). We make it a Layer-3 validation case (C1.6, test T6).

4.4 Worked tetrad (FLRW, so the cross-check is concrete)

For flat FLRW g = diag(−1, a², a², a²) a diagonal tetrad is e^0_t = 1, e^i_j = a(t)δ^i_j, inverse e^t_0 = 1, e^j_i = a^{−1}δ^j_i. The tetrad postulate then gives nonzero spin-connection components

ω_i^{0i} = −ω_i^{i0} = ȧ        (no sum; one per spatial direction),    all others 0.

The curvature 2-form R^{ab}_{μν} = ∂_μω_ν^{ab} − ∂_νω_μ^{ab} + (ω∧ω) then yields R^{0i}_{0i} = ä/a and R^{ij}_{ij} = (ȧ/a)² (frame components), which contract to the same R = 6(ä/a + (ȧ/a)²) as the coordinate path in C1.6 — the T6 cross-check, made fully explicit. The ω∧ω term is what carries the (ȧ/a)² spatial-curvature piece; an engine that drops the quadratic spin-connection term gets R = 6ä/a and fails T6 while passing T1/T4 — exactly the class of bug the tetrad path exists to expose.

4.5 The comoving worldtube tetrad (where L_F is measured)

The forward-distance functional is most cleanly defined on the tetrad transported along the vehicle worldtube W = x^μ(τ, y^a) (corpus §27). Choose e^0_μ = u_μ (the comoving 4-velocity, u^μu_μ = −1) and a triad e^i_μ Fermi-Walker transported along u (no rotation, no boost beyond the acceleration). Then the forward spatial direction is the unit triad vector n^μ = e^μ_{(1)} aligned with the lobe axis, and

L_F = ∫_0^D √( γ_{ij} n^i n^j ) ds,    γ_{ij} = e^μ_i e^ν_j g_{μν} = δ_{ij} (orthonormal triad) ⇒ L_F measured in the frame's own ruler.

Defining L_F this way (rather than in arbitrary coordinates) is itself a fail-closed choice: it removes the freedom to inflate or deflate the headline shortening S_L = 1 − L_{F,deformed}/L_{F,reference} by a coordinate or frame change, because the triad is orthonormal by construction and Fermi-Walker transport is canonical. First failure if skipped: an L_F reported in coordinate length rather than proper (frame) length is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY waiting to happen — the same metric in stretched coordinates would report a different S_L. The worldtube tetrad is the apparatus that makes S_L a physical, frame-independent number.

5. The covariant-derivative / connection layer

The unique connection compatible with g and torsion-free (Levi-Civita) has Christoffel symbols

Γ^λ_{μν} = ½ g^{λρ} ( ∂_μ g_{ρν} + ∂_ν g_{ρμ} − ∂_ρ g_{μν} ),     Γ^λ_{μν} = Γ^λ_{νμ}.

Properties the engine must assert (acceptance test in source 14, "tensor symmetries verified"): - symmetry in lower indices Γ^λ_{μν} = Γ^λ_{νμ} (torsion-free), checked to machine tolerance; - metric compatibility ∇_λ g_{μν} = ∂_λ g_{μν} − Γ^ρ_{λμ} g_{ρν} − Γ^ρ_{λν} g_{μρ} = 0, checked numerically as a residual.

Γ is not a tensor (it does not transform homogeneously), so it is never reported as a candidate observable — only its curvature is. This is itself a first-failure guard: any candidate "effect" whose entire signal lives in Γ and vanishes in every curvature scalar is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY — Γ can be set to zero at any single point by going to a local inertial (Riemann normal) frame.

6. The curvature pipeline: g → g^{-1} → Γ → Riemann → Ricci → R → G

This is the spine of the document. We give it as a deterministic, single-frame algorithm (source 14 module list and pseudocode), then state the validation gates.

6.1 Algorithm (engine spine)

INPUT:  metric ansatz g_{μν}(x; θ)         # symbolic, or grid-sampled with coords x
        mode: {SYMBOLIC | NUMERICAL}
        constant: kappa_inv = M_Pl^2        # carried, typed
OUTPUT: {g_inv, Gamma, Riemann, Ricci, R, G, invariants, gate_card}

1.  detg = det(g)
    IF detg >= 0:  HALT → emit FAIL_DEGENERATE_METRIC(point)        # signature guard
    sqrt_negg = sqrt(-detg)

2.  g_inv = inverse(g)                       # symbolic: cofactor/adjugate
                                             # numerical: LU with condition-number check
    IF cond(g) > COND_MAX:  flag NEAR_DEGENERATE(point)            # do NOT silently proceed

3.  # derivatives of g
    IF SYMBOLIC:  dg[ρ,μ,ν] = ∂_ρ g_{μν}            # exact
    IF NUMERICAL: dg[ρ,μ,ν] = D_ρ g_{μν}            # 4th-order central FD, stencil h
                  record truncation_order = 4, h

4.  Gamma[λ,μ,ν] = ½ g_inv[λ,ρ] ( dg[μ,ρ,ν] + dg[ν,ρ,μ] − dg[ρ,μ,ν] )
    ASSERT  Gamma[λ,μ,ν] == Gamma[λ,ν,μ]            # torsion-free
    ASSERT  ∇_λ g_{μν} ≈ 0   (residual ≤ tol_compat)# metric compatibility

5.  dGamma[σ,λ,μ,ν] = ∂_σ Gamma[λ,μ,ν]               # symbolic exact / FD numerical
    Riemann[ρ,σ,μ,ν] = dGamma[μ,ρ,ν,σ] − dGamma[ν,ρ,μ,σ]
                       + Gamma[ρ,μ,λ]·Gamma[λ,ν,σ] − Gamma[ρ,ν,λ]·Gamma[λ,μ,σ]
    ASSERT antisymmetry  Riemann[ρ,σ,μ,ν] == −Riemann[ρ,σ,ν,μ]
    ASSERT first Bianchi  Riemann[ρ,σ,μ,ν]+Riemann[ρ,μ,ν,σ]+Riemann[ρ,ν,σ,μ] == 0
    (lower ρ with g; ASSERT pair symmetry  R_{ρσμν} == R_{μνρσ})

6.  Ricci[σ,ν] = Riemann[ρ,σ,ρ,ν]                   # contract 1st & 3rd (declared)
    ASSERT  Ricci symmetric  Ricci[σ,ν] == Ricci[ν,σ]

7.  R = g_inv[σ,ν] · Ricci[σ,ν]

8.  G[μ,ν] = Ricci[μ,ν] − ½ R · g[μ,ν]
    ASSERT contracted Bianchi  ∇^μ G[μ,ν] ≈ 0       (residual ≤ tol_bianchi)
                                                     # ⇒ ∇^μ T^{eff}_{μν}=0, conservation

9.  invariants = { R,
                   Ricci2 = Ricci[μ,ν]·Ricci^{μ,ν},
                   Kretschmann = Riemann[μνρσ]·Riemann^{μνρσ},
                   Weyl2 = C[μνρσ]·C^{μνρσ} }

    RETURN all, plus gate_card (C1.10)

The contracted-Bianchi assert in step 8 is doing double duty: mathematically ∇^μ G_{μν} ≡ 0 is an identity, so a nonzero numerical residual is a direct measurement of the engine's discretization error and a tripwire for bugs. It also guarantees ∇^μ T^{eff}_{μν} = 0, i.e. the geometry-implied source is automatically conserved — which is what we will check the declared field source against in the C-level source ledger.

6.2 Validation gates (Layer-3, source 14 "required known-metric tests")

The engine is not trusted until all five canonical cases pass, plus two consistency tests. We give the exact expected outputs so the result is falsifiable.

Worked number, T2 (Schwarzschild, the load-bearing non-trivial check). For g = diag(−(1−r_s/r), (1−r_s/r)^{−1}, r², r²sin²θ) with r_s = 2GM, the engine must return every component of R_{μν} as zero (to tolerance) and simultaneously a nonzero Kretschmann scalar
