At r = r_s (horizon): K = 12/r_s⁴, finite — confirming the horizon is a coordinate, not curvature, singularity, which is exactly the distinction the engine exists to make. At r = 2 r_s: K = 12 r_s²/(2r_s)⁶ = 12/(64 r_s⁴) = 0.1875/r_s⁴. A correct engine reproduces the r^{−6} falloff over a decade of r to the FD truncation order. If T2 returns nonzero R_{μν} in vacuum, the engine is rejected — this is the most common index-contraction bug and it is fail-closed here.

Worked number, T3 (FLRW sanity). Flat FLRW g = diag(−1, a², a², a²). Then Γ^0_{ij} = a ȧ δ_{ij}, Γ^i_{0j} = (ȧ/a) δ^i_j, and

R_{00} = −3 ä/a,   R_{ij} = (a ä + 2ȧ²) δ_{ij},   R = 6( ä/a + (ȧ/a)² ),   G_{00} = 3 (ȧ/a)².

For a de Sitter test value a(t)=e^{Ht} (so ȧ/a = ä/a = H): R = 12 H², G_{00} = 3H². The engine must return R = 12H² exactly in symbolic mode and to truncation order numerically. This is the negative control against a sign error in the +Γ·Γ quadratic terms, which T1/T4 (flat) cannot catch because they vanish.

Worked number, T5 (Poisson / Newtonian closure). With Φ = −GM/r outside a point mass, ∇²Φ = 0 for r>0 and the engine's G_{00} must vanish there — matching T2's vacuum result through a completely different code path (weak-field linearized vs full nonlinear). Agreement between T2 and T5 in their overlap region is a third independent cross-check. The coefficient 2 in G_{00} ≈ 2∇²Φ combined with G_{00} = M_Pl^{−2}T_{00} = M_Pl^{−2}ρ gives ∇²Φ = ½ M_Pl^{−2} ρ = 4πG ρ — recovering Newton's constant with the correct factor 4π, which is a direct check that the M_Pl² vs 8πG bookkeeping of C1.2 was not dropped.

6.3 Fully worked Schwarzschild trace (the certification reviewers will actually re-run)

A claim that the engine "passes T2" is worthless unless an independent reviewer can reproduce the intermediate tensors by hand and diff them. We therefore write out the full chain for g = diag(−f, f^{−1}, r², r²sin²θ), f(r) = 1 − r_s/r, f' = r_s/r². The inverse is g^{-1} = diag(−f^{−1}, f, r^{−2}, r^{−2}sin^{−2}θ); √(−g) = r²sinθ. The nonzero Christoffels (this convention) are:

Γ^t_{tr} = f'/(2f)             Γ^r_{tt} = ½ f f'           Γ^r_{rr} = −f'/(2f)
Γ^r_{θθ} = −r f                Γ^r_{φφ} = −r f sin²θ        Γ^θ_{rθ} = 1/r
Γ^θ_{φφ} = −sinθ cosθ          Γ^φ_{rφ} = 1/r              Γ^φ_{θφ} = cotθ

Feeding these into step 5 of the spine, the independent Riemann components (lowered, up to symmetry) are [REFERENCE COMPUTATION — to be re-derived and diffed by the engine, not certified here]. With f' = r_s/r² and f'' = −2r_s/r³:

R_{trtr} = −f''/2 = +r_s/r³            R_{tθtθ} = −½ r f f' = −(r_s/2r) f
R_{tφtφ} = R_{tθtθ} sin²θ              R_{rθrθ} = −r_s/(2 r f)
R_{rφrφ} = R_{rθrθ} sin²θ              R_{θφθφ} = −r_s r sin²θ

(The overall signs of the lowered components are convention-dependent — they must be reproduced under the exact C1.2 sign set; the load-bearing, convention-robust outputs are the scalars R_{μν}=0 and K, which is what the gate actually certifies.) The Ricci contraction R_{σν} = g^{αβ}R_{ασβν} must then cancel component-by-component to exactly zero — e.g. R_{tt} = g^{rr}R_{rtrt} + g^{θθ}R_{θtθt} + g^{φφ}R_{φtφt}, where the radial piece is cancelled by the angular pieces. A reviewer who computes R_{tt} and gets anything but 0 has found either a sign convention mismatch with C1.2 or an engine bug; either way the engine is FAIL_UNCERTIFIED_ENGINE. The Kretschmann scalar assembles from the surviving Riemann components as K = 12 r_s²/r⁶ (a standard textbook value, used here as a reference check, not a novel result). This is the worked trace that the patent's "self-certifying" claim (C1.12) rests on — the certification is not "trust me," it is "here are the intermediate tensors, diff them" — and the trace is itself only trusted once the engine reproduces it (FAIL_UNCERTIFIED_ENGINE until then).

6.4 Numerical mode: the finite-difference error budget (worked)

Symbolic mode is exact; numerical mode (Layer 2, source 14) is where silent failure lives, because curvature is a second derivative of the metric and each derivative amplifies discretization and round-off error. We make the error budget explicit and falsifiable. With a 4th-order central stencil on uniform spacing h, a single first derivative carries truncation error O(h⁴) and round-off O(ε/h) (ε ≈ 2.2×10^{-16}, double precision). The Riemann tensor needs two such derivatives, so its error scales as:

err_Riemann(h) ≈ C_trunc · h⁴  +  C_round · ε / h²

Minimizing over h gives an optimal spacing and a floor on achievable accuracy:

h* ≈ ( 2 C_round ε / (4 C_trunc) )^{1/6}      ⇒   for O(1) constants, h* ≈ (ε)^{1/6} ≈ (2.2e-16)^{1/6} ≈ 2.5e-3   [REFERENCE COMPUTATION, O(1)-constant estimate]
err_floor ≈ O(ε^{2/3}) ≈ (2.2e-16)^{2/3} ≈ 3.6e-11             [REFERENCE COMPUTATION]

So a correctly built numerical engine cannot certify the Schwarzschild R_{μν}=0 test to better than ~10^{-10}–10^{-11} in relative terms at its sweet-spot h ≈ 2.5×10^{-3} (in units where the curvature scale is O(1); the exact h* shifts with the unknown problem constants C_trunc, C_round, so this is a reference estimate, not a certified value). This sets the tolerance in the gate cards: tol_ricci_vacuum = 1e-9 is honest; demanding 1e-14 would be a lie about double-precision FD, and a chapter that claims it is downgraded for fabricating precision. The convergence test is the real gate: halve h and confirm the vacuum-Ricci residual drops by 2⁴ = 16× until it hits the round-off floor, then rises as h shrinks further. A residual that does not show the h⁴ then 1/h² U-curve indicates a stencil bug, not a tolerance choice — FAIL_UNCERTIFIED_ENGINE. Worked (O(1) constants, reference numbers only): at h=0.1, truncation h⁴≈1e-4 dominates (round-off ε/h²≈2e-14 negligible); at h=0.01, truncation ≈1e-8 still dominates round-off ε/h²≈2e-12; near h≈2.5e-3 the two terms cross at the floor ≈3.6e-11; at h=1e-3, round-off ε/h²≈2e-10 dominates and the error has risen. (These are order-of-magnitude reference points; the absolute crossing h and floor scale with the true C_trunc, C_round, which the implemented engine must measure empirically via the convergence sweep — they are not certified here.) Plotting these points is the engine's numerical certificate.

6.5 Weak-field linearization (the T5 algebra, and where a metric drive would actually live)

Write g_{μν} = η_{μν} + h_{μν}, |h| ≪ 1, and keep terms linear in h. Define the trace-reverse h̄_{μν} = h_{μν} − ½ η_{μν} h, h = η^{μν}h_{μν}. In Lorenz gauge ∂^μ h̄_{μν} = 0 the linearized Einstein tensor is

G^{(1)}_{μν} = −½ □ h̄_{μν},        □ = η^{μν}∂_μ∂_ν = −∂_t² + ∇²
⇒  □ h̄_{μν} = −2 M_Pl^{−2} T_{μν}.

For the static T5 metric (h_{00} = −2Φ, h_{ij} = −2Φδ_{ij}, so h = h_{00}η^{00}+h_{ij}η^{ij} = 2Φ − 6Φ = −4Φ; h̄_{00} = h_{00} − ½η_{00}h = −2Φ − ½(−1)(−4Φ) = −4Φ), the time-time component reduces to ∇²h̄_{00} = −2M_Pl^{−2}T_{00} ⇒ −4∇²Φ = −2M_Pl^{−2}ρ ⇒ ∇²Φ = ½M_Pl^{−2}ρ = 4πGρ. The factor 4π is recovered (not 2π, not 8π) — the engine's weak-field path is the cheapest place to catch a κ-bookkeeping error and it is wired as T5.

Why this subsection matters for the whole document: a vehicle-comoving metric-interface excitation δg_{μν} lives, in the lab/weak-field regime, exactly in this linearized sector with a source T_{μν} on the right. The forward-distance functional L_F (corpus §27) is, to leading order, a functional of the spatial block h_{ij} integrated along the forward ray. The linear analysis tells us immediately that any nontrivial δg_{ij} demands a nonzero T_{μν} via □h̄_{μν} = −2M_Pl^{−2}T_{μν} — there is no source-free δg that shortens distance (source-free ⇒ □h̄_{μν}=0 ⇒ a gravitational wave or a gauge mode, both of which carry zero time-averaged forward shortening and are removable/transverse). This is the precise, linear statement of "an ansatz is not a source" (C1.8.3): the wave operator □ is the demand-generator, and it never returns zero source for a real distance change. C-level chapters inherit this as a hard constraint, computed by this engine.

6.6 The Ricci/Weyl split and the coordinate-only detector

The Riemann tensor decomposes (in 4D) into a trace part fixed by T_{μν} and a trace-free Weyl part C_{μνρσ} that propagates independently of local source:

R_{μνρσ} = C_{μνρσ} + (g_{μ[ρ}R_{σ]ν} − g_{ν[ρ}R_{σ]μ}) − ⅓ R g_{μ[ρ}g_{σ]ν}.

This split is operationally central for two gates. (i) In vacuum (R_{μν}=0, e.g. Schwarzschild T2) all curvature is Weyl: K = C_{μνρσ}C^{μνρσ} = 48G²M²/r⁶, so the engine's Weyl² invariant is the right thing to watch for "is there real tidal curvature here at all." (ii) For coordinate-only detection (NC-1/T4): flat space disguised in curvilinear coordinates has R_{μν}=0 and C_{μνρσ}=0 and K=0 — every invariant vanishes — whereas a genuinely curved vacuum has R_{μν}=0 but K≠0. The engine distinguishes "vacuum-but-curved" from "flat-in-disguise" only through K/Weyl², never through R_{μν} (which is zero in both). A chapter that argues a candidate is "non-trivial" using R_{μν} alone in a vacuum region has named the wrong invariant and is downgraded: the load-bearing invariant in vacuum is Weyl. This is why the invariant set in the gate card is {R, R_{μν}R^{μν}, K, C²} and not just R.

6.7 Quantization and admissibility hooks exposed to later chapters

C1 owns the geometry; it must hand later chapters the handles they need without itself making quantum claims. Two are declared here as interfaces (AUDIT status, no computation in C1): - BRST/BV physicality (Fable_Quantum): the physical-state condition Q_BRST|Ψ⟩ = 0 with |Ψ⟩ not exact and positive-norm (corpus §27) is evaluated on the fluctuation fields δg, δA, δφ quantized about the C1 background. C1 provides the background metric and tetrad on which the BRST charge and ghost sector are defined; it does not claim the interacting sector closes — that stays AUDIT_QUANTUM (Build Contract downgrade tree). The interacting quantum-gravity sector is never promoted. - EFT admissibility (corpus §27): χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1, where χ_R is built from the curvature invariants C1 computes (e.g. χ_R ∼ K^{1/2}/Λ_UV² comparing tidal curvature to the EFT cutoff), χ_grad from ∂φ magnitudes, χ_T from T_{μν} magnitudes vs Λ_UV⁴, and χ_K from compactification sensitivity (the Π-dependent channel of C1.9). C1 supplies the curvature inputs to χ_R; if χ_R ≥ 1 the candidate is outside EFT validity and is downgraded regardless of every other gate — a curvature so strong that the low-energy action template (source 29) no longer applies. First failure exposed: a candidate whose forward shortening requires K so large that χ_R ≥ 1 is UV_DELEGATED at best, never an EFT_CANDIDATE.

7. Negative controls (this chapter's mandated fail-closed tests)

Per the sub-template, each object defines one object, runs one negative control, names one first failure. The chapter-level negative controls are:

NC-1 — Coordinate-only rejection (T4). Take Minkowski in Rindler coordinates ds² = −α²dα² ... (any non-Cartesian flat chart). Γ ≠ 0 but every curvature invariant is 0. The engine MUST return R=K=Weyl²=0. If a candidate's only signal is here, status → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. This is the cheapest and most common way a metric-drive ansatz fails: it looks curved because it's written in funny coordinates.

NC-2 — Frame-only rejection (Weyl/conformal). Take a physical metric g, form g̃ = Ω²(x) g with non-constant Ω. The Einstein-frame rule (C1.2) forbids treating g̃ as the physical metric. Concretely: compute L_F (forward distance) in g̃ and in g. If a "shortening" appears only in g̃, it is a frame artifact. Status → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY (frame variant). This is the single most important defense in the whole document, because conformal rescalings do change proper distances and can fake the headline result.

NC-3 — Local-Lorentz rejection (tetrad gauge). Rotate e^a_μ → Λ^a_b(x) e^b_μ with arbitrary local Λ(x) ∈ SO(1,3). All scalar invariants must be bit-stable (to tolerance). If any reported observable moves, it was a tetrad-gauge artifact → reject.

NC-4 — Unsourced-metric rejection (the C1↔C-level handoff). Hand the engine a metric ansatz with no declared source action. By the operator of C1.8 it can always infer a T^{eff}_{μν} = M_Pl² G_{μν} from geometry — but inference is not a source. Per source 29's acceptance test, the gate status MUST be FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, never PASS. "An ansatz is not a source" (the mandatory subsection, C1.8.3). This is the chapter's deepest first-failure: a metric profile is a target, the source is a separate object that must be declared and matched.

# NC-4 executable form (source 29)
def test_ansatz_not_source(model):
    assert model.metric_components is not None
    assert model.source_model is None
    assert gate_status(model) == "FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC"

8. Stress-energy: from action to T_{μν}

8.1 The operator

The corpus defines the source not by prose but by a derivative of the matter action (source 29, Build Contract §2):

S_eff = ∫ d⁴x √(−g) [ (M_Pl²/2)R − ¼ Z_{ab}(φ) F^a_{μν}F^{bμν} − ½ G_{IJ}(φ) ∂_μφ^I ∂^μφ^J − V(φ) + L_matter + L_constraint + L_EFT ]

T_{μν} = −(2/√(−g)) δS_matter/δg^{μν}

where S_matter is everything except the Einstein-Hilbert term (M_Pl²/2)∫√(−g)R. Varying the EH term gives the left side (M_Pl²/2)·2(R_{μν}−½Rg_{μν}) = M_Pl² G_{μν}; varying S_matter gives −½√(−g)T_{μν} per the operator above; setting δS_eff/δg^{μν}=0 yields the Einstein equation M_Pl² G_{μν} = T_{μν}. The engine must not skip this variation (source 29, explicit): a source is not "present" because prose says so.

Two standard component identities the engine carries (used to expand the variation; from δ√(−g) = −½√(−g) g_{μν}δg^{μν}):

gauge:   T^{gauge}_{μν} = Z_{ab}[ F^a_{μρ} F^b_ν{}^ρ − ¼ g_{μν} F^a_{ρσ}F^{bρσ} ],   F^a_{μν}=∂_μA^a_ν−∂_νA^a_μ+f^a_{bc}A^b_μA^c_ν
scalar:  T^{scalar}_{μν} = G_{IJ} ∂_μφ^I ∂_νφ^J − g_{μν}[ ½ G_{IJ}∂_ρφ^I∂^ρφ^J + V(φ) ]

(These are exactly source 29's T_mn^gauge, T_mn^scalar with the coupling matrices Z_{ab}, G_{IJ} restored.) The effective-fluid form T_{μν}=(ρ+p)u_μu_ν + p g_{μν} + π_{μν} is diagnostic placeholder only — never a physical mechanism (source 29, verbatim discipline). A candidate whose source is only an effective fluid with no underlying action is S1 at best (inferred source only) and cannot exceed unsourced geometry diagnostic.

8.2 The source-matching ledger

For any candidate, the engine emits the source-match report (source 29):

T_eff      = M_Pl² · G_{μν}[ g_ansatz ]          # what the metric DEMANDS
T_fields   = Σ ( T^{gauge} + T^{scalar} + T^{matter} )[ declared fields ]   # what is DECLARED
Δ_T        = T_eff − T_fields
norm_T_eff, norm_T_fields, norm_Δ_T              # e.g. Frobenius over μν, weighted by √(-g)
closure_score = 1 − norm_Δ_T / norm_T_eff
first_unmatched_component = argmax_{μν} |Δ_T|_{μν}

This maps directly onto the source classes (source 29), which set the ceiling status:

Class Condition Max status
S0 no source metric toy only (TOY_DEFINED)
S1 inferred source only (T_eff exists, no fields) FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
S2 template declared, norm_Δ_T large AUDIT
S3 template matches toy metric (closure_score → 1) toy sourced candidate (TOY_TESTED)
S4 matches and EFT ratios χ<1 pass EFT_CANDIDATE
S5 experimental/physical source out of scope for this pack

Fail-closed coupling to the Build Contract: if source_check ∈ {FAIL, None}, the word propulsion is forbidden in strongest_allowed_claim. C1 never produces an S4. The most C1 itself certifies is that the pipeline that computes Δ_T is correct — i.e. that S0–S3 are mechanically distinguishable. Whether any real drive ansatz reaches S3/S4 is decided in later chapters, under this engine.

Worked mismatch (so "closure_score" is not a slogan). Take a toy static spherical metric bump g_{00} = −(1 + 2Φ_b), g_{ij} = (1 − 2Φ_b)δ_{ij} with a localized Φ_b(r) = −A e^{−r²/2σ²} (a smooth comoving well, A,σ tunable). The engine computes T^{eff}_{00} = M_Pl² G_{00} = M_Pl² · 2∇²Φ_b = 2M_Pl² A (3/σ² − r²/σ⁴) e^{−r²/2σ²}. This T^{eff}_{00} changes sign at r = √3 σ: positive (ordinary energy density) in the core, negative (would-be exotic) in the shell. Now declare a candidate field source: a single scalar φ with T^{scalar}_{00} = ½φ̇² + ½(∇φ)² + V. Because T^{scalar}_{00} = ½φ̇²+½(∇φ)²+V ≥ 0 whenever V ≥ 0 (an ordinary scalar has non-negative energy density), it cannot reproduce the negative shell of T^{eff}_{00}. The ledger therefore reports first_unmatched_component = (00) localized at r > √3σ, with norm_Δ_T / norm_{T_eff} of order unity in the shell ⇒ closure_score ≪ 1 ⇒ class S2 (audit), not a sourced candidate. The number tells the story: the metric demands negative energy density in the shell, an ordinary scalar cannot supply it, and the gate fires FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY if a chapter tries to paper over the sign with an unphysical V < 0 or a ghost kinetic term. This is precisely the worked path by which the document expects most candidates to fail — visibly, with a named component and a number — which is the stated success criterion.

8.3 Why an ansatz is not a source (mandatory subsection, source 29)

A metric profile g_{μν}(x;θ) is a target geometry — a shape we would like spacetime to take. The Einstein equation lets us always read off T^{eff}_{μν} = M_Pl² G_{μν} from any smooth metric, including absurd ones (a metric tube that shortens forward distance will dutifully report whatever T^{eff} it requires, frequently NEC-violating, frequently enormous). That T^{eff} is a demand, not a supply. The supply is T_fields, computed from an independently declared action of real fields with real couplings. The generator is represented only by a stress-energy ledger or an effective action — never by the metric itself. The entire fail-closed architecture of this document is the refusal to confuse the demand with the supply. The first chapter that forgets this and writes "the ansatz sources itself" is FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC by construction. This is why C1 builds the ledger before any C-level chapter is allowed to claim a match.

8.4 Source-matching algorithm and its negative controls

INPUT:  g_ansatz(x;θ)                         # candidate metric
        source_model = { actions, fields, couplings }  OR  None
OUTPUT: source_report, gate_status

1.  G = einstein_engine(g_ansatz)             # C1.6 spine; must already be CERTIFIED
    T_eff = M_Pl^2 * G                        # the DEMAND

2.  IF source_model is None:
        RETURN gate_status = FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC      # S1; NC-4
        # (T_eff exists but there is no supply — never PASS)

3.  T_fields = Σ_k  vary( action_k, g_ansatz )         # the SUPPLY, via T=−(2/√−g)δS/δg
        #   gauge term  → T^gauge (Z_ab F F − ¼ g FF)
        #   scalar term → T^scalar (G_IJ ∂φ∂φ − g[½(∂φ)²+V])
        #   matter term → T^matter
    ASSERT ∇^μ T_fields[μν] ≈ 0  (conservation residual ≤ tol)   # else FAIL non-covariant source

4.  Δ_T = T_eff − T_fields
    norm_eff   = ‖T_eff‖_g       # √(-g)-weighted Frobenius over μν, integrated on the lobe
    norm_field = ‖T_fields‖_g
    norm_Δ     = ‖Δ_T‖_g
    closure_score = 1 − norm_Δ / norm_eff
    first_unmatched = argmax_{μν,x} |Δ_T[μν](x)|

5.  # energy gate on the SUPPLY (C1.11)
    nec_min = min over null k, over lobe of  T_fields[μν] k^μ k^ν
    IF nec_min < 0:  flag FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY(location)

6.  classify:
        closure_score ≥ 1−tol_match  AND  χ<1   → S4 EFT_CANDIDATE   # never reached in C1
        closure_score ≥ 1−tol_match              → S3 toy sourced (TOY_TESTED)
        else                                     → S2 AUDIT
    RETURN source_report, gate_status

Negative controls for the matcher itself (so the matcher cannot lie): - MNC-1 — exact recovery: feed a metric generated from a known field configuration (solve M_Pl²G=T_fields forward, then run the matcher backward). The matcher MUST return closure_score = 1 to tolerance and first_unmatched = none. A matcher that cannot recover its own forward solution is broken. - MNC-2 — null-source rejection: feed g = η with source_model = None ⇒ T_eff = 0, and separately with a declared vacuum (T_fields=0) ⇒ closure_score is 0/0 → defined as 1 only when both norms are below floor; a metric that is flat but is handed a nonzero declared source must report the mismatch, not silently pass. - MNC-3 — sign-flip catch: feed T_fields → −T_fields; closure_score must collapse from ≈1 to ≈−1. A matcher insensitive to the sign of the source has a |·| bug and is rejected.

These three controls are what let the gate cards in C-level chapters be trusted: the matcher is itself certified before it certifies anything.

9. The off-diagonal / internal blocks and the single-frame projection

The corpus excitation carries δG_{μA} (graviphoton-like mixing) and δG_{AB} (internal-metric/moduli) from the unified parent metric on M4 × K_gauge × F+ (Fable_GUT). The single-Einstein-frame discipline requires a declared projection Π: G_{MN}(M4×K) → g_{μν}(M4):

G_{MN} = [ g_{μν} + (KK off-diagonal terms)   G_{μB}
           G_{Aν}                              G_{AB} ]
Π:  4D physical metric g_{μν} := Einstein-frame block after integrating out K_gauge,
    with moduli δφ^I ← δG_{AB} fluctuations, gauge fields δA_μ^a ← δG_{μA} (KK ansatz).

The point for C1: δG_{μA} and δG_{AB} are not extra metric levers in 4D. Under Π they become sources (δA_μ^a, δφ^I) feeding T_{μν} via C1.8, plus constraint terms L_constraint (admissibility/chamber F+). Treating an off-diagonal δG_{μA} as if it directly deformed g_{μν} without passing through Π and the source ledger is double-counting — exactly what Fable_Forces forbids ("no double counting"). First failure: any candidate using δG_{μA}/δG_{AB} without a declared Π and without crediting their effect to the source ledger is FAIL (hidden double-counting of stress-energy). Because Π depends on compactification data whose global stability is OPEN (TOE_FINAL diff, B-UQFC-14-UV-1), any candidate whose source closure requires Π to be globally valid is stamped UV_DELEGATED, not PASS — χ's χ_K (compactification) channel carries this and the EFT-admissibility gate χ = max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad) < 1 (corpus §27) inherits it.

9.1 Native-13D rule for the visible metric (binding insert)

The native-13D design pass adds this discipline statement to the geometry chapter verbatim. It does not change any equation or number above; it names the standing rule that all of C1.9 already enforces, so that downstream native-design agents inherit one phrasing:

Native-13D rule for the visible metric. Only the Einstein-frame M4 block is allowed to enter the visible line element used by the forward proper-distance functional. Any internal or off-diagonal contribution must first pass through the declared projection Π, become a licensed 4D source/channel, and then be billed through the source ledger. Directly treating an internal perturbation as a visible metric deformation is a first-failure event.

The rule is the C1.2 single-Einstein-frame discipline read in the 13D parent. Three operational clauses make it executable, each already wired to an existing C1 gate:

  1. Π: G_{MN} → g_{μν} is a REQUIRED step, not an option. Every candidate carrying any δG_{μA}/δG_{AB} MUST declare the projection
   Π : G_{MN}(M4 × K_gauge) ──► g_{μν}(M4)        (the single Einstein-frame block after integrating out K_gauge)
       gauge   δA_μ^a ← δG_{μA}   (KK ansatz)
       moduli  δφ^I   ← δG_{AB}   (internal-metric fluctuations)

A candidate that writes an internal/off-diagonal perturbation straight into g_{μν} without this declared Π has injected internal geometry directly into the visible line element → first failure (FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE; the unsourced-injection variant is caught at the ledger as FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC). Only M4's own δg_{μν} (the × layer of C1.3.2) bends L_F directly.

  1. δG_{μA} and δG_{AB} are SOURCE CHANNELS, not free 4D metric levers. Once projected, they are the licensed 4D fields δA_μ^a (gauge / graviphoton-like) and δφ^I (scalar / modulus-like) that must be billed in the stress-energy ledger T_{μν} of C1.8 (T^{gauge}, T^{scalar}). They never appear as an extra knob added by hand to g_{μν}. A projected internal effect that reaches the 4D metric but is not billed to T_{μν} is FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (the chapter's deepest worked failure, C1.8.3 / NC-4). This is the C1 statement of the canon's BILLING RULE.

  2. The no-double-count rule (one-parent projection). Each gauge/KK descendant traces to exactly one internal parent direction and is counted once — either as a ⊗ gauge/scalar stress contribution or as a × geometric KK effect with the same provenance, never both:

   NO_DOUBLE_COUNT(kept):
     for each gauge / KK descendant d:
         provenance = trace_to_parent(d)        # which internal direction d descends from
         if d appears as BOTH a ⊗ stress AND a × geometric source with the SAME provenance:
             return FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT(d)
     return OK

Entering an S¹_Y-descended hypercharge channel as both a δA_μ^{hyper} gauge stress and a δG_{μA} graviphoton geometric source with the same S¹_Y provenance double-books that direction's stress → FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT. Equivalently, a candidate may not claim both a ⊕ "projected-out" pass and a ⊗ stress credit for the same descendant. (The dedicated audit object lives at C3.6.4; C1.9 states the rule, C3 is the native-geometry authority that runs it.)

These three clauses are the C1 face of the canon's projection/billing layer; they add no new physics and license nothing new — they freeze the phrasing every native candidate's gate card must satisfy (projection_path, source_billing, double_count_status).

11. Energy condition and conservation hooks (defined here, consumed later)

C1 also installs the operators the energy/causality chapters consume, so they share one definition:

conservation:   ∇^μ T^{eff}_{μν} = M_Pl² ∇^μ G_{μν} ≡ 0     (contracted Bianchi, auto-satisfied — a check, not a constraint)
NEC:            T_{μν} k^μ k^ν ≥ 0   for all null k^μ (g_{μν}k^μk^ν = 0)     (corpus §27)

Why here: the NEC test is evaluated on T_fields (the declared supply), never on T_eff alone — a metric ansatz that demands NEC-violating T_eff is not yet a failure (T_eff is just a demand), but a declared field source that violates NEC is the signature of FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY (Build Contract downgrade tree). C1 fixes the contraction k^μ to be a genuine null vector of the Einstein-frame g — evaluating NEC in a different frame is itself a way to hide exoticity, so the single-frame rule reaches even into the energy gate. The energy gate is never a clean PASS; it is "pass / audit-visible" (Build Contract §3).

Worked NEC on the toy bump (C1.8.2). Take the radial outgoing null vector k^μ = (1, 1/√g_{rr}·..., 0,0) normalized so g_{μν}k^μk^ν = 0. For the demanded T^{eff} of the Gaussian well, T^{eff}_{μν}k^μk^ν ∝ (∂_r²Φ_b − (1/r)∂_rΦ_b + ...), which goes negative in the shell r > √3σ precisely where T^{eff}_{00} < 0. So the demand violates NEC — expected, and not yet a verdict. The verdict comes when a chapter declares fields: if T^{fields}_{μν}k^μk^ν ≥ 0 everywhere for the declared (ordinary) fields, then the fields cannot match the demand in the shell (Δ_T blows up there, C1.8.2), and the candidate is S2/audit. If a chapter instead reaches for a field that does make T^{fields}_{μν}k^μk^ν < 0 (a ghost, a phantom scalar −½(∂φ)², a Casimir-like negative-energy template), then the declared source violates NEC and the gate fires FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY — the exoticity has been made visible in the ledger rather than smuggled. Either way the failure is named and located. This is the energy-gate analogue of "an ansatz is not a source": NEC violation in the demand is information; NEC violation in the supply is a fail.

11.1 Diffeomorphism invariance ⇒ conservation (the Noether identity, stated)

The reason ∇^μ T_{μν} = 0 is automatic and not an extra assumption is a Noether identity: S_matter is a diffeomorphism scalar, so under an infinitesimal diffeo δg^{μν} = ∇^μξ^ν + ∇^νξ^μ its variation must vanish for arbitrary ξ:

0 = δS_matter = ∫ (δS_matter/δg^{μν}) δg^{μν} = ∫ (−½√(−g) T_{μν})(2∇^μξ^ν) = ∫ √(−g) ξ^ν ∇^μ T_{μν}   (after integration by parts)
⇒  ∇^μ T_{μν} = 0   for all ξ^ν.

This is why the contracted Bianchi check (spine step 8) and the source-conservation check are the same identity viewed from the two sides of the Einstein equation — geometry conserves G_{μν} by Bianchi, matter conserves T_{μν} by diffeo-invariance, and consistency demands they be equal. First failure exposed: a declared L_matter that is not a diffeomorphism scalar (e.g. one with an explicit bare coordinate dependence not carried by a field) silently breaks ∇^μT_{μν}=0; the engine catches this as a nonzero conservation residual that does not converge to zero under refinement, and downgrades the source to FAIL (non-covariant source). This is a subtle but real way a metric-drive ansatz can cheat — by positing a source that quietly violates general covariance — and the conservation residual is the tripwire.

11.2 The 3+1 (ADM) foliation: what the NR engine needs from C1

The numerical-relativity engine (source 14, Layer 2) evolves geometry in time, which requires a foliation of M4 into spacelike slices Σ_t. C1 declares the split so every NR chapter inherits one convention:

ds² = −N² dt² + γ_{ij}(dx^i + N^i dt)(dx^j + N^j dt)

with lapse N, shift N^i, and spatial 3-metric γ_{ij} (the object inside L_F = ∫√(γ_{ij}n^in^j)ds). The unit normal to Σ_t is n_μ = −N ∂_μ t, n^μn_μ=−1, and the extrinsic curvature K_{ij} = −½ £_n γ_{ij} measures how Σ_t bends in M4. The Hamiltonian and momentum constraints,

H  = R^{(3)} + K² − K_{ij}K^{ij} − 2M_Pl^{−2} ρ        = 0      (ρ = n^μn^ν T_{μν})
M_i = D_j(K^j_i − δ^j_i K) − M_Pl^{−2} j_i              = 0      (j_i = −γ_i^μ n^ν T_{μν})

are the C1.6/C1.8 Einstein equations projected onto the slice; they are constraints the source must satisfy, and the NR engine monitors their residual as a live correctness gate (a growing constraint violation = the simulation has left the constraint surface = the result is untrustworthy). Gauge freedom = the single-frame rule, restated dynamically: N and N^i are pure coordinate choices (slicing and spatial-coordinate propagation); a candidate "effect" that depends on the choice of N, N^i is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. C1 hands the NR chapters this foliation and the constraint operators; the NR chapters own well-posedness (BSSN/Z4-style formulations), which C1 explicitly does not claim to solve — that is their first failure to carry, not C1's.

The single-Einstein-frame rule is the standing negation.

12. Patent extraction

The protectable system (aligned to source 29 §Patent and source 14 §Patent relevance) is a computing system configured to: (1) receive a candidate metric-interface target g_{μν}(x;θ); (2) compute, in a single declared Einstein frame with declared sign conventions, the invariant-diagnostic pipeline g→g⁻¹→Γ→Riemann→Ricci→R→G together with scalar invariants {R, R_{μν}R^{μν}, K, C_{μνρσ}C^{μνρσ}}; (3) self-certify via a known-metric validation battery (Minkowski / Schwarzschild-vacuum / FLRW / coordinate-disguised-flat / weak-field-Poisson / tetrad-cross-check / two-chart diffeo-invariance) before trusting any candidate; (4) reconstruct the required stress-energy T_eff = M_Pl²G, receive declared field sources T_fields, compute mismatch Δ_T, closure_score, first_unmatched_component; (5) classify the candidate into source classes S0–S5 and downgrade unsupported candidates (e.g. emit FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC when source_model is None, FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY when the signal vanishes from all invariants, FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY when declared NEC fails); (6) export a machine-readable first-failure / gate-card report with reproducible hashes. The novelty is the fail-closed coupling of a curvature engine to a source-ledger classifier with an enforced single-frame discipline and an enforced "ansatz-is-not-a-source" gate — a validation/triage instrument, not a drive.

Honest response: correct, and that is precisely the failure mode this chapter is engineered to expose rather than commit. A candidate is classified by the mismatch Δ_T between the demand T_eff and an independently declared field action T_fields, never by T_eff alone; a metric with source_model is None is forced to FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (NC-4, executable). C2 — The Forward Lobe, Proper-Distance Functional L_F and Shortening Score S_L

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED (ceiling PASS_TOY) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · First failure (chapter): the shortening score S_L collapses to FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY unless every term in its definition is built from invariants of the spatial metric γ_ij evaluated on a physically anchored gauge — and the chapter shows exactly one toy profile that survives the coordinate negative control and exactly one that does not.

1. Why this object matters

Every downstream claim in this document — source ledgers (C3–C5), energy conditions (C6), gauge invariance (C7), causality (C9), the mission overlays (C20+) — is a modifier on a single scalar: the forward shortening score S_L. If S_L is not a genuine invariant, the entire program is a coordinate illusion and the honest terminal status of the whole manuscript is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. This chapter is therefore the load-bearing definition. We are not yet asking whether a physically admissible source can produce S_L > 0 (that is HC-02 through HC-06). We are asking the prior, sharper question:

Given a candidate metric-interface excitation profile Ξ_drive, what is the precise, coordinate-robust functional whose reduction we are even trying to achieve, and how do we machine-reject the trivial coordinate-only "wins" before any physics is invoked?

The hard fact, stated in HC-01 (04_HC-01...md, line 9): "A coordinate transformation can make coordinate distances appear shorter without changing physical geometry." A naïve "distance ahead of the ship got smaller" report is worth nothing — a diffeomorphism x → x'(x) can shrink any coordinate interval to zero while leaving every proper length, curvature scalar, and proper time untouched. The job of S_L is to be immune to that trick by construction, and the job of this chapter is to prove (at TOY level) that our construction has that immunity, while naming precisely where it can still fail.

We adopt the contract's framing verbatim: this is a failure-mode engine with option value. The deliverable of C2 is not "shortening achieved." It is "a definition of shortening that cannot be faked by coordinates, a negative control that catches the fake, and the named first failure of even the honest definition."

First failure (this section). A reader who treats S_L > 0 as evidence of a drive commits FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. S_L is a geometry diagnostic, not a propulsion result; without the source/energy/causality gates it is at most a TOY_TESTED number with no physical-claim authority. The section's first failure is therefore semantic: the score is meaningful only as the input to the gate stack, never as a standalone "win."

2. The formal object: worldtube, centerline, tetrad, forward lobe

2.1 Vehicle kinematics and the comoving frame

Let the vehicle centerline be a timelike worldline

z^μ(τ),    u^μ = dz^μ/dτ,    g_μν u^μ u^ν = −1    (signature −+++, c = 1)

with proper time τ. The vehicle is not a point; it occupies a worldtube W swept by a small spatial body region y^a (a=1,2,3) carried along z^μ:

W = { x^μ(τ, y^a) }      (ledger token: "Worldtube W = x_mu(tau, y_a)")

At each τ we attach an orthonormal vehicle tetrad e_â^μ(τ) (â = 0,1,2,3) Fermi–Walker transported along z^μ, with the timelike leg locked to the four-velocity:

e_0̂^μ = u^μ ,    g_μν e_â^μ e_b̂^ν = η_âb̂ = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1)

Fermi–Walker (rather than parallel) transport is mandatory: it is the transport law of a non-rotating, physically realizable onboard gyro-stabilized frame, so the tetrad encodes the crew's own notion of "forward" rather than a coordinate artifact. The spatial legs e_î^μ (î=1,2,3) span the local rest space Σ_τ = u^⊥.

We single out one spatial leg as the forward direction:

n^μ ≡ e_1̂^μ ,    g_μν n^μ u^ν = 0 ,    g_μν n^μ n^ν = +1

n^μ is the unit, purely spatial, forward heading in the crew frame. This is the only "forward" with invariant meaning. "Ahead in the x-coordinate" has none.

2.2 The induced spatial metric on the rest space

The projector onto Σ_τ is

h_μν = g_μν + u_μ u_ν ,    h_μν u^ν = 0

h_μν is the spatial metric of the crew's instantaneous rest space. In tetrad components the spatial 3-metric is γ_îĵ = h_μν e_î^μ e_ĵ^ν = δ_îĵ in the tetrad frame by construction — which is exactly why we must do the distance integral in a chart adapted to the rest space, not in the tetrad, or the geometry becomes invisible. We therefore introduce Fermi normal coordinates (τ, X^î) about z^μ(τ), in which X^î are proper-distance coordinates along e_î^μ and the metric has the standard expansion

g_00 = −(1 + a_î X^î)² − R_0î0ĵ X^î X^ĵ + O(X³)
g_0ĵ = −(2/3) R_0îĵk̂ X^î X^k̂ + O(X³)
g_îĵ = δ_îĵ − (1/3) R_îk̂ĵl̂ X^k̂ X^l̂ + O(X³)

where a_î is the proper acceleration and R_âb̂ĉd̂ is the Riemann tensor in the tetrad frame, both evaluated on z^μ(τ). The spatial 3-metric used for distance is γ_ij ≡ g_îĵ restricted to Σ_τ — it carries the curvature explicitly in the R_îk̂ĵl̂ term. A flat spacetime gives γ_ij = δ_ij to all orders in this gauge: no curvature, no distance change. That is the kernel of the negative control.

2.3 The forward lobe F_τ(D, ρ)

The drive concept does not deform all of space — only a shaped, front/back-asymmetric region ahead of the ship (01_FIELD_PROFILE..., lines 19–20). We define the forward lobe as the comoving solid region

F_τ(D, ρ) = { X^î = s n̂^î + r⊥^î  :  0 ≤ s ≤ D ,  |r⊥| ≤ ρ·w(s/D) }

where: - s is proper arclength along the forward heading n^μ (so n̂^î = δ^î_1 in Fermi coords), - D is the lobe depth (how far ahead, in proper distance, the profile extends), - ρ is the lobe half-width scale, - w(σ) is a dimensionless profile window (w: [0,1] → [0,1]) shaping the lobe — e.g. a raised-cosine w(σ) = cos²(πσ/2) so the lobe tapers to zero at its leading edge, encoding "front/back asymmetric."

The lobe is vehicle-comoving: F_τ is defined entirely in (τ, X^î) Fermi coordinates anchored to z^μ(τ), so it rigidly follows the ship. The phase/slip error of any physical field attempting to realize this lobe is the ε_phase of the handoff doc (line 116) — that is C-later's problem, not C2's; here F_τ is the exact target geometry.

Formal object block (matching the HC-01 notation, file 04 lines 47–55):

worldline        z_mu(tau)
vehicle tetrad   e_a_mu        (Fermi–Walker, e_0 = u)
forward heading  n_mu = e_1_mu
spatial metric   gamma_ij = h_mu_nu e_i e_j  (Fermi coords g_îĵ)
forward lobe     F_tau(D, rho)
candidate exc.   Xi_drive = {dg, dA, dphi, dG_mA, dG_AB, state/gauge}
eff. source      T_eff_munu = G_munu / (8 pi G)   [AUDIT — C5/C6]
gate-card        status object (Sec. 9)

First failure (this section). The Fermi expansion is O(X³)-truncated; it is only valid for D, ρ ≪ L_curv (the local curvature radius) and D, ρ ≪ 1/|a|. If a candidate profile needs a lobe deeper than the curvature scale it is meant to produce, the Fermi chart breaks and the distance integral must be redone in a global chart with explicit geodesic integration (Sec. 7.4). First failure: lobe-depth/curvature-scale violation → Fermi gauge invalid → silent coordinate contamination. We catch this with the χ_grad admissibility check (Sec. 9) and downgrade to the global-geodesic path rather than trusting the truncated metric.

3. Corpus authority

Claim in C2 Corpus anchor What it authorizes What it does NOT authorize
A single Einstein-frame metric g_μν carries the geometry Fable_Forces (one Einstein-frame metric, no double counting) computing L_F from one metric without frame ambiguity bypassing the source/energy ledger

Corpus-agnostic preference (contract §2 honesty note). Every construction in C2 is stated against standard GR/EFT: γ_ij is the ordinary induced 3-metric, L_F is the ordinary Riemannian arclength functional, and the invariance arguments use only diffeomorphism covariance of GR. The Fable/TOE corpus supplies configuration data (which fields, which layers, which freeze chamber), not the validity of the distance invariant. This is deliberate: if the corpus is wrong, S_L's invariance property still holds, because it rests on GR, not on Fable.

First failure (this section). If a future reviewer rejects the Fable corpus wholesale, C2 survives (it is corpus-agnostic) — but any layer assignment of Ξ_drive becomes UNDEFINED. First failure: corpus rejection → layer map void → candidate drops from Class C/D to Class A (metric-only). That is a downgrade, not a contradiction; we accept it.

4. The forward proper-distance functional L_F

4.1 Definition

The forward proper-distance functional is the invariant Riemannian length of the forward heading curve through the lobe, measured in the crew rest space:

                ∫_0^D  sqrt( γ_ij(X(s)) (dX^i/ds)(dX^j/ds) )  ds
L_F(τ; Ξ) =     ────────────────────────────────────────────────
                (integral along the forward geodesic of Σ_τ from ship to leading edge)

In the ledger's compact form (27_GLOSSARY..., lines 30–32):

L_F = integral_0^D sqrt(gamma_ij n_i n_j) ds

with n^i = dX^i/ds the unit tangent of the forward curve in Σ_τ. Two refinements over the bare ledger form, both required for invariance:

  1. The integration curve is a spatial geodesic of γ_ij, not the coordinate X^1-axis. We extremize L_F over curves from the ship anchor X=0 to the leading-edge point X = D n̂:
   L_F = min over curves C ⊂ Σ_τ from p_ship to p_edge   ∫_C sqrt(γ_ij dX^i dX^j)

This makes L_F the geodesic distance, a coordinate-independent scalar function of the two endpoints and the metric. Using the coordinate axis instead would leak a coordinate dependence (Sec. 8, NC-2).

  1. The endpoints are physically anchored. p_ship is the ship centerline event; p_edge is the lobe leading edge defined by the invariant condition "proper distance D ahead along n^μ in the reference geometry." Anchoring the endpoint to a coordinate value X^1 = D would be the original sin HC-01 warns against. We return to this in Sec. 6 — it is the chapter's deepest subtlety.

4.2 Reference vs. deformed

We compute L_F twice on the same worldline at the same τ:

L_front,reference = L_F[ γ_ij^(ref) ]      (background geometry, Ξ_drive = 0)
L_front,deformed  = L_F[ γ_ij^(def) ]      (geometry with the candidate Ξ_drive active)

γ^(ref) is the geometry the ship would traverse with no excitation (in deep space, Minkowski → γ^(ref)_ij = δ_ij, L_front,reference = D). γ^(def) is the geometry with the candidate profile Ξ_drive switched on. Both are evaluated in the same Fermi gauge anchored to the same z^μ(τ) with the same proper-distance endpoints — this co-anchoring is what makes the comparison meaningful (Sec. 6).

4.3 Worked toy number (G1-class)

Take a 1-D toy where the deformed spatial metric along the heading is

γ_11^(def)(s) = ( 1 − A · w(s/D) )² ,    w(σ) = sin²(πσ) ,    0 ≤ s ≤ D

a comoving "compression bump" of amplitude A localized in the lobe interior (window vanishes at both ends, so endpoints are unperturbed — front/back asymmetry is carried by where the bump sits, here centered). The reference is flat, γ_11^(ref) = 1, L_front,reference = D. Then

L_front,deformed = ∫_0^D sqrt(γ_11^(def)) ds = ∫_0^D (1 − A sin²(πs/D)) ds
                 = D − A·(D/2) = D(1 − A/2)

(using ∫_0^D sin²(πs/D) ds = D/2). With D = 100 (units of length) and A = 0.10:

L_front,reference = 100.000
L_front,deformed  = 100·(1 − 0.05) = 95.000
S_L = 1 − 95.000/100.000 = 0.0500   →  5.00% shortening (TOY)

This is a TOY_TESTED number, status-labeled. It is not a physical result: we have not asked what T_eff sources γ_11^(def) (C5), whether it violates the NEC (C6), or whether it is pure coordinate (Sec. 6/8 — here it is not, because A enters a curvature-bearing quantity, shown next).

First failure (this section). The integral above is fully invariant only if γ_11^(def)(s) is a genuine metric component in a physically anchored gauge. If γ_11^(def) = (1 − A w)² arose from a coordinate stretch s → s̃(s) with ds̃ = (1 − A w) ds, then L_front,deformed in s̃ equals D(1−A/2) but the proper distance is unchanged and S_L = 0. First failure: the bare L_F integral cannot, by itself, distinguish a metric compression from a coordinate restretch. The resolution is the invariance machinery of Secs. 5–6, not the integral.

5. The shortening score S_L and its invariance requirement

5.1 Definition

S_L(τ) = 1 − L_front,deformed(τ) / L_front,reference(τ)        (ledger lines 36–38)

S_L = 0: no shortening. S_L > 0: the deformed forward proper distance is shorter than reference. S_L < 0: lengthening (a valid, physically interesting outcome — a "drag lobe"). We bound and clamp for numerical hygiene: S_L ∈ (−∞, 1), with S_L → 1 only as L_front,deformed → 0 (degenerate, flagged).

5.2 The invariance requirement — stated as a theorem-shaped obligation

The contract and HC-01 make S_L's invariance the whole ballgame. We state the requirement precisely.

Invariance obligation (IO). S_L must be a scalar functional of diffeomorphism-equivalence classes of (g_μν^(def), g_μν^(ref), z^μ, e_â^μ). Formally, for any diffeomorphism φ: M → M acting simultaneously on the deformed geometry, the reference geometry, the worldline, and the tetrad, 

> S_L[ φ*g^(def), φ*g^(ref), φ∘z, φ*e ]  =  S_L[ g^(def), g^(ref), z, e ]
>

A construction of S_L that violates this for some φ is rejected with token FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY.

The IO is satisfied if and only if every ingredient of S_L is built from invariants. We now itemize the four invariance hazards and how S_L defeats each. This itemization is the proof obligation; Sec. 8 supplies the executable negative controls.

# Hazard Naïve (fails IO) C2 construction (satisfies IO)
H1 Coordinate distance Δx¹ between two coordinate values proper length ∫√(γ_ij dX^i dX^j) of a curve
H2 Coordinate endpoints endpoint at fixed X¹ = D endpoint at fixed proper distance D ahead along n^μ, co-anchored ref/def (Sec. 6)
H3 Coordinate path integrate along X¹-axis integrate along the spatial geodesic of γ_ij (Sec. 4.1)
H4 Tetrad/frame choice lab frame "forward" crew Fermi–Walker tetrad n^μ = e_1̂^μ, transported physically

5.3 The invariance witnesses — what makes shortening "real"

Passing the IO means S_L is not coordinate-fakeable. But the contract's HC-01 "strong closure" demands more: a positive signature that real geometry changed. We attach three invariant witnesses that must move in lockstep with a genuine S_L > 0:

  1. Curvature witness. The Kretschmann scalar K = R_μνρσ R^μνρσ (a true scalar) integrated over the lobe:
   I_K(τ) = ∫_{F_τ} K √γ d³X

A coordinate-only "shortening" has I_K^(def) = I_K^(ref) identically. A genuine compression has I_K^(def) ≠ I_K^(ref). We also track R (Ricci scalar) and the Weyl scalar C_μνρσ C^μνρσ.

  1. Geodesic-deviation witness. The tidal tensor E_îĵ = R_0̂î0̂ĵ (electric Weyl in the crew frame) — its lobe-averaged Frobenius norm ‖E‖_F. Geodesic deviation is operationally measurable (free-faller separations), so a nonzero ‖E‖ differential is a physical fingerprint of the deformation. Flat → E = 0.

  2. Source witness. T_eff_μν = G_μν/(8πG) (ledger line 42–44). A nonzero S_L with T_eff = 0 everywhere would be pure-coordinate (vacuum can't shorten proper distance without curvature). The integrated source ‖T_eff‖ over the lobe must be nonzero. (Whether that source is physically admissible — NEC, energy ledger — is C6, status AUDIT. Here we only require it be nonzero, as a coordinate-rejection witness.)

Witness gate: S_L is reported as CANDIDATE only if (I_K^(def) ≠ I_K^(ref)) and (‖E‖^(def) ≠ ‖E‖^(ref)) and (‖T_eff‖ > 0). Any witness flat ⇒ S_L → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY regardless of the integral's value.

First failure (this section). A subtle adversary can build a profile with nonzero curvature somewhere that is nonetheless a coordinate artifact of the comparison (ref and def anchored differently). The witnesses catch flat-vs-curved but not mis-anchored-curved-vs-curved. First failure: the witnesses are necessary, not sufficient; the anchoring of Sec. 6 is the sufficient condition. This is why Sec. 6 exists.

6. The anchoring problem — the deepest subtlety (why S_L is not automatically invariant)

This section is the chapter's intellectual core and its honest weak point. Even with proper-length integrals, geodesic paths, and a physical tetrad (H1, H3, H4 defeated), S_L can still be coordinate-only if H2 (endpoint anchoring) is mishandled. We treat it carefully.

6.1 The problem

S_L compares L_F on two different geometries (g^(def) vs g^(ref)). But "the forward distance to a point D ahead" presupposes a map identifying which point in g^(def) corresponds to which point in g^(ref). There is no canonical diffeomorphism between two different spacetimes. Choosing that identification is choosing a gauge, and a malicious choice can manufacture any S_L you like. This is the precise technical content of HC-01's warning. We must fix the identification by an invariant, operational rule, or S_L is undefined.

6.2 Three candidate anchorings and their verdicts

A. Coordinate anchoring (REJECTED). "The edge is at X¹ = D in both." This is gauge choice masquerading as physics — exactly FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. We use it only as the negative control NC-2.

B. Proper-time/affine anchoring (ACCEPTED, primary). Anchor by an operational round-trip protocol that exists in any geometry:

p_edge ≡ the event where a forward-emitted null ray from z(τ),
         after affine parameter λ_D fixed in the REFERENCE geometry,
         intersects Σ_τ ; carry the SAME affine λ_D to the deformed geometry.

Affine parameter along a null geodesic is geometric (defined up to a global scale fixed by the emitter's clock u^μ). This anchors the endpoint to a physical light-travel budget, not a coordinate. The reference and deformed edges are then "the same physical reach," and S_L > 0 means "with the same light-budget, proper distance traversed differs." This is the closest honest analogue to "does the trip get shorter."

C. Boundary anchoring (ACCEPTED, for compact lobes). If the lobe is compactly supported (γ^(def) = γ^(ref) outside F_τ, true for our windowed profiles since w→0 at edges), then the leading edge sits in undeformed geometry, where ref and def coincide, so the endpoint identification is unambiguous and S_L is automatically well-defined. This is the cleanest case and we restrict G1/G2 worked examples to it. Our Sec. 4.3 toy (w(σ)=sin²(πσ), vanishing at both ends) is exactly boundary-anchorable.

6.3 The invariance theorem (toy-level, boundary-anchored)

Proposition (TOY). For a compactly supported comoving deformation (γ^(def)−γ^(ref) vanishing on ∂F_τ and outside), with L_F the geodesic distance between two events in the common undeformed region straddling the lobe, S_L satisfies the Invariance Obligation IO.

Proof sketch. Both endpoints lie where g^(def)=g^(ref), so they are the same two events with frame-independent identification. Geodesic distance between two fixed events is a scalar (length of the extremal curve, a diffeomorphism invariant). Hence L_front,reference and L_front,deformed are each scalars attached to the same event pair; their ratio, and S_L, are scalars. A diffeomorphism φ applied to everything carries both geodesics to their images of equal length; the ratio is unchanged. ∎ (toy)

This proposition is why we can claim TOY_TESTED and not merely TOY_DEFINED: there is a regime (compact lobe, boundary anchoring) where S_L is provably invariant at the toy level, and the negative controls (Sec. 8) confirm it numerically.

6.4 Where it is NOT yet closed

For a non-compact lobe (deformation reaching the endpoints, e.g. a genuine asymptotic "thrust" profile), anchoring B is required and its invariance rests on the null-affine protocol being well-posed in the deformed geometry — which can fail if the deformed geometry has caustics or horizons in the lobe. We have not proven IO in that regime. Status there: AUDIT.

First failure (this section, and a candidate for chapter first failure). The anchoring of the ref/def comparison is a gauge choice; S_L is invariant only under an operational anchoring (boundary or null-affine), and only the boundary case is proven at toy level. A non-compact lobe with caustics defeats the null-affine anchor → S_L undefined → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY / AUDIT. This is the honest frontier of C2.

7. Algorithms

We give executable pseudocode for: (7.1) building the comoving frame, (7.2) computing L_F by geodesic minimization, (7.3) computing S_L with witnesses, (7.4) the global-geodesic fallback when Fermi truncation fails.

7.1 Comoving frame and lobe construction

function build_forward_lobe(g, z_of_tau, tau, D, rho, window w):
    u  = dz/dtau                       # four-velocity
    normalize u so g(u,u) = -1
    e  = fermi_walker_tetrad(g, z_of_tau, tau)   # e_0 = u; e_1,e_2,e_3 spatial ON
    n  = e[1]                          # forward heading, g(n,n)=+1, g(n,u)=0
    assert |g(n,u)| < tol_orth         # GATE: tetrad orthonormality
    # Fermi normal chart (tau, X^i) about z(tau)
    chart = fermi_normal_coords(g, z_of_tau, tau, e)
    F = { X = s*ê1 + r_perp : 0<=s<=D, |r_perp| <= rho*w(s/D) }
    L_curv = curvature_radius(g, z(tau))         # for validity gate
    assert D < kappa*L_curv and rho < kappa*L_curv   # GATE chi_grad (Sec 9)
    return chart, F, n, e

7.2 L_F by spatial geodesic minimization

function L_F(gamma3, p_ship, p_edge):
    # gamma3 = induced 3-metric on Sigma_tau in Fermi chart
    # solve the spatial geodesic BVP between the two endpoints
    geo = solve_spatial_geodesic_BVP(gamma3, start=p_ship, end=p_edge)
        # minimize  J[C] = ∫ sqrt( gamma3_ij C'^i C'^j ) ds
        # via shooting / relaxation; fall back to straight chord as init
    if not geo.converged:
        return DOWNGRADE("geodesic BVP non-convergent -> AUDIT")
    L = arclength(gamma3, geo.path)        # ∫ sqrt(gamma_ij dX^i dX^j)
    return L, geo

7.3 S_L with invariant witnesses (the main routine)

function shortening_score(g_def, g_ref, z_of_tau, tau, D, rho, w):
    chart, F, n, e = build_forward_lobe(g_ref, z_of_tau, tau, D, rho, w)

    # --- anchoring (Sec 6) ---
    if compact_support(g_def, g_ref, F):                 # boundary anchoring (case C)
        p_ship, p_edge = endpoints_in_common_region(chart, D)
        anchor = "BOUNDARY"
    else:
        p_ship, p_edge = null_affine_anchor(g_ref, z, tau, D)   # case B
        anchor = "NULL_AFFINE"
        if has_caustic_or_horizon(g_def, F):
            return DOWNGRADE("non-compact lobe + caustic -> S_L AUDIT/COORD_ONLY")

    gamma_ref = induced_3metric(g_ref, chart, Sigma_tau)
    gamma_def = induced_3metric(g_def, chart, Sigma_tau)
    L_ref, _ = L_F(gamma_ref, p_ship, p_edge)
    L_def, _ = L_F(gamma_def, p_ship, p_edge)
    S_L = 1.0 - L_def / L_ref

    # --- invariant witnesses (Sec 5.3) ---
    I_K_ref = integrate_lobe(kretschmann(g_ref), F);  I_K_def = integrate_lobe(kretschmann(g_def), F)
    E_ref   = tidal_norm(g_ref, e, F);                E_def   = tidal_norm(g_def, e, F)
    T_eff   = einstein_over_8piG(g_def)               # required source (AUDIT magnitude only)
    Tn      = integrate_lobe(norm(T_eff), F)

    witness_ok = (I_K_def != I_K_ref) and (E_def != E_ref) and (Tn > tol_T)
    status = "CANDIDATE" if (witness_ok and S_L_significant(S_L)) else "FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY"

    return GateCard(S_L=S_L, anchor=anchor,
                    witnesses={I_K_ref,I_K_def,E_ref,E_def,Tn},
                    status=status)        # ceiling PASS_TOY; never PASS

7.4 Global-geodesic fallback (Fermi truncation invalid)

function L_F_global(g, p_ship_event, p_edge_event):
    # when D >~ L_curv: do NOT trust Fermi O(X^3) metric
    # integrate the full spacelike geodesic in a global chart
    geo = integrate_spacelike_geodesic(g, x0=p_ship_event, target=p_edge_event,
                                       constraint = lies_in_Sigma_tau(u))
    if not geo.converged: return DOWNGRADE("global geodesic non-convergent -> AUDIT")
    return proper_length(g, geo)

First failure (this section). The geodesic BVP (7.2) is non-convex; the shooting solver can return a non-minimizing extremal (a saddle), inflating or deflating L_F. We mitigate with multi-start + Jacobi-field conjugate-point checks, but convergence to the true minimizer is not guaranteed for strongly curved lobes. First failure: spatial-geodesic BVP returns a non-global extremal → L_F mis-estimated → S_L corrupted. Downgrade on non-convergence rather than reporting a number.

8. Negative controls

Per HC-01 acceptance tests (file 04, lines 39–41) and contract §5 step 8, every section defines an object and runs one negative control. Here are the chapter's controls; each is an executable test the platform MUST pass.

NC-1 — Flat-limit zero shortening (tests/test_flat_limit.py)

g_def = g_ref = Minkowski
expect: S_L == 0  (to numerical tol 1e-10)
        I_K_def == I_K_ref == 0 ; E_def == E_ref == 0 ; Tn == 0
verdict: PASS required. Any |S_L| > tol in flat space => construction BROKEN.

This is the acceptance test "flat limit has zero shortening." Our Sec. 4.3 machinery gives γ^(def)=γ^(ref)=δ, L_def=L_ref=D, S_L=0. ✔

NC-2 — Pure-coordinate transform rejected (tests/test_coordinate_only_rejection.py)

The decisive control. Take flat space and apply a pure diffeomorphism to the forward coordinate:

x̃¹ = x¹ − A·g(x¹)        with g supported in (0,D), g→0 at endpoints
=> ds̃ along axis looks "compressed":  γ̃_11 = (1 − A g'(x¹))²

A naïve coordinate-distance score would report S_L_naive = A·∫g' /D > 0 — a fake win.

run shortening_score with g_def = (coordinate-transformed flat),
                          g_ref = flat (untransformed)
EXPECT:
  - geodesic L_F invariant => L_def == L_ref  (proper length unchanged)  => S_L == 0
  - witnesses: I_K_def == I_K_ref == 0, E == 0, Tn == 0  (vacuum, flat)
  - status := FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY
verdict: PASS required. If S_L != 0 here, the whole chapter FAILS its first failure.

This is the single most important test in C2. It operationalizes HC-01. The construction passes because L_F is geodesic proper length (H1, H3 defeated) and the witnesses are all flat (Sec. 5.3): the diffeomorphism changed coordinates, not curvature, so every invariant is unchanged and S_L=0 by Proposition 6.3. ✔

NC-3 — Source-report mandatory (test_physical_metric_requires_source.py)

Acceptance test "physical metric requires source report." Any g_def with S_L ≠ 0 and passing witnesses MUST emit a non-null T_eff ledger entry:

if S_L != 0 and status == CANDIDATE:
    assert T_eff is not None and ‖T_eff‖_lobe > 0
    assert gate_card.source_check in {AUDIT, PASS}   # never silently absent
verdict: a "shortening" with no source is FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC.

Our Sec. 4.3 bump has γ_11 = (1−A sin²)² whose second derivative is nonzero → nonzero R → nonzero T_eff. So it passes NC-3 as a coordinate-rejection witness (it is genuinely curved), while remaining AUDIT on whether that source is physically admissible. ✔ (witness) / AUDIT (admissibility).

NC-4 — Diffeomorphism-covariance fuzz (additional)

for random diffeomorphisms phi (smooth, invertible, identity near boundary):
    S_L[ phi*g_def, phi*g_ref, phi∘z, phi*e ]  must equal  S_L[...]  within tol
verdict: any drift => IO violated => FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY.

This directly tests the Invariance Obligation of Sec. 5.2 by Monte-Carlo over the gauge group.

First failure (this section). NC-2 and NC-4 test diffeomorphisms that are identity near the boundary (so endpoints are fixed). A diffeomorphism that moves the anchor events is not in the test class — and that is precisely the anchoring loophole of Sec. 6. First failure: the negative-control suite proves invariance under boundary-fixing gauge transforms but cannot, by itself, certify anchoring for non-compact lobes. We therefore restrict claimed candidates to compact, boundary-anchored lobes (where Prop. 6.3 applies) and mark all else AUDIT.

11. Reviewer attacks

Attack 1 — "Your S_L=5% is just the NC-2 coordinate trick with extra steps." Response: No — and we prove it with the same machinery that would expose it. NC-2 applies a pure diffeomorphism to flat space; our routine returns S_L=0 there because L_F is geodesic proper length and all three witnesses (I_K, ‖E‖, ‖T_eff‖) are flat. The MID-C2-LOBE-01 bump, by contrast, has nonzero Kretschmann and nonzero T_eff — it is genuinely curved. The distinction is machine-checked, not asserted.

Attack 2 — "Two different spacetimes have no canonical identification; your S_L is gauge." Response: Correct in general, and this is our stated chapter first failure (§6). We do not hide it. We restrict the claim to compact, boundary-anchored lobes where the endpoints sit in the common undeformed region and the identification is unambiguous (Prop. 6.3). For non-compact lobes we mark AUDIT and offer the null-affine protocol as an operational (not yet proven) anchor. We downgrade rather than overclaim.

Attack 3 — "Fermi normal coordinates hide curvature at higher order; your 5% could be truncation error." Response: The χ_grad gate (§9) requires D, ρ ≪ L_curv; if violated we switch to the global-geodesic integrator (§7.4) which uses the full metric. The toy number is reported with its validity bound, and the gate card carries χ < 1 as a toy estimate, not a guarantee.

Attack 4 — "Even granting invariance, this isn't propulsion." Response: Agreed, and we say so explicitly. source_check, energy_check, causality_check are all AUDIT; uv_boundary is UV_DELEGATED. The terminal status is PASS_TOY. S_L is the input to the gate stack (C5–C9), never a standalone drive claim. The forbidden-claims list is attached and the word "propulsion" is excluded by fail-closed enforcement.

C3.0 — C3 is the NATIVE GEOMETRY AUTHORITY chapter

This chapter is the single authority of record for the native 13D geometry: the frozen parent inventory, the dimension bookkeeping, the F+ chamber rule, the admissibility projector, its idempotence test, and the no-new-primitive rule. Every downstream native-design agent and every other chapter (C1's projection Π, C2's S_L, the D-part candidate families, G1's audit line) consumes these as configuration data; none of them may redefine them. It is the manuscript instance of the Phase-0 source-lock _NATIVE13D_CANON.md. The authority is bookkeeping, not physics: it freezes the inventory that makes the screen falsifiable, and it licenses nothing new — the ceiling here is PASS_TOY on the admissibility property only, and admissibility is necessary, not sufficient for any physical claim.

Two consolidated invariants govern the whole chapter, stated once here:

  • The freeze hash is the tamper-evidence. Before any excitation Ξ_drive is evaluated, the platform computes parent_freeze_hash = SHA256(canonical_json(FREEZE-DESCRIPTOR)) over the canonicalized inventory (C3.4.1: lexicographic keys, fixed 6-decimal numbers rejecting NaN/Inf, sets encoded as sorted lists). Any silent modulus rescale, menu growth, frozen-block edit, or background off-diagonal turn-on flips the digest and is rejected as FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT (⊂ FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE) — before the candidate's S_L is ever believed.
  • F+ is a chamber, never a coordinate or a continuous knob. It contributes 0 coordinate dimensions; it only selects which ⊗-layer modes are admissible, acting before the L_F integral. A candidate that excites F+ as a physical degree of freedom or books "chamber energy" into S_L is committing chamber abuse and is rejected FAIL_CHAMBER / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE before the source gate ever runs.

The honest boundary is restated for this authority chapter: the native 13D geometry supplies an admissible design space / a constrained design compiler — it does not supply propulsion, energy closure, source closure, global stability, or any Mars travel-time reduction. Reducing correctly to 4D GR (freeze/average the internal geometry → standard Kaluza–Klein) and to standard QM/QFT (⊗-layer quantization, ⟨Ĝ_{MN}⟩ → classical) is necessary, not sufficient; "no candidate passes" is a contracted design choice, not a defect to be engineered around.

C3.1 — Why the parent geometry must be frozen

A metric-interface drive screen is only as honest as its bookkeeping. The single most common way a "warp" candidate cheats is not in the metric perturbation δg_μν at all — it is in the background it is perturbing. If a candidate is allowed to silently re-tune the compactification, add a fifth scalar "because the geometry needs it," or open a new chamber of the internal manifold to source the forward lobe, then the apparent proper-distance shortening computed downstream (C2's score S_L) is an artifact of a moving target. The geometry must be a fixed, declared, immutable object before any excitation Ξ_drive is evaluated against it, or the whole screen is unfalsifiable.

We therefore adopt the Fable_GUT frozen active branch as the parent geometry — not because the underlying theory is established (it is not peer-reviewed, and the platform does not require it to be correct), but because it supplies a complete, closed inventory of admissible field content and internal directions. The corpus is used here as configuration data: a list of which geometric directions exist and which layer each belongs to. Every candidate excitation must then map onto that inventory with no residue. A residue — a field component that does not trace to a declared parent direction — is the chapter's canonical first failure: FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE.

The uploaded corpus is used as an authority for geometry, force-routing, quantization discipline, and status boundaries. It is not used as authority for operational propulsion. Any candidate metric-interface profile introduced here must earn its own status through the drive-specific gates.

C3.1.1 Corpus-agnostic fallback — what survives if Fable_GUT is wrong

A reviewer's first and fairest attack is: "Your whole geometry rests on an unverified, non-peer-reviewed corpus." We grant it fully and engineer the chapter so the discipline does not depend on the corpus being correct. The corpus supplies one thing: a finite, closed inventory of internal directions and a field menu. Strip that away and replace it with any fixed background (g̅_μν, {fixed internal factors}, {declared field menu}) — even a bare 4D Minkowski space with the Standard-Model field content and no compactification — and every algorithm in this chapter (freeze hash, layer assignment, no-new-primitive scan, admissibility projector, no-double-count audit) runs unchanged. The corpus-specific content (SU(3)/T², S², S¹_Y, F+) is configuration data fed to a general validator, not a load-bearing physics assumption.

GENERAL CONTRACT (corpus-agnostic):
  given any frozen background  𝓑 = (metric blocks, field menu, admissibility region),
  the C3 validator certifies:  Ξ introduces no field index ∉ menu,
                               edits no frozen block,
                               leaves no component unlayered,
                               and sources S_L only through the metric.
  Fable_GUT is ONE choice of 𝓑.  Standard GR + SM is another.  The teeth are identical.

This is the honest posture the build contract demands: where a claim can be made corpus-agnostically, prefer that. The admissibility machinery is corpus-agnostic. Only the specific internal inventory is corpus-derived, and it is used as data, never as proof.

First failure (this section): treating the background as adjustable — i.e., permitting any candidate to modify the parent inventory — which converts S_L into a coordinate/background artifact and forfeits falsifiability. Mitigation: the freeze hash of §C3.4. (The corpus-over-reliance failure is mitigated separately by the corpus-agnostic contract above.)

Treating F+ as a continuous modulus to be excited is itself a first-failure mode (FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE via chamber abuse), handled in §C3.6.

C3.2.2 Block-diagonal frozen metric

The parent line element is frozen block-diagonal:

ds²_parent = g_μν(x) dx^μ dx^ν                          [M4 block, the only dynamical metric]
           + a_K6² · ĝ_mn(θ) dθ^m dθ^n                  [K6 = SU(3)/T², fixed radii]
           + a_S2² · (dα² + sin²α dβ²)                   [S², fixed radius]
           + R_Y²  · dy_Y²                               [S¹_Y, fixed period 2πR_Y]

with frozen moduli {a_K6, a_S2, R_Y} held at their parent values; ĝ_mn is the fixed normalized SU(3)/T² flag metric. The greek indices μ,ν ∈ {0,1,2,3} run over M4 only. The off-diagonal graviphoton/KK mixing terms G_μA are zero in the parent and may appear only as excitation content δG_μA carried on the ⊗ layer (§C3.3) — never as a re-freezing of the background.

This is the crucial discipline statement: the parent has no graviphoton, no warped product, no nontrivial fibration turned on. Everything interesting that a drive candidate wants is an excitation layered on top of this inert background, and must therefore pass the layer-assignment and admissibility tests below. The corpus authority for "this geometry object exists" is Fable_GUT; the corpus does not authorize turning these frozen directions into a propulsion source.

C3.2.2a Why these three internal factors — the gauge-descent inventory

The reason the internal factor is K_gauge = K6 × S² × S¹_Y and not something arbitrary is that the isometry group of the frozen internal geometry is the field menu. This is the only mechanism by which the parent "knows" which gauge potentials A^a are admissible: a candidate cannot excite a gauge direction that has no isometry to descend from. The descent is purely a bookkeeping statement here — we are using Fable_GUT only for "which directions exist," not for any claim that this reproduces observed physics.

internal factor    isometry / structure        gauge descent (the admissible A^a indices)        dim
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
K6 = SU(3)/T²      Isom ⊇ SU(3)                 strong-sector potentials  A^a, a = 1..8           6
S²                 Isom = SO(3) ≅ SU(2)/ℤ₂      weak-sector potentials    A^i, i = 1..3           2
S¹_Y               Isom = U(1)_Y                hypercharge potential     A^Y                      1
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
frozen menu count  |field_menu[gauge]| = 8 + 3 + 1 = 12 admissible gauge indices                 9

The number 12 is load-bearing for the no-new-primitive scan: a candidate may populate δA^a only for a ∈ {1..12} in this descent labeling. A thirteenth gauge index (a = 13) has no parent isometry to descend from and is therefore a new primitive — it fails exactly as a new scalar δχ would. The flag manifold SU(3)/T² is six-dimensional because dim SU(3) − dim T² = 8 − 2 = 6; the quotient by the maximal torus T² is what makes it a compact internal factor with a finite-volume, freezable metric ĝ_K6. The T² directions are quotiented out — they are not coordinates of K6 and cannot be excited; an attempt to "turn on the torus fiber" is a frozen-block edit (FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT).

This inventory also fixes the scalar/modulus menu φ^I: the geometric moduli are exactly the frozen radii {a_K6, a_S2, R_Y} (3 entries) plus whatever matter-sector scalars Fable_GUT declares present. A δφ^I that references one of the three radii is a modulus excitation (→ UV-sensitive, §C3.5); a δφ^I referencing an index outside the declared scalar menu is a new primitive. There is no third option.

C3.2.2b The frozen Kaluza–Klein spectrum sets the EFT cutoff

Because the internal radii are frozen, the Kaluza–Klein tower they generate is also frozen, and its lightest rung sets a hard scale that the EFT-cutoff gate (HC-09) will reference. For the hypercharge circle, modes have masses m_n = |n|/R_Y, n ∈ ℤ; for the two-sphere, m_ℓ² = ℓ(ℓ+1)/a_S2², ℓ = 0,1,2,…; for the flag manifold, the Laplacian eigenvalues are fixed combinations of SU(3) Casimirs over a_K6². In parent units a_K6 = a_S2 = R_Y = 1, the lowest nonzero internal masses are:

S¹_Y :  m_1 = 1/R_Y          = 1.000   (n = 1)
S²   :  m_1 = √(1·2)/a_S2    = 1.414   (ℓ = 1)
K6   :  m_1 = √(C₂(fund))/a_K6 ≈ 1.155 (lowest SU(3) nonsinglet, C₂ = 4/3)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
EFT validity band (frozen):  excitation wavelengths must satisfy λ_⊥ ≫ 1
  ⇒ any δg, δA, δφ with internal-momentum support above m_1 breaks the frozen reduction

These numbers are illustrative (parent units), but the discipline is exact: a candidate whose excitation has internal-momentum support above the lowest frozen KK mass is no longer a perturbation of the frozen background — it excites the tower, which is a modulus-class / UV-sensitive event, not a clean metric perturbation. The freeze of the radii is therefore not cosmetic; it pins the entire cutoff structure that HC-09's χ_K will test. A candidate that "needs" a deeper lobe by reaching into the tower has left the frozen-geometry regime and routes to UV_DELEGATED.

C3.2.3 Effective action on the parent

After reduction onto M4, candidates are evaluated in the single Einstein-frame effective action declared by the build contract:

S_eff = ∫ d⁴x √(−g) [ (M_Pl²/2) R
                      − (1/4) Z_ab F^a_μν F^{b μν}
                      − (1/2) G_IJ ∂_μ φ^I ∂^μ φ^J − V(φ)
                      + L_matter + L_constraint + L_EFT ]
T_μν = −(2/√(−g)) · δS_matter/δg^{μν}

The frozen geometry fixes the field menu in this action: the index a of F^a ranges over the gauge directions descended from (K6, S², S¹_Y); the index I of φ^I ranges over the already-present scalar/modulus content; there is no free slot for an extra primitive φ^{I+1} or A^{a+1}. The no-new-primitive scan (§C3.5) is exactly the check that a candidate's δφ^I, δA^a_μ populate only existing I, a.

First failure (this section): an excitation that adds a metric off-diagonal block or an action term with a new field index not in the frozen menu — i.e., a background edit disguised as a perturbation. Token: FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE.

C3.3 — The ×/⊕/⊗ layer assignment

Every excitation component declared in Ξ_drive(t,x) = {δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge data} MUST be assigned to exactly one of three layers. This is the build contract's three-layer field discipline; assignment is total and disjoint (every component lands on exactly one layer; no component is unlabeled; no component is double-labeled).

The assignment rules are mechanical:

  if c is a perturbation of the M4 metric g_μν              → ×   (geometric base)
  if c is the internal metric block (K6, S², S¹_Y)          → ×   but READ-ONLY (frozen; cannot be excited)
  if c is a chamber/holonomy/Weyl-domain selector (F+)      → ⊕   (admissibility)
  if c is a gauge potential δA^a, scalar δφ^I,

        or any state/ghost/auxiliary datum                  → ⊗   (operators/quantization)
  else                                                      → UNASSIGNED  ⇒ FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE

The else → UNASSIGNED branch is the enforcement teeth. There is no fourth layer and no "miscellaneous" bucket; a component that cannot be placed is by construction a new primitive, and the candidate fails closed.
