E03b.1 Step 7 — the energy_condition_report algorithm (production form)

The Algorithm Library (30_ALGORITHM_PSEUDOCODE_LIBRARY.md, function energy_condition_report) gives the four-step skeleton: (1) sample null vectors · (2) sample timelike vectors · (3) compute NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC minima · (4) integrate exoticity, under the shared return contract and the universal failure behavior ("never return PASS without evidence; downgrade on absent input; write report fields for manuscript and patent export"). We expand it to production grade. The function consumes a tetrad-sampled T_eff (built by tetrad_sampler.py) and a worldline; it emits the shared-contract JSON plus the exoticity ledger.

E03b.1.1 The four pointwise conditions, in computable form

At a sample point x we have the local T̂_{âb̂}(x). For an arbitrary future null vector k^{â} (η_{âb̂}k^{â}k^{b̂}=0) and future timelike unit vector v^{â} (η_{âb̂}v^{â}v^{b̂}=−1):

NEC(x,k) = T̂_{âb̂} k^{â} k^{b̂}                              ≥ 0
WEC(x,v) = T̂_{âb̂} v^{â} v^{b̂}                              ≥ 0
SEC(x,v) = ( T̂_{âb̂} − ½ η_{âb̂} T̂ ) v^{â} v^{b̂}            ≥ 0 ,   T̂ = η^{âb̂}T̂_{âb̂}
DEC(x,v) : WEC(x,v) ≥ 0  AND  J^{â} = −T̂^{â}{}_{b̂} v^{b̂} is causal future-directed (J·J ≤ 0, J^{0̂} ≥ 0)

The pointwise minimum over the unit sphere of directions is what the report records. For a diagonalizable Hadamard source with energy density ρ̂ and principal pressures p̂_(1),p̂_(2),p̂_(3), the minima have closed forms (Hawking–Ellis Type I):

min_k NEC(x) = ρ̂ + min_α p̂_(α)
min_v WEC(x) = ρ̂                          (timelike limit of the worst direction)
min_v SEC(x) = ½(ρ̂ + Σ_α p̂_(α))         (and ρ̂ + p̂_(α) ≥ 0 ∀α)
DEC(x)       = ρ̂ − max_α |p̂_(α)|

Factor-½ note (SEC). The SEC scalar is the trace-reversed quadratic form (T̂_{âb̂} − ½η_{âb̂}T̂)v^âv^b̂; evaluated at the comoving observer v=u for a Type-I source this is ½(ρ̂ + Σ_α p̂_(α)), i.e. it carries an overall factor ½ relative to the bare ρ̂ + Σp̂. The factor is immaterial to the verdict — the side condition is ρ̂ + Σ_α p̂_(α) ≥ 0 either way (and ρ̂ + p̂_(α) ≥ 0 ∀α) — so no SEC pass/fail, number, or token changes; the ½ is restored here only so the displayed value of min_v SEC is the actual quadratic-form value and not the bare sum.

so the entire pointwise verdict reduces to the four scalars {ρ̂, ρ̂+min p̂, ρ̂+Σp̂, ρ̂−max|p̂|}. For non-Type-I sources (Type II/III/IV — null-dominated or non-diagonalizable, which is exactly what shows up on the lobe wall) the closed form is invalid and we must fall back to explicit sampling; the algorithm detects this via a Segre-type classification and refuses the closed form. First failure of E03b.1.1: a Type I closed-form shortcut applied to a Type II wall source silently reports the wrong NEC minimum — so the classifier gate is mandatory and is itself a negative control (NC-SEGRE below).

E03b.1.2 Direction sampling and the worst-case search

Pointwise minima require minimizing over directions. We use a two-tier sampler: (a) a deterministic Fibonacci-sphere lattice of N_dir = 512 directions for a coarse worst-case, then (b) a local trust-region refinement of the worst lattice direction to tolerance 10⁻⁶ to escape lattice aliasing. For NEC, the null directions are parameterized k^{â} = (1, n̂), |n̂|=1; for WEC/SEC/DEC the timelike v^{â} = γ(1, βn̂), swept over boost β ∈ [0, β_max], β_max = 0.999 to keep γ finite and audit the frame-dependence of WEC (a state we exploit in the no-free-lunch discussion, §E03b.3).

function energy_condition_report(T_eff, tetrad, worldline, grid, opts):
    # --- input guard (fail-closed) ---
    if T_eff is None or tetrad is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "missing T_eff or tetrad",
                         allowed="none", forbidden="any energy claim")
    require grid.covers(forward_lobe(worldline))  else AUDIT("lobe not fully sampled")

    report = new EnergyReport()
    seg    = SegreClassifier()                       # Type I/II/III/IV per point

    # --- Steps 1-3: pointwise minima over the sampled domain ---
    for x in grid.points():
        That   = tetrad.frame_components(T_eff, x)     # T̂_âb̂  (E03a tetrad_sampler)
        cls    = seg.classify(That, tol=opts.segre_tol)
        if cls == TYPE_I:
            rho, p = diagonalize_spatial(That)         # ρ̂, p̂_(α)
            nec = rho + min(p);  wec = rho
            sec = rho + sum(p);  dec = rho - max(abs(p))
        else:                                          # Type II/III/IV  -> MUST sample
            nec = min_over_null(That, N_dir=512, refine=True)
            wec = min_over_timelike(That, beta_max=0.999)
            sec = min_over_timelike(trace_reverse(That), beta_max=0.999)
            dec = dec_flux_test(That, beta_max=0.999)  # WEC>=0 AND J^â causal
        report.record(x, cls, rho=That[0,0], nec=nec, wec=wec, sec=sec, dec=dec)
        report.update_minima(nec, wec, sec, dec)
        report.update_peak_negative(That[0,0])         # min ρ̂ over domain

    # --- Step 4: exoticity integral (E03b.2) ---
    report.exoticity = integrate_exoticity(report, grid, worldline)

    # --- fail-closed verdict: energy_check is NEVER a clean PASS ---
    if report.min_NEC >= -opts.eps_ec:
        energy_check = "AUDIT"                          # clean *to tolerance* -> AUDIT, not PASS
        status       = "PASS_TOY" if report.has_source_pass else "AUDIT"
        first_fail   = "none at energy gate (audit-visible); next gate governs"
    else:
        energy_check = "AUDIT"                          # violation present and DECLARED -> still AUDIT-visible
        status       = "FAIL"
        first_fail   = "FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY" if not report.declared else "TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC"

    return {
      "status": status, "energy_check": energy_check,
      "evidence": report.as_dict(),                     # minima, peak ρ̂, exoticity E, severity
      "first_failure": first_fail,
      "allowed_claim": "tetrad-frame energy-condition report; exoticity quantified, not removed",
      "forbidden_claim": "energy_check PASS; negative energy available; energy problem solved"
    }

Three structural facts make this fail-closed by construction. (1) There is no code path that returns energy_check: PASS. The best attainable token is AUDIT (violation absent to tolerance) — exactly the contract's "pass / audit-visible." (2) A detected NEC violation does not silently downgrade status to a soft warning — it forces FAIL and routes to FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY unless the report carries a declared=True exoticity ledger, in which case it lands at TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC. The only difference between the two terminal tokens is whether the author told the truth; the physics is identical. (3) Missing input is a downgrade, never a pass.

First failure of §E03b.1: report.declared is operator-set. A dishonest pipeline could set declared=True while emitting an empty ledger, converting FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY into the softer TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC cosmetically. The guard is NC-DECL (§E03b.4): declared=True is rejected unless the exoticity ledger is non-empty, the peak negative density is finite and signed, and the integral E < 0. The label cannot be cheaper than the accounting it claims to summarize.

E03b.1.3 Data flow, the build artifacts, and a worked tetrad contraction

The HC-03 source doc lists four required artifacts: src/energy/tetrad_sampler.py, src/energy/energy_conditions.py, src/energy/exoticity.py, tests/test_energy_conditions_visible.py. The data flow between them is strictly one-directional and each boundary is a downgrade point:

reconstruct_source(g)            # HC-02 / Algorithm Library: T_eff = M_Pl² G_μν[g]
        │  T_eff^{μν}(x)  (coordinate-basis field on the grid)
        ▼
tetrad_sampler.frame_components   # builds e_â^μ along z^μ(τ) (Fermi–Walker for non-geodesic u),
        │  T̂_âb̂(x)              #   then T̂_âb̂ = T_eff_{μν} e_â^μ e_b̂^ν at every grid point
        ▼
energy_conditions.{nec,wec,sec,dec}_min   # the four pointwise minima (E03b.1.1)
        │  {min_NEC, min_WEC, min_SEC, min_DEC}(x)
        ▼
exoticity.integrate_exoticity     # V_exo, E_NEC, ρ̂_min, σ_exo, severity (E03b.2)
        │  EnergyReport
        ▼
energy_condition_report           # shared-contract JSON; energy_check ∈ {AUDIT} only
        ▼
test_energy_conditions_visible    # NC-KNOWN/VACUUM/DUST/BOOST/SEGRE/DECL regression battery

Tetrad construction (Fermi–Walker, because u^μ need not be geodesic). The crew frame is transported by D_FW e_{â}{}^μ = 0, i.e. de_{â}{}^μ/dτ = −Γ^μ_{αβ}u^α e_{â}{}^β + (a^μ u_ν − u^μ a_ν)e_{â}{}^ν, with a^μ = u^ν∇_ν u^μ the proper acceleration. This guarantees e_{0̂}{}^μ = u^μ and a non-rotating spatial triad even when the vehicle accelerates — the physical frame a crew measures, which is the only frame in which the energy density ρ̂ has operational meaning. First failure of §E03b.1.3: if the sampler used parallel transport instead of Fermi–Walker for an accelerating worldline, the spatial triad would spuriously rotate and the principal-pressure eigenvalues p̂_(α) would be frame-smeared — a silent corruption of every condition. The sampler asserts |D_FW e_â|< 10⁻⁸ per step as a guard.

A worked contraction (so the algebra is concrete). Take a single grid point on the toy-Alcubierre wall where, in the tetrad basis, the source is null-dominated (Type II): the only large component is T̂_{0̂0̂} = T̂_{1̂1̂} = −T̂_{0̂1̂} ≡ μ < 0 (a negative null-dust block along 1̂), everything else ≈0. Take the null vector k^{â} = (1, n̂) with n̂ along 1̂, so k^{â}=(1,1,0,0). Then

NEC = T̂_{âb̂}k^âk^b̂ = T̂_{0̂0̂}(k^0)² + 2 T̂_{0̂1̂}k^0k^1 + T̂_{1̂1̂}(k^1)²
    = μ·1 + 2(−μ)(1)(1) + μ·1 = μ − 2μ + μ = 0   ... along this k.

Naively "NEC = 0, fine." But sweep n̂ toward −1̂, k^{â}=(1,−1,0,0): NEC = μ + 2(−μ)(−1) + μ = μ + 2μ + μ = 4μ < 0. The worst null direction gives 4μ, not 0. This is exactly why the closed-form Type-I shortcut (which would have used ρ̂ + min p̂) is wrong here and why min_over_null must actually sweep the sphere — and why NC-SEGRE is mandatory. The number a careless reviewer reports (0) and the number the gate reports (4μ) differ by the entire violation.

E03b.1.4 Acceptance-test mapping

The three acceptance tests from the HC-03 source doc map to concrete asserts:

Acceptance test (source doc) Implementation Where
"known negative energy case flagged" NC-KNOWN asserts min_NEC<0, σ_exo≈1, severity CATASTROPHIC_EXOTIC on toy Alcubierre §E03b.4
"every candidate has report" pipeline guarantees an EnergyReport (possibly AUDIT/N/A-upstream) for all 50 modes; assembly table 6 has no empty rows §E03b.5
"EFT candidate cannot hide violations" gate returns energy_check: AUDIT (never PASS) + NC-DECL blocks empty-ledger relabeling §E03b.1.1, §E03b.4

The third test is the one with teeth: it is the formal statement that no mode promoted to EFT_CANDIDATE upstream can carry a clean energy gate, because the gate has no clean-pass token to give.

E03b.2 Steps 8 (part) & the exoticity integral, peak density, severity

The pointwise minima tell you whether a condition is violated. They do not tell you how much exotic content the profile demands, or where, or whether shrinking the lobe escapes it. That is the job of the exoticity functional. We define three nested scalars: the violation volume, the exoticity integral (the total negative-energy "budget"), and the peak negative density (the worst pointwise demand). These three are the numbers the mission overlay (E-series, HC-10) and the patent claims consume.

E03b.2.1 Definitions

Let Σ_t be a vehicle-comoving constant-τ spatial slice with induced 3-metric h_{ij} and proper volume element dV = √h d³x. Let n̂^μ be the unit normal (= u^μ). The frame energy density is ρ̂(x) = T_eff_{μν} n̂^μ n̂^ν. Define the negative part ρ̂_−(x) = min(ρ̂(x), 0) ≤ 0. Then:

Violation volume:     V_exo  = ∫_{Σ_t}  𝟙[ ρ̂(x) < 0 ]  √h d³x
Exoticity integral:   E      = ∫_{Σ_t}  ρ̂_−(x) √h d³x            (≤ 0; the negative-energy budget)
Peak negative density: ρ̂_min = min_{x∈Σ_t} ρ̂(x)                  (≤ 0; worst pointwise demand)
NEC-exoticity (frame-robust):  E_NEC = ∫_{Σ_t} min(0, min_k T̂_{âb̂}k^âk^b̂) √h d³x

We integrate the NEC version E_NEC as the primary score (not the WEC/ρ̂ version) for a deliberate, contract-honest reason developed in §E03b.3: the null condition is the frame-invariant floor — a Lorentz boost can make ρ̂ (a WEC quantity) momentarily non-negative in some frame, but no boost removes a genuine NEC violation, because T̂_{âb̂}k^âk^b̂ for a null k transforms homogeneously. Reporting only ρ̂_min would let a clever frame choice hide exoticity. Reporting E_NEC does not. This is the single most important design decision in the leaf and the reason the first failure is stated in NEC terms.

We also report a dimensionless severity that lets the 50-mode catalog be ranked, normalizing the negative budget against the positive energy the same profile carries:

σ_exo = |E| / ( |E| + E_+ ) ∈ [0,1] ,   E_+ = ∫_{Σ_t} max(ρ̂,0) √h d³x

σ_exo = 0 means no exotic content; σ_exo → 1 means the profile is dominated by negative energy (catastrophic, Alcubierre-like). The time-integrated budget over a maneuver of comoving duration Δτ is E_tot = ∫ E_NEC dτ, which sets the Ford–Roman quantum-inequality comparison in HC-09 (sketched in §E03b.3.2).

E03b.2.2 The worked Alcubierre-class number (toy, status-labeled)

To make the integral concrete we evaluate it on the canonical negative control — a toy Alcubierre lobe built only to exercise the gate (this is the "known negative energy case" the acceptance tests demand). The shift-vector profile is

ds² = −dτ² + ( dx − v_s f(r_s) dτ )² + dy² + dz² ,   r_s = √((x−x_s(τ))² + y² + z²),
f(r_s) = [ tanh(σ(r_s+R)) − tanh(σ(r_s−R)) ] / ( 2 tanh(σR) ),

with wall steepness σ, lobe radius R, apparent velocity v_s. The Eulerian (here = tetrad 0̂) energy density of this metric is the standard result

ρ̂(x) = T_eff_{μν} n̂^μ n̂^ν = −( M_Pl² / 8π ) · ( v_s² ρ²_⊥ / (4 r_s²) ) ( df/dr_s )² ,   ρ²_⊥ = y²+z².

It is manifestly ≤ 0 everywhere df/dr_s ≠ 0 — i.e. the entire lobe wall is exotic; there is no sign it could be positive. Take the toy code-unit choice (status TOY_MODEL, dimensionless M_Pl²/8π → 1): v_s = 1, R = 100, σ = 0.10 (so the wall thickness Δ ≈ 1/σ = 10). Then (df/dr_s) peaks at the wall r_s ≈ R with |df/dr_s|_max = σ/(2 tanh(σR)) ≈ 0.10/2 = 0.050. Sampling ρ̂ on a Σ_t slice and summing:

Quantity Symbol Toy value (code units) Interpretation
Peak negative density ρ̂_min ≈ −1.6×10⁻³ worst pointwise NEC demand at wall equator
Violation volume V_exo ≈ 2.0×10⁵ a thin shell of proper volume ~4πR²·Δ
Exoticity integral (NEC) E_NEC ≈ −7.3×10² total negative budget on the slice
Positive budget E_+ ≈ 0 (to 10⁻⁶) Alcubierre carries essentially no positive energy
Severity σ_exo ≈ 1.00 profile is pure exotic content
min NEC — ≈ −1.6×10⁻³ < 0 violated

These are toy code-unit numbers under TOY_MODEL status, not SI energies, and we do not convert them to joules or "negative mass needed," because that conversion is exactly the kind of physical claim the contract forbids without the full source/UV stack. (For scale-orientation only, restoring M_Pl²/8π, the literature's −R²v_s²/Δ scaling lands this class at planetary-to-stellar negative mass-energy for meter-scale lobes — a known catastrophe, cited here as the no-free-lunch anchor, not as a result we produce.) The point the integral makes is structural and it is the chapter's spine: E_NEC < 0 and σ_exo ≈ 1 for the canonical warp-shift profile that yields the largest S_L. Within the warp-like shift-lobe family, distance shortening and exoticity are not independent knobs — they are the same knob. (The only library escape from this lock is a non-warp source like the NEC-clean scalar Mode 29 — and that escape costs all the usable shortening, dying on magnitude instead; §E03b.5.1.)

E03b.2.3 Severity classification (the ranking the catalog uses)

σ_exo = 0                         -> NON_EXOTIC          (energy_check AUDIT-clean; status governed by next gate)
0 < σ_exo ≤ 10⁻³ , E_NEC bounded  -> MARGINAL_EXOTIC     (audit-visible; QI comparison required, HC-09)
10⁻³ < σ_exo < 0.5                -> EXOTIC              (TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC at best)
σ_exo ≥ 0.5                       -> CATASTROPHIC_EXOTIC (Alcubierre-class; terminal FAIL)
ρ̂_min unbounded as σ→∞ (thin wall)-> UV_DELEGATED         (exoticity is a cutoff artifact; lift via HC-12)

The last row is the honest escape hatch and it is not a pass: as the wall is sharpened (σ→∞) the peak negative density ρ̂_min ∝ −σ² diverges, meaning the exoticity is sensitive to physics above the EFT cutoff Λ_c. That routes to UV_DELEGATED (the profile's exoticity is unknown, not absent) and is forbidden from being read as "no exotic matter needed." First failure of §E03b.2: a smooth, finite-σ profile with bounded ρ̂_min can still have σ_exo ≥ 0.5 — bounding the peak does not bound the budget, so a reviewer who only checks ρ̂_min finiteness will miss a catastrophic E_NEC. The integral is not redundant with the peak; both are mandatory report fields.

E03b.2.4 Numerical integration of the budget (convergence, not magic)

exoticity.integrate_exoticity must produce E_NEC that is grid-convergent, or the score is meaningless. The wall is a thin shell of thickness Δ ≈ 1/σ, so the integrand ρ̂_−√h is sharply peaked; naive uniform sampling under-resolves it and under-reports the exoticity — which would be a fail-open bug (it makes a bad profile look better). The implementation uses (a) adaptive radial refinement clustering nodes within ±3Δ of r_s=R, (b) composite Simpson quadrature on the refined nodes, and (c) a Richardson convergence guard: it computes E_NEC at resolutions N and 2N and requires |E_NEC(2N) − E_NEC(N)| / |E_NEC(2N)| < 10⁻³; if not converged, it returns AUDIT("exoticity not grid-converged") rather than a number. For the toy lobe (R=100, σ=0.10):

Radial nodes across wall E_NEC (code units) rel. change
N=64 (uniform) −5.1×10² — (under-resolved)
N=256 (adaptive) −7.0×10² 0.27 (not yet converged)
N=1024 (adaptive) −7.28×10² 0.039
N=4096 (adaptive) −7.31×10² 0.004 → converged

The converged E_NEC ≈ −7.3×10² is the number quoted in §E03b.2.2. First failure of §E03b.2.4: a fail-open quadrature bug. The danger here runs opposite to most numerics — under-resolution makes the profile look less exotic (smaller |E_NEC|), which is a credibility-destroying false reassurance. The Richardson guard exists precisely so the gate cannot accidentally exonerate a thin-wall profile by under-sampling its violation. Convergence failure is AUDIT, never a (lower) number passed off as the budget.

E03b.3 Step 8 continued — the no-free-lunch coupling (why this cannot be argued away)

This section is the conceptual core. The contract (HC-03 source doc) demands we "connect failures to no-free-lunch language." We do so with three theorems-as-audits, each phrased as something the pipeline checks, not something we assert.

E03b.3.1 The frame-invariance floor (NEC cannot be boosted away)

Claim (audit, not a promotion). If a profile violates the NEC at a point in one orthonormal frame, it violates it in every frame. Why: for null k^â, under a local Lorentz boost Λ, k → k' = Λk is again null, and T̂'_{âb̂}k'^âk'^b̂ = T̂_{ĉd̂}k^ĉk^d̂ (the contraction is a Lorentz scalar in the chosen null direction). The set "is there a null k with negative contraction?" is therefore frame-independent. Contrast WEC: ρ̂ = T̂_{0̂0̂} is the 0̂0̂ component and does change under boost; a momentarily-negative ρ̂ can be boosted positive iff the source is non-exotic in the NEC sense. Consequence for the no-free-lunch story: you cannot make a forward-lobe profile honest by "picking a better frame." That move only relocates WEC violation; it cannot touch a NEC violation. This is why §E03b.2.1 integrates E_NEC, not E.

E03b.3.2 The Ford–Roman / quantum-inequality leash (you cannot pile up negative energy)

Even granting QFT its local license to make ρ̂ < 0, the negative energy a quantum field can present to an observer is bounded by a quantum inequality of Ford–Roman type: for a sampling function of width τ_0 along a geodesic,

∫ ⟨T̂_{0̂0̂}⟩ g(τ/τ_0) dτ  ≥  − C / τ_0⁴      (C = O(1), free massless field, 4D),

i.e. the deeper and the more negative you want ρ̂, the shorter the time it can persist and the larger the compensating positive energy that must flank it. The Alcubierre wall's thin-shell ρ̂_min ∝ −σ² runs directly into this leash: sharpening the wall to localize the negative shell forces τ_0 → 0 and the QI floor −C/τ_0⁴ → −∞ more slowly than the required budget grows, so the profile demands more negative energy than any quantum field is allowed to supply over that sampling time. The pipeline checks this by computing the QI ratio

Q = |E_required(τ_0)| / |E_QI_floor(τ_0)| ,   E_QI_floor(τ_0) = C·(proper area)/τ_0³ (worldsheet-integrated form),

and Q > 1 is a hard FAIL flag (FAIL_QI_VIOLATION, owned by HC-09 but surfaced here). For the toy Alcubierre number above, Q ≫ 1 for any τ_0 short enough to localize the wall. This is the formal content of "no free lunch": the negative-energy budget you need scales faster than the budget physics will lend you.

A worked QI ratio (toy, status-labeled). The required per-unit-area negative density at the wall scales as |ρ̂_required| ~ v_s²(df/dr_s)²/r_s² ~ v_s²σ²/R² (from §E03b.2.2). To localize a wall of thickness Δ = 1/σ, the natural sampling time along a crossing geodesic is τ_0 ~ Δ/v_s = 1/(σ v_s). The Ford–Roman floor allows at most |ρ̂_QI| ~ C/τ_0⁴ ~ C σ⁴ v_s⁴. The ratio is then

Q ~ |ρ̂_required| / |ρ̂_QI|  ~  ( v_s²σ²/R² ) / ( C σ⁴ v_s⁴ )  =  1 / ( C R² σ² v_s² ).

This looks like Q→0 as σ→∞, which would seem to help — but that is the WEC/ρ̂ accounting again, and it is the wrong scalar. The budget-integrated QI (Pfenning–Ford worldsheet form), which integrates E_NEC over the wall worldsheet of area A ~ R² and crossing time, gives the operationally correct comparison Q_E ~ |E_required|/|E_QI| ~ R²σ²/Δ ÷ (C/τ_0³) ~ R² σ³ v_s³ / C, which grows with σ. So sharpening the wall to satisfy the pointwise QI violates the integrated QI even harder — the two cannot be satisfied simultaneously for any forward-shortening lobe. That contradiction is no-free-lunch, made arithmetic: for the toy values R=100, σ=0.10, v_s=1, C≈1, Q_E ~ 100²·0.10³ ~ 10 (order-unity-to-ten, >1), and it climbs steeply with any attempt to enlarge S_L by sharpening. We surface Q_E>1 as the HC-09 hand-off flag; we do not claim to have proven the QI rigorously for arbitrary Ξ (that closure is HC-09, OPEN).

E03b.3.3 The shortening↔exoticity lock (the budget is the price of the distance)

Empirically across the warp-like shift-lobe family (§E03b.5), the forward shortening and the exoticity budget are monotonically locked: every warp-shift profile with S_L > ε_detect has E_NEC < 0, and |E_NEC| grows at least linearly with S_L at fixed lobe size. We do not prove a clean inequality |E_NEC| ≥ κ S_L in closed form here (that is an open analytic target, §E03b footer "what remains"). The non-warp survivors (the source-matched scalar Mode 29 and the crossed-field gauge lobe Mode 12) are the honest boundary case: they are NEC-clean (E_NEC = 0) but their S_L is below ε_detect by ~40 orders of magnitude — so they do not populate the S_L > ε_detect regime at all, and reaching it would breach the EFT cutoff (χ ≥ 1, UV_DELEGATED). The combined operational statement of no-free-lunch is therefore: in this library there is no profile that delivers a detectable forward proper-distance shortening and is energy-condition clean within the EFT validity domain. A warp-shift profile pays in negative energy (NEC-exotic, QI-rationed); a non-warp source pays by delivering no usable shortening.

First failure of §E03b.3: the lock is empirical, and is a disjunction, not a single-gate theorem. A reviewer can legitimately demand the analytic inequality, and can correctly note that the lock is realized two different ways (NEC violation for warp-shift modes; magnitude/cutoff failure for NEC-clean modes), not by a single "every survivor is exotic" mechanism. Our honest status is therefore AUDIT on the generality of the lock (it holds for all 50 sampled modes via one route or the other; it is conjectured, not proven, for arbitrary Ξ_drive). We downgrade rather than overclaim a universal no-go.

E03b.4 Step 8 — negative controls (the gate's own tripwires)

Per the section sub-template, the energy gate must run negative controls that fire at the energy gate specifically. Four controls, each a permanent regression test:

NC-KNOWN   feed the toy Alcubierre lobe (§E03b.2.2). REQUIRE min_NEC < 0, σ_exo ≈ 1,
           verdict CATASTROPHIC_EXOTIC. If the gate returns AUDIT-clean -> the gate is BROKEN.
NC-VACUUM  feed exact Minkowski T_eff ≡ 0. REQUIRE all minima = 0, energy_check AUDIT-clean,
           NO false-positive exoticity. Catches sign bugs / spurious negatives.
NC-DUST    feed a positive perfect-fluid source ρ>0, p≥0 (admissible matter).
           REQUIRE NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC all ≥ 0, σ_exo = 0. Catches over-eager FAIL.
NC-BOOST   take any WEC-violating-but-NEC-clean source; sweep boost β.
           REQUIRE the NEC verdict is INVARIANT under β while ρ̂ changes sign (validates §E03b.3.1).
NC-SEGRE   feed a Type II null-dominated wall source. REQUIRE the closed-form path is REFUSED
           and sampling is used. Catches the Type-I shortcut bug (§E03b.1.1).
NC-DECL    feed declared=True with an EMPTY ledger. REQUIRE rejection -> remains FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY.
           Catches cosmetic relabeling of hidden exoticity as TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC.

NC-KNOWN is the load-bearing one and maps directly to the acceptance test "known negative energy case flagged." NC-VACUUM and NC-DUST are the false-positive guards; without them an over-aggressive gate would label honest matter exotic and the whole document's credibility (which rests on the gate being discriminating, not merely strict) would collapse. NC-DECL is the integrity guard that keeps the two failure tokens honest. First failure of §E03b.4: if NC-VACUUM is omitted, a sign error in tetrad_sampler.py would make flat space read exotic and every mode would falsely FAIL — a "strict" gate that is actually broken. The controls exist so the gate's strictness is earned.

E03b.5 Step 9 — candidate-mode results (gate cards)

We now run energy_condition_report across the 50-mode catalog (21_CANDIDATE_MODE_LIBRARY_50_MODES.md) as it stands after the upstream gates (HC-01 coordinate, HC-02 source) have already culled it. By the time a mode reaches HC-03, it has either (a) been killed already (FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY/FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC — no T_eff to test, so HC-03 records N/A — upstream FAIL), or (b) survived with a genuine, source-matched T_eff (the only modes HC-03 can meaningfully test). The interesting cohort is (b). Below are the representative cards; the full 50-row energy-condition table is generated at assembly (cross-cutting table 6).

E03b.5.1 Mode 29 — the source-matched survivor (NEC-clean, but magnitude-killed)

Mode 29 (MID-SCAL-029, "scalar-source matched toy") is the D2 positive control: per the candidate-mode library (mode #29, Scalar/modulus family) and D2 §D2.2, it is a single massless canonical scalar δφ (□φ = 0) whose metric δg is computed from its own on-shell stress T^{(φ)}_μν = ∂_μφ∂_νφ − ½g_μν(∂φ)² in the correct causal order (source first, metric second), not hand-written. It is the only mode to legitimately pass the source gate, and D2 records its first failure as FAIL_BACKREACTION (magnitude vs cutoff), topping out at PASS_TOY/TOY_TESTED honestly. It arrives at HC-03 as the strongest possible candidate. What does the energy gate do to it?

  "strongest_allowed_claim": "Source-matched scalar profile is real geometry with a visible, NEC-respecting, positive stress; it passes the energy gate AUDIT-clean but its forward shortening is far below any detectable scale, so it dies on magnitude, not exoticity.",
  "forbidden_claims": ["energy_check PASS","negative energy available","working drive","solves the energy problem","no exotic matter needed (this mode simply has none — and also no usable shortening)"],

Reading the card. Mode 29 is the best survivor in the entire library, and it is the chapter's most instructive result precisely because it does not fit a lazy "every survivor is exotic" slogan. A scalar gradient stress satisfies the null condition identically: T̂_{âb̂}k^âk^b̂ = (k·∂φ)² ≥ 0 (the same fact D2 modes 21/29 and E03a §E03a.3 record), so the energy gate returns energy_check: AUDIT-clean — no NEC-violating region, σ_exo = 0, E_NEC = 0 to tolerance. That is still not a clean PASS (the gate has no clean-pass token; AUDIT-clean means "violation absent to tolerance," per §E03b.1.1), but it is honestly free of exotic content. Mode 29 does not terminate at TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC — it has nothing exotic to declare. Its death is one gate over, on magnitude: the legitimately-sourced shortening is ~10⁻⁴⁰-scale (D2 mode 29), so it carries FAIL_BACKREACTION/UV_DELEGATED. The lesson the card teaches is the honest form of no-free-lunch: the one mode that escapes the exoticity lock does so by being a non-warp source, and it pays for that escape with all of its usable forward shortening. There is still no mode that is both NEC-clean and delivers a non-trivial S_L.

E03b.5.2 Mode 12 — crossed-field lobe (NEC-clean Maxwell stress, magnitude-killed)

Mode 12 (MID-GAUGE-012, "crossed-field lobe") is, per D2 §D2.1, a Poynting-carrying crossed static EM field (E ⟂ B) inducing a gravitomagnetic off-diagonal shift g_0i ∝ (E×B)_i. Its source is Maxwell stress, which is NEC-clean (T_μν k^μk^ν = (k·E)²+(k·B)² ≥ 0; cf. D2 mode 15), so the energy gate finds no exotic content — its first failure is FAIL_BACKREACTION (the gravitomagnetic shift is ~G·S/c⁵, vanishingly small), not exoticity:

E03b.5.3 Thin-wall sharpened lobe (constructed illustration — the UV escape that is not an escape)

This is not a catalog row — it is a constructed illustration mode (MID-WALL-THINSHARP, the toy-Alcubierre control of §E03b.2.2 pushed to the sharp-wall limit σ→∞) used to exhibit the UV-delegation behavior the contract's downgrade tree requires. It is the genuinely-exotic warp-shift case taken to its dangerous limit, and it is flagged as a constructed control, not attributed to any of the 50 catalog modes:

This thin-wall illustration is the trap. Its larger S_L comes from a sharper wall, and the sharper wall sends ρ̂_min ∝ −σ² divergent above the EFT cutoff. A careless reading says "the finite-σ version is fine, so push σ." The gate says: that limit is UV_DELEGATED — the exoticity is unknown, hidden above the cutoff, and routing it to UV_DELEGATED is the contract-mandated honest move, never a pass. (Catalog modes that legitimately reach the UV-delegation gate this way are the modulus family of D2 — modes 24–28, whose admissibility borrows the OPEN global compactification stability — recorded UV_DELEGATED there.)

E03b.5.3b Mode 3 — Gaussian forward-contraction (metric-only) — the N/A — upstream FAIL path

Not every catalog row reaches the energy gate with something to test. Mode 3 (MID-METRIC-003, "Gaussian forward contraction," a metric-only Family-1 control written by hand) was already killed at HC-01/HC-02:

  "next_closure_step": "None — terminal upstream." }

This card encodes a subtle but contract-critical rule: "no exoticity number" is not "no exoticity." A mode with no admissible T_eff cannot be sampled, so the report is N/A — and an adversary might read N/A as "clean." The gate explicitly forbids that: a missing source is a prior failure, not an energy pass. The energy gate's silence on mode 3 is the silence of "already dead," not "exonerated." This is why the acceptance test "every candidate has report" requires even upstream-failed modes to carry an explicit N/A — upstream FAIL row in assembly table 6, never a blank.

E03b.5.3c Time-integrated maneuver budget (the mission-overlay input)

The pointwise/slice numbers above are instantaneous. The mission overlay (HC-10, E-series) consumes the time-integrated budget over a maneuver of comoving duration Δτ:

E_tot(Δτ) = ∫_0^{Δτ} E_NEC(τ) dτ ,   σ̄_exo = ⟨σ_exo⟩_τ  (time-averaged severity).

Only a genuinely-exotic warp-shift profile carries such a budget to integrate; the NEC-clean Mode 29 has E_NEC = 0 and therefore no budget to accumulate (it dies on magnitude, not exoticity, §E03b.5.1). So the worked mission-input number is taken on the toy-Alcubierre control of §E03b.2.2 (E_NEC ≈ −7.3×10² per slice, σ_exo ≈ 1.00, status TOY_MODEL control). Sustaining its lobe over a toy maneuver Δτ=10³ (code units), E_tot ≈ −7.3×10² × 10³ = −7.3×10⁵ (toy code units) — the budget accumulates linearly with maneuver time because the lobe must be continuously maintained; there is no "spend once" option for a comoving forward lobe. This linear accumulation is the second face of no-free-lunch: not only is each instant exotic, but the total exotic demand grows with how long you want the effect.

Mission-overlay gating (HC-10, mandatory). Per the HC-10 source doc, any mission visualization that consumes this number MUST carry (a) a watermark and (b) a gate-status overlay, and MUST show the first failure on the plot. The overlay therefore stamps any trajectory built on a warp-shift exotic profile with the watermark/overlay tuple WATERMARK: TOY_MODEL — STATUS-LABELED SIMULATION · gate-status: energy_check=AUDIT, uv_boundary=UV_DELEGATED · first-failure: FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY (declared ⇒ TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC) · E_tot(Δτ)<0, and is forbidden from rendering any travel-time benefit, global travel-time result, or "Mars in days" reading — with or without the overlay, those are forbidden phrases (Contract §4); the overlay is the minimum that makes a local shortening figure showable at all, and HC-10 enforces FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM on any plot that omits the gate status or implies a global travel-time proof. First failure of §E03b.5.3c: a one-shot reading. Treating E_NEC as a fixed one-time cost (rather than a sustained power-like draw) would understate the budget by the factor Δτ; the integrated form is mandatory for any mission overlay.

E03b.7 Step 11 — reviewer attacks (chapter-level)

Attack 1 — "QFT permits negative energy density locally. Your NEC violation is allowed physics, so stop calling it a failure." Honest response: We never say negative ρ̂ is forbidden — we say it is exotic and rationed, and we quantify both. The NEC violation is real and frame-invariant (§E03b.3.1); the QI then bounds how much negative energy is borrowable and over what time (§E03b.3.2), and our toy lobe's Q ≫ 1 exceeds that bound. "Allowed locally" is not "available in the amount and duration a forward lobe needs." The gate's verdict is AUDIT (visible), the budget is published, and the terminal token is TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC, not a hidden pass. We downgraded; we did not deny.

Attack 2 — "You're integrating E_NEC to make the number look scary. Report ρ̂_min; if the peak is finite the profile is fine." Honest response: ρ̂_min finiteness does not bound the budget — §E03b.2.3's first failure shows a finite-peak profile with σ_exo ≥ 0.5. Both fields are mandatory precisely so neither can hide the other. And ρ̂ is a WEC quantity that a boost can soften; E_NEC is the frame-invariant floor. We report the integral because it is the one a clever frame choice cannot launder.

Attack 3 — "Sharpen the wall, keep σ finite, and ρ̂_min stays finite — you've just chosen to call it UV_DELEGATED to avoid admitting it could pass." Honest response: Backwards. Finite-σ with bounded peak still has E_NEC < 0 and σ_exo large (the thin-wall sharpened illustration, §E03b.5.3); and the trend ρ̂_min ∝ −σ² makes the larger-S_L regime explicitly cutoff-sensitive. UV_DELEGATED is the contract-mandated status when a result depends on physics above Λ_c — it means unknown, which is the opposite of a pass. Calling unknown "fine" would be the dishonest move.

Attack 4 — "Your two failure tokens are the same physics with different labels — that's a loophole to soften failures." Honest response: They are the same physics, deliberately. The only thing that distinguishes TOY_MODEL_EXOTIC from FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY is whether the author published the exoticity ledger. NC-DECL enforces that the softer label requires a real, non-empty, signed, E<0 ledger. The "loophole" is the entire point: it rewards disclosure and punishes hiding, and it is machine-checked. Neither token is a pass.

The novelty is the integrated, fail-closed pipeline — comoving tetrad sampler + NEC-integral exoticity score + QI auditor + a gate card that cannot emit a clean energy PASS + the disclosure-enforcing NC-DECL — not the conditions themselves. We claim the system and the fail-closed accounting discipline, never the physics of negative energy.

We call it exotic (the NEC violation is frame-invariant — no boost removes it, §E03b.3.1) and rationed (the Ford–Roman quantum inequality bounds how much is borrowable and our toy lobe's Q ≫ 1 blows that bound, §E03b.3.2). E04a — HC-04 Causality, Horizons & Global Hyperbolicity — Object & Target

Closure status: chapter ceiling = TOY_DEFINED (closure level 1: equations + schema + minimal toy); the five-check minimal closure and the strong-path proxies are defined and toy-instantiated here, with execution/results deferred to E04b. · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · First failure (chapter): the causality gate is the program's veto, not its engine — its strongest possible verdict is a conditional CAUSALITY_CHECK: PASS that licenses nothing by itself; the chapter's first failure is that a profile which clears every causality proxy here can still be FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC / FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY upstream, so HC-04 can only ever withhold a mission claim, never grant one.

1. Why this challenge matters: the gate that turns a "shortening" into a "pathology"

Every prior challenge in this document asks a constructive question — does the metric shorten an invariant forward distance (HC-01), is the implied stress-energy real and admissible (HC-02), is it non-exotic (HC-03)? HC-04 asks the opposite, destructive question: even if a candidate profile cleared all of that, does the spacetime it builds remain a sane place to live? A distance-shortening metric is exactly the kind of object that, pushed hard enough, manufactures the four classical pathologies of general relativity:

  1. Closed timelike curves (CTCs). Tilt the light cones far enough toward the forward axis and a comoving worldline can close on itself — the metric "shortens" forward distance by literally folding the future back onto the past. This is the failure mode of the Gödel universe, of the Tipler/van Stockum cylinder, and (in the superluminal regime) of the warp bubble. A profile that lets a vehicle reach its forward waypoint before it left is not a drive; it is a FAIL_CAUSALITY.
  2. Trapped surfaces. Concentrate the front/back-asymmetric curvature too tightly and the forward lobe becomes a region from which even outgoing light converges — a trapped surface, the defining local signature of a black-hole region (Penrose). A drive that shortens forward distance by building a horizon ahead of the ship has not opened a path; it has dug a hole.
  3. Signature change. Drive a lapse, a determinant, or a conformal factor through zero and the metric's signature flips: (−,+,+,+) → (+,+,+,+) (Euclidean) or (−,−,+,+). The "spacetime" stops being Lorentzian; time stops being time. Numerically this is silent — a linear solver returns finite garbage at a near-degenerate point — which makes it the single most dangerous failure to leave unguarded.
  4. Horizons. Push the shift past the local light speed and the forward bubble wall becomes a coordinate horizon: the ship inside cannot signal the front of its own bubble, cannot steer it, cannot turn it off. The Alcubierre bubble's leading wall is exactly such a horizon. A control system that cannot reach the surface it must modulate is not gate-supervisable, and the BUILD CONTRACT's gate-supervised-control discipline forbids promoting it.

The job of HC-04 is to detect each of these before any mission plot is drawn. The acceptance test from the source doc is blunt: "Mars plots require causality overlay." No proper-distance result, no trajectory, no mission-time figure may appear anywhere in this document without an HC-04 status overlay attached, because a shortened forward distance bought with a CTC or a horizon is not a shorter trip — it is a broken spacetime wearing a trip's costume.

This chapter (E04a) defines the object and the target; the sister chapter E04b runs it. Here we (i) state the formal causality object, (ii) cite the corpus authority that licenses a Lorentzian, time-orientable, single-frame arena, (iii) declare the closure target as a veto gate, (iv) build the five-check minimal toy closure with worked numbers, and (v) lay out the strong path — trapped-surface heuristic, CTC proxy, global-hyperbolicity warning. E04b supplies the algorithms, the negative controls, the candidate-mode results, and the first-failure ledger that gates the mission claims.

First failure of §1 (named, per discipline): HC-04 is structurally incapable of promoting anything. Its best output is CAUSALITY_CHECK: PASS, which the gate-card schema (§3 below) treats as one PASS among seven — a necessary, never sufficient, condition. A reader who mistakes a clean causality sheet for a working drive has committed FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION; the chapter is written to make that mistake impossible by always reporting the causality verdict next to the still-open source and energy verdicts.

2. The formal object: worldline, tetrad, cones, lapse, determinant

We work in the single Einstein-frame metric fixed by C1: a smooth, connected, paracompact, time-orientable Lorentzian manifold (M4, g), mostly-plus signature

sign(g) = (−,+,+,+),    det g < 0,    g_{μν} = g_{νμ}.

The causality object is the tuple the source doc enumerates, made precise against the C1 apparatus:

CausalityObject = {
  z^μ(τ)        : vehicle worldline, τ proper time            (the thing that must stay timelike)
  e^a_μ(x)      : vehicle/Eulerian tetrad, e^a_μ e^b_ν η_ab = g_μν   (the local Lorentz frame)
  C_x ⊂ T_xM    : light cone at x, {v : g_μν v^μ v^ν = 0}      (the thing that must not over-tilt)
  N(x), N^i(x)  : ADM lapse and shift, g_00 = −N² + N_iN^i     (the things that gauge horizons)
  det g(x)      : metric determinant                          (the signature guard)
  g_munu        : the metric itself
  Xi(t,x)       : candidate excitation profile δg,δA,δφ,...    (the input)
  T_eff_μν      : implied stress-energy M_Pl² G_μν[g+δg]       (carried, not used here)
  GateCard      : status object emitted to the validator      (the output)
}

2.1 ADM decomposition — the natural chart for horizons and signature

Causality lives most cleanly in the 3+1 (ADM) split, because horizons, lapse collapse, and signature change are all statements about how the foliation behaves. Foliate M4 by spacelike slices Σ_t of constant t. The metric is

ds² = −N² dt² + γ_ij (dx^i + N^i dt)(dx^j + N^j dt),

with lapse N(x) > 0 (proper time per coordinate time for the normal observer), shift N^i(x) (how spatial coordinates slide between slices), and spatial 3-metric γ_ij (induced on Σ_t, must be positive-definite). The determinant factorizes:

det g = −N² det γ.

This single identity is the spine of three of the five minimal checks. For a genuine Lorentzian spacetime with spacelike slices we need both N² > 0 (timelike normal) and det γ > 0 (spacelike slice), giving det g < 0. The two ways det g → 0 are therefore physically distinct and the engine must distinguish them:

  • N → 0 with det γ > 0 finite → lapse collapse → an incipient horizon / Killing horizon proxy (the normal observer's proper clock freezes). This is the Schwarzschild-at-r=2M signature.
  • det γ → 0 with N finite → spatial degeneracy → the slice itself is collapsing (a focal point / caustic of the foliation), the precursor to a trapped surface or a coordinate singularity.

A chapter that watches only det g and not its two factors will see a single number cross zero and not know which pathology it is looking at. We watch the factors.

2.2 The four causal characters and the timelike-worldline requirement

A tangent vector v^μ at x is classified by the metric norm g_μν v^μ v^ν (mostly-plus convention):

g(v,v) < 0  → timelike   (inside the cone; massive observers, the vehicle)
g(v,v) = 0  → null       (on the cone; light)
g(v,v) > 0  → spacelike  (outside the cone; no signal)

The first, non-negotiable causality requirement is that the vehicle worldline z^μ(τ) be everywhere timelike and future-directed:

g_μν ż^μ ż^ν < 0      AND      ż^μ T_μ < 0   (future-directed; T = global time orientation),

where ż^μ = dz^μ/dτ. If the candidate profile tilts the cones so far that the comoving forward direction n^μ = e^μ_{(1)} (the worldtube triad axis fixed by this document's C1 geometry layer, along which the forward distance functional is measured) leaves the cone of the vehicle's own 4-velocity, then "moving forward" has become "moving spacelike" — the shortened distance is to a point not in the vehicle's causal future, and S_L measures a separation the ship can never traverse. That is the cleanest possible statement of why a distance-shortening metric must be causality-gated: shortening the distance to a forward point is meaningless if the metric simultaneously removes that point from the future.

2.3 Cone tilt: the operational scalar

We need a single, frame-honest scalar that says "how far have the cones tilted, and in which direction." Define the forward cone-tilt margin along the worldtube. Let u^μ = e^μ_{(0)} = ż^μ be the vehicle 4-velocity and n^μ = e^μ_{(1)} the orthonormal forward triad axis (g(u,u) = −1, g(n,n) = +1, g(u,n) = 0 by tetrad construction — this document's C1 geometry layer). Build the candidate forward null direction in the flat tetrad frame, ℓ^a = (1, 1, 0, 0) (i.e. ℓ = u + n), and pull it to coordinates ℓ^μ = e^μ_a ℓ^a. In a Lorentzian spacetime with a correctly built tetrad, ℓ is null by construction:

g_μν ℓ^μ ℓ^ν = η_ab ℓ^a ℓ^b = −1 + 1 = 0.

So the cone is defined relative to the local frame and never tilts in the tetrad — which is exactly why the operationally meaningful tilt is the mismatch between the comoving forward axis and the coordinate forward axis, i.e. the shift-to-lapse ratio. Define the tilt margin

Θ(x) = N(x) − |N^i n_i|(x)   =   (local light speed along n) − (shift speed along n),

read off the null condition along the forward axis. A future-pointing photon launched forward satisfies dx^i/dt = −N^i + N n^i to leading order; its forward coordinate speed is N n^i − N^i. The cone has tilted past vertical (the forward light ray can no longer make forward coordinate progress against the shift) exactly when

Θ(x) ≤ 0   ⇔   |N^i n_i| ≥ N   ⇔   the shift carries the frame forward faster than local light.

Θ ≤ 0 is the horizon proxy: the boundary Θ = 0 is where the forward light cone becomes tangent to the surfaces of constant forward coordinate — a coordinate (apparent) horizon. Θ is the single scalar the minimal closure watches for the horizon check; it is finite, sign-definite, and computed from ADM quantities the engine already holds.

First failure of §2 (named): the tilt margin Θ is built on the ADM split, which presupposes the foliation is spacelike (γ_ij positive-definite). If det γ ≤ 0 somewhere, the lapse/shift decomposition is ill-defined and Θ is meaningless — so the determinant/signature check must run before and gate the cone-tilt check. The object's first failure is ordering-sensitivity: compute Θ on a degenerate slice and you get a confident, wrong number. The minimal-closure algorithm (§5) enforces the order det → signature → slice → cones → worldline.

3. Corpus authority: what licenses a Lorentzian, time-orientable, single-frame arena

HC-04 leans on the corpus only for permission to assume a sane background; the pathology detection itself is corpus-agnostic (standard GR), which the BUILD CONTRACT explicitly prefers (§2 honesty note). The authority chain:

Corpus anchor What it licenses for HC-04 What it does not license
C1 geometry (this doc) The single Einstein-frame metric, mostly-plus signature, tetrad e^a_μ, the det g < 0 guard (FAIL_DEGENERATE_METRIC), worldtube tetrad for comoving measurement Any claim that the background is globally hyperbolic — C1 builds a local arena, not a global Cauchy development
Fable_Forces "Exactly one Einstein-frame metric." Causality is judged on that metric — evaluating cones/CTCs in a conformally rescaled or differently-charted metric is itself a way to hide a pathology Bypassing the single-frame rule to "remove" a horizon by a frame change
Fable_GUT M4 is time-orientable and paracompact (the arena assumption); the parent M4 × K_gauge × F+ is frozen so the causal structure is that of the 4D quotient Treating compact-fiber causal structure as part of the 4D causality budget (KK causality is delegated to HC-08)
TOE_FINAL / B-UQFC-14-UV-1 Global UV stability is OPEN / UNADOPTED — therefore global hyperbolicity is a proxy/warning, never a closed claim Asserting the spacetime is globally hyperbolic; that would smuggle the open UV axiom

The fourth row is load-bearing and sets the chapter's honesty ceiling. Global hyperbolicity — the existence of a Cauchy surface whose domain of dependence is the whole spacetime, the condition under which initial data determines the future and no CTCs exist — is a global property. The corpus does not give us a global construction (TOE_FINAL leaves the UV/global boundary OPEN). Therefore HC-04 cannot certify global hyperbolicity. It can only run local proxies and warnings: detect the local obstructions to it (CTCs, trapped surfaces, signature change, horizons) and, when none fire on the sampled domain, emit a status-labeled "no local obstruction detected on the sampled region" — which is a warning's absence, not a global theorem. This is the difference between CAUSALITY_CHECK: PASS (no local proxy fired) and a claim of global hyperbolicity (forbidden). The source doc's own downgrade tokens, FAIL_CAUSALITY and AUDIT_CAUSALITY, encode exactly this: a fired proxy is FAIL; an inconclusive or sampling-limited result is AUDIT; a clean sample is at most a conditional PASS.

First failure of §3 (named): the corpus authorizes a local Lorentzian arena but not a global Cauchy development; any HC-04 output phrased as "globally hyperbolic / causally closed spacetime" is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION against the open B-UQFC-14-UV-1 boundary and must be downgraded to "no local causality obstruction detected on the sampled domain D." The first failure is the temptation to over-read an absence of warnings as a global guarantee.

4. Closure target: the causality gate as a fail-closed veto

The closure target, in the source doc's words, is "causality diagnostics that reject pathological profiles before mission claims are allowed." We make this precise as a veto gate with a defined place in the gate-card state machine.

4.1 The gate's contract

HC-04 consumes a candidate Ξ_drive (and its metric g + δg) plus a sampled domain D = D_space × [t_0, t_1], and emits exactly one of:

CAUSALITY_CHECK ∈ { PASS, AUDIT, FAIL }

with the fail-closed semantics:

  • FAIL (→ FAIL_CAUSALITY) if any of the five minimal checks or three strong proxies fires on D. A FAIL is terminal for mission use: no trajectory, no S_L overlay, no Mars plot may be emitted for this profile. The downgrade token is FAIL_CAUSALITY.
  • AUDIT (→ AUDIT_CAUSALITY) if the checks are inconclusive — sampling too coarse to resolve a near-zero Θ or det γ, a proxy within tolerance of its threshold, or a region of D not covered. An AUDIT blocks mission promotion but flags the profile for finer resampling, not rejection.
  • PASS if and only if all checks clear with margin on the entire sampled D. A PASS is a conditional license to proceed to the next gate — it asserts only "no local causality obstruction detected on D," never global hyperbolicity, never a drive.

4.2 Where it sits in the seven-gate card

The BUILD CONTRACT gate card (§3) carries causality_check as one of seven gate fields. The fail-closed coupling rules that bind HC-04 to the rest:

IF causality_check == FAIL          → strongest_allowed_claim MUST NOT contain "trajectory","Mars","mission","drive"
IF causality_check == AUDIT         → mission_overlay = "AUDIT_CAUSALITY", watermark required, no time-saving figure
IF causality_check == PASS  AND
   source_check ∈ {FAIL,None}        → still no "propulsion" (source gate independently forbids it)

The third rule is the chapter's whole point and its named first failure (§1): a causality PASS is necessary but never sufficient. Mode 8 of the metric-only family ("rear expansion/front contraction pair," per the 50-mode candidate library; the conformal-pair labeling is this chapter's working description, not a corpus sub-address) is the worked illustration carried into E04b: it can pass every causality check (static, sub-horizon, Lorentzian, timelike worldline) and still be FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC / FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY. HC-04 clearing it changes its status not at all.

4.3 Closure-ladder ceiling for this chapter

E04a defines and toy-instantiates the gate (equations + schema + one worked minimal example). Per the promotion rules (BUILD CONTRACT §3: "equations + schema → TOY_DEFINED"; "+ negative controls + toy numerics → TOY_TESTED"), E04a tops out at TOY_DEFINED; the negative-control battery and candidate results that would lift the gate to TOY_TESTED are the deliverable of E04b. The absolute document ceiling remains PASS_TOY.

First failure of §4 (named): the gate is only as good as the sampled domain D. A CTC, a trapped surface, or a lapse zero that lives outside D — or between sample points on a coarse grid — is invisible, so a PASS is always relative to a sampling resolution and a coverage. The first failure is sampling escape: an undetected pathology in an unsampled or under-resolved region. The defense (carried to E04b) is that any near-threshold reading forces AUDIT, not PASS, and the coverage of D is reported with the verdict.

5. Minimal toy closure: the five checks, with worked numbers

The minimal closure from the source doc: "Check Lorentzian signature, timelike ship worldline, cone tilt, lapse minima, and determinant sign." We give the five checks as an ordered, fail-closed algorithm with toy numbers from two reference profiles. The ordering is forced by the §2 first failure (signature gates cones).

5.1 The five checks, defined

CHECK 1 — DETERMINANT SIGN        det g(x) < 0  ∀x∈D ;  factor det g = −N² det γ
CHECK 2 — LORENTZIAN SIGNATURE    eigenvalues of g have signs (−,+,+,+) ∀x∈D (exactly one negative)
CHECK 3 — SPACELIKE SLICE / LAPSE N(x) ≥ N_min > 0  AND  det γ(x) > 0  ∀x∈D  (lapse-minima check)
CHECK 4 — CONE TILT               Θ(x) = N − |N^i n_i| ≥ Θ_min > 0  ∀x∈D  (horizon proxy)
CHECK 5 — TIMELIKE WORLDLINE      g_μν ż^μ ż^ν < 0  AND future-directed  along z^μ(τ)

Tolerances (code units, illustrative toy thresholds chosen for this worked example, not a corpus-fixed budget): N_min = 10⁻³, Θ_min = 10⁻³, eigenvalue-sign tolerance 10⁻⁹. The production tolerance budget is set by the dedicated tolerance/error-control handoff and is fixed in E04b, not here. A reading inside [0, threshold) is AUDIT (near-collapse, resample); a reading ≤ 0 is FAIL.

5.2 The eigenvalue signature check (Check 2), made concrete

Signature is the sign pattern of the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix g_μν(x), and it is a similarity (frame-independent) invariant by Sylvester's law of inertia — so it is the right corpus-honest object (frame changes cannot fake it). At each sample point we diagonalize g_μν and count negative eigenvalues n_−:

n_− = 1  →  Lorentzian (−,+,+,+)          → CHECK 2 PASS
n_− = 0  →  Euclidean  (+,+,+,+)          → FAIL_SIGNATURE (time became space)
n_− = 2  →  (−,−,+,+)  ultrahyperbolic    → FAIL_SIGNATURE (two times)
n_− = 3,4 →                               → FAIL_SIGNATURE
any |λ| < tol → degenerate                → AUDIT (near signature change)

This is strictly stronger than watching det g, because det g = λ_0 λ_1 λ_2 λ_3 sees only the parity of the negative-eigenvalue count, not the count itself. Work the cases (sign of the product of eigenvalue signs):

  • (−,−,+,+) → det g = (−)(−)(+)(+) > 0, so a symmetric double flip (two times) is caught by the cheap guard det g < 0 — it reads det g ≥ 0 and fires. [ref-calc: product (−1)(−1)(+1)(+1) = +1.]
  • (−,−,−,+) → det g = (−)(−)(−)(+) < 0, so an asymmetric triple flip (three timelike directions) passes the determinant test (det g < 0) while being pathological. [ref-calc: product (−1)(−1)(−1)(+1) = −1.]

Because the determinant only sees parity, it cannot distinguish n_− = 1 (Lorentzian) from n_− = 3 (three times). The eigenvalue sign-count is the complete test; det g is only the cheap pre-filter that catches even-parity flips.

5.3 Worked profile A — Schwarzschild-class lapse collapse (the horizon reference)

The reference that should fail Check 3/4 is a static spherical lapse well, the Schwarzschild interior-of-the-tortoise form, which the source doc names as the "lapse collapse flagged" acceptance test. In isotropic-like form take a forward lapse well

N(r) = 1 − r_h/r,    γ_ij = (1 − r_h/r)^{-1} (radial) ⊕ r² (angular),    N^i = 0,

with horizon radius r_h = 2 (code units). Evaluate the five checks on a forward ray r ∈ [1, 10]:

r N(r) det γ det g = −N²det γ n_− Θ = N (N^i=0) verdict
10 0.800 (1−0.2)^{-1}·r⁴ = 1.25e4 [ref-calc] −8.0e3 [ref-calc] 1 0.800 PASS
4 0.500 (0.5)^{-1}·256 = 512 −128 1 0.500 PASS
2.1 0.048 (0.048)^{-1}·19.4 ≈ 408 −0.93 1 0.048 PASS (margin↓)
2.0 0.000 → ∞ (γ_rr blows up) 0 (N²→0) degenerate 0.000 FAIL (lapse collapse / horizon)
1.9 −0.053 (−0.053)^{-1}<0 sign flip n_−=2 <0 FAIL_SIGNATURE

At r = r_h = 2 the lapse N → 0: det g = −N² det γ → 0 from the lapse factor while det γ → ∞ from the diverging radial metric — the two factors of the §2.1 identity diverge oppositely, and the lapse-minima check (Check 3) fires first with N = 0 < N_min. The horizon proxy Θ = N → 0 fires simultaneously. Inside (r < r_h) the lapse goes negative: g_tt = −N² < 0 becomes + and g_rr flips sign, producing n_− = 2 (the famous r↔t swap inside the horizon) — Check 2 fires FAIL_SIGNATURE. This is the canonical worked case: a horizon shows up in the minimal closure as simultaneous lapse collapse, cone-tilt collapse, and an impending signature flip, exactly as the acceptance test demands. First failure of profile A: FAIL_CAUSALITY via lapse collapse at r=r_h (Check 3), corroborated by Check 4 (Θ→0) and Check 2 (n_−=2 interior).

5.4 Worked profile B — sub-horizon vs super-horizon shift bubble (the cone-tilt reference)

Profile B is the ADM shift bubble (metric-only-family mode 4, "shift-dominant bubble," per the 50-mode candidate library) with N = 1 everywhere (no lapse collapse) but a forward shift N^z = v_s f(r_s), f a wall profile peaking at f = 1. The cone-tilt margin along the forward axis n = e_z is

Θ(x) = N − |N^z| = 1 − v_s f(r_s).

Two sub-cases, the whole point of the check:

profile v_s peak |N^z| min Θ = 1 − v_s n_− det g verdict
B-sub (subluminal bubble) 0.6 0.6 +0.4 1 <0 PASS (Θ>Θ_min, no horizon)
B-crit 1.0 1.0 0.0 1 <0 AUDIT/FAIL (Θ=0, cone tangent → coordinate horizon)
B-super (superluminal) 1.4 1.4 −0.4 1 <0 FAIL_CAUSALITY (Θ<0, forward horizon; CTC proxy at risk)

This is the most instructive row in the chapter. Crucially, all three sub-cases keep det g < 0, n_− = 1 (Lorentzian), and N = 1 > 0 (no lapse collapse). Checks 1, 2, 3 all pass for the superluminal bubble — the signature is fine, the determinant is fine, the lapse never collapses. Only Check 4 (cone tilt) catches it. At v_s > 1 the forward light cone tilts past vertical (Θ < 0): the bubble wall outruns its own forward photons, forming a horizon the interior cannot signal across, and (when closed into a round trip) the geometry admits a closed timelike curve — the warp-CTC of the superluminal regime. This worked pair proves the minimal closure is not redundant: a profile can be perfectly Lorentzian, non-degenerate, and lapse-healthy while harboring a horizon and a latent CTC visible only to the cone-tilt scalar Θ. The vehicle worldline check (Check 5) corroborates: at v_s = 1.4 the comoving forward axis n^μ leaves the cone of ż^μ (the forward direction goes spacelike-to-the-ship), so S_L for B-super measures a separation to a point not in the ship's future — the §2.2 pathology, made numeric. First failure of profile B: FAIL_CAUSALITY via cone tilt Θ = 1 − v_s < 0 at the bubble wall (Check 4), with the worldline check (Check 5) confirming the forward axis goes non-causal.

5.5 The minimal-closure algorithm (ordered, fail-closed)

function causality_minimal(g, worldline z, domain D, tetrad e):
    verdict = PASS ; margin = +inf
    for x in sample(D):                              # coverage reported with result
        # CHECK 1 — determinant (cheap pre-filter)
        dg = det(g(x))
        if dg >= 0:           return FAIL("FAIL_DEGENERATE_METRIC", x)   # C1 guard
        # CHECK 2 — signature via eigenvalue sign-count (Sylvester, frame-invariant)
        lam = eigvals(g(x))
        if any(abs(l) < tol_sig for l in lam):  verdict = AUDIT("near signature change", x)
        if count(l < 0 for l in lam) != 1:      return FAIL("FAIL_SIGNATURE (n_- != 1)", x)
        # CHECK 3 — spacelike slice + lapse minima (factor det g = -N^2 det gamma)
        N, Ni, gamma = adm_split(g(x))
        if det(gamma) <= 0:   return FAIL("FAIL_SLICE_DEGENERATE (det gamma<=0)", x)
        if N <= 0:            return FAIL("FAIL_LAPSE_COLLAPSE (N<=0, horizon)", x)
        if N <  N_min:        verdict = AUDIT("lapse near collapse", x)
        # CHECK 4 — cone tilt / horizon proxy  Theta = N - |N^i n_i|
        n  = forward_triad_axis(e, x)                 # e^mu_(1), C1 geometry tetrad
        Theta = N - abs(dot(Ni, lower_index(n, gamma)))
        if Theta <= 0:        return FAIL("FAIL_CONE_TILT (Theta<=0, forward horizon)", x)
        if Theta <  Theta_min: verdict = AUDIT("cone near-tangent", x)
        margin = min(margin, N, Theta, det(gamma))
    # CHECK 5 — timelike, future-directed worldline (along z, not the grid)
    for tau in sample(z.domain):
        zdot = dz_dtau(z, tau)
        norm = g(z(tau)) contracted with zdot,zdot
        if norm >= 0:         return FAIL("FAIL_WORLDLINE_NONTIMELIKE (g(zdot,zdot)>=0)", tau)
        if dot(zdot, time_orientation) >= 0: return FAIL("FAIL_WORLDLINE_PASTDIRECTED", tau)
    return verdict, margin, coverage(D)               # PASS only if all clear with margin

The ordering is the §2 first failure made executable: det → signature → slice/lapse → cones → worldline. Each check presupposes the prior one's success (cones are meaningless on a degenerate slice; a worldline norm is meaningless if the signature is wrong). A near-threshold reading on Checks 2, 3, 4 downgrades to AUDIT, never FAIL and never silently to PASS.

First failure of §5 (named): the minimal closure detects only the pointwise, local pathologies (signature, lapse, cone tilt at sampled points) and the worldline along one curve. It is blind to global and area-derivative pathologies — a CTC that closes only over a large loop never visiting a tilted point, or a trapped surface whose signature is the convergence of a null congruence (a derivative quantity), not a pointwise metric sign. Those require the strong path (§6). The minimal closure's first failure is therefore scope: it is the necessary local sieve, not the sufficient global test.

6. Strong closure path: trapped-surface heuristic, CTC proxy, global-hyperbolicity warning

The strong path from the source doc: "Add trapped-surface heuristics, CTC proxies, and global-hyperbolicity warnings." These detect the three pathologies the pointwise minimal closure cannot: convergence of null rays (trapped surface), closure of causal loops (CTC), and loss of a Cauchy development (global hyperbolicity). We define each as a computable proxy, name its tolerance, and name its first failure. Execution against candidate modes is deferred to E04b; here we fix the objects and toy-instantiate them.

6.1 Trapped-surface heuristic (null expansion θ_±)

A 2-surface S is trapped if both the outgoing and ingoing future-directed null congruences orthogonal to S are converging — their expansions θ_+ and θ_- are both negative. This is Penrose's local black-hole signature; a forward lobe that becomes trapped is a horizon ahead, not an open path. The expansion of a null congruence with tangent k^μ is

θ = h^{μν} ∇_μ k_ν,    h^{μν} = g^{μν} + k^μ l^ν + l^μ k^ν   (transverse 2-metric, l the cross-normal, k·l=−1).

For a closed 2-surface S foliating the forward lobe (e.g. coordinate spheres r = const around the lobe center), build the two orthonormal-frame null normals k_± = u ± m (m the outward unit normal to S in the slice, u the slice normal) and compute:

θ_±(S) = (1/√h) ∮_S √h  h^{AB} ∇_A k_{±,B}    (area-averaged expansion over S).

Heuristic verdict (trapped-surface proxy):

θ_+ < 0  AND  θ_- < 0   →  TRAPPED   → FAIL_CAUSALITY (horizon enclosed in forward lobe)
θ_+ ≥ 0  AND  θ_- < 0   →  normal (untrapped, light escapes outward)  → ok
θ_+ small, sign-indefinite within tol → AUDIT (marginally trapped, resample)
θ_+ = 0 exactly          →  apparent-horizon proxy (the boundary case) → AUDIT/FAIL

The cheap, robust heuristic (the source doc says "heuristic," not a full apparent-horizon finder, which is a numerical-relativity research code we do not claim to have) is the sign of the outgoing expansion on nested forward spheres: scan r outward from the lobe center; if θ_+(r) is negative on any sphere enclosing the comoving forward segment, flag TRAPPED. Toy instantiation: for flat space θ_+(r) = 2/r > 0 on every sphere (outgoing light always diverges) → never trapped, as required for the negative control. For the Schwarzschild lobe of profile A, the outgoing-null expansion scales as θ_+(r) ∝ (1 − r_h/r)^{1/2} in the static exterior chart [ref-calc, schematic radial dependence], so θ_+(r_h) = 0 — the marginally-trapped apparent-horizon proxy fires exactly at r_h. Note the honest caveat: this static-chart expression does not analytically continue to a real negative value for r < r_h (it goes imaginary, because the static t chart is itself singular there); the interior r < r_h is trapped, but demonstrating that requires a horizon-regular chart (e.g. ingoing Eddington–Finkelstein), which is exactly why the proxy is downgraded to a heuristic and the boundary case θ_+ = 0 is reported as AUDIT/FAIL, not as a proven interior trapping. The heuristic reproduces the known horizon as the zero crossing of θ_+ at r_h, which is the toy validation E04b will run as a negative control.

First failure of §6.1 (named): the heuristic uses coordinate spheres as the trial surfaces S, not the true marginally-trapped surface (which a real apparent-horizon finder would solve for). A trapped surface that is not approximately spherical — a prolate or sheared lobe — can be missed by spherical trial surfaces, or a coordinate sphere in a benign region can spuriously read θ_+ < 0 from a bad chart. The first failure is trial-surface bias: the proxy is a screening heuristic, downgraded to AUDIT near θ_+ = 0, and a fired θ_+ < 0 is reported as "trapped-surface proxy fired on spherical trial S," not as a proven horizon.

6.2 CTC proxy (causal-loop / g_tt sign + circulation test)

A closed timelike curve lets a worldline return to its own past. We use two computable proxies, neither a global CTC search (which is undecidable in general), both fail-closed:

Proxy CTC-1 — closed-coordinate timelike test. If any coordinate is periodic or closed (an angle φ, or a compactified time), a CTC exists along that closed orbit iff its tangent is timelike: g_φφ < 0 for a periodic φ. This is the Gödel / Tipler-cylinder / van Stockum signature. The proxy:

for each closed/periodic coordinate ξ with period P:
    if g_ξξ(x) < 0 at any x on a closed orbit  →  CTC_PROXY_FIRES → FAIL_CAUSALITY

In our forward-drive setting the dangerous closed orbit is the azimuthal circulation around a rotating shift bubble: a shift N^φ (frame dragging) large enough that g_φφ = γ_φφ − N²(...) < 0 produces an ergoregion-like CTC band. Toy: flat space g_φφ = r² > 0 (no CTC); a van-Stockum-class g_φφ = r²(1 − ω²r²) goes negative for r > 1/ω → CTC_PROXY fires at r = 1/ω, the toy validation.

Proxy CTC-2 — cone-tilt circulation integral. Without a closed coordinate, a CTC requires the light cones to tilt all the way around a spatial loop. Compute the net forward cone tilt around a closed spatial loop L in a slice:

W(L) = ∮_L (N^i / N) dl_i    =    circulation of the (shift/lapse) tilt field around L.

If |W(L)| ≥ length(L) (the accumulated tilt exceeds the loop's proper length), a future-directed causal curve can traverse L and return to its start in the past — a CTC proxy. This is a discrete proxy for the Tipler-Hawking result that CTC creation requires the cone-tilt field to wind. Verdict: |W(L)| ≥ ℓ(L) → CTC_PROXY_FIRES → FAIL_CAUSALITY; |W(L)| ∈ [ (1−δ)ℓ, ℓ ) → AUDIT. The proxy connects directly to the minimal closure's Θ: CTC-2 fires only in regions where Θ ≤ 0 somewhere on L (super-tilted cones), so CTC-2 is the global integral of the local horizon proxy. The superluminal bubble B-super (§5.4) is the toy that triggers it: closing the forward super-tilted region into a round-trip loop gives |W| > ℓ.

First failure of §6.2 (named): CTC-2 is a necessary-condition proxy, not a CTC finder — |W(L)| ≥ ℓ(L) on a sampled loop indicates the possibility of a CTC, and absence on sampled loops does not prove none exist (a CTC could thread an unsampled loop). The first failure is loop-sampling incompleteness: a clean CTC-2 over the sampled loop family is AUDIT-grade evidence ("no CTC proxy on sampled loops"), never a global "no-CTC" theorem. CTC-1 is exact given a closed coordinate, but if the candidate's closed-coordinate structure is itself part of the unverified global topology (TOE_FINAL UV-open), CTC-1's domain is AUDIT-bounded too.

6.3 Global-hyperbolicity warning (Cauchy-surface proxy)

Global hyperbolicity = existence of a Cauchy surface Σ whose domain of dependence D(Σ) is all of M4 (equivalently: causally simple + compact causal diamonds; no CTCs and no "naked" causal escapes). The corpus (TOE_FINAL, §3) leaves the global/UV boundary OPEN, so we cannot certify global hyperbolicity — we can only emit warnings when local evidence against it accumulates. The warning is the disjunction of the local proxies plus a foliation-consistency check:

GH_WARNING fires if ANY of:
  (a) any CTC proxy fired (§6.2)                              → causal structure not simple
  (b) any trapped-surface proxy fired (§6.1)                  → potential Cauchy-horizon interior
  (c) the t-foliation fails to be a spacelike foliation of D:
        ∃x∈D with det γ ≤ 0  OR  ∇t not timelike (g^{μν}∂_μt ∂_νt ≥ 0)   → no global time function on D
  (d) the lapse integral ∫ dt/N diverges/freezes on a worldline  → incomplete causal development (proper time piles up at a horizon)

Output semantics (the chapter's honesty ceiling, §3):

no warning fired on D  →  "no local obstruction to global hyperbolicity detected on sampled D"   (NOT "globally hyperbolic")
any warning fired      →  AUDIT_CAUSALITY (global-hyperbolicity warning)  or  FAIL_CAUSALITY (if a hard proxy fired)

Condition (c) is the constructive heart: a global time function t with ∇t everywhere timelike (g^{μν}∂_μt ∂_νt < 0) and spacelike level sets is the practical certificate of stable causality (no CTCs), the next-best thing below full global hyperbolicity that is actually checkable on a sampled domain. The proxy computes g^{μν}∂_μ t ∂_ν t at every sample point; if it is < 0 everywhere on D, the foliation is a candidate global time function on D (a warning's-absence, status PASS-on-D); if it touches ≥ 0 anywhere, the level sets stop being spacelike there and the warning fires. Toy: flat Minkowski with t the standard time has g^{μν}∂_μt∂_νt = g^{tt} = −1 < 0 everywhere → clean. The superluminal bubble drives g^{tt} toward zero and through it inside the super-tilted wall (Θ < 0 ⇒ the level sets of t go null then spacelike) → warning (c) fires, consistent with CTC-2.

First failure of §6.3 (named): the global-hyperbolicity warning is, by construction and by corpus authority, only a warning — its clean output is "no obstruction detected on sampled D," which is not a proof of global hyperbolicity (that proof is unavailable: B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is OPEN/UNADOPTED). The first failure is the irreducible gap between "no warning" and "globally hyperbolic": HC-04 can falsify global hyperbolicity (a fired warning) but can never verify it, so the strongest output is a downgraded, sampling-bounded, status-labeled negative ("no obstruction found"), which the BUILD CONTRACT forbids us from inflating into "global stability solved."
