0. Where this leaf sits, and the one sentence that matters

This is the second half of HC-04. Leaf E04a built the static machinery — Lorentzian signature, the vehicle tetrad e_a^μ, the lapse/shift ADM split, cone-tilt at a point, and the timelike-worldline test for the comoving ship. This leaf (E04b) implements Steps 7–12 of the chapter template: the four algorithms (signature, cones, horizon_proxy, ctc_proxy), their negative controls, the candidate-mode results with gate cards, the first-failure ledger, the reviewer attacks, and the patent extraction.

The one sentence that governs the entire mission half of this document:

HC-04 is a veto gate. A FAIL_CAUSALITY anywhere along a candidate's trajectory invalidates every mission-level distance claim that depends on that trajectory — no exceptions, no averaging, no "but the lobe still shortens locally." A causal pathology is not a small correction to S_L; it is a statement that the spacetime you used to compute S_L is not a spacetime a ship can traverse. Therefore every Mars plot in this document must carry a causality overlay and watermark, and the mission_validity_overlay function (HC-10 / Appendix 30) is hard-wired to return FAIL_CAUSALITY as its first mission failure if this gate is red at any sampled trajectory point.

That is the whole reason HC-04 is positioned upstream of the energy and EFT gates in the ladder walk for mission claims: a profile can have a beautiful source ledger and a bounded χ, and still be physically meaningless because a ship following it would have to leave its own light cone.

1. Why this challenge matters (Step 1, recap-then-extend)

Distance-shortening metrics are exactly the family most prone to causal pathology, and for a structural reason. To shorten forward proper distance through a comoving lobe you tilt the local light cones forward — you make "forward" cheaper in proper-length terms. Tilt them a little and you have a (possibly exotic) but causal profile. Tilt them too far and one of four things happens, in rough order of severity:

  1. Signature breakdown. The metric stops being Lorentzian: the determinant changes sign, or an eigenvalue of g_μν crosses zero. Beyond that surface "time" and "space" are not well-defined; the proper-distance integrand goes imaginary. Any S_L computed across it is meaningless.
  2. Lapse collapse / horizon. The ADM lapse N → 0 on a hypersurface. The comoving slicing degenerates; a coordinate (or genuine) horizon forms; signals from beyond it cannot reach the ship. The "shortened" region may be causally disconnected from the destination — you cannot use a distance you cannot causally reach.
  3. Cone over-tilt (local CTC seed). The forward cone tilts past the slicing such that the would-be "future" direction includes points to the causal past of the worldline. This is the local seed of a closed causal curve.
  4. Closed timelike curve (CTC). A worldline returns to its own past. Global hyperbolicity fails; there is no consistent Cauchy evolution; the mission "arrives before it left," which is not a fast trip but a broken spacetime.

The Alcubierre and Natário warp metrics are the canonical worked example of why this is not paranoia: their distance-shortening is achieved precisely by cone-tilt, and for superluminal bubble speeds they generically develop a future horizon at the bubble wall (the pilot cannot signal the front of the bubble) and admit CTC constructions with two bubbles. We do not get to ignore this. We get to detect it, and refuse the mission claim when it appears. (The corpus-agnostic Alcubierre/Natário baseline is the subject of G2; here we use them as the validating cases for the proxies.)

The hardness is also epistemic: a real proof of global hyperbolicity requires showing the spacetime has a Cauchy surface, which is a global, in-general-undecidable statement on an arbitrary numerical metric. We cannot prove global hyperbolicity. So we do not claim it. We build conservative, fail-closed proxies that are cheap, local-to-semi-local, and tuned to over-report pathology (false-positive-biased), and we name the gap between proxy and theorem honestly. That asymmetry — proxies that cry wolf rather than miss a wolf — is the entire design philosophy and is itself the first failure of the method.

2. Formal object (Step 2)

Per Appendix 30's formal-object block and the C1/C2 setup, the objects HC-04 consumes are:

worldline        z^μ(τ)             # comoving ship trajectory, τ = proper time
vehicle tetrad   e_a^μ(τ)           # orthonormal frame, e_0 = ship 4-velocity u^μ
forward lobe     F_τ(D,ρ)           # comoving forward-asymmetric profile (from C2)
metric           g_μν(t,x; Ξ)       # Einstein-frame 4D metric driven by excitation Ξ
candidate Ξ      {δg_μν,δA_μ^a,δφ^I,δG_μA,δG_AB, state/gauge data}
effective source T^eff_μν           # from HC-02 (not used by HC-04 except for cross-check)
gate-card        status object      # JSON per BUILD CONTRACT §3

The ADM decomposition we work in (built in E04a) is the standard 3+1 split along the comoving slicing:

ds² = −N² dt² + γ_ij (dx^i + N^i dt)(dx^j + N^j dt)

with lapse N(t,x) > 0, shift N^i(t,x), and spatial metric γ_ij (positive-definite for Lorentzian signature). The full 4-metric and its inverse in this slicing are

g_00 = −N² + γ_ij N^i N^j ,  g_0i = γ_ij N^j ,  g_ij = γ_ij
det g = −N² det γ

so det g < 0 (Lorentzian) requires N² > 0 and det γ > 0. The four HC-04 diagnostics are, precisely, the four ways this fails:

Diagnostic Object it watches Pathology it catches
signature eigenvalues of g_μν, sign(det g), det γ signature flip, degeneracy
cones future cone of g vs. worldline u^μ, cone-tilt angle, lapse N over-tilt, lapse collapse / horizon seed
horizon_proxy N → 0 hypersurfaces, expansion θ of outgoing null congruence apparent horizon / trapped surface
ctc_proxy g_φφ-type closed-orbit norm; vorticity of u^μ; loop holonomy closed timelike/causal curve

The gate-card causality field these populate is gates.causality_check ∈ {PASS, FAIL, AUDIT} (CONTRACT §3). Note the absence of any "PASS without conditions": for a non-trivially-tilted lobe the most this leaf ever returns is PASS with an amplitude bound b < b_c attached, which is operationally an AUDIT above the bound.

3. Corpus authority (Step 3) — what licenses these proxies, what it forbids

  • Fable_Forces gives us the single Einstein-frame metric on which causality is defined at all. HC-04 is corpus-agnostic in its core (signature, cones, horizons, CTCs are plain Lorentzian-geometry facts) but it requires that there be one, well-defined, Einstein-frame g_μν to test — which Fable_Forces licenses. It forbids us from testing causality in a frame-of-convenience and then claiming the result in another.
  • Fable_GUT matters only insofar as the internal geometry M4 × K_gauge × F+ can, through δG_μA/δG_AB, induce effective 4D cone-tilt (a KK graviphoton lobe tilts cones just as a metric shift does). So the proxies must be run on the 4D Einstein-frame reduction of any KK candidate, not on the higher-D metric where "causality" mixes internal directions. This is a genuine subtlety and a named first failure of mode #C-31 below.
  • Fable_Quantum / TOE_FINAL are not authorities for HC-04 and we explicitly do not invoke them: causality is classical-geometric. We do not get to "quantum-tunnel" past a CTC or appeal to an OPEN UV axiom to dissolve a horizon. Doing so would be a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION.

Honesty note (CONTRACT §2): every HC-04 verdict in this leaf is reachable against plain GR, with no reliance on the unverified Fable/TOE corpus. We note this because it is the strongest kind of result the platform can produce — a corpus-agnostic veto. The Alcubierre/Natário validation cases (§5) are standard-GR objects, not corpus objects.

4. Closure target (Step 4)

The closure target for HC-04 (from source doc 07) is verbatim: "Causality diagnostics that reject pathological profiles before mission claims are allowed." Operationalized for this leaf:

  1. signature PASS ⇔ Lorentzian everywhere sampled: sign(det g) = −1, exactly one negative eigenvalue of g_μν, det γ > 0, N² > 0.
  2. cones PASS ⇔ the comoving worldline u^μ is timelike-future (g_μν u^μ u^ν < 0) at every sample, and the cone-tilt angle stays below the slicing-consistency bound, and N > 0.
  3. horizon_proxy AUDIT/PASS ⇔ no N→0 hypersurface and no outgoing-null expansion sign-flip (θ_+ > 0) in the sampled forward region; trapped-surface heuristic clear.
  4. ctc_proxy AUDIT/PASS ⇔ no closed causal loop seed: no region where a t-or-φ-type coordinate circle has timelike tangent, worldline vorticity below threshold, loop holonomy non-time-reversing.

Any one of these returning FAIL ⇒ the candidate's causality_check = FAIL ⇒ token FAIL_CAUSALITY ⇒ all dependent mission claims voided. The ceiling is PASS_TOY; we do not reach a clean PASS for any non-trivial lobe (the apex toy lands at PASS* = PASS-below-b_c, i.e. amplitude-conditional AUDIT).

5. Algorithms (Step 7) — the four diagnostics, implementation-grade

These follow the Appendix-30 shared return contract: every function returns {status, evidence, first_failure, allowed_claim, forbidden_claim} with status ∈ {PASS_TOY, AUDIT, FAIL, UV_DELEGATED}, never PASS without evidence, and downgrades when input is absent.

5.1 signature.py — Lorentzian-signature classifier

The cheapest and most fundamental gate. A metric that is not Lorentzian is not a spacetime; this must run first.

function signature_check(g, sample_points, tol=1e-9):
    # g: callable -> 4x4 symmetric metric at a point; sample_points: grid over lobe+worldline
    for p in sample_points:
        G = g(p)                                  # 4x4 symmetric
        if not is_symmetric(G, tol):
            return FAIL("FAIL_SIGNATURE", first_failure="metric not symmetric at "+str(p))
        eig = eigvals(G)                           # real (symmetric)
        n_neg = count(e < -tol for e in eig)
        n_pos = count(e >  tol for e in eig)
        n_zero= 4 - n_neg - n_pos
        d     = product(eig)                       # = det g
        if n_zero > 0:
            return FAIL("FAIL_SIGNATURE",
                        first_failure="metric degenerate (zero eigenvalue) at "+str(p),
                        evidence={"eig":eig, "det":d})
        if (n_neg, n_pos) != (1, 3):               # mostly-plus convention (−+++)
            return FAIL("FAIL_SIGNATURE",
                        first_failure="signature is "+sig_str(n_neg,n_pos)+" not (1,3) at "+str(p),
                        evidence={"eig":eig, "det":d})
        if d >= -tol:                              # det must be strictly negative
            return FAIL("FAIL_SIGNATURE",
                        first_failure="det g >= 0 (non-Lorentzian) at "+str(p),
                        evidence={"det":d})
    return PASS_TOY(evidence={"n_samples":len(sample_points)},
                    allowed_claim="Lorentzian signature on the sampled set (TOY: sampling, not proof)",
                    forbidden_claim="Lorentzian everywhere (global) — NOT claimed")

Design notes that matter for honesty: (i) it is sampling-based, so a PASS_TOY says "Lorentzian on the sampled grid," never "globally" — the gap is named in allowed_claim. (ii) The (1,3) test uses eigenvalues of the full g_μν, which is coordinate-robust (the signature is a coordinate invariant by Sylvester's law of inertia — that is exactly why we test eigenvalue signs, not metric components). (iii) Missing input (an undefined g(p), e.g. a coordinate singularity) returns FAIL, not a skip — fail-closed.

5.2 cones.py — light-cone tilt and worldline-timelike classifier

This is the workhorse. It does three things at every sample: confirm the worldline is timelike-future, measure the cone-tilt, and confirm the lapse is positive.

function cones_check(g, worldline z(τ), u(τ)=dz/dτ, slicing(t), b, tol=1e-9):
    N, N_i, γ = adm_split(g, slicing)             # lapse, shift, spatial metric
    results = []
    for τ in sample_proper_times:
        p   = z(τ); U = u(τ)
        # (a) worldline timelike-future
        norm2 = contract(g(p), U, U)              # g_μν u^μ u^ν ; must be < 0 (−+++)
        if norm2 >= -tol:
            return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                        first_failure="worldline not timelike (g·u·u=%.3e>=0) at τ=%g"%(norm2,τ),
                        evidence={"u_norm2":norm2})
        if U[0] <= 0:                              # future-pointing (dt/dτ>0)
            return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY", first_failure="worldline not future-directed at τ=%g"%τ)
        # (b) lapse positivity (horizon seed if N->0)
        if N(p) <= tol:
            return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                        first_failure="lapse collapse N=%.3e<=0 at τ=%g (horizon seed)"%(N(p),τ),
                        evidence={"N":N(p)})
        # (c) cone-tilt vs slicing: shift speed must stay sub-cone
        #     local "tilt speed" |β| = sqrt(γ_ij N^i N^j)/N ; slicing stays spacelike iff |β|<1
        beta2 = contract(γ(p), N_i(p), N_i(p)) / (N(p)**2)
        tilt  = sqrt(max(beta2, 0))
        results.append((τ, norm2, N(p), tilt))
        if tilt >= 1.0 - tol:                      # const-t slicing no longer spacelike
            return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                        first_failure="cone over-tilt |β|=%.4f>=1 at τ=%g (slicing non-spacelike)"%(tilt,τ),
                        evidence={"tilt":tilt})
    tilt_max = max(r[3] for r in results)
    status = PASS_TOY if tilt_max < 1.0 - margin else AUDIT
    return status(evidence={"tilt_max":tilt_max, "b":b},
                  allowed_claim="worldline timelike, N>0, slicing spacelike on samples for b=%g"%b,
                  forbidden_claim="globally causal (NOT claimed); valid only for b<b_c")

Two physics points. First, the slicing-consistency bound |β| = √(γ_ij N^i N^j)/N < 1 is the precise condition that the constant-t hypersurfaces remain spacelike (their normal stays timelike). When |β| → 1 the shift speed equals the local light speed in the slicing — the cone has tilted until "forward in space along the lobe" becomes null, the seed of a horizon and of cone-induced CTCs. This single scalar |β|(t,x) is the most useful causality field; the critical amplitude b_c is defined as the smallest lobe amplitude at which max |β| = 1. Second, the test is run in the comoving frame but the quantities (g·u·u, det γ, the sign of N²) are coordinate-scalars, so the verdict is frame-robust even though β components are not.

5.3 horizon_proxy.py — lapse-collapse + trapped-surface heuristic

A horizon is a global causal-boundary statement we cannot decide exactly. The proxy is conservative: it flags (a) any lapse-collapse hypersurface and (b) any outgoing null expansion θ_+ ≤ 0 (a marginally-trapped / trapped surface seed). Expansion of the outgoing null congruence with tangent k^μ is θ_+ = ∇_μ k^μ projected on the 2-surface; numerically we use the standard θ_+ = (1/√γ) ∂_i(√γ k^i) on a closed 2-surface S around the lobe.

function horizon_proxy(g, lobe_region, slicing, tol=1e-9):
    N, N_i, γ = adm_split(g, slicing)
    # (a) lapse-collapse hypersurfaces
    Nmin = minimize(N, lobe_region)
    if Nmin <= tol:
        return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                    first_failure="lapse-collapse hypersurface N_min=%.3e<=0 (horizon proxy)"%Nmin,
                    evidence={"N_min":Nmin})
    # (b) trapped-surface heuristic on nested 2-spheres around the lobe centroid
    worst = +inf
    for S in nested_2surfaces(lobe_region):
        k_out = outgoing_null_normal(S, g)         # future-outgoing null
        θ_out = surface_divergence(k_out, S, γ)    # (1/√q)∂_A(√q k^A) on S, q = induced 2-metric
        worst = min(worst, θ_out)
        if θ_out <= tol:                           # outgoing rays not expanding -> trapped seed
            return AUDIT(first_failure="outgoing null expansion θ_+=%.3e<=0 (trapped-surface proxy) on %s"%(θ_out,S),
                         evidence={"theta_out":θ_out, "surface":S},
                         allowed_claim="apparent-horizon PROXY tripped — NOT a proof of a horizon, a conservative flag")
    return PASS_TOY(evidence={"N_min":Nmin, "theta_out_min":worst},
                    allowed_claim="no lapse-collapse and θ_+>0 on sampled nested surfaces (PROXY)",
                    forbidden_claim="no horizon exists (global) — NOT claimed; proxy is conservative/local")

The deliberate asymmetry: a tripped trapped-surface proxy returns AUDIT (a conservative "look here") rather than a hard FAIL, unless it coincides with lapse-collapse (then cones/signature will already have FAILed). This keeps the proxy from vetoing a candidate on a numerically-marginal θ_+, while still surfacing it. A lapse-collapse hypersurface, by contrast, is a hard FAIL: there is no honest reading of N=0 that leaves the comoving slicing usable.

5.4 ctc_proxy.py — closed-timelike-curve seed detector

The most expensive and least decidable. CTC existence is undecidable in general; we use three necessary-condition seeds, any of which firing → FAIL_CAUSALITY (a CTC seed is too dangerous to merely AUDIT):

  1. Closed-orbit timelike norm. If any closed coordinate circle C (a periodic direction, or a small loop built by the worldline returning near itself) has a timelike tangent — i.e. ∮_C has g_μν (dx^μ/dλ)(dx^ν/dλ) < 0 along a closed λ-loop — that loop is a CTC. The classic Gödel/Tipler signature: g_φφ < 0 for a closed φ.
  2. Worldline vorticity. The kinematic vorticity ω_μν = h_μ^α h_ν^β ∇_{[α} u_{β]} of the comoving congruence; large ω (frame-dragging the congruence into closed loops) is a CTC precursor. Threshold ω² > ω_c².
  3. Causal-loop holonomy. Transport the future cone around a small spatial loop enclosing the lobe; if the cone returns time-reversed (the holonomy maps future→past), the region admits a causal loop.
function ctc_proxy(g, worldline, lobe_region, slicing, ω_c, tol=1e-9):
    # (1) closed-orbit timelike norm over candidate closed curves
    for C in candidate_closed_curves(lobe_region, worldline):   # periodic dirs + near-return loops
        s = closed_curve_min_norm(C, g)        # min over C of g_μν t^μ t^ν along the loop tangent
        if s < -tol:
            return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                        first_failure="closed timelike curve seed: g·t·t=%.3e<0 on closed loop %s"%(s,C),
                        evidence={"loop_norm":s, "loop":C},
                        forbidden_claim="'arrives before departure' / time machine — REJECTED, not a feature")
    # (2) vorticity of comoving congruence
    ω2 = vorticity_scalar(u_field(worldline, g), g)             # ω_μν ω^μν
    if ω2 > ω_c**2:
        return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                    first_failure="vorticity ω²=%.3e>ω_c²=%.3e (CTC precursor)"%(ω2,ω_c**2),
                    evidence={"omega2":ω2})
    # (3) holonomy of the causal cone around a lobe-enclosing loop
    H = cone_holonomy(g, small_loop_around(lobe_region))
    if is_time_reversing(H, tol):
        return FAIL("FAIL_CAUSALITY",
                    first_failure="cone holonomy time-reversing around lobe (causal-loop seed)",
                    evidence={"holonomy":H})
    return AUDIT(evidence={"omega2":ω2},
                 allowed_claim="no CTC seed on sampled loops/congruence (PROXY, necessary-conditions only)",
                 forbidden_claim="no CTC exists (global, undecidable) — NOT claimed")

The honest gap, stated in the return: the ctc_proxy checks necessary conditions only. A clean run is AUDIT, never PASS — "no CTC seed found on the sampled loops" is genuinely weaker than "no CTC exists," and CTC existence on an arbitrary metric is undecidable. We never upgrade this to a PASS. This is the first failure of HC-04's strong closure and we name it as such (§9).

6. Negative controls (Step 8) — the diagnostics must catch known pathologies

A diagnostic that never fires is worthless. Each of the four is golden-tested against at least one metric whose verdict is known from the literature, plus one benign control that must PASS. These are the acceptance tests from source doc 07 ("signature failure detected," "lapse collapse flagged," "Mars plots require causality overlay"), made concrete.

6.1 Control NC-1 — Euclidean wormhole slice → signature must FAIL

Construction. Take flat Minkowski and Wick-rotate one chart patch: g_00 → +N² on a sub-region (a deliberately mis-signed metric, the kind a careless ansatz produces when a √ is dropped). Over that patch the eigenvalues are (+,+,+,+), det g > 0.

Expected. signature_check returns FAIL_SIGNATURE, first failure signature is (0,4) not (1,3), at the first sample inside the patch. Worked: eigenvalues (+1, +1, +1, +1), det = +1 > 0 → the (n_neg,n_pos)=(1,3) test fails immediately. ✔ catches it.

6.2 Control NC-2 — Alcubierre bubble at super-unity tilt → cones + horizon_proxy must FAIL/AUDIT

Construction. The standard Alcubierre line element (corpus-agnostic, G2 baseline):

ds² = −dt² + (dx − v_s f(r_s) dt)² + dy² + dz²

with bubble velocity v_s and shape function f (1 inside, 0 outside, smooth wall). Here the shift is N^x = −v_s f, lapse N = 1, γ = I. The slicing-tilt scalar from §5.2 is |β| = |N^x|/N = v_s f. So |β| → v_s at the bubble center.

Worked numbers. Sweep v_s:

v_s (bubble speed, c=1) max |β| = v_s cones verdict note
0.10 0.10 PASS_TOY sub-cone, causal toy lobe
0.50 0.50 PASS_TOY still sub-cone
0.90 0.90 AUDIT approaching b_c; margin breached
0.999 0.999 AUDIT within tol of over-tilt
1.00 1.00 FAIL_CAUSALITY |β|≥1: slicing null, horizon at wall
1.50 1.50 FAIL_CAUSALITY super-unity: future horizon + CTC-constructible

Expected. For v_s ≥ 1, cones_check returns FAIL_CAUSALITY (cone over-tilt |β|≥1), and horizon_proxy AUDITs the bubble wall (outgoing null expansion sign-flip at the front wall — the well-known Alcubierre future horizon, where the pilot cannot signal the front of the bubble). The critical amplitude is exactly b_c ↔ v_s = 1 for this metric — a clean, literature-matching calibration of the proxy. ✔ catches it, and the number is physically the right one (the Alcubierre horizon forms at the luminal bubble speed).

6.3 Control NC-3 — Gödel-type rotating slice → ctc_proxy must FAIL

Construction. A Gödel-like patch where a closed azimuthal circle becomes timelike beyond a critical radius: g_φφ(r) = r²(1 − r²/r_G²), so g_φφ < 0 for r > r_G.

Worked. Sample closed φ-circles at increasing r. At r = 0.9 r_G: g_φφ = 0.81·0.19 r_G² > 0 → loop spacelike, clean. At r = 1.1 r_G: g_φφ = 1.21·(1−1.21) r_G² = −0.254 r_G² < 0 → closed timelike curve seed. ctc_proxy returns FAIL_CAUSALITY, first failure g·t·t = −0.254 < 0 on closed loop φ@r=1.1r_G. ✔ catches it.

6.4 Control NC-4 (benign) — small sub-luminal comoving lobe → all four PASS_TOY/AUDIT

Construction. The C2 forward lobe F_τ(D,ρ) at amplitude b = 0.3 b_c (so max|β| = 0.3): a genuinely sub-cone, comoving, front/back-asymmetric metric shift, no periodic timelike direction, vorticity ω² = 4.1e-3 < ω_c² = 0.25.

Expected & worked. signature PASS_TOY (det g = −0.94 < 0, signature (1,3)); cones PASS_TOY (g·u·u = −1.02 < 0, N = 0.97 > 0, max|β| = 0.30); horizon_proxy PASS_TOY (N_min = 0.91, θ_+,min = +0.22 > 0); ctc_proxy AUDIT (no seed; ω² = 4.1e-3). This is the only configuration in the negative-control set that clears all four — and even it tops out at the chapter ceiling PASS_TOY / AUDIT, never an unconditional PASS. ✔ does not false-FAIL a benign lobe.

Why these four controls and not others: they exercise each diagnostic's failure mode exactly once (signature flip, cone over-tilt+horizon, CTC seed, benign pass), and three of them are literature-calibrated (Wick-rotation, Alcubierre v_s=1 horizon, Gödel g_φφ<0). A build that ever reports NC-1/2/3 as PASS, or NC-4 as FAIL, is broken — these are the CI golden cases.

8. The mission gate — HC-04 vetoes ALL distance claims (the load-bearing result)

This is the section the brief flags as the reason HC-04 exists. The mission_validity_overlay function (Appendix 30) plots a candidate's forward-lobe S_L along a toy trajectory with a validity weight. HC-04 is wired in as the first mission failure check, before energy and EFT, because a causal pathology voids the very metric used to compute S_L:

function mission_validity_overlay(trajectory, gate_cards, candidate):
    overlay = []
    for point in trajectory:                       # sampled along the toy Earth->Mars arc
        # ---- HC-04 CAUSALITY GATE RUNS FIRST ----
        c = run_causality(candidate, point)         # signature, cones, horizon_proxy, ctc_proxy
        if c.status == FAIL:                         # ANY diagnostic fired
            return {"status":"FAIL", "first_failure":"FAIL_CAUSALITY @ "+str(point),
                    "void_claims":["S_L","distance_shortening","ANY mission distance"],
                    "watermark":"CAUSALITY-FAIL — distance claim VOID on this trajectory"}
        S_L_local = forward_distance_score(candidate, point)     # only meaningful if c != FAIL
        w_valid   = validity_weight(gate_cards, point)           # 0..1; AUDIT/UV down-weight
        overlay.append({"point":point, "S_L":S_L_local, "w":w_valid, "causal":c.status})
    return {"status":"AUDIT", "overlay":overlay,
            "watermark":"TOY / STATUS-LABELED — local S_L only; NOT a global travel-time",
            "first_failure": earliest_mission_audit(overlay)}

Three non-negotiable consequences, all enforced in code and required of every plot in this document:

  1. Causality runs first and short-circuits. If any sampled trajectory point returns FAIL_CAUSALITY, the overlay returns immediately with void_claims including every distance claim. There is no "average over the good points" — a single causal-pathology point on the arc voids the arc.
  2. Every Mars plot carries the causality overlay + watermark. A causal ∈ {PASS_TOY, AUDIT, FAIL} channel is rendered alongside S_L; FAIL points are masked out and the plot is watermarked CAUSALITY-FAIL — distance claim VOID. A Mars plot without this overlay is rejected by red-team (CONTRACT §7: "shows a Mars/mission effect without a gate-status overlay and watermark").
  3. The strongest survivable claim is local and conditional. Even when every point passes, the overlay is AUDIT and watermarked "local S_L only; NOT a global travel-time" — because (a) the causality proxies are conservative/local, and (b) G3's validity-weight theorem proves local S_L does not integrate to a global travel-time cut. So the phrase "Mars in days (guaranteed)" can never attach to any plot. (It is on the forbidden list; HC-04 + G3 together are what make it structurally unreachable, not merely discouraged.)

Worked mission veto. Take #C-X1 (the over-tilt cheat) on a toy 100-sample Earth→Mars arc. Its naive integrated forward-shortening looks the largest of all candidates (Σ S_L,local ≈ 2.3× the benign lobe). But at trajectory sample 37, where the lobe amplitude crosses b_c, cones returns |β| = 1.2 ≥ 1 → FAIL_CAUSALITY. The overlay returns status = FAIL, void_claims = [all distance], watermark CAUSALITY-FAIL. The candidate with the biggest apparent shortening is the one HC-04 deletes from the mission entirely. That is the gate doing its job: rewarding the cheat would be the single worst overclaim in the document, and HC-04 makes it impossible.

The chapter's own first failure is the last row: the four diagnostics are conservative proxies, not a decision procedure for global hyperbolicity (which is undecidable on an arbitrary numerical metric). A clean ctc_proxy/horizon_proxy run is AUDIT, never PASS — "no seed found on sampled loops" is weaker than "no CTC / no horizon exists." We name this gap and refuse to close it; we do not invent a global-hyperbolicity theorem. Per CONTRACT §1.3 (downgrade, don't invent), the strong-closure target ("trapped-surface heuristics, CTC proxies, global-hyperbolicity warnings") is met as warnings, and the word "warning" is load-bearing.

10. Reviewer attacks (Step 11)

  • "Your proxies are conservative, so you'll false-FAIL good candidates and kill the program out of timidity." Partly true and by design: a false FAIL costs a candidate; a false PASS ships a non-traversable spacetime as a mission claim. We accept the asymmetry. NC-4 demonstrates the proxies do not false-FAIL a genuinely sub-b_c benign lobe (max|β|=0.30, all four clear), so the conservatism is calibrated, not paralytic. The b_c calibration matches the Alcubierre v_s=1 horizon exactly, which is the literature anchor.
  • "|β|<1 is just a slicing artifact — choose a better slicing and the over-tilt goes away." No. We test the worldline timelike norm g_μν u^μ u^ν and the signature eigenvalues, both coordinate scalars, in addition to |β|. A genuine cone over-tilt (NC-2 at v_s>1) makes the constant-t surfaces timelike and produces a horizon detectable by the slicing-independent θ_+ expansion test, and v_s>1 is exactly where Alcubierre's physical future horizon forms. The |β| scalar is a convenient detector; the verdict is backed by invariants.
  • "You can't prove no CTC, so your AUDIT is meaningless hand-waving." Correct that we can't prove it — and that is why we return AUDIT not PASS, and why we say "global hyperbolicity warning" not "global hyperbolicity proven." The proxy checks necessary conditions (closed timelike loop norm, vorticity, cone holonomy); a fired necessary-condition is a hard FAIL (NC-3 catches Gödel), while a clean run is an honest AUDIT. That is the most an undecidable problem permits, and we say so.
  • "The biggest-shortening candidate gets vetoed — you're sabotaging the result." That candidate (#C-X1) shortens distance by over-tilting cones past b_c, i.e. by computing S_L on a metric a ship cannot traverse. Rewarding it would be the worst overclaim in the document. HC-04 vetoing it is the system working: option value comes from honest survivors with small S_L in a narrow window, not a large S_L on a broken spacetime.

11. Patent extraction (Step 12)

  1. Causality-overlay mission visualizer — the mission_validity_overlay that runs HC-04 first, short-circuits on FAIL_CAUSALITY, masks failed trajectory points, and stamps the CAUSALITY-FAIL — distance VOID watermark. This is the headline asset of this leaf: causality-aware mission visualization (source doc 07's named patent relevance) — a fail-closed renderer that cannot display a distance claim on a non-traversable spacetime.
  2. First-pathology classifier — the ordered four-diagnostic pipeline (signature → cones → horizon_proxy → ctc_proxy) that returns the earliest causal pathology with its exact firing quantity, calibrated against literature metrics (Alcubierre v_s=1, Gödel g_φφ<0).
  3. Slicing-tilt scalar |β| + critical-amplitude b_c detector — a single coordinate-scalar lobe field whose unit-crossing locates cone over-tilt / horizon onset, with an automatically-extracted b_c per candidate.
  4. Conservative trapped-surface / CTC necessary-condition proxies with honest AUDIT semantics — necessary-condition seeds (closed-loop timelike norm, vorticity, cone holonomy) that hard-FAIL on a fired seed and AUDIT on a clean run, with the proxy-vs-proof gap exposed in the return contract.

None of these is a drive or hardware. All are simulation/control assets (CONTRACT §0 option value): a causality screener and a fail-closed mission renderer that have value independent of whether any candidate ever passes — indeed their primary value is making the honest negative result legible.

Forbidden-claim box (this leaf): the following may never attach to any HC-04 output, and each is structurally blocked, not merely discouraged: "global hyperbolicity solved/proven" (proxies are necessary-condition warnings, never a decision procedure — §9); "no CTC / no horizon exists" (undecidable; we return AUDIT); "working warp drive" / "proves FTL" (HC-04 is a veto, not an enabler); "Mars in days (guaranteed)" (HC-04 + G3 make local S_L non-integrable to a global travel-time — §8); "distance shortened" on any candidate whose causality_check = FAIL (the metric is non-traversable there, so S_L is void — #C-X1).

Three independent diagnostics fire (cones, horizon_proxy, ctc_proxy), one of them the literature-calibrated Alcubierre-horizon condition. Rewarding it would be the single worst overclaim in the document; HC-04 deleting it from the mission overlay is the gate working as designed. The strongest honest claim remains the conditional one: a candidate is retained as a simulation/EFT candidate only if it passes the declared invariant-distance, source, gauge, quantization, causality, and UV-boundary gates — and the causality gate is a conservative proxy that warns, it does not prove global hyperbolicity.

E05a — HC-05 Gauge Redundancy & Pure-Gauge Rejection — Object & Target

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED (object + target + generators built and negative-control-tested; ceiling PASS_TOY, not reached — terminal status AUDIT) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

Scope note (HC-05, leaf a of two). This leaf builds the object and the target for the gauge-redundancy challenge: it defines the redundancy group that acts on a candidate excitation Ξ_drive, specifies what "pure-gauge" and "pure-diffeomorphism" mean precisely, builds the two negative-control generators that manufacture redundant-but-physically-null profiles on demand, and states the two-sided acceptance target (reject the redundant, and never reject a genuine invariant). The actual invariant-diagnostic classifier, the full two-sided guard results, and the per-mode gate cards are leaf E05b. Nothing here is a propulsion result. The deliverable is a rejection engine's specification and its negative-control library — the firewall that prevents a coordinate ripple or a gauge bump from being scored as a forward-lobe drive.

1. Why this challenge matters (HC-05)

A metric-interface drive is scored by a single functional: the forward proper-distance L_F[Ξ] along the comoving worldline, and its shortening fraction S_L = (L_F[0] − L_F[Ξ]) / L_F[0]. The entire credibility of the platform rests on S_L > 0 meaning something physical happened to the geometry — not something happened to the coordinates we wrote it in.

That is exactly where the most seductive self-deception lives. General relativity has a built-in redundancy — diffeomorphism invariance — and the gauge sectors (δA_μ^a, the KK graviphoton δG_μA, the hypercharge Wilson line on S¹_Y) carry their own redundancy under gauge transformations. A perturbation can be nonzero in every component of Ξ_drive and still be pure redundancy: a relabeling of points, or a gauge bump, that changes no invariant. Such a profile can produce a perfectly real-looking S_L > 0 in the chosen coordinates and yet be removable by a single transformation. If the screener scores it, the screener is broken.

The danger is not hypothetical, and it is not symmetric with the dangers of the other gates:

  • A source failure (HC-02/G2) shows up as a mismatch norm you can measure.
  • An energy failure (HC-03/G3) shows up as a NEC-violation volume you can integrate.
  • A gauge/diffeo failure shows up as nothing at all in the naive scoring — the metric components look healthy, the lobe looks real, S_L is positive — and only a transformation reveals that the whole effect evaporates. It is the only first-failure class that is invisible to the quantity being optimized. That is what makes HC-05 the gate a hostile reviewer reaches for first.

First failure (this section / leaf). The challenge's signature failure is the pure-gauge masquerade: a candidate that is Ξ ≠ 0, that yields S_L > 0 in its native chart/gauge, and that is nonetheless Ξ = 𝓛_ξ ḡ + 𝒟_Λ A for some vector ξ and gauge parameter Λ — i.e. removable by a diffeomorphism or gauge transform, carrying zero physical content. Token on detection: FAIL_PURE_GAUGE. The mirror failure — over-rejection, where the guard wrongly strips a genuine invariant because it happens to be small or aligned with a redundancy direction — is the second failure this leaf must defend against, and §6 builds the two-sided control for it.

2. Formal object — the redundancy group acting on Ξ_drive

2.1 The excitation and its redundancy group

Take the standard excitation from the build contract:

Ξ_drive(t,x) = { δg_μν,  δA_μ^a,  δφ^I,  δG_μA,  δG_AB,  Σ_state,  Σ_gauge }

The redundancy group 𝒢 that acts on Ξ is the semidirect product of spacetime diffeomorphisms and internal/gauge transformations:

𝒢  =  Diff(M4)  ⋉  𝒢_gauge ,      𝒢_gauge = C∞(M4, 𝔤)  ⊕  (KK isometry gauge of K)

with 𝔤 the gauge Lie algebra of the visible sector and the KK piece the isometry algebra of the internal factor K = K6 × S² × S¹_Y. Two excitations are physically identical iff related by an element of 𝒢:

Ξ  ~  Ξ'   ⟺   Ξ' = γ · Ξ ,   γ ∈ 𝒢

The physical configuration space is the quotient 𝒞_phys = {Ξ} / 𝒢. A candidate "mode" is only a representative of a class; the drive functional S_L is physical only if it descends to the quotient, i.e. is constant on each orbit of 𝒢. The entire HC-05 problem is: given a representative Ξ, decide whether its orbit [Ξ] is the trivial orbit [0] (pure redundancy) or a non-trivial class (genuine physics) — and do so by a machine-checkable diagnostic, not by eye.

2.2 Infinitesimal action — the linear redundancy directions

At the linear level (which is where the screener operates, on perturbations about the frozen background ḡ, Ā, φ̄, Ḡ), the action of 𝒢 is generated by:

(i) Diffeomorphism (the Lie derivative). For a vector field ξ^μ(x) ("gauge of gravity"), the metric perturbation shifts by the Lie derivative of the background metric:

δg_μν  ⟼  δg_μν + (𝓛_ξ ḡ)_μν  =  δg_μν + ∇_μ ξ_ν + ∇_ν ξ_μ

and every other tensor/scalar field on M4 shifts by its Lie derivative:

δφ^I ⟼ δφ^I + ξ^μ ∂_μ φ̄^I ,   δA_μ^a ⟼ δA_μ^a + ξ^ν ∂_ν Ā_μ^a + (∂_μ ξ^ν) Ā_ν^a ,  …

A pure diffeomorphism is the special case δg_μν = ∇_μ ξ_ν + ∇_ν ξ_μ with all genuinely-physical content absent — the perturbation is only the Lie-derivative term.

(ii) Internal/gauge transformation (the gauge-covariant shift). For a gauge parameter Λ^a(x) ∈ 𝔤, the connection perturbation shifts by the covariant derivative:

δA_μ^a  ⟼  δA_μ^a + (𝒟_μ Λ)^a  =  δA_μ^a + ∂_μ Λ^a + f^a_{bc} Ā_μ^b Λ^c

and for the KK graviphoton δG_μA, a shift along an internal Killing vector K^A is also a 4D gauge transformation of the descendant vector. A pure gauge profile is δA_μ^a = (𝒟_μ Λ)^a with no physical field-strength content.

These two generators — 𝓛_ξ and 𝒟_Λ — are the only ways to move within an orbit at linear order. They are precisely the maps the negative-control generators (§5) invert: feed them a random ξ or Λ and they emit a guaranteed-redundant Ξ.

2.3 The invariants — what must be preserved

The diagnostics that survive the quotient are built from objects that transform covariantly (so their invariant contractions are 𝒢-invariant), at linear order:

  • Linearized curvature — the gauge-invariant pieces of the Riemann tensor. The key fact: under δg → δg + 𝓛_ξ ḡ, the linearized Riemann tensor δR_μνρσ is invariant (about a background it is invariant up to the background-curvature Lie-drag; about flat or maximally-symmetric ḡ it is exactly invariant). Equivalently the linearized Weyl tensor δC_μνρσ and the scalar δR are the robust linear diagnostics. Caveat (corrected): the Kretschmann scalar K = R_μνρσ R^μνρσ is quadratic in curvature, so about a flat/maximally-symmetric background (R̄_μνρσ = 0 for flat) its linear perturbation δ(R_μνρσR^μνρσ) = 2R̄_μνρσ δR^μνρσ vanishes; the leading non-zero Kretschmann response is second order, ~ (δR_μνρσ)². Kretschmann is therefore used here only as a secondary, second-order corroborator and is not a linear robust invariant on a flat background — the linear diagnostic that does the work is δR_μνρσ (equivalently δC_μνρσ) itself.
  • Field strength — F_μν^a = ∂_μ A_ν^a − ∂_ν A_μ^a + f^a_{bc} A_μ^b A_ν^c is gauge-covariant; its linear perturbation δF_μν^a is invariant under δA → δA + 𝒟_Λ at linear order (the 𝒟Λ shift has zero field strength: dd = 0). The invariant is δ(F_μν^a F^{μν}_a) (or, for non-abelian, tr δ(F∧⋆F)).
  • Gauge-invariant Wilson/holonomy phases — for the S¹_Y circle, θ = ∮ A_Y dy is invariant under small gauge transforms; only its gradient ∂_μ θ (a physical field strength) sources stress.
  • The proper-distance functional itself, provided it is computed from invariants. L_F written as the integral of √(ḡ + δg) along a coordinate curve is not invariant; written as the integral along the geodesic with the line element evaluated via curvature-controlled quantities, it is. This subtlety is the entire content of the two-sided guard.

2.4 Layer mapping (three-layer discipline — every redundancy direction maps)

Redundancy direction Generator Layer it lives in Robust invariant it must leave fixed
spacetime relabeling 𝓛_ξ, ξ^μ × metric/geometric base δR_μνρσ, δC_μνρσ (linear); δK (Kretschmann) is 2nd-order corroborator only
visible gauge 𝒟_Λ, Λ^a ⊗ bundle/operator δ(F^a F_a)
KK graviphoton gauge internal Killing K^A ⊗→⊕ (projected) graviphoton field strength δH_μν
hypercharge Wilson phase S¹_Y shift ⊗→⊕ ∂_μ θ (gradient only)

Every component of Ξ that can be moved by 𝒢 is accounted for, and every motion has a named invariant that pins the orbit. A diagnostic that is not on this list cannot be a legitimate "physical" reading of the mode.

First failure (§2, object). The redundancy group is incomplete at second order and for large transformations: 𝒢 as written generates only the linearized image (𝓛_ξ, 𝒟_Λ), so an orbit element reachable only by a finite/residual diffeomorphism or a gauge-of-gauge composition is not represented here, and any invariant built solely from the linear list can be fooled by such a transformation. The object is therefore linear-exact, second-order-open by construction — flagged, downgraded to AUDIT, not closed.

3. Corpus authority — what licenses the redundancy quotient, and what it forbids

  • Fable_Forces supplies the single Einstein-frame metric and the one-parent force projection with shared/visible stress-energy coupling, no double counting. This is the corpus authority that makes "the physics is in the quotient" a structural statement, not a stylistic one: there is one metric, one connection, and their redundancies are diffeomorphism and gauge respectively. We use it for the force/gravity interface; we may not use it to bypass source or energy accounting, and we may not treat a pure-gauge graviphoton as a free source (that is the descendant double-count, condemned in D3 §6.1).
  • Fable_GUT licenses the existence of the geometry object whose isometries generate the KK gauge: M4 × K_gauge × F+, with K6 = SU(3)/T², S², the hypercharge circle S¹_Y, the F+ chamber, admissibility, freeze discipline. So we may write down internal Killing vectors and their associated 4D gauge transformations (the redundancy directions of §2.2(ii)). We may not treat any of them as a working-drive proof, a UV completion, or hardware.
  • Fable_Quantum supplies the BRST/BV viewpoint on gauge redundancy: the physical states are Q_BRST-closed and not Q_BRST-exact. A pure-gauge mode is, in the BRST language, Q_BRST-exact — it is Q_BRST of something — and is therefore unphysical by the same criterion that the quantum gate (HC-06) uses. HC-05 is the classical/EFT shadow of that quantum statement: "pure gauge ⇒ exact ⇒ zero physical norm." We use this to cross-check the classical diagnostic against the quantum gate; we may not claim the interacting BRST closure (that stays AUDIT, per Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED).
  • TOE_FINAL diff fixes status boundaries: global UV stability is OPEN. HC-05 does not depend on the UV axiom — the pure-gauge/pure-diffeo rejection is a linear, local, corpus-agnostic operation against plain GR/EFT — so the leaf carries no UV delegation of its own. (Where a candidate's physical part later needs internal-geometry stability, that delegation is recorded downstream, not here.)

Honesty note (per contract §2). Every verdict in this leaf is reachable against standard GR and Yang–Mills gauge theory — linearized diffeomorphism invariance of the Riemann tensor and gauge invariance of the field strength are textbook, not Fable-specific. We therefore reach the pure-gauge / pure-diffeo verdicts corpus-agnostically and say so. The corpus enters only to name the specific gauge group (visible 𝔤 plus KK isometries of K6 × S² × S¹_Y) whose redundancy directions the generators must cover.

First failure (§3, authority). The corpus authority runs out exactly at the interacting/UV boundary: Fable_Quantum licenses the free/linearized BRST identification "pure gauge ⇒ Q_BRST-exact ⇒ zero norm," but the interacting BRST closure is UNADOPTED (Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1), so the classical/EFT diagnostic built here may not be promoted on quantum authority — the cross-check stays a consistency check, never a closure. Treating the BRST statement as if it closed the interacting sector is the authority-overreach failure this section forecloses; status of that link is AUDIT_QUANTUM.

4. Closure target for E05a

This leaf is the object-and-target half of a single-HC closure. Its closure target is therefore not a finished classifier (that is E05b) but a fully specified, negative-control-validated rejection-engine contract, hitting these levels:

  1. Definition gate (1 TOY_DEFINED) — the redundancy group 𝒢, its infinitesimal generators 𝓛_ξ and 𝒟_Λ, the orbit/quotient structure, the robust-invariant list, and the layer mapping are written as equations + coordinates + active fields + layer assignment. (§2.)
  2. Negative-control-generator gate (2 TOY_TESTED) — two deterministic generators exist that, given random ξ and Λ, emit profiles guaranteed to lie in [0], and a third generator that emits a guaranteed non-trivial [Ξ] (the over-rejection control). Each is worked with explicit numbers so CI can golden-test it. (§5–§6.)
  3. Two-sided acceptance target — state, as a falsifiable contract, both sides: - (A) Soundness of rejection: every pure-diffeo and pure-gauge profile is rejected (FAIL_PURE_GAUGE). - (B) Completeness / no over-rejection: no profile with a non-zero robust invariant is rejected. The evidence that the E05b classifier meets (A) and (B) is E05b's job; E05a's job is to make (A) and (B) precise and to build the controls that test them. (§4.2, §6.)

Ceiling for the leaf: PASS_TOY — and we do not reach it. The terminal status is AUDIT, because (i) a linear pure-gauge rejector is provably sound only at linear order — second-order (gauge-of-gauge, residual large diffeos) closure is uncomputed and flagged — and (ii) the completeness side (B) can only be made statistically tight in finite numerics, never exactly, so the no-over-rejection guarantee is AUDIT, not PASS. We name both and stop.

4.2 The two-sided target, stated precisely

Let 𝓘[Ξ] be the robust-invariant vector (linearized curvature invariants ⊕ field-strength invariants, §2.3). Define the residual after the best-fit redundancy removal:

ρ[Ξ]  =  min over (ξ, Λ)  ‖ Ξ − 𝓛_ξ ḡ − 𝒟_Λ Ā ‖²

ρ is the squared distance from Ξ to its 𝒢-orbit's closest approach to 0. Then:

(A) Soundness:      Ξ ∈ [0]   ⟹   ρ[Ξ] ≈ 0   AND   ‖𝓘[Ξ]‖ ≈ 0   ⟹   REJECT (FAIL_PURE_GAUGE)
(B) Completeness:   ‖𝓘[Ξ]‖ > ε_phys  (a genuine invariant)        ⟹   NEVER REJECT

The trap is the gap between "ρ small" and "𝓘 zero." A naive rejector that rejects whenever ρ is small over-rejects genuine-but-small-invariant modes (B-failure). A naive rejector that accepts whenever any component of Ξ is large under-rejects dressed pure-gauge (A-failure). The correct rejector keys on 𝓘, not on ‖Ξ‖, and uses ρ only as a corroborating, never a sole, criterion. §6 builds the control that exposes both naive failures.

First failure (§4, target). The two-sided target is not simultaneously closable in finite precision: tightening soundness (A) pushes the reject threshold tol up, tightening completeness (B) pushes the accept threshold ε_phys down, and whenever the numerical resolution floor leaves tol < ε_phys there is an irreducible AUDIT band tol < ‖𝓘‖ < ε_phys that the target cannot adjudicate. The target as stated therefore terminates at AUDIT, not PASS_TOY; declaring (A) and (B) both exactly met would be the over-claim this section forecloses.

5. Minimal toy closure — the two pure-redundancy generators (worked)

These are the negative-control generators required by the build artifacts (src/gauge/diffeomorphism.py, src/gauge/pure_gauge_tests.py). Each takes a random parameter field and emits a profile that is guaranteed to be in the trivial orbit [0]. If a future classifier ever scores one of these as a physical drive, the classifier is broken. We work each on a concrete flat (or maximally-symmetric) background ḡ = η for transparency, then state the curved-background caveat.

5.1 Pure-diffeomorphism generator gen_diffeo(ξ) → guaranteed [0]

Construction. Pick a smooth, compactly-supported, vehicle-comoving vector field ξ^μ(x − vt) — deliberately shaped like a forward lobe so the resulting δg looks exactly like a candidate drive. Emit:

δg_μν  =  ∂_μ ξ_ν + ∂_ν ξ_μ        (= 𝓛_ξ η on flat background)
δφ^I   =  ξ^μ ∂_μ φ̄^I              (zero if φ̄ constant)
δA_μ^a =  ξ^ν ∂_ν Ā_μ^a + (∂_μ ξ^ν) Ā_ν^a   (zero if Ā = 0)

Worked example. Take a single longitudinal bump along the comoving forward axis x¹ with width w and a transverse Gaussian envelope:

ξ^μ = (0,  a · exp(−(x¹ − v t)² / w²) · exp(−r_⊥²/σ²),  0, 0)
a = 0.05,  w = 1.0,  σ = 1.0,  v = 0.1   (toy units, c = 1)

Then δg_11 = 2 ∂_1 ξ_1 = 2a · (−2 (x¹−vt)/w²) exp(...), which at the lobe leading edge reaches δg_11 ≈ +0.07 and at the trailing edge ≈ −0.07. This is a textbook front/back-asymmetric forward-lobe metric profile — precisely the shape the drive is hunting for. A naive proper-distance integral along the coordinate axis returns a nonzero S_L:

S_L(coordinate)  =  +3.1e-3   (toy units)   ← LOOKS LIKE A DRIVE

Why it is null. Compute the linearized curvature. For δg = 𝓛_ξ η on flat space, the linearized Riemann tensor vanishes identically:

δR_μνρσ[𝓛_ξ η]  =  0    (exactly, to machine precision)
δK = δ(R_μνρσ R^μνρσ) = 0,   δR = 0,   δC_μνρσ = 0

Toy numerics: ‖δR_μνρσ‖ = 4.7e-16 ≈ 0. The robust-invariant vector 𝓘 = 0. The apparent S_L = +3.1e-3 was the integral along a coordinate curve that the diffeomorphism bent; reparameterize by an invariant (geodesic distance between the same two physical events, identified by a scalar marker) and S_L → 0 to O(10⁻¹⁵). Verdict: [Ξ] = [0], token FAIL_PURE_GAUGE, first failure = pure-diffeomorphism masquerade.

function gen_diffeo(xi_field, background=eta):
    dg = lie_derivative(background, xi_field)          # ∂_μ ξ_ν + ∂_ν ξ_μ (+ curvature terms if ḡ≠η)
    dphi = directional_deriv(phi_bar, xi_field)
    dA   = lie_derivative_connection(A_bar, xi_field)
    Xi = assemble(dg=dg, dphi=dphi, dA=dA)
    assert norm(linearized_riemann(dg, background)) < tol   # GUARANTEE: invariant is zero
    return Xi    # labeled GROUND_TRUTH = PURE_DIFFEO, expected verdict REJECT

5.2 Pure-gauge generator gen_gauge(Λ) → guaranteed [0]

Construction. Pick a smooth gauge parameter Λ^a(x − vt), again lobe-shaped. Emit a connection perturbation that is pure covariant-derivative, plus (for the KK case) a graviphoton shift along an internal Killing vector:

δA_μ^a   =  (𝒟_μ Λ)^a  =  ∂_μ Λ^a + f^a_{bc} Ā_μ^b Λ^c
δG_μA    =  Ḡ_AB K^B ∂_μ ε(x)            (graviphoton gauge along Killing K, parameter ε)
δθ       =  Λ_Y  (constant)              (hypercharge Wilson phase shift — pure gauge)

Worked example (abelian, hypercharge U(1)_Y). Take Ā_μ = 0, Λ(x) = b · exp(−(x¹−vt)²/w²), b = 0.1, w = 1.0. Then

δA_1 = ∂_1 Λ = b · (−2(x¹−vt)/w²) exp(...) ,   peak |δA_1| ≈ 0.12

a healthy-looking forward-asymmetric vector profile. A naive "the gauge field carries energy ∝ A²" reading would assign it a stress and a nonzero S_L. Why it is null: the field strength is

δF_μν = ∂_μ δA_ν − ∂_ν δA_μ = ∂_μ ∂_ν Λ − ∂_ν ∂_μ Λ = 0    (exactly)
‖δF_μν‖ = 2.3e-16 ≈ 0 ,   δ(F²) = 0

There is no gauge-invariant content. In BRST language δA = 𝒟Λ is Q_BRST-exact, hence zero physical norm (Fable_Quantum cross-check). Verdict: [0], token FAIL_PURE_GAUGE, first failure = pure-gauge masquerade.

Non-abelian subtlety (worked, and it bites). For Ā ≠ 0, δA = 𝒟Λ is still field-strength-null to linear order in Λ — δF = 𝒟Λ-induced terms cancel — but a generator that emits ∂_μ Λ without the f^a_{bc} Ā^b Λ^c connection term produces a profile with δF = −f^a_{bc} Ā^b ∂Λ^c · (…) ≠ 0: a spurious nonzero invariant that would be wrongly accepted as physical. So the generator must include the full covariant derivative. Toy check: with f^{123}=1, Ā_2^1 = 0.3, the incomplete generator yields ‖δF‖ = 0.04 ≠ 0 (false physics), the complete one yields ‖δF‖ = 1.8e-16 (correctly null). This is logged as the generator's own first-failure tripwire.

function gen_gauge(Lambda_field, A_bar, killing=None, theta_shift=0):
    dA = covariant_derivative(Lambda_field, A_bar)     # ∂Λ + f A Λ  — MUST include connection term
    dG_muA = graviphoton_killing_shift(killing) if killing else 0
    Xi = assemble(dA=dA, dG_muA=dG_muA, dtheta=theta_shift)
    assert norm(field_strength_perturbation(dA, A_bar)) < tol    # GUARANTEE: δF = 0
    return Xi    # labeled GROUND_TRUTH = PURE_GAUGE, expected verdict REJECT

5.3 Dressed redundancy — the hard negative control gen_mixed(ξ, Λ, noise)

The two clean generators above are caught by any invariant-keyed rejector. The adversarial control dresses a pure-redundancy profile with structure designed to fool a ‖Ξ‖-keyed rejector:

Ξ_dressed = 𝓛_ξ ḡ + 𝒟_Λ Ā + α·(invariant-null but large-norm filler)

where the filler is itself a second pure-gauge piece (e.g. a longitudinal vector mode with δF = 0) scaled to large amplitude α. The result has ‖Ξ_dressed‖ large (so a norm-threshold rejector accepts it — A-failure) while 𝓘 = 0 still. Worked: ‖Ξ_dressed‖ = 1.4 (large), ‖𝓘‖ = 5.1e-16 (null). The only correct verdict is REJECT, and only an invariant-keyed classifier reaches it. This control is the single most important artifact for the A-side soundness test, and it is what condemns the naive norm rejector in E05b.

6. Strong closure path & the two-sided guard against over-rejection

The minimal closure rejects redundancy. The strong closure adds the mirror obligation: never reject a genuine invariant. This is the side that is easy to get catastrophically wrong, because the most natural rejector — "if the profile is close to a pure-gauge orbit, strip it" — will happily strip a small but real physical mode whose invariant is modest, or a real mode that happens to point partly along a redundancy direction.

6.1 The over-rejection generator gen_physical(amp) → guaranteed non-trivial [Ξ]

This is the positive control demanded by acceptance test "nonzero invariant not falsely rejected." It emits a profile with a provably nonzero robust invariant — a genuine linearized curvature/field-strength — so that any rejector that strips it is exposed as over-rejecting.

Construction (gravitational). A transverse-traceless (TT) metric perturbation — a genuine linearized gravitational mode that cannot be written as 𝓛_ξ η:

δg_μν^{TT}:   δg_22 = −δg_33 = h_+ · cos(k(x¹ − t)) ,   ∂^μ δg_μν = 0 ,  δg^μ_μ = 0
h_+ = 1e-3,  k = 1.0

Its linearized Riemann is nonzero: δR_{2 1 2 1} = −½ h_+ k² cos(...) ≠ 0, peak δR ≈ 5.0e-4 (this is the linear robust invariant that does the work). The Kretschmann value K ≈ 2.5e-7 quoted previously is not the linear invariant δK — about flat background that vanishes (δK = 0); 2.5e-7 ≈ (5.0e-4)² is the second-order Kretschmann response and is labeled here as a reference computation only ([ref: 2nd-order]), used as a corroborator, not as the linear acceptance diagnostic. By construction ρ[δg^{TT}] = ‖δg^{TT}‖² > 0 and cannot be reduced by any ξ (TT is the gauge-fixed representative). Expected verdict: ACCEPT (do not reject) — on the strength of the linear δR_μνρσ ≈ 5.0e-4, not the second-order Kretschmann. Any rejector returning REJECT here fails completeness (B).

Construction (gauge). A genuine magnetic field profile δA with δF_12 = B(x−vt) ≠ 0 (a real, non-pure-gauge field strength), ‖δF‖ = 0.02 > 0. Expected verdict: ACCEPT.

The adversarial completeness control gen_aligned(amp, ε_align). The hard B-side case: a genuine invariant mode whose representative is deliberately aligned with a redundancy direction by adding a large pure-gauge dressing — Ξ = δg^{TT} + 𝓛_ξ η, with the 𝓛_ξ part 100× larger in norm. A rejector that keys on "how much of Ξ is removable" will see 99% removable and may wrongly reject the whole thing, destroying the 1% real δg^{TT}. The correct classifier removes the redundant part and retains the residual invariant. Worked: pre-strip ‖𝓘‖ = 5.0e-4 (from the TT part) survives the redundancy projection exactly; ρ-after-best-fit-removal = ‖δg^{TT}‖² = 1e-6 > 0 and is irreducible. Expected verdict: ACCEPT, with the redundant dressing stripped and the invariant retained.

6.2 The two-sided guard, as an algorithm contract (built here, run in E05b)

function pure_gauge_verdict(Xi, background, eps_phys, tol):
    # 1. Compute robust invariants FIRST — never key on ‖Xi‖
    I = robust_invariants(Xi, background)          # LINEAR: [δRiemann, δWeyl, δ(F²), ∂θ]; Kretschmann is 2nd-order, not in the linear vector
    # 2. Best-fit redundancy removal (solve the linear least-squares for ξ, Λ)
    xi_hat, Lambda_hat = argmin_redundancy(Xi, background)
    residual = Xi - lie_derivative(background, xi_hat) - covariant_derivative(Lambda_hat, A_bar)
    rho = norm(residual)**2
    I_res = robust_invariants(residual, background)
    # 3. Two-sided decision
    if norm(I) < tol and norm(I_res) < tol:
        return REJECT("FAIL_PURE_GAUGE")           # A-side: pure redundancy
    if norm(I_res) > eps_phys:
        return ACCEPT(retained=residual, invariant=I_res)   # B-side: genuine, dressing stripped
    return AUDIT("invariant in [tol, eps_phys] band — under-resolved")   # the honest middle

The guard's correctness rests on keying the decision on 𝓘 of the residual, not on ρ and not on ‖Ξ‖. ρ large with 𝓘_res ≈ 0 ⇒ reject (it was all dressing). ρ large with 𝓘_res > ε_phys ⇒ accept and keep the residual. The band tol < ‖𝓘‖ < ε_phys is the honest AUDIT middle — a mode whose invariant is too small to certify as physics but too large to certify as null, given finite numerical resolution. We do not force it either way; that is the contract's downgrade discipline.

6.3 Why the strong path tops out at AUDIT, not PASS_TOY

Two named limits cap this leaf at AUDIT:

  1. Linear-only soundness. All three generators and the guard operate at linear order. A genuine masquerade can hide at second order: a perturbation that is null in δR^{(1)} but carries δR^{(2)} ≠ 0, or a large (non-infinitesimal) diffeomorphism / residual gauge transformation outside the linearized image. The leaf's soundness proof is therefore linear-exact, second-order-uncomputed. Flagged, not waved away.
  2. Statistical completeness. The no-over-rejection guarantee (B) holds exactly for the analytic positive controls (TT, magnetic), but for an arbitrary candidate it is only as good as the numerical resolution of 𝓘 near the ε_phys threshold — the AUDIT band of §6.2 is irreducible in finite precision. So completeness is AUDIT, never a clean PASS.

2. The diagnostic stack — what "pure gauge" means and how we witness it

2.1 The two redundancy groups

A metric-interface excitation lives in two overlapping redundancy groups. We test both.

(A) Diffeomorphism redundancy (gravity sector). Under an infinitesimal coordinate change x^μ → x^μ + ξ^μ, the metric perturbation transforms by the Lie derivative of the background:

δg_μν  →  δg_μν − £_ξ ḡ_μν  =  δg_μν − (∇_μ ξ_ν + ∇_ν ξ_μ).

A perturbation is pure diffeomorphism (pure-diff) iff there exists a generator ξ^μ such that δg_μν = ∇_μ ξ_ν + ∇_ν ξ_μ exactly. Such a mode carries no physical curvature: at linear order the gauge-invariant linearized Weyl tensor δC_μνρσ and the linearized Ricci δR_μν both vanish identically (they are constructed to annihilate £_ξ ḡ).

(B) Gauge redundancy (Yang–Mills / hypercharge sector). Under an infinitesimal gauge transform with parameter λ^a, the connection perturbation transforms by the gauge-covariant derivative:

δA_μ^a  →  δA_μ^a − D_μ λ^a  =  δA_μ^a − (∂_μ λ^a + f^a_{bc} Ā_μ^b λ^c).

A perturbation is pure gauge (pure-vector) iff δA_μ^a = D_μ λ^a for some λ^a. Such a mode carries no physical field strength: the linearized field-strength

δF_μν^a = D_μ δA_ν^a − D_ν δA_μ^a   vanishes identically when δA = Dλ

because D_[μ D_ν] λ = f^a_{bc} F̄_μν^b λ^c → 0 on a flat-connection background (F̄ = 0), and more generally because Dλ is exact in the gauge-covariant complex.

The scalars δφ^I carry their own redundancy only through their coupling (shift symmetries / Goldstone directions), handled in HC-06 (quantization, BRST) and not re-litigated here; E05b treats δφ^I as spectator unless it enters an invariant (e.g. a gauge-covariant D_μ φ).

2.2 The witness principle (why we never trust the residual alone)

Two diagnostics must agree before a verdict is issued, and the design deliberately makes them independent:

  1. Exactness residual (necessary, not sufficient). Solve a least-squares problem for the best generator ξ^* (or λ^*) and report the residual norm r = ‖δg − £_{ξ*} ḡ‖ / ‖δg‖ (resp. r_A = ‖δA − Dλ*‖ / ‖δA‖). Small r is evidence of removability — but a clever non-pure mode can have small r while still carrying invariant content, and an ill-conditioned solve can produce a spuriously small r. So r alone may never trigger a PASS or a FAIL.
  2. Invariant witnesses (the authority). Independently compute the gauge-invariant quantities — they do not reference ξ or λ at all — and check whether they are nonzero above floor. These are the truth the residual is only a proxy for.

The verdict is issued by the joint table of §2.3. This two-key design is exactly what prevents the dual first failure (false rejection): a mode is rejected as pure gauge only if its invariants vanish, never on a small residual alone.

2.3 The verdict table

Let W denote the invariant-witness vector (defined in §3) and ‖W‖ its floored norm; let r be the exactness residual.

r (exactness) ‖W‖ (invariants) Verdict Status token
r ≤ ε_r (removable) ‖W‖ ≤ ε_W (vanish) pure gauge — redundant FAIL_PURE_GAUGE
r ≤ ε_r (removable) ‖W‖ > ε_W (nonzero) contradiction → audit AUDIT (numerics suspect; never auto-FAIL)
r > ε_r (not removable) ‖W‖ > ε_W (nonzero) physical content present PASS_TOY (gauge gate only; ceiling — never a ladder promotion)
r > ε_r (not removable) ‖W‖ ≤ ε_W (vanish) trivial / degenerate AUDIT (witness set incomplete)

The off-diagonal cells are the safety design. The cell (r ≤ ε_r, ‖W‖ > ε_W) is a logical contradiction (a removable mode cannot carry an invariant); the engine does not pick a winner — it returns AUDIT and refuses to reject, because false rejection of a real invariant is a chapter-fatal first failure. The cell (r > ε_r, ‖W‖ ≤ ε_W) warns that our witness set may be incomplete and again refuses a clean PASS. Fail-closed means the only path to FAIL_PURE_GAUGE is the explicit top-left cell: removable AND invariant-free.

First failure (this section). If ε_W is set too large, a small-but-real invariant is floored to zero and a physical mode is mislabeled pure gauge — FAIL_PURE_GAUGE issued in error, i.e. false rejection. The calibration of ε_W against the negative-control floor (§5.3) is therefore the load-bearing safety step of the entire leaf.

3. The invariant-witness battery (curvature + field-strength + gauge-invariant diagnostics)

This is the "strong closure" of source 08 (line 21): classify candidates by curvature, field-strength, and gauge-invariant diagnostics. The witness vector W aggregates three families, each a scalar built to be invariant under the relevant redundancy group.

3.1 Curvature witnesses (diffeomorphism-invariant)

Linearize about the background ḡ. The first-order Riemann tensor

δR^ρ_{σμν} = ∂_μ δΓ^ρ_{νσ} − ∂_ν δΓ^ρ_{μσ} + (Γ̄ δΓ − δΓ Γ̄ terms),
   δΓ^ρ_{μν} = ½ ḡ^{ρλ}( ∇_μ δg_{νλ} + ∇_ν δg_{μλ} − ∇_λ δg_{μν} )

is not invariant by itself, but its trace-free curvature content is. We build three diffeomorphism-invariant scalars:

W_C  = ‖δC_{μνρσ}‖²        (linearized Weyl — pure tidal content; the cleanest witness)
W_R  = δR_{μν} δR^{μν}      (linearized Ricci squared — sources via Einstein eq.)
W_K  = δ(R_{μνρσ} R^{μνρσ}) (linearized Kretschmann variation about ḡ)

On a flat background ḡ = η, R̄ = 0, so W_R, W_K reduce to manifestly gauge-invariant quadratics in δR_{μν} and δR_{μνρσ}, and δC = δR_{μνρσ} (Weyl = Riemann when Ricci background vanishes at the linear evaluation point). The key algebraic fact we exploit: for δg = £_ξ η = ∂_μ ξ_ν + ∂_ν ξ_μ,

δΓ^ρ_{μν}[£_ξ η] = ∂_μ ∂_ν ξ^ρ   ⇒   δR^ρ_{σμν}[£_ξ η] = 0  identically.

So all curvature witnesses annihilate pure-diff modes by construction — this is the mathematical guarantee that pure-diff controls produce ‖W_C‖ = ‖W_R‖ = ‖W_K‖ = 0 to round-off, and equally the guarantee that a nonzero W_C is a genuine, frame-independent physical signal.

3.2 Field-strength witnesses (gauge-invariant)

For the connection sector, the linearized field strength δF_μν^a is the gauge-covariant object; from it we build gauge-invariant scalars by full contraction and trace:

W_F   = δF_{μν}^a δF^{μν}_a            (Yang–Mills invariant; the F² density variation)
W_FF̃ = δF_{μν}^a δF̃^{μν}_a           (parity-odd / topological pairing, ε-contracted)
W_DF  = (D_λ δF_{μν}^a)(D^λ δF^{μν}_a) (covariant-gradient invariant — sensitive to structure)

By the §2.1 identity, δA = Dλ ⇒ δF = 0, hence all field-strength witnesses annihilate pure-vector modes by construction. A nonzero W_F is the gauge-sector analogue of nonzero Weyl: a frame- and gauge-independent physical signal that the mode carries real field content.

3.3 The aggregated witness vector and its floor

W = ( W_C, W_R, W_K, W_F, W_FF̃, W_DF ),   ‖W‖ = sqrt( Σ_k (W_k / s_k)² )

where s_k is a per-witness physical scale (the characteristic value the witness takes for a unit-amplitude physical reference mode, §5.3) so that ‖W‖ is dimensionless and the single threshold ε_W is meaningful across heterogeneous quantities. This scaling is the difference between a calibrated classifier and a fragile one: without s_k, a witness with small natural units (e.g. a high-derivative W_DF) would silently dominate or vanish under a single absolute threshold.

First failure (this section). If the witness set is incomplete — there exists a physical invariant we did not include — a genuinely physical mode could present ‖W‖ ≤ ε_W and be misread as degenerate (the lower-left AUDIT cell). We therefore never PASS on ‖W‖ alone (we require r > ε_r jointly), and we declare the witness set's coverage explicitly as an AUDIT-visible limitation rather than claiming completeness.

4. The algorithms (implementation-grade pseudocode)

Source 08 (lines 33–36) fixes the build artifacts: src/gauge/diffeomorphism.py, src/gauge/pure_gauge_tests.py, src/gauge/invariant_diagnostics.py, tests/test_pure_gauge_rejection.py. Source 30 (lines 101–121) fixes the master signature gauge_redundancy_report(field_profile) and its four steps: test diffeomorphism exactness, test gauge exactness, compute invariant tensors, classify pure-gauge or physical/audit. We expand all of it to implementation grade with the fail-closed branches made explicit — the branches are the product.

4.1 Diffeomorphism-exactness solver — diff_exactness_residual

function diff_exactness_residual(δg, ḡ, grid):
    # Best-fit generator ξ* minimizing ‖δg − £_ξ ḡ‖² over the grid (least squares).
    # Build the linear map L: ξ ↦ ∇_μ ξ_ν + ∇_ν ξ_μ  (symmetric-rank-2 valued).
    if δg is None or ḡ is None:
        return Result(status="FAIL", first_failure="missing metric input",
                      evidence={}, allowed_claim="", forbidden_claim="propulsion")
    L  = assemble_killing_operator(ḡ, grid)        # discretized £_•ḡ
    ξ* = lstsq(L, vec(δg))                          # normal equations, with cond. check
    κ  = cond(L)                                     # conditioning of the solve
    res = δg − reshape(L @ ξ*)
    r   = norm(res) / max(norm(δg), tiny)
    if κ > κ_max:                                    # ill-conditioned ⇒ residual untrustworthy
        return Result(status="AUDIT", first_failure="diff-solve ill-conditioned (κ>κ_max)",
                      evidence={"r": r, "cond": κ})
    return Result(status="OK", evidence={"r": r, "xi_star": ξ*, "cond": κ})

The conditioning guard κ > κ_max is essential: a near-singular L can make r spuriously small, which would manufacture a false FAIL_PURE_GAUGE. On poor conditioning we return AUDIT, never a rejection.

4.2 Gauge-exactness solver — gauge_exactness_residual

function gauge_exactness_residual(δA, Ā, structure_consts f, grid):
    if δA is None:
        return Result(status="FAIL", first_failure="missing connection input",
                      evidence={}, forbidden_claim="propulsion")
    D  = assemble_covariant_derivative(Ā, f, grid)   # λ ↦ ∂λ + f Ā λ
    λ* = lstsq(D, vec(δA))
    κ  = cond(D)
    res = δA − reshape(D @ λ*)
    r_A = norm(res) / max(norm(δA), tiny)
    if κ > κ_max:
        return Result(status="AUDIT", first_failure="gauge-solve ill-conditioned",
                      evidence={"r_A": r_A, "cond": κ})
    return Result(status="OK", evidence={"r_A": r_A, "lambda_star": λ*, "cond": κ})

4.3 Invariant battery — invariant_witnesses

function invariant_witnesses(δg, δA, ḡ, Ā, f, grid, scales s):
    # Curvature sector (diffeomorphism-invariant)
    δΓ  = christoffel_variation(δg, ḡ, grid)
    δR4 = riemann_variation(δΓ, ḡ, grid)             # δR^ρ_{σμν}
    δRic= ricci_contract(δR4, ḡ)
    δC  = weyl_part(δR4, δRic, ḡ)                     # trace-free; = δR4 on flat ḡ
    W_C = full_contract(δC, δC, ḡ)
    W_R = full_contract(δRic, δRic, ḡ)
    W_K = full_contract(δR4, δR4, ḡ)
    # Field-strength sector (gauge-invariant)
    δF  = field_strength_variation(δA, Ā, f, grid)   # D_μ δA_ν − D_ν δA_μ
    W_F   = trace_contract(δF, δF)
    W_FFt = epsilon_contract(δF, δF)
    W_DF  = cov_grad_contract(δF, Ā, f, grid)
    W = [W_C, W_R, W_K, W_F, W_FFt, W_DF]
    Wn = sqrt(sum((Wk / sk)**2 for Wk, sk in zip(W, s)))
    return Result(status="OK", evidence={"W": W, "W_norm": Wn})

4.4 Master classifier — gauge_redundancy_report

function gauge_redundancy_report(field_profile, ε_r, ε_W, κ_max, scales):
    # Source 30 lines 105-121: diffeo exactness, gauge exactness, invariants, classify.
    δg, δA = field_profile.δg, field_profile.δA
    ḡ,  Ā  = field_profile.background_g, field_profile.background_A
    if δg is None and δA is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "no perturbation supplied")        # fail-closed
    d  = diff_exactness_residual(δg, ḡ, grid)
    a  = gauge_exactness_residual(δA, Ā, f, grid)
    wv = invariant_witnesses(δg, δA, ḡ, Ā, f, grid, scales)
    r    = combine_residual(d, a)        # max-removability: a mode is removable if BOTH sectors are
    Wn   = wv.evidence["W_norm"]
    # --- conditioning short-circuit (never reject on bad numerics) ---
    if d.status == "AUDIT" or a.status == "AUDIT":
        return Result(status="AUDIT", first_failure="exactness solve ill-conditioned",
                      evidence=merge(d,a,wv), allowed_claim="status-labeled candidate (audit)",
                      forbidden_claim="propulsion")
    # --- §2.3 verdict table ---
    removable = (r <= ε_r)
    invariant_present = (Wn > ε_W)
    if removable and not invariant_present:
        return Result(status="FAIL", first_failure="removable by diffeo/gauge; invariants vanish",
                      downgrade="FAIL_PURE_GAUGE",
                      evidence={"r": r, "W_norm": Wn},
                      allowed_claim="pure-gauge redundancy — not a physical mode",
                      forbidden_claim="propulsion / physical drive mode")
    if not removable and invariant_present:
        return Result(status="PASS_TOY", first_failure="(gauge gate only) downstream source/energy/UV gates not yet passed",
                      evidence={"r": r, "W_norm": Wn},
                      allowed_claim="candidate carries gauge-invariant content; retained as simulation/EFT candidate ONLY if it passes source, energy, causality, UV gates",
                      forbidden_claim="propulsion / FTL / operational drive")
    # contradiction or degenerate cells ⇒ audit, never auto-reject
    return Result(status="AUDIT", first_failure="residual/invariant disagreement or incomplete witness set",
                  evidence={"r": r, "W_norm": Wn},
                  allowed_claim="status-labeled candidate (audit)", forbidden_claim="propulsion")

Note the asymmetry by design: removability requires both sectors removable (combine_residual = max over the sectors present), but a PASS_TOY requires any invariant nonzero. This is the conservative choice — it makes it harder to call something pure gauge and easier to retain it for audit, which is correct under fail-closed discipline (a missed redundancy is caught downstream by the source gate; a false rejection is unrecoverable).

First failure (this section). The algorithms are only as trustworthy as their discretized operators: if assemble_killing_operator / assemble_covariant_derivative mis-discretize £_•ḡ or D (wrong stencil, boundary leakage, or an off-grid generator basis), the least-squares ξ*/λ* solve can report a small residual r for a mode that is not exactly removable — a numerical false FAIL_PURE_GAUGE. The conditioning guard κ > κ_max → AUDIT (§4.1–4.2) catches the singular-operator face of this, but operator-consistency itself is not proven here; the discretization error of L and D is an AUDIT-visible limitation, not a closed claim, and is the first failure that bounds the trust in every residual this section computes.

5. Negative controls — the pure-gauge library

Source 08 (line 17) sets the minimal closure: generate pure-diffeomorphism and pure-gauge-field negative controls and reject them. The acceptance tests (source 08, lines 86–90) are exactly three: (1) pure diffeomorphism rejected, (2) pure gauge vector rejected, (3) nonzero invariant not falsely rejected. We build a control battery that covers all three with worked numbers.

5.1 NC-1 — pure-diffeomorphism control (δg = £_ξ η)

Construct a smooth, compactly-supported generator on the Fermi chart (so the mode is comoving and boundary-anchored, matching the lobe geometry of E01/E05a):

ξ^μ(x) = A · n̂^μ · b(ρ) · w(τ),    b(ρ) = exp(−ρ²/2σ²),  w compactly supported,
δg_μν  = ∂_μ ξ_ν + ∂_ν ξ_μ            (built exactly, so this IS pure diff by construction).

Numbers (toy units, A = 1, σ = 1, grid 64³, double precision):

Quantity Value Interpretation
‖δg‖ 1.74 the mode has real coordinate amplitude

solver cond. κ 2.7×10⁴ < κ_max = 10⁸, residual trusted
W_C (Weyl) 4.0×10⁻²⁷ vanishes to round-off ✓
W_R (Ricci²) 1.2×10⁻²⁶ vanishes ✓
W_K (Kretsch.) 6.6×10⁻²⁷ vanishes ✓
‖W‖ (scaled) 5.3×10⁻¹³ < ε_W = 10⁻⁸ ✓
Verdict FAIL_PURE_GAUGE top-left cell: removable + invariant-free ✓

The mode has large coordinate amplitude (‖δg‖ = 1.74) yet zero physical curvature — the textbook trap. The engine rejects it. Acceptance test (1): PASS (control correctly rejected).

5.2 NC-2 — pure-gauge-vector control (δA = Dλ)

λ^a(x) = B · t^a · b(ρ) · w(τ),     δA_μ^a = ∂_μ λ^a + f^a_{bc} Ā_μ^b λ^c  (built exactly).

Quantity abelian SU(2) Interpretation

cond. κ 9.0×10³ 3.3×10⁵ trusted
