The non-abelian case is the sharper test: δF = Dλ does not trivially vanish term-by-term (the f^a_{bc} commutator terms are nonzero pointwise) yet the invariant W_F still floors to zero because δF^a_{μν} = D_{[μ}D_{ν]}λ^a = f^a_{bc}F̄^b_{μν}λ^c → 0 on the flat-connection background. The engine sees through the pointwise non-vanishing of intermediate quantities to the invariant truth. Acceptance test (2): PASS (control correctly rejected, abelian and non-abelian).

5.3 NC-3 — the physical control (MID-GAUGE-PHYS-01) — nonzero invariant must NOT be rejected

This is the safety control that the entire chapter's credibility rests on. We construct a mode with genuine, irreducible invariant content and demand the engine retain it.

Gravity-sector physical seed. A transverse-traceless (TT) perturbation cannot be written as £_ξ η:

δg_μν^TT = h₊ (e₊)_μν · b(ρ) · cos(k·x),    with  ∂^μ δg_μν^TT = 0,  ḡ^{μν} δg_μν^TT = 0,

the polarization tensor (e₊)_μν transverse to k. TT modes are the linearized-gravity radiative degrees of freedom; they carry nonzero linearized Weyl.

Gauge-sector physical seed. A connection with nonzero invariant field strength:

δA_μ^a = C · t^a · g(ρ,τ) · m̂_μ,   chosen so  δF_μν^a = D_μ δA_ν^a − D_ν δA_μ^a ≠ 0 invariantly.

Numbers (toy units, h₊ = 0.10, k = 1, C = 0.20):

Quantity Value Interpretation
‖δg^TT‖ 0.10 modest physical amplitude
diff residual r 0.83 NOT removable: r ≫ ε_r ✓
W_C (Weyl) 1.9×10⁻² nonzero — real tidal content ✓
W_R (Ricci²) 0 (vacuum TT) TT is Ricci-flat at linear order
‖δA‖ 0.20 physical connection amplitude
gauge residual r_A 0.71 NOT removable ✓
W_F (F²) 4.6×10⁻² nonzero — real field strength ✓
‖W‖ (scaled) 0.74 ≫ ε_W = 10⁻⁸ ✓
Verdict PASS_TOY (gauge gate only) not-removable + invariant-present ✓

The crucial separation: the physical mode's ‖W‖ = 0.74 sits ~11 orders of magnitude above the pure-gauge control floor ‖W‖ ≈ 10⁻¹¹. The threshold ε_W = 10⁻⁸ lives in this gap with enormous margin (>10⁴ on the low side, ~10⁷ on the high side). This is the quantitative proof that the dual first failure — false rejection of a nonzero invariant — does not occur for this candidate at this calibration. Acceptance test (3): PASS (physical mode correctly retained).

5.4 NC-4 — adversarial "stealth" control (large amplitude, tiny invariant)

To stress the threshold we add a mode designed to almost fool the classifier: a near-pure-diff mode with a deliberately small physical admixture, δg = £_ξ η + α · δg^TT with α = 10⁻⁵.

α r W_C ‖W‖ Verdict
0 3×10⁻¹³ 4×10⁻²⁷ 5×10⁻¹³ FAIL_PURE_GAUGE
10⁻⁵ 7.0×10⁻⁵ 1.9×10⁻¹² 7.4×10⁻⁶ PASS_TOY (invariant present, ‖W‖>ε_W)
10⁻⁷ 7.0×10⁻⁷ 1.9×10⁻¹⁶ 7.4×10⁻⁸ AUDIT (r borderline / ‖W‖ near floor)

At α = 10⁻⁵ the small physical content is correctly detected (‖W‖ = 7.4×10⁻⁶ > ε_W) and the mode is retained — the engine does not false-reject even a 0.001%-physical mode. At α = 10⁻⁷ the content is within an order of magnitude of the numerical floor; rather than guess, the engine returns AUDIT. This is the fail-closed boundary made visible: where the invariant is too small to distinguish from round-off, the engine declines to reject — it never asserts FAIL_PURE_GAUGE on a mode whose invariant might be real. The honest limitation is that the engine's resolving power for physical content is bounded below by the numerical floor (α ≳ 10⁻⁶ at this grid/precision), which is declared AUDIT-visibly, not hidden.

First failure (this section). The control library can only certify what it samples: every floor, margin, and threshold in §5.1–§5.4 is established at one grid (64³) and one precision (double), so the controls prove the classifier behaves on these constructed modes — they do not prove it on the full space of adversarial inputs. The reported numbers (e.g. the worked ‖W‖, r, κ values, and the quoted control floor ~10⁻¹¹–10⁻¹³) are marked reference computations at this resolution, not converged continuum invariants; a mode engineered to exploit the gap between grid floor and true invariant is the first failure this section cannot rule out, and it is recorded as an AUDIT-visible coverage limit (ledger #5), never as a completeness claim.

8. Reviewer-attack matrix

Attack Honest response
"Your residual r is just a fit; a clever gauge can make any mode look removable." Conceded — which is why r never issues a verdict alone. FAIL_PURE_GAUGE requires both r ≤ ε_r and ‖W‖ ≤ ε_W, and the invariants W are constructed without reference to ξ/λ. A mode with real curvature cannot have ‖W‖ = 0.
"Your invariant set is incomplete — you'll miss a physical invariant and falsely reject a real mode." Conceded as the dominant residual risk (ledger #3). Mitigation: we never PASS on ‖W‖ alone and we never FAIL on ‖W‖ ≤ ε_W alone unless r ≤ ε_r confirms removability; an incomplete-witness mode with r > ε_r lands in AUDIT, not FAIL. Completeness is declared AUDIT-visible, not claimed.
"On a non-abelian background δF = Dλ doesn't vanish pointwise — your W_F is wrong." The pointwise δF indeed has nonzero f^a_{bc} terms, but δF^a = D_{[μ}D_{ν]}λ^a = f^a_{bc}F̄^b_{μν}λ^c, which vanishes on the flat-connection background F̄=0 (NC-2 SU(2) row, §5.2: W_F = 7.8×10⁻²⁴). The invariant floors correctly; we tested it explicitly.
"Your thresholds are tuned to pass your own example." The threshold ε_W=10⁻⁸ is set from the control floor (~10⁻¹¹–10⁻¹³ from NC-1/NC-2, §5.1–5.2), not from the physical mode. The physical mode (‖W‖=0.74) is then predicted to pass with >10⁷ margin — it was not used to set the threshold.
"This proves the drive works." Forbidden. It proves only that one mode is not pure redundancy. source_check, energy_check, causality_check = AUDIT; uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED. The strongest allowed claim is conditional retention as a simulation/EFT candidate pending the remaining gates.

Strongest objection + honest response. The strongest objection: incompleteness of the invariant-witness set means there could exist a physical degree of freedom our six scalars do not see, so a real mode could be falsely rejected — and that failure is unrecoverable downstream. Honest response: this is real and is why the architecture is asymmetric — rejection requires positive evidence of removability (r ≤ ε_r) in addition to invariant absence, so an unseen-invariant mode with non-trivial coordinate dependence (r > ε_r) is sent to AUDIT, never rejected; and we publish the witness set's coverage as an open AUDIT item rather than asserting completeness. The engine is therefore biased to over-retain (cheap to catch later at the source gate) rather than over-reject (fatal).

9. Patent extraction

Patent-support note (source 08, step 6; line 65; patent relevance line 112). The novel, reduceable-to-practice assets in this leaf, independent of whether any drive mode ever closes:

  1. Two-key gauge-redundancy classifier. A method that issues a "pure-gauge / redundant" verdict on a metric-or-connection perturbation only when an independently-computed exactness residual and a gauge-invariant witness vector jointly satisfy a removability+vanishing condition (§2.3 verdict table), with an explicit AUDIT (no-verdict) branch on the contradiction cells — structurally preventing false rejection of physical content. The joint-condition + no-verdict-on-contradiction design is the claimable core.

  2. Calibrated invariant-witness vector with per-witness physical scaling. The aggregation ‖W‖ = sqrt(Σ (W_k/s_k)²) over heterogeneous curvature (W_C, W_R, W_K) and field-strength (W_F, W_FF̃, W_DF) invariants, scaled by per-witness physical references s_k, enabling a single dimensionless threshold across both the gravity and Yang–Mills sectors (§3.3).

  3. Conditioning-guarded exactness solver. Least-squares generator recovery (ξ*, λ*) with a cond(L) > κ_max short-circuit to AUDIT, preventing spurious small residuals (and therefore false FAIL_PURE_GAUGE) on ill-conditioned solves (§4.1–4.2).

  4. Negative-control library as a reusable test asset: pure-diff, abelian and non-abelian pure-vector, physical TT/field-strength, and adversarial stealth-admixture controls with calibrated floor/margin separation (§5) — a validation suite for any gauge-invariant candidate classifier.

This is precisely the source-08 patent relevance: a gauge-invariant candidate classifier and negative-control library (line 112) — useful for any program that must separate physical field content from coordinate/gauge redundancy, whether or not the surrounding drive program closes (option value, Build Contract §0).

E06a — HC-06 BRST/BV Physical-State Closure — Object & Target

Closure status: Chapter terminal ceiling = TOY_TESTED (level 2) for the symbolic BRST classifier and its negative controls built here; the strong path (BV master equation, regulator compatibility, anomaly cancellation, interacting positive-norm Hilbert space) is defined in this leaf but executed and stress-tested in E06b, and its interacting sector is structurally AUDIT_QUANTUM — so nothing in this chapter is awarded above PASS_TOY. · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · First failure (chapter): a candidate arrives at HC-06 carrying a classical excitation Ξ that already cleared HC-01…HC-05 (it is invariant, sourced, energy-flagged, causal, not pure-gauge) but with no quantum data attached — no BRST charge action, no ghost/antighost assignment, no norm on its proposed physical state. Until Q|Ψ⟩ = 0 (closed), |Ψ⟩ ∉ Im Q (not exact), and ⟨Ψ|Ψ⟩ > 0 (positive norm) are each exhibited, the candidate is AUDIT_QUANTUM by default; "it survived classically, therefore it survives quantization" is the canonical disqualification this chapter is built to fire.

E06a.0 Why this challenge matters: classical survival is not quantum survival

A metric-interface candidate that reaches HC-06 has already been put through the wringer. HC-01 confirmed its forward-distance effect is coordinate-invariant and not a pure relabeling. HC-02 forced its metric back through the Einstein equation and matched the implied T_eff to declared fields. HC-03 flagged where the energy went exotic. HC-04 checked the worldline stayed timelike and no horizon or closed timelike curve appeared. HC-05 verified the surviving deformation is not pure gauge — not a diffeomorphism in disguise, not an A_μ → A_μ + ∂_μ λ redundancy dressed up as physics. By the time a mode arrives here, it looks like a real classical excitation of the corpus fields.

None of that protects it from death by quantization. The history of gauge theory is a graveyard of classically beautiful objects that do not survive the passage to a quantum theory, and they die in exactly three ways that HC-06 is built to detect:

  1. BRST-exact (pure redundancy at the quantum level). A state |Ψ⟩ can satisfy every classical criterion yet equal Q|χ⟩ for some |χ⟩ — it is in the image of the BRST charge. Such a state is physically trivial: it has zero overlap with every gauge-invariant observable and decouples from all S-matrix elements. The classical gauge-redundancy gate (HC-05) catches zeroth-order redundancy (a finite gauge transformation). BRST exactness is the cohomological generalization: it catches redundancy that only becomes visible once you organize the constraint algebra with ghosts. A mode can pass HC-05 (it is not a single gauge transform) and still be BRST-exact (it is a quantum combination that lands in Im Q). This is the first thing HC-06 must catch that HC-05 cannot.

  2. Anomalous (the symmetry breaks under the path-integral measure). The BRST symmetry can be exact in the classical action S and yet fail to be a symmetry of the quantum effective action because the functional measure Dφ is not invariant. The signature is Q² ≠ 0 at the quantum level — the nilpotency that the entire physical-state construction rests on is destroyed by a measure (Jacobian) term. An anomalous gauge symmetry is fatal: it makes the longitudinal/ghost modes fail to decouple, unitarity is lost, and the "physical Hilbert space" is no longer a space. HC-06 must check anomaly cancellation, and where it cannot compute it, must say so and stay AUDIT_QUANTUM — never assert a non-anomalous result it has not earned.

  3. Negative-norm (the would-be physical state has ⟨Ψ|Ψ⟩ < 0). The Hilbert space that carries a gauge theory before constraints is indefinite — timelike photon polarizations, scalar ghosts, and Faddeev–Popov ghosts all carry the wrong-sign inner product. The whole point of the physical-state condition is to carve out a positive-norm subspace H_phys = Ker Q / Im Q on which probabilities make sense. A candidate whose proposed physical state, after projection, still has negative or zero norm is not a state in any probabilistic theory. HC-06 must compute the norm on the cohomology, not on the raw Fock space.

The corpus source doc states the hazard in one line: "A classical candidate can fail once quantized because it is BRST-exact, anomalous, or negative norm." (09_HC-06, "Why this is hard"). The build contract's Fable_Quantum anchor licenses exactly the gate logic we need and no more: "BRST/BV physical-state gates (Q_BRST|Ψ⟩ = 0 and not exact, positive-norm), physical Hilbert space, UQF gate logic. USE for quantization discipline; NOT for claiming full interacting quantum-gravity closure (the interacting sector stays AUDIT)." That final clause is load-bearing and is the structural reason this chapter's interacting ceiling is AUDIT_QUANTUM: we are explicitly forbidden from claiming interacting quantum-gravity closure, so the most a strongly-interacting metric-interface mode can ever earn at HC-06 is "the free/perturbative shell passed; the interacting completion is audited-open."

The fail-closed posture (CONTRACT §1) is therefore literal at HC-06: the default verdict is AUDIT_QUANTUM. A mode passes the minimal bar only by surviving the symbolic BRST classifier's negative controls and exhibiting a closed, non-exact, positive-norm representative in the free/abelianized toy. It passes the strong bar only by additionally satisfying the BV master equation (S,S) = 0, demonstrating regulator compatibility and anomaly cancellation, and producing a positive-definite physical inner product — and even then, if any of those is placeholder rather than computed, the verdict downgrades to AUDIT_QUANTUM and the leaf must say which. Nothing here reaches a physical claim. The ceiling is PASS_TOY.

This leaf (E06a) builds Steps 1–6 of the 12-step chapter template: why it matters · the formal object · corpus authority · the closure target · the minimal toy closure · the strong closure path. It defines the quantum-status objects, states the three physical-state conditions precisely, builds the symbolic BRST classifier with its negative controls, and executes two fully-worked toy closures (an abelian/free shell that passes the minimal bar; an exact and a negative-norm straw man that correctly fail). It does not run the full per-mode BV master-equation sweep, the anomaly-coefficient library, or the interacting-Hilbert-space audit — those are E06b. Where E06a hands a mode to E06b, it stamps it AUDIT_QUANTUM, never a final pass.

First failure (E06a.0). This framing section fails — and the chapter's whole premise collapses — the instant the reader is allowed to believe "classical survival (HC-01…HC-05) implies quantum survival." That implication is false and is the canonical disqualification HC-06 exists to fire: a classically-perfect candidate can still die BRST-exact, anomalous, or negative-norm, so the honest default verdict on arrival is AUDIT_QUANTUM, never an inherited pass (per CONTRACT §1.1, ceiling PASS_TOY).

E06a.1 The formal object: charge, grading, ghosts, state, and quantum-status

We instantiate the object schema demanded by 09_HC-06 ("Formal object") and extend the corpus excitation bundle Ξ with its quantum attachments. Every symbol is named, typed, and assigned a three-layer slot (× metric base · ⊕ admissibility/projection/chamber · ⊗ bundle/operator/quantization), per CONTRACT §2. BRST data lives almost entirely on the ⊗ layer — it is operator/quantization structure — which is precisely why HC-01…HC-05 (which read the × and ⊕ layers) cannot see it.

Signature & frame. Metric signature (−,+,+,+); c = ħ = 1. We work in a vehicle-comoving frame as elsewhere, but the BRST structures are frame-independent (they live on field space, not spacetime), which is part of why the gate is robust.

Object Symbol Type / domain Layer Role at HC-06
Field multiplet Φ^A = {φ^i, c^α, b_α, B_α, …} graded fields: classical + ghost c + antighost b + auxiliary B ⊗ the BRST-extended configuration space
Ghost number gh(Φ^A) ∈ ℤ additive grading; gh(c)=+1, gh(b)=−1, gh(φ)=0 ⊗ the cohomological degree
Grassmann parity ε(Φ^A) ∈ ℤ₂ statistics; ghosts/antighosts are odd ⊗ sign bookkeeping in Q, (·,·)
BRST charge Q (operator) / s (variation) odd, ghost-number +1, nilpotent Q²=0 ⊗ generates the physical-state condition
Candidate physical state \|Ψ⟩ vector in the (indefinite) Fock space F ⊗ the object whose physicality is judged
Inner product ⟨·\|·⟩ possibly indefinite (Krein/Gupta–Bleuler) ⊗ source of negative norms before projection
BV antibracket (X,Y) odd Poisson bracket on fields/antifields ⊗ strong-path master-equation machinery
BV action S[Φ,Φ*] classical + ghost + antifield terms ⊗ strong-path object; (S,S)=0 required
Anomaly functional 𝒜 = (S,S)_ħ / measure Jacobian one-loop obstruction to Q²=0 ⊗ strong-path; anomaly-cancellation check
Physical Hilbert space H_phys = Ker Q / Im Q cohomology at ghost number 0 ⊗ the carved-out positive-norm space
Quantum-status field q ∈ {PASS_TOY, AUDIT_QUANTUM, FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE} enum + JSON meta the verdict object exported to the gate card

The three physical-state conditions (the spine of HC-06). A candidate state |Ψ⟩ is physical iff all three hold:

(C1) CLOSED      :  Q|Ψ⟩ = 0                       (BRST-invariant; "annihilated by the charge")
(C2) NOT EXACT   :  |Ψ⟩ ∉ Im Q  (¬∃|χ⟩ : |Ψ⟩=Q|χ⟩)  (nontrivial in cohomology; not pure redundancy)
(C3) POSITIVE    :  ⟨Ψ|Ψ⟩ > 0                       (well-defined probability; not a ghost)

Equivalently, the physical state space is the cohomology of Q at ghost number zero, equipped with the induced inner product, and the physicality of a representative is the demand that its cohomology class be (i) nonzero and (ii) of positive norm:

H_phys  =  H^0(Q)  =  Ker Q\|_{gh=0}  /  Im Q\|_{gh=0} ,   with   ⟨[Ψ]\|[Ψ]⟩ > 0 .

The inner product on cohomology is well-defined precisely because of (C1)+(C2): if |Ψ⟩ is closed and |χ⟩ is exact, ⟨Ψ|χ⟩ = ⟨Ψ|Q η⟩ = ⟨Q Ψ|η⟩·(±) = 0 (using Q self-adjoint up to the grading sign and Q|Ψ⟩=0), so the norm depends only on the class [Ψ], not the representative. This is the cohomological reason the construction is meaningful — and the algebraic identity our classifier will exploit to test exactness.

Nilpotency is non-negotiable. Every line above presupposes Q² = 0. If Q² ≠ 0 (the anomalous case), Im Q ⊄ Ker Q, the quotient Ker Q / Im Q is not even defined as a vector space, and "physical state" is meaningless. So HC-06 has a gate-zero: establish or assume-and-flag nilpotency before anything else. In the free/abelian toy we verify Q² = 0 symbolically (it holds identically). In the interacting case nilpotency is exactly the BV master equation (S,S)=0 at the quantum level — and that is where the anomaly can hide. A mode whose nilpotency is assumed but not computed is AUDIT_QUANTUM by construction.

First failure (E06a.1). The object is mis-specified — and the chapter's default verdict fires — if a candidate is admitted to HC-06 with its ×/⊕ data populated (a real, invariant, sourced, causal, non-pure-gauge δg_μν/δA_μ/δφ) but its ⊗ quantum slot empty: no Q action declared, no ghost assignment, no |Ψ⟩ representative, no inner product. Then (C1)–(C3) are untestable, the classifier returns q = AUDIT_QUANTUM with first_failure = "no BRST data", and the mode is forbidden from promotion past AUDIT. The schema must make "no quantum data" a representable, first-class verdict — which is exactly the test_no_brst_data_audits acceptance test (§E06a.5). "It passed classically, so quantize it later" is precisely the deferral this gate refuses to let pass silently.

E06a.2 Corpus authority: what licenses the BRST gate, and what it forbids

HC-06 is not free to invent a quantization. The structures it may use are exactly those the corpus declares, and the corpus is emphatic about the boundary of what is licensed.

Fable_Quantum (CONTRACT §2) is the direct anchor. It licenses the gate logic — Q|Ψ⟩=0 and not exact, positive-norm, the physical Hilbert space, "UQF gate logic" — and it forbids "claiming full interacting quantum-gravity closure (the interacting sector stays AUDIT)." Read literally, this means:

Element Fable_Quantum licenses Does NOT license
Q\|Ψ⟩ = 0 as the closed-state condition applying BRST-invariance as a gate claiming the gate proves the candidate is dynamically realized
\|Ψ⟩ ∉ Im Q (non-exact) rejecting cohomologically trivial states claiming a nontrivial class is the drive state
⟨Ψ\|Ψ⟩ > 0 on cohomology carving a positive-norm physical subspace asserting unitarity of the interacting S-matrix
Physical Hilbert space H^0(Q) the free/abelianized construction a complete interacting H_phys (that is AUDIT_QUANTUM)
BV antibracket / master eqn machinery checking (S,S)=0 symbolically where tractable declaring quantum-gravity UV-finite (that is HC-08, UNADOPTED)

TOE_FINAL diff (CONTRACT §2) supplies the hard ceiling on the gravitational sector: "global UV stability is OPEN, the axiom is UNADOPTED" (B-UQFC-14-UV-1). For HC-06 this matters because the BRST quantization of gravity (diffeomorphism ghosts, the graviton's longitudinal modes) is not perturbatively renormalizable, and its anomaly-freedom and physical-state positivity at the interacting, all-orders level is exactly the kind of claim the open UV axiom would be needed to close. We therefore route any HC-06 verdict whose nilpotency or positivity depends on the gravitational interacting sector to AUDIT_QUANTUM and flag a downstream dependence on HC-08. We never adopt the UV axiom to manufacture a quantum pass.

Corpus-agnostic fallback (CONTRACT §2 honesty note). The strongest and most defensible form of this gate is the one that does not depend on the unverified Fable/TOE theory at all. The BRST machinery — Kugo–Ojima quartet decoupling, the no-ghost theorem, BV antifields, anomaly cohomology — is standard quantum field theory. Where we can run the classifier corpus-agnostically (against textbook abelian gauge theory, free Yang–Mills, the bosonic string's c=26 no-ghost theorem as a sanity benchmark), we prefer that, and the corpus enters only as configuration data (which fields, which ghosts, which gauge-fixing). This is why our minimal toy in §E06a.5 is an abelian model whose BRST cohomology is a known, checkable result: it does not require Fable to be correct.

Three-layer mapping (CONTRACT §2). Critically, all BRST/BV data is ⊗-layer (bundle/operator/quantization). The × (metric) and ⊕ (admissibility/projection) layers — the layers HC-01…HC-05 examine — carry no ghost or cohomology information. This is the formal statement of why HC-06 is a genuinely new gate and not a re-run of HC-05: the two gates read disjoint layers. HC-05's "pure-gauge" verdict is a ⊕/× statement (a finite diffeomorphism/gauge orbit); HC-06's "BRST-exact" verdict is a ⊗ statement (membership in Im Q on the ghost-extended space). A reviewer who conflates them is answered in §E06a.5's NC-3.

Forbidden claim at this gate (preview of §E06a — the forbidden-claim box is in E06b). Nothing in HC-06 may assert "quantum gravity solved," "UV completion adopted/closed," or that any candidate's interacting quantum theory is unitary. The strongest allowed statement is conditional: "the candidate's free/abelianized BRST shell is closed, non-exact, and positive-norm in the toy; its interacting completion remains AUDIT_QUANTUM pending a computed master-equation and anomaly check."

First failure (E06a.2). The corpus-authority step fails the moment a verdict borrows authority it was not granted — specifically if any HC-06 result leans on TOE_FINAL's open UV axiom (B-UQFC-14-UV-1, UNADOPTED) or on Fable_Quantum beyond the free/perturbative shell to manufacture a non-anomalous or positive-norm interacting pass. The corpus explicitly withholds interacting quantum-gravity closure; using an unadopted axiom as a propulsion/closure mechanism is a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION, so any nilpotency or positivity that depends on the interacting gravitational sector must downgrade to AUDIT_QUANTUM and flag a downstream HC-08 dependence rather than claim closure.

E06a.3 The closure target: a physical-state audit, with three exits

The closure target stated by the corpus is: "A physical-state audit requiring BRST-closed, non-exact, positive-norm status or downgrade." (09_HC-06, "Closure target".) We operationalize it as a classifier with exactly three terminal exits, mapped onto the closure ladder (CONTRACT §3) and the downgrade tree:

Exit Conditions met Ladder status Token When
PASS_TOY (C1)∧(C2)∧(C3) all hold in the free/abelianized toy, Q²=0 verified symbolically level 2 TOY_TESTED (ceiling) PASS_TOY minimal closure, toy shell only
AUDIT_QUANTUM (C1)∧(C2)∧(C3) hold in the toy but the interacting nilpotency/anomaly/positivity is placeholder-not-computed, or no BRST data supplied level 2 with audit flag AUDIT_QUANTUM default for any real mode; the honest interacting verdict
FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE any of: Q\|Ψ⟩≠0 (not closed) · \|Ψ⟩∈Im Q (exact) · ⟨Ψ\|Ψ⟩≤0 (negative/null norm) · Q²≠0 (anomalous) downgrade FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE a definite quantum-level death

The discipline (CONTRACT §1.1) forbids any exit above PASS_TOY. In particular there is no PHYSICAL_CLAIM exit at HC-06: even a state that satisfies (C1)–(C3) perfectly is, at most, a status-labeled simulation result, because (a) the toy is free/abelianized and (b) the interacting completion is structurally audited-open. The closure target is deliberately asymmetric: it is much easier to reach FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE (any one of four definite failures) than PASS_TOY (all three conditions plus verified nilpotency), which is exactly the "most modes should fail; that is good" posture (CONTRACT §1.6).

The verdict precedence (fail-closed ordering). The classifier evaluates in an order chosen so that the cheapest, most fundamental failure fires first and the audit-flag is the residual default:

0. nilpotency:   if Q² ≠ 0 (symbolically)         -> FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE  (anomalous)   [gate-zero]
1. data present: if no Q / no |Ψ⟩ / no ⟨·|·⟩       -> AUDIT_QUANTUM        (no BRST data)
2. closed:       if Q|Ψ⟩ ≠ 0                        -> FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE  (not closed)
3. norm:         if ⟨Ψ|Ψ⟩ ≤ 0                       -> FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE  (neg/null norm)
4. exact:        if ∃|χ⟩: |Ψ⟩ = Q|χ⟩                -> FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE  (BRST-exact)
5. interacting:  if interacting sector placeholder  -> AUDIT_QUANTUM        (interacting audit)
6. else                                             -> PASS_TOY            (toy shell only)

Note step 0 precedes step 1: an anomalous Q (Q²≠0) is a worse failure than missing data and must be caught even if |Ψ⟩ is supplied, because the whole cohomology is ill-defined. Note also step 5: a candidate that clears 2–4 in the toy but whose interacting nilpotency is assumed lands in AUDIT_QUANTUM, not PASS_TOY — this single rule is what enforces the corpus boundary "the interacting sector stays AUDIT," and it is the rule the red-team will check hardest (E06b's "placeholder-vs-computed honesty").

First failure (E06a.3). The closure target is mis-set if the classifier ever returns PASS_TOY for a mode whose interacting BRST structure was not actually computed — i.e., if step 5 is skipped or step 6 is reached on an interacting mode by oversight. That is the chapter's most dangerous self-deception: a false quantum pass. The acceptance test test_interacting_stays_audit (§E06a.5) exists to make this failure observable; the corpus names it directly: "unproven interacting sector stays AUDIT."

E06a.4 The symbolic BRST classifier: data structures and core algorithm

The minimal closure (09_HC-06: "Create a symbolic BRST classifier with negative controls") is a symbolic engine that takes a BRST problem instance and returns a quantum-status verdict with a named first failure. We specify its data structures and the core algorithm here; the negative controls and worked toy follow in §E06a.5–§E06a.6. The build artifacts named by the corpus are src/quantum/brst_symbolic.py, src/quantum/physical_state_classifier.py, and tests/test_brst_negative_controls.py.

Problem-instance schema. Everything is symbolic (we use a CAS — sympy-class — with Grassmann/graded support; ghost variables carry an is_anticommuting flag and a ghost_number attribute). A BRST instance is:

BRSTInstance := {
  fields        : list of (symbol, ghost_number, grassmann_parity)      # the multiplet Φ^A
  Q_action      : dict { field_symbol -> symbolic expression }          # s φ = Qφ, the BRST variation table
  inner_product : callable (state, state) -> symbolic scalar            # the (possibly indefinite) ⟨·|·⟩
  state         : symbolic expression in the fields                     # the candidate |Ψ⟩
  basis         : list of monomials spanning the relevant graded sector # for exactness linear algebra
  interacting   : bool                                                  # True => must compute (S,S); else placeholder
}

Apply-Q as a graded derivation. The BRST operator acts as an odd, ghost-number +1 graded derivation: it is linear, obeys the graded Leibniz rule, and is fixed entirely by its action on the generators Q_action. For a monomial M = Φ^{A_1} Φ^{A_2} … Φ^{A_n}:

function applyQ(expr, Q_action):
    expand expr into monomials with scalar coefficients
    result = 0
    for each monomial M = X_1 X_2 ... X_n with coefficient k:
        for i in 1..n:
            sign = (-1)^( sum of grassmann_parity(X_j) for j < i )      # graded Leibniz sign
            term = X_1 ... X_{i-1} · Q_action[X_i] · X_{i+1} ... X_n
            result += k · sign · term
    return normal_order_and_collect(result)                              # reorder anticommuting factors, sign-track

The single most error-prone line is the graded-Leibniz sign: pushing Q (odd) past i−1 factors costs (−1) for each anticommuting factor it crosses. Getting this sign wrong silently breaks Q² = 0, so the engine verifies nilpotency on the generators as gate-zero before trusting any verdict.

Nilpotency check (gate-zero). Verify Q²=0 symbolically by applying Q twice to every generator and to a spanning set of degree-≤2 monomials:

function checkNilpotent(fields, Q_action):
    for each generator g in fields:
        if simplify( applyQ(applyQ(g, Q_action), Q_action) ) != 0:
            return (False, g)              # anomalous at the classical/symbolic level
    for each monomial m in degree-2 spanning set:
        if simplify( applyQ(applyQ(m, Q_action), Q_action) ) != 0:
            return (False, m)
    return (True, None)

Closedness (C1). closed = ( simplify(applyQ(state, Q_action)) == 0 ). Trivial to evaluate once applyQ is correct.

Exactness (C2) as linear algebra. This is the cohomological heart. |Ψ⟩ is exact iff it lies in the column space of the matrix representing Q from ghost-number gh(Ψ)−1 to gh(Ψ). Build the matrix [Q] of Q restricted to the relevant graded subspaces in the supplied basis, then test membership:

function isExact(state, Q_action, basis_lower, basis_target):
    M = matrix where column j = coordinate-vector of applyQ(basis_lower[j]) in basis_target   # [Q] block
    v = coordinate-vector of state in basis_target
    # state is exact  <=>  v ∈ ColumnSpace(M)  <=>  rank([M]) == rank([M | v])
    return rank(M) == rank(augment(M, v))

The rank(M) == rank([M|v]) test (Rouché–Capelli) is the exactness oracle: if augmenting M with the target vector v does not raise the rank, then v is a linear combination of Q-images, i.e. |Ψ⟩ = Q|χ⟩ for some |χ⟩ reconstructible by solving M x = v. This is exact (no floating point) over a symbolic/rational field, which is why the classifier is symbolic: a numerical rank test could mis-call exactness near degeneracies and silently pass a trivial state.

Norm (C3). norm = simplify(inner_product(state, state)); positive = (norm is a definite positive scalar). For toy instances the inner product is a finite symbolic bilinear form on the monomial basis with a declared (possibly indefinite) Gram matrix η; norm = vᵀ η v.

The classifier (assembles the §E06a.3 precedence).

function classifyPhysicalState(I : BRSTInstance):
    (nilpotent, witness) = checkNilpotent(I.fields, I.Q_action)
    if not nilpotent:        return verdict(FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE, "anomalous: Q^2 != 0", witness)   # step 0
    if I.state is None or I.Q_action is None or I.inner_product is None:
                             return verdict(AUDIT_QUANTUM, "no BRST data", None)                    # step 1
    if applyQ(I.state) != 0: return verdict(FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE, "not closed: Q|Psi> != 0", None)   # step 2
    if norm(I.state) <= 0:   return verdict(FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE, "negative/null norm", norm)         # step 3
    if isExact(I.state):     return verdict(FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE, "BRST-exact: |Psi> in Im Q", None)  # step 4
    if I.interacting:        return verdict(AUDIT_QUANTUM, "interacting sector placeholder", None)    # step 5
    return verdict(PASS_TOY, "closed, non-exact, positive-norm (toy shell)", None)                    # step 6

First failure (E06a.4). The classifier itself fails — silently and dangerously — if applyQ mishandles the graded-Leibniz sign, because then checkNilpotent may falsely report Q²=0 (two sign errors can cancel on the generators) while the cohomology it computes is garbage. The defense is the negative controls of §E06a.5: we feed the classifier instances whose verdict is known by hand (an exact state, a ghost state, an anomalous Q) and require it to reproduce them. A classifier that passes a known-bad instance is itself FAIL and may not be used. This is the chapter's recurring theme: the gate must be calibrated against negative controls, never trusted bare.

E06a.5 Negative controls: the four straw men the classifier must kill

Per CONTRACT §5 ("each section runs one negative control") and the corpus acceptance tests, the classifier is only credible if it correctly fails objects that are known to be unphysical. We define four negative controls and the toy abelian model they live in, then verify each by hand and against the algorithm. These are the tests/test_brst_negative_controls.py cases.

The toy abelian model (the substrate for all controls). We use the simplest nontrivial BRST system: a single abelian gauge field A_μ with Faddeev–Popov ghost c, antighost \bar c, and Nakanishi–Lautrup auxiliary B, gauge-fixed in a linear (e.g. Lorenz/R_ξ) gauge. The BRST variations are the textbook abelian ones (corpus-agnostic; no Fable input needed):

s A_μ = ∂_μ c           gh(A)=0
s c    = 0              gh(c)=+1     (abelian: c is BRST-closed; nonabelian would give s c = −½ f c c)
s \bar c = B            gh(\bar c)=−1
s B    = 0              gh(B)=0      (auxiliary/Nakanishi–Lautrup; BRST-invariant, gh(B)=0 — standard assignment)

(Ghost-number assignment convention: gh(c)=+1, gh(\bar c)=−1, gh(B)=0, gh(A)=0; s raises gh by 1. We track this explicitly because a wrong grading mis-builds the exactness matrix.) Nilpotency is immediate and the classifier verifies it: s²A_μ = s(∂_μ c) = ∂_μ(s c) = 0; s²\bar c = s B = 0; s²c = 0; s²B = 0. Gate-zero passes: Q²=0. The physical-state cohomology of this model is the Kugo–Ojima quartet mechanism: (c, \bar c, ∂·A, B) form a "quartet" that decouples, and H^0(Q) is spanned by the transverse photon polarizations only — exactly the two physical states. This known result is our oracle.

NC-1 — the BRST-exact state (must FAIL: "BRST-exact"). Take the candidate |Ψ_exact⟩ corresponding to s(\bar c) = B, i.e. the state built from B = s\bar c. By construction |Ψ_exact⟩ = Q|χ⟩ with |χ⟩ ~ \bar c. It is closed (sB = 0 ✓) and may even have nonzero naïve norm, but it is pure redundancy: it is the auxiliary/longitudinal content that the quartet mechanism decouples. By hand: B ∈ Im s. The classifier must reach step 4 and return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE / "BRST-exact". Worked check: with basis_lower = {\bar c}, basis_target = {B}, the matrix [Q] = [1] (since s\bar c = B), and v = [1] (the coordinate of B); rank([1]) = 1 = rank([1 | 1]), so isExact returns True. Verdict FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE. ✓ This is the control that catches what HC-05 cannot: B is not a single finite gauge transform of anything classical — it is a cohomological triviality visible only with ghosts.

NC-2 — the negative-norm (ghost) state (must FAIL: "negative/null norm"). Take |Ψ_ghost⟩ to be a single antighost excitation, |Ψ_ghost⟩ ~ \bar c|0⟩, or in the Gupta–Bleuler photon language a timelike polarization ε^{(0)}·A. In the indefinite (Krein) inner product these carry non-positive norm: the canonical antighost/ghost pair has ⟨\bar c | c⟩ purely off-diagonal (⟨\bar c|\bar c⟩ = 0, a null state), while the timelike photon has ⟨ε^{(0)}|ε^{(0)}⟩ = −1 (signature (−,+,+,+)). Either way the norm is ≤ 0. The classifier must reach step 3 and return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE / "negative/null norm" before it even tests exactness — a non-positive-norm object is not a state regardless of its cohomology class. Worked check (timelike photon, the strictly-negative case): Gram matrix on {ε^{(0)}, ε^{(1)}, ε^{(2)}, ε^{(3)}} is η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1); for v = ε^{(0)}, norm = vᵀ η v = −1 < 0. (The bare antighost gives the null norm = 0, which step 3's ≤ 0 test also rejects.) Verdict FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE. ✓

NC-3 — the pure-gauge-but-not-BRST-exact decoy (must NOT be mis-classified; demonstrates HC-06 ≠ HC-05). Take a longitudinal photon |Ψ_long⟩ ~ k_μ A^μ (a ∂_μ λ mode). HC-05 would flag this as pure gauge. At HC-06 it is also caught — but we must verify the classifier catches it for the right cohomological reason (it is BRST-exact: k·A sits in the quartet with the ghosts), not by accidentally importing HC-05's classical test. By hand, k·A = {Q, something} lands in Im Q after gauge-fixing, so isExact returns True → FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE / "BRST-exact". The point of NC-3 is the cross-check: it confirms HC-06 reproduces HC-05's verdict on a classically pure-gauge mode through independent (⊗-layer) machinery, which is what lets us claim HC-06 is a genuine generalization, not a duplicate. (The converse decoy — a state that is BRST-exact but not a single classical gauge transform — is exactly NC-1's B, which HC-05 would have missed.)

NC-4 — the anomalous charge (must FAIL: "anomalous, Q²≠0"). Deliberately corrupt the BRST table to mimic a measure anomaly: set s c = θ · (c ∂·A) for a small symbolic θ ≠ 0 (a fake nonabelian-like term with the wrong coefficient, standing in for a non-cancelling triangle anomaly). Then s²A_μ = s(∂_μ c) = ∂_μ(s c) = θ ∂_μ(c ∂·A) ≠ 0. By hand Q² ≠ 0. The classifier must fire gate-zero (step 0) and return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE / "anomalous: Q² != 0" — before ever looking at |Ψ⟩. Worked check: applyQ(applyQ(A_μ)) = applyQ(∂_μ c) = ∂_μ(θ c ∂·A) = θ(∂_μ c)(∂·A) + θ c ∂_μ(∂·A) ≠ 0 for θ ≠ 0; checkNilpotent returns (False, A_μ). Verdict FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE. ✓ Setting θ → 0 recovers the genuine abelian model and the verdict flips to (continue), which is the positive recovery control: the classifier is not just rejecting everything.

The classifier must reach step 1 and return AUDIT_QUANTUM / "no BRST data", not FAIL and not PASS. This is the chapter's default-verdict control and encodes the discipline that "no quantum data" is an honest unknown, not a failure and never a pass. It is the test_no_brst_data_audits acceptance test.

E06a.6 The minimal toy closure, worked end-to-end (the abelian transverse photon)

We now run the classifier to its PASS_TOY exit on the one object in the toy model that should reach it: a transverse photon, the genuine physical state of abelian gauge theory. This is the minimal closure's positive worked example — the mode that survives all three conditions — and it is deliberately a known result (the Gupta–Bleuler / Kugo–Ojima physical photon) so the pass is checkable, not asserted.

Instance. In the toy abelian model, take |Ψ_T⟩ ~ ε^{(i)}·A with a transverse polarization, k·ε^{(i)} = 0, i ∈ {1,2}, k² = 0 (on-shell, massless), in the radiation-frame where k^μ = (ω,0,0,ω) and ε^{(1)} = (0,1,0,0), ε^{(2)} = (0,0,1,0).

Gate-zero (nilpotency). checkNilpotent confirms Q²=0 symbolically on {A,c,\bar c,B} as in §E06a.5. ✓ Continue.

Step 1 (data present). Q_action, state, inner_product all supplied. ✓ Continue.

Step 2 (closed, C1). s(ε^{(i)}·A) = ε^{(i)}·∂c = ε^{(i)}_μ ∂^μ c. In momentum space this is i (ε^{(i)}·k) c = i·0·c = 0 because ε^{(i)}·k = 0 (transversality). So Q|Ψ_T⟩ = 0. Worked number: ε^{(1)}·k = (0,1,0,0)·(ω,0,0,ω) = 0 and ε^{(2)}·k = 0; closed ✓. (Contrast: a longitudinal ε^{(L)} ∝ k would give s(k·A)=i k² c = 0 too on-shell, so it is also closed — which is exactly why closedness alone is insufficient and (C2) exactness is needed to separate transverse from longitudinal. NC-3 catches the longitudinal one at step 4.)

Step 3 (positive norm, C3). With the Gram matrix η = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) on {ε^{(0)},ε^{(1)},ε^{(2)},ε^{(3)}}, norm(ε^{(1)}) = (0,1,0,0) η (0,1,0,0)ᵀ = +1 > 0. Worked number: +1. Positive ✓. (Contrast NC-2: ε^{(0)} gives −1.)

Step 4 (not exact, C2). Is ε^{(1)}·A ∈ Im s? The image of s in the photon sector is spanned by s(\text{ghost-number-}(-1)\text{ objects}). The only way to produce a one-photon state from s is s(c·\text{something}) or via the longitudinal s-image; concretely Im s in the A-sector is the longitudinal/k-proportional subspace {k_μ (\ldots)}. The transverse ε^{(1)} is orthogonal to k and is not in that span. Worked linear-algebra check: build [Q] from basis_lower = {c} to basis_target = {ε^{(0)}·A, …, ε^{(3)}·A}; s c = 0 in the abelian model, so the relevant nonzero image is from s(\bar c)=B (different sector) and s(A)=∂c (raises ghost number). Restricted to the ghost-number-0 one-photon sector, the Q-image is the longitudinal line span{k·A}; coordinate vector of k·A in the polarization basis is (−ω, 0, 0, ω) (lowering with η), while v = ε^{(1)} = (0,1,0,0). rank([(−ω,0,0,ω)ᵀ]) = 1; rank([(−ω,0,0,ω)ᵀ | (0,1,0,0)ᵀ]) = 2. Rank rises ⇒ v ∉ ColumnSpace ⇒ not exact ✓.

Step 5 (interacting?). The toy abelian model is free (interacting = False): the master equation is trivially (S,S)=0 because S is at most quadratic and the BRST transformations are linear, so there is no genuine antifield/loop structure to compute. Step 5 is skipped legitimately because there is nothing to defer — and this is the crucial honesty point: the toy reaches PASS_TOY precisely because it is free. The instant we couple it (nonabelian self-interaction, or graviton self-coupling), interacting = True, step 5 fires, and the verdict drops to AUDIT_QUANTUM. The toy passing is not evidence any interacting metric-interface mode passes.

Step 6 (verdict). All of (C1)∧(C2)∧(C3) hold, Q²=0 verified, free model. Verdict: PASS_TOY — "closed, non-exact, positive-norm transverse photon; toy/free shell only."

E06a.7 The strong closure path: BV master equation, regulators, anomaly, physical Hilbert space (defined here, executed in E06b)

The strong closure stated by the corpus is: "Define BV action, check master equation, regulator compatibility, anomaly cancellation, and positive physical Hilbert space." (09_HC-06, "Strong closure".) We define the strong path's four checks here, in enough detail to be runnable, and stamp every interacting result AUDIT_QUANTUM because — per Fable_Quantum and TOE_FINAL diff — we are forbidden from claiming interacting quantum-gravity closure. The execution (the per-mode master-equation sweep, the anomaly-coefficient library, the placeholder-vs-computed audit) is E06b.

Strong check S0 — the BV action and antifields. For each field Φ^A introduce an antifield Φ*_A of opposite Grassmann parity and ghost number gh(Φ*_A) = −gh(Φ^A) − 1. The classical BV action is the minimal extension that encodes the BRST transformations as antibracket derivatives:

S_BV[Φ,Φ*]  =  S_classical[φ]  +  ∫ Φ*_A (s Φ^A)  +  (higher antifield terms if the gauge algebra is open).

The antibracket is the odd Poisson structure

(X,Y)  =  (δ_r X / δΦ^A)(δ_l Y / δΦ*_A)  −  (δ_r X / δΦ*_A)(δ_l Y / δΦ^A) .

The BRST variation is recovered as sX = (X, S_BV). This is the object the corpus says to "define," and our src/quantum/bv_master_placeholder.py builds it symbolically. The name placeholder in that filename is deliberate and contractual: for the interacting/gravitational sector the higher antifield terms and their closure are not computed in this document; the module defines the structure and returns AUDIT_QUANTUM, and E06b's job is to make explicit which terms are placeholder versus genuinely computed. (CONTRACT §1.3: downgrade-don't-invent. We do not fabricate a closed S_BV we have not derived.)

Strong check S1 — the classical master equation (S_BV, S_BV) = 0. Nilpotency of s at the classical level is equivalent to the master equation. Symbolically:

function checkMasterEquationClassical(S_BV):
    expr = antibracket(S_BV, S_BV)
    return simplify(expr) == 0

For the free/abelian toy this is identically zero (verified). For an interacting theory (S_BV,S_BV)=0 is a nontrivial set of identities (the gauge-algebra Jacobi identities, structure-constant constraints). Where the engine can derive it symbolically it reports PASS; where it cannot, AUDIT_QUANTUM — never an assumed pass.

Strong check S2 — the quantum master equation and regulator compatibility. Quantization promotes the classical master equation to the quantum master equation:

(S_BV, S_BV)  −  2 i ħ ΔS_BV  =  0 ,     where  Δ = (−1)^{ε_A+1} (δ_r/δΦ^A)(δ_l/δΦ*_A)  (the BV Laplacian).

The ΔS_BV term is formally the measure Jacobian and is ill-defined without a regulator (it is δ(0)-class). "Regulator compatibility" is the demand that there exist a regularization (Pauli–Villars, dimensional, higher-derivative) under which Δ_reg S_BV is finite and the regulator does not itself break BRST. This is precisely where a theory can have no good regulator — and for quantum gravity the existence of a BRST-compatible regulator at all orders is exactly the open UV question. So S2's honest default for the gravitational/interacting sector is AUDIT_QUANTUM with an explicit pointer to HC-08 (B-UQFC-14-UV-1, UNADOPTED). We never assert regulator compatibility we have not exhibited.

Strong check S3 — anomaly cancellation. If no BRST-invariant regulator exists, the obstruction is the anomaly 𝒜, a nontrivial element of the local BRST cohomology at ghost number 1:

(quantum master eqn fails)   ⟺   𝒜 = ħ · (ghost-number-1 cohomology class) ≠ 0 ,     s𝒜 = 0,  𝒜 ∉ Im s .

Anomaly cancellation (Wess–Zumino consistency + the right field content, e.g. ∑ tr T^a{T^b,T^c} = 0 for chiral gauge anomalies) makes 𝒜 exact, restoring the symmetry. The engine's job (E06b) is to compute the anomaly coefficient for each candidate's field content where tractable, and otherwise hold AUDIT_QUANTUM. First-failure handle: "anomaly leak" — a candidate whose field content gives 𝒜 ≠ 0 — is a FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE death, and the corpus names it directly (09_HC-06, "First failure": "…or anomaly leak").

Strong check S4 — positive physical Hilbert space (interacting). Finally, even with Q²=0 restored and the anomaly cancelled, one must show H^0(Q) = Ker Q / Im Q carries a positive-definite inner product at the interacting level — the Kugo–Ojima criterion (the quartet mechanism survives interactions, the BRST charge is well-defined and the "quartet" of unphysical modes confines/decouples). For non-confining or strongly-coupled sectors this is not known in general. Default for the interacting metric-interface sector: AUDIT_QUANTUM.

The honest strong-path verdict. Reading the right-hand columns top to bottom: the strong path for any realistic, interacting metric-interface candidate terminates at AUDIT_QUANTUM, and the dominant reason is structural, not a failure of diligence — it is the corpus boundary (Fable_Quantum: interacting sector stays AUDIT) reinforced by the open UV axiom (TOE_FINAL: B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED). The strong path's value is therefore not a pass; it is a precise localization of where the quantum closure is open (which of S1–S4 is placeholder vs computed for a given mode), which is exactly what E06b reports and what the patent's "quantum-status field" captures.

First failure (E06a.7). The strong path's first failure is the temptation to assume S2 (a BRST-compatible regulator exists) or S4 (interacting positivity holds) in order to award a higher status. Doing so would silently adopt the UNADOPTED UV axiom and violate CONTRACT §1.3/§1.4 (no self-promotion, downgrade-don't-invent). The fail-closed rule is therefore hard-wired into the precedence (§E06a.3 step 5) and into the filename bv_master_placeholder.py: any interacting check that is not computed in front of the reviewer is AUDIT_QUANTUM, full stop. E06b's "placeholder-vs-computed honesty" is the mechanism that audits this.

First failure (E06a.8). The acceptance suite's own first failure is incompleteness of the witness set: the symbolic classifier tests exactness and norm only on the supplied finite basis. A state could be exact via a generator outside the basis (false not-exact), or have negative norm only in a sector the Gram matrix omitted (false positive). The defense is that the basis is built from the declared field content of Ξ (closed under Q to the relevant ghost degree), and any state requiring an undeclared generator is itself a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (smuggling a field) — but the leaf must record that the classifier's verdicts are relative to the declared field content, never an absolute cohomological theorem. This is the honest limit of a symbolic, finite-basis BRST audit, and it is why even a PASS_TOY is a status-labeled result and not a proof.

E06a.9 Patent extraction

The defensible, simulation-only inventions exposed by this leaf — valuable as audit/screening assets regardless of whether any candidate ever passes, which is the option-value posture (CONTRACT §0):

  1. A symbolic BRST physical-state classifier that ingests a BRSTInstance (graded field multiplet, Q-variation table, indefinite inner product, candidate state, declared basis) and returns a quantum-status verdict ∈ {PASS_TOY, AUDIT_QUANTUM, FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE} with a named first failure, by evaluating closedness (Q|Ψ⟩=0), exactness (membership in Im Q via the Rouché–Capelli rank test rank[Q]=rank[Q|Ψ]), positivity (vᵀηv>0), and nilpotency (Q²=0 on generators) — in a fail-closed precedence where anomaly/Q²≠0 and missing-data are caught before the cohomology test. The exact (symbolic, rational-field) exactness oracle, as opposed to a numerical rank test, is a specific defensible element (it cannot false-pass a trivial state near a degeneracy).
  2. The quantum-status field in the gate card (quantum_status, with nilpotency_Q2, closed_C1, exact_C2, norm_C3, anomaly_check, interacting_sector sub-fields), and the automatic interacting-sector audit downgrade (any interacting=True instance whose master-equation/anomaly checks are placeholder routes to AUDIT_QUANTUM, never PASS_TOY) — i.e. a machine-enforced honesty boundary between free-shell pass and interacting audit.
  3. The BV-master-equation structural builder with explicit placeholder accounting (bv_master_placeholder.py): builds S_BV, the antibracket, and the (classical/quantum) master-equation expressions symbolically, and labels each strong check S0–S4 as computed-vs-placeholder per mode, so a downstream reviewer can see exactly which part of the quantum closure was earned and which was deferred.
  4. The negative-control calibration harness for a cohomological classifier — the requirement that the classifier reproduce hand-verified verdicts on a BRST-exact state, a negative-norm ghost, an anomalous charge, and a no-data instance before any candidate verdict is trusted, with a positive recovery control (transverse photon PASS_TOY, θ→0 recovery) proving the classifier is discriminating rather than rejecting-all.

These are screening/audit/⊗-layer-validity assets — "a tool that proves a candidate isn't a quantum-physical state, and localizes which BRST condition it fails" — independent of any physics outcome and of whether the Fable/TOE corpus is correct.

First failure (E06a.9). The patent claims fail — and must be downgraded — if any of them is read as covering a physical drive result rather than a simulation/audit asset. The defensible inventions here are the classifier, the quantum_status gate-card field, the placeholder-accounting BV builder, and the negative-control harness — all of which derive their value precisely from failing candidates and localizing the open condition, not from any candidate passing. The instant a claim is phrased as "a quantum-validated drive mode" rather than "a fail-closed screen that returns PASS_TOY/AUDIT_QUANTUM/FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE," it is a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and the option-value posture (CONTRACT §0) is lost; the patent scope is therefore the screen, never a drive.

E06b.0 Where E06a stopped and what this leaf must finish

The companion leaf E06a built the front half of the HC-06 closure path (Steps 1–6 of the BUILD CONTRACT §5 template): why a classically admissible metric-interface profile can still die on quantization (it can be BRST-exact — i.e. pure gauge dressed as physics; anomalous — the gauge symmetry that made it consistent is broken by the path-integral measure; or negative-norm — a ghost or a longitudinal/timelike polarization that no physical state should carry); the formal BRST object (Q_BRST, s, gh#); the corpus authority (Fable_Quantum, the Q_BRST|Ψ⟩=0-and-not-exact-and-positive-norm gate); the closure target; the minimal toy closure (a symbolic BRST classifier with negative controls); and the strong-closure path (define the BV action, check the master equation, check regulator compatibility, check anomaly cancellation, and exhibit a positive physical Hilbert space).

E06a deliberately stopped at the cohomology definitions and the free-field toy. It did not attempt the BV antifield extension, the master equation, the anomaly computation, or the physical-state norm classifier on the actual candidate library. This leaf, E06b, executes Steps 7–12 of HC-06: the production algorithms (brst_symbolic, bv_master_placeholder, physical_state_classifier); the negative controls (tests/test_brst_negative_controls.py); the candidate-mode results with gate cards; the first-failure ledger terminating in AUDIT_QUANTUM / FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE; the reviewer attacks; and the patent extraction.

The single load-bearing honesty rule of this entire leaf is carried verbatim from the BUILD CONTRACT §2 (Corpus anchors, Fable_Quantum):

"USE for quantization discipline; NOT for claiming full interacting quantum-gravity closure (the interacting sector stays AUDIT)."

and from §3 (Downgrade tree): "BRST unknown → AUDIT_QUANTUM." So the strongest token this leaf can ever emit on the quantization gate for an interacting metric-interface mode is AUDIT_QUANTUM. There is no gauge_check: PASS or "quantum closure" claim for any interacting candidate anywhere in this document. The thin-spot this leaf was commissioned to fix is precisely the temptation to let a symbolic placeholder masquerade as a proof: bv_master_placeholder is a placeholder, and we label every result that depends on it as a placeholder, on every line where it appears.

Notation carried from E06a (self-contained recap). Fields φ^i (the classical metric-interface content: δg_{μν}, gauge potentials δA_μ^a, scalars δφ^I, and the geometric components δG_{μA}, δG_{AB} of the three-layer object × ⊕ ⊗). Gauge generators R^i_α(φ) with parameters ε^α so that δ_ε φ^i = R^i_α ε^α; here α ranges over diffeomorphisms (parameters ξ^μ) and internal/bundle gauge (parameters λ^a). Ghosts c^α (ghost number gh#=+1), antighosts \bar c_α (gh#=−1), Nakanishi–Lautrup auxiliaries b_α (gh#=0). The classical BRST operator s acts as a graded derivation; on the physical fields s φ^i = R^i_α c^α. The BRST charge Q_BRST generates s on the Fock/Hilbert space: s(\cdot) = [Q_BRST, \cdot} (graded commutator). Nilpotency s^2=0 ⇔ Q_BRST^2=0 is the structural spine of everything below. Signature (−,+,+,+); M_Pl=1 in toy units unless a number needs SI scaling (it never does here — see Forbidden box).

First failure of E06b.0 (scope, AUDIT_QUANTUM): this section only inherits E06a's free-field cohomology definitions and the formal BRST object; it proves nothing new about the interacting sector. The first failure is structural — E06a deliberately stopped before the BV antifield extension, so everything E06b inherits about interacting quantization is undefined on entry and must be downgraded to AUDIT_QUANTUM until Steps 7–12 below either compute it (they do not, for the interacting sector) or flag it as placeholder (they do).

E06b.1 Step 7 — the BV (antifield/antibracket) action and the master equation

E06b.1.1 Why we need BV at all (and why the free case is not the case that matters)

For an irreducible, closed gauge algebra (structure constants f^γ_{αβ} field-independent, generators independent), ordinary BRST quantization with Q_BRST and a gauge-fixing fermion Ψ suffices. The metric-interface object is neither: diffeomorphisms have a field-dependent, open algebra once the metric is dynamical (the commutator of two diffeos closes only on-shell, with structure functions, not structure constants), and coupling the diffeo sector to the internal bundle gauge sector δA_μ^a and to the geometric δG_{μA} mixes the two algebras. The Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) / antifield formalism is the only systematic tool that handles open, reducible, field-dependent algebras. This is exactly why the interacting sector cannot be waved through: the very feature that forces BV (on-shell closure, structure functions) is the feature that makes the master equation a genuine, hard, unfinished computation rather than a textbook exercise.

E06b.1.2 The BV field/antifield content and the antibracket

To every field Φ^A ∈ {φ^i, c^α, \bar c_α, b_α} we adjoin an antifield Φ^*_A of opposite Grassmann parity and ghost number gh#(Φ^*_A) = −gh#(Φ^A) − 1. The antibracket of two functionals X, Y of (Φ, Φ^*) is

(X, Y) = ∫ d^d x [  (δ_R X / δΦ^A)(δ_L Y / δΦ^*_A)  −  (δ_R X / δΦ^*_A)(δ_L Y / δΦ^A) ]

(δ_R, δ_L are right/left functional derivatives; the integral runs over the configuration the field lives on — M4 for the 4D fields, M4 × K_gauge for components that thread the compactification K6 = SU(3)/T², per the Fable_GUT geometry). The antibracket is graded-antisymmetric (X,Y) = −(−1)^{(ε_X+1)(ε_Y+1)}(Y,X), satisfies a graded Jacobi identity, and carries ghost number gh#(X,Y) = gh#(X)+gh#(Y)+1.

E06b.1.3 The classical BV action and the classical master equation

The BV action S[Φ, Φ^*] is built by the standard expansion in antifield/ghost number, seeded by the classical action and the gauge generators:

S = S_0[φ]                                   # classical effective action (BUILD CONTRACT §2 S_eff)
  + φ^*_i R^i_α c^α                           # gauge generators couple to field antifields
  + ½ c^*_γ f^γ_{αβ} c^β c^α                  # structure functions f (field-DEPENDENT here)
  + (higher antifield terms forced by open/on-shell closure)         # <-- the hard, OPEN part

S_0 is the §2 effective action S_eff = ∫ d⁴x √(−g)[ (M_Pl²/2)R − ¼ Z_{ab}F^aF^b − ½ G_{IJ}∂φ^I∂φ^J − V(φ) + L_matter + L_constraint + L_EFT ]. The classical master equation is

(S, S) = 0 .

Expanded order-by-order in antifields, (S,S)=0 reproduces, at successive orders: (0) gauge invariance of S_0 (R^i_α δS_0/δφ^i = 0); (1) the algebra R^j_α δ_j R^i_β − R^j_β δ_j R^i_α = R^i_γ f^γ_{αβ} − (\text{on-shell terms}); (2) the Jacobi/higher-structure consistency of the structure functions; and at higher antifield number, the reducibility and open-algebra completion terms. For the metric-interface object those higher terms are not all known in closed form — they are exactly what bv_master_placeholder flags but does not compute.

E06b.1.4 The quantum master equation and the BV Laplacian Δ

Quantization replaces (S,S)=0 by the quantum master equation (QME) for the quantum action W = S + ℏ M_1 + ℏ² M_2 + …:

½ (W, W) = i ℏ Δ W          ⇔          Δ e^{(i/ℏ)W} = 0 ,
                                        Δ = (−1)^{ε_A+1} (δ_R/δΦ^A)(δ_R/δΦ^*_A)

Δ is the BV Laplacian, the operator that encodes the path-integral measure. At order ℏ^0 the QME is the classical master equation (S,S)=0. At order ℏ^1 it reads

(S, M_1) = i Δ S .                          # <-- the ANOMALY equation

The right-hand side ΔS is generically ill-defined (it is a δ(0), i.e. an unregulated coincident-point functional derivative) and must be regulated. The obstruction to solving (S, M_1) = iΔS for a local counterterm M_1 is the anomaly A: if no local M_1 exists, A ≠ 0 and the gauge symmetry is broken at the quantum level. This is the content of Step 7→9 and the reason the source doc lists "regulator compatibility, anomaly cancellation" as separate strong-closure items: a profile that passes the classical master equation can still die on ΔS.

First failure of E06b.1 (bv_master_placeholder at the antifield-completion order): for the open, field-dependent diffeo⊕bundle algebra of the metric-interface object, the higher-antifield completion terms of S and the order-ℏ term M_1 are not computed in closed form; bv_master_placeholder returns the master-equation residual (S,S) truncated at antifield number ≤ 2 and explicitly tags the truncation. Any interacting mode therefore inherits AUDIT_QUANTUM — the master equation is not verified to all orders, only to the placeholder truncation. We do not claim (S,S)=0 for the interacting sector.

E06b.2 Step 7 (cont.) — the bv_master_placeholder algorithm, honestly bounded

The build artifact is named src/quantum/bv_master_placeholder.py in the source doc — the name itself is a contract: it is a placeholder. Below is the production form. It computes what is computable (free/abelianized residuals, ghost-number bookkeeping, classical-master residual to truncation order) and fail-closes to AUDIT_QUANTUM on everything that is not.

function bv_master_check(S_fields, gauge_generators, opts):
    # ---- input guard (fail-closed, BUILD CONTRACT §3) ----
    if S_fields is None or gauge_generators is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", first_failure="no BV data / no gauge generators",
                         allowed="none", forbidden="any quantum-closure claim")

    bv = build_bv_action(S_fields, gauge_generators)      # seeds S_0, φ*Rc, ½c*fcc
    algebra = classify_algebra(gauge_generators)          # CLOSED | OPEN | REDUCIBLE
    fdep    = structure_functions_field_dependent(gauge_generators)  # bool

    # ---- classical master residual, truncated ----
    res2 = antibracket(bv.S, bv.S, antifield_order_max=2) # (S,S) to af# <= 2, SYMBOLIC
    res2_simplified = simplify(res2)

    if algebra == CLOSED and not fdep and res2_simplified == 0:
        master_status = "PASS_TOY"          # ONLY the closed, field-indep, free/abelianized case
        truncation_exact = True
    else:
        master_status = "AUDIT_QUANTUM"     # open/field-dependent => higher af# terms UNCOMPUTED
        truncation_exact = False

    # ---- quantum master / measure (the BV Laplacian) ----
    deltaS = bv_laplacian(bv.S)             # ΔS  -- generically ill-defined (delta(0))
    if not opts.regulator_provided:
        measure_status = "AUDIT_QUANTUM"    # cannot evaluate ΔS without a regulator
        m1 = None
    else:
        m1 = solve_for_local_counterterm(bv.S, deltaS, opts.regulator)  # (S,M1)=iΔS ?
        measure_status = "PASS_TOY" if (m1 is not None) else "FAIL"     # FAIL == anomaly

    return {
      "status": worst_of(master_status, measure_status),   # fail-closed combine
      "placeholder": True,                                  # <-- ALWAYS true: bv_master_placeholder
      "evidence": {
         "algebra": algebra, "field_dependent_structure_fns": fdep,
         "classical_master_residual_af<=2": res2_simplified,
         "truncation_exact": truncation_exact,
         "deltaS_defined": opts.regulator_provided,
         "M1_local_counterterm_exists": (m1 is not None) if opts.regulator_provided else None
      },
      "first_failure": ("open/field-dependent algebra: higher-antifield master terms uncomputed"
                        if master_status=="AUDIT_QUANTUM"
                        else ("anomaly: no local M1 solves (S,M1)=iΔS" if measure_status=="FAIL"
                              else "none at truncation; free/abelianized toy only")),
      "allowed_claim": "free/abelianized BRST-BV structure consistent at truncation (PASS_TOY)",
      "forbidden_claim": "interacting BV master equation solved / quantum closure"
    }

Two design commitments make this honest. (1) placeholder: True is hard-wired, not computed — the function cannot return a non-placeholder verdict; the only way it ever emits PASS_TOY is the explicitly-guarded closed + field-independent + free/abelianized branch, which is not the metric-interface case. (2) worst_of(...) fail-closed combine: master and measure statuses combine by taking the worst, so a clean classical residual cannot launder a missing regulator. The bv_laplacian call returns a symbolic, unregulated ΔS; absent a regulator_provided flag (which no candidate in the library supplies in closed form), measure_status is pinned to AUDIT_QUANTUM.

First failure of E06b.2 (AUDIT_QUANTUM, by construction of the algorithm): bv_master_check is structurally incapable of certifying the interacting sector — placeholder: True is hard-wired and the only branch that can emit PASS_TOY is explicitly guarded by algebra == CLOSED and not fdep, which the metric-interface diffeo⊕bundle algebra fails. Therefore the first failure of the algorithm itself is that for every interacting candidate deltaS = bv_laplacian(bv.S) returns an unregulated δ(0) and opts.regulator_provided is False (no library mode supplies a simultaneously-compatible regulator in closed form), pinning measure_status to AUDIT_QUANTUM; the worst_of(...) combine then forces the whole verdict to AUDIT_QUANTUM. The algorithm does not compute the higher-antifield completion of S, and we do not claim it does.

Worked truncation residual (the one number this step legitimately produces). For a single abelian gauge field δA_μ with s δA_μ = ∂_μ c, s c = 0, s \bar c = b, s b = 0 (the genuinely free case), the BV action truncates exactly: S = S_0[A] + A^{*μ}∂_μ c + \bar c^* b. Then

(S,S) = 2 ∫ d⁴x [ (δ_R S_0/δA_μ) ∂_μ c ]  =  2 ∫ d⁴x [ ∂^ν F_{νμ} ] ∂^μ c
      = −2 ∫ d⁴x (∂^μ∂^ν F_{νμ}) c  = 0     (antisymmetry of F)

so res2_simplified = 0 and the abelian toy legitimately returns PASS_TOY — a real, machine-checkable result, the only clean master-equation pass in this leaf. The moment we restore the non-abelian ½ c^*_γ f^γ_{αβ}c^βc^α term (internal SU(3) from K6 = SU(3)/T², or the diffeo algebra), f^γ_{αβ} becomes the field-dependent diffeo structure function, the af#≤2 truncation is no longer exact, and the function flips to AUDIT_QUANTUM. That flip is the thin-spot fix made executable.

E06b.3 Step 8 — negative controls (tests/test_brst_negative_controls.py)

Per the source doc acceptance tests — BRST-exact mode fails · negative-norm mode fails · unproven interacting sector stays AUDIT — and the BUILD CONTRACT discipline that every section runs one negative control. A classifier that cannot fail the known-bad inputs is worthless, so these controls are the credibility spine of the whole chapter.

ID Negative control (input) Required verdict Guards against
NC-EXACT A pure-gauge state \|χ⟩ = Q_BRST\|λ⟩ (BRST-exact) FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE (exact ⇒ zero-norm physical, trivial) calling pure gauge "physics"
NC-NEG A negative-norm state (timelike-photon / ghost polarization) ⟨ψ\|ψ⟩ < 0 FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE admitting a non-unitary state to the Hilbert space
NC-OPEN Interacting metric-interface mode (open algebra, field-dep f) AUDIT_QUANTUM (NOT pass) a placeholder masquerading as a proof
NC-NODATA A candidate with no BRST data attached FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE (no data ⇒ cannot certify) silent pass on absent quantization
NC-ANOM A toy with a deliberate anomaly (ΔS has no local M_1) FAIL (anomaly leak) shipping an anomalous gauge symmetry
NC-NILPOT A toy with s² ≠ 0 (broken nilpotency, e.g. wrong f) FAIL (Q_BRST²≠0 ⇒ no cohomology) building cohomology on a non-nilpotent s 
def test_brst_negative_controls():
    # NC-EXACT: exact state must be rejected as trivial/zero-norm
    chi = Q_BRST(lam)                          # |chi> = Q|lam>
    assert classify_state(chi).status == "FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE"
    assert classify_state(chi).reason  == "BRST-exact (trivial cohomology, zero physical norm)"

    # NC-NEG: negative-norm state must be rejected
    psi_neg = timelike_photon_polarization()   # <psi|psi> < 0
    assert classify_state(psi_neg).status == "FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE"
    assert classify_state(psi_neg).reason  == "negative norm (non-unitary)"

    # NC-OPEN: interacting sector must stay AUDIT, never pass
    out = bv_master_check(interacting_mode.S, interacting_mode.generators, opts_no_regulator)
    assert out["status"] == "AUDIT_QUANTUM"
    assert out["placeholder"] is True          # placeholder watermark MUST be present

    # NC-NODATA: missing BRST data must fail closed
    assert classify_state(None).status == "FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE"

    # NC-ANOM: deliberate anomaly must fail
    out = bv_master_check(anomalous_toy.S, anomalous_toy.generators, opts_with_regulator)
    assert out["status"] == "FAIL"
    assert "anomaly" in out["first_failure"]

    # NC-NILPOT: broken nilpotency must fail
    assert nilpotency_residual(bad_s) != 0
    assert classify_state_under(bad_s, any_state).status == "FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE"

    # POSITIVE GUARD: the free abelian toy is the ONLY clean master pass
    out = bv_master_check(free_abelian.S, free_abelian.generators, opts_with_regulator)
    assert out["status"] == "PASS_TOY"
    assert out["evidence"]["classical_master_residual_af<=2"] == 0

The NC-OPEN assertion out["placeholder"] is True is the single most important line in the test file. It guarantees that the only way the interacting sector can ever leave this code path is with the placeholder watermark attached — there is no code branch in which an interacting mode emits a non-placeholder pass. If a future edit ever made bv_master_check "succeed" on an interacting mode, this test breaks. That is the machine-checked form of the thin-spot fix.

First failure of E06b.3: if any negative control is missing or disabled, the classifier is unverified and the whole chapter downgrades to AUDIT_QUANTUM by default — a classifier with no failing inputs has demonstrated nothing.

E06b.4 Step 9 — anomaly cancellation: what brst_symbolic checks and what it cannot

E06b.4.1 The cohomological form of the anomaly (Step 9, real content)

The order-ℏ consistency equation (S, M_1) = i ΔS is, in BRST language, the statement that the anomaly A is s-closed (s A = 0, the Wess–Zumino consistency condition) and the question is whether it is s-exact (A = s M_1 for a local M_1). The anomaly thus lives in the local BRST cohomology at ghost number 1 (for gauge anomalies) and is computed by descent:

s A_0^{1} + d A_1^{0} = 0  →  (descent)  →  A = ∫ A_n^{1}   (ghost number 1, form degree d)

For the internal bundle gauge sector δA_μ^a on the Fable_GUT geometry, the candidate anomaly is the standard non-abelian gauge anomaly, whose coefficient is the symmetrized trace of three generators, the anomaly polynomial d^{abc} = Tr(T^a\{T^b,T^c\}) in the relevant representation. Anomaly cancellation requires Σ_reps d^{abc} = 0. For the diffeo (gravitational) sector the analogue is the gravitational/mixed anomaly, controlled by the chiral fermion content and (in d=4) the mixed gauge–gravitational coefficient Tr(T^a) over chiral fermions.

E06b.4.2 The worked toy numbers (the legitimate computed results of Step 9)

These are real, finite, textbook-checkable group-theory numbers — exactly the kind of "worked numbers where the brief calls for them" the BUILD CONTRACT §6 wants, and they are computed, not placeholder:

  • Pure abelian U(1)_Y cubic anomaly (the hypercharge circle S¹_Y of the corpus): coefficient ∝ Σ_f Y_f^3 over chiral fermions. For one Standard-Model generation with hypercharges Q_L:(+1/6)×2×3, u_R:(−2/3)×3, d_R:(+1/3)×3, L:(−1/2)×2, e_R:(+1):
  Σ Y^3 = 6·(1/6)^3 − 3·(2/3)^3 + 3·(1/3)^3 − 2·(1/2)^3 + (1)^3
        = 6/216 − 3·8/27 + 3/27 − 2/8 + 1
        = 1/36 − 8/9 + 1/9 − 1/4 + 1 = 0.           # cancels exactly ✓
  • Mixed gauge–gravitational U(1)_Y anomaly: coefficient ∝ Σ_f Y_f:
  Σ Y = 6·(1/6) − 3·(2/3) + 3·(1/3) − 2·(1/2) + 1 = 1 − 2 + 1 − 1 + 1 = 0.   # cancels ✓
  • Non-abelian SU(3)_c cubic (K6 = SU(3)/T² colour): vector-like ⇒ d^{abc} contributions of q_L and q_R cancel pairwise ⇒ 0 by vector-likeness. ✓

So the Standard-Model-like fermion content threaded on the Fable geometry passes the gauge-anomaly arithmetic at the level of the known spectrum. This is a genuine PASS_TOY result for the internal gauge anomaly of the matter sector, and the chapter records it as such.

E06b.4.3 What the anomaly check cannot close — and why it stays AUDIT

The cancellation above is for the internal gauge anomalies of a known chiral spectrum. It does not certify the quantum consistency of the metric-interface excitation itself, for four reasons we state plainly rather than paper over:

  1. The BV measure of the gravitational/diffeo sector (the ΔS for the diffeo ghosts c^μ, on an open algebra) is the part with no closed-form local counterterm here — bv_master_placeholder does not produce M_1 for the diffeo sector. Diffeomorphism anomalies vanish in d=4 for a non-chiral gravitational coupling, but the mixed metric-interface ⊗ bundle terms (δG_{μA}) are exactly the untreated cross-sector pieces.
  2. The regulator must be simultaneously compatible with every gauge symmetry (diffeo and internal and the compactification isometries of SU(3)/T²). Exhibiting one such regulator is a real computation we have not performed; we only check anomaly coefficients, which is necessary, not sufficient.
  3. The EFT operators L_EFT in S_eff (the higher-dimension metric-interface couplings that actually do the front/back-asymmetric work) carry their own potential anomalous variation; these are not in the renormalizable spectrum whose anomalies cancel above.
  4. The forward-lobe profile is a nontrivial background, not the vacuum; anomaly inflow / boundary terms on the lobe wall are uncomputed.

First failure of E06b.4 (AUDIT_QUANTUM): anomaly coefficient cancellation of the known chiral spectrum is PASS_TOY and computed; regulator compatibility across diffeo⊕bundle⊕isometry, the diffeo-sector M_1, the L_EFT operator anomalies, and lobe-background inflow are NOT computed — brst_symbolic returns them as AUDIT_QUANTUM with the bv_master_placeholder watermark. The chapter does not claim "anomaly cancellation proven for the metric-interface mode."

E06b.5 Step 10 — the physical-state classifier and the positive Hilbert space

E06b.5.1 The three gates of physical_state_classifier

The corpus gate (Fable_Quantum) is: a physical state must be BRST-closed, not BRST-exact, and positive-norm. Formally, the physical Hilbert space is the BRST cohomology at ghost number zero,

H_phys = Ker(Q_BRST) / Im(Q_BRST)   restricted to gh# = 0 ,   with  ⟨Ψ|Ψ⟩ > 0  ∀ |Ψ⟩ ∈ H_phys .

src/quantum/physical_state_classifier.py implements the three gates as a fail-closed cascade:

function classify_state(psi, Q_BRST, inner_product):
    if psi is None or Q_BRST is None:
        return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE("no BRST data")                       # NC-NODATA

    # Gate 1: CLOSED?  Q|psi> == 0
    if not is_zero(Q_BRST(psi)):
        return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE("not BRST-closed (Q|psi> != 0)")      # gauge-variant junk

    # Gate 2: NOT EXACT?  |psi> != Q|lambda> for some lambda
    if is_in_image(psi, Q_BRST):
        return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE("BRST-exact (pure gauge, trivial in cohomology)")  # NC-EXACT

    # Gate 3: POSITIVE NORM?  <psi|psi> > 0
    n = inner_product(psi, psi)
    if n <= 0:
        return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE("non-positive norm (ghost/longitudinal)")  # NC-NEG
    if n is INDETERMINATE:                                               # interacting inner product
        return AUDIT_QUANTUM("inner product not computable in closed form (interacting)")  # NC-OPEN

    return PASS_TOY("BRST-closed, non-exact, positive-norm (free/asymptotic sector)")

Worked free-sector example (real, computed). Take the abelian gauge field. In the BRST-extended Fock space the one-particle states are spanned by the four polarizations ε_μ^{(λ)}, the ghost, and the antighost. The BRST charge acts (in momentum space, k^2=0) as Q_BRST a^†_{scalar} ∝ k·ε-type relations: it maps the scalar (timelike) photon to the ghost and the antighost to the longitudinal photon. The cohomology computation gives, at gh#=0:

  • Closed & exact (killed): the longitudinal polarization ε_μ^L ∝ k_μ is Q-exact ⇒ removed (Gate 2). ✓ matches NC-EXACT.
  • Not closed (killed): the scalar/timelike ε_μ^0 is not annihilated by Q ⇒ removed (Gate 1). Its negative norm ⟨0|0⟩<0 is exactly the would-be ghost — and Gate 1 removes it before the norm even matters. ✓ matches NC-NEG.
  • Survives: the two transverse polarizations ε_μ^{(1)}, ε_μ^{(2)} with k·ε^{(i)}=0 are closed, non-exact, and positive-norm (⟨i|i⟩ = +1). ⇒ PASS_TOY, exactly the expected 2 physical photon states.

So classify_state reproduces the textbook result 4 − 1(\text{long, exact}) − 1(\text{scalar, not closed}) = 2 transverse physical states with positive norm. This is the legitimate computed PASS_TOY of the free sector and the positive guard in the test file.

E06b.5.2 Why the interacting physical Hilbert space stays AUDIT_QUANTUM

Gate 3 returns AUDIT_QUANTUM whenever the inner product is not computable in closed form, which is precisely the interacting metric-interface case:

  • Positivity of the BV/BRST inner product on an open algebra is not guaranteed by the free-sector construction; it requires the interacting Q_BRST to be nilpotent off-shell (it is only on-shell here) and the cohomology to be computed with the full S, including the placeholder higher-antifield terms.
  • Asymptotic completeness — the statement that the interacting physical states are in one-to-one correspondence with free positive-norm states (the Kugo–Ojima criterion / quartet mechanism) — is an assumption, not a theorem, for this non-renormalizable EFT on a nontrivial lobe background.
  • The lobe background breaks Poincaré invariance, so the very notion of "asymptotic one-particle state" with a clean norm is itself AUDIT.

First failure of E06b.5 (FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE / AUDIT_QUANTUM): free/asymptotic transverse states are PASS_TOY (computed: 2 positive-norm photon states, ghost/longitudinal/timelike correctly killed); the interacting physical Hilbert space — positivity, nilpotency off-shell, Kugo–Ojima completeness, norm on the lobe background — is NOT established and returns AUDIT_QUANTUM. Any mode whose state carries a negative norm, is BRST-exact, or has no BRST data returns FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE.
