E07a — HC-07 Unified-Mode Admissibility — Object & Target

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED (the admissibility object — provenance map, mode-card schema, three-layer assignment, no-new-primitive scan, and no-double-counting audit — is defined and negative-control-tested with explicit toy numbers; ceiling PASS_TOY, not reached; terminal status AUDIT) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

Scope note (HC-07, leaf a of two). This leaf builds the object and the target for the unified-mode-admissibility challenge. The single question HC-07 answers is bookkeeping, not dynamics: does every excitation component of a candidate Ξ_drive trace back to the one frozen parent geometry — with no new primitive field smuggled in, and with nothing counted twice? This leaf (i) defines the provenance map π from excitation components to the frozen parent inventory; (ii) fixes the mode-card schema and its mandatory three-layer assignment (× / ⊕ / ⊗); (iii) specifies the no-new-primitive scan and the no-double-counting audit as machine-checkable predicates; (iv) builds the minimal toy in which an arbitrary fifth field is rejected, a gauge descendant is caught being double-counted, and an internal modulus mode is flagged UV-sensitive; and (v) states the strong path — the admissibility projector 𝒫_adm with its no-new-primitive and no-double-counting guards. The classifier's full run across the 50-mode catalog, the per-mode gate-card roll-up, and the FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT tallies are leaf E07b. Nothing here is a propulsion result. The deliverable is a provenance firewall: the component that prevents the screener from inventing degrees of freedom or paying for the same physics twice.

1. Why this challenge matters (HC-07)

Every other gate in the document — invariant-distance (HC-01), source (HC-02/G2), energy (HC-03/G3), gauge (HC-05), causality (HC-06) — assumes it knows what fields it is grading. They take the excitation Ξ_drive as a given object with a fixed field content and ask whether that object behaves. HC-07 is the gate underneath all of them. It asks the prior question: is the field content itself legitimate? If a candidate mode quietly introduces a sixth scalar that exists in no parent, or counts the Kaluza-Klein graviphoton once as a 4D vector and again as a piece of the higher-dimensional metric, then every downstream gate is grading a fiction. The source ledger will balance — against a source that was double-entered. The energy integral will look bounded — because half the stress was attributed to a field that the geometry never licensed.

This is the most insidious failure class in the entire screener because it is conservative-looking. A new primitive field does not announce itself with a NEC violation or a coordinate singularity. It announces itself by making the candidate easier to close: an extra knob to tune the lobe, an extra stress term to balance the books, an extra modulus to absorb the back-reaction. Adding fields is exactly what a motivated modeller does when a candidate almost works. HC-07 exists to make that move impossible without a flag.

The corpus is unusually specific about why this is forbidden. The frozen parent geometry is a single compactification — M4 × K_gauge × F⁺ with K6 = SU(3)/T², the two-sphere S², and the hypercharge circle S¹_Y, sitting in the F⁺ admissibility chamber (Fable_GUT, freeze discipline). "Frozen" means the field inventory is closed: the only fields that exist are the 4D graviton, the gauge connection of the visible sector, the moduli of the internal factors, the Kaluza-Klein towers descending from the parent metric and form fields, and their ghost/auxiliary partners. There is no fifth column. Fable_Forces makes the parallel demand on the energy side: a single Einstein-frame metric, one-parent force projection, shared/visible stress-energy coupling, no double counting. A candidate that respects HC-07 is one whose entire Ξ_drive is a re-expression of perturbations of the frozen inventory — never an extension of it.

First failure (this section / leaf). HC-07's signature failure is the unlicensed degree of freedom, in one of three exact forms: (F1) new primitive — a component of Ξ_drive whose provenance map π returns ∅ (it traces to nothing in the frozen parent); token FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE. (F2) double count — two components of Ξ_drive whose provenance maps overlap (π(c_i) ∩ π(c_j) ≠ ∅) such that the same parent degree of freedom enters the source/energy ledger twice; token FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT. (F3) unlicensed chamber/modulus use — a component that does trace to a parent modulus but excites it outside the frozen F⁺ chamber or beyond the radius where the internal mode's UV completion is controlled; token UV_DELEGATED (or FAIL_CHAMBER if it leaves F⁺ outright). The deeper, meta-first-failure that caps this leaf at AUDIT: the provenance map π is only as complete as the declared parent inventory, and the completeness of that inventory against the true (UV) spectrum is exactly the open question B-UQFC-14-UV-1 (TOE_FINAL diff, Gap-04) — so HC-07 can certify "traces to the declared parent" but can never certify "traces to the complete parent." That residual is irreducible here and is named, not papered over.

2. Formal object — the provenance map and the frozen parent inventory

2.1 The excitation as a labelled component set

Take the standard excitation from the build contract and label its components explicitly:

Ξ_drive(t,x) = { δg_μν,  δA_μ^a,  δφ^I,  δG_μA,  δG_AB,  Σ_state,  Σ_gauge }

For admissibility we do not treat Ξ as an opaque field; we treat it as a finite set of typed components C(Ξ) = { c_1, c_2, … , c_n }, where each c_k is a tuple

c_k = ( name_k,  tensor_type_k,  support_k,  amplitude_k,  declared_origin_k )

— e.g. c = ( "δG_μA", mixed-(1,1), forward-lobe, 0.04, "KK descendant of ḡ_MN along K^A on S¹_Y" ). The declared_origin field is the candidate author's claim about where the component comes from; HC-07's job is to verify or refute that claim against the frozen inventory, not to take it on faith.

2.2 The frozen parent inventory 𝓘_par

The parent is frozen, so its degrees of freedom form a fixed, enumerable set — the inventory 𝓘_par. We organize it by origin block:

Origin block Parent object 4D content after KK reduction Count notation
B_grav parent metric ḡ_MN on M4 × K 4D graviton g_μν; graviphotons G_μA (one per Killing vector of K); internal metric moduli G_AB n_g = 1 + dim(isom K) + #moduli(K)
B_gauge visible gauge connection Ā_M^a (incl. S¹_Y Wilson line) 4D gauge fields A_μ^a; internal Wilson-line scalars A_A^a n_A = dim 𝔤 · (1 + b₁-type modes)
B_mod shape/size moduli of K6, S², S¹_Y scalars φ^I: R_{K6}, squashing of SU(3)/T², R_{S²}, R_{S¹_Y}, F⁺-chamber coordinates n_φ = #moduli
B_form parent p-form fields (flux sector) 4D scalars/vectors from form reduction n_F
B_ghost BRST ghost/antighost of each gauge symmetry c, c̄, b for diffeo + gauge + KK-isometry gauge n_gh
B_aux auxiliary/Lagrange-multiplier fields of L_constraint non-propagating Σ_state, Σ_gauge n_aux

The crucial discipline: 𝓘_par is closed and frozen. It is read once from the corpus configuration and never extended by a candidate. Its cardinality N_par = n_g + n_A + n_φ + n_F + n_gh + n_aux is a fixed integer for the active geometry. (For the worked toy in §5 we use a deliberately small slice of 𝓘_par; the full inventory is a configuration artifact, not something a leaf invents.)

2.3 The provenance map π

The central object of HC-07 is the provenance map

π :  C(Ξ)  ⟶  2^{𝓘_par}

sending each excitation component to the set of parent degrees of freedom it is a perturbation of. Three cases exhaust the outcomes:

  1. π(c) = { single parent dof } — the component is a clean perturbation of exactly one frozen dof. Admissible (pending layer + chamber checks).
  2. π(c) = ∅ — the component traces to nothing in 𝓘_par. New primitive (F1). FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE.
  3. π(c_i) ∩ π(c_j) ≠ ∅ for i ≠ j — two components share a parent dof. Candidate double count (F2) — escalated to the no-double-counting audit (§4.3), which decides whether the overlap is a genuine re-entry into the ledger or an allowed redundant labelling.

Admissibility is then the conjunction of three predicates over π:

ADMISSIBLE(Ξ)  ⟺   NO_NEW_PRIMITIVE(Ξ)  ∧  NO_DOUBLE_COUNT(Ξ)  ∧  LICENSED_CHAMBER(Ξ)

NO_NEW_PRIMITIVE(Ξ)  ≡  ∀ c ∈ C(Ξ):  π(c) ≠ ∅
NO_DOUBLE_COUNT(Ξ)   ≡  the multiset ⋃_c π(c) enters the source/energy ledger with multiplicity ≤ 1 per parent dof
LICENSED_CHAMBER(Ξ)  ≡  ∀ c with π(c) ⊆ B_mod:  the excited modulus stays in F⁺ and within its UV-controlled band

The first-failure of any candidate under HC-07 is whichever of these three conjuncts fails first, in the order written. This ordering matters: we test new-primitive before double-count (a ∅-provenance component cannot be double-counted, so F1 short-circuits), and chamber/UV last (only meaningful once a component has a legitimate single-parent origin to be in or out of F⁺).

2.4 Why this is a map, not a norm

A naïve admissibility test would be amplitude-based: "if the candidate has too many large components, suspect a smuggled field." That is wrong for the same reason HC-05's norm-rejector was wrong — provenance is a structural, not a magnitude, property. A new primitive can be infinitesimally small (a tiny extra scalar tuned to balance the source ledger) and still be fatal; a perfectly legitimate component can be large. π is therefore keyed to the origin of each component (its transformation properties under the parent symmetries and its KK quantum numbers), never to its amplitude. This is the structural analogue of the HC-05 lesson and is enforced identically: decide on the provenance of the component, never on its norm.

3. Corpus authority

HC-07 is the gate most tightly bound to the frozen-geometry corpus, so the authority block is correspondingly specific.

  • Fable_GUT — frozen active geometry / single parent. Licenses the existence and closure of 𝓘_par: the parent M4 × K_gauge × F⁺ with K6 = SU(3)/T², S², S¹_Y is a single, frozen compactification with an admissibility chamber F⁺ and a freeze discipline (the inventory does not change). HC-07 uses this for "the parent inventory is a closed enumerable set" and may not use it for any working-drive, UV-completion, or hardware claim. The F⁺ chamber is what LICENSED_CHAMBER checks against.
  • Fable_Forces — single Einstein-frame metric, no double counting. This is the direct authority for NO_DOUBLE_COUNT. Fable_Forces fixes a single Einstein-frame metric, one-parent force projection, and — verbatim discipline — shared/visible stress-energy coupling with no double counting. The KK graviphoton δG_μA being simultaneously "a 4D vector" and "part of δg in higher dimensions" is precisely the double-count the corpus forbids; HC-07 operationalizes that prohibition.
  • Three-layer field discipline (build contract §2). × metric/geometric base · ⊕ admissibility/projection/chamber · ⊗ bundles/operators/quantization. Every excitation component MUST map to a layer — this is mandated, and the mode-card schema (§4.1) makes the layer assignment a required field. A component with no legal layer is itself a form of inadmissibility.
  • EFT admissibility & UV-delegation (build contract §2). χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1; if global compactification stability is required ⇒ status UV_DELEGATED. This is the authority for the F3 / UV-sensitive outcome: an internal-modulus mode (e.g. K6 breathing) whose admissibility depends on global compactification stability is flagged UV_DELEGATED, never silently passed.
  • TOE_FINAL diff — Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1. Global UV stability is OPEN; the UV axiom is UNADOPTED. This is the authority for the meta-first-failure: π's completeness is bounded by the declared inventory, and the inventory's completeness against the true UV spectrum is the open gap. HC-07 may certify provenance against the declared parent only; it may never adopt the open UV axiom to claim the inventory is complete.
  • Fable_Quantum — BRST/BV physical-state gates. Authority for treating the ghost/auxiliary blocks B_ghost, B_aux as real, enumerated members of 𝓘_par (ghosts are legitimate parent dof, not new primitives) while keeping their physical-state status (Q_BRST|Ψ⟩ = 0, positive-norm) as a downstream gate handled by the quantization leaf, not by HC-07.

What HC-07 may not lean on: it may not assume the parent is UV-complete (Gap-04 open), may not promote a UV-delegated mode, and may not certify "no hidden field" in any absolute sense — only "no field outside the declared frozen inventory."

4. The mode card, the layer assignment, and the two audit predicates

4.1 The mode-card schema

Every candidate that appears in this document carries a gate-card JSON (build contract §3). HC-07 additionally requires, per component, a mode card — the row-level provenance record that the gate card summarizes. The mode-card schema (one card per excitation component) is:

ModeCard:
  component        : str           # e.g. "δG_μA"
  tensor_type      : str           # e.g. "mixed-(1,1) 4D vector × internal index"
  declared_origin  : str           # author's provenance claim
  provenance π(c)  : set[dof_id]   # resolved parent dofs; ∅ ⇒ FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE
  layer            : {×, ⊕, ⊗}     # MANDATORY three-layer assignment
  kk_quantum_no    : tuple         # (level n, internal rep, isometry charge) — the structural key
  chamber_status   : {IN_F+, OUT_F+, UV_BAND}   # for B_mod components
  ledger_role      : {sources_T, pure_gauge, redundant_label, none}
  first_failure    : str           # the component's own first failure, or "none@layer"
  status           : {ADMIT, FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE, FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT, UV_DELEGATED, FAIL_CHAMBER}

The kk_quantum_no field is the structural key that π actually matches on: a component is a perturbation of parent dof d iff it carries d's Kaluza-Klein quantum numbers (level, internal representation, isometry/Wilson charge). This is what makes provenance machine-checkable rather than a matter of the author's prose — two components with the same kk_quantum_no are perturbing the same parent dof, which is the entire signature of a double count.

4.2 The mandatory three-layer assignment

The build contract requires every component to map to a layer. The assignment is not free; it is fixed by the component's role:

Layer Symbol Meaning Which components live here
Metric / geometric base × the geometric substrate being perturbed δg_μν (4D graviton), δG_AB (internal metric moduli), δG_μA as a geometric object
Admissibility / projection / chamber ⊕ the chamber, projector, and modulus-licensing layer δφ^I chamber coordinates of F⁺; the projected/admitted parts of any descendant; δG_μA as a chamber-projected 4D vector
Bundles / operators / quantization ⊗ the gauge bundle, operators, ghosts, quantization data δA_μ^a (gauge connection), B_ghost (c, c̄, b), Σ_gauge, BRST operators

Two facts make the layer assignment load-bearing for HC-07. First, a component with no legal layer is inadmissible by construction — there is nowhere in the frozen discipline for it to live, which is a structural restatement of "new primitive." Second, the layer assignment is exactly where the graviphoton double-count is exposed: δG_μA legitimately appears in two layers — as a geometric object (×, part of the parent metric) and as a chamber-projected 4D vector (⊕). That dual appearance is allowed as a labelling but forbidden as a double entry in the ledger. The no-double-counting audit (§4.3) is precisely the rule that lets the same dof wear two layer-labels while paying into the source/energy ledger only once.

4.3 The no-new-primitive scan

predicate NO_NEW_PRIMITIVE(Ξ):
    for each component c in C(Ξ):
        key   ← structural_key(c)        # (tensor type, kk_quantum_no, transf. under parent symmetries)
        match ← lookup(𝓘_par, key)       # exact match on the frozen inventory
        if match is ∅:
            return FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE at c
    return PASS

structural_key extracts the component's transformation properties (spin/tensor type), its KK quantum numbers, and its charges under the parent gauge/isometry groups. lookup is an exact match against the frozen inventory — not a nearest-neighbour or amplitude-tolerant match. A component matches a parent dof iff it carries that dof's exact structural key. The scan is fail-closed: a key with no match is a new primitive, full stop. There is deliberately no "close enough" branch — that branch is exactly where a smuggled field would hide.

4.4 The no-double-counting audit

The double-count audit is subtler than the new-primitive scan because the same parent dof legitimately appears under multiple labels (a KK descendant is both "part of the metric" and "a 4D field"). The audit therefore operates on the ledger multiset, not on the label set:

predicate NO_DOUBLE_COUNT(Ξ):
    ledger ← empty multiset of parent dofs
    for each component c in C(Ξ):
        for each dof d in π(c):
            if ledger_role(c) == "sources_T":          # only ledger-paying roles count
                ledger.add(d)
    for each parent dof d:
        if multiplicity(ledger, d) > 1:
            return FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT at d
    return PASS

The key design decision: only components whose ledger_role == "sources_T" (i.e. that actually contribute to the effective stress-energy T_eff or to the energy integral) increment the multiset. A component that re-expresses the same dof in a different layer for a different purpose — e.g. δG_μA appearing in × as geometry and in ⊕ as a projected vector — increments the ledger once, because only one of those appearances carries ledger_role = "sources_T"; the other carries redundant_label. This is the operational form of Fable_Forces' "single Einstein-frame metric, no double counting": the dof may be described twice but may source only once.

This is also where the audit can be fooled in exactly one way, which we record as a first failure: if a candidate author mislabels the second appearance's ledger_role, the same dof can be entered twice. The audit defends against this by cross-checking ledger_role against the layer: a ×-layer geometric appearance and a ⊕-layer projected appearance of the same kk_quantum_no may not both be sources_T. (§5.2 worked example exercises exactly this.)

5. The minimal toy closure (G1-level): an explicit admissibility pass with three rejections

We now build the minimal toy. It is small by design — a handful of components against a small slice of 𝓘_par — so that every number is checkable by hand. The toy exercises all three acceptance tests from the source doc: arbitrary fifth field rejected, gauge descendant not double counted, internal mode marked UV-sensitive.

5.0 The toy inventory slice

Use a minimal frozen inventory of five dofs (a deliberately small 𝓘_par):

𝓘_par(toy) = {
  d1 : g_μν           (4D graviton)          block B_grav   layer ×
  d2 : A_μ            (one U(1) gauge field)  block B_gauge  layer ⊗
  d3 : G_μ5           (graviphoton, K^A = ∂_y on S¹_Y)  block B_grav  layers ×/⊕
  d4 : R_{S¹_Y}       (radius modulus of S¹_Y)  block B_mod   layer ⊕
  d5 : c, c̄, b        (diffeo+U(1) BRST ghosts)  block B_ghost  layer ⊗
}
N_par(toy) = 5 distinct propagating-or-ghost dofs.

Every legitimate excitation component must trace to one of d1…d5. Note d3 (the graviphoton) is exactly the corpus's canonical double-count hazard: it descends from the parent metric (so it is "geometry", ×) and it is a 4D vector (so it is "a field", ⊕).

5.1 Acceptance test 1 — arbitrary fifth field rejected (F1 / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE)

Construct a candidate that almost works by adding a tuned scalar:

Ξ_A = {
  c1 = ( δg_11,  4D metric,  forward lobe,  +0.05,  "graviton" ),
  c2 = ( δA_1,   4D vector,  forward lobe,  +0.02,  "U(1) gauge" ),
  c3 = ( δψ,     4D scalar,  forward lobe,  −0.03,  "stabilizer scalar (NEW)" )
}

c3 is the arbitrary fifth field — a scalar ψ introduced solely to soak up the back-reaction and balance the source ledger. Run the no-new-primitive scan:

structural_key(c1) = (spin-2, KK level 0, isom charge 0)        → lookup → d1 ✓
structural_key(c2) = (spin-1, KK level 0, U(1) charge 0, A-type) → lookup → d2 ✓
structural_key(c3) = (spin-0, KK level 0, isom charge 0,
                      NOT a modulus of S¹_Y, NOT a Wilson scalar) → lookup → ∅  ✗

c3 carries a structural key (a charge-0, level-0 4D scalar that is not the R_{S¹_Y} modulus d4 and not an A_A Wilson scalar) that matches no member of 𝓘_par(toy). π(c3) = ∅. The scan returns FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE at c3. The candidate is rejected before any source or energy gate runs — which is the whole point: had c3 survived, the source ledger would have balanced (the tuned scalar would have absorbed the mismatch) and HC-02/G2 would have falsely passed. The first failure is the field's existence, not its dynamics. Worked toy number: with c3 present, the toy source mismatch norm would have read ‖ΔT‖ = 8×10⁻⁴ (apparently balanced); with c3 correctly stripped, the residual mismatch the candidate actually owes is ‖ΔT‖ = 4.1×10⁻² — a factor ~50 larger. The fifth field was hiding a real source failure.

5.2 Acceptance test 2 — gauge descendant not double counted (F2 / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT)

Construct a candidate that uses the graviphoton d3 twice — once as geometry, once as a 4D vector — and tries to enter both into the source ledger:

Ξ_B = {
  c4 = ( δG_15,  mixed-(1,1) geom,  forward lobe,  +0.04,  "metric component G_μ5", ledger_role=sources_T ),
  c5 = ( δG̃_1,   4D vector,         forward lobe,  +0.04,  "graviphoton A^{KK}_μ",   ledger_role=sources_T )
}

c4 and c5 are the same parent dof d3 wearing two labels. Resolve provenance:

kk_quantum_no(c4) = (level 0, isom charge of ∂_y on S¹_Y = +1)  → π(c4) = {d3}
kk_quantum_no(c5) = (level 0, isom charge of ∂_y on S¹_Y = +1)  → π(c5) = {d3}
π(c4) ∩ π(c5) = {d3} ≠ ∅   → candidate double count, escalate to ledger audit

Run the ledger audit. Both components are declared ledger_role = sources_T, so the multiset receives d3 twice:

ledger = { d3, d3 }   →  multiplicity(d3) = 2 > 1   →  FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT at d3

Token FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT. The audit also reports the layer cross-check that diagnoses why: c4 is a ×-layer geometric appearance and c5 is a ⊕-layer projected appearance of the same kk_quantum_no, and the no-double-counting rule forbids both being sources_T. The correct admissible version keeps both labels but pays once:

Ξ_B' = {
  c4' = ( δG_15, geom, +0.04, ledger_role = redundant_label ),   # description only, pays 0
  c5' = ( δG̃_1,  4D vector, +0.04, ledger_role = sources_T )      # pays once
}
→ ledger = { d3 } → multiplicity 1 → PASS_TOY

Worked toy number: the double-entered stress in Ξ_B reads T_00^{(B)} = 2 × (½ |δG̃|² + …) = 3.2×10⁻³; the single-entered, admissible Ξ_B' reads T_00^{(B')} = 1.6×10⁻³ — exactly the factor of 2 the double count manufactured. A screener that took Ξ_B at face value would have credited the candidate with twice the stress (and twice the apparent lobe-sourcing capacity) it actually has. This is the corpus's "no double counting" made quantitative.

5.3 Acceptance test 3 — internal mode marked UV-sensitive (F3 / UV_DELEGATED)

Construct a candidate that excites the internal radius modulus d4 = R_{S¹_Y}:

Ξ_C = {
  c6 = ( δR_{S¹_Y},  internal scalar,  breathing,  +0.10,  "hypercharge-circle radius modulus" )
}

Provenance is clean: π(c6) = {d4}, a legitimate frozen modulus — no new primitive, no double count. But c6 lives in B_mod, so LICENSED_CHAMBER runs. Two sub-checks:

(a) chamber:  does the excited modulus stay in F⁺?
      R_{S¹_Y} background = R̄ = 1.00 (chamber units);  δR = +0.10  → R = 1.10
      F⁺ chamber band for R_{S¹_Y} : [0.62, 1.84]  → 1.10 ∈ F⁺  ✓  (chamber_status = IN_F+)
(b) UV band:  does admissibility require global compactification stability?
      EFT admissibility χ for a breathing modulus:
        χ_grad = (∂δR / Λ_KK)²  with Λ_KK = 1/R̄ ;  δR varies over lobe scale ℓ ≈ 5 R̄
        χ_grad = (0.10 / (5·1)·1)² ≈ (0.02)² = 4×10⁻⁴      ✓ < 1
        χ_R, χ_K, χ_T  ≈ 1e-2…1e-1 (toy)                   ✓ < 1
      BUT: the modulus potential V(R_{S¹_Y}) stabilizing R̄ is set by the GLOBAL
      compactification, which is OPEN (Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1, UNADOPTED).

So the local EFT admissibility χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) = 0.1 < 1 passes, but the mode's admissibility ultimately depends on the global compactification stability that the corpus marks OPEN. By the build contract's UV-delegation rule ("if global compactification stability is required ⇒ status UV_DELEGATED"), c6 is flagged UV-sensitive, not passed:

status(c6) = UV_DELEGATED   (chamber_status = IN_F+, but uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED)

This is the third acceptance test exactly: an internal mode is marked UV-sensitive rather than silently admitted. Token UV_DELEGATED. The candidate is not failed (it is a real modulus, in chamber, locally fine) — it is routed: its closure is delegated to the open UV question, and it may never be promoted past UV_DELEGATED while Gap-04 stands.

5.4 The minimal-toy gate card

{ "model_id": "MID-HC07-TOY", "challenge_id": "HC-07",
  "object_definition": {
    "equations": ["π : C(Ξ) → 2^{𝓘_par}",
                  "ADMISSIBLE = NO_NEW_PRIMITIVE ∧ NO_DOUBLE_COUNT ∧ LICENSED_CHAMBER"],
    "coordinates": "comoving worldline chart; frozen parent M4 × (S¹_Y slice) toy",
    "active_fields": ["δg_μν","δA_μ","δG_μ5","δR_{S¹_Y}","ghosts"],
    "layer_assignments": {"δg_μν":"×","δA_μ":"⊗","δG_μ5":"×/⊕","δR_{S¹_Y}":"⊕","ghosts":"⊗"} },
  "gates": { "definition":"PASS", "negative_controls":"PASS",
    "invariant_check":"N/A-here", "source_check":"N/A-here",
    "gauge_check":"N/A-here", "energy_check":"N/A-here", "causality_check":"N/A-here",
    "uv_boundary":"UV_DELEGATED" },
  "negative_controls": {
    "Ξ_A_fifth_field":  "π(δψ)=∅ → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE (hid ‖ΔT‖: 8e-4 fake vs 4.1e-2 real) → expected REJECT",
    "Ξ_B_double_count": "π(c4)∩π(c5)={d3}, both sources_T → FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT (T_00 2×: 3.2e-3 vs 1.6e-3) → expected REJECT",
    "Ξ_B'_relabelled":  "one sources_T + one redundant_label → ledger mult 1 → expected ADMIT (PASS_TOY)",
    "Ξ_C_modulus":      "π(δR)={d4}, IN_F+, χ=0.1<1 BUT global stability OPEN → UV_DELEGATED → expected FLAG" },
  "first_failure": "unlicensed degree of freedom — new primitive (π=∅), or double count (π overlap both sources_T), or modulus admissibility delegated to OPEN global UV; meta: π complete only against the DECLARED inventory, not the true UV spectrum (Gap-04)",
  "strongest_allowed_claim": "A provenance-keyed admissibility object that (toy-order) rejects an arbitrary fifth field, rejects a double-counted gauge descendant, and flags an internal modulus mode UV-sensitive — retained as a simulation/EFT screening asset only; completeness of the inventory is AUDIT and bounded by the open UV gap.",
  "forbidden_claims": ["working warp drive","proves FTL","solves the energy problem",
                       "negative energy available","global stability solved","UV completion adopted","operational propulsion"],
  "next_closure_step": "E07b: run π + the two audits across the 50-mode catalog; emit per-mode mode-cards + gate cards; tally FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT / UV_DELEGATED." }

The four downstream gates read N/A-here because HC-07 is deliberately narrow: it answers exactly one question (is the field content legitimate?) and routes everything else — source, energy, gauge, causality — onward to its own leaf. uv_boundary = UV_DELEGATED because the toy contains a modulus mode whose closure is delegated.

6. The strong closure path — the admissibility projector 𝒫_adm

The minimal toy detects inadmissibility by hand on a few components. The strong path constructs the projector that enforces admissibility on an arbitrary candidate, with the two audits as its guard rails. This is the build artifact the source doc names (src/modes/mode_card.py, layer_assignment.py, no_new_primitive.py).

6.1 The projector contract

Define 𝒫_adm as the map that takes a raw candidate Ξ and returns either an admitted, deduplicated excitation Ξ_adm or a fail token:

𝒫_adm :  Ξ  ⟼  ( Ξ_adm , audit_report )    or    ( ⊥ , first_failure_token )

Ξ_adm = Σ_{c ∈ C(Ξ)}  𝟙[ π(c) ≠ ∅ ] · 𝟙[ ledger_role(c) ≠ "redundant_label" ] · c
        restricted to components with a legal layer and IN_F+/UV-banded chamber status

𝒫_adm is a genuine projector in the bookkeeping sense — idempotent on its admissible image:

𝒫_adm ∘ 𝒫_adm = 𝒫_adm        (an already-admitted, deduplicated Ξ_adm is a fixed point)

Idempotence is the formal statement that the audit is complete in one pass: applying it twice strips nothing further. This is checkable (§7 negative control nc_idempotent) and is the property that distinguishes a sound projector from a heuristic filter.

6.2 The three guards, in fail-closed order

function 𝒫_adm(Ξ):
    # GUARD 1 — no new primitive (structural, fail-closed)
    for c in C(Ξ):
        if π(c) == ∅:
            return ⊥, FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE at c          # short-circuit: cannot be double-counted

    # GUARD 2 — legal layer (a component with no layer is a structural new-primitive)
    for c in C(Ξ):
        if layer(c) ∉ {×, ⊕, ⊗} or not layer_consistent(c, π(c)):
            return ⊥, FAIL_NO_LAYER at c

    # GUARD 3 — no double counting (ledger multiset, layer cross-checked)
    ledger ← empty multiset
    for c in C(Ξ):
        for d in π(c):
            if ledger_role(c) == "sources_T":
                ledger.add(d)
    for d in ledger.distinct():
        if ledger.multiplicity(d) > 1:
            return ⊥, FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT at d
        # layer cross-check: the same kk_quantum_no may not be sources_T in two layers
        if exists c_i, c_j with kk(c_i)==kk(c_j) and layer(c_i)≠layer(c_j)
           and ledger_role(c_i)==ledger_role(c_j)=="sources_T":
            return ⊥, FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT at kk(c_i)

    # GUARD 4 — chamber / UV licensing (route, do not silently pass)
    status ← ADMIT
    for c in C(Ξ) with π(c) ⊆ B_mod:
        if chamber_status(c) == OUT_F+:
            return ⊥, FAIL_CHAMBER at c
        if requires_global_stability(c):                # Gap-04 dependency
            status ← UV_DELEGATED                        # flag, never fail, never pass
    return Ξ_adm(Ξ), {status, ledger, layers}

The guard order is the fail-closed order from §2.3: new-primitive → layer → double-count → chamber/UV. Each guard fails closed (returns ⊥ rather than a tolerant pass) except guard 4, which routes modulus modes to UV_DELEGATED rather than failing them — because a real modulus in F⁺ is not a violation, it is an open dependency.

6.3 What the strong path can and cannot certify

The strong path certifies, at the level of the declared inventory:

  • Soundness (toy/structural order): every ⊥ it emits is a genuine inadmissibility — no false rejection of a legitimate frozen-inventory perturbation (negative control nc_physical_admit, §9, guards this).
  • No-double-counting completeness: every dof that enters the source/energy ledger does so with multiplicity ≤ 1 (the graviphoton test, §5.2, is the worked case).

It cannot certify, and explicitly delegates:

  • Inventory completeness. π's codomain is 2^{𝓘_par} with 𝓘_par the declared parent. If the true UV spectrum contains a dof not in the declared inventory, a "new primitive" that is actually a legitimate-but-undeclared parent dof would be wrongly rejected — and, more dangerously, the absence of such a dof cannot be certified. This is the meta-first-failure, and it is exactly Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1. Status: irreducibly AUDIT.
  • Second-order provenance. At quadratic order, products of admissible components can carry KK quantum numbers of a third dof (mode-mixing). Whether such composite contributions are correctly attributed is uncomputed here; the linear/structural audit is PASS_TOY, the second-order audit is AUDIT.

7. Algorithms — resolving π and the structural key

The two audits are only as trustworthy as the routine that computes π. The whole HC-07 firewall reduces to one function — structural_key — and one lookup. We specify both concretely so the audit cannot be hand-waved.

7.1 The structural key

A component's provenance is decided by three quantum numbers, none of which is its amplitude:

function structural_key(c):
    # (i) 4D Lorentz transformation type — spin / tensor rank after KK reduction
    spin  ← lorentz_rep(c.tensor_type)            # ∈ {0, 1, 2, mixed, ghost}
    # (ii) Kaluza-Klein data — the level and internal harmonic the component rides on
    level ← kk_level(c)                            # n ∈ {0,1,2,…} on K = K6×S²×S¹_Y
    irrep ← internal_rep(c)                        # rep of isom(K) the harmonic sits in
    # (iii) charges under the parent symmetries
    gcharge ← gauge_charge(c, 𝔤_visible)          # rep of the visible gauge group
    icharge ← isometry_charge(c, killing(K))      # charge under each Killing vector (Wilson/isom)
    return KEY(spin, level, irrep, gcharge, icharge)     # amplitude DELIBERATELY absent

Amplitude is excluded by construction (§2.4): a key is a structural fingerprint. Two components with identical keys are perturbing the same parent dof — that is the definition the double-count audit relies on, and it is why a tiny smuggled scalar (§5.1) cannot hide: its key is checked, not its size.

7.2 Resolving the provenance map

function resolve_pi(c, 𝓘_par):
    key  ← structural_key(c)
    hits ← { d ∈ 𝓘_par : key(d) == key }          # EXACT match, no tolerance band
    return hits                                     # ∅, {single}, or (degenerate) {several}

function admissibility_pass(Ξ, 𝓘_par):
    cards ← []
    for c in C(Ξ):
        c.π ← resolve_pi(c, 𝓘_par)
        if c.π == ∅:                                # GUARD 1
            cards.append(ModeCard(c, status=FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE)); return FAILED(cards)
        c.layer ← assign_layer(c, c.π)              # GUARD 2 (table §4.2); ⊥ ⇒ FAIL_NO_LAYER
        cards.append(ModeCard(c))
    if not no_double_count(cards): return FAILED(cards)     # GUARD 3
    status ← license_chamber(cards)                         # GUARD 4 → ADMIT | UV_DELEGATED | FAIL_CHAMBER
    return RESULT(cards, status)

The degenerate {several} case (one key matching two inventory dofs) is itself a declared-inventory defect, not a candidate failure: it means the frozen inventory was enumerated with a degeneracy, and the firewall raises INVENTORY_DEGENERATE rather than guessing. Fail-closed: the audit never picks a winner.

7.3 Complexity and determinism

resolve_pi is O(|𝓘_par|) per component on an unindexed inventory and O(1) with a hash on the structural key; the full pass is O(n · |𝓘_par|) or O(n) indexed, for n = |C(Ξ)|. It is deterministic and side-effect-free — the same Ξ always yields the same verdict, which is the property that lets E07b cache per-mode cards across the 50-mode catalog. There is no randomness, no threshold the verdict depends on except the explicit χ < 1 EFT band and the F⁺ chamber band, both read from corpus configuration.

8. Candidate-mode preview (the 50-mode library, HC-07 lens)

E07b runs the full classifier; here we preview how representative members of the 50-mode candidate library (source doc 21) resolve under HC-07, to show the firewall bites across all five families. Amplitudes and full gate cards are E07b's; this is the expected first failure per mode, the HC-07 acceptance-test that catches it.

Mode (library #) Family Expected HC-07 verdict Why / which dof
1 pure coordinate transform metric-only ADMIT (then FAIL_PURE_GAUGE at HC-05) all components trace to d1; provenance clean, gauge is HC-05's job
3 Gaussian forward contraction metric-only ADMIT pure δg_μν → d1, single ledger entry

The preview makes the HC-07 thesis concrete across families: the scalar/modulus family is where UV_DELEGATED concentrates (every internal-radius mode is globally-UV-dependent); the gauge-stress and KK/mixed families are where FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE and FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT concentrate (extra stabilizers, double-entered descendants); and the metric-only family mostly passes HC-07 (its failures live downstream, at HC-05 gauge or HC-02 source). The negative-control modes (20, 27, 30, 37, 39, 40) are designed to fire exactly one HC-07 token each — the systematic, machine-checked failure the corpus prizes.

9. Negative controls (the admissibility firewall's own tests)

Per the build contract, each section runs one negative control; the strong path requires a small battery. These are the tests in tests/test_mode_admissibility.py.

Control Construction Expected verdict What it condemns if it fires wrong
nc_fifth_field inject δψ with π = ∅ (§5.1) FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE a provenance map that "rounds" an unmatched key to a near neighbour
nc_double_count graviphoton entered as sources_T in two layers (§5.2) FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT a ledger that counts labels instead of dofs
nc_relabel_ok same graviphoton, one sources_T + one redundant_label (§5.2) ADMIT (PASS_TOY) an over-strict audit that forbids legitimate dual-labelling
nc_modulus_uv R_{S¹_Y} breathing, IN_F+, χ<1, global stability OPEN (§5.3) UV_DELEGATED a gate that silently passes a UV-sensitive modulus
nc_out_of_chamber R_{S¹_Y} driven to R = 2.0 ∉ [0.62,1.84] FAIL_CHAMBER a chamber check that ignores the F⁺ band
nc_physical_admit clean graviton+gauge, all π≠∅, single ledger entry, IN_F+ ADMIT an over-rejecting audit (the soundness mirror of HC-05's over-rejection)
nc_idempotent apply 𝒫_adm to an already-admitted Ξ_adm unchanged (𝒫_adm²=𝒫_adm) a non-projector "filter" that keeps stripping on re-application

The pairing of nc_double_count (must reject) with nc_relabel_ok (must admit) is the analogue of HC-05's two-sided guard: the audit must reject the double entry without rejecting the dual label. The pairing of nc_modulus_uv (must flag) with nc_out_of_chamber (must fail) distinguishes the two modulus outcomes — UV-delegated (real, in-chamber, but globally open) vs. chamber-violating (out of F⁺, a hard fail). And nc_physical_admit is the over-rejection defense: an admissibility firewall that rejects everything is trivially "sound" and useless; this control forces the firewall to actually admit clean physics.

10. Worked numbers summary (the toy ledger)

E07b.0 Where E07a stopped and what this leaf must finish

The companion leaf E07a built the front half of the HC-07 closure path — Steps 1–6 of the BUILD CONTRACT §5 chapter template. E07a deliberately stopped at the layer assignment. It built the cards and proved each component can be typed and routed; it did not run the projector to ground, did not execute the no-double-count audit against a populated ledger, and did not produce the candidate-mode results table with terminal tokens. This leaf, E07b, executes Steps 7–12:

  • Step 7 (Algorithms): the admissibility projector interface Π_adm in production form (§E07b.1); the no-new-primitive scan as a falsifiable production algorithm with residue norm (§E07b.2); the no-double-count audit over the stress-ledger (§E07b.3); and the internal-modes-are-UV-sensitive flagging rule (§E07b.4).

  • Step 10 (First-failure ledger): the ledger terminating in FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE / FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT / UV_DELEGATED (§E07b.7).
  • Step 11 (Reviewer attacks): the four strongest objections and the honest responses (§E07b.8).
  • Step 12 (Patent extraction): the unified excitation data model, layer-assignment engine, and admissibility validator (§E07b.9).

The single non-negotiable carried verbatim from the BUILD CONTRACT (§1.1) and from C3's projector definition governs this entire leaf:

A clean pass of the admissibility gate returns PASS_TOY for the admissibility property only. It does not assert that the candidate is sourced, energy-honest, causal, or UV-stable.

So the strongest token this leaf can ever emit is PASS_TOY, and it emits it for one narrow property: "this excitation imported no new primitive and booked no stress twice." Everything else is delegated downstream (HC-02 source, HC-03 energy, HC-04 causality, HC-08/09 UV) or rejected here.

Notation carried from C3 / E07a (self-contained recap). The frozen parent geometry is

𝓜_parent  =  M4  ×  K_gauge  ×  F+
             (spacetime)  (gauge)  (chamber)
K_gauge  =  K6 × S² × S¹_Y ,   K6 = SU(3)/T²  (dim 6) ,   S²  (dim 2) ,   S¹_Y  (hypercharge circle, dim 1)

F+ is the positive Weyl/holonomy chamber — a discrete admissibility label, dim 0 as a coordinate factor, carrying no independent stress-energy. The field menu descended from this geometry is finite and frozen: gauge indices a ∈ {1..12} (descended from the isometries of K6 ⊕ S² ⊕ S¹_Y), scalar/modulus indices I over the already-present content (including the geometric moduli a_K6, a_S2, r_Y — the radii/Kähler data of the internal factors), the metric g_μν, mixed/graviphoton G_μA, and internal-metric G_AB. A candidate excitation is the typed object

Ξ_drive(t,x)  =  { δg_μν , δA^a_μ , δφ^I , δG_μA , δG_AB , state/gauge data }

Each component c ∈ Ξ carries a kind (one of the eight) and is routed by the layer-assignment engine to a layer ℓ(c) ∈ {×, ⊕, ⊗}: × = metric/geometric base, ⊕ = admissibility/projection/chamber (gates membership, no stress), ⊗ = bundles/operators/quantization. The freeze descriptor of the parent is a content-addressed object

freeze = { coords, factors:{K6,S²,S¹_Y}, F+:"positive", field_menu:{a:1..12, I:[...]},
           frozen_moduli:{a_K6,a_S2,r_Y}, forbidden:{add-index, edit-modulus, open-chamber, bg-offdiag} }
hash    = SHA256( canonical_json(freeze) )

The hash is the tamper anchor: any candidate whose reduction silently edits the menu or a modulus changes the hash and is rejected before its excitation is even read.

First failure (this orientation section). The load-bearing risk of the E07a→E07b handoff is a silent scope slip: a reader treats this leaf's PASS_TOY ceiling as if it certified the drive, when it certifies only the admissibility property (no new primitive, no double count, fully layer-typed, inside F+). Taking any survivor of this chapter as sourced, energy-honest, causal, or UV-stable is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM: admissibility is a necessary, not sufficient condition, and every clean card here carries source_check / energy_check / causality_check = AUDIT and so excludes the word "propulsion" from its strongest allowed claim by fail-closed enforcement (BUILD CONTRACT §3). The recap above redefines ε_adm from C3's normalized ratio ‖Ξ − Π_adm·Ξ‖/‖Ξ‖ ∈ [0,1] to an integer residue cardinality #{c : keep(c)=0}; the two are consistent (both vanish iff nothing is annihilated) but the integer form is the one used throughout this leaf, declared here so no downstream section reads a normalized fraction where an integer count is meant.

E07b.1 Step 7a — the admissibility projector interface (production form)

C3 defined the strong-closure object: the admissibility projector

Π_adm  =  Π_layer  ∘  Π_chamber  ∘  Π_geom        (idempotent: Π_adm² = Π_adm)

acting on the formal vector space 𝓥_Ξ spanned by the candidate's typed components, with a candidate admissible iff it is a fixed point: Π_adm Ξ = Ξ. This leaf turns that operator into a production interface — a deterministic, fail-closed function with a typed contract, a residue object, and a status token — because an operator that is only defined "in principle" is not a gate.

E07b.1.1 The three sub-projectors, as computable filters

The three sub-projectors are diagonal in the typed-component basis — each acts component-by-component and either keeps the component (eigenvalue 1) or annihilates it (eigenvalue 0). This is what makes them commute by construction (a diagonal-operator product is order-independent) and what makes Π_adm a genuine projector rather than an arbitrary map.

Π_geom    (c) =  c   if  ref_indices(c) ⊆ field_menu(freeze)  AND  c does not edit a frozen modulus value
              =  0   otherwise                         # kills new primitives + frozen-modulus edits
Π_chamber (c) =  c   if  chamber_label(c) ∈ F+  AND  c asserts no stress from the chamber
              =  0   otherwise                         # kills out-of-chamber + chamber-as-source
Π_layer   (c) =  c   if  ℓ(c) ∈ {×,⊕,⊗}  (assignment succeeded, exactly one layer)
              =  0   otherwise                         # kills unassignable / multiply-assigned components

The composite annihilates a component if any sub-projector annihilates it (a logical AND of "kept"). The admissibility residue is the annihilated part:

R_adm(Ξ)  =  Ξ − Π_adm Ξ  =  Σ_c (1 − keep(c)) · c        # the components that were killed
ε_adm     =  | R_adm(Ξ) |  =  #{ c ∈ Ξ : keep(c) = 0 }    # cardinality of the residue (integer ≥ 0)

A candidate is admissible iff ε_adm = 0 (equivalently Π_adm Ξ = Ξ). The residue is retained and reported — we never silently drop killed components, because which component was killed determines the first-failure token (a frozen-modulus edit → UV_DELEGATED; a new index → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE; a chamber-as-source → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE via chamber abuse).

E07b.1.2 The projector as an explicit diagonal matrix (worked instance)

Because the sub-projectors are diagonal in the typed-component basis, the composite Π_adm on any finite candidate is a 0/1 diagonal matrix and its action is exhibited by inspection. Take the four-component candidate MID-MIX-031 of §E07b.2.2, ordered (c1, c2, c3, c4) where c1 = δG_μA, c2 = δA^{7}, c3 = δa_K6 (frozen modulus, amplitude ≠ 0), c4 = δχ (a smuggled fifth scalar, index I_max+1). Evaluate each sub-projector's diagonal entry:

component:     c1=δG_μA   c2=δA^7   c3=δa_K6   c4=δχ
Π_geom  diag:     1          1          1*         0      (* c3 in menu, but FROZEN-VALUE-EDIT ⇒ UV-flag, not killed)
Π_chamber diag:   1          1          1          1      (none assert chamber stress; all in F+)
Π_layer diag:     1          1          1          0      (δχ has a layer slot only if its index existed — it does not)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Π_adm   diag:  diag(1, 1, 1, 0)    ⇒    Π_adm Ξ = (c1, c2, c3, 0)
R_adm(Ξ) = (0, 0, 0, c4) = {δχ} ,  ε_adm = 1 ,  menu_dist = 1 (one out-of-menu index ref from c4)

So MID-MIX-031 as written is inadmissible (ε_adm = 1): the fifth scalar c4 = δχ is annihilated by Π_geom/Π_layer and lands in the residue → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE. Note the bookkeeping subtlety the matrix makes visible: c3 = δa_K6 is kept by every sub-projector (its index is in the menu, so it is not a new primitive) yet carries a UV-flag from the frozen-modulus edit. Killing and flagging are different operations — the projector kills new primitives; the UV-delegation rule (§E07b.4) flags admissible-but-UV-sensitive components. Once c4 is removed, the reduced candidate (c1, c2, c3) is admissible (ε_adm = 0) but terminates at UV_DELEGATED because of c3, exactly the §E07b.2.2 result. The matrix form also shows idempotency by inspection: diag(1,1,1,0)² = diag(1,1,1,0), so Π_adm²Ξ = Π_admΞ — the NC-IDEM invariant holds for any 0/1 diagonal.

E07b.1.3 The production interface contract

function admissibility_projector(Xi, freeze, opts) -> AdmissibilityReport:
    # --- input guard (fail-closed) ---
    if Xi is None or freeze is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "missing excitation or freeze descriptor")   # never PASS on absent input
    if sha256(canonical_json(freeze)) != freeze.hash:
        return downgrade("FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT", "freeze descriptor tampered")  # menu/modulus edited

    residue = []
    kept    = []
    for c in typed_components(Xi):           # each c already carries (kind, ref_indices, chamber_label, layer)
        k_geom    = (ref_indices(c) ⊆ freeze.field_menu) and not edits_frozen_modulus(c, freeze)
        k_chamber = (c.chamber_label in F_PLUS) and not asserts_chamber_stress(c)
        k_layer   = (c.layer in {"x","⊕","⊗"}) and assigned_exactly_once(c)
        if k_geom and k_chamber and k_layer:
            kept.append(c)
        else:
            residue.append( (c, reason(k_geom, k_chamber, k_layer, c, freeze)) )

    eps_adm = len(residue)
    # --- idempotency self-test (CI invariant; see NC-IDEM) ---
    assert project(project(Xi)) == project(Xi)

    if eps_adm == 0:
        status = "PASS_TOY"                  # ceiling: admissibility property ONLY
        first_failure = "none-on-this-gate (source/energy/causality/UV still owed downstream)"
    else:
        status, first_failure = classify_residue(residue, freeze)   # FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE | UV_DELEGATED | FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT*
    return AdmissibilityReport(status, eps_adm, residue, kept, first_failure)
    # *double-count is detected by the LEDGER audit (§E07b.3), folded into classify_residue's caller

Three contract properties make this a gate and not a formatter:

  1. Fail-closed on absent/tampered input. Missing Ξ, missing freeze, or a hash mismatch returns a downgrade token, never PASS_TOY. The hash check is what makes "freeze the geometry before you excite it" enforceable: a candidate cannot defeat the no-new-primitive scan by adding its new index to the menu, because that edits freeze, changes the hash, and trips FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT first.
  2. Idempotency as a CI invariant. Π_adm² = Π_adm is asserted at runtime. If a code change ever makes the projector non-idempotent (e.g., a stateful filter that mutates Ξ), the assertion fires and the build is red. This is negative control NC-IDEM (§E07b.5).
  3. Residue retention. The killed components are returned, classified, and exported to the gate card and patent ledger. A gate that throws away its evidence cannot name a first failure; a gate that cannot name a first failure is invalid under BUILD CONTRACT §1.2.

ε_adm = 0 is necessary, not sufficient for any physical claim. It says only: this excitation lives entirely inside the frozen field menu, inside the F+ chamber, and is fully layer-typed. It says nothing about whether the metric perturbation is sourced, energy-honest, or UV-stable. Those are the next four gates.

First failure (this section): a candidate excitation that is not a fixed point of Π_adm (ε_adm > 0), or a freeze descriptor whose recomputed hash does not match its recorded hash (FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT). The projector interface is the operator-level statement of the chapter's first failure.

E07b.2 Step 7b — the no-new-primitive scan (production algorithm)

The no-new-primitive scan is the algorithmic heart of HC-07. C3 gave its skeleton; this leaf gives the production form with the residue norm, the menu-distance, and the explicit eight-kind classifier so the scan is falsifiable rather than rhetorical.

E07b.2.1 What "a new primitive" precisely means

A primitive is a field that the frozen geometry already provides — an entry of field_menu. A new primitive is any field a candidate references that is not in the menu and not a licensed descendant/composite of menu fields. Three sub-cases, each with its own token:

Sub-case Example Why it is a new primitive Token
New field index a 5th scalar δχ with index I = I_max+1; a 13th gauge index δA^{13} no parent isometry to descend from; S¹_Y, S², K6 give exactly 12 FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE
Excited frozen modulus δφ turning on a_K6 (the K6 Kähler/volume modulus) the index is in the menu, but its value is frozen; exciting it re-tunes the compactification UV_DELEGATED
Chamber-as-source F+ asserting T^{F+}_μν ≠ 0 F+ is dim-0 / no stress; "energy from the chamber" invents a primitive ledger FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE (chamber abuse)

The middle row is the subtle one and is the reason this leaf carries a UV_DELEGATED terminal token alongside the two FAIL_* tokens. Exciting a frozen modulus is not a new field — the index exists — so it does not fail the index check. But the modulus value was frozen precisely because changing it changes the internal volume, which changes the 4D effective couplings, which is exactly the open global-compactification-stability question (B-UQFC-14-UV-1, UNADOPTED; see E08). The scan therefore does not reject it outright; it delegates it to the UV boundary and forbids promotion. This is the formal home of the brief's "internal modes are UV-sensitive."

E07b.2.2 The production scan with residue norm

function NO_NEW_PRIMITIVE_SCAN(Xi, freeze) -> ScanReport:
    if Xi is None or freeze is None: return downgrade("FAIL", "missing input")
    residue   = []
    menu_dist = 0          # Σ over components of d_c (0 if index in menu, 1 if not)
    uv_flags  = []
    for c in typed_components(Xi):
        kind = classify(c)     # metric|mixed|internal|gauge|scalar|matter|ghost|auxiliary|chamber
        # (1) layer assignment must succeed
        if layer_of(kind) is None:
            residue.append((c, "UNASSIGNED-no-layer")); continue
        # (2) index references must be in the frozen menu
        for idx in ref_indices(c):
            d_c = 0 if idx in freeze.field_menu else 1
            menu_dist += d_c
            if d_c == 1: residue.append((c, f"new-index {idx}")); 
        # (3) frozen-modulus edits → UV-delegate, do not pass
        if kind == "internal" or (kind == "scalar" and idx in freeze.frozen_moduli):
            if amplitude(c) != 0:
                uv_flags.append((c, "excites-frozen-modulus → UV-sensitive"))
        # (4) chamber must not assert stress
        if kind == "chamber" and asserts_chamber_stress(c):
            residue.append((c, "chamber-as-source"))
    # --- residue norm (instrumentation for manuscript + patent export) ---
    eps_npp = len(residue)                          # admissibility residue cardinality
    if eps_npp > 0:
        return ScanReport("FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE", eps_npp, menu_dist, residue, uv_flags)
    if uv_flags:
        return ScanReport("UV_DELEGATED", 0, menu_dist, residue, uv_flags)
    return ScanReport("PASS_TOY", 0, menu_dist, residue, uv_flags)   # admissibility property ONLY

The menu-distance menu_dist = Σ_c d_c is a single integer that quantifies how far a candidate is from the frozen menu: 0 means every referenced index is licensed; n>0 means n index references point at non-menu fields. It is reported even on a clean pass (where it is 0) so the gate card carries positive evidence of admissibility, not just an absence of failure. The uv_flags list is non-empty exactly when an admissible candidate touches a frozen modulus — the canonical UV_DELEGATED route.

Worked micro-example (so the integers are real). Take a candidate MID-MIX-031 (a KK/mixed excitation from D3's Family 4) declaring three components:

c1 = δG_μA  (mixed, graviphoton, references A^{a=4} ∈ menu)     → kind=mixed,    layer=×/⊗, d=0
c2 = δA^a_μ (gauge, a=7 ∈ {1..12})                              → kind=gauge,    layer=⊗,   d=0
c3 = δφ^I   (scalar, I = a_K6 ∈ frozen_moduli, amplitude≠0)     → kind=scalar,   layer=⊗,   d=0, UV-flag

Then residue = [] (no new index, no chamber-as-source), eps_npp = 0, menu_dist = 0, but uv_flags = [(c3, "excites-frozen-modulus")]. Terminal: UV_DELEGATED — admissible (imported nothing new) but cannot be promoted because c3 re-tunes the K6 volume modulus and delegates to the open UV question. Contrast MID-X5-099 (a candidate declaring a fifth scalar δχ, index I_max+1): residue = [(δχ, "new-index")], eps_npp = 1, menu_dist = 1 → terminal FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE.

First failure (this section): any component whose referenced index is outside field_menu (d_c = 1), any unassignable component (UNASSIGNED-no-layer), or any chamber-kind component asserting stress. Token: FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE. A clean scan that nonetheless touches a frozen modulus downgrades to UV_DELEGATED, never to a clean pass.

E07b.3 Step 7c — the no-double-count audit

The no-new-primitive scan stops a candidate from adding a field. The no-double-count audit stops a candidate from counting an existing field twice — once as an independent primitive and again through the parent it descended from. This is the Fable_Forces "one-parent projection, no double counting" discipline made into an algorithm. It is a distinct gate because a candidate can pass the no-new-primitive scan (every index in the menu) and still cheat by booking the same stress contribution into the source ledger twice, inflating the apparent forward-lobe drive.

E07b.3.1 The descent graph and the single-count invariant

Every menu field has a provenance: it is either a root (the 4D metric g_μν, the genuine independent gauge/scalar content) or a descendant of a root via the compactification (a KK tower mode, a graviphoton G_μA from off-diagonal metric, an internal-metric G_AB mode). The provenance forms a directed acyclic graph Γ_prov:

roots:        g_μν ,  A^a (a∈1..12) ,  φ^I (genuine moduli/scalars)
descendants:  G_μA  ⟵  g (off-diagonal M4×K)        # graviphoton: a metric descendant
              G_AB  ⟵  g (internal block)            # internal-metric mode
              KK_n  ⟵  {A^a or φ^I} (tower index n)  # Kaluza–Klein excitation of a parent field
edges:        descendant → its unique parent root    # one-parent rule ⇒ out-degree exactly 1

The one-parent rule (Fable_Forces) is the structural guarantee that makes the audit finite and decidable: every descendant has exactly one parent edge. A candidate that tries to source a node both as an independent primitive and through its parent is creating a second path to the same stress, i.e. a cycle-free double path — which the audit detects as a node with two distinct ledger entries.

E07b.3.2 The stress-ledger and the audit

Each candidate carries a stress ledger L = { (node, ΔT_node) } — the contribution each component makes to the effective source T_eff^{μν} = M_Pl² G^{μν}[g_bg + δg]. The audit verifies that each independent stress contribution appears exactly once, by checking that no node is booked both directly and via its parent.

function NO_DOUBLE_COUNT_AUDIT(Xi, ledger L, prov_graph Γ) -> AuditReport:
    if L is None or Γ is None: return downgrade("FAIL", "missing ledger or provenance")
    seen   = {}                       # node -> list of ledger entries booking it
    for (node, dT) in L:
        seen.setdefault(node, []).append(dT)
        # walk to the unique parent; if the parent ALSO has an entry that already
        # accounts for this descendant's stress, the descendant is double-booked
        parent = Γ.parent(node)
        if parent is not None and parent in seen and overlaps(seen[parent], dT):
            return AuditReport("FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT", node, parent,
                               reason="descendant booked independently AND through parent")
    # also catch a node booked twice directly (same node, two non-zero entries)
    for node, entries in seen.items():
        if count_nonzero(entries) > 1 and not orthogonal(entries):
            return AuditReport("FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT", node, node, reason="node booked twice directly")
    return AuditReport("PASS_TOY", None, None, reason="single-count invariant holds")

Two predicates do the real work and are worth stating precisely:

  • overlaps(parent_entries, dT) is true when the descendant's stress is already contained in the parent's booked stress — e.g. a graviphoton G_μA whose energy is already inside the off-diagonal metric block that the candidate also books as an independent δg source. The off-diagonal metric and "the graviphoton" are the same degree of freedom; counting both is the canonical double-count.
  • orthogonal(entries) allows the legitimate case where two distinct components contribute to the same node along independent tensor channels (e.g. trace vs. trace-free) and genuinely add. The audit must not false-positive on honest additive sources; orthogonality of the booked tensors is the discriminator.

Worked micro-example. D3's MID-KK-037 declares both δG_μA (graviphoton, a metric descendant) and an independent off-diagonal δg_{μA} source for the same A-direction. Provenance: G_μA ⟵ g. Ledger: {(g, ΔT_g), (G_μA, ΔT_{G_μA})} with overlaps([ΔT_g], ΔT_{G_μA}) = True (the graviphoton energy is inside ΔT_g). Audit terminal: FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT at node G_μA, parent g. The apparent extra forward-lobe stress that MID-KK-037 advertised is an accounting artifact: it counted one degree of freedom along two ledger paths.

First failure (this section): any node booked both directly and through its unique parent (overlaps = True), or any node booked twice directly with non-orthogonal tensor channels. Token: FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT. The audit is the reason a candidate cannot manufacture drive by re-labeling one descendant as two sources.

E07b.4 Step 7d — internal modes are UV-sensitive (the delegation rule)

The brief's fourth Step-7 requirement — "internal modes UV-sensitive" — is a status rule, not a rejection rule, and it is the cleanest place in the document to show downgrade-don't-invent at work. An internal-kind component (one that excites K6, S², S¹_Y geometry or their moduli a_K6, a_S2, r_Y) is admissible (it imports no new primitive; the index is in the menu) and yet cannot be promoted, because changing internal geometry changes the compactification, and global compactification stability is the document-wide OPEN question.

The delegation rule is a single decision:

if  any admissible component c excites internal geometry / a frozen modulus  (uv_flags non-empty):
        uv_boundary  := "UV_DELEGATED"
        forbidden_claims += { "global stability solved", "UV completion adopted" }
        max_status   := UV_DELEGATED        # cannot rise to EFT_CANDIDATE on this path
else:
        uv_boundary  := "PASS"              # admissibility-local; full UV gate still runs in HC-08/09

Two honesty consequences follow directly from BUILD CONTRACT §3 fail-closed enforcement:

  1. UV_DELEGATED is a terminal status, not a way-station. A candidate that delegates to the UV boundary is not "almost passing." It is parked at UV_DELEGATED and the phrase "global stability solved" is added to its forbidden-claims list. The only thing that could move it is the adoption of B-UQFC-14-UV-1 — which is UNADOPTED — and adoption requires owner/attorney escalation (§1.4), never agent self-promotion.
  2. The internal mode keeps option value. We do not delete UV-sensitive modes from the library. They remain TOY_DEFINED/UV_DELEGATED candidates with full gate cards, because if the open UV question were ever independently closed (outside this document's authority), they are the modes that would re-enter the screen. This is the "failure-mode engine with option value" posture: a flagged delegation is an asset, not a discard.

First failure (this section): an internal/modulus excitation reported with uv_boundary: PASS or any claim of "global stability solved" / "UV completion adopted." Token: UV_DELEGATED (forced) and, if the false PASS was asserted, FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION.

E07b.4.1 Why the four gates run in this order (and cost grows monotonically)

The four Step-7 gates run projector → no-new-primitive → double-count → UV-delegation, and the first-failure ledger (§E07b.7) reports the earliest gate a candidate trips. The ordering is not cosmetic; it is a cheapest-first sequence so that the most common and cheapest-to-detect cheats are caught before the more expensive structural checks, and so the reported first failure is the most fundamental one:

Gate Per-component cost Detects Why it runs here
Π_adm projector O(N_comp) — diagonal, one pass new index, frozen-modulus edit, chamber stress, unassigned layer cheapest; a candidate that is not even layer-typed should never reach an audit
no-new-primitive scan O(N_comp · N_idx) — index membership smuggled field index, menu-distance refines the projector's Π_geom kill into a token + integer
no-double-count audit O(N_ledger · depth(Γ)) — graph walk descendant booked twice needs a populated stress ledger, which only exists for components that survived admissibility
UV-delegation rule O(N_flags) — flag scan UV-sensitive internal/modulus mode a status cap, applied last to admissible survivors

The monotone cost (O(N_comp) → O(N_comp·N_idx) → O(N_ledger·depth)) is the engineering reason; the honesty reason is stronger. If a candidate both smuggles a new field and double-books a descendant, the ledger says it failed admissibility first — we do not let it claim "but my ledger was fine" when its excitation was never admissible to begin with. The earliest failure is the load-bearing one, and reporting it is what BUILD CONTRACT §1.2 ("every section names a first failure") demands: a single, most-fundamental first failure, not a basket of co-equal complaints. A candidate that is inadmissible has no meaningful ledger to audit, so the double-count gate is skipped (not "passed") for it — the ledger records gate-not-reached, never a spurious PASS.

E07b.5 Step 8 — negative controls

A gate that never says NO is not a gate. Five controls exercise each failure path; each must produce the indicated token or the gate is presumed broken and the build is red. These run in tests/test_mode_admissibility.py and mirror the three acceptance tests the source doc names ("arbitrary fifth field rejected," "gauge descendant not double counted," "internal mode marked UV-sensitive").

Control Construction Must yield Guards against
NC-5THFIELD candidate MID-X5-099 declares a fifth scalar δχ, index I_max+1 FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE (menu_dist = 1) scan rubber-stamping a new field
NC-DESCENDANT MID-KK-037 books G_μA independently and via parent g FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT at G_μA/g ledger silently summing one dof twice
NC-CHAMBER MID-CHAMBER-077: F+ asserts T^{F+}_μν ≠ 0 FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE (chamber abuse) chamber treated as a stress source
NC-MODULUS MID-MOD-030 excites frozen a_K6 (amplitude ≠ 0) UV_DELEGATED (admissible, not PASS) UV-sensitive mode promoted to clean PASS
NC-IDEM apply Π_adm twice to any Ξ; assert Π_adm²Ξ = Π_admΞ equality (idempotency) a stateful/buggy projector

Two positive controls (the gate must not false-positive) complete the suite:

Positive control Construction Must yield
PC-CLEAN-METRIC MID-METRIC-001: pure δg_μν, all indices in menu, no chamber stress, single ledger entry PASS_TOY (admissibility only)
PC-ORTHO-SUM two components booking the same node along trace vs trace-free (orthogonal channels) PASS_TOY (not a double-count)

PC-ORTHO-SUM is the most important positive control: it proves the double-count audit discriminates genuine additive sources from re-labeled single sources via the orthogonal(entries) predicate. Without it, the audit could pass its negative controls by simply rejecting every multi-component candidate — a gate that is "correct" only by being uselessly strict. First failure (this section): any control yielding the wrong token, or either positive control yielding a FAIL_* (a false positive makes the gate too aggressive and is itself a defect).

E07b.8 Step 11 — reviewer attacks

Attack 1 — "Your whole admissibility check rests on an unverified, non-peer-reviewed corpus (the Fable geometry). Strip the corpus and your gate evaporates." Honest response: Granted in full, and engineered around. The corpus supplies exactly one thing to this leaf: a finite, closed field_menu and a frozen_moduli list. Replace M4 × (SU(3)/T² × S² × S¹_Y) × F+ with any fixed background — even bare 4D Minkowski with Standard-Model field content and no compactification — and feed its menu to freeze, and the projector, the no-new-primitive scan, the double-count audit, and the UV-delegation rule run byte-for-byte unchanged. The corpus content is configuration data fed to a general validator, not a load-bearing physics assumption. What the corpus cannot do is promote anything: it is not peer-reviewed, and the document's claims do not require it to be correct (BUILD CONTRACT §2 honesty note). The gate is a discipline about bookkeeping, and bookkeeping discipline is corpus-agnostic.

Attack 2 — "The double-count audit is a tautology: you defined overlaps to be true exactly when you want a fail. You could hide a real double-count by declaring the channels orthogonal." Honest response: The discriminator is not a free label — orthogonal(entries) is tested on the booked stress tensors themselves (trace vs trace-free decomposition of ΔT), not on the candidate's say-so, and PC-ORTHO-SUM is the positive control that proves the audit accepts genuinely orthogonal additive sources while NC-DESCENDANT proves it rejects the overlapping case. The honest residual weakness: if a candidate's ledger lies about the tensor structure of ΔT_node, the audit can be fooled — but that lie is caught downstream by HC-02, where T_eff = M_Pl² G^{μν}[g_bg+δg] is recomputed from the metric and compared to the declared ledger. The double-count audit is the cheap front-line check; the source gate is the expensive backstop. We do not claim the front-line check is complete on its own.

Attack 3 — "UV_DELEGATED is a euphemism for 'we couldn't make it work, so we punted.' You should just FAIL these modes." Honest response: UV_DELEGATED is a more honest token than FAIL, not less. The internal/modulus modes are genuinely admissible — they import no new primitive and book no stress twice; calling them FAIL would mis-state why they are blocked. They are blocked by a single, named, document-wide open question (B-UQFC-14-UV-1, UNADOPTED), and we refuse to either (a) adopt that open axiom to force a pass (forbidden by §1.3, downgrade-don't-invent) or (b) pretend the mode is structurally broken when it is not. The token tells a future reader exactly what would unblock the mode, and preserves its option value if the UV question is ever independently closed. Punting honestly, with the blocker named, is the design.

Attack 4 — "Idempotency and a hash check are software hygiene, not physics. None of this tells me the drive works." Honest response: Correct, and that is the point. This leaf makes no physics claim about whether any candidate drives. Its ceiling is PASS_TOY for the admissibility property only — "this excitation imported no new primitive and booked no stress twice." The entire value of the gate is negative: it is the cheapest possible filter that throws out the most common cheats (smuggled fields, chamber-as-source, double-booked descendants, UV-smuggled moduli) before the expensive invariant-distance, source, energy, causality, and UV gates run. A candidate that survives this gate has earned only the right to be screened by the next one. The honest framing is: this is the bouncer at the door, not the verdict on the drive.

First failure (this section). The reviewer-attack matrix is only as honest as its completeness: the deepest failure here is a fifth attack we did not anticipate — most dangerously, a candidate engineered so its inadmissibility is not expressible as an out-of-menu index, a chamber-stress assertion, or an overlapping ledger entry (the three things the gate decides), so it slips past all four sub-checks while still being ill-posed. We do not claim the attack set is exhaustive; the gate's decidable surface is exactly "menu membership + chamber-stress + layer assignment + single-count," and any ill-posedness outside that surface is explicitly out of scope for this leaf and delegated downstream (HC-02 source recompute, HC-05 gauge-triviality, HC-09 cutoff). Mistaking this leaf's four answered attacks for a closed defense is itself the FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM this section guards against; the red-team pass is charged with adding any newly found evasion to the negative-control battery (§E07b.5) rather than letting it pass unrecorded.

E07b.9 Step 12 — patent extraction

PATENT EXTRACTION BOX — HC-07 Unified-Mode Admissibility (Projector & Results)

Field / problem. Computer-implemented systems for screening candidate spacetime-metric-interface excitation profiles inevitably accept ill-posed candidates that (i) silently introduce field degrees of freedom absent from a declared base geometry, (ii) treat a non-dynamical admissibility label as a stress source, (iii) double-count a single physical degree of freedom along two accounting paths, or (iv) re-tune a frozen geometric modulus — each of which invalidates any downstream physical figure of merit (e.g. a proper-distance score) by perturbing a moving rather than fixed target. No prior screening pipeline enforces a content-addressed freeze of the base geometry before excitation evaluation, nor a layer-typed projector that fails such candidates closed.

Independent-claim seeds (process + system + medium). 1. A method comprising: receiving a typed excitation object whose components each carry a kind and layer; computing a content-addressed freeze descriptor of an immutable base-geometry object including a finite field menu and a frozen-modulus list; rejecting the excitation when a recomputed descriptor hash diverges from a stored hash (background-drift detection). 2. The method of claim 1, further comprising applying an admissibility projector composed of commuting diagonal sub-projectors that annihilate (a) components referencing indices outside the field menu or editing frozen-modulus values, (b) components outside a declared admissibility chamber or asserting stress from a non-dynamical chamber label, and (c) components lacking a unique layer assignment; and emitting an admissibility residue and an integer menu-distance as the rejection evidence. 3. The method of claim 1, further comprising a no-double-count audit over a stress ledger and a single-out-degree provenance graph, rejecting any node booked both directly and through its unique parent when the booked stress tensors are non-orthogonal, while accepting orthogonal additive contributions. 4. The method of claim 1, further comprising flagging any admissible component that excites internal/modulus geometry as UV-delegated, attaching a forbidden-claims set, and capping the candidate's status below an EFT-candidate level pending external resolution of a named open boundary condition. 5. A system / non-transitory medium executing claims 1–4 and emitting a status-labeled gate card whose strongest allowed claim is constrained by an automated forbidden-promotion scan.

Distinguishing features over prior art. (a) content-addressed freeze-before-excite discipline with hash-based drift detection; (b) a layer-typed idempotent projector as the admissibility operator with retained, classified residue; (c) a single-count invariant over a one-parent provenance graph with a trace/trace-free orthogonality discriminator; (d) a delegation status (UV-sensitive) distinct from both pass and fail, preserving option value. Strongest allowed claim: simulation/EFT-screening method only — no operational propulsion, no working-drive, no physical claim asserted or implied.

Defensive-publication fallback. If unpatentable, publish the freeze-descriptor + projector + double-count-audit triad as prior art to bar others from claiming the screening method.

FORBIDDEN-CLAIM BOX (BUILD CONTRACT §4). This chapter does not assert and explicitly negates: any working warp drive; any claim that the screen proves faster-than-light / proves FTL; that it solves the energy problem / energy solved; that global stability solved (the UV-delegated modes are parked, not solved); that UV completion adopted / UV completion closed (B-UQFC-14-UV-1 remains UNADOPTED); any operational propulsion; negative energy available; quantum gravity solved. No hardware-construction, high-energy-source, reactor, pulsed-power, or beam instruction appears or is derivable. The strongest allowed status emitted anywhere in this leaf is PASS_TOY for the admissibility property only.

First failure (patent section). Several seeds lean on building blocks that are individually well-known software bookkeeping — content-addressed hashing of a configuration object, a feature-flag-like "delegation" status, a diagonal projector, and graph provenance walks are all prior art — so a patentability challenge could read claims 1–5 as generic data-validation tooling and bar them. The defensible novelty is therefore not any single building block but the physics-specific integration: the freeze-before-excite discipline anchoring a finite descended field menu, the layer-typed idempotent admissibility projector with retained/classified residue, the single-count invariant over a one-parent provenance graph discriminated by a trace/trace-free tensor-orthogonality test, and the UV-delegation status as a distinct option-value-preserving token tied to a named open boundary condition. We say this to the examiner up front and fall back to defensive publication (above) if the integrated method is held unpatentable. The strongest allowed claim remains a simulation/EFT-screening method only — no operational propulsion, no working-drive, no physical claim asserted or implied.

E07b.10 What this leaf established (compressed)

The unified-mode admissibility gate is now a production interface, not a slogan. The admissibility projector Π_adm = Π_layer ∘ Π_chamber ∘ Π_geom is fail-closed, idempotent (CI-asserted), hash-anchored against background drift, and returns a classified residue. The no-new-primitive scan emits an integer menu_dist and routes smuggled fields → FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE, frozen-modulus edits → UV_DELEGATED.
