7. Reviewer attacks

The hostile-review packet for HC-08. Each attack is the strongest version of the objection, then the honest response — including, where the objection lands, the downgrade we actually take.

Attack 1 — "You are using UV_DELEGATED as a euphemism for 'we couldn't make it work, so we're hiding the failure behind a label.' A delegated mode is a dead mode; call it FAIL." Response (partial concession, with a real distinction). We concede UV_DELEGATED is not a pass and carries no positive claim — the mode is parked, makes no stability or shortening claim, and forbids "global stability solved." But it is not FAIL either, and the distinction is substantive: FAIL means "the mode is wrong / a coordinate fake / unsourced / overclaims." UV_DELEGATED means "the mode depends on a named, real, open physics problem (B-UQFC-14-UV-1 / Gap-04) that might be closed by an owner/attorney decision we are not authorized to make." Keeping the two distinct is the point: a delegated mode is a correctly-quarantined open dependency, recoverable if and only if the axiom is adopted; a failed mode is dead. Conflating them would either hide honest open problems as failures, or worse, let overclaims hide among honest dependencies.

Attack 2 — "Naming an axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 and declining to adopt it is theater. Either the compactification is stable or it isn't; your refusal to commit is just unfalsifiability dressed up as rigor." Response. The axiom is fully falsifiable — §2.2 states (A)–(D) as concrete, checkable claims (a global minimum with PSD Hessian, a positive barrier ΔV ≥ B_min, a UV-finite scheme-independent ρ_vac, all internal masses m² > 0). We decline to assert them because, as standard physics, they are open: moduli stabilization with a positive barrier is an unsolved compactification computation, and a calculable ρ_vac is the cosmological-constant problem. Asserting an open premise to manufacture a pass is exactly the dishonesty the Build Contract forbids (§1.3: "NEVER invent a missing theorem to make something pass"). Declining to adopt a named, falsifiable, currently-open axiom is the opposite of unfalsifiability — it is stating precisely what would have to be proven, and admitting it has not been.

Attack 3 — "Your FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION for vacuum-energy engineering is overbroad. Casimir energy is a real, measured effect; rejecting any mention of vacuum energy throws out legitimate physics." Response (sharp distinction). We do not reject vacuum energy as physics; we reject it as an engineerable propulsion resource. The Casimir effect is real and computable, but (i) it is tiny, (ii) it is not freely tunable to a "desired value" under a moving ship, and (iii) the total ρ_vac (the quantity a drive would need to control) is the unsolved cosmological-constant value, not the Casimir piece. R2/R3 fire specifically on control/extraction/propulsion claims ("set ρ_vac to a desired value", "negative energy available", "powered by lowered ρ_vac"), not on computing a Casimir contribution as an AUDIT-level term in a source ledger. A mode that merely reports a Casimir term in T^eff_μν with energy_check = AUDIT is delegated, not forbidden; a mode that runs its drive on tuning the vacuum is forbidden. The line is engineering/extraction, not mention.

Attack 4 — "Even your honest UV_DELEGATED modulus modes are dead on arrival: moving r_{S¹_Y} moves the hypercharge coupling g_Y, which is measured. You should FAIL them, not delegate." Response (concession — and it strengthens the chapter). Correct for MID-MOD-S1Y specifically, and this is exactly D2's recorded finding (the r_{S¹_Y} ↔ g_Y(r) lock: moving the modulus moves an observationally-fixed coupling). For that mode the composition is UV_DELEGATED and FAIL_CONSTRAINT — and FAIL_CONSTRAINT is the binding one (an observational contradiction outranks an open-axiom delegation). We carry both tokens and let the stronger govern. The general lesson: UV_DELEGATED is the floor for a UV-coupled mode, not a free pass — a mode can be additionally killed by a constraint gate (as S¹_Y is) or an admissibility gate (as F+ is). HC-08 supplies the UV floor; downstream gates can drive it lower, never higher.

Attack 5 — "Your classifier's only real output is 'this is hard, ask the owner.' There's no physics here, just a routing rule." Response (narrowed novelty, full honesty). Conceded that the classifier does not solve UV physics — by design it cannot, and claiming it did would be the cardinal sin here. The deliverable is precisely a disciplined routing + non-promotion engine: the four-hook dependency surface tied to a named axiom, the overclaim-before-delegation ordering, the structural (R3) load-bearing-dependency test that catches rephrased vacuum-engineering, the adoption-spoof guard (NC-6) enforcing that no agent can self-adopt, and the sticky UV_DELEGATED propagation. The value is in never letting an open UV dependency be silently closed or an overclaim slip through — option value independent of whether B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is ever adopted. We claim the non-promotion workflow, not a UV completion.

First failure (this section). The attack matrix is adversarial only to the depth of the adversary we simulate. First failure: a sharper reviewer finds a vacuum-engineering construction phrased so as to evade both the R2 word list and the R3 dependency test (e.g. routing the ρ_vac dependence through an intermediate field so the mechanism graph hides the load-bearing edge). Mitigation: R3 is run on the transitive closure of the mechanism dependency graph (any path from the propulsion claim to a ρ_vac/UV_wall node trips it), and the red-team pass is empowered to edit this file in place, add the construction to the ledger, and tighten the graph test rather than defend a gap.

8. Patent extraction

Simulation-only, hardware-free assets crystallized by E08b. Source 11 (lines 89, 110) gives the HC-08 patent relevance: "unresolved-theory dependency classifier and status downgrading workflow." We expand to five claimable assets, each useful regardless of whether B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is ever adopted (the contract's option value — indeed most useful precisely because it does not depend on closing the open physics).

  1. Unresolved-theory dependency classifier — uv_boundary_classifier: a method that maps a candidate field configuration to {PASS, UV_DELEGATED, FAIL} by testing dependence on an enumerated set of UV/global-stability hooks {(A) global minimum, (B) positive wall, (C) definite vacuum energy, (D) no light destabilizer} tied to a named, version-controlled, adoption-statused axiom (B-UQFC-14-UV-1), and delegating rather than deciding any dependency whose closing axiom is unadopted. Novel as a non-promotion routing instrument, not a physics solver.
  2. Overclaim-before-delegation ordering + structural load-bearing test — forbidden_promotion_scan: checking assertion/engineering of an open premise (rules R1/R2, lexical) and, critically, the rephrasing-invariant R3 test that trips when a propulsion/effect claim is load-bearing on an open hook via the transitive closure of the mechanism dependency graph — catching smuggled vacuum-energy engineering that a word filter misses.
  3. Adoption-spoof guard — the NC-6 mechanism enforcing that axiom-adoption status is read only from a signed, append-only owner/attorney escalation log and can never be written true by an automated agent; an automated ADOPTED without a valid owner log fails closed to UNADOPTED. A machine-checkable separation-of-authority control.
  4. Sticky-delegation propagation — UV_DELEGATED as a non-clearable flag that propagates unchanged into every downstream gate card, forbids the closed claim "global stability solved", and is cleared only by a logged adoption event — preventing the silent inheritance/laundering of an open dependency across a long pipeline.
  5. Named-axiom status-downgrading workflow + gate card — the end-to-end HC-08 workflow that, for any candidate Ξ_drive, names the exact open axiom its effect depends on, emits a machine-readable gate card carrying the hooks, the axiom id, its adoption status, and the forbidden-claim list, and downgrades to UV_DELEGATED / FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION accordingly — a triage instrument for any simulation program that must remain honest about its dependence on unproven foundational premises, independent of the specific theory.

First failure (this section). Patent value is conditional on novelty surviving prior art. First failure: items 1 and 5 resemble generic dependency-tracking / feature-flag tooling, so a patentability challenge could read them as well-known software bookkeeping. The defensible novelty narrows to the physics-specific combination: the four-hook UV/global-stability surface tied to a named falsifiable axiom, the overclaim-before-delegation ordering, the structural load-bearing-dependency test (R3) for vacuum-energy engineering, and the separation-of-authority adoption-spoof guard — i.e. items 2 + 3 + the integration, not generic flagging. We claim the fail-closed non-promotion workflow for an unproven-foundational-premise dependency, and say so to the examiner up front (cross-ref the I-series prior-art memo).

9. Closure summary

E08b delivered steps 7–12 of HC-08. It named the exact axiom — B-UQFC-14-UV-1 — as a four-part, falsifiable, currently-OPEN premise (§2), and kept it UNADOPTED by wiring the only promotion path through an owner/attorney adoption that no agent may perform. It implemented uv_boundary_classifier (overclaim-before-delegation, five fail-closed exits, the ADOPTED branch unreachable by any agent) and forbidden_promotion_scan (R1 assert / R2 engineer / R3 structural load-bearing). It ran a six-control battery — UV-clean → PASS, modulus-motion → UV_DELEGATED (acceptance test 2), axiom-assert → FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (acceptance test 1), vacuum-engineering → FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (acceptance test 3), F+-chamber → UV_DELEGATED→FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION, adoption-spoof → FAIL. The candidate table shows one UV-clean pass-through, three honest delegations, three overclaim rejections, and zero modes reaching PASS_TOY at HC-08. Two gate cards (a delegated mode and a rejected vacuum-engineering mode — the rejection is the product), the earliest-gate-ranked first-failure ledger, five reviewer attacks with honest downgrades, and five simulation-only patent assets complete the leaf. The three acceptance tests passed by refusing to do three things: adopt the axiom, grant a global modulus claim, or permit vacuum-energy engineering. That is the intended outcome.

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED · chapter ceiling PASS_TOY but no HC-08 candidate reaches it — UV-coupled honest modes terminate at UV_DELEGATED, overclaiming modes at FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION, and the single UV-clean mode (MID-METRIC-001) merely defers to HC-02…HC-04 (all AUDIT); B-UQFC-14-UV-1 remains UNADOPTED. · First failure: UV_DELEGATED — a candidate's effect depends on a hook in {(A) global minimum, (B) positive UV wall, (C) definite/calculable vacuum energy, (D) no light destabilizer} whose closing axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 is OPEN (Gap-04) and which no agent may adopt (fired on MID-MOD-K6, -S2, -S1Y); and FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION — a candidate asserts that open axiom (R1) or claims to engineer/extract vacuum energy (R2) or builds its drive load-bearing on an open hook (R3) (fired on MID-MOD-K6-ASSERT, MID-VAC-ENG, MID-FPLUS-EXC). · What remains to close: (i) an owner/attorney decision on B-UQFC-14-UV-1 — the only lever that could lift any UV_DELEGATED mode, and one outside agent authority (Build Contract §1.4); (ii) for that decision to be possible at all, the corpus's Gap-04 must first be closed by an actual moduli-stabilization + positive-barrier + calculable-ρ_vac proof (the cosmological-constant and global-stability problems — not attempted here); (iii) a signed, append-only owner-log infrastructure so the adoption-spoof guard (NC-6) cannot be forged; (iv) extension of the hook set (A)–(D) and the R3 mechanism-graph closure to catch un-enumerated UV dependencies and rephrased vacuum-engineering. Until (i)–(iv), every UV-coupled mode is parked or rejected. · Patent extraction: unresolved-theory dependency classifier; overclaim-before-delegation ordering with the rephrasing-invariant R3 load-bearing test; separation-of-authority adoption-spoof guard; sticky-UV_DELEGATED propagation; named-axiom status-downgrading workflow + HC-08 gate card — all simulation-only, no hardware, valuable precisely because they do not depend on closing the open UV physics. · Reviewer attack: "UV_DELEGATED is a euphemism for failure you're hiding behind a label, and naming an axiom you refuse to adopt is unfalsifiable theater — either the compactification is stable or it isn't." Honest response: UV_DELEGATED is explicitly not a pass (no stability or shortening claim; "global stability solved" forbidden) but it is also not FAIL — it is a correctly-quarantined dependency on a named, falsifiable, currently-OPEN problem, recoverable only by an owner/attorney adoption of B-UQFC-14-UV-1 we are not authorized to make; the axiom is fully falsifiable ((A)–(D) are concrete checkable claims), and we decline to assert it precisely because asserting an open premise to force a pass is the dishonesty the Build Contract forbids. Naming exactly what must be proven, and admitting it has not been, is the opposite of unfalsifiability — it is the honest face of HC-08.

E09a — HC-09 EFT Cutoff & Backreaction — Object & Target

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED → 2 TOY_TESTED (the four cutoff ratios χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad, the admissibility scalar χ = max(...), and the backreaction object are defined as equations + schema and exercised against two negative controls with hand-computed numbers; ceiling PASS_TOY is not reached — terminal status AUDIT) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

Scope note (HC-09, leaf a of two). This leaf builds the object and the target for the EFT-cutoff-and-backreaction challenge. It answers one question precisely: does a candidate excitation Ξ_drive produce its useful-looking forward-lobe effect using curvature, gradients, and stress that stay inside the controlled effective-field-theory regime, or does it secretly need physics above the cutoff Λ where the truncated action is no longer trustworthy? Concretely it defines the four dimensionless ratios χ_R (curvature/cutoff), χ_K (Kretschmann/cutoff), χ_T (stress/cutoff), χ_grad (field-gradient/cutoff); the single admissibility scalar χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad); and the requirement χ < 1 from the build contract (§2). It builds the minimal toy (a Gaussian lobe whose χ is computable by hand) and specifies the strong path (propagate cutoff sensitivity — ∂χ/∂Λ and a Wilson-coefficient backreaction estimate — into the mission and patent reports). The per-mode χ-table, the dynamic-status machinery, and the propagation results are leaf E09b. Nothing here is a propulsion result. The deliverable is the EFT-validity overlay's specification and its negative-control library — the gate that stops a candidate whose lobe is built out of trans-cutoff curvature from being scored as a drive.

E09a.1 Why this challenge matters (HC-09)

Every other gate in Part E asks whether a candidate's forward-lobe effect is real in some sense: invariant rather than coordinate (HC-01), sourced rather than asserted (HC-02), within the energy budget rather than hiding exoticity (HC-03), causal (HC-04), not pure gauge (HC-05). HC-09 asks something logically prior and quietly fatal: even granting that the effect is invariant, sourced, and causal — is it computed inside the regime where our equations are allowed to be used at all?

The effective action we work with,

S_eff = ∫ d⁴x √(−g) [ (M_Pl²/2)R − (1/4)Z_ab F^a F^b − (1/2)G_IJ ∂φ^I ∂φ^J − V(φ) + L_matter + L_constraint + L_EFT ],

is an expansion, not a closed theory. It is the leading terms of a tower

L = L_(0) + (1/Λ²) Σ c_i O_i^(6) + (1/Λ⁴) Σ d_j O_j^(8) + … ,   O^(6) ∈ {R², R_μν R^μν, R_μνρσ R^μνρσ, (∂φ)⁴, R(∂φ)², …}

where Λ is the EFT cutoff (the mass scale of the omitted physics — heavy KK modes, the compactification scale, whatever UV completion eventually sits above), and c_i, d_j are dimensionless Wilson coefficients expected to be O(1) by naive dimensional analysis. The truncation L ≈ L_(0) is trustworthy only where the higher terms are small corrections. The dimensionless control parameter of every higher term is some local physical scale divided by Λ. When a candidate's lobe is sculpted from curvature √|R|, Kretschmann K^{1/4}, stress |T|^{1/2}, or field gradients |∂φ| that approach Λ, the omitted 1/Λ² operators stop being corrections and become the leading physics — and the leading physics is precisely what we threw away. The truncated screener then reports a confident number that the full theory would overwrite.

This is the most seductive failure mode of all, and it differs in character from the others:

  • A source failure (HC-02) shows up as a measurable mismatch norm.
  • An energy failure (HC-03) shows up as an integrable NEC-violation volume.
  • A cutoff failure shows up as a perfectly self-consistent computation that is simply outside its own domain of validity. The metric is smooth, the source matches, the energy is bounded, the causality is clean — and the entire result is meaningless because it was obtained by extrapolating a Taylor series far past its radius of convergence. The truncated theory cannot detect its own breakdown from inside; the breakdown is only visible by comparing the local scales to Λ, which is exactly what the four χ ratios do.

There is a second, subtler half: backreaction. Even when the background-level scales are sub-cutoff, the candidate excitation Ξ_drive carries its own stress-energy T_Ξ, and that stress curves the background it was computed on. If T_Ξ is large enough to shift the background metric by an O(1) fraction, then the linearized lobe was computed about the wrong background — the perturbative split g = ḡ + δg with |δg| ≪ |ḡ| has failed, and the "small" excitation is actually a large deformation masquerading as a perturbation. A candidate can be sub-cutoff and non-perturbative; HC-09 must catch both.

First failure (this section / leaf). The challenge's signature failure is the trans-cutoff lobe: a candidate that is invariant, sourced, energy-quantified, and causal, yet whose forward-lobe effect is produced by local curvature / Kretschmann / stress / gradient magnitudes that drive χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) ≥ 1, so that the omitted 1/Λ² operators are O(1) or larger and the truncated screener's number is not computed by a valid EFT. Token on detection: when the breach is attributable to a known heavy sector (the compactification scale), UV_DELEGATED; when it is an excitation-control cutoff breach (the local scales themselves reach Λ), FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF. A logically separate event — the excitation's stress shifting its own background at O(1) so the perturbative split g = ḡ + δg fails (β ≥ 1) — carries the distinct token FAIL_BACKREACTION; the two are kept separate (§E09a.2.3, §E09a.7) because a lobe can breach the cutoff with a perfectly small backreaction, and vice versa. The mirror failure — declaring a candidate valid because its χ looks small while a single un-sampled hotspot exceeds the cutoff — is the second failure this leaf must defend against, and §E09a.6/§E09a.8 build the sup-norm and sampling controls for it.

E09a.2 Formal object — the four ratios, the admissibility scalar, and the backreaction operator

E09a.2.1 The candidate, its background, and the cutoff

We work, as everywhere in Part E, with a candidate excitation about a frozen background,

Ξ_drive(t,x) = { δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, Σ_state, Σ_gauge },   g_μν = ḡ_μν + δg_μν,  φ^I = φ̄^I + δφ^I,  …

and a single declared EFT cutoff Λ (units of mass; we use natural units ħ = c = 1, so length⁻¹ = mass). Λ is the lowest scale of physics omitted from S_eff. In this corpus Λ is bounded above by the compactification / lightest-KK scale M_KK of K = K6 × S² × S¹_Y — above M_KK the 4D truncation is simply wrong because the tower of internal modes switches on. We therefore carry Λ as an explicit, declared input (never a free knob tuned to pass), and the leaf's strong path (§E09a.7) makes every verdict a function of Λ so that a hostile reviewer can move it and watch the status change.

Define the Planck mass M_Pl from the action's R coefficient. The two scales obey Λ ≤ M_KK ≲ M_Pl; gravity's own EFT cutoff is M_Pl, but the internal-geometry cutoff M_KK is generically far lower and is the binding one. We never assume Λ = M_Pl (that would be the most permissive and least honest choice); the default is Λ = M_KK, declared per candidate and flagged UV_DELEGATED if unknown.

E09a.2.2 The four cutoff ratios

Each ratio compares a local physical scale, raised to whatever power makes it a mass (so the ratio is dimensionless), to the cutoff Λ. All are pointwise fields over the sampled domain D; the gate uses their suprema, never their averages (a violation is local, and an average hides it).

(R) Curvature ratio. Build a curvature mass scale from the Ricci scalar:

χ_R(x) = |R(x)|^{1/2} / Λ          [R has mass dimension 2 ⇒ |R|^{1/2} is a mass]

This is the control parameter of the R² and R_μν R^μν dimension-6 operators: their contribution to the action relative to the Einstein term is ~ R/(M_Pl² ) · (M_Pl²/Λ²) ~ |R|/Λ² per the NDA estimate, i.e. χ_R². χ_R < 1 ⟺ the R²-type corrections are sub-leading.

(K) Kretschmann ratio. The Ricci scalar is blind to Weyl (tidal) curvature; a Ricci-flat lobe can still have huge tidal curvature. Use the Kretschmann scalar K = R_μνρσ R^μνρσ (mass dimension 4):

χ_K(x) = |K(x)|^{1/4} / Λ          [|K|^{1/4} is a mass]    ← CANONICAL DEFINITION OF χ_K (used identically in E09a and E09b)

χ_K is the control parameter of the genuinely-tidal dimension-6 operator R_μνρσ R^μνρσ. Reporting both χ_R and χ_K separately is load-bearing: a candidate can have χ_R ≈ 0 (Ricci-small) and χ_K ≈ 1 (Weyl-huge), and only χ_K catches it. This is the curvature analogue of the HC-03 lesson that T_00 alone is blind.

Canonical channel definitions (binding on both leaves E09a and E09b). To forbid any a↔b symbol drift, the admissibility scalar is composed of exactly these channels, with exactly these formulas, in both chapters: - χ_R = |R|^{1/2}/Λ — Ricci-scalar curvature ratio (dim-6 R², R_μν²). - χ_K = |K|^{1/4}/Λ — Kretschmann/Weyl (tidal) curvature ratio (dim-6 R_μνρσ²). This is the curvature channel; it is NOT the gauge channel. - χ_T = |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ — intrinsic matter-stress ratio (dim-8 T²/Λ⁴); see §E09a.2.2(T). This is the stress channel; it bounds the matter sector, not the induced curvature (which χ_R already covers). - χ_grad = 1/(Λ ℓ_var) — field-gradient / derivative-expansion ratio. - χ_F = |F^a F^a|^{1/2}/Λ² — gauge field-strength ratio (dim-8 (F²)²/Λ⁴), a fifth, separately-named channel that E09b uses when a candidate carries gauge content. It is reported under its own symbol χ_F; it is never folded into χ_K.

The admissibility gate is χ = sup_D max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad[, χ_F]) < 1. The χ_F channel is null for the scalar/metric toys of E09a (no gauge content) and so does not appear in §E09a.5's arithmetic; it is listed here so E09b's gauge-carrying modes have a named channel rather than overloading χ_K.

(T) Stress ratio. The effective source T_eff (the matched stress from HC-02, in mass dimension 4) sets the scale of matter-sector higher operators and of the curvature it must support via G_μν = M_Pl⁻² T_eff:

χ_T(x) = |T_eff(x)|^{1/4} / Λ ,     |T_eff| := ( T_eff^{μν} T_eff_{μν} )^{1/2}    (a frame-invariant magnitude)
                                                          ← CANONICAL DEFINITION OF χ_T (used identically in E09a and E09b)

We use the full contraction magnitude (not T_00) so the ratio is frame-invariant and catches anisotropic stress. χ_T < 1 ⟺ the source's intrinsic energy scale is sub-cutoff, so matter-sector operators ~ T²/Λ⁴ are corrections. χ_T is deliberately the intrinsic stress scale |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ, NOT the induced-curvature scale √(R)/Λ ~ √(T/M_Pl²)/Λ. The induced-curvature check is already carried by χ_R (via R ∼ M_Pl⁻² T); building χ_T from T/M_Pl² would merely duplicate the curvature channel (it collapses onto χ_R — for the §E09a.5 toy both would read ≈6×10⁻⁵) and would lose the independent dim-8 matter-operator (T²/Λ⁴) bound that is χ_T's entire purpose. This canonical (|T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ) form is binding on both leaves.

(grad) Gradient ratio. Scalar and gauge field gradients control the derivative-expansion operators (∂φ)⁴/Λ⁴, R(∂φ)²/Λ², (∂F)²/Λ². Build a gradient mass scale from the steepest field variation:

χ_grad(x) = max over fields of the dimensionally-correct per-field form below:
  scalar:   χ_grad^φ(x) = |∂_μ φ^I ∂^μ φ^I|^{1/2} / Λ²    [canonical φ has mass dim 1 ⇒ |∂_μφ∂^μφ|^{1/2} is mass² ⇒ /Λ²]
  gauge:    χ_grad^A(x) = |∂F|^{1/3}/Λ     and    |F|^{1/2}/Λ   (field-strength scale)
χ_grad(x) = max over fields of the above.

Equivalently and more robustly, χ_grad is built from the shortest variation length ℓ_var(x) of any field in Ξ: if a field varies appreciably over a length ℓ_var, the derivative expansion's parameter is 1/(Λ ℓ_var), so

χ_grad(x) = 1 / (Λ · ℓ_var(x)) ,    ℓ_var(x) = min over fields f of  |f(x)| / |∂f(x)|  (the local e-folding length).

This length form is what the algorithm (§E09a.4) actually evaluates, because it is robust to which field is steepest and reduces cleanly for each component.

E09a.2.3 The admissibility scalar and the contract gate

The single number the gate consumes is the sup over the domain of the max over ratios:

χ ≡ sup_{x ∈ D}  max( χ_R(x), χ_K(x), χ_T(x), χ_grad(x) ).            (the build-contract admissibility scalar)

The build-contract requirement (§2, "EFT admissibility") is literally:

χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1.                                   ← the gate.

χ < 1 ⟹ every omitted higher operator is a sub-leading correction at every sampled point ⟹ the truncated S_eff is a valid description of the candidate ⟹ uv_boundary may read PASS (subject to the other gates). χ ≥ 1 ⟹ at least one local scale meets or exceeds the cutoff ⟹ the truncation is not valid there ⟹ downgrade. The max is deliberately the worst of the four (fail-closed): a candidate is only as valid as its least-valid ratio. The sup over D is deliberately the worst point (fail-closed): one trans-cutoff hotspot invalidates the lobe.

We also define a margin m = 1 − χ and a near-cutoff band χ ∈ [χ_audit, 1) (default χ_audit = 0.3) in which the candidate is PASS_TOY but flagged AUDIT — because at χ = 0.3 the leading omitted operator is already a ~9% correction and the screener's two-significant-figure S_L is no longer reliable. The gate is therefore three-valued, not two-valued:

Condition Verdict Token
χ < χ_audit (default 0.3) EFT regime clean PASS_TOY (cutoff sub-gate clean)
χ_audit ≤ χ < 1 near-cutoff, corrections non-negligible AUDIT (cutoff-marginal)
χ ≥ 1, breach from known heavy sector trans-cutoff via compactification UV_DELEGATED
χ ≥ 1, breach from excitation control (β still sub-unity) trans-cutoff: truncated EFT invalid there FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF (cutoff breach)
β ≥ 1 (separately) perturbative split g=ḡ+δg invalid FAIL_BACKREACTION

Note the deliberate separation: a χ-breach (a cutoff failure — local scales reach Λ) is not the same event as a β-breach (a perturbative-control failure — δg is not small). A candidate can have a tiny β yet χ ≥ 1 (NC-2: a sub-stress but spatially-sharp lobe), so tagging a pure cutoff breach FAIL_BACKREACTION would be a mislabel — backreaction did not fail. We therefore carry a distinct token FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF for the cutoff breach and reserve FAIL_BACKREACTION strictly for β ≥ 1. (Both are FAIL-class downgrades under the contract's downgrade tree; neither promotes anything.)

E09a.2.4 The backreaction object

The four ratios test whether local scales are sub-cutoff. Backreaction tests whether the perturbative split itself is valid: was δg actually small compared to ḡ, given the stress T_Ξ the excitation carries? Define the excitation's own stress (the second-order-in-Ξ piece of T_eff, the part that gravitates the background rather than living on it):

T_Ξ_μν  =  (effective stress carried by Ξ itself, e.g. for a scalar:  ∂_μ δφ ∂_ν δφ − (1/2) ḡ_μν (∂δφ)² + … ).

The backreaction ratio compares the metric shift this stress would induce to the background metric it was computed on. Two equivalent, complementary forms:

β_amp(x)  = |δg_μν(x)| / |ḡ_μν(x)|                         (amplitude form — is the perturbation small?)
β_dyn(x)  = | M_Pl⁻² T_Ξ_μν(x) | · ℓ_var(x)²               (dynamical form — does Ξ's stress curve ḡ at O(1) over the lobe?)
β(x)      = max(β_amp(x), β_dyn(x)) ,     β ≡ sup_{x∈D} β(x).

β_dyn is the physically sharp one: M_Pl⁻² T_Ξ is the curvature Ξ sources, and multiplying by the lobe scale² ℓ_var² converts it to the dimensionless metric deformation Ξ would produce over its own size. The perturbative-background assumption is valid iff β < 1 (and comfortably so for AUDIT vs clean, with the same 0.3 band). The backreaction object is reported alongside χ; the candidate is EFT-admissible only if both χ < 1 and β < 1. The downgrade token for a β-breach is FAIL_BACKREACTION precisely (the perturbation was never a perturbation).

E09a.2.5 Three-layer mapping (every ratio maps to a layer)

Quantity What it bounds Layer (×/⊕/⊗) First failure it guards
χ_R = |R|^{1/2}/Λ scalar-curvature higher operators (R², R_μν²) × metric/geometric base Ricci-driven trans-cutoff lobe
χ_K = |K|^{1/4}/Λ tidal/Weyl higher operator (R_μνρσ²) × metric/geometric base Ricci-flat-but-Weyl-huge lobe
χ_T = |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ matter-sector operators (T²/Λ⁴) ⊕ admissibility/source coupling trans-cutoff source scale
χ_grad = 1/(Λ ℓ_var) derivative expansion ((∂φ)⁴, R(∂φ)², (∂F)²) ⊗ bundle/operator (fields) steep-gradient sub-grid hotspot
β = max(β_amp, β_dyn) validity of g = ḡ + δg split × (back-acts on base) non-perturbative excitation

Every component of Ξ that can carry a trans-cutoff scale is covered, and every ratio names a distinct failure it alone catches. A "validity" reading not on this list is not a legitimate EFT-admissibility statement.

E09a.3 Corpus authority — what licenses the cutoff gate, and what it forbids

  • The build contract (§2, "EFT admissibility") supplies the gate verbatim: χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1, and the UV-delegation rule: "if global compactification stability is required ⇒ status = UV_DELEGATED." This is the controlling authority for the entire leaf — the four-ratio max, the <1 threshold, and the delegation token are not our invention but the contract's. We may compute and report them; we may not weaken the threshold, drop a ratio, or convert a delegation into a closed claim.
  • Fable_GUT supplies the geometry whose isometry/compactification scale sets the cutoff Λ ≤ M_KK. The frozen parent M4 × K_gauge × F+, K6 = SU(3)/T², S², S¹_Y, the F+ chamber and freeze discipline fix the lightest internal mode M_KK and therefore the binding cutoff. We use it to name and bound Λ; we may not use it to claim a working drive, a UV completion, or that the compactification is globally stable (that is the open boundary — HC-08).
  • Fable_Forces supplies the single Einstein-frame metric and the shared/visible stress-energy coupling, no double counting, which is what makes χ_T and β_dyn well-posed: there is one T_eff and one background it curves, so "the excitation's own stress backreacts on the background" is a single, non-double-counted statement. We use it for the source/curvature interface; we may not treat the graviphoton's descendant stress as a free extra source (that double-count is condemned in D3 §6.1 and would corrupt χ_T).
  • Fable_Quantum supplies the discipline that the interacting quantum corrections to the Wilson coefficients are not closed: the BRST/BV physical-state gates fix the classical/free sector, but c_i(μ) running and the interacting UV completion stay AUDIT (Gap-04, B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED). We use this to keep our Wilson-coefficient estimates at O(1) NDA values flagged AUDIT, never computed-and-closed; we may not claim "quantum gravity solved" or that the higher operators are known.
  • TOE_FINAL diff fixes the status boundary that makes HC-09's downgrade mandatory: global UV stability is OPEN, the axiom UNADOPTED. Therefore whenever a candidate's sub-cutoff validity depends on the compactification being stable above Λ, the leaf must read UV_DELEGATED — it cannot close the UV boundary itself.

Honesty note (per contract §2). The four ratios and the χ < 1 gate are reachable against standard effective field theory — naive dimensional analysis, the derivative/curvature expansion, and the perturbative-background criterion are textbook (Burgess, Donoghue, Weinberg-EFT), not Fable-specific. We therefore reach every verdict corpus-agnostically and say so. The corpus enters only to fix the numerical value of Λ (via M_KK of K6 × S² × S¹_Y) and to forbid closing the UV boundary (TOE_FINAL OPEN). Where Λ is unknown we carry it as a declared parameter and report χ(Λ), never a single magic number.

First failure (this section). Borrowed-authority overclaim — reading more out of the corpus than it licenses: using Fable_GUT to assert the compactification is stable (it only names M_KK), or treating an NDA O(1) Wilson estimate as a computed coefficient (Fable_Quantum's interacting sector is AUDIT). The detector is the per-corpus USE/NOT split above; on fire the token is UV_DELEGATED (stability) or AUDIT_QUANTUM (coefficients). This section's authority licenses measurement and bounding only, never closure.

E09a.4 Closure target for E09a

This leaf is the object-and-target half of the HC-09 closure. Its target is not the finished per-mode χ-table or the dynamic-status propagation (those are E09b) but a fully specified, negative-control-validated EFT-admissibility-engine contract, hitting these levels:

  1. Definition gate (1 TOY_DEFINED) — the four ratios χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad, the admissibility scalar χ = sup max(...), the three-valued threshold (PASS_TOY/AUDIT/breach), the backreaction object β = max(β_amp, β_dyn), the cutoff Λ ≤ M_KK, and the layer mapping are all written as equations + coordinates + active fields + layer assignment. (§E09a.2.)
  2. Negative-control gate (2 TOY_TESTED) — at least two deterministic controls exist with hand-computed χ: (NC-1) a flat/trivial profile that must read χ ≈ 0, β ≈ 0 (the zero-point — proves the ratios don't manufacture a breach); and (NC-2) a known trans-cutoff profile whose χ ≥ 1 is computable in closed form (the tripwire — proves the gate fires and downgrades). A third control (NC-3, the Ricci-flat-but-Weyl-large profile) certifies that χ_K catches what χ_R misses. Each is worked with explicit numbers so CI can golden-test it. (§E09a.8.)
  3. The minimal toy with real numbers — a single Gaussian-lobe candidate carried end-to-end: pick δg, δφ, an assumed Λ, compute R, K, T_eff, ℓ_var, all four ratios, χ, and β, by hand, and read the verdict. (§E09a.5.)
  4. The strong-path specification — define ∂χ/∂Λ (cutoff sensitivity), the Wilson-coefficient backreaction estimate, and the contract by which both are propagated into the mission overlay and the patent report. (§E09a.7.)
  5. Two-sided acceptance target — state, as a falsifiable contract, both sides: - (A) Soundness of breach detection: every trans-cutoff candidate (χ ≥ 1 at some sampled point, or β ≥ 1) is downgraded (UV_DELEGATED for a heavy-sector cutoff breach / FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF for an excitation-control cutoff breach / FAIL_BACKREACTION for a β ≥ 1 perturbative-split breach); no trans-cutoff candidate reads PASS_TOY. - (B) No false breach: no genuinely sub-cutoff, perturbative candidate is downgraded by a sampling artifact or a units error. The evidence that the E09b engine meets (A) and (B) is E09b's job; E09a's job is to make (A) and (B) precise and to build the controls that test them.

Ceiling for the leaf: PASS_TOY — and we do not reach it. The terminal status is AUDIT, because (i) the gate is sampling-bounded — χ = sup_D is only a sup over the sampled D, so a sub-grid trans-cutoff hotspot can escape (a χ < 1 reading is "no breach detected on D," never "no breach exists"); (ii) the cutoff Λ is itself only bounded, not known (Λ ≤ M_KK, and M_KK rests on the OPEN compactification boundary), so every verdict carries a UV_DELEGATED shadow; and (iii) the Wilson coefficients c_i are NDA O(1) estimates flagged AUDIT, never computed. We name all three and stop.

First failure (this section). Target-creep — mistaking E09a's object-and-target deliverable for the closure itself, i.e. reading the two-sided acceptance contract (A)/(B) as evidence already met rather than as the contract E09b must satisfy. The detector is the explicit ceiling above (terminal AUDIT, not PASS_TOY) and the three independent caps (i)–(iii); on fire the token is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION (claiming a closure this leaf does not deliver). E09a defines and controls the gate; it does not run it.

E09a.5 Minimal toy closure — a Gaussian lobe carried through χ and β by hand (Step 5)

We build the smallest non-trivial candidate that exercises all four ratios and the backreaction object, and we compute every number by hand so the result is a CI golden fixture. All quantities are in Λ-units (set Λ = 1 and restore at the end), which is the honest way to present a cutoff gate: every breach is "this many cutoffs."

E09a.5.1 The toy candidate

A static, spherically-symmetric scalar "lobe" sourcing a small metric perturbation about flat space, the minimal stand-in for a forward-lobe mode:

ḡ_μν = η_μν  (flat background) ;   δφ(r) = A · exp(−r²/(2σ²))  (a Gaussian scalar bump of amplitude A, width σ) ;
δg_μν induced at linear order via  G_μν = M_Pl⁻² T_φ_μν .

Two declared dimensionless inputs (everything is Λ-units, so σ is a length = 1/(mass)):

A = 0.05  (dimensionless field amplitude in Λ-units, i.e. δφ_max = 0.05 Λ) ;
σ = 5     (lobe width = 5 / Λ , i.e. five cutoff-lengths wide — a "gentle" lobe) ;
Λ = M_KK  (declared; we carry it symbolically and set =1 for the arithmetic) ;
M_Pl = 100 Λ  (a declared, deliberately-conservative hierarchy: cutoff two decades below Planck).

E09a.5.2 The gradient ratio χ_grad (the binding one for a gentle lobe)

The scalar's gradient is ∂_r δφ = −(r/σ²) A e^{−r²/2σ²}, maximized in magnitude at r = σ where |∂_r δφ|_max = (A/σ) e^{−1/2} = (0.05/5)(0.6065) = 6.07×10⁻³ (in Λ²-units). The local e-folding length there is ℓ_var = |δφ|/|∂δφ|. At r = σ, |δφ| = A e^{−1/2} = 0.05·0.6065 = 0.0303 and |∂δφ| = 6.07×10⁻³, so ℓ_var = 0.0303 / 6.07×10⁻³ = 5.0 (= σ, as expected for a Gaussian: its variation length is its width). Then

χ_grad = 1 / (Λ · ℓ_var) = 1 / (1 · 5) = 0.20.

Reading: χ_grad = 0.20 < 0.3 ⟹ sub-cutoff but approaching the AUDIT band's lower edge — a five-cutoff-wide lobe has a 20% derivative-expansion parameter. A one-cutoff-wide lobe (σ = 1) would give χ_grad = 1.0 — an outright breach — which is the whole point: lobe sharpness is the first thing that breaks EFT validity.

E09a.5.3 The stress ratio χ_T

The scalar stress magnitude is dominated by the gradient term T_φ ~ (∂δφ)². Its invariant magnitude scale (mass⁴) peaks near r = σ: |T_φ| ≈ (∂_r δφ)² = (6.07×10⁻³)² = 3.68×10⁻⁵ (in Λ⁴-units; the potential term is smaller for a free/gentle bump). Then

χ_T = |T_eff|^{1/4} / Λ = (3.68×10⁻⁵)^{1/4} / 1 = 0.0779 ≈ 0.078.

Reading: χ_T ≈ 0.08 < 0.3 ⟹ the source's intrinsic energy scale is comfortably sub-cutoff. Matter-sector higher operators are ~ χ_T⁴ ≈ 4×10⁻⁵ corrections — negligible. (Note χ_T < χ_grad: for a gradient-dominated lobe the derivative expansion bites before the stress magnitude does — exactly why both ratios are needed.)

E09a.5.4 The curvature ratios χ_R, χ_K

Linear Einstein equations give R ~ M_Pl⁻² T_φ (the curvature the source induces). With M_Pl = 100 Λ, M_Pl⁻² = 10⁻⁴ (in Λ⁻²-units):

|R| ≈ M_Pl⁻² |T_φ^trace-scale| ≈ 10⁻⁴ · 3.68×10⁻⁵ = 3.68×10⁻⁹  (Λ²-units)
χ_R = |R|^{1/2}/Λ = (3.68×10⁻⁹)^{1/2} = 6.07×10⁻⁵.

Kretschmann for a weak, smooth induced curvature is, as an order-of-magnitude estimate only (K = R² is not an identity — Kretschmann K = R_μνρσR^μνρσ equals R² only up to O(1) factors in special cases; we use it here because this toy's induced curvature is Ricci-dominated with no independent Weyl part, so the O(1) factor is irrelevant to the magnitude), K ≈ R² ~ (3.68×10⁻⁹)² = 1.35×10⁻¹⁷ (Λ⁴-units), so

χ_K = |K|^{1/4}/Λ = (1.35×10⁻¹⁷)^{1/4} = 6.07×10⁻⁵ ≈ χ_R   (consistent: this toy has no independent Weyl excess).

Reading: χ_R ≈ χ_K ≈ 6×10⁻⁵ ≪ 1 — utterly negligible. The lesson is structural: because gravity is weak (M_Pl⁻² = 10⁻⁴ suppresses induced curvature), the curvature ratios are tiny while the gradient ratio is the binding constraint. A reviewer who checked only curvature would declare this lobe gloriously valid and miss that its sharpness (χ_grad) is the real limit. The max over four ratios is what makes the gate honest.

E09a.5.5 The admissibility scalar and the backreaction ratio

χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) = max(6.07×10⁻⁵, 6.07×10⁻⁵, 0.078, 0.20) = 0.20   (binding ratio: χ_grad).

Backreaction, amplitude form: the induced |δg|/|ḡ|. Linearized, δg ~ M_Pl⁻² ∫ T_φ over the lobe; dimensionally |δg| ~ M_Pl⁻² |T_φ| σ² = 10⁻⁴ · 3.68×10⁻⁵ · 25 = 9.2×10⁻⁸, so β_amp ≈ 9.2×10⁻⁸ ≪ 1. Dynamical form: β_dyn = |M_Pl⁻² T_Ξ| ℓ_var² = 10⁻⁴ · 3.68×10⁻⁵ · 25 = 9.2×10⁻⁸. Hence

β = max(β_amp, β_dyn) ≈ 9.2×10⁻⁸ ≪ 1   ⟹ perturbative split valid by ~7 orders of margin.

E09a.5.6 Verdict of the minimal toy

χ = 0.20  (< 0.3) ,  β = 9.2×10⁻⁸  (≪ 1)   ⟹  cutoff sub-gate: PASS_TOY (EFT regime clean), margin m = 0.80.

But the first failure is already visible in the toy: the verdict is binding on χ_grad, and χ_grad = 1/(Λσ) scales as 1/σ. The same candidate at σ = 1.5 (a lobe 1.5 cutoff-lengths wide) gives χ_grad = 0.67 → AUDIT; at σ = 1 gives χ_grad = 1.0 → breach. The toy thus demonstrates the gate's teeth without us having to invent a pathological mode: forward lobes want to be sharp (a sharp lobe is what shortens proper distance over a short baseline), and sharpness is exactly what pushes χ_grad → 1. The drive's own design pressure runs toward the cutoff. That tension — sharper lobe ⇒ bigger S_L ⇒ bigger χ_grad — is the physics HC-09 exists to surface, and E09b quantifies it as the S_L-vs-χ Pareto frontier per mode.

χ_grad 1/(Λ ℓ_var), ℓ_var = σ = 5 0.20 binding; approaching AUDIT band
χ_T |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ 0.078 clean

E09a.6 Strong closure path — propagating cutoff sensitivity (Step 6)

The minimal toy returns a single χ at a single declared Λ. The strong path's job — per the source doc's strong-closure line, "Propagate cutoff sensitivity into mission and patent reports" — is to make every downstream artifact a function of Λ, and to expose the backreaction-via-Wilson-coefficients correction. Three components.

E09a.6.1 Cutoff sensitivity ∂χ/∂Λ and the breach-Λ

Because every ratio is (local scale)/Λ (or 1/(Λ ℓ)), χ is exactly ∝ 1/Λ for the curvature/stress/gradient ratios. Therefore the breach cutoff — the value of Λ at which χ hits 1 — is closed-form:

Λ_breach = sup_{x∈D} max( |R|^{1/2}, |K|^{1/4}, |T_eff|^{1/4}, 1/ℓ_var ).

A candidate is EFT-valid iff the declared cutoff exceeds Λ_breach: Λ > Λ_breach ⟺ χ < 1. This recasts the whole gate as a single physically transparent statement — "the candidate needs the cutoff to be at least Λ_breach; is the actual cutoff above that?" — and makes the sensitivity trivial: ∂χ/∂Λ = −χ/Λ. The strong-path report ships Λ_breach per candidate, not just χ, so a reviewer who disputes Λ = M_KK can read off instantly whether their preferred Λ clears it. For the §E09a.5 toy: Λ_breach = max(6.07×10⁻⁵, 6.07×10⁻⁵, 0.0779, 1/5) = 0.20 (in the same scale units), i.e. the lobe is valid for any Λ > 0.20·(scale) — comfortable margin to M_KK.

E09a.6.2 The Wilson-coefficient backreaction band (AUDIT)

The NDA estimate took c_i ~ O(1). Honest UV-agnostic practice carries a band c_i ∈ [c_min, c_max] (default [1/(4π)², (4π)²], the strong/weak-coupling NDA window) and propagates it: the leading omitted-operator correction to any observable O (e.g. S_L) is

ΔO/O  ≈  c_lead · χ_*²  ,   χ_* = the binding ratio,   c_lead ∈ [c_min, c_max].

For the toy (χ_* = χ_grad = 0.20): ΔS_L/S_L ∈ [ (1/(4π)²)(0.04), (4π)²(0.04) ] = [2.5×10⁻⁴, 6.3]. The upper edge exceeding 1 is itself a finding: even at χ = 0.2, a strongly-coupled UV completion could shift S_L by O(1). This is why χ ∈ [0.3,1) is AUDIT and why the toy at χ = 0.20 is "clean but flagged near the band." The band is reported, never collapsed to a point — collapsing it would be the forbidden "Wilson coefficients known" overclaim. Status of the band: AUDIT (Fable_Quantum: interacting sector not closed).

E09a.6.3 Propagation contract into mission and patent reports

Every downstream consumer inherits the cutoff state through a structured handoff (the mission overlay of HC-10, the patent's validity-overlay claim of I1):

EFTValidityRecord = {
  chi: float, chi_breakdown: {R,K,T,grad}, binding_ratio: str,
  Lambda_declared: float, Lambda_breach: float, margin_m: 1 − chi,
  beta: float, beta_form: "amp|dyn",
  wilson_band: [c_min, c_max], deltaSL_over_SL_band: [lo, hi],
  status: "PASS_TOY|AUDIT|UV_DELEGATED|FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF|FAIL_BACKREACTION",
  sampled_domain_only: true,        # the honesty flag — χ is a sup over D, not over all space
  uv_note: "Lambda <= M_KK; M_KK rests on OPEN compactification boundary (TOE_FINAL); UV_DELEGATED if Lambda unknown"
}

Contract: no mission plot (S_L-vs-trajectory) may render without an attached EFTValidityRecord; if status ∈ {AUDIT, UV_DELEGATED, FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF, FAIL_BACKREACTION} the plot is watermarked with the status and the deltaSL_over_SL_band (so a near-cutoff S_L is never shown as a crisp number); any FAIL-class record (FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF or FAIL_BACKREACTION) blocks the plot entirely — for FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF the S_L was computed by a truncated EFT outside its domain of validity, for FAIL_BACKREACTION it was computed about an invalid background; either way the number is not trustworthy. This is the fail-closed coupling of HC-09 into HC-10, mirroring the HC-04 causality-overlay rule.

First failure (this section). Sensitivity-as-knob — using the closed-form Λ_breach/∂χ/∂Λ machinery the wrong way: raising the declared Λ toward M_Pl until Λ > Λ_breach to manufacture a pass, or collapsing the Wilson band [c_min,c_max] to a point to claim the correction is "known." The detector is the UV_DELEGATED flag on any candidate whose validity needs Λ > M_KK (F5) and the band-never-a-point rule of §E09a.6.2; on fire the token is UV_DELEGATED (knob abuse) or AUDIT_QUANTUM (band collapse). The strong path reports sensitivity so a reviewer can move Λ and watch the status change — it is never a lever the author may pull to pass.

E09a.7 Algorithm / pseudocode (Step 7) — the cutoff-ratio and backreaction engine

The minimal functions the source doc requires (src/eft/cutoff_ratios.py, src/eft/backreaction.py) reduce to two routines plus a verdict mapper. All operate on sampled fields over D; all return suprema and worst-point locations, never averages.

# ---- src/eft/cutoff_ratios.py ----
function cutoff_ratios(Xi, background, Lambda, domain D):
    # Xi: candidate excitation fields; background: (g_bar, phi_bar, A_bar); Lambda: declared cutoff (mass)
    chi_R = chi_K = chi_T = chi_grad = 0.0
    worst = {}
    for x in sample_grid(D):                                  # deterministic Fibonacci/Sobol grid + adaptive refine
        R   = ricci_scalar(g_bar + Xi.dg, x)                 # from validated tensor engine (F1)
        K   = kretschmann(g_bar + Xi.dg, x)                  # R_{abcd}R^{abcd}
        Teff= source_magnitude(matched_T_eff(Xi, x))         # (T^{ab}T_{ab})^{1/2}, from HC-02 matcher — NOT the ansatz
        lvar= min_efolding_length(Xi, x)                     # min over fields of |f|/|∂f|
        cR = sqrt(abs(R))/Lambda
        cK = abs(K)**0.25/Lambda
        cT = abs(Teff)**0.25/Lambda
        cG = 1.0/(Lambda*lvar)
        for (name, val) in [("R",cR),("K",cK),("T",cT),("grad",cG)]:
            if val > worst.get(name, -1): worst[name] = (val, x)   # track sup AND its location
        chi_R, chi_K, chi_T, chi_grad = map(max, [chi_R,chi_K,chi_T,chi_grad], [cR,cK,cT,cG])
    chi = max(chi_R, chi_K, chi_T, chi_grad)
    binding = argmax_name(chi_R, chi_K, chi_T, chi_grad)
    Lambda_breach = Lambda * chi                             # since chi ∝ 1/Lambda exactly
    return {chi, breakdown:{chi_R,chi_K,chi_T,chi_grad}, binding, Lambda_breach, worst}

# ---- src/eft/backreaction.py ----
function backreaction(Xi, background, M_Pl, domain D):
    beta = 0.0
    for x in sample_grid(D):
        b_amp = norm(Xi.dg(x)) / norm(background.g_bar(x))               # |δg|/|ḡ|
        T_Xi  = self_stress_of_excitation(Xi, x)                          # 2nd-order-in-Ξ stress
        lvar  = min_efolding_length(Xi, x)
        b_dyn = norm(M_Pl**-2 * T_Xi) * lvar**2                          # induced metric deformation over lobe
        beta = max(beta, b_amp, b_dyn)
    return beta

# ---- verdict mapper (fail-closed, three-valued) ----
function eft_verdict(ratios, beta, chi_audit=0.3, breach_attributable_to_KK):
    chi = ratios.chi
    if beta >= 1.0:                  return "FAIL_BACKREACTION"          # perturbative split failed — tested FIRST, hardest downgrade
    if chi  >= 1.0:                                                      # cutoff breach (distinct event from a β breach)
        return "UV_DELEGATED" if breach_attributable_to_KK else "FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF"
    if chi  >= chi_audit:            return "AUDIT"                      # near-cutoff: corrections non-negligible
    return "PASS_TOY"                                                    # ceiling — never higher

Three load-bearing design choices, each a defense against a named first failure: 1. Sup, not mean (worst tracking) — defends against the averaged-away hotspot: a candidate with a tiny mean χ but one trans-cutoff spike must fail, and only the sup catches it. The worst-point location is returned so E09b can refine the grid there (adaptive sampling — the §E09a.8 NC-2 control proves this fires). 2. max over four ratios — defends against the blind-spot ratio: §E09a.5 showed a candidate clean in three ratios and binding on the fourth. Dropping any ratio reopens a class of breaches. 3. β ≥ 1 ⇒ FAIL_BACKREACTION before the χ test — defends against the non-perturbative masquerade: if the split g = ḡ + δg failed, the χ ratios were computed on the wrong background and are themselves untrustworthy, so backreaction is the first, hardest gate.

E09a.8 Negative controls (Step 8) — the tripwire library, with hand-computed numbers

A green EFT-validity suite that never trips proves nothing. The controls below are regression fixtures: their χ and β are computable by hand, so CI certifies both the zero-point (the engine doesn't manufacture breaches) and the detection power (the engine fires on real breaches).

NC-1 — Trivial profile (zero-point control). Ξ = 0 (flat space, no excitation).

  • Every field and its gradient vanish ⇒ R = K = T_eff = 0, ℓ_var → ∞. ⇒ χ_R = χ_K = χ_T = 0, χ_grad = 1/(Λ·∞) = 0.
  • χ = 0, β = 0 ⇒ verdict PASS_TOY (cutoff sub-gate clean). Certifies: the ratios do not invent a breach where there is no physics. First failure it guards: false-positive cutoff breach (the over-rejection mirror failure, side (B) of §E09a.4).

NC-2 — Trans-cutoff sharp lobe (tripwire control). The §E09a.5 toy at σ = 1/2 (a half-cutoff-wide lobe), A = 0.05, Λ = 1.

  • ℓ_var = σ = 0.5 ⇒ χ_grad = 1/(Λ·0.5) = 2.0.
  • χ = max(..., 2.0) = 2.0 ≥ 1 ⇒ verdict breach. Breach attributable to lobe sharpness (excitation control), not a heavy sector, and the backreaction here is tiny (β ≪ 1 — a gentle-amplitude but spatially-sharp lobe) ⇒ token FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF (cutoff breach), not FAIL_BACKREACTION (the perturbation was small; it is the cutoff, not the split, that failed). Certifies: the gate fires on a hand-computed trans-cutoff value and emits the correct downgrade token, and that the cutoff breach is correctly distinguished from a backreaction breach. First failure it guards: the trans-cutoff lobe (the chapter's signature failure) slipping through as PASS_TOY.

NC-3 — Ricci-flat, Weyl-large profile (blind-spot control). A vacuum-type perturbation with R = 0 but large Kretschmann K = 16 (Λ⁴-units), e.g. a strong tidal/gravitational-wave-like packet.

  • χ_R = |0|^{1/2}/Λ = 0 (Ricci sees nothing!), but χ_K = |16|^{1/4}/Λ = 2.0.
  • χ = max(0, 2.0, ...) = 2.0 ≥ 1 ⇒ breach, token FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF when the tidal packet is an excitation feature, or UV_DELEGATED if the Weyl excess is attributable to a known heavy sector (the attribution is a per-candidate input, defaulting to the fail-closed FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF when undetermined). Certifies: χ_K catches a trans-cutoff tidal curvature that χ_R is structurally blind to — the curvature analogue of HC-03's T_00-blindness. First failure it guards: a Ricci-flat-but-Weyl-huge lobe reading clean because only the Ricci ratio was checked.

NC-4 — Non-perturbative amplitude (backreaction control). Flat ḡ = η, but an injected δg with |δg|/|ḡ| = 1.5 (a "perturbation" larger than the background).

  • β_amp = 1.5 ≥ 1 ⇒ verdict FAIL_BACKREACTION regardless of χ (the β test precedes the χ test). Certifies: the backreaction gate fires first and rejects a candidate whose "small" excitation isn't small. First failure it guards: a non-perturbative deformation masquerading as a linear lobe (the χ-ratios would be computed on a meaningless split).
Control Construction χ (hand) β (hand) Verdict Guards first-failure
NC-1 Ξ = 0 0 0 PASS_TOY false-positive breach
NC-2 toy at σ=0.5 2.0 (grad) small (≪1) FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF trans-cutoff lobe slips through
NC-3 R=0, K=16 2.0 (K) small (≪1) FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF (or UV_DELEGATED if heavy-sector) Weyl blind-spot
NC-4 \|δg\|/\|ḡ\|=1.5 (any) 1.5 FAIL_BACKREACTION non-perturbative masquerade

The acceptance tests named in the source doc map onto these controls: "cutoff breach downgrades" = NC-2/NC-3/NC-4 must each downgrade; "EFT candidate has ratios" = any candidate that survives must carry a populated EFTValidityRecord (no record ⇒ CI fail); "assumption changes update status" = changing Λ (e.g. NC-2 re-run at Λ = 4, giving χ_grad = 1/(4·0.5) = 0.5 → AUDIT) must flip the verdict — proving the gate is genuinely a function of the declared cutoff, not a hard-coded label. This last test is the ∂χ/∂Λ machinery of §E09a.6.1 exercised as a regression.

The chapter's terminal first failure (the one that caps the leaf at AUDIT): a χ < 1 reading is "no cutoff breach detected on the sampled domain D, at the declared Λ," not "the candidate is EFT-valid." The sup is over D, not over all space (F4); the Λ is bounded, not known (F5); the Wilson band's upper edge can exceed 1 even at χ = 0.2 (F6). Each independently forbids promotion above PASS_TOY, and the binding one is whichever fires first per candidate.

E09a.11 Reviewer attacks (Step 11)

Attack 1 — "χ < 1 is not a real validity certificate; it's just local-scale < Λ, which any smooth metric satisfies if you pick Λ = M_Pl. You've defined a gate you can always pass by raising the cutoff." Honest response: That is precisely why Λ is declared, bounded, and propagated, never tuned. The binding cutoff is Λ ≤ M_KK (Fable_GUT: the lightest internal mode switches on there and the 4D truncation fails above it), and we ship Λ_breach and ∂χ/∂Λ per candidate so a reviewer who disputes M_KK can substitute their Λ and read the verdict off directly (§E09a.6.1). Raising Λ to M_Pl to force a pass is exactly the move the UV_DELEGATED flag exists to catch: a candidate whose validity needs Λ > M_KK is delegating its validity to the un-closed compactification (F5), which is an AUDIT/UV_DELEGATED status, never a closed claim. The gate is unbeatable-by-fiat only because the cutoff is corpus-fixed, not free.

Attack 2 — "Your four ratios are arbitrary; why these powers, why max, why not an L² norm that wouldn't blow up on a single point?" Honest response: The powers are NDA-forced, not chosen: each ratio is the unique dimensionless control parameter of a specific omitted operator (χ_R² for R², χ_grad² for the derivative expansion, etc.), so the powers 1/2, 1/4, 1/4, 1 are fixed by the operators' mass dimensions — §E09a.2.2 derives each. max (not L² or mean) is fail-closed by design: EFT validity is a worst-case statement — the truncation must hold at every point, so a single trans-cutoff point is a genuine breach, and an L² norm that averages it away would license a screener to compute S_L using physics it doesn't have at the lobe's wall. NC-2/NC-3 (single-point breaches that must fire) are the regression fixtures proving an averaging gate would wrongly pass.

Attack 3 — "Backreaction is double-counted: χ_T already bounds the stress, so β is redundant." Honest response: They test different things and §E09a.5 shows them diverging by orders of magnitude. χ_T = |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ asks is the source's energy scale sub-cutoff? (a UV question). β = |M_Pl⁻² T_Ξ|ℓ_var² asks does the excitation's stress curve the background it was computed on by an O(1) fraction over the lobe? (a perturbative-control question, weighted by M_Pl⁻² and the lobe size²). A candidate can be sub-cutoff (χ_T ≪ 1) yet non-perturbative (β ≥ 1) if M_Pl⁻²T_Ξ ℓ_var² is large — and vice versa. NC-4 (a β breach with arbitrary χ) is the fixture proving β catches a failure χ_T is blind to. Far from redundant, β is tested first because if it fails the χ ratios were computed on the wrong background.

Attack 4 — "Even at χ = 0.2 your own Wilson band says S_L could shift by O(1). So your 'clean' toy isn't clean — your gate is theater." Honest response: That is the chapter's most important admission, and we publish it rather than hide it (§E09a.6.2): the band ΔS_L/S_L ∈ [2.5×10⁻⁴, 6.3] at χ = 0.20 has an upper edge above 1, which is exactly why χ ∈ [0.3,1) is AUDIT and why even a χ = 0.20 toy is flagged "clean but near the band." The honest reading is not "S_L is trustworthy to two figures" — it is "S_L is trustworthy to two figures only if the leading Wilson coefficient is near its weak-coupling NDA value; under strong coupling it isn't, and that uncertainty is AUDIT because Fable_Quantum's interacting sector is not closed." A gate that surfaced this and stopped is doing its job; a gate that reported S_L = 0.07 ± nothing would be the theater.

First failure (this section). Rhetorical-pass — answering a reviewer attack so persuasively that the answer is mistaken for a closure of the objection rather than an honest downgrade. The detector: each "honest response" above ends not in a clean pass but in an explicit residual status (UV_DELEGATED for the Λ-tuning attack, AUDIT/AUDIT_QUANTUM for the Wilson-band attack, FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF/FAIL_BACKREACTION for the breach attacks); on fire (an answer that claims to defeat rather than bound the objection) the token is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION. The attacks are answered by disclosure, never by promotion.

E09a.12 Patent extraction (Step 12)

Four magnitude-independent, drive-agnostic simulation assets surface in this leaf, each a method/system/medium claim usable whether or not any drive effect is ever achievable:

  1. Four-ratio EFT-admissibility scorer — the method of computing, over a sampled domain of a candidate metric/field configuration, the four dimensionless cutoff ratios (|R|^{1/2}/Λ, |K|^{1/4}/Λ, |T|^{1/4}/Λ, 1/(Λℓ_var)) and gating on their sup-over-domain max against a declared cutoff. The novel, defensible step is the simultaneous Ricci-and-Weyl pair (χ_R and χ_K) plus the e-folding-length gradient ratio 1/(Λℓ_var), which distinguishes from single-curvature-invariant validity checks (the prior-art blind-spot, NC-3).
  2. Closed-form breach-cutoff Λ_breach and sensitivity ∂χ/∂Λ — the method of reporting, per candidate, the minimum cutoff at which the candidate is valid (Λ_breach = sup max(|R|^{1/2},|K|^{1/4},|T|^{1/4},1/ℓ_var)) and its sensitivity, so a downstream consumer can re-evaluate validity under any disputed cutoff without re-running the simulation. This is the "assumption changes update status" acceptance test made into a constant-time query.
  3. Two-channel backreaction guard — the method of testing the perturbative-background assumption by the larger of an amplitude ratio |δg|/|ḡ| and a dynamical ratio |M_Pl⁻²T_Ξ|ℓ_var², evaluated before the cutoff ratios, with a FAIL_BACKREACTION token that blocks downstream S_L emission. Distinguishes from stress-magnitude-only checks (NC-4 trap).
  4. Cutoff-aware validity overlay / EFTValidityRecord — the data-structure/medium claim: a record carrying χ, its breakdown, Λ_breach, β, the Wilson band, the deltaSL/SL band, and a sampled_domain_only honesty flag, which structurally cannot present a near-cutoff S_L as a crisp number (it carries the correction band) and watermarks or blocks any mission plot accordingly. This is the source doc's "cutoff-aware simulation outputs" / "EFT-validity scoring" patent-relevance line, realized as a propagated artifact.

All four avoid any working-drive, exotic-matter-engineering, high-energy-source, or UV-completion-construction claim (contract avoid-list); they claim validity measurement, sensitivity reporting, and disclosure machinery, which is precisely what survives regardless of feasibility.

First failure (this section). Claim-scope inflation — a patent claim drifting from "we measure EFT validity" toward "we achieve an EFT-valid drive," i.e. importing a feasibility or propulsion assertion into a measurement/disclosure claim. The detector is the contract §4 avoid-list checked against each claim's operative verb (all four read compute / report / guard / disclose, none read produce / power / propel); on fire the token is FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION. The assets are deliberately magnitude- and feasibility-independent: they describe the gate, never a drive.

The following must never appear unqualified anywhere downstream of this leaf, and the EFT-validity report is built so they cannot be asserted from its outputs:
