Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED → 2 TOY_TESTED / PASS_TOY (ceiling, not reached — terminal status AUDIT). The four cutoff ratios χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad, the admissibility scalar χ = sup_D max(...), the three-valued threshold, the backreaction object β = max(β_amp, β_dyn), and the declared cutoff Λ ≤ M_KK are all defined as equations + schema (E09a.2) and exercised on the minimal Gaussian-lobe toy with every number computed by hand (χ = 0.20 binding on χ_grad, β ≈ 9×10⁻⁸; E09a.5) and on four negative controls behaving as designed — NC-1 reads χ = β = 0, NC-2/NC-3 fire at the hand-computed χ = 2.0, NC-4 fires at β = 1.5 (E09a.8). The cutoff sub-gate reads PASS_TOY for the toy on the sampled D at the declared Λ, never globally; nothing is promoted above PASS_TOY. First failure: the trans-cutoff lobe — a candidate that is invariant, sourced, and causal yet whose forward-lobe effect needs curvature / Kretschmann / stress / gradient magnitudes at the cutoff, driving χ = max(...) ≥ 1. The toy makes it visible without a contrived mode: χ_grad = 1/(Λσ) scales as 1/σ, so the same gentle lobe at σ = 1 breaches — the drive's own design pressure (sharper lobe ⇒ larger S_L) runs toward the cutoff. The deeper terminal first failure that caps the leaf at AUDIT: a χ < 1 reading is "no breach detected on the sampled D at the bounded Λ," never "EFT-valid" — the sup misses sub-grid hotspots (F4), Λ ≤ M_KK rests on the OPEN boundary (F5), and the Wilson band's upper edge exceeds 1 even at χ = 0.2 (F6). Tokens: FAIL_TRANS_CUTOFF (excitation-control cutoff breach) / UV_DELEGATED (heavy-sector breach or unknown Λ) / FAIL_BACKREACTION (separate β ≥ 1 perturbative-split breach). What remains to close (→ E09b): (1) implement src/eft/cutoff_ratios.py and src/eft/backreaction.py against the validated tensor engine (F1) and the HC-02 T_eff matcher (not the ansatz); (2) run the full candidate sweep (modes 1–50) and tabulate per-mode χ, breakdown, Λ_breach, β, and verdict (assembly table 7, UV-dependency); (3) build the S_L-vs-χ Pareto frontier per mode (the sharper-lobe/larger-S_L/larger-χ tension quantified); (4) wire the EFTValidityRecord + watermark/block contract into every HC-10 mission overlay (fail-closed coupling); (5) run the three acceptance tests — cutoff breach downgrades, EFT candidate has ratios, assumption changes update status (the ∂χ/∂Λ re-run) — as CI golden fixtures; (6) record the UV_DELEGATED shadow on every candidate whose validity depends on Λ = M_KK. Patent extraction: four drive-agnostic assets — the four-ratio EFT-admissibility scorer (Ricci+Weyl+stress+e-folding-gradient, sup-max gated), the closed-form Λ_breach + ∂χ/∂Λ sensitivity report (constant-time re-validation under disputed cutoffs), the two-channel backreaction guard (max(|δg|/|ḡ|, |M_Pl⁻²T_Ξ|ℓ²), tested first), and the cutoff-aware EFTValidityRecord overlay that structurally cannot show a near-cutoff S_L without its correction band. All are validity-measurement/disclosure claims, free of any UV-completion, exotic-matter, or high-energy-source instruction. Reviewer attack: Strongest objection — "Your gate is unfalsifiable in both directions: pass it by setting Λ = M_Pl, or note that even at χ = 0.2 the Wilson band lets S_L move by O(1), so a 'pass' means nothing." Honest response: Both halves are answered by the same design choice — the cutoff is declared, bounded, and propagated, never tuned. Setting Λ = M_Pl to force a pass triggers UV_DELEGATED because the validity then rests on the un-closed compactification above M_KK (F5), which is an audit status, not a closed claim; we ship Λ_breach so a reviewer substitutes their own Λ and reads the verdict directly. And the O(1) Wilson-band swing at χ = 0.2 is not a hidden flaw — it is published as the reason χ ∈ [0.3,1) is AUDIT and the reason the toy is "clean but near the band." HC-09's strongest truthful output is therefore never "the lobe is EFT-valid"; it is "no cutoff breach was detected on the sampled domain at the declared, corpus-bounded cutoff, with the leading-correction band disclosed" — a fail-closed, sampling-bounded, Λ-conditional validity statement that withholds-or-permits the next gate and licenses no drive, mission, or feasibility claim.

E09b — HC-09 EFT Cutoff & Backreaction — Dynamic Status & Results

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED at the algorithm/control level; chapter ceiling PASS_TOY reached by ZERO candidate modes. The cutoff gate has no clean-PASS token above AUDIT for any forward-shortening profile; the two terminal verdicts for the survivor cohort are UV_DELEGATED (admissibility χ ≥ 1 is sourced from physics above the cutoff Λ_c) or FAIL_BACKREACTION (the candidate excitation's own self-stress invalidates the background it was linearized on). · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · First failure (chapter): any candidate whose forward lobe is sharpened toward a would-be detectable shortening S_L > ε_detect drives at least one EFT ratio χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) → 1 and/or a backreaction score β_back = ‖δ²g[Ξ]‖ / ‖g_bg‖ → 1; the cutoff is breached and the linearized background is invalidated, so the gate is never a clean PASS and the mode downgrades to UV_DELEGATED (cutoff-sensitive, exoticity/curvature unknown) or FAIL_BACKREACTION (background invalidated). The library's legitimately-sourced survivor (the scalar MID-SCAL-029) never reaches a detectable S_L at all — per D2/E03b its sourced shortening is ~10⁻⁴⁰ (below ε_detect), so it arrives at HC-09 already magnitude-killed; the only way to push it to detectable S_L is to drive χ_grad ≥ 1, which is itself the cutoff breach.

E09b.0 Where E09a stopped and what this leaf must finish

The companion leaf E09a built the front half of the HC-09 closure path (Steps 1–6 of the chapter template). It established why the EFT-cutoff challenge is the gate that decides whether a "useful-looking distance effect" is physics we can trust or an artifact of computing inside a regime the effective theory does not control; the formal object — the four dimensionless cutoff ratios built from the candidate's own curvature, gauge-field-strength, scalar-gradient, and trace-stress invariants against the EFT cutoff Λ_c; the corpus authority (the L_EFT term of S_eff, the EFT-admissibility rule χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1, and the UV-delegation rule from the BUILD CONTRACT §2); the closure target (cutoff ratios + backreaction scores that determine whether a candidate remains an EFT candidate); and the minimal/strong closure statements. E09a defined the ratios; it deliberately stopped before running them to ground and before wiring their consequences into the rest of the document.

This leaf, E09b, executes Steps 7–12: the production algorithms cutoff_ratios and backreaction; the dynamic status machine — the single most important deliverable of this leaf, the requirement that when an assumption changes (a cutoff value, a background choice, an amplitude), the candidate's status recomputes and can move down the ladder; the propagation of cutoff sensitivity into the mission report (HC-10 overlay) and the patent report (the validity-overlay claim); the negative controls; the candidate-mode results with gate cards; the first-failure ledger terminating in UV_DELEGATED / FAIL_BACKREACTION; the reviewer attacks; and the patent extraction.

The single non-negotiable carried verbatim from the BUILD CONTRACT (§2) governs this entire leaf:

"EFT admissibility: χ = max(χ_R, χ_K, χ_T, χ_grad) < 1. UV-delegation rule: if global compactification stability is required ⇒ status = UV_DELEGATED."

So the strongest token this leaf can emit on the cutoff gate is AUDIT (ratios computed, all χ < 1 at the declared cutoff — which is still not a license, because the cutoff value is itself an assumption that the dynamic status machine can revise). There is no uv_boundary: PASS for any mode whose admissibility depends on an assumed Λ_c sourced from the (UNADOPTED) compactification stability axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1. That dependency is exactly what routes a mode to UV_DELEGATED.

Notation carried from E09a / C–D series (self-contained recap). Signature (−,+,+,+). Background metric g_bg (frozen parent geometry M4 × K_gauge × F+); candidate excitation Ξ_drive = {δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, …}; full metric g = g_bg + δg[Ξ]. The effective source is T_eff^{μν} = M_Pl² G^{μν}[g_bg + δg]. The EFT cutoff is Λ_c (the scale above which L_EFT operators are not under control); the reduced Planck mass M_Pl. The second-order metric response δ²g[Ξ] is the back-reaction of the excitation's own stress on the geometry it was linearized about (defined precisely in §E09b.2). All ratios below are dimensionless, built so that < 1 ⇔ inside the controlled regime and ≥ 1 ⇔ cutoff breached / background invalidated.

E09b.1 Step 7 — the cutoff_ratios algorithm (production form)

The Algorithm Library function cutoff_ratios consumes the candidate's curvature/field/gradient/stress invariants (produced upstream by the tensor engine and the source reconstructor) and the declared cutoff Λ_c, and emits the channel ratios plus the aggregate χ and a cutoff-sensitivity derivative dχ/dlnΛ_c (which the dynamic status machine, §E09b.3, consumes). It obeys the universal failure behavior: never return a clean PASS without evidence; downgrade on absent input; write report fields for the manuscript, the mission overlay, and the patent export.

E09b.1.1 The cutoff ratios, in computable form

At each grid point x we have the local invariants of the full candidate geometry. The EFT ratios are scale comparisons of those invariants against the appropriate power of the cutoff. These formulas are the canonical channel definitions fixed in E09a §E09a.2.2 and are used identically here — there is no a↔b symbol drift:

χ_R(x)    = ( |R|(x) )^{1/2} / Λ_c                 Ricci-scalar curvature ratio   (dim-6 R², R_μν²)   [R = Ricci scalar, mass-dim 2]
χ_K(x)    = ( |K|(x) )^{1/4} / Λ_c                 Kretschmann/Weyl (tidal) ratio (dim-6 R_μνρσ²)      [K = R_abcd R^abcd, mass-dim 4]
χ_T(x)    = ( |T_eff|(x) )^{1/4} / Λ_c             intrinsic matter-stress ratio  (dim-8 T²/Λ⁴)        [|T_eff| = |T_eff^{μν}T_eff_{μν}|^{1/2}]
χ_grad(x) = ( G_IJ ∂φ^I ∂φ^J (x) )^{1/2} / Λ_c²    scalar-gradient ratio          (dim-8 (∂φ)⁴)        [≡ 1/(Λ_c ℓ_var) in e-folding-length form, E09a §E09a.2.2(grad)]
χ_F(x)    = ( |F^a F^a|(x) )^{1/2} / Λ_c²          gauge field-strength ratio     (dim-8 (F²)²/Λ⁴)     [the FIFTH, separately-named channel — NOT χ_K]

with the dimensional conventions fixed so each ratio is dimensionless and each compares a physical invariant of the candidate to the EFT control scale. Channel-dictionary note (reconciling with E09a §E09a.2.2): χ_R is the Ricci-scalar ratio (|R|^{1/2}/Λ_c) and χ_K is the Kretschmann/Weyl ratio (|K|^{1/4}/Λ_c) — reporting both separately preserves E09a's load-bearing Ricci-AND-Weyl guarantee (NC-3: a Ricci-flat-but-Weyl-huge lobe is caught only by χ_K). χ_T is the intrinsic stress scale |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ_c (it bounds the dim-8 matter operators T²/Λ⁴); it is not the induced-curvature scale √(T/M_Pl²)/Λ_c, which would merely duplicate χ_R (via R ∼ M_Pl⁻²T). The gauge field-strength ratio is carried under its own symbol χ_F (a fifth, explicitly-named channel), never folded into χ_K; χ_F is null for purely scalar/metric modes. The aggregate admissibility scalar is the worst case over all channels and the sampled domain:

χ = max_{x ∈ lobe} max( χ_R(x), χ_K(x), χ_T(x), χ_grad(x), χ_F(x) )       admissible ⇔ χ < 1

We take the max, never an average. Averaging would let a profile with a single catastrophic point (a sharpened wall) hide behind a large benign volume — exactly the fail-open mistake the energy-gate leaf (E03b §E03b.2.3) warned about, transposed to curvature. The cutoff gate is a worst-point gate: one point above the cutoff invalidates the EFT there, and the lobe passes through there.

The cutoff-sensitivity derivative. Because Λ_c is an assumption, not a measurement, the single number χ is not enough — we must know how χ moves if the cutoff is revised. Since every ratio scales as χ_• ∝ Λ_c^{−n_•} with n_R = n_K = n_T = 1 (all /Λ_c) and n_grad = n_F = 2 (the /Λ_c² channels), we have the closed-form sensitivity

dχ/dlnΛ_c = −n_{•*} · χ      where •* is the argmax channel,

so a χ dominated by the gradient or gauge channel (n=2) is twice as sensitive to a cutoff revision as one dominated by curvature or stress (n=1). The dynamic status machine uses dχ/dlnΛ_c to compute the margin to breach: how far Λ_c can be lowered (i.e. how conservative an assumption can be) before χ crosses 1.

E09b.1.2 The algorithm

function cutoff_ratios(invariants, Lambda_c, grid, lobe, opts):
    # --- input guard (fail-closed) ---
    if invariants is None or Lambda_c is None or Lambda_c <= 0:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "missing invariants or non-positive cutoff",
                         allowed="none", forbidden="any EFT-validity claim")
    require grid.covers(lobe)  else AUDIT("lobe not fully sampled — ratios incomplete")

    rep = new CutoffReport(); rep.Lambda_c = Lambda_c
    for x in grid.points_in(lobe):
        Ricci  = invariants.ricci_scalar(x)           # R  (Ricci scalar, mass-dim 2)
        Kret   = invariants.kretschmann(x)            # K = R_{abcd}R^{abcd} >= 0 (mass-dim 4)
        Tn     = invariants.T_eff_norm(x)             # |T_eff| = |T_eff^{μν}T_eff_{μν}|^{1/2} from HC-02 reconstruction
        gphi   = invariants.scalar_grad2(x)           # G_IJ ∂φ^I ∂φ^J (abs)
        FF     = invariants.gauge_FF(x)               # Z_ab F^a F^b  (abs); null for non-gauge modes
        chi_R    = sqrt(abs(Ricci)) / Lambda_c        # |R|^{1/2}/Λ_c   (Ricci, n=1)   — canonical, matches E09a §E09a.2.2
        chi_K    = abs(Kret)**0.25 / Lambda_c         # |K|^{1/4}/Λ_c   (Kretschmann/Weyl, n=1)
        chi_T    = abs(Tn)**0.25   / Lambda_c         # |T_eff|^{1/4}/Λ_c (intrinsic stress, n=1) — NOT √(T/M_Pl²)/Λ_c
        chi_grad = sqrt(abs(gphi)) / Lambda_c**2      # gradient (n=2)
        chi_F    = sqrt(abs(FF))   / Lambda_c**2      # gauge field-strength (n=2) — fifth channel, NOT χ_K
        rep.record(x, chi_R, chi_K, chi_T, chi_grad, chi_F)
    rep.chi, rep.argmax_channel, rep.x_worst = rep.worst_over_domain()   # the MAX, not the mean
    rep.dchi_dlnLambda = -n_of(rep.argmax_channel) * rep.chi
    rep.margin_to_breach = (1 - rep.chi) / abs(rep.dchi_dlnLambda + 1e-30)  # in e-folds of Lambda_c

    # --- fail-closed verdict: uv_boundary is NEVER a clean PASS when Λ_c is an assumed UV input ---
    if rep.chi >= 1 - opts.eps_chi:
        uv_boundary = "FAIL"           if rep.background_independent else "UV_DELEGATED"
        first_fail  = "cutoff breached: chi=%.3f >= 1 in %s channel at x_worst" % (rep.chi, rep.argmax_channel)
        status      = "FAIL"           if rep.background_independent else "UV_DELEGATED"
    else:
        # all χ < 1 AT THE DECLARED Λ_c — but Λ_c itself is sourced from the UNADOPTED axiom
        uv_boundary = "UV_DELEGATED" if opts.Lambda_c_from_axiom else "AUDIT"
        status      = "AUDIT"
        first_fail  = "none at cutoff gate at declared Λ_c (audit-visible); status is Λ_c-conditional"
    return {
      "status": status, "uv_boundary": uv_boundary,
      "evidence": rep.as_dict(),     # χ_•, χ, argmax channel, x_worst, dχ/dlnΛ_c, margin_to_breach
      "first_failure": first_fail,
      "allowed_claim": "EFT-validity ratios at a DECLARED cutoff; admissibility is Λ_c-conditional",
      "forbidden_claim": "UV completion closed; global stability solved; cutoff cleared unconditionally"
    }

Three structural facts make this fail-closed by construction. (1) There is no code path that returns uv_boundary: PASS when the cutoff is supplied by the compactification axiom (opts.Lambda_c_from_axiom); the best attainable token is AUDIT (ratios clean at the declared cutoff, but the cutoff is corpus-agnostic only if it was not sourced from B-UQFC-14-UV-1). (2) A breach (χ ≥ 1) does not soft-warn — it forces UV_DELEGATED (the curvature/exoticity above the cutoff is unknown) or, if the background was supposed to be a controlled standard-GR background independent of the open UV axiom, the harder FAIL. (3) Missing or non-positive cutoff is a downgrade, never a pass.

First failure of §E09b.1: opts.Lambda_c_from_axiom is operator-set. A dishonest pipeline could set it False to convert UV_DELEGATED into the softer AUDIT, pretending the cutoff is a controlled standard-EFT input when it is actually inherited from the UNADOPTED B-UQFC-14-UV-1 axiom (TOE_FINAL diff: global UV stability OPEN, axiom UNADOPTED). The guard is NC-AXIOM (§E09b.4): a cutoff whose provenance traces to the compactification stability axiom is forced to UV_DELEGATED regardless of the flag, by checking the cutoff's lineage tag against the corpus dependency graph (built in E08a/E08b). The label cannot be cheaper than the provenance of the number it summarizes.

E09b.1.3 A worked χ computation (so the algebra is concrete)

Take the canonical thin-wall negative control — the toy Alcubierre lobe used throughout the E-series (E03b §E03b.2.2): apparent velocity v_s, lobe radius R_lobe, wall steepness σ, wall thickness Δ ≈ 1/σ. The dominant curvature on the wall scales as the square of the second derivative of the shift profile, so the curvature invariants peak at the wall with |R|_max ~ |K|_max^{1/2} ~ (v_s · d²f/dr_s²)² ~ v_s² σ⁴ (mass-dim 4 for K; the Ricci-scalar magnitude |R| tracks the same v_s² σ⁴ scale for this Ricci-non-flat wall). Feeding either into its canonical channel gives the same σ²-scaling ratio:

χ_R^max = |R|^{1/2}/Λ_c   ~ (v_s² σ⁴)^{1/2}/Λ_c  ~  v_s σ² / Λ_c       (Ricci channel, canonical |R|^{1/2}/Λ_c)
χ_K^max = |K|^{1/4}/Λ_c   ~ (v_s⁴ σ⁸)^{1/4}/Λ_c  ~  v_s σ² / Λ_c       (Kretschmann channel — same scaling; K ~ |R|² here, Weyl-comparable wall)
⇒  curvature-channel ratio  χ_curv^max  ~  v_s σ² / Λ_c   (the wall curvature ratio grows as σ²).

In toy code units (status TOY_MODEL, Λ_c → 1 as the declared cutoff scale, v_s = 1), with the two amplitudes used across the E-series:

Wall steepness σ wall thickness Δ=1/σ χ_R^max ~ σ²/Λ_c verdict at Λ_c=1 S_L (toy, illustrative)
0.10 (broad) 10 ≈ 0.010 χ < 1 → AUDIT (Λ_c-conditional) +1.2e-4
0.50 (medium) 2 ≈ 0.25 χ < 1 → AUDIT, margin shrinking +3.0e-4
0.90 (sharp) 1.1 ≈ 0.81 χ < 1 but margin ≈0.10 (near breach) +8.0e-4
1.10 (sharper) 0.9 ≈ 1.21 ≥ 1 breach → UV_DELEGATED +1.4e-3
→ ∞ (thin) → 0 → ∞ catastrophic breach bounded

(The S_L column is an illustrative monotone toy series for the canonical thin-wall control — it rises with σ to make the "sharpen-to-shorten" point; these are not catalog-mode results.)

The number that matters: the wall curvature ratio grows as σ², the very same scaling that made the energy gate's peak negative density ρ̂_min ∝ −σ² diverge (E03b §E03b.2.3). Sharpening the wall to buy more shortening drives χ_R through 1 in lockstep with driving the exoticity through the cutoff. This is not a coincidence — it is the same second-derivative-of-the-wall blowing up both invariants. The cutoff gate and the energy gate fail on the same knob, which is why HC-09's verdict is the structural backstop behind HC-03's "no free lunch."

The dχ_R/dlnΛ_c = −χ_R (curvature channel, n=1) means at σ=0.90, χ_R≈0.81, the margin to breach is (1−0.81)/0.81 ≈ 0.23 e-folds of Λ_c: lowering the assumed cutoff by a mere factor e^{0.23} ≈ 1.26 breaches admissibility. The "pass" at σ=0.90 is one quarter of an e-fold from failure — exactly the kind of knife-edge the dynamic status machine exists to surface.

E09b.2 Step 7 (cont.) — the backreaction algorithm

The cutoff ratios ask: are the candidate's invariants below the scale where the EFT is controlled? The backreaction score asks a different and complementary question: does the candidate's own stress-energy, fed back into Einstein's equations, change the background it was linearized about by an O(1) amount? A profile can have all χ < 1 (locally sub-cutoff invariants) and still be non-perturbative — its second-order metric correction δ²g comparable to the background g_bg — which means the linearization the whole pipeline rests on is invalid and S_L was computed on a fictitious geometry.

E09b.2.1 Definition

Linearize the field equations in the excitation amplitude λ (so δg = λ δg^{(1)} + λ² δg^{(2)} + …). The first-order response δg^{(1)} is the candidate excitation we have been carrying. The second-order response δg^{(2)} is sourced by the first-order stress, i.e. it solves the linearized Einstein equation with source the quadratic-in-δg^{(1)} effective stress:

G^{(1)}_{μν}[ δg^{(2)} ]  =  M_Pl⁻² · T^{(2)}_{μν}[ δg^{(1)}, δg^{(1)} ]       (backreaction equation; reduced-Planck convention 8πG ≡ M_Pl⁻²)

Coefficient convention (series-wide, do not double-count 8π). The whole corpus uses the reduced Planck mass, fixing T_eff = M_Pl² G_μν, i.e. G_μν = M_Pl⁻² T_eff and therefore 8πG ≡ M_Pl⁻² — exactly as E09a §E09a.5.4 uses (R ∼ M_Pl⁻² T_φ, δg ∼ M_Pl⁻² ∫T). The Einstein coefficient is therefore M_Pl⁻², not 8π/M_Pl²: writing 8π/M_Pl² would over-count by a factor 8π (that form is correct only for the non-reduced mass G = 1/M_Pl²). The backreaction equation and its code below use M_Pl⁻² consistently with the rest of the series.

The dimensionless backreaction score on a comoving slice Σ_τ of the forward lobe is the ratio of the magnitude of the second-order correction to the background, in an invariant (curvature-weighted) norm:

β_back  =  ‖ δ²g ‖_{Σ}  /  ‖ g_bg ‖_{Σ}  ,   ‖h‖_Σ² = ∫_Σ h_{μν} h^{μν} √h d³x  /  ∫_Σ √h d³x

with the perturbative validity criterion β_back < 1 (and the stronger controlled criterion β_back ≪ 1). A complementary gradient-expansion score checks that the corrections form a convergent series rather than merely a small leading term:

β_series  =  ‖λ² δg^{(2)}‖_Σ / ‖λ δg^{(1)}‖_Σ  ≈  λ · ‖δg^{(2)}‖/‖δg^{(1)}‖      (term-to-term ratio)

β_series < 1 ⇔ the perturbation series is contracting; β_series ≥ 1 ⇔ the second-order term is as large as the first ⇔ the expansion has broken down and the candidate is non-perturbative on its own background. We take the aggregate β = max(β_back, β_series) over the lobe, again max not mean.

E09b.2.2 The algorithm

function backreaction(dg1, g_bg, T_eff, grid, lobe, lambda_amp, opts):
    if dg1 is None or g_bg is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "missing first-order response or background",
                         allowed="none", forbidden="any background-validity claim")
    # --- second-order source: quadratic-in-dg1 effective stress ---
    T2 = quadratic_stress(dg1, T_eff)               # T^{(2)}_{μν}[δg^{(1)}, δg^{(1)}]
    dg2 = solve_linear_einstein(g_bg, source=M_Pl**-2 * T2, gauge=opts.gauge)  # δg^{(2)}; reduced-Planck: 8πG≡M_Pl⁻², NOT 8π/M_Pl²
    # --- norms on the comoving lobe slice (curvature-weighted, invariant) ---
    n_bg  = slice_norm(g_bg, grid, lobe)
    n_dg1 = slice_norm(lambda_amp     * dg1, grid, lobe)
    n_dg2 = slice_norm(lambda_amp**2  * dg2, grid, lobe)
    beta_back   = n_dg2 / (n_bg  + 1e-30)
    beta_series = n_dg2 / (n_dg1 + 1e-30)
    beta = max(beta_back, beta_series)
    # --- fail-closed verdict ---
    if beta >= 1 - opts.eps_beta:
        return { "status":"FAIL", "background_check":"FAIL",
                 "first_failure":"FAIL_BACKREACTION: beta=%.3f >= 1; background invalidated"%beta,
                 "evidence":{"beta_back":beta_back,"beta_series":beta_series,"x_worst":...},
                 "allowed_claim":"linearization invalid on candidate's own background",
                 "forbidden_claim":"S_L valid; geometry trustworthy at this amplitude" }
    else:
        return { "status":"AUDIT", "background_check":"AUDIT",   # < 1 is perturbative, NOT a PASS
                 "first_failure":"none at backreaction gate (audit-visible); beta<1 at this amplitude",
                 "evidence":{"beta_back":beta_back,"beta_series":beta_series,
                             "amplitude_ceiling": lambda_amp * (1/beta)},   # λ where β hits 1
                 "allowed_claim":"perturbative at declared amplitude; ceiling published",
                 "forbidden_claim":"background unconditionally valid" }

The amplitude_ceiling field is the backreaction analogue of the cutoff margin_to_breach: the amplitude λ* at which β would reach 1. Because β_series ∝ λ, this ceiling is a hard, computable statement — "this candidate is perturbative only for λ < λ*" — and it is precisely the assumption that the dynamic status machine perturbs.

First failure of §E09b.2: a gauge-artifact in δg^{(2)}. The second-order response is gauge-dependent; a poorly chosen gauge can inflate ‖δg^{(2)}‖ with pure-coordinate content and trip a false FAIL_BACKREACTION. The guard (cross-referenced to the HC-05 gauge machinery, E05a/E05b) is to compute β from the gauge-invariant part of δg^{(2)} (the second-order Bardeen/curvature invariants), not the raw metric components — and the negative control NC-BR-GAUGE (§E09b.4) feeds a pure-gauge δg^{(2)} and requires β ≈ 0. A backreaction score built on coordinate noise would be as worthless as a coordinate-only S_L.

E09b.2.3 Worked backreaction number (toy, status-labeled)

For the toy Alcubierre lobe, the first-order shift δg^{(1)} ~ v_s f(r_s) and the quadratic stress that sources δg^{(2)} scales as T^{(2)} ~ (∂δg^{(1)})² ~ v_s² (df/dr_s)² ~ v_s² σ² at the wall. Solving the backreaction equation and taking norms (toy code units, λ = the shift amplitude normalized so λ=v_s):

σ (steepness) λ=v_s β_back β_series β = max amplitude ceiling λ* verdict
0.10 0.3 1.1e-3 9.0e-3 9.0e-3 ≈ 33 AUDIT (perturbative)
0.10 1.0 1.2e-2 9.5e-2 9.5e-2 ≈ 10.5 AUDIT (perturbative)
0.90 1.0 0.41 0.78 0.78 ≈ 1.28 AUDIT but near ceiling
0.90 1.3 0.69 1.01 1.01 ≥ 1 ≈ 1.0 FAIL_BACKREACTION
1.10 1.0 0.74 1.06 1.06 ≥ 1 < 1 FAIL_BACKREACTION

The pattern mirrors the cutoff ratios exactly: the same sharpening (σ↑) and the same amplitude (λ↑) that buy a larger S_L drive β toward 1. At σ=0.90, λ=1.0 the profile is "perturbative" (β=0.78 < 1) but its amplitude ceiling is λ*≈1.28 — a 28% margin. Push to λ=1.3 to enlarge the shortening and the series term overtakes the first-order term (β_series=1.01): the linearization on which S_L was computed is invalid, and the geometry is fictitious. The shortening that looked attractive at λ=1.3 was computed on a background that the excitation itself has destroyed.

E09b.3 Step 7 (cont.) — the DYNAMIC STATUS machine (the leaf's spine)

This is the acceptance test with teeth: "assumption changes update status." A static gate that stamps a verdict once and forgets the assumptions behind it is exactly how an overclaim survives — someone later nudges the cutoff up, or the amplitude down, the old AUDIT stays glued on, and a UV_DELEGATED mode is silently read as "cleared." The dynamic status machine forbids this: the candidate's status is a pure function of its assumption set, recomputed on every assumption change, and is monotone-down — assumptions can only ever lower the ladder, never raise it, without owner/attorney escalation (CONTRACT §1.4).

E09b.3.1 The assumption vector and the status function

A candidate's EFT verdict is a function of a declared assumption vector:

A = { Λ_c,                  # the EFT cutoff scale (provenance-tagged: corpus-agnostic | from B-UQFC-14-UV-1)
      g_bg,                 # the background (frozen parent | standard-GR baseline)
      λ_amp,                # the excitation amplitude
      grid,                 # the sampling resolution (under-resolution = fail-open hazard)
      Λ_c_provenance }      # lineage tag from the corpus dependency graph (E08a)
status_EFT(A) = combine( cutoff_ratios(·,Λ_c), backreaction(·,λ_amp,g_bg), provenance_rule(Λ_c_provenance) )

The combiner takes the earliest/worst of the three sub-verdicts (fail-closed min on the ladder):

function status_EFT(A):
    c = cutoff_ratios(invariants(A.g_bg, Ξ), A.Λ_c, A.grid, lobe)
    b = backreaction(dg1(Ξ), A.g_bg, T_eff, A.grid, lobe, A.λ_amp)
    if b.background_check == "FAIL":            return "FAIL_BACKREACTION"   # background gone — earliest, worst
    if c.uv_boundary == "FAIL":                 return "FAIL"               # cutoff breached on a controlled bg
    if c.uv_boundary == "UV_DELEGATED":         return "UV_DELEGATED"       # cutoff breached OR Λ_c from axiom
    if A.Λ_c_provenance == "from_B-UQFC-14-UV-1": return "UV_DELEGATED"     # NC-AXIOM: provenance forces it
    return "AUDIT"                                                          # χ<1 AND β<1 AND Λ_c corpus-agnostic

FAIL_BACKREACTION outranks (is worse than) a cutoff breach because a destroyed background means there is no geometry on which to even define the cutoff ratios — the very invariants cutoff_ratios consumed were computed on a metric the excitation has invalidated. Order matters; the machine reports the earliest-firing failure, consistent with the document's earliest-gate-ranking discipline (H1).

E09b.3.2 Worked status transitions (the acceptance test, executed)

We exercise the machine on the source-matched survivor MID-SCAL-029 (the single massless canonical scalar δφ; the only mode to pass the HC-02 source gate at PASS_TOY; carried through D2/E03b). Note that this mode's legitimately-sourced S_L is ~10⁻⁴⁰ — below the detection floor — so it has already failed on magnitude (FAIL_BACKREACTION, owned by D2) before it reaches this gate; the transitions below are run on its toy-amplitude curvature/gradient invariants purely to exercise the status machine, and the χ/β numbers are status-machine probe values at the toy code-unit amplitude, not evidence of a detectable effect. We start from its declared assumptions and change one assumption at a time, showing the status moves:

# Assumption changed New value χ β Old status New status Why it moved
0 (baseline) Λ_c=1, λ=1.0, Λ_c corpus-agnostic 0.34 0.21 — AUDIT χ<1, β<1, cutoff corpus-agnostic
1 cutoff provenance Λ_c sourced from B-UQFC-14-UV-1 0.34 0.21 AUDIT UV_DELEGATED NC-AXIOM: admissibility now leans on the UNADOPTED axiom
2 lower the cutoff Λ_c: 1 → 0.5 0.68 0.21 AUDIT AUDIT (margin halved) χ doubled (n=1 channel) but still <1; margin now 0.47
3 lower further Λ_c: 1 → 0.30 1.13 0.21 AUDIT UV_DELEGATED χ≥1: cutoff breached; curvature now above the (lower) cutoff
4 raise amplitude λ: 1.0 → 2.4 0.34 1.05 AUDIT FAIL_BACKREACTION β_series≥1: second-order term overtakes first; background invalid
5 coarsen the grid N: 4096 → 256 0.31* 0.19* AUDIT AUDIT (with flag) under-resolved; ratios under-report* — flagged AUDIT, not trusted
6 swap background frozen parent → standard-GR baseline 0.34 0.21 UV_DELEGATED(#1) AUDIT corpus-agnostic background removes the axiom dependency (G2)

Reading the table. Row 1 is the headline: merely declaring that the cutoff's value comes from the compactification stability axiom — without changing a single number — moves the mode from AUDIT to UV_DELEGATED. The physics is identical; the honesty about provenance is what the status tracks. Rows 3 and 4 are the two distinct first failures of the chapter realized as transitions: lower the cutoff enough and you breach it (UV_DELEGATED); raise the amplitude enough and you invalidate the background (FAIL_BACKREACTION). Row 5 is the fail-open guard: coarsening the grid lowers χ (under-resolution misses the wall peak), which would look like an improvement — the machine refuses to trust a lowered χ from a coarsened grid and emits AUDIT (under-resolved), never an upgrade. Row 6 is the corpus-agnostic escape (G2): re-deriving on a standard-GR baseline that does not depend on B-UQFC-14-UV-1 legitimately removes the axiom dependency and returns AUDIT — this is the one upward move allowed, and it is allowed precisely because it removes an assumption rather than promoting a claim.

First failure of §E09b.3: a non-monotone status function. If status_EFT could move up the ladder on an assumption change other than provenance-removal (row 6), an adversary could "tune to pass" by cherry-picking a generous cutoff. The machine forbids this: status is min-combined and the only sanctioned upward transition is removing a corpus dependency (making a claim more general), which is escalation-free precisely because it weakens, not strengthens, the assumption set. Every numerical knob (Λ_c value, amplitude, resolution) can only hold or lower the status. Tuning-to-pass is structurally impossible.

E09b.3.3 Acceptance-test mapping

Acceptance test (HC-09 source doc) Implementation Where
"cutoff breach downgrades" χ ≥ 1 ⇒ UV_DELEGATED/FAIL; rows 3 of §E09b.3.2; NC-BREACH §E09b.1.2, §E09b.4
"EFT candidate has ratios" every mode reaching HC-09 carries {χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad,χ_F, β_back, β_series} (χ_F null for non-gauge modes); no empty rows in table 7 §E09b.5

E09b.4 Step 8 — negative controls (the gate's own tripwires)

Five controls, each a permanent regression test that fires at the cutoff/backreaction gate specifically:

NC-BREACH   feed the sharpened toy wall (σ=1.10). REQUIRE χ≥1 in the curvature channel,
            verdict UV_DELEGATED. If the gate returns AUDIT-clean -> the gate is BROKEN (fail-open).
NC-SUBCUT   feed a broad, smooth lobe (σ=0.05) with all invariants << Λ_c. REQUIRE χ<1, β<1,
            verdict AUDIT (NOT a clean PASS). Catches over-eager FAIL and confirms the AUDIT ceiling.
NC-AXIOM    feed a sub-cutoff lobe whose Λ_c provenance = B-UQFC-14-UV-1. REQUIRE the verdict is
            forced to UV_DELEGATED regardless of the operator flag. Catches cosmetic AUDIT-laundering.
NC-DYNAMIC  feed a mode at AUDIT, then lower Λ_c past breach AND raise λ past the ceiling.
            REQUIRE status moves to UV_DELEGATED then FAIL_BACKREACTION (never stays AUDIT).
            Catches a frozen/static status that ignores assumption changes.
NC-BR-GAUGE feed a PURE-GAUGE δg^{(2)} (coordinate-only second-order response). REQUIRE β≈0
            (the gauge-invariant backreaction is null). Catches a false FAIL_BACKREACTION on coordinate noise.
NC-GRID     feed the σ=0.90 wall at N=256 then N=4096. REQUIRE the coarse χ is FLAGGED under-resolved
            and NOT trusted as an improvement over the fine χ. Catches the fail-open under-sampling bug.

NC-BREACH is the load-bearing one and maps to the acceptance test "cutoff breach downgrades." NC-SUBCUT is the false-positive guard — without it an over-aggressive gate would label every smooth lobe cutoff-breached and the document's credibility (which rests on the gate being discriminating) would collapse. NC-DYNAMIC is the integrity guard for the whole leaf: it is the executed form of "assumption changes update status." NC-BR-GAUGE keeps the backreaction score honest against the coordinate-artifact hazard of §E09b.2. First failure of §E09b.4: if NC-GRID is omitted, a coarsened grid silently lowers χ and a thin-wall breach passes as AUDIT — the same fail-open under-resolution hazard the energy gate guarded with its Richardson criterion (E03b §E03b.2.4), here transposed to curvature ratios. The controls exist so the gate's strictness is earned and its leniency is bounded.

E09b.5.5 Step 9 (cont.) — propagation to the MISSION and PATENT reports

The closure target's strong clause (HC-09 source doc) is: "propagate cutoff sensitivity into mission and patent reports." This is the second deliverable of the leaf, and it is what makes the cutoff gate load-bearing on the rest of the document rather than a local audit.

(a) Propagation to the MISSION report (HC-10 overlay). The mission_validity_overlay function (HC-10 / Appendix 30) consumes the per-trajectory status_EFT verdict and is hard-wired to refuse to render a forward-distance benefit without the cutoff/backreaction watermark. The propagation contract is:

for each sampled trajectory point τ along a mission plot using mode M:
    A_τ = assumption_vector(M, Λ_c, g_bg, λ_amp(τ), grid)
    s_τ = status_EFT(A_τ)
    if s_τ == "FAIL_BACKREACTION":  overlay.void_point(τ)   # S_L meaningless: bg invalid here
    if s_τ == "UV_DELEGATED":       overlay.watermark(τ, "UV_DELEGATED · χ=%.2f · Λ_c from B-UQFC-14-UV-1")
    overlay.attach(τ, {chi, beta, margin_to_breach, amplitude_ceiling})
# any plot that renders S_L>0 at a point whose s_τ ∈ {UV_DELEGATED, FAIL_BACKREACTION}
# without the watermark/void -> HC-10 raises FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

So a Mars plot using mode 29 carries a doubly disqualifying annotation: its sourced S_L is ~10⁻⁴⁰ (below ε_detect — it is already magnitude-killed, so there is no renderable benefit to begin with), and even the toy-amplitude geometry it is drawn on is watermarked at every point UV_DELEGATED · χ≈0.34 · Λ_c from B-UQFC-14-UV-1; a plot that tried to sharpen the lobe to enlarge the local shortening to detectability would drive χ_grad ≥ 1 and hit points where β ≥ 1, and the overlay voids those points (the geometry there is fictitious). The cutoff gate is thereby the mechanism that prevents a locally-pretty Mars plot from becoming a mission overclaim — it stamps the validity of the very geometry the trajectory is drawn on. First failure of §E09b.5.5(a): an unwatermarked benefit. A plot rendering any apparent S_L > 0 at a UV_DELEGATED/FAIL_BACKREACTION point without the overlay is, by construction, FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM (HC-10's first failure), and HC-09's propagation contract is exactly what supplies HC-10 the per-point verdict it needs.

(b) Propagation to the PATENT report. The patent-support matrix (I-series) consumes the cutoff/backreaction outputs as the evidentiary basis for the validity-overlay and cutoff-aware-output claims (HC-09 patent-relevance line: "EFT-validity scoring and cutoff-aware simulation outputs"). The propagation is: every gate card's {χ_•, β, margin_to_breach, amplitude_ceiling, Λ_c_provenance} block becomes a claim-support exhibit — the patent claims a method for annotating candidate-metric simulation outputs with a recomputed-on-assumption-change EFT-validity status, and the exhibit is the §E09b.3.2 transition table demonstrating the status actually moves. First failure of §E09b.5.5(b): a patent claim that asserts validity rather than scoring it. The claim must be to the scoring/annotation method (process), never to "an EFT-valid drive"; the §101 memo (I2) leans on exactly this distinction. The forbidden version — "a cutoff-cleared metric" — is negated on sight.

E09b.7 Step 11 — reviewer attacks (chapter-level)

Attack 1 — "Just pick a high enough cutoff Λ_c and every χ < 1. Your gate is one free parameter away from passing everything." Honest response: That is precisely the move the dynamic status machine + NC-AXIOM forbid. The value of Λ_c is provenance-tagged: a cutoff high enough to clear a sharp wall does not come from a standard-EFT estimate — it comes from the compactification stability axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1, which the corpus (TOE_FINAL diff) leaves UNADOPTED with global UV stability OPEN. NC-AXIOM forces any such mode to UV_DELEGATED regardless of the operator flag. You cannot buy a pass with a cutoff you are not licensed to assume; you can only relabel the unknown as UV_DELEGATED, which is what we do. The one legitimate way to lower the status to AUDIT is to re-derive Λ_c corpus-agnostically (the G2 standard-GR baseline) — and for the sharp-wall modes that estimate sits below the wall curvature, so they breach anyway.

Attack 2 — "β_back < 1 means the backreaction is small. That is a pass — admit your best mode is perturbatively fine." Honest response: β < 1 means the linearization has not yet broken down at the declared toy amplitude — it is AUDIT, not PASS, because (i) the amplitude ceiling λ* is finite and published, so the same mode becomes FAIL_BACKREACTION the moment you push λ toward the shortening you actually want (MID-SCAL-029: λ*≈2.4 at the toy probe amplitude — and note its sourced S_L is ~10⁻⁴⁰, already below detection, so "the shortening you actually want" is unreachable without also breaching χ_grad; thin-wall illustration: λ*<1), and (ii) β<1 says nothing about the cutoff, the energy condition, or causality — all of which MID-SCAL-029 carries as AUDIT/UV_DELEGATED as well. "Perturbatively fine at this toy amplitude" is not "a working background at mission amplitude," and we never let the former masquerade as the latter.

Attack 3 — "You take the max over the lobe. One bad point shouldn't condemn an otherwise-controlled profile — average it." Honest response: The lobe passes through the bad point. A worst-point breach is not a measure-zero nuisance; it is the statement that the EFT is uncontrolled exactly where the geometry is doing the work (the wall). Averaging is the fail-open mistake — it is how a thin-wall catastrophe hides behind a large benign volume (the same reason E03b integrates the worst-case NEC, not a frame-soft average). And NC-GRID shows the opposite hazard: coarsening the grid lowers the max by missing the wall, which we refuse to trust. The max is not alarmism; it is the only resolution-robust statement.

Attack 4 — "UV_DELEGATED is just a fancy way of refusing to fail and refusing to pass. It is a non-answer." Honest response: It is the correct answer and it is contract-mandated (§2 UV-delegation rule). UV_DELEGATED is a precise claim: the result depends on physics above the cutoff that this framework does not control, so the admissibility is unknown, not absent. That is the opposite of a non-answer — it is a located, named dependency (B-UQFC-14-UV-1, UNADOPTED) with an explicit closure path (HC-12 / E08b, or a corpus-agnostic re-derivation). Calling unknown "fine" would be the dishonest move; calling it UV_DELEGATED is what keeps the document from overclaiming a cleared cutoff.

E09b.8 Step 12 — patent extraction

Simulation-only, hardware-free, magnitude-independent assets crystallized in E09b (per the HC-09 patent-relevance line "EFT-validity scoring and cutoff-aware simulation outputs"):

  1. EFT cutoff-ratio scoring engine — the channel ratios {χ_R (Ricci), χ_K (Kretschmann/Weyl), χ_T (intrinsic stress), χ_grad (gradient), χ_F (gauge field-strength)}, the worst-point aggregate χ = max_x max_• χ_•, and the closed-form cutoff-sensitivity derivative dχ/dlnΛ_c = −n_{•*}χ with the resulting margin-to-breach in e-folds of Λ_c. The simultaneous Ricci-and-Weyl pair (χ_R and χ_K, distinct curvature channels) is the load-bearing novelty over single-invariant validity checks. Method claim; useful for any candidate metric in any EFT.
  2. Self-consistent backreaction auditor — the second-order response δg^{(2)} solver, the curvature-weighted backreaction score β_back = ‖δ²g‖/‖g_bg‖, the gradient-expansion ratio β_series, and the amplitude ceiling λ* at which perturbativity fails — computed on the gauge-invariant part of δg^{(2)} to avoid coordinate-artifact false positives.
  3. Dynamic, assumption-indexed status machine — status_EFT(A) as a pure, monotone-down function of a provenance-tagged assumption vector, recomputed on every assumption change, with the only sanctioned upward transition being corpus-dependency removal. This is the leaf's novel core: a status that cannot be tuned to pass.
  4. Provenance-forced UV-delegation rule (NC-AXIOM) — the lineage check that forces any admissibility resting on an UNADOPTED UV axiom (B-UQFC-14-UV-1) to UV_DELEGATED regardless of operator flags, against a corpus dependency graph.
  5. Cutoff-aware mission/patent propagation — the contract that pushes per-trajectory {χ, β, margin, ceiling, provenance} into the mission overlay (watermark/void) and the patent claim-support matrix, so that no downstream artifact can render a benefit without the validity annotation.

First failure (patent section): these claims lean on textbook EFT power-counting (ratios of invariants to a cutoff) and standard cosmological-perturbation backreaction, so the underlying estimates are prior art. The novelty is the integrated, fail-closed, dynamic pipeline — provenance-tagged assumption vector + monotone-down status function that cannot be tuned to pass + NC-AXIOM provenance forcing + the cutoff→mission/patent propagation contract — not the power-counting itself. We claim the system and the assumption-indexed status discipline, never the physics of UV completion.

Forbidden-claim box. This leaf does not and cannot assert: UV completion adopted/UV completion closed; global stability solved; cutoff cleared unconditionally; that any mode is EFT-admissible in an assumption-free sense; working warp drive; or negative energy available. Every such phrase is negated on sight by the gate's structure: the best token is AUDIT (ratios clean at a corpus-agnostic declared cutoff), and any reliance on the compactification axiom is forced to UV_DELEGATED. The strongest allowed statement is the conditional contract form: a profile is retained as a TOY_MODEL / EFT-audit candidate only with its cutoff ratios, backreaction score, and cutoff provenance published, and only if its admissibility is established without leaning on the UNADOPTED B-UQFC-14-UV-1 axiom — which, for every forward-shortening survivor in this library, it currently is not.

What remains to close: (1) a corpus-agnostic, standard-EFT derivation of Λ_c for the parent geometry that does not lean on B-UQFC-14-UV-1 (would lift the best survivors from UV_DELEGATED to AUDIT; currently OPEN — HC-12/E08b); (2) a proven inequality relating the breach margin to the shortening (χ ≥ 1 ⇐ S_L > S_*) replacing the empirical cutoff↔shortening lock — currently AUDIT on generality; (3) a non-perturbative (full Einstein-equation) re-solution for the FAIL_BACKREACTION modes to determine whether any controlled large-amplitude geometry exists at all, or whether the breakdown is genuine; (4) extension of the backreaction auditor beyond second order (δg^{(3)} and the convergence radius of the full series); (5) SI-unit cutoff accounting, deliberately not done here to avoid a forbidden physical-magnitude claim, gated behind the full source + UV stack. E10a — HC-10 Mars Mission Relevance — Object & Target

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED (object + target + local-shortening estimator built and negative-control-tested on a toy two-body transfer; ceiling PASS_TOY, not reached — terminal status AUDIT) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

Scope note (HC-10, leaf a of two). This leaf builds the object and the target for the Mars-mission-relevance challenge. It does exactly six things, in order: (1) it states, as a theorem-shaped obligation, that a local forward-lobe metric effect does not imply a shorter Earth→Mars mission; (2) it defines the formal objects — the toy transfer trajectory, the vehicle tetrad, the forward lobe F_τ, and the local-shortening functional — that let us attach a lobe to a path without lying about what was measured; (3) it builds the local shortening estimator and works it on a concrete two-body transfer with explicit numbers; (4) it specifies the gate-status overlay and the simulation watermark that every mission figure must carry; (5) it specifies the integration contract that keeps the metric-interface system an optional overlay on a retained classical baseline, never a replacement; (6) it builds the negative controls that catch the signature failure — a mission plot that omits gate status or implies a global travel-time proof. The actual five hostile scenarios (coordinate-only fake, unsourced metric, exotic failure, UV-delegated mode, best surviving toy) and their per-scenario gate cards are leaf E10b. Nothing here is a propulsion result, a travel-time result, or a flight-subsystem placement. The deliverable is a validity-weighted mission visualization contract and its negative-control library — the firewall that prevents a local, status-labeled, possibly-coordinate-only lobe effect from being rendered as "Mars faster."

1. Why this challenge matters (HC-10)

Every other hard challenge in this corpus is about whether a candidate excitation Ξ_drive does anything physical and local: does it carry a real invariant (HC-05), a real source (HC-02), a non-exotic energy ledger (HC-03), a causal cone (HC-04)? HC-10 is the challenge about the last and most dangerous extrapolation: the leap from a local, comoving, status-labeled lobe to a sentence a reader will remember — "this gets us to Mars faster." That sentence is the single most quotable, most over-claimable, and most physically unlicensed statement the entire document could produce. HC-10 exists to make that statement impossible to assemble from anything this platform computes.

The hardness is structural, not rhetorical. Three independent gaps separate "local lobe shortens a proper-distance functional" from "the mission is shorter," and each gap can be a full FAIL on its own:

  1. The locality gap. The forward proper-distance functional L_F[Ξ] is evaluated along a short comoving segment in the vehicle's instantaneous frame — a tube of a few lobe-widths around the worldline. A shortening S_L > 0 of that segment is a statement about a metre-to-kilometre-scale neighbourhood of the ship, in coordinates that move with the ship. The Earth→Mars mission is an ~10⁸-km, multi-month, heliocentric two-body (really N-body) boundary-value problem in a fixed inertial frame. There is no theorem that integrates the first into the second. A local lobe is a local lobe.

  2. The invariance gap. As HC-05 established at length, a positive S_L computed along a coordinate curve can be pure diffeomorphism — δR_μνρσ = 0, effect evaporates under reparameterization. A mission plot built on such an S_L is plotting a coordinate artifact as a mission gain. The mission layer inherits every upstream invariance, source, energy, causality, gauge, and UV failure and must display them, not launder them.

  3. The accounting gap. Even a genuine, invariant, sourced local shortening does not reduce time-of-flight unless it is connected to the vehicle's actual equations of motion with a closed momentum/energy ledger — propellant, Δv, power, the works. This platform does not compute that connection (it is exactly the propulsion claim the build contract forbids). So the mission figure can show a local effect overlaid on a baseline; it may never redraw the baseline's arrival time.

First failure (this section / leaf). The challenge's signature failure is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM: a mission figure that (a) omits the gate-status overlay, or (b) omits the simulation watermark, or (c) renders the local shortening as a change to the global time-of-flight / arrival date, or (d) replaces, rather than overlays, the retained classical baseline. Any one of (a)–(d) is the first failure. The mirror failure this leaf must also defend against is under-claim-by-omission — silently dropping a genuine, gated, status-labeled local effect so the figure says nothing — which would make the visualization useless as an option-value artifact. §6 builds the two-sided control for both.

2. Formal object — trajectory, tetrad, lobe, and the local-shortening functional

We define five objects. Together they are the smallest set that lets us attach a forward lobe to a real trajectory and read off a local number, with every coordinate/frame dependence made explicit so it can be audited.

2.1 The toy transfer trajectory z^μ(τ)

The baseline is a classical heliocentric two-body Hohmann-like transfer, Earth orbit → Mars orbit, parameterized by proper time τ (toy units, c = 1, lengths in AU, the Sun at the focus). The worldline is

z^μ(τ) = ( t(τ),  x(τ) )  ,   x(τ) ∈ R³ heliocentric inertial

with x(τ) the solution of the toy two-body problem

d²x/dt² = − μ_☉ x / |x|³ ,   μ_☉ = GM_☉ (toy-normalized) ,
x(0) = r_E ê ,  ẋ(0) = v_peri ê_⊥   (transfer-orbit injection at Earth radius r_E = 1 AU)

and the transfer ellipse chosen so aphelion = r_M = 1.524 AU (Mars radius). The baseline time of flight T_baseline is the half-period of the transfer ellipse:

a_t = (r_E + r_M)/2 = 1.262 AU ,   T_baseline = π √(a_t³ / μ_☉)

In standard (non-toy) units this is the textbook ≈ 259 days; in our toy units we carry it as a number with a status label, T_baseline = T_baseline(toy), and we never redraw it. It is the immovable reference.

2.2 The vehicle tetrad e_a^μ(τ)

To attach a lobe that is comoving and front/back-asymmetric we need the ship's instantaneous rest frame. The tetrad e_a^μ(τ) (a = 0,1,2,3) is built by transporting an orthonormal frame along z^μ:

e_0^μ = u^μ = dz^μ/dτ           (timelike, the four-velocity, ḡ_μν u^μ u^ν = −1)
e_1^μ = forward unit (Fermi–Walker transported, instantaneous velocity direction)
e_2^μ, e_3^μ = transverse, completing the orthonormal triad
ḡ_μν e_a^μ e_b^ν = η_ab

e_1^μ is the forward axis: the direction along which the lobe's front/back asymmetry is defined. Fermi–Walker (not parallel) transport keeps the frame non-rotating relative to gyroscopes, which is the physically correct comoving frame and matters for the §4 caveat: the lobe lives in this frame, not in the heliocentric inertial frame, and the mapping between them is exactly where the locality gap bites.

2.3 The forward lobe F_τ(D, ρ)

The forward lobe is the comoving excitation profile, expressed as a function of comoving longitudinal coordinate D (signed distance ahead of the ship along e_1) and transverse radius ρ:

F_τ(D, ρ) = A(τ) · g(D) · h(ρ) ,
g(D) = front/back-asymmetric kernel,  g(D>0) ≠ g(−D)   (the asymmetry is the whole point)
h(ρ) = exp(−ρ²/σ²)                                       (transverse confinement)

A concrete toy kernel (used in §3) is the asymmetric difference-of-Gaussians

g(D) = exp(−(D − d₀)²/w_f²) − β · exp(−(D + d₀)²/w_b²) ,
d₀ = 0.5,  w_f = 0.8,  w_b = 1.2,  β = 0.6   (front sharper/closer, back broader/weaker)

The lobe enters the metric as the build-contract excitation Ξ_drive restricted to the comoving tube; in the toy we take a scalar-lapse-like longitudinal component

δg_DD(τ, D, ρ) = 2 A(τ) g(D) h(ρ) ,   A(τ) = amplitude schedule along the trajectory

This is the object HC-05 would test for pure-gauge content and HC-02/03 for source/energy content. Here we do not re-derive those gates; we carry their verdicts as inputs (the gate-status object, §2.5) and forbid the mission layer from acting on a lobe whose upstream gates have not passed.

2.4 The local forward proper-distance functional and the LOCAL shortening

The forward proper-distance functional, evaluated locally in the comoving tube over a fixed comoving aperture D ∈ [0, D_max] at trajectory parameter τ:

L_F[Ξ; τ] = ∫₀^{D_max} √( ḡ_DD + δg_DD(τ, D, 0) )  dD        (on-axis, ρ = 0)
L_F[0; τ]  = ∫₀^{D_max} √( ḡ_DD )  dD = D_max               (baseline, flat aperture)

The LOCAL shortening fraction at trajectory point τ is

S_L(τ) = ( L_F[0; τ] − L_F[Ξ; τ] ) / L_F[0; τ]

This is a number between (typically) −1 and 1, defined per trajectory point, in the comoving frame, over a fixed local aperture. It is emphatically not a change in T_baseline. The central design decision of this leaf is captured in one equation — the forbidden contraction:

   FORBIDDEN:   T_mission  ?=  T_baseline · ( 1 − ⟨S_L⟩ )       ← NEVER. No such law.

There is no licensed map from ⟨S_L⟩ (an average of a local, comoving, aperture-dependent number) to T_mission. The mission dashboard may display S_L(τ) as a local overlay along the path and may display T_baseline as the retained baseline, but it may not multiply one by the other. §3 computes the overlay; §4–§6 enforce the prohibition.

2.5 The gate-status object Γ(τ)

Every point of the overlay carries a gate-status object, the same JSON schema the rest of the document uses, evaluated for the lobe at that point:

Γ(τ) = { invariant: PASS|FAIL|AUDIT,  source: PASS|FAIL|AUDIT,
         energy: PASS|AUDIT,          causality: PASS|FAIL|AUDIT,
         gauge: PASS|FAIL|AUDIT,      uv: PASS|UV_DELEGATED|FAIL,
         net: worst-of-the-above }

Γ.net = worst-of is fail-closed: a single FAIL anywhere makes the point red; an AUDIT makes it amber; only all-PASS (with energy at most PASS/audit-visible) makes it green. The overlay is colored by Γ.net, and a non-green Γ.net forbids any quantitative shortening from being rendered as anything but a status-labeled, watermarked, local artifact. This object is the bridge that makes HC-10 inherit every upstream gate rather than bypass it.

2.6 Layer mapping (three-layer discipline — every object maps)

Mission object Symbol Layer What it is constrained by
transfer worldline z^μ(τ) × metric/geometric base classical two-body GR/Newtonian baseline
vehicle tetrad e_a^μ(τ) × (frame on the base) Fermi–Walker transport
forward lobe F_τ(D,ρ), δg_DD × (perturbation) ⊕ (admissibility) χ = max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad) < 1
local shortening S_L(τ) derived diagnostic invariance gate (HC-05) keys its validity
gate-status object Γ(τ) ⊕ projection/validity worst-of upstream gate cards

Every mission object maps to a layer, and every quantitative object (S_L) is gated by the validity layer ⊕ through Γ. A mission figure that renders a quantity not backed by a layer-mapped, Γ-gated object is invalid.

3. Minimal toy closure — local shortening along a toy transfer (worked)

This is the minimal closure required by the build artifacts src/mission/orbits_toy.py and src/mission/local_lobe_along_path.py. We compute the local shortening S_L(τ) at a handful of points along the toy Earth→Mars transfer, with explicit numbers, and we show — by construction — that the mission time of flight is untouched.

3.1 Build the toy transfer (orbits_toy.py)

function build_toy_transfer():
    mu = 1.0                          # toy-normalized solar GM
    r_E, r_M = 1.0, 1.524             # AU
    a_t = (r_E + r_M)/2               # = 1.262 AU
    T_baseline = pi * sqrt(a_t**3 / mu)   # half-period (toy units)
    # integrate two-body ODE from peri (Earth) to apo (Mars)
    states = integrate_kepler(r_E, v_injection(a_t, r_E), steps=N)
    return states, T_baseline         # states = [(t_k, x_k, v_k)], T_baseline IMMOVABLE

Worked baseline numbers (toy units, μ = 1):

a_t = 1.262 AU
T_baseline = π √(1.262³) = π √(2.010) = π · 1.418 = 4.454   (toy time units)

T_baseline = 4.454 is the only time-of-flight number this leaf produces, and it is the baseline. It is never modified below.

3.2 Sample five trajectory points and build the comoving frame

We sample at fractional path positions f = 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (Earth injection → mid-transfer → Mars arrival), build the tetrad e_a^μ at each via build_tetrad(state_k), and orient the lobe forward axis e_1 along the instantaneous velocity v_k.

3.3 Attach the lobe and compute LOCAL S_L(τ) (local_lobe_along_path.py)

We use the §2.3 asymmetric kernel with an amplitude schedule A(τ) that ramps up mid-transfer (where, in a hypothetical that we do not endorse, a candidate mode might be "engaged") and the fixed local aperture D_max = 4.0 (four lobe-widths). On-axis (ρ = 0):

function local_S_L(state, A, kernel, D_max=4.0, n=2000):
    integrand_base  = lambda D: sqrt(1.0)                  # ḡ_DD = 1 (flat aperture)
    integrand_lobe  = lambda D: sqrt(max(1.0 + 2*A*kernel(D), 1e-12))
    L0 = quad(integrand_base, 0, D_max, n)                 # = D_max = 4.0
    LF = quad(integrand_lobe, 0, D_max, n)
    return (L0 - LF)/L0                                    # LOCAL shortening fraction

Worked numbers (asymmetric kernel g(D) of §2.3, h = 1 on-axis):

Substantiated reference computation (red-team-corrected). The values below were re-derived directly from the §2.3 kernel (d₀=0.5, w_f=0.8, w_b=1.2, β=0.6) over the aperture D ∈ [0, D_max=4.0]. They correct an earlier draft that reported a positive (shortening) sign: with this kernel and aperture the back lobe sits at D = −d₀ = −0.5, outside the integration window [0,4], so only the forward (positive) peak contributes — ∫₀^{D_max} g(D) dD = +0.80 > 0, hence ∫ δg_DD dD = 2A·∫g dD > 0, hence L_F[Ξ] > L_F[0] and S_L < 0. The local effect of this toy lobe over this aperture is therefore a local lengthening, not a shortening. This is carried as a status-labeled reference number, not a claim.

f (path frac) A(τ) schedule L_F[0;τ] L_F[Ξ;τ] S_L(τ) (LOCAL) Γ.net (input)
0.00 (Earth inj.) 0.00 4.000 4.000 0.0000 green (lobe off)
0.25 0.05 4.000 4.039 −0.0098 amber (AUDIT)
0.50 (mid) 0.10 4.000 4.078 −0.0194 amber (AUDIT)
0.75 0.05 4.000 4.039 −0.0098 amber (AUDIT)
1.00 (Mars arr.) 0.00 4.000 4.000 0.0000 green (lobe off)

The peak local effect is S_L = −1.94 % (a lengthening of the on-axis local proper distance) at mid-transfer, over a four-lobe-width comoving aperture, with the lobe at amplitude A = 0.10. The sign is negative because, over the aperture [0, D_max], only the forward (positive) peak of the asymmetric kernel is captured — the broader back lobe centered at D = −d₀ lies outside the window — so ∫ δg_DD dD > 0 and the line-element integral grows. Crucially, for HC-10 the sign is immaterial to the verdict: whether the local number is a shortening or a lengthening, it is a local, comoving, aperture-dependent number that does not enter the heliocentric equations of motion and therefore cannot move T_baseline. A draft that had reported a positive +1.55% "shortening" here would have been doubly dangerous (right-signed for the overclaim narrative and numerically wrong); the red-team correction removes both hazards while leaving the firewall logic intact.

3.4 The mission time of flight is UNTOUCHED — by construction

The critical output of the minimal closure is the non-result:

T_baseline           = 4.454   (computed once, §3.1)
T_with_overlay       = 4.454   (IDENTICAL — the overlay does not enter the equations of motion)
ΔT                   = 0.000

The lobe was attached to the visualization of the trajectory, not to the dynamics of the trajectory. The two-body ODE that produced T_baseline has no term for δg_DD; nothing in the mission-time computation reads S_L(τ). This is not an oversight — it is the contract. The platform does not possess a licensed mechanism to feed a local, comoving, status-labeled S_L back into the heliocentric equations of motion (that mechanism would be propulsion, with a closed momentum/energy ledger, which is out of scope and forbidden). So the mission figure shows a local overlay on an unchanged baseline, and the arrival date is the baseline arrival date. Any version of this figure in which T moves is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

3.5 What the minimal closure has and has not shown

Has shown: a forward lobe can be attached to a real toy transfer and produces a well-defined, local, per-point number with explicit values (peak |S_L| = 1.94%, a local lengthening, over a 4-width aperture at A = 0.10 — see the substantiated reference computation in §3.3). Has not shown: that the mission is shorter (it is not — ΔT = 0; indeed the toy local effect is a lengthening, not a shortening), that S_L is invariant (that is HC-05's verdict, carried in as Γ.invariant), that the lobe is sourced or non-exotic (HC-02/03, carried in as Γ.source/Γ.energy), or that any of this survives at mission scale (the locality gap, §4). The minimal closure's entire epistemic content is: "here is the local number, here is the untouched baseline, and here is why one does not become the other."

4. Corpus & integration authority — what licenses the overlay, and what it forbids

  • Engineering handoff doc 07 (Spacecraft Integration & Classical Rocket Interface) is the governing authority for this leaf. It fixes the integration philosophy verbatim: "The metric-interface system should be modeled as an optional mission overlay, not as a replacement for all classical spacecraft systems." The baseline spacecraft retains trajectory planning, attitude control, thermal management, communications, crew/cargo environment, and conventional propulsion assumptions for baseline comparison. This is the corpus authority that makes "overlay, never replacement" a structural requirement, not a stylistic preference. We use it for the integration contract (§5); we may not use it to place the system on any actual subsystem — the doc's own answer to "where does this go on a super-heavy-lift launch vehicle?" is "Nowhere yet."

  • The handoff doc's interface table is adopted as the §5 contract: navigation: vehicle state → lobe frame; mission planning: trajectory → validity-weighted metric; control: target profile → gate-supervised command abstraction; telemetry: observables → gate status; safety: hazard flags → abort/downgrade; patent/software: configs/reports → figures/claims. These are requirements/interface-level boundaries only — inputs and outputs, never build steps. The handoff doc is explicit: "treats integration at the requirements/interface level only."

  • The handoff doc's "What not to claim" list is imported directly into the §8 forbidden box: not "no propellant needed," not "no classical propulsion needed," not "Mars transfer solved," not "operational drive replaces rockets." The permitted sentence is exactly the handoff doc's: "The framework evaluates whether candidate metric-interface profiles produce local, status-labeled changes along a Mars-transfer trajectory." Every word of that sentence is load-bearing: local, status-labeled, along (not "of") a trajectory.

  • HC-10 closure path doc (source 13) fixes the closure target — "a validity-weighted Mars visualization that links local metric effects to mission metrics without overclaiming" — and the minimal closure — "attach forward lobe to a toy trajectory and compute local shortening with gate overlays." It fixes the first failure as "Mission plot omits gate status or implies global travel-time proof" and the downgrade token as FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. It fixes the three acceptance tests — watermark present, gate status overlay present, first failure shown on mission plot — which §5.3 makes machine-checkable. We adopt all of these as the binding contract for this leaf.

  • Build-contract corpus anchors (Fable/TOE). HC-10 consumes the upstream verdicts rather than re-deriving them: the invariance verdict comes from HC-05 (Fable_Forces single-metric / diffeo redundancy), the source/energy verdicts from HC-02/03 (Fable_Forces shared/visible stress-energy, no double counting), and the UV boundary from TOE_FINAL diff (global UV stability OPEN, B-UQFC-14-UV-1 UNADOPTED). Therefore any lobe whose UV gate is UV_DELEGATED propagates that token into Γ.uv, and the overlay must render it as delegated — never as a closed mission gain. This is the mechanism by which the "global stability solved" forbidden phrase is structurally prevented from ever reaching a mission figure.

Honesty note (per contract §2). The locality gap, the invariance gap, and the accounting gap are all statable against standard GR and classical orbital mechanics — no Fable-specific structure is needed to see that a local comoving line-element change does not integrate into a heliocentric time-of-flight. We therefore reach the central HC-10 verdict — "local ≠ global" — corpus-agnostically and say so. The corpus enters only to name the gates (Γ) whose worst-of verdict colors the overlay.

5. The visualization contract & integration contract — built here, run in E10b

5.1 The validity-weighted metric (validity_weighted_metrics.py)

The dashboard never displays a raw S_L(τ). It displays a validity-weighted quantity in which the gate status multiplies the number down toward zero exactly to the degree the gates are not green:

S_L^valid(τ) = W(Γ(τ)) · S_L(τ) ,
W(Γ) = 0                       if Γ.net == FAIL          (red: render zero quantitative effect)
W(Γ) ∈ (0,1)  (e.g. 0.3)       if Γ.net == AUDIT         (amber: down-weighted, status-labeled)
W(Γ) = 1                       if Γ.net == PASS          (green: full local number, still LOCAL)

W is a fail-closed validity weight, not a probability and not a confidence: it encodes "how much of this local number are we licensed to show as a candidate effect, given the gates." A red point shows S_L^valid = 0 regardless of how large the raw coordinate S_L was — this is precisely how a coordinate-only fake (HC-05 FAIL_PURE_GAUGE → Γ.invariant = FAIL → Γ.net = FAIL) is rendered as zero mission-relevant effect while still being plotted in grey as a rejected candidate so the figure tells the truth about what was tried. Worked, applied to §3.3:

f raw S_L Γ.net W S_L^valid
0.25 −0.0098 AUDIT 0.3 −0.0029
0.50 −0.0194 AUDIT 0.3 −0.0058
0.75 −0.0098 AUDIT 0.3 −0.0029

The mid-transfer effect, validity-weighted by its amber gate, is −0.58% local (a down-weighted lengthening) — and still local, still over a 4-width aperture, still attached to an unchanged T_baseline = 4.454. (The sign carries through unchanged: W ≥ 0, so validity-weighting only shrinks the magnitude toward zero; it never flips a lengthening into a shortening.)

5.2 The mission dashboard contract (mars_dashboard.py)

function render_mars_dashboard(states, T_baseline, S_L_series, Gamma_series):
    fig = new_figure()
    # PANEL A: classical baseline — ALWAYS present, ALWAYS first, never redrawn
    plot_transfer_ellipse(states, label="CLASSICAL BASELINE (retained)")
    annotate(f"T_baseline = {T_baseline}  [UNCHANGED]")        # immovable
    # PANEL B: local overlay along the path — colored by Gamma.net
    for k, (s, S, G) in enumerate(zip(states, S_L_series, Gamma_series)):
        color = {PASS:"green", AUDIT:"amber", FAIL:"grey"}[G.net]
        S_valid = validity_weight(G) * S
        plot_local_lobe_marker(s, magnitude=S_valid, color=color)
        attach_gate_badge(s, G)                                # the gate-status overlay
    # MANDATORY annotations — acceptance tests
    assert_watermark(fig, "TOY MODEL · SIMULATION ONLY · NOT A FLIGHT RESULT")
    assert_gate_overlay_present(fig, Gamma_series)
    assert_first_failure_caption(fig, "FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM if T moves or gates hidden")
    forbid_global_time_axis(fig)        # no axis, annotation, or curve that redraws T
    return fig

Three structural guarantees are wired into the renderer and cannot be turned off: (i) Panel A (the classical baseline) is always drawn first and never modified — the overlay is literally a second panel/layer, enforcing "optional overlay, not replacement"; (ii) every local marker carries a gate badge from Γ(τ); (iii) forbid_global_time_axis raises if any figure element would render the local effect as a change to mission time. The renderer that omits any of these does not produce a figure — it raises.

5.3 The three acceptance tests, made machine-checkable

The HC-10 source doc's three acceptance tests become three assertions the figure must pass before it is emitted:

function check_mission_figure(fig):
    t1 = has_watermark(fig, required="SIMULATION ONLY / TOY MODEL")          # "watermark present"
    t2 = every_local_marker_has_gate_badge(fig)                             # "gate status overlay present"
    t3 = has_first_failure_caption(fig, token="FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM")     # "first failure shown on plot"
    t4 = baseline_T_unchanged(fig)        # ADDED: no global-time redraw (the (c)/(d) guard)
    t5 = baseline_panel_present(fig)      # ADDED: classical baseline retained, not replaced
    return all([t1, t2, t3, t4, t5])      # ALL must pass or the figure is rejected

t1–t3 are the source doc's literal acceptance tests; t4–t5 are the leaf's own additions that close the "implies global travel-time proof" and "replaces the baseline" halves of the first failure. A figure failing any of t1–t5 is not emitted and the candidate is logged FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

5.4 The integration contract — optional overlay, retained baseline

From handoff doc 07, the integration boundaries are requirements-level only. The contract this leaf binds:

Interface Input Output Fail-closed rule
navigation vehicle state z^μ, e_a^μ lobe frame if frame ill-defined → no lobe attached
mission planning trajectory z^μ(τ), T_baseline validity-weighted metric S_L^valid(τ) baseline T is read-only
control target profile Ξ gate-supervised command abstraction abstraction only; never a hardware command
telemetry observables gate status Γ missing observable → Γ.net = AUDIT
safety hazard flags abort/downgrade any hazard → W = 0, overlay greyed
patent/software configs/reports figures/claims claims software/system-method only

The answer to "where does this go on a super-heavy-lift launch vehicle?" is the handoff doc's, reproduced exactly as a guard string the dashboard prints in its provenance footer: "Nowhere yet. The near-term artifact is not a flight subsystem; it is a simulation and validation stack that can be run against Mars-transfer mission profiles. Physical integration would require a candidate mode that survives source, energy, causality, gauge, quantum, UV, and EFT gates." The asset that survives this leaf is therefore the validation stack itself — a discriminator that retains value to any rigorous frontier-R&D program regardless of whether a flight subsystem ever exists, because what it protects is the screening discipline, not a survivor.

6. Negative controls — catching the signature failure (worked)

These are the negative-control generators that make the §5 contract testable. Each fabricates a mission figure or input designed to overclaim, and the correct behavior is for check_mission_figure to reject it. They are the HC-10 analog of HC-05's gen_diffeo/gen_gauge — adversaries that try to get a forbidden claim past the firewall.

6.1 gen_global_time_overclaim() → must be REJECTED (the primary first failure)

The most seductive overclaim: take the magnitude of the local series (|⟨S_L⟩|, with the 3-amber mean ≈ 0.0130 and the 5-point mean ≈ 0.0078 from the §3.3 substantiated computation) and apply the forbidden contraction of §2.4 — illegitimately treating the local number as if it were a fractional time saving — to redraw the mission time. The overclaim machine is deliberately sign-blind: a dishonest figure would just take |S_L| and shorten T, regardless of whether the underlying local effect was a lengthening or a shortening — which is exactly why the firewall must reject it on structure, not on the sign of the number.

function gen_global_time_overclaim(S_L_series, T_baseline):
    S_mag  = abs(mean(S_L_series))               # |5-pt mean| ≈ 0.0078  (or amber-only ≈ 0.0130)
    T_fake = T_baseline * (1 - S_mag)            # 4.454 * (1 - 0.0078) = 4.419  ← FORBIDDEN
    fig = render_with_redrawn_time(T_fake)        # redraws arrival earlier
    return fig    # GROUND_TRUTH = OVERCLAIM, expected verdict REJECT

Worked: it would render T_fake = 4.419 (using the 5-point magnitude; ≈ 4.396 if the inflated amber-only mean is used) — a fake ~0.8–1.3% faster Mars. Why it is rejected: forbid_global_time_axis and t4 baseline_T_unchanged both fire — the figure redraws T, which has no licensing law (there is no T = T_baseline(1−⟨S_L⟩) theorem; the two-body ODE never read S_L, and the local number is in fact a lengthening, so even the sign the overclaim assumes is fabricated). Verdict: REJECT, token FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM, first failure = implied global travel-time proof. This is the single most important negative control in the leaf, and it directly exercises the §2.4 prohibition.

6.2 gen_no_gate_overlay() → must be REJECTED (gate-status omission)

function gen_no_gate_overlay(S_L_series):
    fig = render_local_overlay(S_L_series, gate_badges=False)   # plots S_L, hides Γ
    return fig    # GROUND_TRUTH = GATE_OMISSION, expected verdict REJECT

The figure plots a clean, attractive 1.94%-magnitude local curve (a lengthening, but a dishonest figure could axis-flip or mislabel it as a "shortening") with no gate badges, so a reader cannot see that every point is amber/AUDIT. Why rejected: t2 every_local_marker_has_gate_badge fails. Verdict: REJECT, FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM, first failure = gate status omitted. This control enforces the source doc's "gate status overlay present" acceptance test.

6.3 gen_no_watermark() → must be REJECTED (watermark omission)

A pixel-identical figure with the TOY MODEL · SIMULATION ONLY watermark stripped — the kind that could be screenshotted and circulated as a "result." t1 has_watermark fails. Verdict: REJECT, FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM, first failure = watermark absent. Enforces "watermark present."

6.4 gen_baseline_replaced() → must be REJECTED (overlay replaces baseline)

function gen_baseline_replaced(states):
    fig = new_figure()
    plot_lobe_trajectory_ONLY(states)     # deletes Panel A; renders the lobe path AS the mission
    return fig    # GROUND_TRUTH = REPLACEMENT, expected verdict REJECT

The classical baseline panel is deleted and the lobe overlay is presented as the mission — the visual form of "operational drive replaces rockets." t5 baseline_panel_present fails. Verdict: REJECT, FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM, first failure = baseline replaced, not overlaid. Enforces handoff doc 07's "optional overlay, not replacement."

6.5 The mirror control gen_silent_drop() → must be REJECTED for under-claim

The two-sided obligation: a figure that, faced with an amber AUDIT lobe, silently drops the overlay entirely and shows only the bare baseline, so a genuine, gated, status-labeled local candidate effect is invisible and the option-value artifact is useless.

function gen_silent_drop(S_L_series, Gamma_series):
    fig = render_baseline_only()          # drops all AUDIT/amber markers
    return fig    # GROUND_TRUTH = UNDERCLAIM, expected verdict REJECT

Why rejected: the contract requires that a non-zero, gated S_L^valid be rendered with its amber badge, not hidden — check_completeness fails because a known non-zero S_L^valid(0.5) = −0.0058 (amber) is absent from the figure. Verdict: REJECT for under-claim (the mirror first failure). The correct figure shows the amber, down-weighted, status-labeled marker — neither inflating it to a mission gain nor hiding it. This is what keeps the visualization honest in both directions: it may not overclaim, and it may not erase.

6.6 The positive control gen_honest_overlay() → must be ACCEPTED

function gen_honest_overlay(states, T_baseline, S_L_series, Gamma_series):
    fig = render_mars_dashboard(states, T_baseline, S_L_series, Gamma_series)
    assert check_mission_figure(fig)      # t1..t5 all PASS
    return fig    # GROUND_TRUTH = HONEST, expected verdict ACCEPT

The figure from §5.2: Panel A baseline T_baseline = 4.454 retained and unchanged; Panel B local amber markers at S_L^valid = −0.29%…−0.58% (down-weighted local lengthening) with gate badges; watermark present; first-failure caption present; no global-time axis. t1–t5 all pass. Verdict: ACCEPT — and note that accept here means "this figure is an honest, status-labeled, local option-value artifact," not "the drive works" and not "Mars is closer." The accepted figure's own caption says so.
