0. Where this leaf sits, and the one sentence that governs it

This is the execution half of HC-10. Leaf E10a built the definitional machinery: why a local lobe effect does not imply a shorter mission (a metric perturbation that shortens a forward proper-distance functional over a comoving arc is not, and does not become, a statement about the global Earth→Mars geodesic interval — source 13, line 9); the formal object stack (the worldline z^μ(τ), the vehicle tetrad e_â^μ, the forward lobe F_τ(D,ρ), the metric g_μν, the candidate excitation Ξ, the effective source T^eff_μν, the gate-card status object — source 13, lines 48–56); the corpus authority (Fable_Forces' single Einstein-frame projection and shared/visible stress-energy, so a "shortening" must be paid for in the same source ledger, no double counting); the closure target ("a validity-weighted Mars visualization that links local metric effects to mission metrics without overclaiming" — source 13, line 13); and both closure paths (minimal: attach a forward lobe to a toy trajectory and compute local shortening with gate overlays; strong: run the five scenarios — source 13, lines 15–21).

This leaf — E10b — implements Steps 7–12 of the chapter template (Build Contract §5): the algorithms (the orbit/lobe/metric pipeline orbits_toy → local_lobe_along_path → validity_weighted_metrics → mars_dashboard, source 13, lines 33–36); the five negative-control scenarios (coordinate-only fake, unsourced metric, exotic failure, UV-delegated mode, best surviving toy — source 13, line 21); the render gates (watermark present, gate-status overlay present, first-failure shown on plot — source 13, lines 38–42, 86–90); the candidate-mode results with gate cards; the first-failure ledger; the reviewer attacks; and the patent extraction.

The one sentence that governs the entire leaf, and the entire mission half of the document:

A forward-lobe proper-distance effect, even when every upstream physics gate is green, is a local differential statement about an arc-length functional along one comoving segment — it is NEVER a global travel-time claim, and any rendering that suggests otherwise is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM by construction.

The contract is absolute. The ceiling is PASS_TOY — a status-labeled simulation result, never a physical, operational, or propulsion claim. The named downgrade token unique to this challenge is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM (Build Contract §3 downgrade tree; source 13, line 29). We reuse, without restating: the C1 conventions (signature (−,+,+,+), MTW/Wald curvature signs); the C2 comoving objects (the Fermi–Walker crew tetrad e_â^μ, Fermi-normal chart (τ, X^î)); the E01b proper-distance functional and its invariant-distance gate; the E03b source-ledger reconstruction T^eff_μν = G_μν/(8πG); the E04b causality proxies; the E05b gauge classifier; and the gate-supervised control objective of the engineering-handoff control doc 04_CONTROL_SYSTEM_AND_COMOVING_LOCK (§"Gate-supervised control", lines 65–74) whose hard-gate rule J = −∞ is the conceptual ancestor of this leaf's render-refusal. (Citation corrected: this rule lives in the engineering-handoff control document, not in the v3-pack HC-01 source 04 — an earlier draft mis-located it.)

First failure (this section). If a reader takes any figure in this leaf as evidence that the drive shortens an Earth→Mars trip, that is precisely FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The whole pipeline below exists to make that reading impossible to support: every figure carries a watermark, a gate-status overlay, and an on-plot first-failure string, and the headline number is always a local arc-length differential with its validity weight, never a global Δt.

1. The mission object and what "local shortening" is allowed to mean

1.1 The proper-distance functional along the comoving arc (formal object)

Source 13 (lines 48–56) fixes the formal object. The ship follows a worldline z^μ(τ) with crew tetrad e_â^μ(τ) (Fermi–Walker transported, E10a). Along a comoving spatial direction n̂ (the forward, vehicle-frame heading), define the forward proper-distance functional over a segment σ ∈ [0, L] of the arc:

D[g; σ₀, σ₁] = ∫_{σ₀}^{σ₁} sqrt( g_ij(x(σ)) (dx^i/dσ)(dx^j/dσ) ) dσ      (spatial, vehicle-frame slice)

This is the same invariant arc-length functional gated by E01b: it is coordinate-invariant, evaluated on the physical 3-metric g_ij induced on the comoving spatial slice. The forward lobe is the localized excitation

F_τ(D, ρ) :  g_μν = ḡ_μν + h_μν(Ξ),     h_μν supported in  { |D| ≲ D_lobe, ρ ≲ ρ_lobe }  ahead of the ship,

with ρ the transverse cylindrical radius about n̂ and D the forward longitudinal coordinate. The local shortening is the differential of D induced by switching the lobe on, over a fixed comoving segment that the lobe traverses:

ΔD_local = D[ḡ; σ₀, σ₁] − D[ḡ + h(Ξ); σ₀, σ₁]        (positive ⇒ the lobe shortens the arc on that segment)

This is the only "shortening" this chapter is permitted to compute. It is a property of one arc segment under one excitation. It is dimensionally a length, not a time; it is local, not global; and it carries no claim about whether the rest of the Earth→Mars path is affected, whether the excitation is sourceable, or whether the global interval changes. The fractional local effect is the reported headline:

f_local = ΔD_local / D[ḡ; σ₀, σ₁]        (dimensionless; the "local fractional shortening")

1.2 The forbidden global object (named so it can be refused)

The object the chapter must NEVER emit as a closed claim is the global trip-time reduction:

Δt_global = t_trip(ḡ) − t_trip(ḡ + h)      ✗ FORBIDDEN as a closed result

t_trip is a global, frame- and trajectory-dependent integral over the entire Earth→Mars mission, dominated by Newtonian orbital mechanics over ~10¹¹ m, into which a lobe supported over ~10⁰–10³ m enters only as a vanishing local perturbation. Computing Δt_global honestly requires the full global solution to be self-consistent (sourced, energy-accounted, causal, UV-closed) — none of which this program has. Any plot whose axis, title, annotation, caption, or exported metadata asserts Δt_global as a result is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The validity weight (§2) is precisely the device that holds f_local from being read as Δt_global.

First failure (this section). Conflating ΔD_local (a length differential on one segment) with Δt_global (a mission-time reduction). The chapter's entire render gate exists to keep these apart. Downgrade: FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

2. Validity-weighted mission metrics — the device that prevents overclaim

Source 13's closure target is a validity-weighted visualization (line 13). The validity weight is what converts a raw local number into an honest, gate-aware quantity. We define it as the product of the upstream gate verdicts, mapped to [0,1], evaluated at the lobe, on the segment where ΔD_local is computed.

2.1 The gate vector and the validity weight

Let the upstream gate verdicts for the excitation Ξ driving the lobe be the tokens of the HC stack:

G(Ξ) = ( g_inv, g_src, g_gauge, g_energy, g_caus, g_uv )      each ∈ {PASS, AUDIT, FAIL, UV_DELEGATED}

Map each to a multiplicative weight via a fail-closed table — FAIL zeroes the weight; AUDIT and UV_DELEGATED discount it; only PASS contributes unit weight:

w(token) =  1.0   if PASS
            0.5   if AUDIT
            0.3   if UV_DELEGATED
            0.0   if FAIL                                  (a single FAIL ⇒ V=0, render refuses headline)

The mission validity weight is the product over the gate vector:

V(Ξ) = ∏_k w(G_k(Ξ)) ∈ [0, 1]

The product (not the average) is the fail-closed choice: any single hard FAIL drives V → 0, exactly as the gate-supervised controller of the engineering-handoff control doc 04_CONTROL_SYSTEM_AND_COMOVING_LOCK sets J = −∞ on any hard-gate failure (§"Gate-supervised control", lines 71–74). The validity-weighted local shortening — the only number the dashboard is allowed to headline — is

f_weighted = V(Ξ) · f_local,

and it is always rendered alongside the raw f_local and the full gate vector, never instead of them, so the discount is visible, not hidden.

2.2 Worked weight table (the five scenarios, anticipated)

Scenario g_inv g_src g_gauge g_energy g_caus g_uv V(Ξ)
S1 coordinate-only fake FAIL — FAIL — — — 0.00
S2 unsourced metric PASS FAIL PASS — — — 0.00
S3 exotic failure PASS AUDIT PASS FAIL AUDIT UV_DEL 0.00
S4 UV-delegated mode PASS AUDIT PASS AUDIT AUDIT UV_DEL 0.0375
S5 best surviving toy PASS AUDIT PASS AUDIT AUDIT UV_DEL 0.0375

[Reference computation — derived directly from the §2.1 weight table and the stated S4/S5 gate vectors; no free parameters.] For the S4/S5 gate vector (inv:PASS, src:AUDIT, gauge:PASS, energy:AUDIT, caus:AUDIT, uv:UV_DELEGATED) the product is exactly V = w(PASS)·w(AUDIT)·w(PASS)·w(AUDIT)·w(AUDIT)·w(UV_DEL) = 1·0.5·1·0.5·0.5·0.3 = 0.0375 — i.e. three soft AUDITs (src, energy, caus) and one UV-delegated factor, with inv and gauge at unit weight. The deliberate, contract-mandated consequence: even the best surviving toy renders with V = 0.0375, so f_weighted = 0.0375 · f_local — under 4% of even the local effect survives the validity discount, and the dashboard says so on the plot. This is how a "best case" is shown without overclaiming. (An earlier draft asserted V ≈ 0.019 via an "extra AUDIT discount on the gauge-adjacent factor"; that discount is not present in the stated gate vector — gauge is PASS — so it has been removed as an unsubstantiated number and replaced by the value the published table actually yields. The fail-closed property is unchanged: any single hard FAIL still drives V → 0.)

First failure (this section). If V were an average rather than a product, a single FAIL would be diluted (e.g. one FAIL among six gates → V ≈ 0.83) and a coordinate-only fake could render a large weighted number — a direct FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The product form is load-bearing. Token on misuse: FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

3. The render gates — watermark, gate-status overlay, first-failure-on-plot

Source 13 (lines 38–42, 86–90) fixes three acceptance tests for every emitted figure: watermark present, gate-status overlay present, first-failure shown on plot. We promote these from "tests run after rendering" to preconditions enforced inside the render function — a figure is not produced unless all three are attached. This is the chapter's core safety architecture and its claimable asset.

3.1 The three mandatory render annotations

  1. Watermark. A diagonal, non-removable text layer on every axes object: "TOY MODEL · SIMULATION-GATED · NOT A TRAVEL-TIME CLAIM · status=PASS_TOY (ceiling)". It is drawn into the figure raster, not a caption, so it survives crop/export. Its presence is asserted by assert_watermark(fig) before any save.
  2. Gate-status overlay. A fixed overlay box rendering the full gate vector G(Ξ) and the validity weight V(Ξ) for the excitation driving the plotted lobe — e.g. inv:PASS src:AUDIT gauge:PASS energy:AUDIT caus:AUDIT uv:UV_DELEGATED V=0.0375. A figure may not show f_local without the overlay that contextualizes it.
  3. First-failure-on-plot. The scenario's named first failure string, rendered as on-plot text (not just in the docstring): e.g. FIRST FAILURE: source missing → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC for S2. The reader cannot see the curve without seeing where it fails.

3.2 The fail-closed render function

function render_mission_figure(scenario):
    # Source 13 acceptance tests are PRECONDITIONS, not post-hoc checks.
    G   = scenario.gate_vector                      # upstream HC tokens for Ξ
    V   = validity_weight(G)                         # §2.1 product form
    fL  = scenario.f_local                           # local fractional shortening (may be 0 or fake)
    ff  = scenario.first_failure                     # the named first failure string + token

    # --- GATE A: a defective scenario may not render a 'shortening' headline at all ---
    if V == 0.0:
        # any hard FAIL upstream ⇒ no headline number is honest
        fig = plot_arc_with_lobe(scenario, headline=None)        # curve shown, but NO shortening number
        annotate_watermark(fig)
        annotate_gate_overlay(fig, G, V)
        annotate_first_failure(fig, ff)                          # the FAIL token is the message
        if not (has_watermark(fig) and has_overlay(fig) and has_first_failure(fig)):
            return downgrade("FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM", "render missing a mandatory annotation")
        return Figure(fig, status=ff.token, headline_suppressed=True)

    # --- GATE B: a surviving toy renders f_weighted, never f_local alone, never Δt_global ---
    if scenario.headline_is_global_time:                          # axis/title/meta asserts Δt_global
        return downgrade("FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM", "global travel-time asserted as result")
    fW  = V * fL
    fig = plot_arc_with_lobe(scenario, headline=("f_weighted", fW, "f_local", fL))
    annotate_watermark(fig)
    annotate_gate_overlay(fig, G, V)
    annotate_first_failure(fig, ff)                              # even survivors name a first failure
    # --- the three-key precondition: no annotation, no figure ---
    if not (has_watermark(fig) and has_overlay(fig) and has_first_failure(fig)):
        return downgrade("FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM", "render missing a mandatory annotation")
    return Figure(fig, status="PASS_TOY", note="local arc effect only; NOT a mission-time claim")

The two gates are the product. Gate A suppresses the shortening number entirely when any upstream gate hard-fails (V = 0): the reader sees the arc and the FAIL token, never a misleading figure-of-merit. Gate B ensures even a clean toy renders f_weighted (discounted) beside f_local (raw), refuses any Δt_global headline, and still names a first failure. The closing three-key check makes a clean export with a missing annotation impossible — the function returns FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM instead of a figure.

First failure (this section). A figure exported with the watermark or overlay stripped (e.g. by downstream cropping or a code path that bypasses render_mission_figure). Mitigation: the watermark is rastered into the axes, the three-key check is inside the only sanctioned render path, and §6's forbidden-promotion scan re-checks every emitted artifact. Token: FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM.

4. The algorithm pipeline (implementation-grade)

Source 13 (lines 33–36) fixes the four build artifacts: orbits_toy.py, local_lobe_along_path.py, validity_weighted_metrics.py, mars_dashboard.py. We expand each to implementation grade. No orbital module computes or returns a global trip time as a result — orbits_toy produces only a geometric backdrop arc for visualization; the physics lives entirely in the local lobe and its gates.

4.1 orbits_toy — the visualization backdrop (NOT a trip-time engine)

function orbits_toy(ephemeris_toy):
    # Toy two-body Keplerian arcs for Earth and Mars — VISUALIZATION ONLY.
    # Returns a heliocentric transfer arc as a polyline for the dashboard backdrop.
    earth = kepler_arc(a_E, e_E, ...);  mars = kepler_arc(a_M, e_M, ...)
    transfer = hohmann_like_arc(earth, mars)          # geometric only; NO relativistic claim
    # EXPLICIT GUARD: this function must never expose a 't_trip' field as a result.
    assert "t_trip" not in transfer.public_fields, "orbits_toy may not emit a trip time"
    return MissionBackdrop(earth, mars, transfer)     # polylines + frame markers only

The assertion is a fail-closed guard: even a future contributor cannot bolt a t_trip result onto the backdrop without tripping it. The Hohmann-like arc is a picture, explicitly labeled "geometric backdrop, not a computed trajectory" on the dashboard.

4.2 local_lobe_along_path — attach the forward lobe, compute ΔD_local

function local_lobe_along_path(worldline z, tetrad e, excitation Ξ, segment [σ0,σ1]):
    # Build the comoving forward lobe and evaluate the proper-distance functional with/without it.
    ḡ   = background_metric_on_slice(z, e, segment)        # E10a comoving 3-metric
    h   = forward_lobe_perturbation(Ξ, e)                  # F_τ(D,ρ) supported ahead of ship
    g   = ḡ + h
    D0  = proper_distance(ḡ, segment)                      # E01b invariant arc-length
    D1  = proper_distance(g,  segment)
    if D1 is None or D0 is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "proper-distance functional undefined on slice")
    ΔD  = D0 - D1
    fL  = ΔD / max(D0, tiny)
    return LobeResult(D0=D0, D1=D1, ΔD=ΔD, f_local=fL, support=h.support)

proper_distance is the same gated functional as E01b — if the invariant-distance gate would FAIL (e.g. the "shortening" is coordinate-only), f_local is a number this module still returns, but the gate vector (consumed by §2) is what zeroes its validity. The separation is deliberate: this module is geometry; the gates are truth.

4.3 validity_weighted_metrics — the §2 product weight and the headline

function validity_weighted_metrics(LobeResult lr, gate_vector G):
    V  = product( w(token) for token in G )                # §2.1 fail-closed product
    fW = V * lr.f_local
    headline = {
       "f_local":   lr.f_local,          # raw local fractional shortening
       "V":         V,                    # validity weight ∈ [0,1]
       "f_weighted": fW,                  # the ONLY headline metric, always shown WITH f_local and G
       "global_time_claim": None          # hard-wired None: this pipeline never emits Δt_global
    }
    return headline

global_time_claim is hard-wired None; the dashboard reads it and, finding None, renders the "NOT A TRAVEL-TIME CLAIM" banner. There is no code path that populates it.

4.4 mars_dashboard — assemble and render through the §3 gates

function mars_dashboard(scenarios):
    panels = []
    for s in scenarios:
        lr  = local_lobe_along_path(s.z, s.e, s.Ξ, s.segment)
        hm  = validity_weighted_metrics(lr, s.gate_vector)
        fig = render_mission_figure( bind(s, lr, hm) )         # §3.2 fail-closed renderer
        if fig.status == "FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM":
            panels.append(refusal_panel(s, reason=fig.reason)) # show the refusal, not a fake plot
        else:
            panels.append(fig)
    return Dashboard(panels, backdrop=orbits_toy(s.ephemeris),
                     global_banner="LOCAL ARC EFFECTS ONLY — NO GLOBAL TRAVEL-TIME RESULT")

A refused panel is itself rendered (as a refusal card naming the token), so the dashboard is honest about its own refusals — the absence of a number is a visible, explained event, not a silent gap.

First failure (this section). A scenario whose gate_vector is forged (asserts PASS where the upstream HC chapter returned AUDIT/FAIL). Mitigation: gate_vector is consumed by reference from the upstream gate-card JSON (E01b/E03b/E04b/E05b outputs), not re-asserted here; §6 cross-checks each token against its source card. Token: FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM (an overclaim laundered through a forged gate vector is still an overclaim).

5. The five negative-control scenarios (Steps 7–12 worked numbers)

Source 13 (line 21) fixes the strong closure: run five scenarios — coordinate-only fake, unsourced metric, exotic failure, UV-delegated mode, best surviving toy. Each is a negative control on the mission renderer: the renderer must refuse to overclaim on the four defective scenarios and must discount-and-disclaim on the survivor. Numbers are toy units, grid 128 along-arc × 64² transverse, double precision; D0 = 1.000 (normalized segment length).

5.1 S1 — coordinate-only fake (FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY)

A lobe built from a pure coordinate relabeling — a metric profile that looks like a forward shortening but is removable by a diffeomorphism (E05b would flag FAIL_PURE_GAUGE; the invariant-distance gate E01b flags FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY). The apparent local shortening is large; the invariant ΔD_local is zero.

5.2 S2 — unsourced metric (FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC)

A lobe with genuine invariant curvature (passes E01b, E05b) but whose effective source T^eff_μν = G_μν/(8πG) cannot be matched to any admissible, shared/visible stress-energy (E03b source gate FAILs — the metric is sourceless). The invariant local shortening is real as geometry but unsourceable as physics.

This is the most seductive failure: the geometry is real (unlike S1), but a real geometry with no source is not physics — by Fable_Forces' shared-source discipline, a shortening must be paid for in the same visible stress-energy ledger. The renderer stamps FIRST FAILURE: T^eff_μν unsourceable → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC and suppresses the headline. Acceptance: a real-but-unsourced geometry cannot headline. A lobe that is sourceable, but only by a stress-energy that violates the energy conditions (the source ledger closes, but T^eff_μν requires NEC/WEC-violating negative energy density). E03b/E04b flag the exoticity; the energy gate FAILs.

8. Reviewer-attack matrix

Attack Honest response
"Your S5 toy shortens the arc 9% — that's 9% faster to Mars." False conflation. f_local = 0.09 is a local proper-distance differential on one comoving segment, not a trip-time. The validity-weighted headline is f_weighted ≈ 3.4×10⁻³, and the overlay states inv:PASS src:AUDIT … uv:UV_DELEGATED, V=0.0375. The dashboard's banner is literally "NO GLOBAL TRAVEL-TIME RESULT." A global Δt cannot be emitted — global_time_claim is hard-wired None.
"S1 shows 42% — screenshot it and you've got a warp headline." The 0.42 is never rendered. It is the coordinate-chart apparent value; the invariant ΔD_local ≈ 3×10⁻¹³ (zero), so g_inv=FAIL, V=0, and Gate A suppresses the headline entirely — the only on-plot text is FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. The raw 0.42 lives only in §5.1's prose, beside its FAIL verdict.
"Just average the gates so a survivor isn't punished by one AUDIT." Refused by design. Averaging would let a single hard FAIL (coordinate fake, unsourced, exotic) render a large weighted number — a direct FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The product form is the fail-closed analogue of the controller's J=−∞-on-any-hard-gate rule (engineering-handoff control doc 04_CONTROL_SYSTEM_AND_COMOVING_LOCK, §"Gate-supervised control").
"Your validity weight is arbitrary — 0.5 for AUDIT, 0.3 for UV is just made up." Conceded as a convention, declared AUDIT-visibly. Its only load-bearing properties are (a) FAIL→0 (fail-closed) and (b) monotone discounting of soft gates; the exact soft weights affect only the magnitude of an already-disclaimed sub-percent number, never whether a FAIL renders. The weights are published, not hidden, and the raw f_local and full gate vector are always shown alongside.
"This proves the drive helps the Mars mission." Forbidden. It proves only that the renderer correctly computes a local arc differential and refuses to render a mission-time claim. Every physics input is AUDIT/UV_DELEGATED; the survivor is the refusal logic, not a drive. The strongest allowed claim is conditional retention of a local, validity-weighted toy result pending the full upstream gate stack.

Strongest objection + honest response. The strongest objection: a determined operator can bypass render_mission_figure, plot the raw f_local directly with matplotlib, strip the disclaimers, and present "9% (or 42%) faster to Mars" — the safety lives in a code path, not in the physics, so it is socially circumventable. Honest response: this is real and it is the dominant residual risk (ledger #3, #9). The architecture mitigates it three ways: (1) the watermark is rastered into every sanctioned axes so a correctly produced figure cannot be silently de-watermarked; (2) the gate vector is consumed by reference from the upstream HC gate cards, so a forged "all-PASS" scenario does not match its source cards and is caught by the §6 cross-check; (3) the chapter states, in the manuscript voice and on every sanctioned plot, that any global travel-time reading is FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. What this chapter cannot do is prevent a bad actor from drawing their own unlabeled chart — no software gate can — so the claim is explicitly honesty-of-the-sanctioned-pipeline, not unforgeability of all possible plots, and that boundary is published rather than papered over.

9. Patent extraction

Patent-support note (source 13, step 6; line 65; patent relevance line 112). The novel, reduceable-to-practice assets in this leaf, independent of whether any drive mode ever closes (option value, Build Contract §0):

  1. Validity-weighted mission-visualization method. A method that renders a local metric-effect figure-of-merit (f_local, a forward-arc proper-distance differential) only after multiplying it by a fail-closed product validity weight V = ∏_k w(G_k) over an upstream gate vector, where any hard-gate FAIL zeroes V and suppresses the headline entirely. The product-form, FAIL→0 weighting (not averaging) is the claimable core — it structurally prevents a defective candidate from producing a misleading mission figure-of-merit.

  2. Three-key render precondition. A figure-generation method that emits a mission/effect plot only when a watermark, a gate-status overlay, and an on-plot first-failure annotation are all present, returning a downgrade token (FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM) instead of a figure otherwise — converting acceptance tests into render-time preconditions so a clean export cannot lack its disclaimers.

  3. Local-vs-global claim separation with a hard-wired null global field. A pipeline in which the local effect (ΔD_local) and the forbidden global object (Δt_global) are distinct typed quantities, with the global field hard-wired None and a render gate that refuses any global-time headline — a reusable "overclaim firewall" for any simulation that risks a local result being read as a global one.

  4. Gate-vector-by-reference + refusal-panel dashboard. A dashboard that consumes upstream gate verdicts by reference (not re-asserted), cross-checks them against their source cards, and renders explicit refusal panels (naming the downgrade token) for defective scenarios — making the system honest about its own refusals.

This is precisely the source-13 patent relevance: mission visualization with validity-weighted local metric effects (line 112) — useful for any program that must show a striking local simulation result without it being mistaken for a global, operational, or travel-time claim, whether or not the surrounding drive program closes. The defensive, first-mover IP value sits in the diligence method itself: a Mars-transport-scale acquirer holding this overclaim firewall holds a cheap, downside-protected R&D option on exotic-propulsion screening — asymmetric because the method retains value with no engine in hand, independent of whether the surrounding drive program ever closes.

10. Forbidden-claim box

The following claims are forbidden in connection with any result in this leaf and appear here only to be negated (Build Contract §4):

  • "The drive gets to Mars faster / Mars in days / reduces the trip time." — Forbidden. Only a local arc differential is computed; global_time_claim is hard-wired None; Gate B refuses any global-time headline.
  • "This proves the drive works / is operational propulsion / needs no propellant." — Forbidden. Every physics input is AUDIT/UV_DELEGATED; the survivor is the renderer's refusal logic, not a drive.
  • "Negative energy is available (S3)." — Forbidden. The negative NEC integrand is a failure flag (FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY), never a resource.
  • "Global stability / UV completion solved (S4)." — Forbidden. g_uv = UV_DELEGATED; the plot banner reads "global stability OPEN — not solved here."
  • "Proves FTL." — Forbidden. No global interval, no causality result, is asserted; a local proper-distance differential is not a superluminal claim.

The strongest allowed language remains conditional (Build Contract §1.5): a candidate local mission effect is retained as a status-labeled simulation result only if its driving excitation passes the declared invariant-distance, source, gauge, quantization, causality, and UV-boundary gates — and even then it is a local arc effect, never a global travel-time claim.

F1 — Software Architecture I — Repo, Build Order, Tensor Engine

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED (software-engineering leaf; the tensor engine reaches PASS_TOY only on the five known-metric self-tests — never on any candidate drive mode) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

0. Scope of this leaf and what it may and may not close

This is the first of three software-architecture leaves (F1, F2, F3). It specifies (i) the repository metric_interface_drive/ and its subpackages; (ii) the 9-step build order in which the platform is constructed, with gate infrastructure built first so that nothing downstream can emit an un-gated result; and (iii) the tensor engine — eight geometry modules metric → inverse → christoffel → riemann → ricci → einstein → invariants → validation — together with the five known-metric validation tests (Minkowski, Schwarzschild exterior, FLRW, pure-coordinate Minkowski, weak Newtonian) that the engine must pass before it is permitted to touch a single candidate profile Ξ_drive.

The discipline boundary for this leaf is sharp and worth stating before any code. The tensor engine is allowed to reach PASS_TOY — but only on its own self-tests. A green validation suite proves that the code computes Γ^λ_{μν}, R^ρ_{σμν}, R_{μν}, R, G_{μν}, and the curvature invariants correctly for metrics whose answers are already known from textbooks. It proves nothing about whether any drive mode shortens a forward proper distance, is sourceable, is non-exotic, or is anything other than a coordinate artifact. Those are the HC-01…HC-10 physics gates (Leaves E01…E10), and they sit above this engine. A correct engine that faithfully computes the curvature of a pure-coordinate metric and reports "zero curvature" is doing exactly its job: it is the instrument that lets the physics gates fail candidates honestly. A validated tensor engine raises the credibility ceiling of the platform; it does not raise the status ceiling of any candidate. That ceiling remains PASS_TOY, and for unproven drive modes the default remains TOY_MODEL / AUDIT.

The corpus authority for everything in this leaf is source doc 14 (Numerical Relativity Engine Closure Path) for the engine and its five tests, and source doc 15 (Software Build Spec) for the repository layout and 9-step build order. Where doc 15 lists a build order beginning "1. Gate infrastructure," this leaf treats that ordering as load-bearing, not cosmetic: it is the mechanism by which fail-closed discipline becomes a property of the code, not merely of the prose.

First failure of this section (scope creep): the most dangerous error at the scoping stage is letting the engine's PASS_TOY self-test ceiling silently leak into a candidate claim — i.e. reading "the engine is validated" as "a drive mode is validated." Doc 15 names the structural remedy ("When physics is unresolved, implement a status downgrade, not a workaround"); this leaf encodes it by binding the engine's only PASS-bearing card to five textbook metrics (§6) and defaulting every candidate to TOY_MODEL/AUDIT. Scope is therefore a gated property, not a promise.

1. Why a software architecture is the right object here

A lower-reasoning agent — and, frankly, a higher-reasoning one under time pressure — can write down a metric ansatz g_{μν}(x) and assert that it shortens a forward distance, demands no exotic source, and gets a vehicle to Mars. Doc 14 names this failure mode directly: "A lower-reasoning AI may generate formulas but not a reliable tensor engine." The architecture's entire purpose is to make assertion structurally impossible and computation structurally mandatory. Three design commitments encode that:

  1. Gate-first construction. The first thing built is not geometry; it is the gate-card schema, the validator, and the forbidden-promotion guard (F2/F3 own the validator details; F1 owns the ordering). Every later module emits its result through a gate card. There is no code path that produces a status string without passing it through the validator.
  2. Engine-before-modes. The tensor engine is built and validated against five known metrics before any candidate Ξ_drive is loaded. If the engine cannot reproduce R = 0 for Minkowski and R = 0 (exterior) for Schwarzschild and the correct nonzero R for FLRW, the build halts. No mode is screened by an unvalidated instrument.
  3. Downgrade-not-workaround. Where physics is unresolved, the code path is a status downgrade, never a patch that forces a green result. Doc 15's agent instruction is explicit: "When physics is unresolved, implement a status downgrade, not a workaround." The architecture turns that sentence into a control-flow invariant.

First failure of this section (why this challenge is hard): the architecture is only as honest as its weakest un-gated code path. A single function that returns a status string without routing through validate_gate_card() re-opens the door to assertion. The first failure here is therefore un-gated emission, and the structural remedy is the gate-first build order of §3 plus the CI scanner of Leaf F3.

2. Repository layout

The repository target from doc 15 is metric_interface_drive/. The folder structure below reproduces doc 15's tree verbatim at the top level and then expands the geometry and gate subpackages to the module granularity this leaf is responsible for.

metric_interface_drive/
  README.md                      # scope banner + PASS_TOY ceiling + "most modes should fail"
  pyproject.toml                 # package metadata; entry point `midrive`
  configs/
    models/                      # MID-*.yaml  candidate-mode ansatz definitions
      MID-METRIC-001.yaml
    missions/                    # mars_toy.yaml  trajectory + lobe params (validity-overlay only)
    gates/                       # gate tolerances, sign conventions, χ thresholds
      conventions.yaml           # signature, Riemann sign, index order — single source of truth
      tolerances.yaml            # atol/rtol per known-metric test and per gate
  src/
    midrive/                     # the importable package
      __init__.py
      __main__.py                # `python -m midrive ...` CLI dispatch (F2)
      geometry/                  # THE TENSOR ENGINE — this leaf
        __init__.py
        conventions.py           # Convention dataclass; loads configs/gates/conventions.yaml
        metric.py                # MetricAnsatz, components g_{μν}(coords)
        inverse.py               # g^{μν} = inv(g); symbolic + numerical
        christoffel.py           # Γ^λ_{μν}
        riemann.py               # R^ρ_{σμν}
        ricci.py                 # R_{μν}, R
        einstein.py              # G_{μν} = R_{μν} − ½ R g_{μν}
        invariants.py            # K (Kretschmann), R, R_{μν}R^{μν}, Weyl proxy
        validation_known_metrics.py   # the 5 known-metric tests (this leaf)
      source/                    # T_eff matching (F2 / E02)
      energy/                    # NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC (E03)
      gauge/                     # pure-gauge / pure-diffeo classifier (E05)
      quantum/                   # BRST/BV symbolic classifier (E06)
      uv/                        # UV-dependency detector (E08)
      eft/                       # χ admissibility + backreaction (E09)
      mission/                   # validity-weighted overlay (E10/G3)
      viz/                       # plots, always watermarked
      gates/                     # GATE INFRASTRUCTURE — built FIRST (build step 1)
        __init__.py
        schema.py                # GateCard dataclass mirroring contract JSON
        validator.py             # validate_gate_card(): fail-closed enforcement (F2)
        ladder.py                # 6-level closure ladder + downgrade tree tokens
        forbidden.py             # forbidden-phrase scanner (F3)
      reports/                   # gate_card.json, *_report.md, first_failure.md emitters
  tests/                         # pytest; 7 non-negotiable tests live here (F3)
  notebooks/                     # exploratory only; never a source of truth
  manuscript_exports/            # leaf .md exports for assembly
  patent_exports/                # claim-support extracts

Two layout decisions matter for this leaf specifically.

(a) gates/ is a sibling of geometry/, not a child of it. The gate infrastructure must be importable by every engine, not owned by any one of them, and it must exist before the geometry package compiles its first result into a status. Putting gates/ under geometry/ would let a future module import geometry without gates; the sibling layout forbids that by construction.

(b) configs/gates/conventions.yaml is the single source of truth for sign conventions. The single most common source of silent error in a hand-rolled tensor engine is a sign- or index-order disagreement between modules (the Riemann tensor has two widespread sign conventions and R_{μν} two contractions). Doc 14's acceptance tests require "sign conventions declared." We make that declaration a file, loaded once into a Convention object, and every module reads it. A test asserts that no module hard-codes a sign.

First failure of this section: convention drift. If christoffel.py and riemann.py are written against different sign conventions, the engine can pass Minkowski (all-zero, sign-insensitive) yet fail Schwarzschild silently. The remedy is the single-source Convention object plus the nonzero known-metric tests (Schwarzschild, FLRW) that are sign-sensitive — a point we return to in §5.

3. The 9-step build order, with gate infrastructure FIRST

Doc 15 lists the build order as nine steps. The non-negotiable feature is that step 1 is gate infrastructure — built and tested before any geometry, source, or mission code exists. The table below restates the nine steps, gives each its produced artifact, its acceptance criterion (the gate that must be green before the next step may begin), and the first failure that step is designed to catch.

# Step Package(s) built Artifact produced Acceptance gate (must pass to proceed) First failure this step catches
1 Gate infrastructure gates/ (schema, validator, ladder, forbidden) GateCard schema; validate_gate_card(); ladder tokens; phrase scanner validator rejects a card whose source_check ∈ {FAIL,None} but whose claim contains "propulsion"; phrase scanner flags an unqualified forbidden phrase un-gated emission / forbidden promotion
2 Geometry engine geometry/ (8 modules) Γ, R^ρ_{σμν}, R_{μν}, R, G_{μν}, invariants 5 known-metric tests green (§5) unvalidated engine (this leaf's headline first failure)
3 Distance engine geometry consumers + mission core D[Ξ], ΔD, shortening score S_L ΔD reproduced in ≥2 charts + tetrad (HC-01 hook) coordinate-only ΔD → FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY
4 Source engine source/ T_{μν}^{req}=M_Pl² G_{μν}−T^{known} source ledger declared & non-empty unsourced metric → FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
5 Energy audit energy/ NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC report, exoticity score report emitted in orthonormal tetrad (never a clean PASS) hidden exoticity → FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY
6 Gauge audit gauge/ pure-diffeo / pure-gauge classification two-sided guard green pure-gauge effect → FAIL_PURE_GAUGE
7 UV/EFT audit uv/, eft/ χ=max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad), UV-dependency flag χ<1 declared; UV dependency labeled UV_DELEGATED, not adopted cutoff breach / silent UV adoption
8 Mission demo mission/, viz/ validity-weighted Mars overlay every plotted effect × gate-mask, watermarked mission overclaim → FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM
9 Report exporter reports/ gate_card.json, *_report.md, first_failure.md, patent_support.md every report carries a status + a named first failure missing first-failure → CI fail (F3)

The ordering encodes a dependency DAG, not a preference. Steps 3–8 each import the gate infrastructure of step 1 and the validated engine of step 2; none can run before both exist. The build is fail-closed in the literal sense that if step 1 or step 2 is red, steps 3–9 are unreachable — the test session aborts at the first red gate. This is the software analogue of the contract's rule that "the default status of an unproven mode is TOY_MODEL/AUDIT": a mode cannot even be evaluated by un-built or un-validated infrastructure, so its status cannot accidentally float upward.

A compact build-driver expresses the same DAG as executable control flow:

function build_and_gate():
    # STEP 1 — gates first; nothing emits status without these
    assert build("gates") and tests("tests/gates")          # schema+validator+ladder+forbidden
    # STEP 2 — engine; validated before any candidate is loaded
    assert build("geometry")
    assert run_known_metric_suite() == ALL_GREEN             # the 5 tests of §5
    # STEPS 3..8 — each consumes gates(step1) + engine(step2)
    for step in [distance, source, energy, gauge, uv_eft, mission]:
        assert depends_on(step, ["gates", "geometry"])
        build(step)
    # STEP 9 — exporter; refuses to write a report with no first_failure
    build("reports")
    for report in all_reports():
        assert report.status is not None
        assert report.first_failure is not None              # else CI fails (F3)
    return BUILD_GREEN

First failure of this section: step-skipping under schedule pressure — an agent building "the interesting part" (a candidate mode, step 3+) before steps 1–2 are green. The remedy is the assert chain above plus F3's CI, which runs the known-metric suite as a prerequisite job; downstream jobs do not start if it is red.

4. The tensor engine — eight modules

The engine implements the standard pseudo-Riemannian curvature pipeline of doc 14. We fix conventions once (signature (−,+,+,+); Riemann R^ρ_{σμν}=∂_μΓ^ρ_{νσ}−∂_νΓ^ρ_{μσ}+Γ^ρ_{μλ}Γ^λ_{νσ}−Γ^ρ_{νλ}Γ^λ_{μσ}; Ricci R_{σν}=R^ρ_{σρν}; R=g^{σν}R_{σν}) and load them from conventions.yaml so every module agrees. Each module is a pure function of its inputs and the Convention object; symbolic (SymPy) and numerical (finite-difference) backends share one interface, satisfying doc 14's three-layer structure (symbolic / numerical / validation-by-cross-check).

4.1 metric.py — the metric

A MetricAnsatz loads g_{μν}(x) from a MID-*.yaml config or from a named known metric. It exposes components(coords) → g (an n×n symbolic matrix or a grid of numerical n×n arrays). It also records the coordinate symbols and the Convention.

class MetricAnsatz:
    coords: [t, x1, x2, x3]            # symbolic coordinate symbols
    g: Matrix(n, n)                    # g_{μν}, symmetric by construction
    conv: Convention                   # signature, sign flags
    def components(self): return self.g
    def assert_symmetric(self): require g[i,j] == g[j,i]   # negative control on input

Definition / negative control / first failure. Defines g_{μν}. Negative control: assert_symmetric rejects a non-symmetric input matrix (a frequent transcription error). First failure: degenerate metric — det(g)=0 makes the next module (inverse) ill-posed; caught in §4.2.

4.2 inverse.py — the inverse metric

Computes g^{μν} with g^{μλ}g_{λν}=δ^μ_ν. Symbolic backend uses exact matrix inversion; numerical backend uses numpy.linalg.inv per grid point. A guard checks |det(g)|>ε before inverting.

def inverse(g, conv):
    if abs(det(g)) < conv.det_floor:   # det_floor from tolerances.yaml
        raise SingularMetric           # downgrade, do NOT pseudo-invert silently
    g_inv = inv(g)
    require max_abs(g_inv @ g - I) < conv.atol_inverse   # negative control
    return g_inv

Negative control: verifies g^{μλ}g_{λν}=δ^μ_ν to tolerance. First failure: coordinate singularity — e.g. Schwarzschild at r=2M makes g_{tt},g_{rr} blow up; the engine must exclude the horizon radius from its evaluation grid and report the exclusion, not silently regularize. Hiding a coordinate singularity is exactly the kind of "workaround" the build contract forbids.

4.3 christoffel.py — the connection

Computes the Levi-Civita connection

Γ^λ_{μν} = ½ g^{λσ} ( ∂_μ g_{σν} + ∂_ν g_{σμ} − ∂_σ g_{μν} ).

Symbolic backend differentiates exactly; numerical backend uses centered finite differences ∂_μ g ≈ (g(x+h e_μ) − g(x−h e_μ))/(2h) with step h from tolerances.yaml. The output is symmetric in (μ,ν) by construction; a test asserts Γ^λ_{μν}=Γ^λ_{νμ}.

Negative control: lower-index symmetry Γ^λ_{μν}=Γ^λ_{νμ}. First failure: finite-difference truncation — the numerical connection error is O(h²) for centered differences, so on a too-coarse grid the connection (and everything built on it) drifts. The validation layer (§4.8) cross-checks numerical vs symbolic to bound this; the FLRW test (§5) is the sharpest tripwire because its Γ are nonzero and analytically known.

4.4 riemann.py — the curvature tensor

Computes

R^ρ_{σμν} = ∂_μ Γ^ρ_{νσ} − ∂_ν Γ^ρ_{μσ} + Γ^ρ_{μλ} Γ^λ_{νσ} − Γ^ρ_{νλ} Γ^λ_{μσ}.

Negative controls (symmetries): antisymmetry in (μ,ν) (R^ρ_{σμν}=−R^ρ_{σνμ}); the first Bianchi identity R^ρ_{[σμν]}=0; and, after lowering the first index with g, antisymmetry in (ρ,σ) and pair symmetry R_{ρσμν}=R_{μνρσ}. Doc 14's acceptance list requires "tensor symmetries verified" — these are the tests. First failure: sign/convention drift — if Γ and R were written against different conventions, the symmetry tests can still pass (they are convention-internal) while the value is wrong; only the nonzero known-metric comparison (Schwarzschild Kretschmann, §5) exposes it.

4.5 ricci.py — Ricci tensor and scalar

Contracts R_{σν}=R^ρ_{σρν} and R=g^{σν}R_{σν}. Negative control: R_{μν}=R_{νμ} (symmetry). First failure: wrong contraction index — contracting the second covariant slot instead of the first flips a sign in some conventions; caught by Schwarzschild (R_{μν}=0 exterior is contraction-insensitive, so this test does not catch it) and definitively by FLRW (R≠0, contraction-sensitive). This is precisely why the five tests include both a vacuum case and a non-vacuum case.

4.6 einstein.py — Einstein tensor

G_{μν}=R_{μν}−½ R g_{μν}. Negative control: in any vacuum (R_{μν}=0) case, G_{μν}=0 identically; the contracted Bianchi identity ∇^μ G_{μν}=0 is checked symbolically where tractable. First failure: trace-term sign — the −½ R g_{μν} term is where a stray sign hides; the weak-Newtonian test (§5) ties G_{00} to the Poisson equation and so pins the sign to physics, not just to internal symmetry.

4.7 invariants.py — coordinate-invariant diagnostics

Computes the Ricci scalar R, R_{μν}R^{μν}, the Kretschmann scalar K=R_{ρσμν}R^{ρσμν}, and a Weyl-tensor magnitude proxy. These are the coordinate-invariant quantities the whole platform leans on: a chart-dependent ΔD is meaningless, but K(r)=48M²/r⁶ for Schwarzschild is a number every observer agrees on. Negative control: all invariants vanish for Minkowski in any chart (this is the pure-coordinate test of §5). First failure: invariant computed in one chart only — an "invariant" that is only evaluated in one coordinate system has not been shown invariant. The remedy (HC-01, Leaf E01) is to recompute in ≥2 charts and in an orthonormal tetrad and require agreement; invariants.py exposes the per-chart values so that gate can compare them.

4.8 validation_known_metrics.py — the validation harness

This module runs the five tests of §5 and is the gate for build step 2. It owns the symbolic-vs-numerical cross-check (doc 14 Layer 3): for each test metric it computes the target invariant both symbolically and numerically and requires agreement to tolerance, and requires agreement with the closed-form textbook value. It emits a small report-hash record (doc 14: "export report hashes") so the engine's validated state is auditable and so F3's CI can detect drift.

Negative control: the harness is required to self-test its own failure path — a deliberately corrupted metric (e.g. a Schwarzschild metric with the g_{tt} sign flipped) must make the suite go red, proving the harness can fail. First failure of this subsection: a harness that cannot fail — a validation module that only ever exercises the green path (or whose tolerance is so loose it never trips) is decorative, not protective; it would rubber-stamp a broken engine. The remedy is the mutation/negative case above plus the convergence-order check of §5.8, both asserted by F3's CI so the harness's ability to reject is itself version-controlled.

First failure of §4 as a whole: an engine that is self-consistent but wrong. All of §4.1–4.7's negative controls are internal (symmetries, identities) and can be satisfied by a uniformly-wrong-convention engine. Internal consistency is necessary but not sufficient. The cure is §5: comparison against metrics whose curvature is known from outside the code.

5. The five known-metric validation tests

Doc 14 enumerates exactly five required known-metric tests. Each is implemented in validation_known_metrics.py with a declared tolerance from tolerances.yaml, run in both backends, and compared to the closed-form value. The five are chosen to be collectively sign-, contraction-, and chart-sensitive: no single uniform error survives all five. The table summarizes; the subsections give the worked target numbers.

# Metric Coordinates Target diagnostic Expected value What it pins down
1 Minkowski (t,x,y,z) all curvature Γ=R=R_{μν}=K=0 engine zeroes; baseline
2 Schwarzschild exterior (t,r,θ,φ), r>2M R_{μν}, K R_{μν}=0; K=48M²/r⁶ nonzero curvature with vacuum Ricci
3 FLRW (toy, flat, a(t)) (t,x,y,z) R R=6(ä/a+(ȧ/a)²) contraction sign; non-vacuum R≠0
4 Pure-coordinate Minkowski nonlinear chart of flat space all curvature R=R_{μν}=K=0 coordinate-only rejection
5 Weak Newtonian g_{00}=−(1+2Φ), g_{ij}=(1−2Φ)δ_{ij} G_{00}/R_{00} ∇²Φ (Poisson) absolute sign via physics

5.1 Test 1 — Minkowski

g_{μν}=diag(−1,1,1,1), constant. Every derivative of g vanishes, so Γ^λ_{μν}=0, hence R^ρ_{σμν}=0, R_{μν}=0, R=0, K=0. Pass criterion: max|Γ|=0 and max|R^ρ_{σμν}|=0 exactly (symbolic) and <atol (numerical, where atol from tolerances.yaml, typically 1e-10). First failure caught: a nonzero result here means a wiring error so basic (e.g. differentiating a constant incorrectly, or an index transposition) that nothing else is trustworthy. Minkowski is the smoke test; it is sign-insensitive (all zeros), so passing it proves almost nothing on its own — which is exactly why tests 2–5 exist.

5.2 Test 2 — Schwarzschild exterior

ds²=−(1−r_s/r)dt²+(1−r_s/r)^{−1}dr²+r²dθ²+r²sin²θ dφ², with r_s=2M, evaluated on r>r_s. Two targets:

  • Vacuum Ricci: R_{μν}=0 everywhere outside the source. This is doc 14's stated requirement ("known Ricci scalar zero outside source"). Note R_{μν}=0 ⟹ R=0, but R_{μν}=0 is the stronger, more diagnostic statement and is what the test asserts.
  • Kretschmann scalar: K=R_{ρσμν}R^{ρσμν}=48M²/r⁶=12 r_s²/r⁶. This is nonzero, chart-independent, and the single most valuable known number in the suite: it certifies that the engine produces correct nonzero curvature, not merely correct zeros.

Worked number. Take geometric units M=1 so r_s=2. At r=10M=10: K=48·1²/10⁶=48/1,000,000=4.8×10⁻⁵. At r=3M=3 (just outside the photon sphere region of interest): K=48/3⁶=48/729≈6.5844×10⁻². At r=4M=4: K=48/4096≈1.1719×10⁻². The engine must reproduce these to rtol≈1e-8 (symbolic exact; numerical limited by finite-difference order and grid h). First failure caught: a sign/contraction error that survived test 1 (because test 1 is all zeros) is exposed here, because R_{μν}=0 requires cancellation between nonzero Γ-quadratic and ∂Γ terms — getting R_{μν}=0 out of nonzero connection coefficients is a genuine, convention-sensitive computation. And K=48M²/r⁶ is a value match, not a symmetry match, so it catches a uniformly-wrong-magnitude engine.

5.3 Test 3 — FLRW (toy, spatially flat)

ds²=−dt²+a(t)²(dx²+dy²+dz²). The Ricci scalar is

R = 6 ( ä/a + (ȧ/a)² ).

For the test we use a closed-form scale factor so the target is an exact symbolic expression. Two convenient choices:

  • de Sitter a(t)=e^{Ht}: then ȧ/a=H, ä/a=H², so R=6(H²+H²)=12H² — a constant. With H=1: R=12. The engine must return R=12H² symbolically and ≈12.000 numerically at H=1.
  • Matter-like a(t)=t^{2/3}: ȧ/a=(2/3)/t, ä/a=−(2/9)/t²; R=6(−2/9+4/9)/t²=6·(2/9)/t²=(4/3)/t². At t=2: R=(4/3)/4=1/3≈0.3333.

First failure caught: FLRW is the contraction-sign tripwire. R here is nonzero and its sign and magnitude depend on contracting the correct Ricci slot and on the correct −½R g_{μν} bookkeeping downstream. An engine that passed Minkowski (zeros) and even Schwarzschild (R_{μν}=0 is contraction-insensitive because zero contracts to zero) can still get FLRW's nonzero R wrong. That is why the suite deliberately pairs a vacuum metric (test 2) with a non-vacuum metric (test 3): together they are sensitive to errors that either alone misses.

5.4 Test 4 — pure-coordinate transform of Minkowski

Take flat Minkowski and apply a nonlinear, invertible coordinate change so the metric components are nontrivial functions of the new coordinates, yet the geometry is still flat. A clean choice is Rindler-like or simply spherical/parabolic coordinates on flat space; e.g. flat space in spatial spherical coordinates ds²=−dt²+dr²+r²dθ²+r²sin²θ dφ² has nonzero Γ (e.g. Γ^r_{θθ}=−r, Γ^θ_{rθ}=1/r) but zero Riemann. The test asserts Γ≠0 and R^ρ_{σμν}=0, R_{μν}=0, K=0 to tolerance.

First failure caught — and why this test is special. This is the coordinate-only rejection test (doc 14 acceptance list: "coordinate-only case rejected"). It is the engine-level analogue of the platform-level FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY downgrade. It proves the engine does not mistake nonzero connection coefficients for real curvature — i.e. it does not confuse a ruler/clock relabeling with physics. An engine that returns nonzero K here would manufacture spurious curvature from any sufficiently baroque coordinate choice, and every candidate Ξ_drive written in fancy coordinates would falsely "shorten distances." Test 4 is the firewall against exactly the most seductive failure mode of the whole project. First failure: if the engine reports nonzero curvature here, the build halts; no candidate may be screened by an instrument that hallucinates curvature from coordinates.

5.5 Test 5 — weak Newtonian (Poisson limit)

Linearized metric g_{00}=−(1+2Φ), g_{ij}=(1−2Φ)δ_{ij}, with |Φ|≪1 and Φ=Φ(x) (static, weak field). To first order in Φ, the time-time Ricci component reduces to

R_{00} ≈ ∇²Φ,

and through the field equation G_{00}≈2∇²Φ ties to the Newtonian source via ∇²Φ=4πG ρ (Poisson). The test feeds a known potential — e.g. Φ=−GM/r (so ∇²Φ=0 for r>0, point source) or a smooth test potential Φ=½ k(x²+y²+z²) (so ∇²Φ=3k, constant) — and asserts the engine returns R_{00}≈∇²Φ to first order, to a tolerance that accounts for the dropped O(Φ²) terms.

Worked number. With Φ=½k(x²+y²+z²) and k=10⁻⁶ (kept tiny so linearization holds): ∇²Φ=3k=3×10⁻⁶, so the engine must return R_{00}≈3×10⁻⁶ with relative error dominated by the O(Φ²)~10⁻¹² truncation — i.e. agreement to ~1e-5 relative is the physically correct expectation, and demanding 1e-10 here would be wrong because the limit itself is approximate. First failure caught: test 5 pins the absolute sign of the whole pipeline to physics: a mass produces an attractive potential, ∇²Φ>0 for ρ>0, and R_{00} must come out with the sign that yields attraction. Internal symmetry tests cannot fix an overall sign; only contact with the Newtonian limit can. It also encodes doc 14's required "flat-limit invariants zero" in its k→0 sub-case, where R_{00}→0.

Worked Test-4 trace (the firewall, hand-checked). Flat space in spherical spatial coordinates has the same nonzero spatial Christoffel symbols as Schwarzschild's angular sector but none of the radial-redshift terms: Γ^r_{θθ}=−r, Γ^r_{φφ}=−r sin²θ, Γ^θ_{rθ}=Γ^φ_{rφ}=1/r, Γ^θ_{φφ}=−sinθcosθ, Γ^φ_{θφ}=cotθ. Compute one Riemann component the engine must zero out — the R^θ_{\ rθr} block:

R^θ_{rθr} = ∂_θ Γ^θ_{rr} − ∂_r Γ^θ_{θr} + Γ^θ_{θλ}Γ^λ_{rr} − Γ^θ_{rλ}Γ^λ_{θr}.

(Marked reference computation — the two surviving terms and their cancellation.) With Γ^θ_{rr}=0, the ∂_θ Γ^θ_{rr} term and the Γ^θ_{θλ}Γ^λ_{rr} term both vanish. The two terms that survive are the derivative term −∂_r Γ^θ_{θr}=−∂_r(1/r)=+1/r² and the quadratic term −Γ^θ_{rλ}Γ^λ_{θr}=−Γ^θ_{rθ}Γ^θ_{θr}=−(1/r)(1/r)=−1/r². Their sum is (+1/r²)+(−1/r²)=0. The exact cancellation is the whole point: nonzero connection, zero curvature. This is a reference result, not an in-code claim: the full tensor was checked symbolically (every component of R^ρ_{σμν} for flat space in spherical coordinates vanishes identically), so R^θ_{rθr}=0 is substantiated rather than asserted. An engine that returns anything but 0 here is hallucinating curvature from a coordinate choice — the single most dangerous failure for a platform whose candidates are written in clever coordinates. The engine is required to reproduce this cancellation symbolically (exact 0) and numerically (|R^θ_{rθr}|<atol).

5.6 Configuration of the known-metric suite

The five tests are not hard-coded magic; they are declared in configs/gates/ so the suite is auditable and extensible. A representative entry:

# configs/gates/known_metrics.yaml
- name: schwarzschild_exterior
  coordinates: [t, r, theta, phi]
  params: {M: 1.0}
  metric_diag: ["-(1 - 2*M/r)", "1/(1 - 2*M/r)", "r**2", "r**2*sin(theta)**2"]
  exclude_region: "r <= 2*M"          # report the horizon exclusion; do NOT regularize silently
  targets:
    ricci_tensor: "0"                  # vacuum: all components zero
    kretschmann:  "48*M**2/r**6"       # nonzero invariant; the value-match
  tolerances: {ricci_atol: 1e-10, kretschmann_rtol: 1e-8}
- name: flrw_de_sitter
  coordinates: [t, x, y, z]
  params: {H: 1.0}
  metric_diag: ["-1", "exp(2*H*t)", "exp(2*H*t)", "exp(2*H*t)"]
  targets: {ricci_scalar: "12*H**2"}
  tolerances: {ricci_scalar_rtol: 1e-8}
- name: weak_newtonian
  coordinates: [t, x, y, z]
  params: {k: 1e-6}
  potential: "0.5*k*(x**2 + y**2 + z**2)"
  metric_diag: ["-(1 + 2*Phi)", "(1 - 2*Phi)", "(1 - 2*Phi)", "(1 - 2*Phi)"]
  targets: {ricci_00: "laplacian(Phi)"}   # == 3*k
  tolerances: {ricci_00_rtol: 1e-5}       # deliberately loose: O(Phi^2) truncation

The exclude_region field is the codified version of the §4.2 first failure: a coordinate singularity is reported and excluded, never silently regularized. The deliberately loose ricci_00_rtol: 1e-5 on the weak-Newtonian test is the codified version of the §5.5 honesty point: the limit itself is O(Φ²)-approximate, so demanding machine precision would fail a correct computation. First failure caught: a test added without a documented tolerance rationale; F3's CI rejects a known_metrics.yaml entry whose tolerance lacks a comment justifying its magnitude.

5.6b Why exactly these five (collective coverage argument)

The five are not redundant. The coverage table makes the argument explicit: each error class is caught by at least one test, and no uniform error survives all five.

Error class T1 Mink T2 Schwz T3 FLRW T4 coord-only T5 Newton
Gross wiring (differentiate const wrong) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
Riemann/Ricci sign convention — ✓ (K value) ✓ — ✓
Contraction index (Ricci) — — (zero) ✓ — ✓
Magnitude scale error — ✓ (K value) ✓ — ✓
Coordinate→curvature hallucination — — — ✓ —
Overall absolute sign (vs physics) — — — — ✓
Finite-difference truncation (numeric) — ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓

The bolded cell in each row is the test that is most diagnostic for that error. Two rows are uniquely covered: coordinate→curvature hallucination only by Test 4, and absolute physical sign only by Test 5. Dropping either would leave a blind spot that is exactly a project-critical failure mode (false shortening from coordinates; wrong-sign gravity). This is the formal justification for doc 14's list of five.

First failure of this subsection (coverage gaps and overconfidence): the coverage table is itself a claim, and its first failure is an unproven row — an error class asserted "caught" by a test without a negative control that actually demonstrates the catch. The table is necessary but not self-certifying: five tests cover the enumerated error classes, yet a curvature error orthogonal to all five rows (e.g. a tetrad-frame convention bug that only bites grid-scale visualization metrics with no closed form) would pass every cell here. The honest downgrade is to treat this table as a floor, not a proof of completeness, and to require each ✓ to be backed by the corresponding §5.x negative control that mutates the relevant convention and observes the predicted red.

First failure of §5 as a whole: a tolerance that is too loose hides a real error; a tolerance that is too tight fails a correct approximation (Test 5). The remedy is per-test tolerances in tolerances.yaml with documented rationale (exact-zero for T1/T4, rtol~1e-8 value-match for T2/T3, rtol~1e-5 for the deliberately-approximate T5), all version-controlled and asserted by F3's CI.

5.7 Worked Schwarzschild trace — what "correct nonzero curvature" looks like

To make Test 2 concrete (and to give F3's golden gate-cards a hand-checkable reference), we trace the non-trivial Schwarzschild Christoffel symbols and confirm the Kretschmann target. With f(r)=1−r_s/r and f'(r)=r_s/r², the non-zero connection coefficients are

Γ^t_{tr}=f'/(2f)=r_s/(2r² f),   Γ^r_{tt}=f f'/2=r_s f/(2r²),   Γ^r_{rr}=−f'/(2f)=−r_s/(2r² f),
Γ^r_{θθ}=−r f,                   Γ^r_{φφ}=−r f sin²θ,
Γ^θ_{rθ}=Γ^φ_{rφ}=1/r,          Γ^θ_{φφ}=−sinθ cosθ,   Γ^φ_{θφ}=cotθ.

These are nonzero, yet the engine must produce R_{μν}=0 from them — the cancellation between the ∂Γ and ΓΓ pieces of the Riemann tensor is what makes Test 2 a genuine convention probe rather than a triviality. The independent curvature components (orthonormal-frame magnitudes) scale as R^{\hat t\hat r}_{\ \ \hat t\hat r}=−2M/r³ and R^{\hat θ\hat φ}_{\ \ \hat θ\hat φ}=2M/r³ (with M=r_s/2), and squaring-and-summing the six independent blocks gives the Kretschmann invariant

K = R_{ρσμν}R^{ρσμν} = 48 M² / r⁶ = 12 r_s² / r⁶.

Worked check at M=1, r=6M=6: K=48/6⁶=48/46656≈1.0288×10⁻³ (reference computation, symbolically verified: K·r⁶/M²=48 exactly). At the marginally-stable circular-orbit radius r=6M this is the number the engine must return; if the numerical backend on a grid of step h=10⁻³ returns 1.0288×10⁻³(1±~10⁻⁶), the finite-difference truncation (O(h²)) is within the declared rtol. This single value, derived outside the code, is what separates a correct engine from a merely self-consistent one — and it is the value F3 freezes as a golden number.

First failure of this subsection (golden-number rot): the danger of freezing a hand-checked golden number is that it can be frozen wrong, or frozen against the wrong convention, after which CI faithfully defends an error. The remedy is that the golden K=48M²/r⁶ is independently re-derivable — it is a textbook invariant, not an artifact of this code's sign choices — and F3 must re-derive it symbolically from the metric on every CI run (not read a cached constant), so a convention change that alters the engine also alters the freshly-derived target and the mismatch surfaces instead of being masked.

5.8 Numerical backend, convergence, and the symbolic↔numerical cross-check

The two backends exist so that neither is trusted alone (doc 14 Layer 3). The symbolic backend is exact but does not scale to grid-evaluated visualization metrics; the numerical backend scales but carries finite-difference error. Their agreement on shared cases is the validation. For centered differences the per-derivative error is ≈ (h²/6) ∂³g, so a curvature scalar built from second derivatives carries error O(h²); halving h should cut the error by ≈4×. The harness asserts this convergence order rather than a single tolerance, which is a far stronger test:

function assert_second_order(metric, target_fn, h0):
    e1 = abs(numerical_invariant(metric, h0)   − symbolic_invariant(metric))
    e2 = abs(numerical_invariant(metric, h0/2) − symbolic_invariant(metric))
    order = log2(e1 / e2)
    require 1.8 < order < 2.2        # centered diff ⇒ ~2; window absorbs round-off

Worked convergence example (de Sitter FLRW, H=1, symbolic R=12). Suppose the numerical backend returns R(h=10⁻²)=12.000133 (error 1.33×10⁻⁴) and R(h=5×10⁻³)=12.0000333 (error 3.33×10⁻⁵). Then order=log₂(1.33×10⁻⁴ / 3.33×10⁻⁵)=log₂(3.99)≈2.00 — second order confirmed. A backend with a hidden one-sided difference would show order≈1 and fail this gate even if its single-h error happened to fall under a loose atol. First failure caught: an engine whose numerical error is small by luck on one grid but not converging — i.e. a subtly wrong stencil — is exposed by the order check, not by a point tolerance. As h→0 round-off eventually dominates and order degrades; the harness records the h at which the symbolic↔numerical gap reaches its floor and uses an h above it, documenting the choice.

5.9 Error-propagation order along the pipeline

Errors compound along metric → inverse → christoffel → riemann → ricci → einstein → invariants. The connection is built from first derivatives of g; Riemann from derivatives of Γ (hence second derivatives of g); invariants are quadratic in Riemann. So a relative input error ε in g propagates roughly as: g_inv ~ ε, Γ ~ ε + ε_h (where ε_h is the finite-difference floor), Riemann ~ ε + 2ε_h, K ~ 2(ε + 2ε_h) (quadratic ⇒ relative error doubles). The practical consequence, encoded in tolerances.yaml, is that invariant tolerances must be ~4–8× looser than metric tolerances to avoid false reds, and that the dominant numerical error in a deep pipeline is the second-derivative finite-difference floor, not matrix inversion. This is why the symbolic backend is the reference for the five tests wherever it is tractable, and the numerical backend is validated against it before being trusted on grid-scale visualization metrics that have no closed form. First failure caught: mis-budgeted tolerances that either flood CI with false reds (too tight on K) or let a real magnitude error through (too loose); the propagation table above is the documented rationale F3 audits.

6. Engine output flows into a gate card (the hand-off to F2/E-leaves)

To keep the engine fail-closed, its validated diagnostics are emitted only through a gate card. The engine does not decide whether a candidate passes a physics gate — it supplies the numbers the gate decides on, and the validator (F2) enforces fail-closed logic. The relevant fragment for this leaf is the engine's own self-test card, which is the only place the engine reaches PASS_TOY:

{ "model_id": "ENGINE-SELFTEST",
  "challenge_id": "F1-numrel-engine",
  "object_definition": {
    "equations": ["Gamma=½ g^{λσ}(∂g+∂g−∂g)", "R^ρ_{σμν}=∂Γ−∂Γ+ΓΓ−ΓΓ",
                  "R_{μν}=R^ρ_{σρν}", "G_{μν}=R_{μν}−½R g_{μν}", "K=R_{ρσμν}R^{ρσμν}"],
    "coordinates": "per-test (Cartesian/Schwarzschild/comoving/spherical/weak-field)",
    "active_fields": ["g_μν (known metrics only)"],
    "layer_assignments": {"g_μν": "× metric/geometric base"} },
  "gates": {
    "definition": "PASS", "negative_controls": "PASS",
    "invariant_check": "PASS",        /* Minkowski K=0 in any chart; Schwarzschild K=48M²/r⁶ */
    "source_check": "AUDIT",          /* engine does not source anything; N/A for known metrics */
    "gauge_check": "PASS",            /* Test 4: coordinate-only ⇒ zero curvature */
    "energy_check": "AUDIT", "causality_check": "AUDIT",
    "uv_boundary": "PASS" },
  "first_failure": "engine is self-consistent only; correctness is established ONLY on the 5 known metrics — any candidate Ξ_drive remains TOY_MODEL/AUDIT and must pass HC-01…HC-10 separately",
  "strongest_allowed_claim": "The tensor engine correctly reproduces curvature for five known metrics (PASS_TOY on self-test). No claim about any candidate drive mode follows.",
  "forbidden_claims": ["working warp drive", "proves FTL", "the engine validates the drive"],
  "next_closure_step": "F2 data schemas + validator; then candidate screening via E01…E10" }

Note the deliberate AUDIT on source_check, energy_check, causality_check: a known metric has no candidate source ledger to evaluate, and the engine self-test makes no physics claim — so those gates are audit-visible, never a clean PASS. The card's strongest_allowed_claim is the strongest sentence this entire leaf is permitted to assert, and it is carefully bounded to the five known metrics.

First failure of this section: mistaking a green engine self-test for a green candidate. The structural guard is that model_id="ENGINE-SELFTEST" is the only card the engine emits with PASS-heavy gates; every MID-* candidate card is built by the E-leaf gates, defaults to TOY_MODEL, and cannot inherit the engine's PASS.

7. Patent extraction for this leaf

Doc 14 states the disclosable asset directly: "a computing system configured to compute invariant diagnostics for candidate metric-interface profiles." The patentable, theory-agnostic assets introduced or anchored by F1 are: (a) the gate-first build order (a method of constructing a physics-screening pipeline in which gate infrastructure and a validated tensor engine are prerequisites to any candidate evaluation, such that un-validated computation cannot emit a status); (b) the five-metric self-validation harness with its collective-coverage selection (vacuum + non-vacuum + coordinate-only + weak-field), as a method for certifying a curvature engine before screening; (c) the single-source convention object binding signature/sign/index-order across modules; and (d) the report-hash export that makes the engine's validated state auditable and CI-checkable. None of these require any unified theory to be correct — they are software/method claims with option value regardless of whether any candidate Ξ_drive ever survives a gate.

First failure of this section (claim overreach): the patent's first failure is drafting a claim that reads on "a metric-interface drive" rather than on the screening method — i.e. accidentally claiming the propulsion outcome instead of the gate-supervised simulation pipeline. The honest scope is strictly the software/method/medium: a computing system configured to compute invariant diagnostics and route them through fail-closed gates. No claim here asserts that any candidate shortens a proper distance, is sourceable, or propels anything; doing so would be a FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION and is out of scope for this leaf. The remedy is that every F1 claim seed is checked against the contract's forbidden-claim list and is bounded to the engine's PASS_TOY-on-self-test ceiling before it can enter patent_exports/.
