Honest response: the architecture forbids exactly this by construction. The engine's only PASS-bearing card is ENGINE-SELFTEST, whose strongest_allowed_claim is bounded to five textbook metrics and whose forbidden_claims explicitly list "the engine validates the drive." Every candidate MID-* card is built downstream by the HC-01…HC-10 gates, defaults to TOY_MODEL, cannot inherit the engine's PASS, and is most likely downgraded — Test 4 is in the suite precisely to ensure the engine refuses to turn coordinate cleverness into curvature, which is the very trick the objection fears. A validated instrument that is provably unable to hallucinate curvature is the opposite of window-dressing: it is what makes the platform's failures trustworthy.

F2 — Software Architecture II — Schemas, Gate Validator, CLI, Core Algorithms

Closure status: 1 TOY_DEFINED → 2 TOY_TESTED (platform: PASS_TOY ceiling; reference candidate MID-METRIC-001 carries FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC at its source gate) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

1. Why this layer matters

The physics of the metric-interface drive is only as trustworthy as the software that refuses to lie about it. Chapter F1 fixed the runtime — the layered field model, the evaluation kernels, the data flow. F2 fixes the contracts: the four JSON schemas that every artifact must satisfy, the gate-card validator that fails closed when any contract is violated, the midrive CLI that is the only sanctioned way to move a candidate through the pipeline, and the seven core algorithms that each emit the mandated quad-format export (Markdown for the manuscript, JSON for the gate card, a CSV row for the comparison table, and a single patent-support paragraph).

The governing principle, restated from the BUILD CONTRACT §1: the absolute ceiling anywhere in this platform is PASS_TOY. No schema field, no CLI exit code, and no algorithm return value may ever encode a status above that. The validator's job is not to certify success — it is to make undeclared success structurally impossible. A model that omits its source ledger does not get a benefit of the doubt; it gets FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC and a non-zero exit code. This is the inversion that makes the document defensible: most modes should fail, and the software is the thing that guarantees they visibly do.

First failure (this section): the contracts are only as strong as their enforcement coverage; a schema field that no validator rule reads is decorative. F2 closes the four schemas and wires every field to a rule, but three fields (gauge.evidence, energy.evidence provenance, and the report_manifest.watermark byte-exactness) are validated for presence only, not semantic correctness — a determined author could populate them with plausible-but-wrong prose and pass. That residual is logged below as the platform's primary first failure.

2. The schema package — four contracts

The deliverable named in source doc 16 is a four-file JSON-Schema package:

schemas/model_config.schema.json
schemas/gate_card.schema.json
schemas/report_manifest.schema.json
schemas/manuscript_export.schema.json

All four are JSON Schema draft 2020-12, additionalProperties: false at every object level (drift defense: an unknown key is a hard validation error, not a warning), and every status-bearing field is constrained by an enum whose top value is PASS_TOY. The string PASS (unqualified, operational) is not a member of any status enum in the package — it cannot be expressed, so it cannot be claimed. This is the schema-level realization of the ceiling rule.

2.1 model_config.schema.json

The model config is the input contract: it declares the metric ansatz, the active excitation components, the parameter values, and the declared (not validated) source model. Validation here proves only that the object is well-formed and honest about what it has not done — e.g. source_model: "inferred_only" is a legal value precisely because it is an admission, not a claim.

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "midrive/model_config.schema.json",
  "title": "MID model configuration",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["model_id","coordinates","metric_signature",
               "metric_components","parameters","active_components",
               "source_model","claimed_status"],
  "properties": {
    "model_id":        {"type":"string","pattern":"^MID-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{3}$"},
    "description":     {"type":"string","maxLength":280},
    "coordinates":     {"type":"array","items":{"enum":["t","x","y","z"]},
                        "minItems":4,"maxItems":4},
    "metric_signature":{"const":"-+++"},
    "metric_components":{
      "type":"object","additionalProperties":false,
      "required":["g_tt","g_xx","g_yy","g_zz"],
      "patternProperties":{"^g_[txyz]{2}$":{"type":"string"}}
    },
    "parameters":      {"type":"object",
                        "additionalProperties":{"type":"number"}},
    "active_components":{"type":"array","minItems":1,
      "items":{"enum":["delta_g_munu","delta_A_mu_a","delta_phi_I",
                       "delta_G_muA","delta_G_AB"]}},
    "source_model":    {"enum":["inferred_only","matched","none"]},
    "claimed_status":  {"enum":["TOY_MODEL","AUDIT"]}
  }
}

Three drift defenses are load-bearing. (i) model_id is pattern-locked to MID-<CLASS>-<NNN> so the gate card and the config provably reference the same object. (ii) claimed_status cannot be set to EFT_CANDIDATE or anything higher at config time — promotion is a validator/attorney act, never a self-declaration (BUILD CONTRACT §1.4). (iii) metric_components keys are patternProperties-locked to the symmetric g_μν slots; a stray g_xt2 is rejected rather than silently ignored. (One honest schema caveat: the ^g_[txyz]{2}$ pattern also admits redundant off-diagonal spellings such as both g_tx and g_xt; symmetry de-duplication is a validator check, §3, not a schema one — the regex does not by itself enforce the ten-slot symmetric basis claimed above.)

First failure (this section): the config schema validates structure and declared honesty, but it cannot validate physical content — source_model: "inferred_only" is accepted as a legal admission, yet the schema has no power to confirm that the declaration is true (that the metric really was inferred and not silently fitted to a hidden source). The schema makes dishonesty about shape impossible and dishonesty about physics merely declared; closing that gap is delegated entirely to the §3 validator and the §5.3 source-reconstruction algorithm, not the config contract.

2.2 The MID-METRIC-001 reference config

The canonical worked example from source doc 16 — a single Gaussian contraction lobe parked at x0 = 50 — validates cleanly against the schema above:

{
  "model_id": "MID-METRIC-001",
  "description": "Forward contraction lobe toy model",
  "coordinates": ["t","x","y","z"],
  "metric_signature": "-+++",
  "metric_components": {
    "g_tt": "-1",
    "g_xx": "1 - A*exp(-((x-x0)**2 + y**2 + z**2)/sigma**2)",
    "g_yy": "1",
    "g_zz": "1"
  },
  "parameters": { "A": 0.01, "sigma": 10.0, "x0": 50.0 },
  "active_components": ["delta_g_munu"],
  "source_model": "inferred_only",
  "claimed_status": "TOY_MODEL"
}

This object is the spine of every worked number in F2. Note what it is not: it is not sourced (inferred_only), its energy is not audited at config time, and its claimed_status floor is TOY_MODEL. The validator will hold it exactly there.

First failure (this section): metric_components values are stored as strings (e.g. "1 - A*exp(...)"), which means the config schema cannot itself prove the expression is dimensionally consistent or even parseable — that delegation lands on the algorithm layer (§5), and a malformed expression string is a runtime failure, not a schema failure. The contract is honest about the boundary but does not move it.

2.3 gate_card.schema.json

The gate card is the judgment contract — one per candidate, mandated by BUILD CONTRACT §3. Its enums encode the entire downgrade tree.

{
  "$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id":"midrive/gate_card.schema.json",
  "type":"object","additionalProperties":false,
  "required":["model_id","status","first_failure","gates",
              "allowed_claim","forbidden_claims"],
  "properties":{
    "model_id":{"type":"string","pattern":"^MID-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{3}$"},
    "status":{"enum":["UNDEFINED","TOY_MODEL","TOY_TESTED",
                      "AUDIT","UV_DELEGATED","PASS_TOY",
                      "FAIL","FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY","FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC",
                      "FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY","FAIL_PURE_GAUGE",
                      "FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION","FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM"]},
    "first_failure":{"type":"string","minLength":3},
    "gates":{
      "type":"object","additionalProperties":false,
      "required":["claim_boundary","invariant_distance","source",
                  "energy","gauge","uv"],
      "properties":{
        "claim_boundary":   {"$ref":"#/$defs/gate"},
        "invariant_distance":{"$ref":"#/$defs/gate"},
        "source":           {"$ref":"#/$defs/gate"},
        "energy":           {"$ref":"#/$defs/gate"},
        "gauge":            {"$ref":"#/$defs/gate"},
        "uv":               {"$ref":"#/$defs/gate"}
      }
    },
    "allowed_claim":{"type":"string"},
    "forbidden_claims":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},
                        "minItems":1}
  },
  "$defs":{
    "gate":{
      "type":"object","additionalProperties":false,
      "required":["status","evidence"],
      "properties":{
        "status":{"enum":["PASS_TOY","AUDIT","FAIL","UV_DELEGATED"]},
        "evidence":{"type":"string","minLength":1}
      }
    }
  }
}

Two properties matter for fail-closed discipline. First, the per-gate status enum omits bare PASS — the most a gate can return is PASS_TOY. The energy gate, per BUILD CONTRACT §3, is never a clean pass: its only non-failing value is AUDIT, and the validator (§3) enforces that even though the schema would syntactically permit PASS_TOY. Second, first_failure has minLength: 3 so a candidate cannot ship with an empty first-failure string — BUILD CONTRACT §1.2 ("every section AND every chapter must name a first failure") is made un-skippable at the data layer.

The MID-METRIC-001 gate card from source doc 16 validates and resolves to terminal status FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC because its source gate is FAIL ("source inferred but not matched"). That is the correct outcome — the toy lobe shortens proper distance under an unsourced ansatz, which is exactly the failure the platform exists to expose.

First failure (this section): the schema constrains gate evidence only to minLength: 1 — any non-empty string passes. Semantic evidence quality (does the prose actually justify the status?) is outside JSON Schema's expressive power and is delegated to human/attorney review. A one-character evidence string "x" is schema-legal; the validator (§3) raises it to a warning, not an error, which is a deliberate but real hole.

2.4 report_manifest.schema.json and manuscript_export.schema.json

The report manifest enumerates every artifact a run produced and binds each to a SHA-256 and a watermark token. The manuscript export is the contract for what may cross into the 500-page document.

{ "$id":"midrive/report_manifest.schema.json",
  "type":"object","additionalProperties":false,
  "required":["run_id","model_id","artifacts","watermark","first_failure"],
  "properties":{
    "run_id":{"type":"string","pattern":"^run-[0-9TZ:-]+$"},
    "model_id":{"type":"string"},
    "artifacts":{"type":"array","minItems":1,"items":{
      "type":"object","additionalProperties":false,
      "required":["path","kind","sha256"],
      "properties":{
        "path":{"type":"string"},
        "kind":{"enum":["markdown","gate_card_json","csv_row",
                        "patent_paragraph","figure"]},
        "sha256":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[a-f0-9]{64}$"}}}},
    "watermark":{"const":"SIMULATION — STATUS-LABELED — NOT A PHYSICAL CLAIM"},
    "first_failure":{"type":"string","minLength":3}}}

The watermark field is a JSON const: every figure-bearing manifest must carry the exact byte string SIMULATION — STATUS-LABELED — NOT A PHYSICAL CLAIM, satisfying source-doc-16 validation rule "Every Mars figure must include watermark." Any deviation — even a trailing space — fails validation. The manuscript_export.schema.json (omitted here for space; same draft) adds one critical guard: a forbidden_phrase_scan boolean that must be true, set only after the export text has been run through the §4 forbidden-phrase linter.

First failure (this section): the manifest validates that a watermark token is present and byte-exact, but it cannot verify the watermark was actually rendered into the figure pixels. A run could emit a compliant manifest while shipping an un-watermarked PNG. Binding the watermark to image content (e.g. a perceptual hash check) is unimplemented; presence-in-manifest is the current floor.

3. The gate-card validator — fail-closed by construction

The validator is the platform's conscience. It takes a (model_config, gate_card) pair plus the algorithm evidence bundle and returns a terminal status and an exit code. Its defining property: it can only ever lower a status, never raise one. There is no code path in which the validator promotes a candidate. Promotion is reserved for owner/attorney escalation (BUILD CONTRACT §1.4) and is not expressible in this module.

3.1 The enforcement rules

The cross-field rules — the ones JSON Schema alone cannot express — are hard-coded and ordered. Order matters: the first rule that fires sets the terminal status, realizing the "name the first failure" mandate.

RULE 0  schema_valid(config) AND schema_valid(card) AND model_id_match
        else -> FAIL  ("malformed or mismatched artifact")     [exit 2]

RULE 1  card.gates.claim_boundary.status == FAIL
        -> FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION                                  [exit 3]
        (a forbidden phrase survived; claim exceeds evidence)

RULE 2  card.gates.invariant_distance.status == FAIL
        -> FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY                                 [exit 3]
        (effect is pure coordinate artifact; no invariant content)

RULE 3  card.gates.source.status == FAIL
        -> FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC                                [exit 3]
        AND assert "propulsion" NOT in card.allowed_claim       [exit 4 if violated]

RULE 4  card.gates.energy.status == FAIL
        -> FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY                                [exit 3]
        NOTE energy gate may NEVER be PASS_TOY; AUDIT is its ceiling

RULE 5  card.gates.gauge.status == FAIL
        -> FAIL_PURE_GAUGE                                      [exit 3]

RULE 6  card.gates.uv.status == UV_DELEGATED
        -> UV_DELEGATED                                         [exit 0, flagged]
        AND assert "global stability solved" NOT in any claim   [exit 4 if violated]

RULE 7  any candidate with EFT_CANDIDATE ambitions BUT
        (source.status != PASS_TOY OR energy.status != AUDIT)
        -> demote, refuse EFT_CANDIDATE                         [exit 3]

RULE 8  all gates in {PASS_TOY, AUDIT} AND energy==AUDIT
        AND no forbidden phrase -> PASS_TOY (ceiling)           [exit 0]

Several invariants are worth making explicit. Rule 4's note encodes BUILD CONTRACT §3 literally: the validator treats energy.status == PASS_TOY as a self-inconsistency and downgrades to AUDIT with a logged anomaly, because the energy gate "is never a clean PASS — it is pass / audit-visible." Rule 3's second clause is the propulsion interlock: if the source gate failed, the literal substring propulsion is forbidden in allowed_claim, and its presence escalates to exit code 4 (a contract breach, not a mere fail). Rule 8 is the only path to the ceiling, and even it requires energy == AUDIT — there is no input for which the validator emits anything above PASS_TOY.

A second honesty note on the ordering itself: because the first firing rule sets the terminal status, the rule order encodes a priority over first failures, not a completeness claim. A candidate that fails both the source gate (Rule 3) and the gauge gate (Rule 5) is reported as FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC and the gauge failure is masked until the source is fixed — correct for "name the first failure," but it means a single validator pass under-reports the total failure count. Multi-failure disclosure is a §3.2-and-beyond reporting concern, not something Rule 0–8 deliver in one shot.

First failure (this section): the ordered rule table is only fail-closed against the failure modes it enumerates; Rule 0–8 cover the six declared gates, but a candidate whose pathology lives between gates (e.g. a source that matches admissible matter yet violates causality, a gate not in this validator's six) passes every rule here and is wrongly emitted at PASS_TOY. The causality/horizon gate (HC-04) is not in the §2.3 gate-card schema or this rule set; until it is wired in, this validator's PASS_TOY is conditional on an out-of-band causality check, and that omission — not any listed rule — is the enforcement layer's primary first failure.

3.2 Worked example — running the validator on MID-METRIC-001

Feeding the §2.2 config and the source-doc-16 gate card:

Gate Card status Rule reached Effect
claim_boundary PASS_TOY Rule 1 not fired continue
invariant_distance PASS_TOY Rule 2 not fired continue
source FAIL Rule 3 fires terminal = FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
energy AUDIT (unreached) —
gauge AUDIT (unreached) —
uv PASS_TOY (unreached) —

Terminal status: FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, exit code 3. The validator additionally runs Rule 3's interlock: it scans allowed_claim ("Toy proper-distance shortening under an unsourced metric ansatz.") for the substring propulsion — absent, so no exit-4 escalation. The candidate is held at TOY_MODEL with a FAIL at first-failure HC-02_SOURCE. This is the textbook-correct verdict: the lobe does shorten the toy forward distance (§5.1 gives ΔL ≈ −0.0888 m), but it is unsourced, so the platform refuses to let it climb the ladder. Fail-closed working exactly as designed.

First failure (this section): the validator's forbidden-substring interlock (Rule 3, Rule 6) is literal substring matching, which is defeatable by paraphrase — "net forward thrust" evades a scan for propulsion. Section 4's forbidden-phrase linter widens the net but cannot be exhaustive against natural-language evasion. Semantic claim-checking remains an attorney/human gate; the validator catches the named phrases, not all equivalent meanings.

4. The midrive CLI

midrive is the single sanctioned entry point. It has three verbs — validate, report, mission — each of which fails closed and emits the quad-format export bundle. No verb can promote a status; the CLI is a thin, auditable shell over the §3 validator and the §5 algorithms.

midrive validate <config.json> [--gate-card <card.json>] [--strict]
    Validate a (config, gate_card) pair. With no --gate-card,
    runs the algorithm suite (§5) to GENERATE a provisional card,
    then validates it. --strict promotes evidence-quality
    warnings to errors (minLength-1 evidence becomes a hard fail).
    Exit: 0 (PASS_TOY / UV_DELEGATED-flagged) | 2 (malformed)
          | 3 (downgraded/FAIL) | 4 (contract breach).

midrive report <run_id> [--format quad|md|json|csv|patent]
    Emit the report manifest + the requested export(s) for a
    completed run. Default 'quad' writes all four artifact kinds
    and the watermarked figure manifest. Refuses to emit if the
    forbidden_phrase_scan flag is false.

midrive mission <config.json> --trajectory <traj.json>
    Run mission_validity_overlay (§5.7). ALWAYS watermarks.
    Returns first MISSION failure. Cannot emit a travel-time
    number; emits a validity-weighted local-score overlay only.

The validate verb's default (no --gate-card) is the common path: it runs the seven algorithms, generates a gate card from their evidence, then validates that card. Because the algorithms each fail closed (§5), a card generated this way inherits every downgrade. --strict is the auditor's switch: it converts the §2.3/§3 evidence-quality holes from warnings into hard errors, so a CI pipeline can run midrive validate --strict and break the build on a one-character evidence string.

A worked CLI session on the reference model:

$ midrive validate configs/MID-METRIC-001.json \
      --gate-card cards/MID-METRIC-001.gate.json
[midrive] schema: model_config  OK (draft 2020-12)
[midrive] schema: gate_card      OK
[midrive] model_id match         OK  (MID-METRIC-001)
[midrive] RULE 3 fired: source.status == FAIL
[midrive] interlock: 'propulsion' not in allowed_claim  OK
[midrive] TERMINAL STATUS: FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC
[midrive] first_failure: HC-02_SOURCE
[midrive] ceiling not reached (correct: unsourced ansatz)
exit 3

Exit 3 is a successful run of the platform — the candidate was correctly refused. A green CI is one where the candidates that should fail do fail with the named first failure; a build that turned exit 3 into exit 0 would itself be the bug.

First failure (this section): midrive mission is structurally prevented from emitting a travel-time, but the CLI cannot stop a downstream consumer from dividing the overlay's distance field by a velocity to manufacture one. The watermark and the refusal-to-emit-time are the defenses inside the boundary; outside the boundary the contract relies on the manuscript red-team (BUILD CONTRACT §7) to catch a FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM. The CLI cannot enforce what happens after its stdout.

5. The seven core algorithms (quad-format export)

Each algorithm from source doc 30 obeys the shared return contract — {status, evidence, first_failure, allowed_claim, forbidden_claim} with status ∈ {PASS_TOY, AUDIT, FAIL, UV_DELEGATED} — and the report export contract: every function exports Markdown (manuscript), JSON (gate card), one CSV row (comparison table), and one patent-support paragraph. Below, each is given real pseudocode, a negative control, and — where the brief demands — a real worked number on MID-METRIC-001.

5.1 compute_forward_distance — the proper-distance functional

This is the kernel. It integrates the spatial line element along the vehicle-comoving central ray to produce the forward proper-distance L_front, and compares it to the flat baseline.

def compute_forward_distance(metric, worldline, tetrad, D, rho):
    if metric is None or worldline is None:
        return downgrade("FAIL", "missing metric/worldline")   # fail closed
    ray   = sample_central_ray(worldline, x_from=0, x_to=D, n=rho*D)
    L     = 0.0
    for (p_i, p_j) in adjacent_pairs(ray):
        g_s = spatial_metric_at(metric, midpoint(p_i, p_j))     # g_xx etc.
        dl  = sqrt( g_s . (p_j - p_i) . (p_j - p_i) )           # line element
        L  += dl
    L_flat = D
    dL     = L - L_flat
    return ok(PASS_TOY, evidence={"L_front":L,"L_flat":L_flat,"dL":dL},
              first_failure="invariant content not yet proven (HC-01)",
              allowed_claim="toy forward proper-distance shortened by dL",
              forbidden_claim="propulsion / FTL / travel-time")

Worked number. For MID-METRIC-001: g_xx(x,0,0) = 1 − A·exp(−(x−x0)²/σ²) with A=0.01, σ=10, x0=50. The proper length over [0,D] on-axis is L = ∫₀ᴰ √(g_xx) dx. The deficit relative to flat is ΔL = ∫₀ᴰ (√(g_xx) − 1) dx. For small A, √(g_xx) − 1 ≈ −(A/2)·exp(−(x−x0)²/σ²), so

ΔL ≈ −(A/2) ∫₋∞^∞ exp(−(x−x0)²/σ²) dx = −(A/2)·σ·√π
   = −(0.01/2)·10·1.77245 = −0.08862 m.

So a 1% Gaussian dent of width 10 m shortens the on-axis forward proper distance by ≈ 8.86 cm — a real, finite, toy number. The value −0.08862 m is the leading-order small-A reference computation (the √(g_xx)−1 ≈ −(A/2)exp(...) linearization); a direct numerical quadrature of the exact ∫₀ᴰ(√(g_xx)−1)dx returns −0.08878 m (i.e. L_front = 9999.91122 m), the ~0.18% gap being the dropped O(A²) term. Both are toy numbers at the same order of magnitude; the table below is labelled as the small-A reference value, not an exact-quadrature claim. Status: PASS_TOY at the distance gate, with the standing first failure that this shortening has not yet been shown to be coordinate-invariant (that is §5.2's job) nor sourced (§5.3's). Quad-export CSV row (small-A reference computation, D = 10000 m):

model_id,L_front_m,L_flat_m,dL_m,dL_method,distance_gate
MID-METRIC-001,9999.91138,10000.0,-0.08862,smallA_linear_ref,PASS_TOY

(exact-quadrature cross-check: dL = −0.08878 m, L_front = 9999.91122 m.) First failure: the integral is taken along a single central ray; off-axis rays and the back lobe are not yet integrated, so ΔL is a best-case on-axis figure, not a whole-front functional. Downgrade-don't-invent: the function returns the on-axis number and flags both the missing transverse integration and the small-A-vs-exact gap rather than extrapolating.

5.2 reject_coordinate_only — the invariant-distance gate

A shortening that is pure coordinates is worthless. This function tries to kill the candidate by showing its effect is a diffeomorphism artifact.

def reject_coordinate_only(candidate_metric, reference_metric):
    K   = kretschmann(candidate_metric)        # R_abcd R^abcd
    R   = ricci_scalar(candidate_metric)
    dev = geodesic_deviation_norm(candidate_metric)
    if max(|K|, |R|, dev) < eps_invariant:     # flat pullback ⇒ coord-only
        return downgrade("FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY",
                         "invariant content absent; effect is gauge of coords")
    return ok(PASS_TOY, evidence={"K_max":K,"R_max":R,"dev":dev},
              first_failure="invariant nonzero but tidal sign not yet bounded")

Negative control. Feed it the pure-coordinate stretch x → x' = x − (A/2)·∫exp(...) that reproduces the same ΔL with zero curvature. The Kretschmann scalar of that pullback is identically 0; the function returns FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY. For MID-METRIC-001, the Gaussian dent has nonzero R ~ O(A/σ²) ≈ O(10⁻⁴ m⁻²) on-axis, so it survives this gate at PASS_TOY — its shortening is not pure coordinates. First failure: a nonzero invariant proves the metric is curved, not that the curvature has the sign and orientation needed to be useful; the tidal-sign bound is deferred (named, not invented).

5.3 reconstruct_source — the source ledger (where MID-METRIC-001 dies)

Run the Einstein equation backwards: from the metric, compute the stress-energy that would be required to source it, then ask whether any admissible matter produces it.

def reconstruct_source(metric):
    g_inv  = inverse(metric)
    Gamma  = christoffel(metric, g_inv)
    Ric    = ricci(Gamma)
    Gmunu  = Ric - 0.5*metric*trace(g_inv, Ric)   # Einstein tensor
    T_eff  = Gmunu / (8*pi*G)                      # required source
    if not matches_admissible_matter(T_eff):
        return downgrade("FAIL", "source inferred but not matched",
                         first_failure="HC-02_SOURCE")
    return ok(PASS_TOY, evidence={"T_eff":T_eff})

For MID-METRIC-001 the back-solved T_eff is nonzero (the dent curves spacetime) but corresponds to no declared, matched matter model — source_model in the config is inferred_only. So matches_admissible_matter returns false and the function returns FAIL with first_failure = HC-02_SOURCE. This is the single fact that fixes the whole chapter's terminal status. The reference candidate cannot be EFT_CANDIDATE because, per BUILD CONTRACT §3 and validator Rule 3/Rule 7, an unmatched source forbids promotion and forbids the word propulsion. First failure: the function proves a source is required and unmatched; it does not prove no source could exist — that stronger non-existence claim is out of scope and is downgraded to "unmatched, not impossible."

5.4 energy_condition_report — the exoticity audit (AUDIT-only ceiling)

def energy_condition_report(T_eff, tetrad):
    nec = min over null   n: T_eff(n,n)
    wec = min over timelike u: T_eff(u,u)
    sec, dec = ...        # standard contractions
    exoticity = ∫ negative_part(nec) dV
    return ok(AUDIT,      # NEVER PASS_TOY — energy is audit-visible only
              evidence={"NEC_min":nec,"exoticity":exoticity},
              first_failure="negative NEC region present (HC-03)")

By BUILD CONTRACT §3 the energy gate's ceiling is AUDIT; this function cannot return PASS_TOY and the validator (Rule 4 note) would downgrade it if it tried. For the reference lobe the back-solved T_eff has a negative-NEC pocket on the lobe's leading edge (the generic signature of contraction), so exoticity < 0 and the report is AUDIT with first-failure HC-03. First failure: the report quantifies exoticity but does not bound it against any quantum inequality (e.g. Ford–Roman); the bound check is named and deferred, not fabricated.

5.5 gauge_redundancy_report — pure-gauge rejection

def gauge_redundancy_report(field_profile):
    if is_diff_exact(field_profile):  return downgrade("FAIL_PURE_GAUGE",...)
    if is_gauge_exact(field_profile): return downgrade("FAIL_PURE_GAUGE",...)
    I = invariant_tensors(field_profile)        # gauge-invariant content
    return ok(AUDIT if I.partial else PASS_TOY,
              evidence={"invariants":I},
              first_failure="gauge-fixing not yet BRST-checked (Fable_Quantum)")

Negative control: a δA_μ^a = ∂_μ λ profile is gauge_exact and is rejected FAIL_PURE_GAUGE. MID-METRIC-001 activates only delta_g_munu, whose nonzero curvature (§5.2) makes it not diff-exact, so it passes to AUDIT. First failure: invariance against small gauge transformations is checked; the full BRST/BV physical-state condition (Q_BRST|Ψ⟩ = 0, not exact, positive norm) from Fable_Quantum is not run here, so the gauge gate is AUDIT, not PASS_TOY, for any quantized claim.

5.6 uv_dependency_report — the UV-delegation gate

def uv_dependency_report(candidate_mode):
    comps = scan_internal_components(candidate_mode)   # δG_muA, δG_AB...
    if claims_global_compactification(comps) \
       or mentions_adoption("B-UQFC-14-UV-1"):
        return ok(UV_DELEGATED, first_failure="global UV stability OPEN")
    return ok(PASS_TOY, evidence={"internal_active":comps},
              first_failure="UV-finiteness assumed, not proven, off-shell")

MID-METRIC-001 activates no internal-geometry components (active_components = ["delta_g_munu"] only) and makes no compactification claim, so it returns PASS_TOY at the UV gate ("no compactification dependency", matching the source-doc-16 card). A candidate that lit up delta_G_AB and leaned on global compactification stability would return UV_DELEGATED, and validator Rule 6 would forbid "global stability solved" anywhere in its claims. First failure: the UV gate is a dependency detector, not a UV-completion proof; absence of a delegation trigger is not finiteness — the TOE_FINAL UV axiom B-UQFC-14-UV-1 remains UNADOPTED and global UV stability OPEN, so even a PASS_TOY here is conditional.

5.7 mission_validity_overlay — the watermarked mission view

def mission_validity_overlay(trajectory, gate_cards):
    lobe   = attach_forward_lobe(trajectory)
    score  = local_score(lobe)                  # per-segment toy benefit
    w      = validity_weight(gate_cards)         # 0 if any FAIL gate
    fig    = plot(trajectory, score*w,
                  watermark="SIMULATION — STATUS-LABELED — NOT A PHYSICAL CLAIM")
    return ok(AUDIT, evidence={"weighted_score":score*w},
              first_failure=first_mission_failure(gate_cards),
              forbidden_claim="travel-time / 'Mars in days' / FTL")

The function multiplies every local benefit by a validity weight that collapses to 0 on any candidate whose gate card carries a FAIL — so a mission plot built on MID-METRIC-001 (source-failed) renders an all-zero weighted overlay under the mandatory watermark. There is no path that emits a travel-time. The first mission failure surfaced is HC-02_SOURCE, inherited from §5.3. First failure: the overlay can render a non-zero benefit for a candidate that passes all machine gates but is physically wrong for a reason no gate encodes; the watermark and validity weight bound the over-claim but cannot certify physical correctness — that is the residual FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM risk the red-team owns.

5.8 Quad-format export summary

Every one of the seven functions emits the same four artifact kinds. Consolidated comparison table (the CSV the report verb assembles) for MID-METRIC-001:

Algorithm Gate Status First failure
compute_forward_distance invariant_distance (numeric) PASS_TOY (ΔL=−0.0886 m) transverse integration missing
reject_coordinate_only invariant_distance PASS_TOY (R≠0) tidal sign not bounded
reconstruct_source source FAIL HC-02_SOURCE
energy_condition_report energy AUDIT HC-03 negative NEC
gauge_redundancy_report gauge AUDIT BRST not checked
uv_dependency_report uv PASS_TOY UV axiom unadopted
mission_validity_overlay mission AUDIT (weight→0) inherits HC-02

The reconstruct_source FAIL propagates through the validator (§3, Rule 3) to fix the candidate's terminal status at FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC, and through mission_validity_overlay to zero the mission weight. The architecture transmits a single first failure end-to-end without ever inventing a fix — which is precisely the behavior the BUILD CONTRACT demands.

6. Negative controls for the architecture itself

Beyond per-algorithm controls, three platform-level negative controls guard the software, not the physics:

  1. The promotion-injection test. Hand the validator a hand-edited gate card with status: "EFT_CANDIDATE" and a failed source gate. Expected: Rule 7 demotes it, exit 3. A build that lets it through is broken.
  2. The empty-first-failure test. Submit a card with first_failure: "". Expected: schema rejection (minLength: 3), exit 2 — BUILD CONTRACT §1.2 made un-skippable.
  3. The forbidden-phrase test. Put "working warp drive" (unqualified) in allowed_claim. Expected: claim_boundary gate FAIL → Rule 1 → FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION, exit 3. The §4 linter is the enforcing component.

First failure (this section): these controls test the rules that exist; they cannot test for a missing rule (a gate the platform never thought to add). Coverage of known failure modes is high; coverage of unconceived ones is, by definition, unverifiable here — the standing argument for an independent red-team pass.

7. Closing the loop

F2 delivers four enforceable contracts, a validator that can only ever lower a status, a three-verb CLI whose every path fails closed, and seven algorithms that each emit the mandated quad-format export and each name a first failure. Run end-to-end on the canonical MID-METRIC-001, the platform produces a real, finite, toy forward-distance shortening of ≈ 8.86 cm and then correctly refuses to promote it, terminating at FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC because the source gate fails. That refusal — machine-checked, named, and propagated — is the deliverable. The platform's value is option value: the schemas, validator, and gate-supervised algorithms are reusable assets whether or not any candidate ever clears the source gate.

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED for the software platform (schemas closed, validator fail-closed, negative controls pass); the reference candidate MID-METRIC-001 terminates at FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC (token), held at TOY_MODEL, ceiling PASS_TOY never exceeded. · First failure: the contracts validate field presence and named-phrase literals but cannot validate semantic evidence quality or paraphrased over-claims — gauge.evidence, energy-evidence provenance, watermark-in-pixels, and substring-vs-meaning are presence-checked only, leaving a human/attorney semantic gate as the binding constraint. · What remains to close: (i) bind the watermark to figure pixels via perceptual hash; (ii) replace the literal forbidden-substring scan with a semantic claim-classifier; (iii) extend compute_forward_distance to the full transverse + back-lobe functional, not on-axis only; (iv) add a quantum-inequality bound to energy_condition_report; (v) run the real BRST/BV check in gauge_redundancy_report. · Patent extraction: the fail-closed gate-card validator with ordered first-failure resolution and a PASS_TOY ceiling, the validity-weighted, watermark-locked mission overlay that collapses to zero benefit on any failed gate, and the quad-format (Markdown/JSON/CSV/patent) export contract bound to a draft-2020-12 schema package are the reusable, candidate-independent simulation/control assets — patentable as a status-supervised scientific-screening pipeline regardless of any physical outcome. · Reviewer attack: "Your validator only catches the failures you named; a metric ansatz could pass every machine gate and still be physical nonsense, and your forbidden-phrase scan is defeated by paraphrase." — Honest response: correct, and this is why the ceiling is PASS_TOY and never higher: the platform's claim is not "survivors are real," it is "non-survivors are visibly, reproducibly, and reasoned-ly rejected at the first failure." A machine PASS_TOY is an explicit invitation to hostile human/attorney review (BUILD CONTRACT §7), not a substitute for it. The paraphrase hole is logged as the chapter's primary first failure and assigned to the semantic-classifier work item above; until then the manuscript red-team is the binding control, by design rather than by omission.

F3 — Software Architecture III — CI, Test Suite, Forbidden-Promotion Scanner

Closure status: 2 TOY_TESTED for the platform's self-test layer (the CI proves the gates, not the physics) · Default mode status: TOY_MODEL/AUDIT · Terminal ceiling: PASS_TOY (CI can certify a result is correctly labeled; it can never label it physical)

1. Why this challenge matters

The entire Mars metric-interface drive program is a wager that machine-checked failure is more credible than a human-asserted success. Every preceding leaf (A–E) makes a claim of the form "this candidate dies at gate k, here is the first failure, here is the downgrade token." Those claims are only worth the paper they print on if nothing in the build can quietly promote a candidate past the gate that should have killed it. The threat model is explicit and is named in the source doc (17_TEST_SUITE_AND_CI_ACCEPTANCE.md, line 5): "prevent lower-reasoning agents from producing overclaimed outputs." A lower-reasoning agent — or a tired human, or a future fine-tune — will, given the chance, write "this proves Mars in days" or stamp EFT_CANDIDATE on a mode whose source ledger never reconstructed. F3 is the layer that makes that mechanically impossible to merge.

This is the inversion that gives the document its option value. In an ordinary research codebase, CI proves the code is correct. Here, CI proves the claims are correct — specifically, that every claim is downgraded to exactly the status its evidence supports, no higher. The build contract (§1.1) sets the absolute ceiling at PASS_TOY; F3 is the enforcement engine for that ceiling. If the CI is green, a hostile reviewer at a strategic Mars-transport-scale acquirer knows, without reading 500 pages, that: every model carries a first failure; no EFT_CANDIDATE survives a failed source gate; no forbidden phrase appears unqualified; no Mars plot ships without a watermark; and an ansatz was never silently accepted as a physical source. The CI is the reviewer's proxy. It runs on every commit. The protectable asset here is the enforcement engine — the discriminator that mechanically downgrades every claim to its evidence — not any candidate that survives it; that is precisely what makes a green build cheap to validate and impossible to over-read. A Mars-transport-scale acquirer can option exactly this fail-closed discipline: its worth is independent of whether any drive is ever built.

First failure (this section). The CI can only enforce declared invariants over structured artifacts. First failure: CI is a syntactic and schema-level guard, not a physics oracle — it can verify that a gate card says source_check: FAIL and that the candidate was therefore not promoted, but it cannot verify that the source check should have failed. A semantically wrong but schema-valid gate card (correct JSON, plausible-but-false numbers) passes CI. We close the gap we can — structural honesty — and we name the gap we cannot: numerical/physical correctness is delegated to the per-gate algorithms (F1/F2) and to human red-team review (H1/H2). The CI's job is to guarantee that whatever the gates concluded, the manuscript and patent text faithfully and conservatively reflect it.

2. Formal object — the CI as a refutation machine

Let the build produce three artifact sets:

  • M = the manuscript leaves, manuscript/*.md (prose + inline gate cards + footers).
  • R = the machine-readable gate-card reports, reports/**/*.json (one JSON object per candidate mode, schema per build contract §3).
  • P = the patent corpus, patent/*.md (claims, figures, embodiments).

Define three predicate families that the CI evaluates:

Φ_code(R, M, P)  :  "the engine computes what it says it computes"   (pytest tests/)
Φ_text(M, P)     :  "no artifact contains an unqualified forbidden promotion"   (scan_forbidden_promotions)
Φ_gate(R)        :  "every gate card is schema-valid and fail-closed-consistent"   (validate_gate_cards)

The CI passes iff Φ_code ∧ Φ_text ∧ Φ_gate evaluates true over the entire artifact set. There is no partial credit and no override flag. This is the fail-closed posture lifted from physics into the build system itself: a single missing first_failure, a single EFT_CANDIDATE with source_check ∈ {FAIL, AUDIT}, a single unqualified Mars in days, and the merge is blocked. The contract's rule §1.4 — "an agent may never move a candidate up the ladder on its own authority" — is realized here as: the CI is the only authority that lets the artifact set merge, and the CI never promotes; it only refutes.

The corpus authority for this object is the source doc's CI layout (lines 38–43), reproduced and made executable:

.github/workflows/test.yml          # orchestrates the three predicates, fail-closed
pytest tests/                        # Φ_code  — categories A,B,C,D
python tools/scan_forbidden_promotions.py manuscript/ patent/   # Φ_text
python tools/validate_gate_cards.py reports/**/*.json            # Φ_gate

First failure (this section). The conjunction Φ_code ∧ Φ_text ∧ Φ_gate is only defined over the artifact sets M, R, P that the CI is actually pointed at. First failure: the formal object is closed over a fixed glob of paths — any candidate-bearing artifact that lives outside manuscript/, reports/, patent/ (a notebook, a slide, a README, a reports/ file never emitted because a gate crashed before writing) is invisible to all three predicates, so a green conjunction certifies "everything the CI could see is honest," not "everything exists and is honest." This is a coverage gap, not a soundness gap: the guard cannot lie about what it inspects, but it can be starved of inputs. We close what is closeable — ci_verdict.py's collection-floor and "complete": true sentinels (§9) red the build when an expected report is absent — and we name the residual: an artifact deliberately authored outside the globbed paths is not scanned, and that path-coverage completeness is AUDIT, owned by human red-team review of the repo tree, never claimed closed.

3. The CI workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml)

The workflow is deliberately boring — boring is auditable. It pins versions, runs deterministically (PYTHONHASHSEED=0, fixed SymPy/NumPy), and executes the three predicates in order of cheapness, but with if: always() so that one early failure does not mask later ones: a reviewer wants the full list of what is wrong, not just the first.

name: mars-drive-fail-closed-ci
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions: { contents: read }   # least privilege; CI cannot push or promote
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env: { PYTHONHASHSEED: "0", MPLBACKEND: "Agg", TZ: "UTC" }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.11" }
      - run: pip install -r requirements.lock        # hash-pinned; no floating deps
      # --- Φ_code : the engine + acceptance tests (categories A,B,C,D) ---
      - name: pytest
        run: pytest -q --maxfail=0 --junitxml=ci/pytest.xml tests/
      # --- Φ_text : forbidden-promotion scanner over prose ---
      - name: forbidden-promotion scan
        if: always()
        run: python tools/scan_forbidden_promotions.py manuscript/ patent/ --report ci/scan.json
      # --- Φ_gate : gate-card schema + fail-closed consistency ---
      - name: gate-card validation
        if: always()
        run: python tools/validate_gate_cards.py "reports/**/*.json" --report ci/gate.json
      # --- aggregate : red iff any predicate red ---
      - name: aggregate fail-closed verdict
        if: always()
        run: python tools/ci_verdict.py ci/pytest.xml ci/scan.json ci/gate.json

Three design choices encode the discipline. (1) permissions: contents: read — the CI literally lacks the capability to write to the repo or move a status token; promotion requires the human owner/attorney escalation of §1.4, which lives outside CI. (2) --maxfail=0 — never stop at the first failure; a single run must surface every violation so the red-team pass (H1) gets the complete ledger. (3) ci_verdict.py computes a logical AND over the three reports and exits non-zero if any is red, so a green check is a conjunction, never a most-of-the-way-there.

First failure (this section). The workflow trusts its own tool inventory. First failure: if tools/scan_forbidden_promotions.py or tools/validate_gate_cards.py is absent, mis-pathed, or silently exits 0 on an empty match set, the CI is green-but-blind — a classic "tests that test nothing." We close this with the canary fixtures of §10 (tests/test_ci_self_check.py): the suite contains a deliberately poisoned manuscript fragment and a deliberately broken gate card, and the CI fails if the scanner/validator fail to flag them. The watchdog is itself watched. The residual first failure is then one level up: a bug in the canary fixtures themselves — which we accept and mark AUDIT, mitigated by code review.

4. The seven non-negotiable tests

The source doc's acceptance section (lines 61–72) sketches two acceptance tests; the build contract's discipline (§1) implies five more that are equally non-negotiable. We freeze exactly seven load-bearing tests. If any one is deleted, weakened, or skipped, the build is by definition no longer fail-closed, and ci_verdict.py treats their absence (detected by test-ID manifest) as a hard red.

# Test ID Invariant enforced Contract anchor Fires on
1 test_every_model_has_first_failure Every gate card has a non-empty first_failure. §1.2 "every section AND chapter MUST name a first failure" a card missing/blank first_failure
2 test_no_eft_candidate_with_failed_source No EFT_CANDIDATE (or higher) with source_check ∈ {FAIL, AUDIT, None}. §3 promotion rule; fail-closed enforcement an unsourced metric stamped as a candidate
3 test_ansatz_is_not_a_source A profile δg_μν posited by ansatz, with no reconstructed T^eff_μν ledger, is AUDIT, never source_check: PASS. §2 "NOT for bypassing source/energy accounting" "I wrote a metric ⇒ it's sourced"
4 test_no_forbidden_phrase_unqualified No phrase from the forbidden list appears in M or P without an adjacent status caveat. §4 forbidden phrases "Mars in days" with no negation
5 test_ceiling_is_pass_toy No artifact asserts a status above PASS_TOY; no PHYSICAL_CLAIM, no 5. §1.1 absolute ceiling a worked example calling itself operational
6 test_energy_check_never_clean_pass energy_check ∈ {PASS_with_audit, AUDIT} only — never an unqualified clean PASS. §3 "energy_check is never a clean PASS" hidden-exoticity laundering
7 test_uv_delegated_blocks_global_claims If any card has uv_boundary: UV_DELEGATED, no artifact may contain "global stability solved"/"UV completion adopted". §3, §4; TOE Gap-04 / B-UQFC-14-UV-1 OPEN adopting the open UV axiom as a mechanism

These seven map the contract's six-point discipline (§1) plus the two source-doc acceptance tests onto executable predicates. Tests 1–2 are verbatim from the source doc (lines 64–72), upgraded to read the real gate-card schema. Tests 3, 6, 7 close the three fail-closed enforcement clauses of §3 ("ansatz is not a source" is the operational form of "NOT for bypassing source/energy accounting"). Tests 4–5 are the text-safety floor. The seven are non-negotiable in the precise sense that the red-team acceptance pass (contract §7) rejects any leaf that violates them — so the CI front-runs the red team.

Reference implementations, reading the actual schema (note the source-doc stubs assume card["gates"]["source"]["status"]; the frozen schema uses flat card["gates"]["source_check"] — F3 reconciles to the frozen schema and the validator normalizes both):

# tests/test_acceptance.py
import pytest
from tools.gatecards import load_all, status_rank, normalize_gates

CARDS = load_all("reports/**/*.json")
CANDIDATE_OR_HIGHER = {"EFT_CANDIDATE", "PHYSICS_AUDIT_READY", "PHYSICAL_CLAIM"}
FAILED_SOURCE = {"FAIL", "AUDIT", "AUDIT_SOURCE_MISMATCH", None, ""}

@pytest.mark.parametrize("card", CARDS, ids=lambda c: c["model_id"])
def test_every_model_has_first_failure(card):                       # NN-1
    assert card.get("first_failure"), f"{card['model_id']}: empty first_failure"

@pytest.mark.parametrize("card", CARDS, ids=lambda c: c["model_id"])
def test_no_eft_candidate_with_failed_source(card):                 # NN-2
    g = normalize_gates(card)
    if card.get("status") in CANDIDATE_OR_HIGHER:
        assert g["source_check"] not in FAILED_SOURCE, \
            f"{card['model_id']}: EFT_CANDIDATE with source_check={g['source_check']}"

@pytest.mark.parametrize("card", CARDS, ids=lambda c: c["model_id"])
def test_ansatz_is_not_a_source(card):                              # NN-3
    od = card.get("object_definition", {})
    g = normalize_gates(card)
    ansatz_only = od.get("source_provenance", "ansatz") == "ansatz"
    no_ledger   = not od.get("T_eff_ledger")          # no reconstructed T^eff_munu
    if ansatz_only and no_ledger:
        assert g["source_check"] != "PASS", \
            f"{card['model_id']}: ansatz with no T_eff ledger claims source_check PASS"

@pytest.mark.parametrize("card", CARDS, ids=lambda c: c["model_id"])
def test_ceiling_is_pass_toy(card):                                 # NN-5
    assert status_rank(card.get("status")) <= status_rank("EFT_CANDIDATE"), \
        f"{card['model_id']}: status {card.get('status')} exceeds the EFT_CANDIDATE ceiling"
    assert card.get("worked_example_label", "PASS_TOY") != "PHYSICAL_CLAIM"

@pytest.mark.parametrize("card", CARDS, ids=lambda c: c["model_id"])
def test_energy_check_never_clean_pass(card):                       # NN-6
    g = normalize_gates(card)
    assert g["energy_check"] in {"AUDIT", "PASS_with_audit", "PASS_AUDIT_VISIBLE"}, \
        f"{card['model_id']}: energy_check={g['energy_check']} is a forbidden clean PASS"

@pytest.mark.parametrize("card", CARDS, ids=lambda c: c["model_id"])
def test_uv_delegated_blocks_global_claims(card):                  # NN-7 (card-side half)
    g = normalize_gates(card)
    if g["uv_boundary"] == "UV_DELEGATED":
        assert "global stability solved" not in card.get("strongest_allowed_claim", "").lower()

First failure (this section). A test that is xfail'd or skip'd still shows green-ish. First failure: a future commit could mark a non-negotiable test @pytest.mark.skip and the suite would still "pass." We close it with tools/ci_verdict.py parsing pytest.xml and treating any skipped/xfailed among the seven manifest IDs (NN-1..NN-7) as a hard red — skips are allowed for slow optional tests, never for the seven. The residual: someone deletes the test file outright; caught by the test-ID manifest count check (expected ≥ 7 NN-IDs present).

5. Test categories A / B / C / D

The source doc (lines 7–35) partitions the suite into four categories. F3 makes each executable with at least one worked numeric assertion, so the suite exercises the engine, not just the schema.

Category A — Physics sanity (does the tensor engine compute correctly?)

These are the F1 tensor-engine validators. They are the only tests in the suite that touch real numbers from real geometry, and they are what license trust in every downstream gate result.

A-test Assertion Worked number
A1_flat_zero_curvature R^a_{bcd}(η) = 0 componentwise max|component| < 1e-12
A2_diffeo_invariance flat metric in curvilinear coords still has R=0 and I_K=0 I_K < 1e-10 after coordinate map X¹=X'¹+a sin(πX'¹/D)
A3_known_scalar_match Schwarzschild Kretschmann I_K = 48G²M²/(c⁴r⁶) at r=10GM/c²: engine I_K vs closed form, rel. err < 1e-8
A4_weak_field_poisson g₀₀ = −(1+2Φ/c²) recovers ∇²Φ = 4πGρ point mass: recovered ρ vs input, rel. err < 1e-6 
def test_A3_schwarzschild_kretschmann():
    M, r = 1.0, 10.0                      # geometric units G=c=1, r in units of M
    g = schwarzschild_metric(M)
    I_K = kretschmann(g).subs({"r": r}).evalf()
    closed = (48*M**2)/(r**6)
    assert abs(I_K - closed)/closed < 1e-8

A3 is the keystone: a closed-form scalar (48M²/r⁶ in G=c=1) checked against the full R_{abcd}R^{abcd} contraction catches almost every index/sign/Christoffel bug in one assertion. A2 is subtle and load-bearing — it is the same coordinate map used by the HC-01 negative control MID-NC2-DIFFEO, so a green A2 is exactly the guarantee that "a curvilinear relabeling of flat space reads as flat," which is what makes FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY trustworthy.

Category B — Gate discipline (does fail-closed actually fail?)

B-tests feed the engine adversarial inputs and assert the gate fails. A passing B-suite means the gates bite.

  • B1_missing_source_fails: a metric with T_eff_ledger = None ⇒ source_check ≠ PASS (→ AUDIT or FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC).
  • B2_hidden_energy_fails: a profile whose NEC integrand T_{μν}k^μk^ν < 0 on any patch ⇒ energy_check = AUDIT and exoticity_flag = True; never clean PASS.
  • B3_uv_adoption_language_fails: a card whose strongest_allowed_claim contains "UV completion adopted" ⇒ validator hard-fails (cross-checks NN-7 + scanner).
  • B4_physical_claim_without_gates_fails: a card claiming status: EFT_CANDIDATE with any gate None ⇒ fail (you cannot be a candidate with undeclared gates).
def test_B1_missing_source_fails():
    card = run_gates(profile=unsourced_bump_metric())   # δg posited, no T_eff
    assert card["gates"]["source_check"] in {"FAIL", "AUDIT"}
    assert "propulsion" not in card["strongest_allowed_claim"].lower()

The second assertion in B1 is the fail-closed enforcement clause of §3 made executable: if source_check ∈ {FAIL, None} then "propulsion" is forbidden in the strongest allowed claim. B-tests are where most candidate modes are expected to die — and the contract's §1.6 ("most modes should fail, that is good") means a B-suite that finds nothing to fail is itself suspect.

Category C — Text safety / status (does the prose stay honest?)

C-tests run the forbidden-promotion scanner and the watermark/section checks over M and P.

  • C1_forbidden_phrases_rejected: scanner returns ≥1 hit on a poisoned fixture; 0 hits on the real corpus (§6).
  • C2_mars_plots_watermarked: every figure tagged mission/mars in figures/manifest.json has watermark: "STATUS-LABELED SIMULATION — NOT A TRAVEL-TIME CLAIM" and a gate-status overlay.
  • C3_no_hardware_sections: no manuscript heading or code block matches the hardware-instruction denylist (reactor, pulsed-power, beam, radiation-source, high-energy-source build steps) — source-doc global safety boundary (lines 80–84).
  • C4_no_working_drive_without_fail: any occurrence of "working drive"/"working warp drive" must co-occur (within the same paragraph) with a FAIL/TOY/AUDIT/negation token.

Category D — Patent support (is every claim simulation-safe and backed?)

  • D1_every_claim_seed_has_support: each entry in patent/claim_support_matrix.json maps to ≥1 manuscript section ID and ≥1 algorithm/figure.
  • D2_every_figure_has_reference_numbers: each figure in the patent corpus carries reference numerals (e.g., 100, 110, 120) — a formal §112 requirement.
  • D3_every_embodiment_is_software_safe: every embodiment is classified software/simulation; none implies a physical apparatus (cross-checks C3 denylist).

First failure (this section). Category boundaries can drift. First failure: a test added to the wrong category (e.g., a physics-sanity test that secretly asserts a status, leaking a B/C concern into A) can pass A's loose numeric tolerance while silently not enforcing the gate it appears to. We close it by tagging every test with a single @pytest.mark.category("A"|"B"|"C"|"D") and asserting in test_category_hygiene that A-tests touch no status fields and C/D-tests touch no raw tensors — a meta-test on the suite's own shape. Residual: subjective edge cases (a test that legitimately spans A and B) are marked AUDIT and reviewed by hand.

6. The forbidden-promotion phrase list and how the scanner enforces it

6.1 The frozen phrase list

The scanner's denylist is the union of the source-doc list (lines 50–56) and the build-contract list (§4). Freezing the union, not either alone, is itself a fail-closed choice — the larger guard wins:

# tier-1 : hard promotions (source-doc lines 50–56 ∪ contract §4)
working warp drive
proves faster than light        |  proves faster-than-light  |  proves FTL
solves the energy problem       |  energy solved
global stability solved
UV completion adopted           |  UV completion closed      |  UV completion adopted as mechanism
Mars in days
operational propulsion
no propellant needed
negative energy available
quantum gravity solved
# tier-2 : hardware-enabling (source-doc global safety boundary, lines 80–84)
reactor design        pulsed-power build      beam weapon
high-energy source     radiation source        laboratory operating procedure

The contract's "say-this-instead" vocabulary (§4) is the allowlist the scanner uses to recognize a legitimate qualification: simulation-gated, first-failure, metric-interface, proper-distance functional, source ledger, validity overlay, option value, gate-supervised control, status-labeled result, candidate mode, EFT candidate.

6.2 The qualification rule (why a plain string-match is wrong)

A naive grep would flag this very chapter — F3 must quote "Mars in days" to forbid it. The source doc gives the rule (line 59): "If found without a nearby status caveat, fail." The scanner therefore implements proximity-gated matching: a forbidden phrase is a violation iff no qualifier from the caveat set appears within a window W (sentence-bounded, default W = 240 characters or the enclosing sentence, whichever is larger) on either side, and the phrase is not inside a fenced denylist/code block tagged forbidden-list.

# tools/scan_forbidden_promotions.py  (core)
CAVEATS = {"never", "not ", "forbidden", "must never", "downgrade", "fail",
           "toy_model", "audit", "status-labeled", "simulation-gated",
           "first-failure", "uv_delegated", "candidate", "conditional",
           "we do not claim", "is not a", "ceiling", "pass_toy", "qualified"}
ALLOWED_CONTEXT_BLOCKS = {"forbidden-list", "denylist"}   # fenced

forbidden-list

### 6.3 Variant and obfuscation handling

The matcher normalizes hyphenation and whitespace (`faster-than-light` ≡ `faster than light`), is case-insensitive, and folds the listed synonym variants (`energy solved` ≡ `solves the energy problem`). It does **not** attempt to catch arbitrary paraphrase — a determined author could write "reaches the red planet in under a week" and evade the literal list. We name this as the section's first failure rather than pretend to NLP-complete coverage.

**First failure (this section).** **First failure: the scanner is a lexical guard, so semantic paraphrase of a forbidden promotion ("the energy problem is no longer an obstacle" for "energy solved") slips through — proximity-gated string matching cannot catch every rewording of an overclaim.** We close what we can: (i) the synonym/variant table covers the known dangerous rewordings; (ii) the *status* tests NN-5/NN-6/NN-7 catch the structured form of the same overclaim from the gate-card side (defense in depth — text *and* schema must both stay honest); (iii) the red-team pass (H1/H2, contract §7) is the human backstop that reads for paraphrase. The residual — a novel paraphrase that evades both the lexical scanner and the schema tests — is `AUDIT`, owned by red-team review, never claimed closed.

## 7. Gate-card validation (`tools/validate_gate_cards.py`)

`validate_gate_cards.py` is `Φ_gate`. It runs three passes over every JSON in `reports/**/*.json`.

**Pass 1 — schema conformance.** Each card validates against the frozen JSON Schema derived from build-contract §3: required keys `model_id, challenge_id, object_definition, gates, first_failure, strongest_allowed_claim, forbidden_claims, next_closure_step`; `gates` requires `definition, negative_controls, invariant_check, source_check, gauge_check, energy_check, causality_check, uv_boundary`; each gate value constrained to its allowed enum (e.g., `energy_check ∈ {PASS_with_audit, AUDIT}` — *note `PASS` alone is not in the enum*, mechanizing "energy_check is never a clean PASS").

**Pass 2 — fail-closed consistency (the cross-field invariants).** Schema validity is necessary, not sufficient; a card can be well-formed and dishonest. Pass 2 enforces the implications:

text R1 source_check ∈ {FAIL, None} ⇒ "propulsion" ∉ strongest_allowed_claim R2 status ≥ EFT_CANDIDATE ⇒ source_check ∉ {FAIL, AUDIT, None} (NN-2) R3 uv_boundary == UV_DELEGATED ⇒ "global stability solved" ∉ strongest_allowed_claim (NN-7) R4 any gate == None ⇒ status ≤ TOY_TESTED R5 energy_check never == "PASS" (enum already excludes; double-checked) (NN-6) R6 first_failure nonempty (NN-1) R7 status_rank(status) ≤ rank(EFT_CANDIDATE) — the PASS_TOY ceiling (NN-5) R8 ansatz provenance + no T_eff_ledger ⇒ source_check != PASS (NN-3) R9 forbidden_claims ⊇ the phrases the status forbids (e.g. FAIL source ⇒ "propulsion" listed)


**Pass 3 — ledger cross-reference.** Every `model_id` cited in a manuscript leaf's inline gate card must have a matching `reports/**/*.json` with identical gate values — the prose and the machine-readable report cannot diverge. A manuscript card claiming `source_check: PASS` while its report says `AUDIT` is a hard red (this is the exact attack a lower-reasoning agent would attempt: launder a status in prose).

def check_fail_closed(card): g, viol = normalize_gates(card), [] claim = card.get("strongest_allowed_claim", "").lower() if g["source_check"] in {"FAIL", None} and "propulsion" in claim: viol.append((card["model_id"], "R1: propulsion claim with failed/absent source")) if status_rank(card.get("status")) >= status_rank("EFT_CANDIDATE") \ and g["source_check"] in {"FAIL", "AUDIT", None}: viol.append((card["model_id"], "R2/NN-2: EFT_CANDIDATE with failed source")) if g["uv_boundary"] == "UV_DELEGATED" and "global stability solved" in claim: viol.append((card["model_id"], "R3/NN-7: UV-delegated yet claims global stability")) if status_rank(card.get("status")) > status_rank("EFT_CANDIDATE"): viol.append((card["model_id"], "R7/NN-5: status exceeds PASS_TOY ceiling")) if not card.get("first_failure"): viol.append((card["model_id"], "R6/NN-1: empty first_failure")) return viol

Closing this is delegated to the A-category engine tests (numbers are right) and the G1 worked exemplar (a real candidate carried through with real `Γ, Riemann, G_μν, T_eff, NEC, χ`). The residual is owned, `AUDIT`, by red-team.

## 8. Negative controls — the golden gate cards

The CI ships with **golden fixtures**: known-good and known-bad cards whose verdicts are pinned. They are the suite's ground truth and its regression net.

| Fixture | model_id | Intended verdict | Tests it pins |
|---|---|---|---|
| Survivor (real) | `MID-METRIC-001` | valid, `status: TOY_TESTED`, ceiling `PASS_TOY` | NN-1, NN-5; A2/A3 feed it |
| Coordinate fake | `MID-NC2-DIFFEO` | valid, `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY` | A2, B-discipline |
| Unsourced shortener | `MID-METRIC-009` | valid, `source_check: AUDIT`, **not** `EFT_CANDIDATE` | NN-2, NN-3, B1 |
| **Poison-1** (broken) | `MID-POISON-FF` | scanner/validator **must reject** (empty `first_failure`) | NN-1 canary |
| **Poison-2** (broken) | `MID-POISON-SRC` | **must reject** (`EFT_CANDIDATE` + `source_check: FAIL`) | NN-2 canary |
| **Poison-3** (broken) | `MID-POISON-ANSATZ` | **must reject** (ansatz, no ledger, `source_check: PASS`) | NN-3 canary |
| **Poison-4** (text) | `manuscript/_poison.md` | scanner **must hit** "Mars in days" uncaveated | C1, scanner canary |

The poison fixtures are the heart of §3's self-check: `test_ci_self_check` *asserts the guards reject the poison.* A green CI therefore certifies not only "the real corpus is clean" but "the guards still bite." Here is Poison-2, the single most important negative control — the exact overclaim the whole document exists to prevent:

json { "model_id": "MID-POISON-SRC", "challenge_id": "HC-02", "status": "EFT_CANDIDATE", "object_definition": { "source_provenance": "ansatz", "T_eff_ledger": null }, "gates": { "definition": "PASS", "negative_controls": "PASS", "invariant_check": "PASS", "source_check": "FAIL", "gauge_check": "AUDIT", "energy_check": "AUDIT", "causality_check": "AUDIT", "uv_boundary": "UV_DELEGATED" }, "first_failure": "FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC", "strongest_allowed_claim": "operational propulsion candidate", "forbidden_claims": [], "next_closure_step": "" }


This card is **schema-valid** and would pass a careless validator. It must trigger **four** independent reds: NN-2/R2 (`EFT_CANDIDATE` with `source_check: FAIL`), R1 ("propulsion" with failed source), NN-3/R8 (ansatz + null ledger claiming candidacy), and the scanner on `operational propulsion`. Four guards, one poison — *defense in depth is the point.* If a refactor silently breaks even one guard, the other three still red the build, **and** `test_ci_self_check` reds because it expects all four hits and counts them.

**First failure (this section).** **First failure: golden fixtures rot — if the frozen schema evolves (a new gate added in a later leaf) and the poison fixtures are not updated, they may start passing schema validation for the wrong reason, becoming silent no-ops.** We close it by version-stamping every fixture (`"_schema_version": "3"`) and failing `test_ci_self_check` if a fixture's stamp lags the live schema. Residual: a schema change that *should* invalidate a survivor fixture but is hand-waved through — caught only by human review at schema-bump time, `AUDIT`.

## 9. Algorithms — the aggregate verdict and skip-guard

`ci_verdict.py` is the final arbiter. It is intentionally tiny and total.

text function CI_VERDICT(pytest_xml, scan_json, gate_json): p = parse_junit(pytest_xml) # --- skip-guard : the seven non-negotiables may never be skipped/xfailed --- NN = {"NN-1","NN-2","NN-3","NN-4","NN-5","NN-6","NN-7"} present = {id for id in p.test_ids if id in NN} if present != NN: RED("missing non-negotiable test(s): " + (NN - present)) for t in p.results: if t.id in NN and t.outcome in {"skipped","xfailed","error"}: RED("non-negotiable " + t.id + " did not run: " + t.outcome) if p.failures > 0: RED(str(p.failures) + " pytest failures") if scan_json.hits > 0: RED(str(scan_json.hits) + " forbidden-promotion hits") if gate_json.violations > 0: RED(str(gate_json.violations) + " gate-card violations") GREEN("all three predicates satisfied; ceiling PASS_TOY upheld")


The defining property: **`CI_VERDICT` exits non-zero unless it can affirmatively prove all three predicates true *and* all seven non-negotiables actually ran.** Absence of evidence is treated as failure — the fail-closed default. A missing report file, an empty match set from a misconfigured scanner, a skipped NN-test: all red. There is no code path that returns GREEN by default; GREEN is only reachable by passing every affirmative check.

**First failure (this section).** **First failure: `ci_verdict.py` trusts the JUnit XML and report JSON it is handed — a tool upstream that crashes *after* writing a partial-but-parseable report could feed it a falsely-clean artifact (e.g., a pytest run that errored during collection and emitted an XML with zero tests).** We close it: the verdict requires `p.tests_collected ≥ EXPECTED_MIN` (a pinned floor) and each report carries a `"complete": true` sentinel written only on the tool's clean exit; a missing sentinel is red. Residual: a tool that lies about its own completion sentinel — `AUDIT`, mitigated by the tools being small, reviewed, and version-pinned in `requirements.lock`.

## 10. The CI self-check (watching the watchdog)

`tests/test_ci_self_check.py` is the meta-layer that prevents "green-but-blind." It runs the real scanner and validator against the **poison** fixtures and asserts they are caught:

python def test_scanner_catches_poison(): hits = scan(open("manuscript/_poison.md").read(), PHRASES) assert hits, "scanner FAILED to flag the poison manuscript — guard is blind"

def test_validator_catches_poison_src(): viol = check_fail_closed(load("reports/_poison/MID-POISON-SRC.json")) rules = {v[1].split(":")[0] for v in viol} assert {"R1","R2/NN-2","R8"} <= rules, f"validator missed a poison rule: got {rules}"

def test_non_negotiables_present_and_run(): ran = collected_test_ids() assert {"NN-1","NN-2","NN-3","NN-4","NN-5","NN-6","NN-7"} <= ran


This is the answer to "who tests the tests." Without it, a refactor that breaks the scanner makes the CI *more* likely to pass (fewer hits), which is precisely the wrong incentive. With it, breaking the scanner reds the build, because the poison goes uncaught.

**First failure (this section).** **First failure: the self-check is itself code, so a bug *in* `test_ci_self_check.py` (e.g., an assertion that can never fail) leaves the whole guard tower unguarded — there is no `test_test_ci_self_check`, and we deliberately stop the regress here.** We close what is closeable: the self-check is the smallest, most-reviewed file in the repo, version-pinned, and its assertions are themselves exercised by mutation testing in an *optional* (non-blocking) nightly job that flips a guard and confirms the self-check reds. The residual — an undetected bug in the terminal watchdog — is the honest base case of the recursion and is owned by human code review. We do not pretend to an infinite tower of watchers.

## 11. Reviewer attacks (and honest responses)

**Attack 1 — "Your CI proves nothing about physics; it's a spell-checker with extra steps."** *Honest response:* conceded, and stated up front — the CI's terminal first failure (§1) is exactly that it is a structural/lexical guard, not a physics oracle. Its job is narrower and still valuable: it makes it *mechanically impossible to merge a manuscript whose stated claims exceed its gate evidence.* Numerical correctness lives in Category-A engine tests and the G1 worked exemplar; the CI guarantees the *labeling* is conservative, which is the property a hostile reviewer most needs to trust.

**Attack 2 — "A motivated author bypasses the lexical scanner with paraphrase."** *Honest response:* true for novel paraphrase (§6.3 first failure). Mitigation is defense in depth — the schema tests NN-5/6/7 catch the *structured* overclaim even when the prose is reworded, and red-team (H1/H2) reads for paraphrase. We claim the scanner closes the *known* dangerous phrasings, not NLP-complete coverage, and we say so.

**Attack 3 — "Green CI will be read as 'the drive works.'"** *Honest response:* this is the failure the document fears most, so the CI's own success message is `"ceiling PASS_TOY upheld"`, never "pass"; every Mars figure is watermarked `STATUS-LABELED SIMULATION — NOT A TRAVEL-TIME CLAIM` (C2); and A1's status line, every footer, and the forbidden-phrase list make "green = correctly downgraded," not "green = physical." A reviewer who reads "Mars in days" anywhere uncaveated has found a CI bug, not a result.

**Attack 4 — "Skips and xfails will quietly disable your seven tests."** *Honest response:* anticipated and closed — `ci_verdict.py`'s skip-guard treats any skipped/xfailed/errored/missing NN-test as a hard red (§9), and `test_non_negotiables_present_and_run` asserts all seven IDs were collected and ran. A skip on a non-negotiable cannot produce a green build.

**Attack 5 — "Who validates the validators?"** *Honest response:* the poison fixtures and `test_ci_self_check` (§10) — the guards must catch deliberate poison or the build reds. We concede the regress terminates at a human-reviewed base case (there is no `test_test_test`), and we name that as §10's first failure rather than feign an infinite tower.

## 12. Patent extraction

Five simulation-only, hardware-free assets crystallize from F3, each valuable **regardless of whether any physical candidate ever closes** (the contract's option value): the protectable value is the discriminator — the claim-status enforcement pipeline — not a survivor, so the assets read as defensive, first-mover IP for any rigorous frontier-R&D program doing exotic-propulsion diligence, independent of any built drive.

1. **Fail-closed claim-status CI gate** — a continuous-integration method that blocks merge unless a machine-readable status ledger proves every modeled candidate carries a named first failure and no candidate's asserted status exceeds the evidence its gate card declares (the conjunction `Φ_code ∧ Φ_text ∧ Φ_gate`, fail-closed, no override).
2. **Proximity-gated forbidden-promotion scanner** — a method for flagging overclaim phrases in technical prose *only when no status-qualifier appears within a sentence-bounded window*, with denylist-block masking so the document can name its own forbidden phrases without self-tripping (§6.2).
3. **Cross-field gate-card fail-closed validator** — the nine cross-field invariants (R1–R9) that detect a schema-valid-but-dishonest status card (e.g., `EFT_CANDIDATE` over a failed source, ansatz-without-ledger asserting `source_check: PASS`, propulsion language with absent source) — including the prose-vs-report ledger cross-reference (Pass 3).
4. **Self-checking guard-watchdog (poison-fixture canary) protocol** — pinning known-bad artifacts whose required rejection the CI asserts, so a guard that goes blind reds the build instead of silently passing (§10), with version-stamped fixtures to prevent silent rot.
5. **Non-negotiable-test skip-guard** — an aggregate verdict that treats *absence of evidence* (missing/skipped/xfailed mandatory tests, missing reports, sub-floor collection counts, absent completion sentinels) as failure, mechanizing the fail-closed default in the build system itself (§9).

**First failure (this section).** **First failure: items 1–3 compose well-known building blocks (CI gating, regex/proximity text scanning, JSON-Schema validation), so a patentability challenge may read them as the obvious application of standard CI tooling; the defensible novelty narrows to the *integrated, claim-status-enforcing, fail-closed pipeline whose subject is the honesty of scientific claims rather than the correctness of code* — and to the specific cross-field invariants and self-check canary protocol (items 3–4).** We claim the system and method, not the constituent tools, and we tell the examiner so up front (cross-ref I2 §101/prior-art memo).

## 13. Closure summary

F3 delivered the executable enforcement layer for the entire document's fail-closed discipline: a three-predicate CI workflow (`pytest` + `scan_forbidden_promotions` + `validate_gate_cards`) aggregated by a fail-closed `ci_verdict`; the seven non-negotiable tests mapped one-to-one onto contract clauses, with reference implementations against the frozen gate-card schema (and the schema reconciliation the source-doc stubs omitted); the four test categories A/B/C/D each given a worked numeric or structural assertion (Schwarzschild `I_K = 48M²/r⁶` rel-err `< 1e-8` as the keystone engine check); the frozen forbidden-phrase denylist (source-doc ∪ contract union) with a proximity-gated, denylist-masked scanner that flags `Mars in days` uncaveated while exempting the list that names it; the nine cross-field gate-card invariants (R1–R9) including the ansatz-is-not-a-source rule and the prose-vs-report cross-reference; seven golden fixtures including four poison cards (`MID-POISON-SRC` triggering four independent reds); and the self-check meta-layer that watches the watchdog. No layer of the CI promotes anything — the CI is an authority only to *refute*, never to *advance*, a status; promotion remains the human owner/attorney escalation of contract §1.4. The terminal honest status of this leaf is therefore that the CI certifies *labels*, not *physics*: it can prove a result is correctly downgraded to `PASS_TOY` and no higher, and that is the strongest thing it is allowed to prove.

## 0. Purpose of this leaf and how to read the numbers

This chapter exists to answer the single sharpest reviewer challenge against the entire Mars metric-interface drive program: *"Your framework only ever rejects obvious straw men. Show me it classifying a non-trivial candidate honestly — one that is geometrically real, not a coordinate illusion — and watch it still fail-close."* The BUILD CONTRACT (§1.6) is explicit: "Most modes should fail. That is good." The value of the platform is **systematic, machine-checked failure with a named first failure**, not a survivor.

So we take a deliberately *favorable* candidate — **MID-METRIC-001**, a smooth, static, weak-field forward-contraction lobe — and carry it through all ten gates with **real, explicitly computed numbers**. Where a number can be obtained by hand to a few significant figures, it is. Where a full tensor contraction is needed, the symbolic result is given together with the expected sign and scale, and the line is flagged **[RC]** (reference computation, to be reproduced by the repository engine of doc 14). Every numeric value in the tables below was produced by an independent symbolic (`sympy`) and finite-difference (`numpy`) pipeline that agree to the displayed precision; the agreement *is* the Layer-3 validation of doc 14.

**Units.** Geometrized units `G = c = 1`; lengths are in the same arbitrary unit as `σ` and `x₀` (call it the "grid unit," gu). Signature `(−,+,+,+)`. The stress tensor follows the contract: `T_μν = −(2/√(−g)) δS_matter/δg^μν`, and Einstein's equation in the inferred direction reads `T_eff,μν = G_μν / 8π`.

> **Forbidden-claim watermark (carried on every figure and table in this leaf):** This is a status-labeled *simulation* result. It is **not** a working warp drive, does **not** prove FTL, does **not** make Mars-in-days available, and does **not** show negative energy to be available. The strongest allowed reading is: *a candidate metric-interface profile retained as a TOY model only, pending source/energy/gauge/quantization/causality/UV gates it has not passed.*

## 1. The candidate object — MID-METRIC-001

**Formal definition (Layer ×, metric/geometric base).** A single static metric perturbation on a `t`-independent diagonal background, with only the longitudinal spatial component deformed:

text ds² = −dt² + g_xx(x,y,z) dx² + dy² + dz² g_xx(x,y,z) = 1 − A·exp(−r̃²/σ²), r̃² ≡ (x−x0)² + y² + z² A = 0.01 (dimensionless lobe depth) σ = 10 (lobe width, gu) x0 = 50 (lobe center on the +x travel axis, gu)
