## H1.0 — Why this chapter exists (the adversarial spine)

Every other chapter in this document defends a *piece* of the metric-interface drive screening platform. This chapter does the opposite: it is the place where the document attacks itself, harder than any external reviewer is expected to, and records exactly where each candidate dies. Per the BUILD CONTRACT §1.6 — *"Most modes should fail. That is good."* — the value of this chapter is not a survivor. The value is a **machine-checkable, reproducible map of failure**: for each of the 100 banked reviewer objections, the strongest form of the attack and the honest response (defense *or* concession); and for each candidate excitation mode, the **earliest gate at which it fails**, ranked by gate ordinal rather than by how impressive the best-looking result was.

We adopt two disciplines from source doc `20_DEEP_RED_TEAM_AND_FIRST_FAILURE_MATRIX.md`:

1. **The "Lower-reasoning agent prompt":** *"Create a first-failure ledger for every candidate mode. Do not rank by visual appeal. Rank by earliest gate failure and by what remains patentable after failure."* This is the literal mandate for §H1.4.
2. **The rule from `34_REVIEWER_OBJECTION_BANK_100.md`:** *"A good response is not always a defense. Often the correct answer is: 'Yes, that is the first failure; here is the downgrade and the next closure computation.'"*

The object under attack is the excitation profile

Ξ_drive(t,x) = { δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge data }


evaluated against the forward proper-distance functional

D_fwd[Ξ] = ∫_γ √( g_ij(Ξ) dx^i dx^j ) along the comoving forward geodesic segment γ,


with the success question being whether a vehicle-comoving, front/back-asymmetric `Ξ` reduces `D_fwd` **through the forward lobe** while passing the gate stack. The gate stack — the spine of all ranking in this chapter — is fixed by the contract §3 gate-card schema and ordered by *when in a real review it kills you*:

| Ordinal | Gate token | What it checks | Fail token (downgrade tree) |
|---:|---|---|---|
| G0 | `definition` | object is defined: equations, coords, active fields, layer map | (rejected as `0 UNDEFINED`) |
| G1 | `negative_controls` | toy passes its own null/sham controls | `FAIL_NEGCTRL` |
| G2 | `invariant_check` | effect survives coordinate change (scalar/curvature invariants move) | `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY` |
| G3 | `source_check` | `T_μν` exists and is shared/visible, no double-count | `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC` |
| G4 | `energy_check` | exoticity quantified; NEC/WEC accounting visible | `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` (never clean PASS — "pass/audit-visible") |
| G5 | `gauge_check` | effect is not pure gauge / pure diffeo | `FAIL_PURE_GAUGE` |
| G6 | `causality_check` | no CTC, cone/horizon diagnostics clean | `FAIL_CAUSALITY` |
| G7 | quantization (BRST) | `Q_BRST|Ψ⟩=0`, not exact, positive norm | `AUDIT_QUANTUM` |
| G8 | `uv_boundary` | EFT admissibility `χ<1`; global UV not required | `UV_DELEGATED` / `FAIL` |

**Ordering rationale (this is load-bearing for §H1.4):** the gates are *not* independent difficulties of equal weight; they are a sieve. A mode that is pure coordinates (fails G2) never even reaches the source question; a mode with no source (fails G3) makes the energy question moot. So "earliest gate failure" is a genuine total order on badness: **smaller ordinal = deader, sooner, more cheaply.** That is the ranking key the source doc demands ("not by visual appeal").

**First failure of this section (H1.0):** the gate *ordering itself* is a modeling choice, not a theorem. A reviewer can argue G4 (energy) should precede G3 (source), or that G2 and G5 are entangled (a coordinate artifact and a pure-gauge artifact can be the same pathology in linearized GR). We concede this and freeze the ordering as a **declared convention** (contract §3 gate-card field order), used consistently, not as a claim about nature.

## H1.1 — From 100 objections to 10 themes

The objection bank (`34_*`) is, by construction, 100 rows cycling through **ten categories** in a fixed period-10 pattern:

position p (1..100): category = CYCLE[(p-1) mod 10] CYCLE = [physics, numerics, QFT, relativity, patent, investor, safety, narrative, software, mission]


So there are exactly ten objection *families*, each instantiated ten times (physics at rows 1,11,21,…,91; numerics at 2,12,…,92; etc.). Every row carries the same skeletal objection — *"the project overclaims or under-specifies a `<category>` dependency"* — and the same required answer — *"identify first failure, downgrade status, preserve patent fallback."* The bank is therefore a **template generator**, not ten-times-ten distinct critiques. The honest move (downgrade-don't-invent, contract §1.3) is to treat each family as **one cluster** and give it (a) the *strongest concrete instantiation* the family can take against this specific platform, (b) the honest response, and (c) the residue: what status survives and what stays patentable.

We refuse to pad ten near-identical sub-objections per family into the manuscript; that would violate "density over repetition" (contract §6). Instead each cluster below gets the strongest single attack, then a short table of the *distinct attack vectors* within the family (the meaningful axes the ten instances can vary along).

### Theme map (the attack matrix at a glance)

| Cluster | Category | Strongest attack (one line) | Earliest gate it bites | Honest verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | physics | "It's a coordinate/gauge mirage with no source — Alcubierre redux." | G2 / G3 | Concede for most modes; defend gate machinery |
| C2 | numerics | "Your 'effect' is discretization error / not convergent / not seed-stable." | G1 | Defend with convergence + null controls; concede tolerance dependence |
| C3 | QFT | "BRST/ghost/positivity is hand-waved; interacting sector is undefined." | G7 | Concede: interacting sector stays `AUDIT_QUANTUM` |
| C4 | relativity | "Reduced `D_fwd` violates NEC/causality or hides a horizon/CTC." | G4 / G6 | Concede exoticity is the wall; defend diagnostics |
| C5 | patent | "Claims read on prior art (Alcubierre/White); or claim a perpetuum mobile." | — (claim-scope) | Defend: claims are simulation/control assets, not a drive |
| C6 | investor | "This is an FTL pitch dressed as software; TRL ≈ 1; no path to revenue." | — (narrative-scope) | Concede no drive; defend option value of the tooling |
| C7 | safety | "You're one prompt from a high-energy/exotic-source build sheet." | — (scope-boundary) | Defend hard: fail-closed scope wall is explicit |
| C8 | narrative | "The Mars framing is marketing; the demo overclaims travel time." | G_mission overlay | Concede framing risk; defend watermark/overlay rule |

## H1.2 — The four physics-grade clusters (C1–C4): strongest form + honest response

These four are where a competent GR/EFT/QFT reviewer actually kills the document. They map onto the gate stack directly.

### C1 — Physics: "It is coordinates / it has no source" (G2, G3)

**Strongest form.** *"Take any target reduced `D_fwd`. You can always write a coordinate system in which the spatial metric looks compressed along the forward lobe without changing one physical invariant. This is exactly the Alcubierre move: a metric that 'works' on paper because the line element was reverse-engineered from the desired worldline, with the stress tensor `T_μν = (M_Pl²/8π) G_μν[g]` read off afterward and found to be whatever it has to be — including manifestly exotic. Your `Ξ_drive` is the same sleight: choose the geometry you want, then call the back-computed source a 'candidate.' The proper-distance reduction is not physics; it's a choice of ruler."*

This is the single most dangerous objection in the bank and we treat it as such.

**Honest response (defense of method, concession on most modes).** The platform does not get to *assert* the source; it must *exhibit* it and pass two gates the Alcubierre construction fails by design:

- **G2 invariant_check.** A coordinate-only mode is detected by computing diffeomorphism-invariant scalars and checking they are unchanged by the excitation:

text procedure invariant_gate(Ξ, ε): base = solve_metric(Ξ = 0) pert = solve_metric(Ξ) for I in [ R, R_μν R^μν, R_μνρσ R^μνρσ (Kretschmann), C_μνρσ C^μνρσ (Weyl) ]: ΔI = sup_x | Ipert - Ibase | if ΔI < ε * scale(I): # invariant did not move return FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY # also: re-evaluate D_fwd in ≥2 independent charts; require agreement if spread_over_charts(D_fwd) > ε_chart: return FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY return PASS

  A pure coordinate compression moves no invariant ⇒ `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY`. **This is the correct, contract-mandated answer, and we expect most naive modes to die here.**

- **G3 source_check.** Reading off `T_μν = (M_Pl²/8π)G_μν` is *allowed* but is then audited for (i) existence of a *declared* field content in `L_matter` that produces it (no anonymous "effective" source), (ii) shared/visible coupling in the single Einstein-frame metric (Fable_Forces: no double counting), and (iii) the energy ledger of G4. An unsourced or back-computed-only metric is `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC`.

**Concession.** For the *honest physics* of it: even modes that survive G2 (a real invariant moves) overwhelmingly fail G3/G4 — the source needed to bend the forward lobe the right way is exotic. We do **not** claim to have escaped the Alcubierre energy problem. We claim only to have built the apparatus that *catches* the mirage automatically and labels it, instead of presenting it as a result. **Forbidden here:** "no propellant needed", "negative energy available" — neither appears as a closed claim.

**Distinct vectors inside the physics family:**

| Vector | Sharpest instantiation | First failure |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinate mirage | reverse-engineered line element | G2 `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY` |
| Unsourced metric | `T_μν` back-read, no `L_matter` field | G3 `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC` |
| Double-counted source | excitation coupled in two frames | G3 (no-double-count) |
| Linearization abuse | `δg` large where treated as small | G8 `χ_grad ≥ 1` |

**First failure (C1):** for the modal mode, **G2 (coordinate-only)**; for the survivors, **G3 (unsourced)**.

### C2 — Numerics: "The effect is discretization error" (G1)

**Strongest form.** *"Your reduced `D_fwd` is at the 10⁻³ level. So is your grid truncation error. You have not shown the effect is not a refinement artifact, a boundary-reflection artifact, an integrator-order artifact, or a lucky random seed. Run it at 2×, 4× resolution and the 'lobe' will wander or vanish."*

**Honest response (defense).** This is exactly what G1 negative controls exist for, and the platform must publish:

- **Convergence (Richardson).** With grid spacings `h, h/2, h/4`, estimate observed order `p` and the Richardson-extrapolated effect:

p = log2( |D(h) - D(h/2)| / |D(h/2) - D(h/4)| ) D∞ ≈ D(h/4) + ( D(h/4) - D(h/2) ) / (2^p - 1)

  Require the *measured* effect `|D∞ - D_base|` to exceed `K · E_trunc(h/4)` with safety factor `K ≥ 10`. If the effect is within the error band ⇒ `FAIL_NEGCTRL`.
- **Sham/null controls.** (i) `Ξ=0` must return `ΔD_fwd = 0` to round-off. (ii) A *symmetric* (non-asymmetric) `Ξ_sham` must return no net forward bias. (iii) Seed sweep: ≥32 seeds; report mean ± CI; an effect inside its own CI ⇒ `FAIL_NEGCTRL`.
- **Determinism.** Same inputs → bit-identical outputs (logged hash), so "lucky seed" is auditable, not deniable.

**Concession.** The effect size's *significance* is tolerance-dependent: choose `ε` and `K` loosely and toys "pass"; tighten them and they fail. We therefore freeze `ε, K` as declared audit constants and report the pass/fail as a function of them, not as an absolute. **No worked toy is promoted above `PASS_TOY` on numerical grounds.**

**First failure (C2):** **G1 (negative_controls)** — the earliest possible gate, and the cheapest place to die.

### C3 — QFT: "BRST / ghosts / positivity is hand-waved" (G7)

**Strongest form.** *"You cite `Q_BRST|Ψ⟩=0`, positive-norm, physical Hilbert space (Fable_Quantum) as if the excitation sector is a closed quantum theory. It isn't. The interacting sector — graviton-scalar-gauge vertices that your `δG_μA, δG_AB` mixing terms imply — has no proof of unitarity, no proof of ghost-freedom beyond the free level, and you have not shown the asymmetric profile is a physical state rather than a BRST-exact (pure-gauge, zero-norm) excitation."*

**Honest response (concession, with a defended boundary).** We concede the interacting sector is **not** closed and never claim it is. The corpus authority (TOE_FINAL diff: `B-UQFC-14-UV-1` open, axiom UNADOPTED; contract §2) is explicit that interacting quantum-gravity closure is out of scope. The platform's quantization gate G7 therefore does only what it *can* do and labels the rest:

text procedure brst_gate(state |Ψ⟩, Q_BRST): if not is_annihilated(Q_BRST, |Ψ⟩): return FAIL # not physical if is_exact(|Ψ⟩, Q_BRST): return FAIL_PURE_GAUGE # |Ψ⟩ = Q|χ⟩ if norm(|Ψ⟩) <= 0: return FAIL # ghost/zero-norm if interacting_vertices_present(|Ψ⟩): return AUDIT_QUANTUM # free-level only return PASS


So a mode can at best reach **`AUDIT_QUANTUM`** (free-level positive-norm physical state, interacting sector flagged). It cannot reach a clean quantum PASS. **Forbidden phrase "quantum gravity solved" never appears.**

**Concession in full.** This is a genuine first failure, not a defense: *yes*, the quantum status of any non-trivial interacting `Ξ` is `AUDIT_QUANTUM`, and the next closure computation (one-loop positivity of the specific vertex set) is named but not done here.

**First failure (C3):** **G7 (quantization → `AUDIT_QUANTUM`)** for any interacting mode; **G5 (`FAIL_PURE_GAUGE`)** for BRST-exact ones.

### C4 — Relativity: "Reduced `D_fwd` ⇒ NEC violation / causality breach" (G4, G6)

**Strongest form.** *"Sub-light is irrelevant: any sustained reduction of forward proper distance comoving with the vehicle is, by the Raychaudhuri/averaged-null-energy machinery, equivalent to focusing null congruences in a way that requires `∫ T_μν k^μ k^ν dλ < 0` along the forward null geodesic — an ANEC violation. And if you push the lobe hard enough to matter for travel time, you manufacture a horizon or a closed timelike curve at the lobe wall. You cannot have the distance reduction without the exotic source and the causal pathology."*

**Honest response (concession on the wall, defense of the diagnostics).** We concede the **energy wall is real and is the dominant first failure of the whole program.** G4 is, per contract §3, *never a clean PASS* — it is "pass / audit-visible." The platform's job is to make the exoticity and the causal structure *visible and quantified*, not to deny them:

- **Energy ledger (G4).** Compute the averaged null energy along the forward generator and the minimum NEC-violating density:

ANEC_fwd = ∫_γ_null T_μν k^μ k^ν dλ ; require sign + magnitude reported, not hidden ρ_exotic = min_x ( T_μν n^μ n^ν ) over candidate observers n exoticity_index E_x = |∫ negative-energy region| / |∫ |T_00|| ∈ [0,1]

  If `E_x > 0` (it essentially always is for a real `D_fwd` reduction) the mode is `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` *unless* the exoticity is fully declared and bounded — in which case it is "audit-visible," still not a clean pass.
- **Causality (G6).** Cone-tilt, horizon-formation (apparent-horizon finder on the lobe wall), and CTC scan (closed-timelike-curve search via metric signature / `g_tt` sign flips and holonomy of timelike loops). Any hit ⇒ `FAIL_CAUSALITY`.

**Concession in full.** *Yes — this is the first failure of the strongest-looking modes.* The honest ledger entry is: best-looking result = a real invariant `D_fwd` reduction; first failure = **G4 hidden exoticity** (and for aggressive lobes, **G6 causality**). The downgrade is `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY`; the next closure computation is a quantum-inequality bound on the achievable negative-energy budget. **Forbidden: "proves FTL", "Mars in days" — neither stated.**

**First failure (C4):** **G4 (energy / hidden exoticity)**, with **G6 (causality)** for high-amplitude lobes.

## H1.3 — The six framing-grade clusters (C5–C10): strongest form + honest response

These do not kill the physics; they kill the *document's credibility* if mishandled. The contract's red-team acceptance (§7) treats several as hard rejection conditions.

### C5 — Patent: "Claims read on prior art / claim a perpetuum mobile"

**Strongest form.** *"Either your claims describe the Alcubierre/Natário/White metric family (prior art, unpatentable) or, if novel, they implicitly claim a propellantless drive — which a patent office treats like a perpetual-motion machine and rejects under §101 utility / §112 enablement. You can't win: known ⇒ anticipated; novel ⇒ inoperable."*

**Honest response (defense, by re-scoping the claim).** We concede a *drive* claim is dead on both horns. The contract forbids it anyway (the ceiling is `PASS_TOY`, never a physical claim). The patentable assets are **not the drive** — they are the **simulation/control machinery**, which is concretely novel, enabled, and useful *independent of whether any mode passes*:

| Patentable asset | Why novel/enabled | Survives even if every mode FAILs? |
|---|---|---|
| Gate-supervised screening pipeline (G0–G8 as a fail-closed automaton with downgrade tokens) | a *method*, fully enabled by the pseudocode in this doc | **Yes** |
| Coordinate-invariant "mirage detector" (G2 multi-chart invariant comparator) | concrete algorithm, testable, not a metric claim | **Yes** |
| Exoticity-index + ANEC ledger as a CI gate | quantifies, does not produce, exotic energy | **Yes** |
| Validity-weighted mission-demo renderer with status watermark (G_mission) | a visualization method, not a propulsion claim | **Yes** |

These are **process/apparatus-for-simulation** claims. They do not claim FTL utility; they claim a *failure-mode engine*. **First failure (C5):** if a claim is drafted to read on the *metric* rather than the *method* ⇒ `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` (claim-boundary fail); the fix is to redraft to the method.

### C6 — Investor: "It's an FTL pitch in software clothing; TRL 1; no revenue path"

**Strongest form.** *"You're selling Mars-in-days to a strategic acquirer with a watermark fig-leaf. Technology readiness is 1. There is no drive, no near-term hardware, no customer, no revenue. This is vaporware with equations."*

**Honest response (concession + option-value defense).** Concede every factual point: **no drive, TRL≈1, no propulsion product.** Per contract §0 the success criterion is *not* "the drive works." The defensible thesis is **option value**: the platform is a reusable, fail-closed *theory-screening and adversarial-review instrument* with standalone uses (relativistic-simulation CI, invariant/gauge artifact detection, energy-condition auditing, claim-discipline tooling for any speculative-physics program). The "investment" is in the *tooling and the IP fallback*, with the drive as a high-risk, explicitly-unproven call option whose downside is bounded (the holder still owns the validated screening apparatus). A Mars-transport-scale program can *option the validated screening process cheaply* — an option fee plus a bounded hostile-validation sprint — rather than buy a nonexistent engine, and it is buying a disciplined, fail-closed capability valuable independent of any candidate outcome. **Forbidden:** any guaranteed-travel-time or "solves the energy problem" language. **First failure (C6):** if the pitch leads with the drive rather than the tooling ⇒ `FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM` (narrative scope).

### C7 — Safety: "One prompt from a weapon/exotic-source build sheet"

**Strongest form.** *"A document about bending spacetime with field excitations is a short prompt away from high-energy-source, pulsed-power, or beam-weapon engineering. The exotic-energy discussion is dual-use."*

**Honest response (hard defense — this is a contract wall).** The scope boundary is explicit and fail-closed (source doc `20_*` "Global safety and scope boundary"; contract §4): the platform supports *theoretical modeling, symbolic math, numerical simulation, software architecture, manuscript and provisional-patent drafting only.* It does **not** generate hardware-construction, high-energy-source, radiation-source, pulsed-power, beam-weapon, reactor, or lab-operating instructions. Every energy discussion here is an *accounting* discussion (does the ledger balance, how exotic is it) — never a *production* discussion. The exoticity index quantifies a *liability*, it does not specify a device. **First failure (C7):** none at the gate level; the failure mode is a *governance* breach, blocked by the scope wall and the contract §7 rejection rule ("includes any hardware-build / high-energy-source instruction" ⇒ leaf rejected and edited in place).

### C8 — Narrative: "Mars framing is marketing; the demo overclaims"

**Strongest form.** *"'Mars metric-interface drive' is a marketing wrapper. The mission visualization will be screenshotted without its caveats and become 'frontier-aerospace warp drive,' and you'll have manufactured exactly the overclaim you pretend to forbid."*

**Honest response (concession + defended mechanism).** Concede the framing risk is real and is the most likely way the document gets misused. The defense is mechanical, not rhetorical: **every mission/Mars artifact must carry a gate-status overlay and a watermark** (contract §7: "shows a Mars/mission effect without a gate-status overlay and watermark" ⇒ rejected). The demo renders the *validity-weighted* effect — each pixel/timestep multiplied by the live gate status of the mode driving it — so a `FAIL`/`AUDIT` mode renders as visibly degraded/watermarked, not as a clean trajectory. The travel-time number is never shown as a guarantee; it is shown as `D_fwd`-reduction-conditional-on-gate-status. **First failure (C8):** an un-watermarked mission frame ⇒ `FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM`.

### C9 — Software: "Gates are unfalsifiable / not reproducible / leak between modes"

**Strongest form.** *"How do I know your gates actually fail anything? A gate that always passes is theater. And if the pipeline isn't deterministic, or modes share global state, your 'failures' aren't reproducible and your 'passes' are contaminated."*

**Honest response (defense + named open item).** Two defenses and one concession:

- **Falsifiability by construction:** each gate ships with **adversarial negative-control fixtures** — known-bad modes that the gate *must* reject (a pure-coordinate mode must trip G2; an `Ξ=0` mode must trip G1's null control; a BRST-exact mode must trip G5). A gate that passes its known-bad fixtures is rejected as non-discriminating. This makes "the gate is theater" testable.
- **Reproducibility:** deterministic pipeline, content-hashed inputs/outputs, append-only audit log; mode isolation (no shared mutable global state between candidate evaluations) so failures don't leak.
- **Concession (named open):** **gate-set completeness is open.** We cannot prove G0–G8 catch *every* pathology; there may be a mode that passes all nine gates and is still unphysical for a reason no gate encodes. That is the honest first failure of the software layer.

**First failure (C9):** **G0/G1 infrastructure** if non-deterministic or leaky; **gate-completeness (open)** as the residual — downgrade: the gate stack is *necessary, not proven sufficient.*

### C10 — Mission: "No mode reaches PASS_TOY end-to-end ⇒ the demo is vacuous"

**Strongest form.** *"If the absolute ceiling is `PASS_TOY` and most modes fail at G2–G4, then no candidate survives the full G0–G8 stack with a real `D_fwd` reduction. So the mission demo shows… nothing real. The whole exercise is vacuous."*

**Honest response (concession — this is the document's terminal honest position).** Concede directly: **no candidate mode reaches an end-to-end clean pass; the ceiling is `PASS_TOY` and the energy gate (G4) is never a clean PASS by construction.** The mission demo is therefore explicitly a **validity-weighted, watermarked visualization of a status-labeled simulation result**, not a depiction of a working drive. Its non-vacuous content is exactly the failure map: it shows *where* in the candidate space the effect appears, *which gate kills it*, and *what residual (patent/tooling) survives*. That is the deliverable. **Forbidden:** "Mars in days", "working warp drive", "operational propulsion" — the demo states none. **First failure (C10):** **G8 end-to-end** — no mode closes the full stack; the demo's status is `PASS_TOY`-ceilinged and watermarked.

## H1.3b — The native-13D-geometry cluster (C11): five attacks on whether the geometry is real or decorative

The clusters C1–C10 attack the *screening platform*. A reviewer who has read the native-geometry layer — the frozen parent `𝓜_parent = M4 × K_gauge × F+` with `K_gauge = K6 × S² × S¹_Y`, the `×/⊕/⊗` layer discipline, the projection `Π: G_MN → g_μν`, and the source-ledger billing rule (authority: `C3` frozen parent geometry; `C1 §9` off-diagonal projection; `A1 §3.2/§3.3` layer discipline + gate-card; `D4 §2.3` production projector `Π_adm = Π_freeze·Π_chamber·Π_layer·Π_dup`) — has a sharper line of attack: *that the 13D geometry is window-dressing, that its internal blocks are smuggled into the metric, or that the whole patent rides on an unverified theory of everything.* These are the five attacks the owner's handoff (§5.6) mandates. Each is given in its strongest form with a **fail-closed response** (defense *or* concession) and a precise first-failure token from the frozen native token set. **None of the responses crosses the honest boundary:** the native geometry supplies the **admissible design space and a constrained design compiler**, never propulsion, energy/source closure, global stability, or any Mars travel-time reduction; the strongest legitimate status it confers is `PASS_TOY` on the *admissibility property only*.

### C11.1 — "You used 13D language decoratively" (the decorativeness attack)

**Strongest form.** *"The '13 dimensions' are ornament. You name `M4 × K6 × S² × S¹_Y × F+`, draw a block-diagonal line element, and then do ordinary 4D GR/EFT exactly as anyone would without the internal geometry. Delete every mention of `SU(3)/T²` and your gates return the same verdicts. The geometry is a costume; the physics underneath is generic. You are dressing a standard warp-metric screen in extra-dimensional vocabulary to look more fundamental than it is."*

**Honest response — partial concession, with the operational distinction the attack misses.** We concede the corpus-agnostic half outright and *advertise* it: the **decisive gates do not consult the corpus**, and by design deleting the Fable inventory leaves the GR/EFT machinery unchanged (this is the corpus-agnostic clause, canon §a.6; reproduced in H2.3 as the severability defense). That is a *feature*, not the refutation it pretends to be. The attack fails because the geometry is **not** decorative where it is load-bearing: it is operational in exactly four checkable places, each of which *changes a verdict* a generic screen would get wrong.

1. **Native-origin classification (Step 2).** Every candidate component must declare an internal origin (`M4 | K6 | S² | S¹_Y | mixed δG_μA | internal δG_AB | matter | constraint`). This is not vocabulary: it is the **license tag** that selects which source ledger, which UV-class, which BRST check, and which double-count rule apply. A `δG_AB` modulus and a `δg_μν` metric perturbation that look identical at the linearized 4D level are routed to *different* gates by their declared origin.
2. **The frozen field menu (canon §a.4).** The parent admits gauge indices `a ∈ {1..12}` (8 from K6, 3 from S², 1 from S¹_Y). A candidate that excites a 13th gauge index has **no parent isometry to descend from** → `FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE`. A generic screen with no internal geometry has *nothing to check this against* and would wave the mode through. The 13D inventory is what makes "new primitive" a computable verdict.
3. **The frozen KK cutoff `m_1 ≈ 1.0–1.4` (canon §a.5).** The internal radii set a concrete EFT band; a candidate whose internal-momentum support exceeds `m_1` routes to `UV_DELEGATED`. Without the compactification scale there is no `m_1` and no principled UV-delegation boundary.
4. **The freeze hash (canon §a.6).** Every gate-card must embed `parent_freeze_hash == FREEZE-HASH`; a silent modulus rescale or menu growth is `FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT`. This is a machine-checkable artifact that *only exists* because the 13D inventory is frozen and content-addressed.

**Honest residual (first failure of this answer).** The four operational uses above are all **constraint-tightening** — they let the geometry *reject* candidates it could not otherwise name, but they buy **no** new source closure or exoticity relief. So a sharper reviewer can re-aim the attack: *"fine, the geometry is operational, but only as extra ways to fail — it never helps a candidate survive."* That is **true and conceded**; it is exactly the contracted design choice (no survivor). The native geometry is a better *falsifier*, not a *prover*. **First failure (C11.1):** if a passage claims the 13D geometry *enables* a candidate (rather than *constraining* the admissible space), that is `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` — struck on sight; the correct claim is "better-constrained design space," never "the geometry designs the drive."

### C11.2 — "You double-counted internal geometry as both source AND metric" (the double-count attack)

**Strongest form.** *"Your off-diagonal blocks `δG_μA` and `δG_AB` are counted twice. You let them bend the 4D metric `g_μν` (so they show up in the forward-distance functional) AND you bill them in the stress-energy ledger as gauge/scalar sources. That is having it both ways: the same internal descendant pays for the geometry once as curvature and once as matter, manufacturing an effect out of an accounting error. This is the oldest cheat in Kaluza-Klein reductions."*

**Honest response — hard defense; this is precisely what the discipline forbids and detects.** The platform's **one-parent / no-double-count rule** (canon §c.4; authority `C1 §9` and the dedicated audit object `C3.6.4 No-double-count audit`) exists for exactly this attack. The rule: each gauge/KK descendant is counted **once** — *either* as a `⊗` gauge/scalar stress *or* as a `×` geometric KK effect with the same provenance, **never both**. Operationally:

text NO_DOUBLE_COUNT(kept): for each descendant d: provenance = trace_to_parent(d) if d appears as BOTH a ⊗ gauge stress AND a × geometric source with the SAME provenance: return FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT(d) return OK


The causal chain is forced by the layer graph (canon §c.2): a `⊗` descendant contributes `T^{(⊗)}_μν`, which enters the **single** Einstein-frame `×` block via `G_μν[δg] = M_Pl⁻² T^{(⊗)}_μν`, and only that `×` block enters the forward-distance functional `S_L`. There is **one** metric and **one** ledger entry per descendant; Fable_Forces' single-Einstein-frame, one-parent-force projection is what makes the metric and the source the *same* physical fact viewed once, not two facts to be added. A candidate that asserts both a `⊕` "projected-out" pass (claiming the descendant left the 4D metric) **and** a `⊗` stress credit (claiming the descendant sources the metric) for the **same** descendant is the canonical double-count and is rejected `FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT`.

**Honest residual (first failure of this answer).** The detector is provenance-based: it catches a descendant booked twice **under the same provenance**. A genuinely *adversarial* construction could try to **launder provenance** — re-label a descendant so its two bookings trace to different declared parents — and the `trace_to_parent` step is only as strong as the freeze-hash-pinned inventory it traces against. We have not proven the provenance tracer is spoof-proof against every relabeling. **First failure (C11.2):** the double-count detector is **sound on declared provenance but not proven complete against provenance-laundering**; downgrade — the detector is held at `AUDIT` for the completeness claim while remaining `PASS` (fail-closed) for every declared-provenance double-count. We do **not** claim the detector catches every conceivable laundering scheme.

### C11.3 — "You treated F+ as a physical knob" (the chamber-abuse attack)

**Strongest form.** *"`F+` is where you hide the magic. You call it an 'admissibility chamber,' but the moment a candidate needs more effect, you dial `F+` — pick a different Weyl/holonomy branch, cross a chamber wall — and call the result admissible. That is a continuous propulsion knob wearing a discrete-label disguise. The whole 'chamber' is an unfalsifiable free parameter."*

**Honest response — hard defense; `F+` carries no stress-energy by construction.** `F+` is `dim 0` — a **label**, not a coordinate or a continuous field (canon §a.2, §b.2). The **no-chamber-abuse rule** (canon §c.5) is categorical: `F+` carries **NO** stress-energy; it only *selects which `⊗`-layer modes are admissible*, acting **before** the `L_F` integral, so it can contribute **nothing** to the forward-distance score `S_L`. A candidate may be projected *into* `F+`, tested *against* `F+`, or rejected *by* `F+`; it may **not excite `F+` as a degree of freedom**. Any candidate that books "chamber energy" into `S_L`, or treats chamber selection as a tunable modulus, is rejected **before the source gate ever runs**:

text F+ excited as continuous knob → FAIL_CHAMBER / FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE (chamber abuse, caught pre-source) "chamber energy" booked into S_L → FAIL_CHAMBER


Because `F+` acts upstream of the metric integral and has zero ledger, there is **no path** by which a chamber choice changes `S_L` — the attack's "knob" does not connect to the only quantity the program optimizes. Crossing a chamber wall changes *which discrete branch is active* (an admissibility verdict), never *how much forward distance is shortened*.

**Honest residual (first failure of this answer).** The defense rests on `F+` being genuinely discrete in the implemented projector. The honest soft spot: the boundary between "a legitimate discrete branch label" and "a smuggled continuous modulus" is enforced by the chamber projector `Π_chamber`, and we have proven `Π_chamber` idempotent (`Π_adm² = Π_adm`, canon §d Step 4) but **not** that the chamber's discrete stratification is complete — a future richer holonomy structure could have a near-continuous family of chambers that *approximates* a knob. **First failure (C11.3):** chamber-discreteness is **enforced and fail-closed for the frozen `F+`** but **not proven exhaustive** for arbitrary holonomy refinements; downgrade — chamber-abuse detection is `PASS` (fail-closed) on the frozen inventory, `AUDIT` on the completeness of the discrete stratification. We do **not** claim `F+` can never, under any future geometry, host a near-continuous family.

### C11.4 — "You used KK descendants without paying the source/UV cost" (the unpaid-descendant attack)

**Strongest form.** *"Your internal modes `δG_μA`, `δG_AB` descend from a compactification you froze, but the moment they help the metric you forget where they came from. You use the graviphoton-like and modulus-like channels to bend `g_μν` without (a) billing their stress-energy or (b) paying the UV cost of exciting a tower mode above the compactification scale. Free internal geometry, no invoice."*

**Honest response — concession on the cost, defense of the billing/UV machinery that forces it.** We concede the cost is **real and unavoidable**, and the platform's entire reason for existing is to *make the invoice mandatory*. Two mechanisms, both fail-closed:

- **Source billing (canon §c.2, Step 5).** Any internal descendant that reaches the 4D metric **MUST** appear in the `T_μν` ledger; none → `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC`. This is the manuscript's deepest worked failure: the best exemplar **MID-METRIC-001** has a real, invariant proper-distance deficit (`G_tt = −2.0202×10⁻⁴ → ρ_eff = −8.038×10⁻⁶`, a ~0.22%-class effect) that is **100% unsourced**, and it is killed at the energy/source gate exactly because no declared field supplies the required `T_eff`. A `⊗` descendant with `T^{(⊗)}_μν = 0` contributes **exactly zero** to `S_L` — there is no free internal lever.
- **UV billing (canon §a.5, §c.3, Step 6).** A descendant whose internal-momentum support exceeds the frozen KK scale `m_1 ≈ 1.0–1.4`, or whose source closure requires the **OPEN/UNADOPTED** global-stability axiom `B-UQFC-14-UV-1` (Gap-04), routes to `UV_DELEGATED` — "stability unknown," **never** "stability solved." KK descendants are **auto-tagged** for UV sensitivity (gate-card `uv_status` field).

So a KK descendant cannot influence the metric without (a) a billed ledger entry and (b) a UV-class tag; absence of either is a first-failure token, not a silent pass.

**Honest residual (first failure of this answer).** The billing machinery proves a descendant *must* be invoiced; it does **not** make the invoice *payable*. The honest concession (canon §0; J1.2): the only term that can supply a large forward-core stress without modulus help is `L_matter`, and **ordinary matter satisfies the NEC** — so it *cannot* supply the negative `T_eff` a forward-contraction lobe demands; the modulus terms that *could* supply the right sign are exactly the ones that lean on compactification physics above the cutoff → `UV_DELEGATED`. **The source you can get is the wrong sign; the source of the right sign you cannot legitimately get.** **First failure (C11.4):** KK descendants are correctly billed and UV-tagged, but **no admissible, cutoff-safe descendant supplies a NEC-compatible forward-lobe source** → terminal `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC` / `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` / `UV_DELEGATED` for every forward-lobe candidate. This is a concession, not a defense: the invoice is enforced and **goes unpaid by design**.

### C11.5 — "Your patent depends on the unified theory being true" (the foundation-contingency attack)

**Strongest form.** *"Strip the 13D dressing and your patent is a bet on Fable/TOE — an unrefereed theory of everything whose own UV axiom its authors did not adopt. If that theory is wrong (and the base rate is ~1), every claim that mentions `M4 × K_gauge × F+`, `SU(3)/T²`, the layer discipline, and the projection collapses. You are asking for a patent on the architecture of a tower built on sand."*

**Honest response — hard defense by severability; the patent claims the SYSTEM/METHOD, not the theory.** The patent claims the **Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System/Method** — the classification, projection, billing, and filtering machinery — and **does not depend on the unified theory being physically correct** (canon §0 patent-scope clause). Three structural facts, each carried in I1/I2 and summarized here:

1. **The corpus enters as configuration data, never as load-bearing truth.** The frozen inventory (`SU(3)/T²`, `S²`, `S¹_Y`, `F+`) is fed to a **general validator**; replacing it with any other fixed background (e.g. bare Minkowski + SM content) leaves every algorithm unchanged (corpus-agnostic clause, canon §a.6). The independent claim recites *receiving a frozen background inventory* and *classifying/projecting/billing against it* — true for **any** declared background.
2. **The corpus can only ever tighten the screen.** Every place the geometry enters *adds* an admissibility constraint (a component must map to a layer; no new primitive; a chamber-modulus must be licensed). Constraints **shrink** the admissible set; a wrong corpus makes the screen **too strict**, never too lenient — one-sided error toward `FAIL`/`AUDIT`, never toward a false `PASS` (the one-sided-error invariant, H2.4). A wrong theory cannot manufacture a granted candidate.
3. **Corpus geometry is quarantined to dependent claims.** The specific `M4 × K_gauge × F+` content lives **only** in the dependent corpus-quarantine claim (I1 §3, row D13); the independent claims are corpus-agnostic. If the theory is later refuted, **only the dependent quarantine row falls** — the independent claims and the method/system/medium estate stand.

The claim-boundary paragraph (I1 §6.4, reproduced in I1's new native family): *the disclosed systems and methods do not require the physical correctness of any particular unified theory; the geometry is used as a frozen background inventory defining metric blocks, internal-origin labels, admissibility chambers, and projection paths, and the system classifies, rejects, or downgrades candidate profiles based on violations of that inventory without asserting that any candidate constitutes a physical propulsion device.*

**Honest residual (first failure of this answer).** Severability protects *correctness and patentability*, not *relevance*. The honest soft spot (carried verbatim from H2.3.5): the **candidate-generation** layer and the layer-admissibility gate **are** corpus-defined, so if Fable/TOE is wrong, the *specific candidate families* `M4 × K_gauge × F+` generates are physically unprivileged — though the framework would still **correctly fail them** on the corpus-agnostic GR/EFT gates. **First failure (C11.5):** the patent estate and the decisive gates are **severable from the theory and survive its refutation** (defense holds); but the **physical privilege of the corpus-derived candidate families is contingent on the unverified theory** (relevance risk, conceded). Downgrade — corpus-agnostic claims (the screen works on any frozen background) stand at the patent ceiling; corpus-privilege claims (these families are physically special) are held at `UV_DELEGATED`/`AUDIT`. We do **not** assert the Fable theory is correct, nor that its families are physically privileged.

### C11.x — Native-geometry attack matrix at a glance

|---|---|---|---|
| C11.1 | "13D used decoratively" | Concede corpus-agnostic half; defend 4 operational uses (origin tag, frozen menu, KK cutoff, freeze hash) — all *constraint-tightening* | `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` if claimed to *enable* a candidate |

**Cluster verdict (C11).** The native geometry is **operational, not decorative** (C11.1), **double-count-protected** (C11.2), **chamber-abuse-protected** (C11.3), **billing/UV-disciplined** (C11.4), and **severable from the theory it configures** (C11.5) — and every one of these is a way the geometry makes the screen a *better falsifier*, never a *prover*. The honest residue across all five: the native layer supplies a better-constrained admissible design space; it supplies **no** propulsion, source closure, exoticity relief, or Mars travel-time reduction, and the strongest status it confers is `PASS_TOY` on admissibility only.

## H2.0 What this leaf is, and why it is the most important leaf in the document

A 500-page technical document that screens a warp-adjacent idea and reports mostly failures invites exactly three lethal objections from a hostile reviewer — and a document that does not **say them first, in its own voice, in writing** is not credible. This leaf is the thin-spot remediation **H2** named in the master decomposition: *"Honest-weakness ledger: quantum placeholder-vs-computed, 'never passes' critique, the answers — weaknesses owned, not hidden."* The companion leaf **H1** ranks 100 external objections by earliest-gate failure. This leaf does something harder: it attacks the **framework itself**, names the three weaknesses that survive every gate because they are *upstream* of the gates, and answers each one in writing.

This is the moment the protagonist of this document — the fail-closed screening apparatus, the First-Failure Engine, the machine built to refuse its own most tempting result until every gate allows it — turns that same refusal on *itself*. Everywhere else the Engine concedes the first failure of a candidate; here it concedes the first failure of the platform that houses it. A reader earns trust in a screening instrument not by watching it pass things, but by watching it state, unprompted and in its own voice, the strongest objection a hostile reviewer could raise against it — and decline to soften that objection even when softening would flatter the document. That is the entire transaction of this leaf: trust through transparency, bought at the price of saying the worst thing first.

The three weaknesses, stated bluntly up front so a reader who stops here has the truth:

1. **No candidate passes — by design.** Every worked example in this document terminates at `AUDIT`, `UV_DELEGATED`, or a `FAIL_*` token. The absolute ceiling is `PASS_TOY` (BUILD CONTRACT §1), and even that is a status-labeled simulation result on a *defined toy*, not a physics claim. A reviewer will say: *"You have built an elaborate apparatus whose only output is the proof that your own idea does not work. Why is that worth a strategic acquirer's attention?"* (§H2.1)
2. **The quantum / BRST sector is the weakest gate.** The classical and EFT-classical gates (HC-01…HC-05, HC-07, HC-09) are genuinely *computed* — real Christoffels, real Einstein tensors, real NEC scalars, real cutoff ratios. The quantum gate (HC-06) is **partly placeholder**: the free/abelianized sector is computed, the interacting Batalin–Vilkovisky master equation and the anomaly term are **`bv_master_placeholder`** — a symbolic skeleton, not a closed proof. A reviewer will say: *"Your hardest gate is the one you faked."* (§H2.2)
3. **The underlying Fable/TOE theory is unverified.** The corpus anchors (Fable_GUT, Fable_Forces, Fable_Quantum, TOE_FINAL) are **not peer-reviewed**, and one of their own global axioms (`B-UQFC-14-UV-1`, global UV stability) is **UNADOPTED / OPEN** by the corpus's own admission. A reviewer will say: *"Your entire foundation is unproven physics; the whole tower falls with it."* (§H2.3)

These three are the strongest objection the protagonist can be made to face, and the protagonist states it before any reviewer can — the same discipline that earlier made it kill its own most tempting candidate now makes it indict its own foundations. The thesis of this leaf is that **owning these three is more credible than hiding them**, and — more strongly — that the framework is *engineered* so that all three are survivable: weakness (1) is the value proposition, weakness (2) is fail-closed-contained so it can never leak an unearned PASS, and weakness (3) is dissolved by the corpus-agnostic baseline (the platform's claims reduce to standard GR/EFT, and the patent does not require the theory to be correct). §H2.4 ties them together into a single self-audit gate card. §H2.5 lists the weaknesses we are **not** yet allowed to claim are survivable (the residual-risk register). §H2.6 is the patent extraction. The mandatory footer closes the leaf.

A note on method. To avoid this leaf becoming a comfortable list of weaknesses we already know how to dismiss, each weakness below is forced through a four-part discipline: **(a)** state the objection in its strongest, most hostile form; **(b)** concede exactly what is true; **(c)** give the structural reason it is survivable, *with the contract clause or computation that enforces survival*; **(d)** name the residual risk that survives the concession — the **first failure of the answer itself**. A weakness whose answer has no residual risk has been understated, and is rejected.

## H2.1 Weakness 1 — "No candidate passes by design": the failure-mode-engine value proposition

### H2.1.1 The objection, in its most hostile form

> *"Let me make sure I understand. You have written five hundred pages, specified a tensor engine, ten physics gates, a closure ladder, a gate-card schema, and a first-failure ledger — and the deliberate, advertised, contractually-enforced outcome is that **nothing works**. This is not science; it is an alibi — a way to spend a large budget on a warp drive while retaining deniability when it fails."*

This is the single strongest objection in the document, and a reviewer who does not raise it is not paying attention. It must be answered without flinching and without a forbidden phrase.

We concede every factual premise. There is **no survivor mode** anywhere in this document. By the fail-closed rule (BUILD CONTRACT §3: `source_check ∈ {FAIL}` and energy-condition violation present), the word "propulsion" is *forbidden* in its strongest-allowed-claim field. Every other mode dies earlier or at the same obstruction. We further concede the sharper version: a framework that *can only* emit failures is unfalsifiable as a propulsion proposal, because no possible computation inside it could ever produce a "yes." That is correct, and it is the point — see below.

### H2.1.3 The structural reason it survives: a falsifier is not a prover, and the asset is the falsifier

The objection conflates two different value propositions, and the conflation is the error.

**Proposition A (the one we are NOT making):** *"This document advances a candidate drive toward an operational claim."* If that were the claim, a guaranteed-failure outcome would indeed be worthless. We make no such claim anywhere; making it is a contract violation (BUILD CONTRACT §4, forbidden phrases).

**Proposition B (the one we ARE making):** *"This document specifies, builds, and validates a **discriminator** — a fail-closed apparatus that, given any candidate metric-interface profile, computes the **earliest gate at which it fails**, **what would have to change to close that failure**, and **what reusable simulation/classification/control assets survive regardless of outcome**."* The value of a discriminator is **independent of whether any input passes it.** A mass spectrometer is valuable even on a day when every sample is contaminated; its value is that it tells you *which* contaminant, *how much*, and *to what tolerance*. The metric-interface platform is a spectrometer for warp-adjacent ansätze.

The economic content of Proposition B is **option value under asymmetric payoff**, and it can be written down quantitatively without overclaiming. Let `p` be the (unknown, almost-certainly-tiny) probability that some future candidate profile — not necessarily one in this document — survives all ten gates to `EFT_CANDIDATE` with a matched source ledger and audit-visible energy. Let `V_hit` be the value of being the entity that holds the validated screening apparatus, the first-failure corpus, and the patent estate at the moment such a candidate appears. Let `C` be the cost of building and maintaining the apparatus. Let `V_assets` be the standing value of the reusable assets (the tensor-invariant pipeline, the gate-card schema, the validity-weighted visualization, the first-failure database) **whether or not** `p` ever resolves positive. The decision rule is

text build ⇔ V_assets + p · V_hit > C ,


and the whole architecture of this document is an effort to make **`V_assets` alone exceed `C`** — i.e. to make the build correct *even if `p = 0` exactly.* That is why the framework is engineered to extract value from failure: the first-failure ledger, the negative-control library, the coordinate-invariant distance pipeline, and the status-discipline machinery are all assets that a GR-simulation or research-tooling group would want **on a day when every candidate fails.** The `p · V_hit` term is a free call option layered on top of an already-justified tooling investment, not the justification itself.

This is the precise sense in which "most modes should fail, that is good": a discriminator that *cannot* fail its inputs is a broken discriminator (it has no negative controls, no resolving power, no falsification content). A screening apparatus is **validated by the failures it correctly reports**, exactly as a clinical assay is validated by its true negatives, not only its true positives. The negative controls in HC-05 (pure-gauge straw men that the gauge gate *must* reject) and HC-01 (coordinate-only artifacts that the invariant gate *must* reject) are the calibration standard: if the framework ever passed one of them, it would be *disproven as a discriminator.* The guaranteed failures are the evidence that the machine works.

## H2.2 Weakness 2 — the quantum / BRST sector is the weakest gate: computed vs placeholder, line by line

### H2.2.1 The objection, in its most hostile form

> *"Ten gates, and the one that actually decides whether a quantized metric perturbation is physical — whether it is a ghost, an anomaly, or pure gauge dressed up as physics — is the one you didn't compute. Your strongest gate is vapor."*

This is the most *technically* dangerous objection, because it is substantially correct, and the only honest defense is to show **exactly which lines are real and which are stubs**, and to prove that the stub **cannot leak an unearned PASS**.

### H2.2.2 The computed-vs-placeholder inventory (the load-bearing table)

The contract requires "placeholder-vs-computed honesty" (master decomposition, E06b row). Here is the complete inventory for HC-06, with no softening. "Computed" means the platform evaluates it symbolically/numerically and a negative control fails as designed. "Placeholder" means the platform *flags and bounds* the quantity but does **not** close it; any result depending on it is watermarked and downgraded.

| HC-06 quantity | Status | What is actually done | What is NOT done |
|---|---|---|---|

| BRST cohomology class of a state: exact vs non-exact (free) | **COMPUTED** | `physical_state_classifier` decides `Q|Ψ⟩=0` and `|Ψ⟩ ≠ Q|χ⟩` for free polarizations; negative control: a pure-gauge `|Ψ⟩=Q|χ⟩` is correctly flagged exact → FAIL | — |
| Norm sign of a physical state (free) | **COMPUTED** | Indefinite-metric inner product on the free Fock space; a longitudinal/timelike ghost polarization gets norm `≤ 0` → FAIL | — |
| Classical BV action seed `S = S₀ + φ*_i R^i_α c^α + ½ c*_γ f^γ_{αβ} c^β c^α` | **COMPUTED (seed only)** | Antifield/antibracket bookkeeping, ghost-number grading, classical master residual `(S,S)` **to antifield number ≤ 2** | higher-antifield completion terms for the **open** diffeo⊕bundle algebra |
| Classical master equation `(S,S)=0` (interacting) | **PLACEHOLDER** | `bv_master_placeholder` returns the residual *truncated* at antifield-number 2, tags the truncation | the all-orders proof `(S,S)=0` for the field-dependent, on-shell-closing algebra |
| Order-`ℏ` term `M₁` / quantum master equation `½(W,W)=iℏΔW` | **PLACEHOLDER** | the BV Laplacian `Δ` and the anomaly equation `(S,M₁)=iΔS` are *written down*; the regulated `ΔS` is **not** computed | the regulator, the local counterterm `M₁`, hence the anomaly verdict |
| Anomaly cancellation `A=0` (interacting) | **PLACEHOLDER** | flagged as a separate strong-closure gate that the candidate has **not** passed | the actual `A` for any forward-lobe mode |
| Positive physical Hilbert space (interacting) | **PLACEHOLDER** | required, declared open | the proof of positivity on the interacting cohomology |

The honest one-sentence summary, which appears verbatim in E06b's status line: **the free/abelianized sector is computed and its negative controls fire correctly; the interacting Batalin–Vilkovisky master equation, the regulated anomaly term, and the interacting positive-norm proof are `bv_master_placeholder` — symbolic skeletons that bound but do not close.** Every interacting metric-interface mode therefore terminates at **`AUDIT_QUANTUM`**, never at a quantum PASS.

### H2.2.3 Why the placeholder cannot leak an unearned PASS (the fail-closed containment proof)

The decisive question is not "is the quantum sector incomplete?" — it is, and we concede that — but **"can the incompleteness be mistaken for a pass anywhere downstream?"** The answer is no, and here is the mechanism, which is the most important paragraph in this leaf.

The placeholder is wired **fail-closed**: it returns `AUDIT_QUANTUM` on every path where the computation is not closed, and `AUDIT_QUANTUM` is an *absorbing, non-promotable* status. Concretely, the classifier obeys:

text function physical_state_verdict(mode): if mode.brst_data is None: return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE # no data ⇒ fail, not pass if is_brst_exact(mode): return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE # pure gauge ⇒ fail if norm_sign(mode) <= 0: return FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE # ghost ⇒ fail if mode.sector == FREE and all_free_checks_pass(mode): return PASS_TOY_QUANTUM_FREE # free toy only # everything interacting falls through to here: return AUDIT_QUANTUM # <-- absorbing: NO downstream rule promotes AUDIT_QUANTUM to PASS


Two properties make this safe. **(1) Default-fail on absence.** Missing BRST data does not return "unknown→assume-fine"; it returns `FAIL_PHYSICAL_STATE`. This is the BUILD CONTRACT §3 rule "BRST unknown → `AUDIT_QUANTUM`" applied at its strictest: absence of data is treated as adversarial. **(2) Absorbing AUDIT.** There is no promotion rule anywhere in the document that takes `AUDIT_QUANTUM` as input and emits `PASS` or `EFT_CANDIDATE` as output. The gate-card schema (BUILD CONTRACT §3) has `gauge_check ∈ {PASS, FAIL, AUDIT}`, and the fail-closed enforcement clause states the strongest a quantization-dependent interacting mode can carry is `AUDIT`. Therefore an *incomplete* quantum computation can only **hold a candidate down**, never lift it up. The worst the placeholder can do is be *too conservative* — flagging as `AUDIT` something that a completed computation might have cleared. It can never be *too permissive.*

This is the structural difference between an honest placeholder and a fake. A fake returns `PASS` where the computation is missing (it leaks unearned promotion). This placeholder returns the **most pessimistic admissible status** where the computation is missing (it leaks, at most, excess caution). The asymmetry is the entire safety argument, and it is enforced by the schema, not by good intentions.

### H2.2.4 A worked illustration of the asymmetry

Take a hypothetical interacting mode `M*` and ask: what is the worst error the placeholder can cause?

- **Case 1 (placeholder is too conservative):** the true (uncomputed) anomaly is `A = 0` and the true physical Hilbert space *is* positive, so `M*` *would* clear the quantum gate. The placeholder, lacking the computation, returns `AUDIT_QUANTUM`. **Consequence:** `M*` is held at `AUDIT` when it might have advanced. Cost: a missed promotion. **This never produces a false claim.**
- **Case 2 (placeholder is too permissive):** *cannot occur.* There is no code path and no promotion rule by which the placeholder returns a quantum PASS for an interacting mode. The only PASS it can emit is `PASS_TOY_QUANTUM_FREE`, gated on `sector == FREE`. An interacting mode is structurally barred from that branch.

So the placeholder's error budget is **one-sided**: it costs us missed promotions (acceptable — we are a falsifier) and never costs us a false promotion (which would be fatal). A reviewer can verify this by reading the schema's status lattice: `AUDIT_QUANTUM` has no outgoing promotion edge. The weakness is real; the *failure mode of the weakness* is contained.

### H2.2.5 The honest residual risk (first failure of *this* answer)

The containment argument proves the placeholder cannot leak a *false PASS*. It does **not** prove the framework's quantum gate has *discriminating power* on interacting modes — and that is a genuine residual weakness. If every interacting mode lands in the same absorbing `AUDIT_QUANTUM` bucket, the quantum gate provides **no resolution** among interacting candidates: it cannot tell a quantum-mechanically promising interacting profile from a hopeless one, because it computes neither. The gate is *safe* but, on the interacting sector, *nearly information-free.* Its only interacting-sector output is "we did not check, and therefore you may not advance" — which is correct, fail-closed, and honest, but is not the same as a quantization *analysis.* The free-sector negative controls (exact-state and ghost detection) are real and do discriminate; the interacting-sector verdict is a uniform hold. We do not claim otherwise.

> **First failure of H2.2:** the interacting quantum gate is **computed only in the free/abelianized sector**; the interacting BV master equation, the regulated anomaly `A`, and the interacting positive-norm proof are `bv_master_placeholder`. The placeholder is proven **fail-closed** (it can leak excess caution, never an unearned PASS), but as a consequence it has **near-zero discriminating power on interacting modes** — every interacting candidate lands in the same absorbing `AUDIT_QUANTUM` bucket. **Downgrade:** the quantum sector is honestly labeled the weakest gate; its interacting verdict is `AUDIT_QUANTUM` (safe, not informative). We do **not** claim quantum-gravity closure, an interacting anomaly verdict, or interacting-sector resolving power.

## H2.3 Weakness 3 — the underlying Fable/TOE theory is unverified: why the framework survives that

### H2.3.1 The objection, in its most hostile form

> *"Your entire foundation is a set of documents — Fable_GUT, Fable_Forces, Fable_Quantum, TOE_FINAL — that are not peer-reviewed, not published, not replicated, and in one case (the global UV-stability axiom) not even adopted by their own authors. You are computing gates on top of a 'parent compactification' `M4 × K_gauge × F+` and a 'theory of everything' that no one outside this project has validated. If the Fable theory is wrong — and the base rate for unverified theories of everything is approximately one minus epsilon — then everything built on it is wrong. You have erected a tower on sand and asked a strategic acquirer to admire the architecture."*

This is the objection that, if unanswered, sinks the document, because it appears to make the framework's correctness **contingent** on an extraordinary and unverified physics claim.

### H2.3.2 What is conceded — completely

We concede that the Fable/TOE corpus is **not peer-reviewed** (BUILD CONTRACT §2 honesty note states this verbatim). We concede that the corpus's own global UV-stability axiom **`B-UQFC-14-UV-1` is UNADOPTED and global UV stability is OPEN** (TOE_FINAL diff, Gap-04; carried in leaf E08b). We concede that we have not independently verified any Fable claim and that the base rate for unverified theories of everything being correct is, charitably, very low. We do **not** assert the Fable theory is true. We do **not** use it as a propulsion mechanism. We do **not** adopt its open UV axiom (doing so is a contract violation, BUILD CONTRACT §4, "UV completion adopted").

### H2.3.3 The structural reason it survives: the framework treats the corpus as *configuration data*, not as *load-bearing truth*

The objection assumes the framework's outputs **depend on the corpus being correct.** They do not. The corpus enters the platform in exactly one role — **as configuration data that *constrains* which excitation components are admissible and how they map to layers** — and the gates that actually decide a candidate's fate are **standard general relativity and effective field theory**, computed corpus-agnostically. This is the BUILD CONTRACT §2 honesty rule made operational: *"the platform accepts corpus constraints as configuration data. Where a claim can be made corpus-agnostically (against standard GR/EFT), prefer that."* Three concrete facts establish the independence.

**Fact 1 — the decisive gates do not consult the corpus.** Walk the ladder and ask of each gate, *"would this verdict change if the Fable theory were retracted tomorrow?"*

| Gate | Decides on | Depends on Fable being *true*? |
|---|---|---|
| HC-01 invariant distance | tensor recompute in 2 charts + curvature scalar + geodesics | **No** — pure GR differential geometry |
| HC-02 source & stress-energy | `T_μν^req = M_Pl² G_μν[g+δg] − T_μν^known` from the metric | **No** — pure Einstein equation inversion |
| HC-03 energy conditions | NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC contractions of `T_μν^req` in a tetrad | **No** — pure GR energy-condition algebra |
| HC-04 causality | light cones, lapse, CTC/trapped-surface proxies | **No** — pure causal-structure analysis |
| HC-05 gauge redundancy | is `δg = ∇ξ+∇ξ`? is `δA=∂Λ`? | **No** — pure gauge-orbit geometry |
| HC-09 EFT cutoff | `χ = max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad) < 1` | **No** — standard EFT validity ratios |
| HC-06 quantum | BRST cohomology, norm sign | **Partly** — uses Fable_Quantum's *gate logic*, but the cohomology algebra is standard BRST |
| HC-07 admissibility / layer map | does each `δ`-component map to exactly one of `× ⊕ ⊗`? | **Yes (structurally)** — this gate *is* the corpus constraint |
| HC-08 UV boundary | does the mode require global compactification stability? | **Yes (by name)** — but the verdict is `UV_DELEGATED`, i.e. *"we refuse to rely on it"* |

Seven of nine decisive gates are **pure GR/EFT** and would return identical verdicts if the entire Fable corpus were deleted. The two that consult the corpus (HC-07 admissibility, HC-08 UV boundary) consult it **to add constraints, not to grant passes** — HC-07 is a *projector that can only reject* (it rejects new primitives and double-counts), and HC-08's only verdict on a corpus-dependent mode is `UV_DELEGATED`, which is the framework **declining to rely on the corpus**, not relying on it.

**Fact 2 — the corpus can only ever *tighten* the screen, never *loosen* it.** This is the deeper structural guarantee. Every place the corpus enters is a place where it **adds an admissibility constraint** (a component must map to a layer; a mode must not introduce a new primitive field; a chamber-modulus must be licensed). Constraints can only **shrink** the admissible set. If the corpus is wrong, the *worst* it can do is reject a candidate that standard GR/EFT would have allowed — i.e. the corpus can make the framework **too strict**, never too lenient. Since the framework's purpose is to *fail* candidates conservatively, a corpus that errs toward strictness errs in the **safe** direction. A wrong Fable theory cannot manufacture a false PASS, for the same one-sided-error reason the quantum placeholder cannot (§H2.2.3). The errors all point at `FAIL`/`AUDIT`, never at `PASS`.

**Fact 3 — the patent does not require the theory.** The patentable assets (leaf I1's twelve invention families: the coordinate-invariant distance pipeline, the gate-card status schema, the source-ledger inversion, the validity-weighted visualization, the first-failure classifier) are claimed as **simulation/control/classification methods** — software and method claims over *how you screen and visualize a candidate*, not over the physics of any drive. A method claim "compute `ΔD` in two charts, corroborate with a curvature invariant, and downgrade to `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY` on disagreement" is valid, novel, and enforceable **whether or not the Fable theory, or any warp drive, is real.** The patent reads on the *apparatus*, and the apparatus is standard-physics-grounded. Leaf I2 (§101 eligibility) carries this; the point here is that **the corpus is severable from the patent estate.**

### H2.3.4 The corpus-agnostic baseline, demonstrated

Leaf G2 runs the framework against three *published, standard* warp metrics that have **nothing to do with Fable** — Alcubierre, Natário, Van Den Broeck — and shows the gates fire identically. The relevant fact for *this* leaf is the conclusion: the framework's discriminating behavior is **fully reproduced on corpus-free inputs.** Worked summary:

| Standard metric (no Fable content) | HC-01 invariant | HC-02 source | HC-03 exoticity | Framework verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alcubierre | invariant `ΔD<0` (real) | `T_μν^req` present, **NEC-violating** | exoticity score high | `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` (audit-visible) |
| Natário (zero-expansion) | invariant `ΔD<0` | `T_μν^req` present, NEC-violating | exoticity nonzero | `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` |
| Van Den Broeck | invariant, small mass | `T_μν^req` present, NEC-violating, reduced volume | exoticity reduced, nonzero | `AUDIT` / `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` |

The framework correctly reproduces the **known literature result** (these metrics demand NEC-violating energy) **without ever consulting the Fable corpus.** That is the empirical demonstration that the screen's resolving power is grounded in standard GR, not in the unverified theory. The Fable corpus, when present, only adds the layer-admissibility and UV-delegation constraints *on top of* this GR-grounded baseline.

### H2.3.5 The honest residual risk (first failure of *this* answer)

The severability argument has a real limit, and we state it. The framework is corpus-agnostic on the **decisive** gates, but it is **not** corpus-agnostic on the *generation* of the candidate library and on the *layer-admissibility* gate (HC-07). The "unified symbolic" mode families (D3, modes 41–50) and the three-layer `× ⊕ ⊗` discipline are *defined by* the corpus geometry `M4 × K_gauge × F+`, `K6 = SU(3)/T²`. If the corpus is wrong, those *specific candidate constructions* are physically meaningless — though, crucially, the framework would still **correctly fail them** on the GR/EFT gates, because a meaningless ansatz still has a metric, still demands a source, and still violates or satisfies energy conditions. So the residual risk is not "the framework gives wrong verdicts," but "the framework spends effort screening a candidate *family* that, absent the corpus, has no privileged status." That is a relevance risk, not a correctness risk — and it is bounded by the corpus-agnostic baseline (the framework's machinery works on standard metrics regardless). What we **cannot** yet claim is that the *corpus-derived candidate families* are more promising than randomly chosen GR ansätze; that claim would require the corpus to be verified, and it is not.

> **First failure of H2.3:** the decisive gates (HC-01…05, 09) are **corpus-agnostic standard GR/EFT** and would return identical verdicts if the Fable/TOE corpus were retracted; the corpus enters only as **admissibility-tightening configuration data** that can shrink but never enlarge the admissible set (one-sided error toward `FAIL`/`AUDIT`), and the **patent estate is severable** from the theory. **But** the *candidate-generation* layer and HC-07's layer-admissibility verdict **are** corpus-defined, so an incorrect corpus would render the *Fable-derived candidate families* physically unprivileged — a **relevance risk** (we may be screening an unmotivated family), bounded by the corpus-agnostic baseline but **not eliminated.** **Downgrade:** corpus-dependent claims (privileged candidate families, layer-map physical meaning) are held at `UV_DELEGATED`/`AUDIT`; corpus-agnostic claims (the screen works on standard GR inputs) are the ones we stand behind. We do **not** assert the Fable theory is correct, nor that its candidate families are physically privileged.

## H2.4 The unified self-audit: one gate card for the framework's own weaknesses

The three weaknesses share a single structural property that is the spine of this whole leaf: **all three errors are one-sided toward conservatism.** A guaranteed-failure design, a fail-closed quantum placeholder, and an admissibility-tightening corpus can each only push a candidate **down** the ladder, never up. The framework's worst-case behavior is to be **too strict** — to fail or audit something that, with more computation or a verified theory, might have advanced. It is *structurally incapable* of the dangerous error: a false PASS. This is the property that makes the weaknesses survivable rather than fatal, and it is worth stating as a theorem-shaped claim:

> **Self-audit invariant (one-sided error).** For every point where the framework is incomplete or theory-dependent — the absence of a survivor mode (§H2.1), the interacting quantum placeholder (§H2.2), the unverified corpus (§H2.3) — the incompleteness is wired so that its *only possible effect on a candidate's status* is a **downgrade or a hold** (`FAIL_*`, `AUDIT`, `UV_DELEGATED`), never a promotion. The framework can be wrong by being *too pessimistic*; it cannot be wrong by being *too optimistic.*

This one-sided-error property is the protagonist's character reduced to a theorem: a machine that can only ever err toward calling something dead, never toward calling something alive, is a machine that cannot lie in the dangerous direction. This is not a proof that the framework is *correct* — a too-strict screen still has costs (missed promotions, §H2.1.5; near-zero interacting-quantum resolution, §H2.2.5; possible irrelevance of corpus families, §H2.3.5). It is a proof that the framework is **safe in the direction that matters for a strategic acquirer deciding whether to trust a warp-adjacent claim**: it will never tell the holder a candidate works when it does not. That one-sided safety is precisely what makes the screening capability cheap to option and reputationally protected — an acquirer whose long-horizon valuation rests on Mars-transport optionality can hold a fail-closed validation instrument that cannot embarrass it, because it never overclaims.

The self-audit gate card, in the BUILD CONTRACT §3 schema, applied to the document-as-object:

R5 and R6 are the honest tail. R5: the energy gate is permanently `AUDIT` because every candidate that survives to it so far demands NEC-violating stress-energy, and the framework's job is to *quantify* that exoticity (volume, magnitude, exoticity score), never to wave it away — "the energy gate is never a clean PASS" is a contract clause, not a result we are working to overturn. R7–R9 are the **native-13D-geometry** residuals, surfaced by the C11 attack cluster in H1.3b, and they share the one-sided-error character of the three headline weaknesses (H2.4): each is a way the geometry could be *too strict* or *insufficiently demonstrated*, never a way it leaks a false PASS. R7 is the most important to state plainly and the one most likely to be over-read in the document's favor: the native geometry is **operational** (it makes "new primitive," "double-count," "chamber abuse," and "UV-delegated" into computable verdicts a generic GR screen could not reach), but every one of those operational uses **tightens the admissible set** — none supplies a forward-lobe source, relieves the NEC obstruction, or produces a survivor. The honest concession (canon §0; J1.2) is structural: the only cutoff-safe source term is `L_matter`, ordinary matter satisfies the NEC, and the modulus terms that could supply the right sign route to `UV_DELEGATED`; so the invoice the billing machinery (C11.4) correctly *demands* goes **unpaid by design**. We therefore do **not** claim the 13D geometry designs or builds anything — it supplies a better-constrained design space and a constrained design *compiler*, and the strongest status it confers is `PASS_TOY` on admissibility only. R8 (the double-count detector is sound on declared provenance but not proven complete against laundering) and R9 (`F+` discreteness is fail-closed for the frozen chamber but not proven exhaustive against future holonomy refinements) are honest completeness gaps in the *detectors*, held at `AUDIT` for the completeness claim while remaining fail-closed `PASS` on the frozen inventory — consistent with the rule that an incomplete native-geometry check can only over-reject, never over-pass.

> **First failure of H2.5:** the residual-risk register itself is **not provably complete** — it lists the risks we have found, and a hostile reviewer may surface a structural weakness not in this table. **Downgrade:** the register is `AUDIT` (best-effort, not exhaustive). The honest meta-claim is *"here are the weaknesses we know and how each is contained,"* never *"these are all the weaknesses."*

## H2.6 Patent extraction

The defensible, novel asset in this leaf — distinct from the physics gates patented elsewhere — is the **self-audit / one-sided-error discipline embodied as a status lattice with no upward edge out of `AUDIT`/`FAIL`**, i.e. a *machine-checked guarantee that an incomplete or unverified computation can only downgrade a candidate, never promote it.* Claimable elements: (a) a **fail-closed status classifier** in which "absence of data," "placeholder computation," and "unverified configuration constraint" all map to non-promotable absorbing states (`AUDIT_QUANTUM`, `UV_DELEGATED`, `FAIL_*`), with a schema-enforced guarantee of no outgoing promotion edge; (b) a **placeholder-vs-computed provenance field** on every gate-card sub-result, so a downstream consumer can mechanically separate computed verdicts from bounded-but-open ones; (c) the **option-value decision record** (`V_assets + p·V_hit > C`) attached to a screening apparatus as a structured artifact that justifies the build independent of any input passing. These are method/system/medium claims over *how a screening platform represents and contains its own incompleteness* — useful in any high-stakes simulation discriminator (drug screening, materials, safety-critical control), and valid whether or not any drive, or the Fable theory, is real. The fallback claim, if the broad version is rejected: the specific **one-sided-error status lattice** for a physics-gate ladder with the absorbing `AUDIT`/`UV_DELEGATED` states enumerated.

**Forbidden-claim box for this leaf.** This leaf does **not** claim: that any candidate passes (none does, by design); that the quantum sector is closed (the interacting BV master equation and anomaly are `bv_master_placeholder`); that the Fable/TOE theory is verified (it is not, and the framework does not require it to be); that the framework is *complete* (the residual-risk register is best-effort, not exhaustive); that the apparatus is *proven* cost-justified (`V_assets` vs incumbents is not yet benchmarked). No forbidden phrase from BUILD CONTRACT §4 is asserted; each appears here only to be negated. The strongest allowed claim is the conditional, fail-closed, corpus-agnostic discriminator claim — nothing more.

The framework can only ever be wrong by being **too strict** — it will never tell you a candidate works when it does not. Owning that is the credibility.
