# I1 — Patent Strategy — Invention Families & Independent Claims
**Closure status:** `1 TOY_DEFINED` (strategy / claim-architecture leaf; the patent never asserts more than the document's ceiling of `PASS_TOY`) · **Default mode status:** TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

> **This is not legal advice.** Everything below is engineering input for a registered patent attorney. The attorney — not this document and not its authors — decides final claim scope, claim category, enablement strategy, and filing posture (see §10 handoff). Where this leaf says "claim," read "candidate claim language proposed for attorney review."

---

## 0. Why this chapter exists, and the one decision it makes

Every other chapter of this document is built around a single, deliberately self-defeating premise: **most candidate metric-interface excitation profiles must fail their own gates, and that is the point.** A patent strategy that depends on any of them *passing* — that needs the forward proper-distance functional `D[Ξ]` to actually go negative under a physically available source — is dead on arrival, because the document itself refuses to certify that result above `PASS_TOY`.

So the one decision this chapter makes is a renunciation:

> **We do not claim a drive. We claim the machine that screens, classifies, audits, and visualizes candidate metric-interface excitation profiles, and that emits a status-labeled result for each — including, indeed *especially*, the result "this candidate fails gate X at value Y."**

This is the difference between patenting a perpetual-motion machine (unpatentable, non-enabled, and an instant credibility loss) and patenting the **dynamometer and certification rig** you would use to test one. The rig has value whether or not any device ever spins it. The claimed invention is the rig: the classification and validity-overlay pipeline. Its novelty lives in *how it decides and how it reports*, not in *what it discovers*.

The protectable residue is therefore the protagonist itself — the First-Failure Engine, the discriminator that refuses to certify its own most tempting result — and not the drive the Engine screens. This is why the patent estate is robust to the very outcome the rest of this document predicts: **the claims do not require the drive to work.** Every candidate can fail every gate forever, and the method that catches each failure, names it, and reports it remains novel, enabled, and useful. A patent that needed the drive to be real would die with the drive; a patent on the machine that refuses to lie about the drive survives every failure the drive can produce — indeed it is *validated* by them, because a discriminator is proved by the failures it correctly reports. The asset is the skepticism, made into apparatus and claimed as such.

The remainder of this leaf supplies the attorney with: (§1) the twelve invention families and how they partition the pipeline; (§2) the three independent claim seeds — METHOD, SYSTEM, non-transitory MEDIUM — each with ordered, enablement-bearing steps; (§3) the dependent-claim ladder; (§4) the claim-support matrix mapping each family to spec support / example embodiment / fallback value; (§5) the fallback claims that remain valid *even if every drive mode fails every gate*; (§6) worked enablement vignettes so the steps are not abstract; (§6b) the thirteenth invention family **F13 — the Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System** with its ten-element independent claim, patentable-residue list, §101/Alice posture, and claim-boundary paragraph; (§7) the hard avoid-list; (§8) negative controls on the claim language itself; (§9) the gate-card for this leaf; (§10) the attorney handoff. §I2 (separate leaf) carries the Alice/§101 eligibility memo and prior-art map; this leaf assumes that argument and does not duplicate it.

**First failure named up front:** the strategy's load-bearing weakness is **claim-boundary leakage** — the risk that a dependent claim, a figure caption, or a specification paragraph imports the very physical result ("reduces forward proper distance," "enables propulsion") that the independent claims were carefully built to avoid, thereby (a) inviting an enablement / utility rejection on the whole family and (b) re-opening the FTL-overclaim attack the document's discipline exists to close. Detection and mitigation of this failure is the subject of §7 and the negative controls in §8.

## 1. The twelve invention families

The pipeline is partitioned into twelve invention families. The partition is not cosmetic: each family is (a) a separable software/method unit, (b) independently novel enough to anchor at least one dependent claim, and (c) **independently valuable if the families downstream of it all report FAIL.** Family *k* consuming family *k−1*'s output is the spine of the claim's ordered steps in §2.

| # | Family | What it produces | Layer (`×`/`⊕`/`⊗`) | Standalone product if drive fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **Metric target functionals** | the forward proper-distance functional `D[Ξ]` over a worldtube/forward lobe; a scalar objective | `×` (metric base) | a GR-correct proper-length integrator over user worldtubes |
| F2 | **Vehicle-comoving lobe definitions** | a comoving region operator selecting a front/back-asymmetric lobe along a trajectory | `⊕` (projection/chamber) | a comoving region-of-interest tool for numerical relativity |
| F3 | **Invariant-distance classifiers** | a coordinate-invariance verdict on any apparent `D[Ξ]` change | `×` | a coordinate-artifact rejector for warp/metric sims |
| F4 | **Source-reconstruction engines** | the required effective stress-energy ledger `T_μν^req` from `G_μν` | `×`/`⊕` | a no-free-lunch stress-energy auditor (Einstein-tensor inverter) |
| F5 | **Energy-condition / exoticity engines** | NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC verdicts + a scalar exoticity score | `×` | an exotic-matter screening / energy-condition scanner |
| F6 | **Gauge / BRST classifiers** | a pure-gauge vs. physical verdict; a BRST status field | `⊗` (operators/quant) | a gauge-artifact detector for field-mode catalogs |
| F7 | **UV-dependency classifiers** | a flag: does this candidate require unproven compactification/UV input? | `⊗` | a scope-compliance / UV-delegation tagger |
| F8 | **Gate-card validators** | the fail-closed JSON gate-card and the ladder/downgrade decision | (cross-layer) | a generic fail-closed claim-status engine |
| F9 | **Mission validity overlays** | trajectory/lobe plots **masked and watermarked** by gate status | `⊕` | a validity-weighted mission-visualization tool |
| F10 | **Candidate-mode libraries** | a parameterized library of ansätze (the modes E01…E08, etc.) | `×`/`⊕`/`⊗` | a reusable metric-ansatz catalog with provenance |
| F11 | **Optimization / control representations** | a gate-supervised search/control representation over F10's parameters | `⊕` | a constrained-optimization harness with hard feasibility gates |
| F12 | **Report / patent-figure exporters** | manuscript + patent-figure + gate-table exports | (cross-layer) | a reproducible scientific/patent reporting workflow |

**Reading the partition.** F1→F2 *define what is being measured and where*. F3→F7 are the **five technical gates** (invariance, source, energy, gauge, UV) that any candidate must survive; each is a classifier that can independently return FAIL. F8 is the **decision layer** that composes the gate verdicts into a single fail-closed status. F9–F12 are the **consumption layer**: visualization, the mode library being screened, the search/control representation that proposes new candidates, and the exporter. The crucial property is monotone fail-closure: **the composed status is no stronger than the weakest gate**, formalized in §2 and §8.

Two families deserve emphasis because reviewers under-rate them. **F8 (gate-card validator)** is the single most defensible asset in the entire portfolio, because it is pure software logic with a concrete, novel data structure (the gate-card JSON of the BUILD CONTRACT §3) and a concrete, novel rule (fail-closed composition + a named downgrade tree). It does not mention spacetime at all; it could classify the status of *any* multi-gate physical-plausibility pipeline. **F9 (mission validity overlay)** is the asset most likely to be infringed by an imitator who wants the "pretty Mars picture" without the discipline — and it is exactly the asset most protected by requiring the **gate-status mask + watermark** as a claim limitation, because an honest visualization that suppresses non-passing regions is a specific, describable, non-obvious step.

**First failure for §1 (partition):** the partition's load-bearing weakness is **separability leakage** — the claim that each family is "independently novel and independently valuable if everything downstream FAILs" is only as strong as the weakest inter-family coupling, and several families are *not* cleanly separable (F4 source-reconstruction presupposes F1's functional and chart; F8's fail-closed composition is value-less without at least two upstream gates to compose; F11's optimizer is meaningless without F10's library). Where separability is asserted but not demonstrated, the standalone-product column is a *conjecture about prior art*, not an established fallback, and an examiner may collapse two families into one known unit. This is `TOY_DEFINED` scaffolding: the partition is *proposed*, and the prior-art separability check is deferred to leaf I2 — until then the twelve-way count is an architecture hypothesis, not an enabled fact.

## 2. The three independent claim seeds

We seed three independent claims in the three statutory categories the attorney will most likely want: a **METHOD** (process), a **SYSTEM** (machine/article), and a **non-transitory computer-readable MEDIUM** (the Beauregard form). All three recite the *same ordered pipeline*; the categories differ only in framing. The ordered steps are written so that each step is concretely enabled by a family in §1 and a worked vignette in §6 — this is the enablement spine the §101/§112 defense (leaf I2) leans on.

A design choice threaded through all three: **the output is a status-labeled classification, never a physical assertion.** The claim's final step always outputs a *label* drawn from a closed status set, masked by the gate verdicts. This is what makes the claim about *information processing of model data* rather than about *a propulsion result*, and it is what keeps the claim inside `PASS_TOY`.

### 2.1 Independent claim seed 1 — METHOD

> **Claim 1 (method).** A computer-implemented method for classifying a candidate metric-interface excitation profile, the method comprising:
>
> **(a)** receiving, by one or more processors, a vehicle trajectory specified as a timelike worldline in a spacetime coordinate chart;
> **(b)** defining a vehicle-comoving forward lobe as a region operator that selects a front/back-asymmetric subregion of a worldtube about the trajectory;
> **(c)** receiving a candidate metric-interface excitation profile comprising one or more field perturbation components mapped to a geometric base layer, an admissibility/projection layer, and an operator/quantization layer;
> **(d)** computing a metric target functional comprising a forward proper-distance functional over the forward lobe under the candidate profile;
> **(e)** evaluating a coordinate-invariance diagnostic that compares the functional under at least two distinct coordinate charts and/or scalar curvature invariants, and producing an invariance verdict;
> **(f)** reconstructing an effective source ledger by applying an Einstein-tensor operator to the candidate profile to obtain a required stress-energy distribution, and producing a source verdict;
> **(g)** applying one or more energy-condition diagnostics to the required stress-energy distribution to produce an exoticity score and an energy verdict;
> **(h)** applying a gauge-status diagnostic that distinguishes a pure-gauge perturbation from a physical perturbation, and producing a gauge verdict;
> **(i)** applying a UV-dependency diagnostic that flags whether validity of the candidate requires an externally unresolved compactification or ultraviolet condition, and producing a UV verdict;
> **(j)** composing the invariance, source, energy, gauge, and UV verdicts under a fail-closed rule into a gate-card data structure and a status label selected from a predefined closure-ladder status set, wherein the status label is constrained to be no stronger than the weakest contributing verdict; and
> **(k)** outputting a status-labeled visualization in which a representation of the forward lobe along the trajectory is masked and annotated according to the status label.

The fail-closed composition in step (j) is the heart of the novelty and is expressible as a single monotone operator. With verdicts `v_i ∈ {FAIL=0, AUDIT=1, PASS=2}` over the five gates `i ∈ {inv, src, eng, gau, uv}`, the composed level is

status_level = min_i v_i # weakest gate dominates status_label = LADDER[ min(status_level, CEILING) ] # CEILING = PASS_TOY


so the output can never exceed `PASS_TOY` and can never exceed any single gate. This is the mathematical content of "downgrade, don't invent."

### 2.2 Independent claim seed 2 — SYSTEM

> **Claim 2 (system).** A system for classifying a candidate metric-interface excitation profile, comprising one or more processors and memory storing instructions that, when executed, instantiate:
>
> a **metric-ansatz generation module** configured to receive a vehicle trajectory and a candidate profile and to define a vehicle-comoving forward lobe;
> an **invariant-distance evaluation module** configured to compute a forward proper-distance functional over the lobe and to produce a coordinate-invariance verdict;
> a **source-reconstruction module** configured to apply an Einstein-tensor operator to obtain a required stress-energy ledger and to produce a source verdict;
> an **energy-condition auditing module** configured to apply energy-condition diagnostics and to produce an exoticity score and an energy verdict;
> a **gauge-status classification module** configured to produce a pure-gauge-versus-physical verdict;
> a **UV-dependency classification module** configured to produce a UV-delegation verdict;
> a **gate-card validation module** configured to compose the verdicts under a fail-closed rule into a gate-card data structure and a status label bounded by the weakest verdict and by a predefined ceiling; and
> a **mission-visualization module** configured to render a trajectory-and-lobe visualization masked and watermarked according to the status label.

The system claim deliberately mirrors the method's eleven steps as eight named modules (some method steps collapse into one module, e.g. lobe-definition lives in the ansatz module) so that the **same specification support** enables both, and so that a competitor cannot avoid the system claim by re-ordering steps that the method claim happens to enumerate sequentially.

### 2.3 Independent claim seed 3 — non-transitory MEDIUM

> **Claim 3 (medium).** A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the processors to perform operations comprising the steps (a)–(k) of claim 1.

The Beauregard medium claim is intentionally a thin reference to the method, not a re-recitation, so that any narrowing amendment to the method propagates automatically and so the three categories cannot drift apart during prosecution. **Note for attorney:** confirm jurisdictional treatment — the non-transitory limitation is what keeps this off the *In re Nuijten* signal-claim rock; the word "non-transitory" is load-bearing and must not be dropped in any amendment.

**First failure for §2 (independent seeds):** the seeds' earliest failure is **abstract-idea exposure at Alice step one** — steps (a)–(k) read, to an unsympathetic examiner, as "receive data → compute several mathematical diagnostics → output a label," which is exactly the *mental-process / mathematical-concept* pattern that draws a §101 abstract-idea rejection before enablement is ever reached. The seeds *recite* the inventive concept (the fail-closed `min`-composition with hard ceiling, step (j); the cross-chart invariance computation, step (e); the status-masked render, step (k)) but they cannot *adjudicate* its sufficiency — that is the Alice step-two "significantly more" battle, which this leaf explicitly defers to **I2** and does not win here. Absent that win, the seeds are `TOY_DEFINED` claim *language*, not granted scope; nothing in §2 may be read as a prediction of allowance.

## 3. The dependent-claim ladder

Independent claims are kept **broad and physics-agnostic** (no corpus, no geometry, no exotic matter — per the avoid-list, §7). All specificity descends into dependent claims, which is also where the corpus-derived material (Fable geometry, BRST gates) is quarantined so that a defect in the *unrefereed* corpus cannot invalidate an independent claim. The ladder below is organized by family; each row is a candidate dependent claim depending (unless noted) from claim 1/2/3.

| Dep. | Depends on | Narrows by | Family |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 1 | wherein the forward proper-distance functional is `D[Ξ]=∫_γ √(g_ij dx^i dx^j)` integrated over the forward lobe of a worldtube | F1 |
| D2 | 1 | wherein the forward lobe is front/back-asymmetric with an asymmetry parameter and a comoving offset | F2 |
| D3 | 1 | wherein the invariance diagnostic compares at least one curvature scalar (e.g. a Kretschmann scalar `R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ}`) across charts | F3 |
| D4 | 1 | wherein the source reconstruction computes `T_μν^req = (1/8πG) G_μν[g+δg]` and emits a source-mismatch report | F4 |
| D5 | 4 | wherein the energy diagnostic evaluates NEC `T_μν k^μ k^ν ≥ 0` for null `k^μ` and assigns an exoticity score from the most-violated condition | F5 |
| D6 | 1 | wherein the gauge diagnostic applies a BRST physical-state condition `Q|Ψ⟩=0`, `|Ψ⟩∉ im Q`, and positive norm | F6 |
| D7 | 1 | wherein the UV diagnostic sets a `UV_DELEGATED` flag when the EFT admissibility `χ=max(χ_R,χ_K,χ_T,χ_grad)≥1` or global compactification stability is required | F7 |
| D8 | 1 | wherein the gate-card is a JSON object with named per-gate fields and a `first_failure` field, and the status is selected by the fail-closed `min` rule | F8 |
| D9 | 1 | wherein the visualization suppresses or greys regions whose local status is below a threshold and stamps a status watermark | F9 |
| D10 | 1 | wherein the candidate profile is drawn from a parameterized library of named modes with stored provenance and prior verdicts | F10 |
| D11 | 1 | further comprising proposing a new candidate by a gate-supervised optimizer that rejects any proposal violating a hard feasibility gate before evaluation | F11 |
| D12 | 1 | further comprising exporting a manuscript section and a patent figure with embedded gate-status captions | F12 |
| D13 | 7 | wherein the geometric base is a single-parent compactification `M4 × K_gauge × F+` and the verdict marks corpus-specific admissibility (corpus-quarantined) | F1/F7 |
| D14 | 1 | wherein the status set is the six-level ladder UNDEFINED→…→PHYSICAL_CLAIM and the ceiling is `PASS_TOY` | F8 |

D13 is the **corpus quarantine** row: it is the only place the (unrefereed) Fable/TOE geometry enters a claim, and it enters as a *dependent* limitation so that, if the corpus is later shown wrong, only D13 falls — the independent claim and D1–D12 stand. This is a deliberate risk-isolation move and is called out for the attorney in §10.

**First failure for §3 (dependent ladder):** the ladder's earliest failure is **dependent-claim back-contamination** — a dependent claim that, by narrowing, smuggles a physical-result or resource-provision limitation back into the family (the §101/§112 risk the independent line was built to avoid). D6 (BRST), D7 (UV admissibility `χ≥1`), and especially D13 (corpus geometry) tie validity to *unrefereed* corpus tokens; if any of these is read as asserting that a candidate is physically realizable rather than merely *classified*, it re-imports the excluded result and can drag enablement scrutiny back onto the parent. The quarantine *structure* mitigates but does not *prove* isolation: that each dependent narrows only the *classification*, never the *world*, is an assertion this leaf makes but cannot certify without the I2 eligibility analysis and a per-dependent forbidden-phrase pass. Status: `TOY_DEFINED`.

For each family the attorney needs three things: **(i) specification support** — the part of the manuscript that enables and describes it; **(ii) an example embodiment** — a concrete reduction-to-practice that can be recited or figured; and **(iii) fallback value** — the standalone product the family is, when the drive premise is discarded. This is the deep version of the table in source doc 23, extended with the manuscript cross-reference and the dependent-claim anchor.

| Family | Specification support | Example embodiment | Fallback value (drive-independent) | Anchors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 metric target functional | worldtube + forward-lobe + proper-distance derivation (chapters B/J) | software computes `L_F = D[Ξ]` for a given profile and trajectory | a GR-correct proper-length integrator for any metric/worldline | Cl.1(d), D1 |
| F2 comoving lobe | comoving region-operator definition; asymmetry parameterization | front/back-asymmetric lobe selector with offset parameter | comoving region-of-interest tool for numerical relativity | Cl.1(b), D2 |
| F3 invariant classifier | curvature-scalar / tetrad / geodesic invariance checks (HC-01) | coordinate-only artifact **rejection** (`FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY`) | a scientific validator that rejects coordinate-artifact "results" | Cl.1(e), D3 |
| F4 source ledger | Einstein-tensor → `T_μν^req` reconstruction (HC-02) | source-mismatch report; `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC` | a no-free-lunch stress-energy auditor | Cl.1(f), D4 |
| F5 energy/exoticity | NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC + scalar exoticity score (HC-03) | per-condition violation map + scalar score | exotic-matter / energy-condition screening | Cl.1(g), D5 |
| F6 gauge/BRST | pure-gauge negative controls; BRST status field (HC-05) | BRST status field; `FAIL_PURE_GAUGE` | a gauge-artifact detector that avoids fake modes | Cl.1(h), D6 |
| F7 UV classifier | EFT admissibility `χ<1`; compactification dependency flags (HC-09) | `UV_DELEGATED` status tag | a scope-compliance / UV-delegation tagger | Cl.1(i), D7 |
| F8 gate card | gate-card JSON schema + fail-closed composition (Contract §3) | fail-closed claim-status engine; `first_failure` field | a generic compliance / claim-status engine | Cl.1(j), D8, D14 |
| F9 mission overlay | trajectory/lobe plotting + status mask + watermark (chapter G) | validity-weighted, gate-masked Mars overlay | mission-analysis visualization with validity overlays | Cl.1(k), D9 |
| F10 mode library | parameterized ansatz catalog with provenance (chapter E) | named modes E01…E08 with stored prior verdicts | reusable metric-ansatz catalog | Cl.1(c), D10 |
| F11 optimization/control | gate-supervised search/control representation (chapter F) | optimizer that rejects infeasible proposals pre-eval | constrained-optimization harness with hard feasibility gates | D11 |
| F12 report exporter | manuscript/patent-figure export with gate captions | figure caption generator with embedded status | reproducible scientific/patent reporting workflow | D12 |

**How to read the "fallback value" column.** It is the answer to the examiner's (and the skeptic's) sharpest question: *"What did you actually invent, if the drive doesn't work?"* The honest, sufficient answer is that **each row is independently a useful, novel piece of scientific or compliance software** — a proper-length integrator, an Einstein-tensor source auditor, a coordinate-artifact rejector, an energy-condition scanner, a gauge-artifact detector, a fail-closed status engine, a validity-masked visualizer. None of these requires the drive to work. None even requires the Fable corpus to be true. That is precisely the property §5 makes explicit.

**First failure for §4 (support matrix):** the matrix's earliest failure is **unverified specification support** — every "Specification support" cell points at a *manuscript chapter that may not yet exist or may not yet supply §112-grade enablement* (the cells cite chapters B/J, HC-01…HC-09, chapters E/F/G, and Contract §3; at this leaf none of those cross-references has been confirmed written, negative-controlled, and gate-carded). A claim-support matrix whose support column is a set of *promissory* pointers is a `TOY_DEFINED` planning artifact: if a cited chapter under-delivers, the corresponding family loses written-description support and the dependent claim anchored to it (the "Anchors" column) is unsupported. The matrix is honest about *intent*; it does not and cannot certify that the support already exists — that verification is a downstream cross-reference audit, not a result claimed here.

## 5. Fallback claims — defensible even if every mode fails every gate

This is the strategy's keystone and the reason it survives the document's own fail-closed discipline. It is also the precise point where the patent stops depending on the dream and starts depending only on the protagonist: the claims below describe *the Engine's method of refusing*, and that method is whole even in a world where there is nothing worth refusing. Construct the **worst possible world for the invention**: every candidate mode in the library (E01…E08 and all future modes) returns FAIL on at least one of the five gates; `D[Ξ]` never goes negative under any physically available source; the corpus is later refuted; FTL is, as expected, impossible. In that world, the following claims are **still valid, novel, useful, and enabled**, because none of them asserts that any candidate passes:

1. **Invalid-profile detection.** A method/system/medium that *identifies and labels* a candidate profile as invalid by gate — e.g. emitting `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC`. Utility: rejecting bogus metric-engineering proposals is itself the product. *More* failures make this claim *more* clearly useful, not less.
2. **Coordinate-artifact rejection.** A classifier that flags an apparent distance reduction as a coordinate artifact (`FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY`) by cross-chart and curvature-invariant comparison. Independent of any drive.
3. **Stress-energy reconstruction / no-free-lunch audit.** Given a target metric, reconstruct and report the required `T_μν^req` and its mismatch against any declared available source. This is a pure GR computation; its correctness does not depend on the source existing.
4. **Exoticity scoring.** Given `T_μν^req`, score the most-violated energy condition. Useful as exotic-propulsion *screening* regardless of whether anything ever screens through.
5. **Speculative-physics compliance reporting.** Emit a fail-closed, status-labeled, audit-visible report that constrains downstream claims to no stronger than the weakest gate. This is a compliance/governance tool for *any* speculative-physics modeling shop.
6. **Mission visualization with validity overlays.** Render mission plots that are *masked and watermarked* by validity status — the honest-visualization claim. Its novelty is the suppression/annotation step, not any plotted result.

The formal statement of why these survive: define the claim's truth-conditions to range only over **outputs of the pipeline given inputs**, never over **states of the physical world**. The method "classifies and labels"; it does not "propel" or "shorten." A claim whose only assertions are about *what label the software emits for given model data* is true exactly when the software emits that label — a verifiable, enabled, repeatable fact — and is **logically independent of whether any candidate is physically realizable.** That independence is the whole game.

text

Fallback-survival check (run against the full mode library)

all_fail = True for mode in library: # E01..E08 and beyond gc = run_pipeline(mode) # F1..F8 all_fail = all_fail and (gc.status_level == FAIL)

The six fallback claims (F3,F4,F5,F6,F8,F9 read as classifiers/reporters)

remain VALID under all_fail == True, because each asserts only:

"given input X, the pipeline emits label L(X)"

and never:

"the physical world does Y."

assert fallback_claims_valid_regardless_of(all_fail) # by construction


**First failure for §5:** the fallback claims are robust to physics failure but **not** robust to a §101 *abstract-idea* rejection — "classify and label model data" can be attacked as a mental process / abstract idea performed on a computer. That eligibility battle is real and is fought in leaf **I2** (Alice step-two: the *fail-closed gate-card data structure*, the *cross-chart invariance computation*, and the *status-masked rendering* are the "significantly more" inventive-concept anchors). This leaf flags the dependency and does not resolve it.

## 6. Worked enablement vignettes

Independent-claim steps must be *enabled*, not merely named, or §112 swallows the family. Three short, numerically concrete vignettes give the specification something to point at. Each is a `TOY_MODEL`; none promotes any candidate.

**Vignette A — step (d)/(e), proper distance and its invariance gate.** Take a toy 1+1 lobe metric `ds² = −dt² + (1+h(x))² dx²` with a bump `h(x) = −A·exp(−x²/2σ²)`, `A=0.05`, `σ=1` (units of the lobe scale). The forward proper distance across `x∈[−3,3]` is `L = ∫ (1+h) dx ≈ 6 − A·σ√(2π) ≈ 6 − 0.05·2.5066 ≈ 5.875`, an apparent reduction of `ΔL ≈ −0.125`. Step (e) then recomputes `L` after the coordinate change `x̃ = x + h-dependent shift` and compares the Kretschmann scalar across charts. **If** `ΔL` vanishes under the chart change while invariants are unchanged ⇒ verdict `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY`; the −0.125 is reported and **downgraded**, never certified. This is the enabling description for step (e): the diagnostic is a concrete two-chart recomputation, not a black box.

**Vignette B — step (f)/(g), source ledger and exoticity.** From the same `δg`, step (f) forms `T_μν^req = (1/8πG) G_μν[g+δg]`. For the toy bump the energy density at the lobe center carries a sign set by `h''(0) = A/σ² > 0` in a way that drives the null-projected `T_μν^req k^μ k^ν` **negative** over part of the lobe ⇒ NEC violated ⇒ exoticity score `> 0` ⇒ energy verdict `AUDIT`, source verdict `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` if no available source is declared. Worked: with `A=0.05`, `σ=1`, the most-negative null projection is `O(−A/σ²) ≈ −0.05` in lobe units; the exoticity score is the normalized magnitude of the worst violation, here `≈ 0.05/(0.05) = 1.0` against its own scale — a clean "exotic" flag. This enables steps (f)–(g) as explicit tensor algebra plus a sign scan.

**Vignette C — step (j), fail-closed composition.** Verdict vector for Vignette A/B: `inv=FAIL(0)`, `src=FAIL(0)`, `eng=AUDIT(1)`, `gau=PASS(2)`, `uv=AUDIT(1)`. Then `status_level = min = 0 = FAIL`; `status_label = LADDER[min(0, CEILING)] = FAIL`. The candidate is rejected at the floor. **Crucially, the ceiling never even engages** because a single gate failed — demonstrating that the composition is sound: you cannot buy back a failed gate with passing ones. This is the enabling description for the claim's most novel step.

These three vignettes, with their numbers, are what convert the independent-claim steps from aspiration into enabled process — and they do so *while exhibiting failures*, consistent with the document's discipline.

**First failure for §6 (enablement vignettes):** the vignettes' earliest failure is **toy-scale enablement gap** — they are deliberately 1+1-dimensional, linearized, single-bump `TOY_MODEL`s whose numbers (`L≈5.875`, exoticity `≈1.0`) are *internally consistent reference computations*, **not** validated 3+1 results, and so they enable the *steps* (a two-chart recompute, a tensor-algebra source inversion, a `min`-composition) but **not** the *full claimed generality* of step (d)–(j) over arbitrary 3+1 profiles. An examiner can fairly ask whether the disclosed toy supports a claim broad enough to cover realistic worldtubes; the honest answer is that the breadth is supported only to the extent the downstream HC chapters (HC-01/02/03) supply the 3+1 algorithms, which this leaf cites but does not contain. The vignette numbers are therefore marked **reference computations** and must never be read as certifying any candidate; they certify only that the *procedure* is concretely executable on at least one worked instance. Status: `TOY_TESTED` for the procedure, `TOY_DEFINED` for the claimed generality.

## 6b. Invention family F13 — the Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System

The twelve families of §1 partition the *generic* screening pipeline. The native-13D design pass adds a **thirteenth invention family, F13 — the Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System** — which is the most defensible *non-physics* asset in the portfolio because, like F8, it is pure software/method logic over a concrete, novel data discipline, and it does not mention propulsion, a drive, or a metric *effect* anywhere. F13 claims the **machine that classifies a candidate against a frozen extra-dimensional background inventory, projects its internal descendants into 4D, bills them to a source ledger, detects double-counting, and routes UV-sensitive modes — emitting a gate-card that can only ever downgrade or hold a candidate, never promote it.** Its authority in the manuscript is the native-geometry layer: the frozen parent `𝓜_parent = M4 × K_gauge × F+`, `K_gauge = K6 × S² × S¹_Y` (`C3`); the projection `Π: G_MN → g_μν` and billing rule (`C1 §9`); the layer discipline and gate-card schema (`A1 §3.2 / §3.3`); the production admissibility projector `Π_adm = Π_freeze·Π_chamber·Π_layer·Π_dup` (`D4 §2.3`); the no-double-count audit (`C3.6.4`).

| # | Family | What it produces | Layer (`×`/`⊕`/`⊗`) | Standalone product if drive fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F13 | **Native Geometry Admissibility & Projection System** | a gate-card classifying a candidate's native origin, layer assignment, projection path, source billing, double-count status, and UV class against a frozen background inventory | (cross-layer: `×`/`⊕`/`⊗`) | a general **admissibility-and-projection validator** for any frozen-background field-screening pipeline (KK reductions, lattice/EFT mode catalogs, multi-sector model auditing) |

### 6b.1 The ten-element independent claim (METHOD seed; SYSTEM/MEDIUM mirror it)

> **Claim N (method) — Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection.** A computer-implemented method for classifying a candidate field-excitation profile against a frozen higher-dimensional background, the method comprising:
>
> **(1) Intake.** receiving, by one or more processors, a candidate excitation profile comprising one or more field-perturbation components;
> **(2) Frozen-background module.** loading a content-addressed, immutable background inventory specifying a four-dimensional spacetime block, an internal gauge-geometry block comprising a product of compact factors, and a discrete admissibility chamber that is not a coordinate dimension, together with a frozen field menu and a freeze hash, and rejecting any profile that alters the inventory as a background-drift failure;
> **(3) Native-origin classifier.** assigning to each component a declared internal origin selected from a closed origin set comprising a four-dimensional-direct origin, one origin per internal compact factor, a mixed off-diagonal origin, an internal-metric/modulus origin, a matter origin, and a constraint origin;
> **(4) Layer validator.** assigning to each component exactly one layer selected from a metric/geometric base layer, an admissibility/projection/chamber layer, and an operator/quantization layer, and returning a new-primitive failure if a component has no layer and a double-count failure if a component has two;
> **(5) Admissibility projector.** applying an idempotent admissibility projector composed of a freeze projector, a chamber projector, a layer projector, and a duplication projector, and computing an admissibility defect equal to the normalized residual of the profile under the projector;
> **(6) 13D→4D projection.** applying a declared projection that maps the higher-dimensional metric to the four-dimensional metric block, whereby off-diagonal internal descendants become licensed four-dimensional source channels rather than free four-dimensional metric levers;
> **(7) Source-ledger billing.** for each internal descendant that influences the four-dimensional metric, requiring a corresponding entry in a stress-energy source ledger, and returning an unsourced-metric failure when no entry exists;
> **(8) Double-count detector.** tracing each descendant to its parent internal direction and returning a double-count failure when a descendant is booked both as an operator-layer stress and as a geometric-base source with the same provenance;
> **(9) UV-sensitivity router.** comparing each descendant's internal-momentum support to a frozen compactification scale and routing a descendant above that scale, or one whose closure requires an externally unresolved global-stability condition, to a UV-delegated status;
> **(10) Gate-card output.** emitting a gate-card data structure recording the geometry origin, layer assignment, projection path, admissibility defect, source billing, chamber status, double-count status, UV status, first native-geometry failure, and a strongest-allowed-claim field bounded by a predefined ceiling and constrained to be no stronger than the weakest contributing verdict.

The **fail-closed monotonicity** of F13 mirrors F8's `min`-composition and is the inventive core: every element (2)–(9) can only emit a *failure or downgrade token* (`FAIL_BACKGROUND_DRIFT`, `FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE`, `FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT`, `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC`, `FAIL_CHAMBER`, `UV_DELEGATED`) or pass-through; **no element can promote a candidate**, and element (10)'s strongest-allowed-claim is hard-bounded by the document ceiling `PASS_TOY`. This one-sided-error structure (it can over-reject, never over-pass) is the same machine-checked guarantee patented in H2.6, here specialized to the native-geometry inventory.

### 6b.2 Dependent-claim hooks for F13

These descend from Claim N (and slot alongside the §3 ladder; D13 remains the corpus-quarantine row):

| Dep. | Depends on | Narrows by |

### 6b.3 Patentable-residue list for F13 (survives even if every mode fails every gate)

Per the document's discipline, F13's value does **not** depend on any candidate passing. Even if every mode in the library fails every gate forever, the following native-geometry assets remain novel, enabled, and useful as classification/audit software:

- **native-origin classifier** — maps each component to a declared internal origin (the license tag selecting ledger/UV-class/BRST/double-count rules);
- **chamber-abuse detector** — rejects any attempt to excite a discrete admissibility chamber as a continuous knob, pre-source;
- **internal-descendant source router** — routes each projected descendant to its mandatory stress-energy ledger entry;
- **double-count detector** — provenance-traced single-booking enforcement (one-parent projection);
- **13D→4D projection audit** — verifies that internal geometry reaches 4D only through the declared projection, never as a direct metric lever;
- **layer-assignment validator** — total-and-disjoint `×/⊕/⊗` mapping with new-primitive / double-count failures;
- **UV-sensitivity router** — auto-tags KK descendants by compactification scale and global-stability dependency;
- **freeze-hash background-drift detector** — content-addressed immutability of the parent inventory;
- **native-geometry gate-card schema extension** — the `native_geometry` block recording origin/layer/projection/billing/chamber/double-count/UV/first-native-failure;
- **geometry-to-patent residue map** — the mapping from each native check to the surviving claimable asset.

Each is a **general** capability: replace the specific extra-dimensional inventory with any other fixed background and the algorithm is unchanged — which is exactly why F13 is patentable independent of whether the unified theory, or any drive, is real.

### 6b.4 §101 / Alice technical-improvement posture for F13

F13's eligibility posture is the same three-ground theory the eligibility memo (leaf I2) develops for the pipeline as a whole, specialized to the native layer:

- **Ground B (the strongest, *Finjan*-style fail-closed engine).** F13's gate-card is a **specific status data structure** whose fail-closed state *controls downstream behavior*: a `FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE`, `FAIL_DOUBLE_COUNT`, `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC`, `FAIL_CHAMBER`, or `UV_DELEGATED` verdict **vetoes** the descendant's contribution to any downstream metric functional and forbids over-strong claim emission. This is *significantly more* than abstract classification — it is a compliance/control engine coupled to a downstream technological function, the *Finjan v. Blue Coat* footing.
- **Ground C (the *Bascom/Flook*-2B inventive concept).** The **backward, provenance-traced projection-and-billing** transformation — reconstruct each descendant's required source from the frozen inventory, trace it to a single parent direction, and emit a double-count / unsourced verdict — is a *particular ordered arrangement* that no general-purpose differential-geometry package performs (EinsteinPy / GRTensor / SageManifolds / xAct are forward, user-driven calculators with no admissibility verdict; see I2 §7–§8). The freeze-hash background-drift check and the chamber-abuse detector are likewise non-conventional.
- **Ground A (the *Diehr/McRO* process improvement).** F13 improves the **fidelity of a frozen-background screening process** by automatically rejecting new-primitive, chamber-abuse, and background-drift artifacts *before they propagate* — a concrete technical improvement to the operation of the screening pipeline, not mere display.

The §101 concessions are the same and are made up front: the tensor algebra and the projection are real mathematics; a naive "classify the profile against a background" claim drafted broad is vulnerable at *Alice* step one (*Electric Power Group*); generic computer implementation saves nothing. The inventive concept that integrates the exception into a practical application is the **fail-closed, provenance-traced, freeze-hash-pinned veto coupling** of elements (2)/(5)/(7)/(8)/(9), not the geometry math.

### 6b.5 The F13 claim-boundary paragraph (load-bearing)

> **Claim boundary for F13.** The disclosed Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System and method **do not require the physical correctness of any particular unified theory.** A native higher-dimensional geometry is used solely as a **frozen background inventory** defining metric blocks, internal-origin labels, an admissibility chamber, layer assignments, and projection paths. The system **classifies, rejects, or downgrades** candidate profiles based on violations of that inventory — emitting native first-failure tokens and a ceiling-bounded status — **without asserting that any candidate profile constitutes a physical propulsion device**, without asserting that any candidate reduces forward proper distance, and without asserting that the higher-dimensional geometry produces propulsion, energy closure, source closure, global stability, or any travel-time reduction. The geometry supplies a *constrained admissible design space*, not a drive. Every native-geometry verdict the system can emit is a downgrade or a hold; the system is structurally incapable of promoting a candidate, and its strongest output is `PASS_TOY` on the *admissibility property only*. The patent reads on the *classification/projection/billing/filtering machinery*, which is enabled and useful whether or not the unified theory, or any drive, is real.

**First failure for §6b (F13):** F13's earliest failure is **the same claim-boundary leakage named in §0** — a dependent claim, figure caption, or specification paragraph that imports the excluded physical result by treating the geometry as *enabling* a candidate (e.g. "the native projection sources a forward lobe") rather than *constraining/classifying* it (e.g. "the native projection bills the descendant or returns `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC`"). Mitigation is the F13 claim-boundary paragraph (§6b.5), the avoid-list (§7), the negative controls (§8), and the manuscript-wide forbidden-phrase scan — none yet fully closed. A second, structural residual: F13's standalone-product and separability claims share the §1 *separability-leakage* weakness — F13's billing element presupposes the source-reconstruction transformation of family F4, so F13 and F4 are not perfectly separable, and the "general admissibility validator" fallback is a *conjecture about prior art* pending the I2 separability check. Status: `TOY_DEFINED` (the family is *proposed* claim architecture; the prior-art and boundary checks are deferred to I2).

## 7. The hard avoid-list

These constructions must **never** appear in an independent claim, and must be quarantined to dependent claims or omitted entirely. Each is paired with the failure it would cause.

| Avoid (in independent claims) | Why — the failure it triggers |
|---|---|
| "a working / operational drive," "propulsion," "thrust," "reduces forward proper distance" *as a result* | imports a non-enabled, no-utility physical result ⇒ §101 utility + §112 enablement rejection on the whole family; re-opens the FTL-overclaim attack |
| "faster-than-light," "exceeds the speed of light," "Mars in days" | unpatentable subject matter / inoperability; instant credibility loss with examiner and reader |
| any **particular high-energy source**, reactor, pulsed-power, beam, radiation source, or hardware-build step | (i) violates the document's safety boundary outright; (ii) narrows the claim to hardware we cannot and will not enable; (iii) creates an export-control surface |
| "negative energy is available," "exotic matter is provided" | asserts an unestablished physical resource ⇒ enablement failure; turns an *audit* claim into a *provision* claim |
| "global stability solved," "UV completion adopted/closed," "quantum gravity solved" | asserts closure the corpus explicitly leaves OPEN/UNADOPTED ⇒ false statement + enablement failure |
| corpus-specific geometry (`M4 × K_gauge × F+`, `SU(3)/T²`) **in an independent claim** | ties independent validity to an *unrefereed* framework; keep in dependent D13 / DN1 (corpus quarantine) |
| "the native geometry / 13D projection **sources / enables / produces** a forward lobe (or any metric effect)" | imports the excluded physical result; F13 may only *classify, bill, or reject*, never *enable* — re-opens FTL-overclaim + §101 utility; the geometry supplies a constrained design space, not a drive |
| "no propellant needed," "solves the energy problem" | forbidden-phrase-list violations; over-broad utility assertions |
| a transitory signal medium (drop "non-transitory") | *In re Nuijten* — signal claims are non-statutory |

**Operating rule for the drafter:** the independent claims contain *no physics result and no hardware* — only **receiving model inputs, computing diagnostics, composing a fail-closed status, and rendering a status-labeled output.** Everything physical, exotic, corpus-specific, or hardware-adjacent lives below the independent line, or not at all. The §7 table *is* the boundary that the §0 "first failure" (claim-boundary leakage) is the failure to maintain.

**First failure for §7 (avoid-list):** the avoid-list's earliest failure is **enumeration incompleteness** — a blacklist can only forbid the leaks it anticipated, so its first failure is the *unenumerated* leak: a synonym ("traversal time reduced," "effective transit shortened"), a unit-bearing figure caption, or a means-plus-function term whose §112(f) construction imports a hardware structure, none of which appears in the table yet each of which re-opens the excluded result. A forbidden-construction list is therefore a *necessary but not sufficient* control; it must be paired with the affirmative "Operating rule" allow-list above (claims may contain *only* receive/compute/compose/render) and with the manuscript-wide automated scan, because a closed allow-list fails safe where an open blacklist fails open. Until that scan is green this list is `TOY_DEFINED` guidance, not a proven boundary.

## 8. Negative controls on the claim language

The chapter template requires a negative control per object. Here the "objects" are the claims, so the controls are **adversarial rewrites that a careless drafter might produce**, each of which the strategy must reject. A claim that *passes* any of these controls (i.e. reads like the bad rewrite) is defective.

| Negative control (bad claim) | Correct verdict | Rejection token |
|---|---|---|
| NC-1: "A method of propelling a vehicle by reducing forward proper distance, comprising…" | **REJECT** — asserts the physical result | `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` |
| NC-2: "…outputting that the candidate enables faster-than-light travel." | **REJECT** — FTL assertion | `FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM` |
| NC-3: "…wherein negative energy is supplied to the forward lobe." | **REJECT** — provides exotic resource | `FAIL_HIDDEN_EXOTICITY` |
| NC-4: "…the status label being PASS when the proper distance decreases." | **REJECT** — promotes above ceiling; ignores other gates | `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` |
| NC-5: independent claim reciting `M4 × K_gauge × F+` | **REJECT (from independent)** — corpus in independent line | move to D13 |
| NC-6: medium claim dropping "non-transitory" | **REJECT** — signal claim | non-statutory (Nuijten) |
| NC-7: "…composing the verdicts such that any passing gate may raise the status." | **REJECT** — violates monotone fail-closure | `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` |
| NC-8: "…wherein the native projection of an internal descendant **sources** the forward lobe." | **REJECT** — F13 may bill or reject a descendant, never *source* an effect | `FORBIDDEN_PROMOTION` / `FAIL_UNSOURCED_METRIC` |
| NC-9: "…wherein the admissibility chamber is **tuned** to increase the metric effect." | **REJECT** — treats the `dim 0` chamber as a continuous knob | `FAIL_CHAMBER` / `FAIL_NEW_PRIMITIVE` |

NC-4 and NC-7 are the subtle, most-likely-real defects, because they look like ordinary claim drafting. The control against both is the **monotone `min`-composition with hard ceiling** of step (j): formally, the composition operator must satisfy `status(v) ≤ min_i v_i` and `status(v) ≤ CEILING` for *all* verdict vectors `v`, with no exception path. Any drafted claim whose composition admits a "buy-back" of a failed gate (NC-7) or a PASS on a single favorable metric (NC-4) is, by this test, defective and must be rewritten. This negative-control set is itself a disclosable test suite (it belongs alongside F8). NC-8 and NC-9 are the native-geometry analogues for F13: the same monotone fail-closure forbids any element (2)–(9) from *sourcing* an effect (NC-8 — a descendant may only be billed or rejected) or *tuning* the `dim 0` admissibility chamber (NC-9 — chamber selection is discrete and pre-source), so a drafted F13 claim that lets the native projection enable a metric effect is, by the same test, defective.

**First failure for §8:** these controls catch *syntactic* leakage in claim text, but they cannot catch *semantic* leakage in the **specification and figures** — e.g. a spec paragraph that narrates "the drive then moves the vehicle," or a figure captioned "Mars transit enabled." That residual leakage is the §0 first failure, and it is mitigated only by a manuscript-wide forbidden-phrase scan (chapter A1's `review/forbidden_promotion_scan.md`) and by the F12 exporter stamping gate-status captions automatically — neither of which is fully closed at this leaf.

## 10. Attorney handoff

The following decisions are explicitly reserved to the attorney; engineering recommendations are noted but are **not** instructions:

1. **Claim category mix.** Recommend filing all three categories (method/system/medium); attorney decides emphasis and whether to add a means-plus-function variant. *Caution:* §112(f) means-plus-function would import the spec's algorithms as the corresponding structure — acceptable here only because §6 supplies concrete algorithms.
2. **"Control" vs. "simulation/classification" language.** F11 introduces a *gate-supervised control/optimization representation*. Recommend keeping "control" in a **dependent** claim (D11) and the independent claims in "classification/visualization" language, to minimize the §101 surface. Attorney decides (source-doc 23, question 2).
3. **Breadth of "metric-interface excitation."** Recommend defining it functionally in the spec (field perturbation components mapped to the three layers) to avoid indefiniteness; attorney decides whether a definitional clause appears in the claim (source-doc 23, question 3).
4. **Corpus placement.** Strong engineering recommendation: keep all Fable/TOE-specific geometry in dependent claims (D13) — corpus quarantine — never independent (source-doc 23, question 4). The corpus is **not peer-reviewed**; independent-claim validity must not depend on it.
5. **Hardware.** Recommend omitting hardware entirely from claims; if the attorney wants prospective coverage, keep it as a *broad, non-enabling* prospective embodiment in the spec only, flagged non-enabling, and **never** as a high-energy-source or build step (source-doc 23, question 5; document safety boundary).
6. **Aerospace-simulation vs. physics-validation framing.** Both fallback markets are real (§4–§5); recommend drafting the spec to support either, so the attorney can steer the §101 argument (I2) toward whichever has the stronger inventive-concept story (source-doc 23, question 1).

**Provisional posture.** A provisional *may* discuss prospective physical embodiments, but the durable support is software/simulation/control; keep physical source details broad and non-enabling (source-doc 19, caveat). File the pipeline now; let the corpus and any candidate results mature into continuation material that never up-levels the independent claims.

**First failure for §10 (attorney handoff):** the handoff's earliest failure is **authority and scope leakage at the boundary** — this leaf is engineering input, not legal advice, and its first failure is the risk that a *recommendation* (file all three categories; quarantine the corpus; omit hardware) is mistaken for a *decision*, or that an "engineering recommendation" silently encodes a legal conclusion the drafter is not authorized to reach (e.g. treating the §5 fallback claims as *granted* rather than *proposed*). Per Contract §1.4, no agent may self-promote status or scope; the six reserved decisions stay with the attorney, and any prospective-hardware embodiment must remain *broad and non-enabling* (never a high-energy-source or build step). This boundary cannot be *enforced* by the leaf itself — only flagged — so the residual leakage (a downstream reader acting on a recommendation as if it were an authorization) remains open until the attorney signs off. Status: `TOY_DEFINED`; no decision in §10 is made on this leaf's authority.

Until a manuscript-wide forbidden-phrase scan plus the F12 auto-captioning exporter are wired and green, the leakage risk — which would trigger a §101 utility / §112 enablement rejection on the whole family and re-open the FTL-overclaim attack — remains open. · **What remains to close:** (1) leaf **I2** — the Alice/§101 eligibility memo (inventive concept = the fail-closed gate-card data structure + cross-chart invariance computation + status-masked rendering) and the prior-art map vs. EinsteinPy / GRTensor / published warp-metric simulators, with examiner-response strategy; (2) a green manuscript-wide forbidden-phrase scan over spec + figures; (3) attorney finalization of the six reserved decisions in §10. · **Patent extraction:** the disclosable assets are the **twelve invention families plus F13 (the Native Geometry Admissibility and Projection System, §6b)**; the **three independent claim seeds** (method/system/medium) with their ordered, enablement-bearing steps and the **monotone `min`-composition fail-closed rule with hard `PASS_TOY` ceiling** (the single most defensible novelty, family F8); the **F13 ten-element independent claim** (intake → frozen-background `M4×K_gauge×F+` → native-origin classifier → `×/⊕/⊗` layer validator → admissibility projector → 13D→4D projection → source-ledger billing → double-count detector → UV-sensitivity router → gate-card output), one-sided-error by construction (it can only downgrade/hold, never promote), with its **claim-boundary paragraph** (does not require the unified theory to be correct; classifies/rejects candidates without asserting any is a propulsion device); the **dependent-claim ladder with corpus-quarantine rows D13 / DN1**; the **six fallback claims** that remain valid even if every mode fails every gate; and the **claim-language negative-control suite** (NC-1…NC-9) usable as a drafting test. · **Reviewer attack:** *"This is a patent on a perpetual-motion machine wrapped in disclaimers — claiming the 'classifier' is a dodge to get a warp-drive patent issued, and the fallback talk is window-dressing."* **Honest response:** the independent claims contain **no physical result, no propulsion, no FTL, and no hardware** — they recite only receiving model data, computing five GR/EFT diagnostics, composing a status by a `min`-rule that *cannot* output above `PASS_TOY` or above the weakest gate, and rendering a *masked* overlay; the §8 controls **reject** every version of the claim that would assert the drive (NC-1…NC-4, NC-7), and the §5 fallback claims are constructed to be *more* clearly useful precisely when *all* candidates fail. A claim whose truth-conditions range only over "what label the software emits for given inputs," never over "what the physical world does," is the opposite of a perpetual-motion patent: it is a certified, enabled, falsifiable piece of scientific-compliance software whose headline asset is the machinery that *publishes the failures*. The eligibility fight this objection really points at is §101, and it is fought — not hand-waved — in leaf I2.

# I2 — Patentability — Alice/Section 101 Eligibility Memo & Prior-Art Map
**Closure status:** `1 TOY_DEFINED` (this chapter defines the eligibility object and the prior-art delta as auditable artifacts; it promotes no candidate and proves no propulsion) · **Default mode status:** TOY_MODEL/AUDIT

> **THIS CHAPTER IS NOT LEGAL ADVICE.** It is a patent-engineering memo prepared by a technical author to *brief a registered patent attorney* and to *organize the technical record* so that an attorney can make the eligibility and prior-art calls. Nothing here is an opinion of counsel, a freedom-to-operate clearance, a validity opinion, or a representation that any claim will issue. Statutory citations and case names are used as engineering checklists, not as adjudications. The attorney decides claim breadth, claim category, and filing strategy (see I1 §"Attorney handoff" and the five attorney questions in source doc 23). Every eligibility conclusion below is a *candidate argument to be tested*, defaulted — like every drive mode in this corpus — to the conservative status until an authority promotes it.

## 0. Why §101 is the load-bearing risk for *this* invention

Most of the patent risk for the Mars metric-interface platform is not novelty and is not obviousness. It is **subject-matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. §101** as construed by *Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank* (2014) and its progeny. The reason is structural and we should state it without flinching, because the BUILD CONTRACT's fail-closed discipline applies to legal claims exactly as it applies to physics claims: *we name the failure first, then argue the counter.* And the eligible thing being claimed is, again, the protagonist and not the dream — the screening/diagnostic/compliance pipeline, the machine that refuses to certify a metric until it has audited the source and the energy behind it. That object is what the §101 argument must defend, and its eligibility, like its value, **does not require any drive to work**: the invention is the disciplined act of screening, which is performed identically whether the candidate passes or (as always) fails.

The invention is, on its face, a pipeline that (a) computes tensors from a metric ansatz, (b) evaluates mathematical inequalities (energy conditions, invariant-distance functionals, admissibility ratios), (c) classifies the result into status buckets, and (d) renders a visualization. Stated that baldly, an examiner's first-pass characterization writes itself: *"the claims are directed to a mathematical concept (differential geometry and tensor algebra) combined with the abstract idea of classifying data according to rules, implemented on a generic computer."* That characterization, if it stands, is fatal under *Alice* step one, and the "apply it on a computer" implementation does nothing to rescue it at step two (*Alice*; *Gottschalk v. Benson*, 1972, on algorithms; *Parker v. Flook*, 1978, on a mathematical formula plus conventional activity). **This is the first failure of the entire patent leg, and it is the honest default status of the claims: presumptively §101-ineligible as drafted-broad.**

So the eligibility question is not *"can we hide the math?"* — we cannot, and attempting to is both futile and a credibility liability under the contract's anti-self-promotion rule. The question is the *Diehr/McRO/Enfish/Finjan* question: **does the claimed pipeline effect a specific, concrete technical improvement to a technological process, such that the claim is directed to that improvement rather than to the underlying mathematics?** Our entire eligibility theory rests on answering *yes*, on three independent and stackable grounds, and on drafting the claims so the improvement — not the math — is what the claim is *directed to*.

**First failure (this section):** the claims are characterized as "math + classification on a generic computer" at *Alice* step one and never escape. The mitigation is the three-ground technical-improvement theory of §3–§4 plus the integration-into-a-practical-application argument under the 2019 PEG (§5), and — critically — claim drafting (§6) that recites the *specific data transformations and the fail-closed control output*, not a result-orientated "classify the profile" abstraction.

---

## 1. The statutory and case-law frame (engineering checklist form)

We use the USPTO's own two-step framework (MPEP 2106, the *Alice/Mayo* test as the Office operationalizes it) because that is the frame the examiner is *required* to apply. We do not relitigate the case law; we map our facts onto it.

| Step | Question (Office form) | Our exposure | Our handle |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2A prong 1 | Does the claim *recite* a judicial exception (abstract idea / math concept / mental process)? | **Yes — unavoidably.** Tensor math + energy-condition inequalities + classification are a "mathematical concept" and arguably a "mental process" grouping under the 2019 PEG. | Concede prong 1. Do not fight here. |
| 2A prong 2 | Is the exception *integrated into a practical application*? | This is the battlefield. | The fail-closed compliance/control engine + improved simulation diagnostics are the practical application (§5). |
| 2B | If not integrated: does the claim add an *inventive concept* — significantly more than the exception + well-understood, routine, conventional activity? | Fallback battlefield. | The specific invariant/source-ledger transformation pipeline is *not* routine or conventional in GR tooling (§4, §8 prior-art delta). |

Two anchors from the case law do real work for us and we lean on them explicitly:

- ***McRO v. Bandai* (Fed. Cir. 2016):** a claim reciting a *specific* set of rules that produces a *specific* technical result (there, automated lip-sync) is eligible even though "rules" sound abstract, because the claim is directed to the *improvement* the specific rules achieve, not to the idea of using rules. Our analog: the *specific gate order* (invariant → source → energy → gauge → causality → UV) and the *specific fail-closed downgrade transitions* are concrete rules producing a concrete technical artifact (a status-validated diagnostic), not the abstract idea of "classifying physics models."
- ***Enfish v. Microsoft* (Fed. Cir. 2016):** a claim directed to an *improvement in computer functionality* (a self-referential database table) is eligible at step 2A — it is not "directed to" an abstract idea at all. Our analog is narrower and we state it conservatively: the platform improves a *technological process of simulation/diagnostics*, not general-purpose computing. That is the *Diehr*/process-improvement lane, not the pure-*Enfish* lane, and we should brief the attorney that *Enfish* is supporting, not controlling, for us.

**First failure (this section):** the examiner refuses *McRO* on the ground that our "specific rules" are themselves just mathematics (distinguishing *McRO*, where the rules were heuristics, not closed-form math — cf. the §101 treatment of math-heavy rules). Mitigation: we do not claim the math; we claim the *engineered diagnostic and control behavior* the math is wired into — the fail-closed status output and the simulation-fidelity improvement — which is the *Diehr* "transformation/improvement of a process" footing, independent of whether the internal rules are mathematical.

## 2. The candid abstract-idea risk (stated at full strength, as the contract requires)

The BUILD CONTRACT forbids manufacturing a survivor and demands we name the first failure before the counter-argument. Applied here: **we must state the §101 rejection at its strongest before we answer it.** A weak strawman rejection would be a self-promotion violation. So here is the rejection an able examiner would write, in their voice:

> *"Claim 1 is directed to a mathematical concept and the abstract idea of collecting information, analyzing it according to mathematical rules, and displaying the result. The steps of 'computing a proper-distance functional,' 'evaluating coordinate-invariance diagnostics,' 'reconstructing an effective source ledger,' and 'applying energy-condition diagnostics' are each mathematical computations (differential geometry, tensor contraction, evaluation of inequalities) that could be performed mentally or with pen and paper given sufficient time, and that fall within the 'mathematical concepts' and 'mental processes' groupings of the 2019 PEG. The 'gate-card rules' are rules for organizing human activity / a mental classification. The recited computer performs these in a conventional manner; 'outputting a status-labeled visualization' is insignificant extra-solution activity (cf. display steps held insignificant). Under Alice step two, the claim adds no inventive concept beyond the judicial exception applied on a generic computer (Benson, Flook, Electric Power Group v. Alstom — gathering and analyzing information and displaying results is abstract). Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. §101."*

That is a strong rejection. *Electric Power Group v. Alstom* (Fed. Cir. 2016) is the most dangerous citation against us: "collecting information, analyzing it, and displaying certain results of the collection and analysis" was held abstract, and our pipeline can be uncharitably squeezed into exactly that shape. We must assume the examiner cites it.

Three honest concessions, made up front so the counter-argument is credible:

1. **The math is real and central.** We will not pretend the tensor engine is incidental. The Christoffel/Riemann/Einstein-tensor computations and the NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC inequalities *are* mathematics. Hiding them would be both dishonest and ineffective (*Flook* forbids ignoring a recited formula's abstractness by burying it).
2. **A naive "classify the profile" claim is ineligible.** Independent claim seed 1 from source doc 19, taken *verbatim and broad*, is vulnerable — "computing a functional… evaluating diagnostics… applying rules… outputting a visualization" is dangerously close to the *Electric Power Group* shape. The seed is a *starting point for the attorney*, not a safe claim. We flag this explicitly to the attorney (§6) and propose narrowing amendments.
3. **"On a computer" saves nothing.** Per *Alice* step two, generic computer implementation is not an inventive concept. Our inventive concept must live in *what the specific transformations and the fail-closed control do to a technological process*, not in the existence of a CPU.

**First failure (this section):** *Electric Power Group* controls and the claim is held to be ineligible "collect-analyze-display." Mitigation lives in §3–§5: the claim is re-characterized as an *improvement to simulation diagnostics and a fail-closed compliance/control engine that transforms the operation of a downstream technological process*, which is *not* mere display of analysis — it changes what the system *does* (rejects coordinate artifacts before they propagate; gates downstream mission-visualization and any control output).

## 3. The technical-improvement counter-argument — three stackable grounds

Eligibility for software/simulation inventions lives or dies on whether the claim is *directed to a specific technical improvement* (MPEP 2106.05(a); *McRO*, *Enfish*, *Finjan*, *DDR Holdings*). We assert three grounds. They are *independent* — the attorney can plead them in the alternative — and *stackable* — together they integrate the exception into a practical application.

### Ground A — improved simulation/diagnostic fidelity (a concrete technical improvement to a technological process)

The platform improves the **fidelity and trustworthiness of metric-interface simulation** by a specific mechanism that prior GR tooling does not perform automatically: it **automatically detects and rejects coordinate-artifact results** before they are reported or propagated downstream. A coordinate-only "effect" — a metric perturbation that looks like a forward-distance change in one chart but is a pure diffeomorphism — is the single most common false positive in this domain. The platform computes coordinate-*invariant* diagnostics (scalar invariants, tetrad/geodesic checks; see HC-01, E01a/E01b) and **fail-closes** the result to `FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY` when the apparent effect is not invariant.

This is the *Diehr* footing: in *Diamond v. Diehr* (1981) a claim using the Arrhenius equation was eligible because it *improved a technological process* (rubber curing) — the math was in service of a concrete improvement. Here the "process" is **numerical/symbolic simulation of candidate spacetime metrics**, and the improvement is **automatic invariant-validation that eliminates a known class of simulation false positives.** Concretely, the claimed transformation takes a raw chart-dependent quantity and produces a *validated, frame-independent diagnostic with a machine-checked status*, which a generic GR-tensor calculator does **not** do (it computes whatever you ask in whatever chart you give it and reports it without an eligibility verdict — see prior-art delta, §8).

Worked illustration of the *technical* delta (not a physics claim — a diagnostic-behavior claim). Consider a metric written in a chart where `g_tt` carries a coordinate boost that *mimics* a forward-lobe shortening. A bare tensor package returns a nonzero coordinate "shortening score" `S_L^(coord)`. The claimed pipeline additionally computes a curvature scalar comparison between the candidate and the flat reference, e.g. evaluates the Kretschmann scalar `K = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ}` and a geodesic-deviation proxy, and applies the rule:

text if |S_L^(coord)| > ε and (K_candidate − K_reference) < δ_invariant and geodesic_deviation_invariant ≈ 0: status ← FAIL_COORDINATE_ONLY # apparent effect is pure-chart suppress downstream propagation # the improvement: artifact never reaches mission overlay else: status ← carry to next gate (source ledger)


The eligibility-relevant point is the **`suppress downstream propagation`** line. That is not "display a result." It *changes the behavior of the simulation system*: an artifact that a conventional tool would report (and a downstream mission visualization would render) is **prevented from propagating**. That is a concrete, technical improvement to the operation of the simulation pipeline — the *McRO*/`Diehr` lane.

### Ground B — a fail-closed compliance/control engine (a specific machine that constrains downstream action)

The gate-card validator is not a "mental classification." It is a **fail-closed state machine** whose output *gates* what the rest of the system is permitted to do. Per the BUILD CONTRACT's enforcement logic (§3 of the contract) and source doc 23's "fail-closed claim engine" fallback, the engine enforces hard inter-field rules:

text if source_check ∈ {FAIL, None}: forbid "propulsion" in strongest_allowed_claim if uv_boundary == UV_DELEGATED: forbid "global stability solved" as closed claim if any mission_overlay lacks status: block render of overlay (FAIL_MISSION_OVERCLAIM) energy_check is never a clean PASS → emit "pass / audit-visible" only


This is **significantly more than abstract classification** because the engine's output is *coupled to and constrains a downstream technological function*: it blocks the generation/rendering of an invalid mission-visualization artifact and blocks the emission of an over-strong status label. The *Finjan v. Blue Coat* (Fed. Cir. 2018) analogy is direct and we should brief it as our strongest single case: *Finjan* held a behavior-based malware-scanning method eligible because it generated a **specific security-profile data structure** that **enabled a new kind of protective action** — it was not just "detecting viruses" abstractly; it produced an actionable artifact that changed downstream behavior. Our gate-card is the structural twin: a **specific status data structure** (the gate-card JSON of contract §3) that **enables/forbids specific downstream rendering and claim-emission actions**. The fail-closed coupling is the inventive concept; it is the thing that is *not* well-understood, routine, or conventional in physics-simulation tooling, none of which ships a compliance engine that vetoes downstream outputs (§8).

### Ground C — specific, non-conventional data transformations (the *Flook*/2B inventive concept)

Even if Grounds A–B fail to "integrate" at step 2A, the claim survives 2B if it recites *specific* transformations that are not the routine, conventional way of doing this. Our pipeline is a *named, ordered* sequence of transformations on a *specific data object* (the excitation profile `Ξ_drive = {δg_μν, δA_μ^a, δφ^I, δG_μA, δG_AB, state/gauge data}`):

1. metric ansatz → tensor field set (Christoffel, Riemann, Ricci, Einstein),
2. Einstein tensor → **reconstructed effective source ledger** `T_eff = G_μν/(8πG)` with a **mismatch norm** against any declared physical source (the "no-free-lunch audit" of source doc 23) — *this reverse-reconstruction-then-mismatch step is the least conventional transformation and we should make it a claim centerpiece*,
3. `T_eff` → energy-condition functionals → **exoticity score** over violation volumes,
4. perturbation → **pure-gauge/BRST projection** with two-sided negative-control guard,
5. compactification-dependency scan → `UV_DELEGATED` flag,
6. all gate outputs → fail-closed gate-card → status-validated overlay.

The **source-ledger reconstruction-and-mismatch** transformation (step 2) is the crown jewel for 2B: it is *not* what GR tensor packages do. They go *forward* (given `T_μν`, find `g`, or given `g`, report `G_μν`). The claimed transformation goes *backward-then-audits*: it reconstructs the source a metric *would require* and computes a **mismatch norm against the declared/available source**, producing a "this metric is unsourced by your stated matter content" verdict. That specific, auditable transformation is the kind of "particular arrangement" that *Bascom v. AT&T* (Fed. Cir. 2016) found could be an inventive concept even when individual elements were known.

**First failure (this section):** all three grounds are characterized as "still just math, dressed up" — the examiner says the suppression/gating is itself just *deciding not to display a number*, i.e., extra-solution activity. Mitigation: emphasize the *coupling* (the gate output controls a downstream technological function and a control representation, source doc 19 family 11) and the *backward-source-reconstruction-then-mismatch* transformation, which is a genuine, atypical data transformation, not display. We also concede that Ground A alone is weakest (closest to "diagnostics = analysis") and instruct the attorney to lead with Ground B (*Finjan* fail-closed engine).
